\tag{P.2.3a.2a.1}
$$
Give $N$ the discrete topology and put $\mathscr R(U)=A^U$ with coordinate restrictions for every $U\subseteq N$. For a nonempty topological boundary, take
$$
\overline\Omega=\Omega\sqcup\{\infty\},
\qquad
\tau_{\rm amb}=\mathcal P(\Omega)\cup\{\overline\Omega\}.
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.2}
$$
Then $\Omega$ is open and dense in $\overline\Omega$ and $\partial\Omega=\{\infty\}$. Every registered ontic update below is extended by fixing $\infty$.

Join the two nodes by one noiseless edge and define the integer-time update
$$
F(x_1,x_2)=(x_2,x_1).
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.3}
$$
Node $1$ predicts node $2$'s next word by $p_{1\to2}(x)=x_1$, and node $2$ predicts node $1$'s next word by $p_{2\to1}(x)=x_2$. Let $\mathfrak M_{\rm fin}$ be the finite predictive-unit response model with state carrier $|\mathfrak M_{\rm fin}|=\Omega$, update $F$, and coordinate protocols $q_{i,k}(x)=(x_i)_k$. The carrier map $\iota:\Omega\to|\mathfrak M_{\rm fin}|$ is the identity.

On probability vectors $\mu\in\mathbb R_+^\Omega$, define the external coordinate-read instrument and internal word flips by
$$
(\mathcal I_i^a\mu)(x)=\mathbf1_{\{x_i=a\}}\mu(x),
\qquad
(\mathcal U_i^v\mu)(x)=\mu(x_1,\ldots,x_i\oplus v,\ldots,x_2),
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.4}
$$
where $a\in A$ and $0\ne v\in A$. Write $\mathcal F=F_*$ for the swap pushforward on probability vectors.

For the epistemic boundary, fix integers $1\le m\le M$, the finite query set $Q=\{q_1,\ldots,q_M\}$, and the finite predictor class $\mathcal P=\{\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_m\}$ with $\pi_j:Q\to\{0,1\}$. Let $\mathcal D=\{D_1,\ldots,D_m\}$ be a finite formal system sort and define the injective constructor $d(j)=q_j=\ulcorner D_j\urcorner$. A lookup interpreter $U(j,q)=\pi_j(q)$ represents and simulates every nominated predictor; equality of returned bits is decidable; and Boolean negation and finite table composition are admitted. Give each $D_j$ the explicit finite response table
$$
r_j(q)=
\begin{cases}
1-U(j,d(j)),&q=d(j),\\
U(j,q),&q\ne d(j).
\end{cases}
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.5}
$$
Every $d(j)$ is an admitted live query, and the finite model record $\mathfrak M_{\rm fin}$ includes the sorts $Q,\mathcal D$, the tables $U,r_j$, and the displayed Boolean operations.
The associated deterministic external instrument is
$$
(\mathcal D_j^b\mu)(x)
=\mathbf1_{\{b=r_j(d(j))\}}\mu(x),
\qquad b\in\{0,1\}.
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.6}
$$
Every outcome subchannel in the $\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal D$ families has the identity ontic transition. The nominated external operations are the normalized whole instruments specified below; the $\mathcal U_i^v$ are nominated internal controls.

Three optional finite response layers are carried on the same $\Omega$. First, for settings $s,t\in\{0,1\}$ and outcomes $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, define the no-write instrument
$$
(\mathcal J_{st}^{ab}\mu)(x)
=\frac12\mathbf1_{\{a\oplus b=st\}}\mu(x).
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.7}
$$
The nominated external-operation class consists of the whole instruments $\{\mathcal I_i^a\}_{a\in A}$, $\{\mathcal D_j^b\}_{b\in\{0,1\}}$, and, when this optional layer is admitted, $\{\mathcal J_{st}^{ab}\}_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}$; it excludes the internal families $\mathcal U$ and $\mathcal K$.
Second, fix $0<\eta<1/2$, let $c(x)=(x_1)_1$, and put
$$
P_\eta(z=1\mid x)=\frac12+\eta(2c(x)-1),
\qquad
(\mathcal K_\eta^z\mu)(x)=P_\eta(z\mid x)\mu(x),
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.8}
$$
with $P_\eta(0\mid x)=1-P_\eta(1\mid x)$. A finite ownership ledger assigns every displayed map in the $\mathcal I$, $\mathcal D$, $\mathcal U$, $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal J$, and $\mathcal K$ families exactly once to the respective typed bookkeeping labels coordinate read, diagonal read, internal flip, network update, contextual response, and internal context bias.

Finally, on $\ell^2(\Omega)$ put
$$
U_F|x\rangle=|F(x)\rangle,
\qquad
P_-:=\frac{I-U_F}{2},
\qquad
H_F:=\pi P_-.
\tag{P.2.3a.2a.9}
$$
The clock domain is $\mathbb Z$ with metric $|t-s|$, orientation $t\mapsto t+1$, and calibration one update per unit. On $\ell^\infty(\Omega)$ use the counting trace $\operatorname{Tr}_\Omega(f)=\sum_xf(x)$ and the uniform density $h_*(x)=|\Omega|^{-1}$.

<a id="theorem-p23a2b-nonempty-finite-constitutive-simulation-coexistence-branch"></a>**Theorem P.2.3a.2b (Nonempty Finite Constitutive-Simulation Coexistence Branch).** Construction P.2.3a.2a has the following properties.

1. It is a two-node distributed simulator: for $\{i,j\}=N$,
   $$
   p_{i\to j}(x)=\operatorname{pr}_j(Fx),
   $$
   where $\operatorname{pr}_j:\Omega\to A$ is coordinate projection. The map $\iota$ is injective, response-faithful, and update-intertwining.
2. The presheaf $\mathscr R$ has unique global gluing: every compatible family of local words is the restriction of exactly one element of $A^N$. The swap and word-flip state maps extend continuously to $\overline\Omega$, preserve $\Omega$, and fix the invariant nonempty boundary $\partial\Omega=\{\infty\}$.
3. The reads are normalized, nonvacuous, and ontically no-write:
   $$
   \sum_{a\in A}\mathcal I_i^a=\operatorname{id},
   \qquad
   \sum_{b\in\{0,1\}}\mathcal D_j^b=\operatorname{id},
   \qquad
   \sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}\mathcal J_{st}^{ab}=\operatorname{id}.
   \tag{P.2.3a.2b.1}
   $$
   The coordinate outcome separates all eight local words. Every $\mathcal U_i^v$ is a normalized internal control and changes a retained response for some state. The common diagrams are
   $$
   \mathcal I_i^a\mathcal U_i^v=\mathcal U_i^v\mathcal I_i^{a\oplus v},
   \qquad
   \mathcal I_j^a\mathcal U_i^v=\mathcal U_i^v\mathcal I_j^a\ (i\ne j),
   \qquad
   \mathcal F\mathcal U_i^v=\mathcal U_j^v\mathcal F.
   \tag{P.2.3a.2b.2}
   $$
4. For every $j$, the lookup predictor $\pi_j$ fails on its admitted coded system:
   $$
   r_j(d(j))\ne U(j,d(j)).
   \tag{P.2.3a.2b.3}
   $$
   Thus the displayed finite coding, interpreter, query, Boolean-closure, and causal no-write records jointly realize Definition P.5.2 for the nominated predictor and external-operation classes.
5. The optional measurement layer is no-disturbance and has uniform one-site marginals, while it admits no global outcome assignment $(a_0,a_1,b_0,b_1)$. Indeed such an assignment would require
   $$
   a_0\oplus b_0=a_0\oplus b_1=a_1\oplus b_0=0,
   \qquad
   a_1\oplus b_1=1,
   \tag{P.2.3a.2b.4}
   $$
   whose fourfold XOR is $0=1$. Hence shared-carrier gluing and protocol contextuality coexist here because they concern differently typed objects. In the sign variables $(-1)^a$ and $(-1)^b$, with the settings $(s,t)$ in the role of $(x,y)$, the table (P.2.3a.2a.7) is the formula (G.1.7a.12.1) at parameter value $1$. Its CHSH value is $4$, above the bound $2\sqrt2$ obeyed by local dichotomic Born measurements, so the layer is carried by the joint setting-indexed instrument $\{\mathcal J_{st}^{ab}\}$ on $\Omega$ and belongs to the no-disturbance tables outside the Born range of Theorem G.1.7a.12.
6. The context-bias instrument is normalized, its displacement from the unbiased response has sup norm $\eta>0$, and every $\mathcal K_\eta^z$ commutes with every coordinate-read subchannel. The finite ownership ledger assigns each displayed map exactly one typed bookkeeping label. Thus the formal context response and external no-write reads coexist with an unambiguous operation inventory.
7. Since $F^2=I$, $U_F$ is a self-adjoint unitary, $P_-$ is an orthogonal projection, $H_F$ is bounded and self-adjoint, and
   $$
   e^{-iH_F}=U_F.
   \tag{P.2.3a.2b.5}
   $$
   Thus the displayed discrete clock, generator, metric, orientation, and calibration are mutually consistent.
8. The coordinate bits separate all $64$ carrier states and generate $\ell^\infty(\Omega)$ as a unital pointwise algebra. Moreover
   $$
   \operatorname{Tr}_\Omega h_*=1,
   \qquad
   -\operatorname{Tr}_\Omega(h_*\log h_*)=\log64.
   \tag{P.2.3a.2b.6}
   $$
   A uniform node marginal has entropy $\log|A|=3\log2$, equal to the Shannon capacity of one directed use of the noiseless $A$-valued edge.

*Proof.* The swap gives $\operatorname{pr}_j(Fx)=x_i$ for $\{i,j\}=N$; identity of carriers proves response faithfulness and intertwining. Coordinate restrictions on the discrete two-point cover glue uniquely. The topology (P.2.3a.2a.2) makes $\Omega$ open, gives $\overline\Omega$ as its closure, and leaves $\{\infty\}$ as its boundary. The preimage of every open subset of $\Omega$ under an extended swap or flip is again a subset of $\Omega$, while the preimage of $\overline\Omega$ is $\overline\Omega$; hence the extensions are continuous and fix the boundary. Equations (P.2.3a.2a.4), (P.2.3a.2a.6), and (P.2.3a.2a.7) give (P.2.3a.2b.1), and direct substitution gives (P.2.3a.2b.2). Equation (P.2.3a.2a.5) proves (P.2.3a.2b.3), while the finite lookup and circuit tables verify all nominated closure operations.

Summing (P.2.3a.2a.7) over either remote outcome gives the uniform marginal $1/2$ independently of the remote setting; the XOR contradiction proves contextuality. With $A=(-1)^a$ and $B=(-1)^b$, (P.2.3a.2a.7) reads $\tfrac14\bigl(1+AB(-1)^{st}\bigr)$, which is (G.1.7a.12.1) at parameter value $1$; its correlators are $E_{st}=(-1)^{st}$ and $E_{00}+E_{01}+E_{10}-E_{11}=4$. For Hermitian $A_0,A_1$ on one tensor factor and $B_0,B_1$ on the other with $A_s^2=B_t^2=I$, the operator $\mathcal B=A_0\otimes(B_0+B_1)+A_1\otimes(B_0-B_1)$ satisfies $\mathcal B^2=4I-[A_0,A_1]\otimes[B_0,B_1]$, so $\lVert\mathcal B\rVert\le2\sqrt2$ and every Born value of the CHSH combination has modulus at most $2\sqrt2$. The same bound holds for Hermitian contractions, because the combination is affine in each observable and every Hermitian contraction on a finite-dimensional space is a convex combination of Hermitian unitaries. Equation (P.2.3a.2a.8) is normalized, differs from $1/2$ by exactly $\eta$, and commutes with the coordinate reads because both act by diagonal multiplication. The ownership assertion follows from the displayed one-entry-per-map ledger. The spectral identities for an involutive permutation give claim 7. Finally, coordinate bits separate points, their products generate point indicators, and direct counting gives (P.2.3a.2b.6) and the one-use capacity identity. ∎

<a id="corollary-p23a2c-attained-two-register-minimum-in-the-fixed-capacity-class"></a>**Corollary P.2.3a.2c (Attained Two-Register Minimum in the Fixed-Capacity Class).** Consider architectures whose static carrier is a Cartesian product $R_1\times\cdots\times R_{n_{\mathrm{reg}}}$, where each register satisfies $|R_i|\le2^{K_0}$ with $K_0=3$, and whose encoding of every state of $\Omega$ is injective. Then $n_{\mathrm{reg}}\ge2$, and Construction P.2.3a.2a attains equality.

*Proof.* The Cartesian-product carrier has at most $2^{n_{\mathrm{reg}}K_0}$ distinguishable states. Injectivity therefore requires $2^{n_{\mathrm{reg}}K_0}\ge|\Omega|=2^{2K_0}$, hence $n_{\mathrm{reg}}\ge2$. The displayed coordinate representation into two registers is bijective. ∎

<a id="remark-p23a2d-scope-of-the-finite-witness"></a>**Remark P.2.3a.2d (Scope of the Finite Witness).** Theorem P.2.3a.2b proves nonemptiness and simultaneous consistency of a distributed constitutive carrier, response-faithful predictive identity, finite Authentic boundaries, normalized no-write reads, internal controls, global world gluing, protocol contextuality, a context-dependent response, an exact discrete clock, a finite trace, and one-use cut saturation. Corollary P.2.3a.2c proves minimal register count on the fixed per-register-capacity exact-injection class. Absolute quantification over unregistered predictors or interventions, selection against monolithic carriers of at least $2K_0$ bits, a thermodynamic arrow, physical CC realization and energy cost, physical source exhaustion and no-double-counting, a cosmological observer trace, and physical horizon identification are governed by the corresponding fields of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{CS}}$.

<a id="construction-p23a2e-two-node-executed-diagonal"></a>**Construction P.2.3a.2e (Two-Node Executed Diagonal).** Extend the word-swap component of Construction P.2.3a.2a by attaching a finite machine to each node $p\in\{0,1\}$. Its registers are
$$
m_p=(\mathrm{pc}_p,q_p,a_p,o_p)
\in\{\mathrm{load},\mathrm{query},\mathrm{write},\mathrm{halt}\}
\times\{0,1\}^3.
$$
The phase uses two bits. Together with the three-bit word $x_p$, each node has eight bits, and the world carrier $X$ has $2^{16}$ states. Fix an arbitrary table $U:\{0,1\}^2\to\{0,1\}$. One update $G_U$ swaps the words and applies one action at each node:
$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\mathrm{pc}_p&\text{register assignment}&\text{next phase}\\\hline
\mathrm{load}&q_p\leftarrow p&\mathrm{query}\\
\mathrm{query}&a_p\leftarrow U(p,q_p)&\mathrm{write}\\
\mathrm{write}&o_p\leftarrow1-a_p&\mathrm{halt}\\
\mathrm{halt}&\text{no change}&\mathrm{halt}
\end{array}.
\tag{P.2.3a.2e.1}
$$
Registers absent from an assignment retain their values. The three registered operations in a step are the channel word swap and the two node actions. Each load, query or write action records one reset of $q_p$, $a_p$ or $o_p$, respectively, owned by node $p$; swap and halt record none. Define the operation cost to count written register bits: six for the swap, three for each non-halt machine action, and zero for halt.

The sixteen read protocols return the individual register bits. At perspective $p$, let $b_{p,k}=x_{p,k}$ be the predicted next word bit of node $1-p$, and put
$$
b_{p,\mathrm{out}}=
\begin{cases}1-a_p,&\mathrm{pc}_p=\mathrm{write},\\o_p,&\mathrm{pc}_p\ne\mathrm{write}.
\end{cases}
$$
The task comprises these four predictions at each of the two perspectives. For each of the word and output groups, a rule chooses one of the five laws: uniform, point mass at $b$, point mass at $1-b$, point mass at $0$, or point mass at $1$. There are twenty-five rules. Copy or flip costs three read bits for the word group and four for the output group; the other choices cost zero. The budget is seven read bits. The chosen rule uses the point mass at $b$ for both groups. All protocols outside the task receive the uniform law. Verification accepts an outcome exactly when its assigned probability is positive.

Compare two implementations on these same read protocols. The compact implementation stores the sixteen bits. The padded implementation has carrier $X\times\{0,1\}^2$ and update
$$
\widetilde G_U(x,z_0,z_1)
   =(G_Ux,o_0(x),o_1(x)).
\tag{P.2.3a.2e.2}
$$
The observer reads only the $X$ coordinates, and the objective is the declared register-bit count, sixteen or eighteen.

<a id="proposition-p23a2f-executed-refutation-prediction-score-and-register-ledger"></a>**Proposition P.2.3a.2f (Executed Refutation, Prediction Score and Register Ledger).** Construction P.2.3a.2e has the following properties for every table $U$.

1. From every state in which machine $p$ starts in the load phase, three updates leave it in state $(\mathrm{halt},p,U(p,p),1-U(p,p))$. Consequently the nominated lookup predictor $P_j(c)=U(j,c)$ fails on the three-update output of its own coded machine $j$.
2. The chosen rule fits the seven-bit read budget and predicts every task outcome exactly in every state. Its mean success probability per task prediction is one, against one half for the uniform baseline. It maximizes that score over the declared twenty-five-rule class under every distribution on initial world states. Every protocol's verification cut accepts the actual next outcome.
3. Two world states merged by $G_U$ have at least one registered reset between them. Within a fixed load, query or write phase, the machine successor forgets exactly the indicated overwritten bit. Starting both machines in load, the first three updates record exactly six resets, three per node, and thirty-six written register bits. Later updates record no machine reset.
4. The compact and padded implementations have identical retained read outcomes at every time on corresponding initial states. Their objectives are sixteen and eighteen, so the compact implementation uniquely minimizes the objective in this two-member comparison class.

*Proof.* Starting in load, the successive machine states are
$$
(\mathrm{query},p,a,o),\qquad
(\mathrm{write},p,U(p,p),o),\qquad
(\mathrm{halt},p,U(p,p),1-U(p,p)).
$$
The final output differs from $U(p,p)$, proving item 1. The swap sends the current word of $p$ to node $1-p$, and the output assignment in (P.2.3a.2e.1) is exactly $b_{p,\mathrm{out}}$. Thus the chosen rule is exact on all eight task predictions. Its read cost is $3+4=7$, and no probability-of-correct-prediction score exceeds one. The uniform law scores one half on each binary outcome. The remaining protocol laws are uniform and hence accept either outcome, proving item 2.

If neither of two states records a reset, both machines are halted in both states. On that subspace the update is the invertible word swap and the identity on the machines, so distinct states cannot merge. For a fixed non-halt phase, the assignment table preserves every other machine register and replaces only $q_p$, $a_p$ or $o_p$; equality of successors is therefore precisely agreement on those other registers. From two load phases, the reset list is $\mathrm{load}_0,\mathrm{load}_1,\mathrm{query}_0,\mathrm{query}_1,\mathrm{write}_0,\mathrm{write}_1$. There are three swaps and six non-halt machine actions, of total write count $3\cdot6+6\cdot3=36$. Both machines then stay halted. This proves item 3. Projection of (P.2.3a.2e.2) onto $X$ commutes with the update. Induction on time gives identical retained read outcomes. The strict inequality $16<18$ proves item 4. ∎

The diagonal conclusion concerns the nominated two-row lookup class. The read budget and write count are finite register accounts; the three updates are logical steps. A physical time or heat claim additionally uses the corresponding clock or Definition 28 reset implementation. The minimum in item 4 concerns its two specified implementations and its register-bit objective.

<a id="proposition-p23a3-separated-certificate-consequences"></a>**Proposition P.2.3a.3 (Separated Certificate Consequences).** Theorem P.2.3a.2b proves that the displayed finite constitutive-model class is nonempty and that its architecture, Authentic boundaries, gluing, control, contextual response, clock, trace, and cut records can coexist. Physical realization is supplied separately by an accepted $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{CS}}$, which establishes a PPI-physicalizable constitutive-simulation candidate on $(\mathfrak P,\mathcal E)$, a response-faithful MPU representation, and one shared world-response object up to the declared equivalence.

If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{sel}}$ verifies Principle P.14.9c, it selects the constitutive candidate as the better compression within its named theory class. If it verifies the physical PCE comparison, it selects the constitutive architecture within its named realization class. If both components of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{auth}}$ pass, the model is an Authentic Simulation on their declared classes. An accepted $\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{CS}}$ proves the registered distributed realization; its additional selection or mutual-prediction-escape conclusion is supplied by the corresponding extra clause. Perspective access, zero disturbance, and temporal realization follow separately from $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{persp}}$ and $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{CS}}$. An accepted $\mathfrak O_{\mathrm{CS}}$ proves its specified observer-algebra, trace, and entropy realization; its cosmological observable is supplied by the complete physical-map package in field 9. An accepted $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{CS,CC}}$ proves coexistence of the nominated internal context-to-control and external no-write protocols. A constitution-to-control implication requires its own checked implication proof in that field. The accepted extensions $\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{ctx}}$ and $\mathfrak H_\Sigma$ supply protocol contextuality and horizon saturation, respectively. Empirical attribution is the realization claim and exclusion region registered in $\mathfrak F_{\mathrm{CS}}$.

*Proof.* Construction P.2.3a.2a and Theorem P.2.3a.2b prove formal existence and coexistence, and Corollary P.2.3a.2c proves exactly its stated fixed-capacity minimum. Physical model existence and the common response object follow from fields 1, 2, 3, and 6 of Definition P.2.3a.2. Principle P.14.9c and the physical PCE comparison give the two distinct selection conclusions from $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{sel}}$. Definition P.5.2 requires exactly the two records in $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{auth}}$. Every remaining conclusion is the acceptance predicate of its separately named field or extension; the independence clauses in Definition P.2.3a.2 keep those predicates separate. ∎

### P.2.4 Cogito-Relative Binary Epistemic Classification

The certainty derived from the Cogito is not merely existential; it is informational. The self-verification inherent in "I think, therefore I am" establishes a fundamental epistemic distinction:
*   **Epistemic Certainty (Value '1'):** The knowledge of the thinking self's existence. This is assigned binary value '1', representing a state of zero doubt *about this specific proposition*.
*   **Epistemic Uncertainty (Value '0'):** All other propositions (about the external world, specific thoughts, memories, etc.) that are subject to doubt. These are assigned binary value '0' *relative to the foundational certainty of the '1'*.

This is a two-class epistemic bookkeeping convention relative to Cogito-grade warrant. Identifying it with a physical bit, a thermodynamic record, an ontological self/non-self partition, or the binary verification quotient used later requires a separately stated map and realization certificate.

## <a id="p25-from-the-cogito-to-plurality-the-minimal-anomaly-free-predictive-block"></a>P.2.5 From the Cogito to Plurality: The Minimal Anomaly‑Free Predictive Block

The Cogito (Section P.2.1) establishes the existence of at least one knowing subject, but it does not settle solipsism: is this single locus of awareness all that exists? Within the consciousness‑first ontology (Section P.2.2), the Problem of Other Minds becomes structural: what, within PU, grounds multiple perspectives rather than one solitary predictor?

PU records two branch-relative motivations for plurality:

1. **Modeling motivation:** a multi-perspective model can realize the cross-perspective correlations required by Definition P.2.5.1; their occurrence rests on the stochastic and coupling premises of Thesis P.2.5.1a.

2. **Finite representation obstruction:** Theorem P.1 proves that no single $\mathbb C^8$ carrier carries an anomaly-free representation satisfying its declared simultaneous nontrivial $SU(3)$ and $SU(2)$ action conditions. This excludes a single-MPU realization of that nominated SM-like representation class.

Applying the second result to the realized world additionally requires the PU-to-SM carrier identification. The conclusion that multiple loci of awareness are present further uses the separate Minimal Awareness interpretive convention (Section P.2.5.4).

### P.2.5.1 Foundational Support: Genuine Novelty as Structured Novelty

Definition P.5.2 requires independently certified epistemic and causal no-write boundaries. Structured novelty is introduced here as an additional modeling desideratum with its own stochastic and coarse-graining certificates.

<a id="definition-p251-structured-novelty"></a>**Definition P.2.5.1 (Structured Novelty).**
Let $(X_i(t))_{i\in \mathcal{I}}$ be a collection of outcome processes associated with distinct predictive perspectives (MPUs or aggregates) within a candidate universe. The universe exhibits structured novelty if:

(i) **Irreducibility:** For each $i\in \mathcal{I}$, there exists $\tau>0$ such that
$$
H\!\left(X_i(t+\tau)\mid \mathcal{H}_t\right)>0,
$$
where $\mathcal H_t$ is the complete actual history up to time $t$. The conditional-Shannon convention is extended to arbitrary alphabets by $H(X\mid\mathcal H_t)=\sup_{\xi}H(\xi(X)\mid\mathcal H_t)$, over all finite measurable outcome partitions $\xi$. It agrees with ordinary finite/countable conditional Shannon entropy and expresses residual uncertainty independently of measurement units. Definition P.2.5.1e and Theorem P.2.5.1f give its complete classifier; Proposition P.2.5.1i treats differential entropy separately relative to a specified reference measure. Operationally, the conditioning uses the complete actual past, not a finite history window or an oracle for future outcomes; clause (i) requires residual uncertainty even given that complete past, consistent with SPAP (Theorems 10–11).

(ii) **Relational dependence:** There exist $i\neq j$ such that
$$
I\!\left(X_i(t);X_j(t)\right)>0,
$$
so outcomes are not merely independent noise across perspectives.

(iii) **Scale structure:** Let $X_i^{(\ell)}(t)$ denote a coarse‑graining of $X_i(t)$ at resolution level $\ell$ (finer $\ell$ → more detailed; coarser $\ell$ → more macroscopic). Define the correlation‑content function
$$
\mathcal{I}(\ell):=\sum_{i<j} I\!\left(X_i^{(\ell)}(t);X_j^{(\ell)}(t)\right).
$$
Structured novelty requires that $\mathcal{I}(\ell)$ is non‑constant in $\ell$: there exist $\ell_1\neq \ell_2$ with $\mathcal{I}(\ell_1)\neq \mathcal{I}(\ell_2)$.

A system satisfying (i) alone produces novelty as noise. A system satisfying (i)–(iii) produces novelty that is both irreducible and organized—precisely the kind of novelty that can support persistent laws, emergent structure, and predictive leverage.

<a id="thesis-p251a-conditional-plurality-for-structured-novelty"></a>**Thesis P.2.5.1a (Conditional Plurality for Structured Novelty).** Let a candidate model contain at least two outcome processes with positive residual conditional entropy, a response-active coupling producing nonzero cross-perspective mutual information, and a registered coarse-graining for which $\mathcal I(\ell)$ is nonconstant. Then it exhibits structured novelty in the sense of Definition P.2.5.1. A singleton perspective cannot satisfy clause (ii) of that definition.

*Justification.* The conclusion is immediate from the three defining clauses. SPAP alone does not imply positive conditional entropy for each nominated process; coupling alone does not imply nonzero mutual information; and aggregation alone does not imply scale-dependent correlation content. Those are independently falsifiable stochastic and coarse-graining premises. The authentic-simulation reading treats this certified structure as a modeling desideratum, not as a PCE-selected or generic consequence. $\square$

<a id="theorem-p251c-finite-structured-novelty-witness-and-architecture-nonidentifiability"></a>**Theorem P.2.5.1c (Finite Structured-Novelty Witness and Architecture Nonidentifiability).** Let $\{Z_t,N_{1,t},N_{2,t}:t\in\mathbb Z\}$ be independent fair binary variables and set
$$
X_i(t)=(Z_t,N_{i,t}),
\qquad i\in\{1,2\}.
\tag{P.2.5.1c.1}
$$
Take the fine coarse-graining to be the identity and the coarse one to discard the shared coordinate,
$$
X_i^{(\ell_{\mathrm c})}(t)=N_{i,t}.
\tag{P.2.5.1c.2}
$$
Then this two-perspective process satisfies Definition P.2.5.1:
$$
H(X_i(t+1)\mid\mathcal H_t)=2\ln2,
\qquad
I(X_1(t);X_2(t))=\ln2,
\tag{P.2.5.1c.3}
$$
while
$$
\mathcal I(\ell_{\mathrm f})=\ln2,
\qquad
\mathcal I(\ell_{\mathrm c})=0.
\tag{P.2.5.1c.4}
$$
The same joint response law can be implemented by homogeneous isomorphic carriers or by differently encoded carriers. Definition P.2.5.1 therefore determines neither that architecture label nor an ordering between their attained PCE objectives; such an ordering requires the separately fixed complete cost and value ledger.

*Proof.* Independence across time makes $(Z_{t+1},N_{i,t+1})$ independent of the complete past and uniformly distributed on four outcomes, which proves the entropy identity. The two fine variables share exactly $Z_t$ and have conditionally independent private coordinates, so their mutual information is $H(Z_t)=\ln2$. After the projection in (P.2.5.1c.2), the retained variables $N_{1,t}$ and $N_{2,t}$ are independent and their mutual information is zero. Relabeling or re-encoding a realization without changing these joint laws preserves all four quantities. A PCE order depends additionally on its declared objective ledger, which the response law does not determine. ∎

<a id="theorem-p251d-structured-novelty-classification-on-stationary-finite-markov-perspectives"></a>**Theorem P.2.5.1d (Structured-Novelty Classification on Stationary Finite Markov Perspectives).** Let $\mathcal I$ be finite with $|\mathcal I|\ge2$, and let the joint outcome process $Y_t=(X_i(t))_{i\in\mathcal I}$ take values in a finite product alphabet $\mathcal Y=\prod_i\mathcal X_i$. Let the registered coarse-graining ladder $\mathfrak L$ act coordinatewise, $X_i^{(\ell)}(t)=c_i^{(\ell)}(X_i(t))$, and contain the identity level $\ell_{\mathrm f}$ and a terminal level $\ell_\top$ at which every $c_i^{(\ell_\top)}$ is constant.

1. At every fixed time $t$, clause (iii) of Definition P.2.5.1 holds if and only if clause (ii) holds, and clause (ii) holds if and only if the law of some pair $(X_i(t),X_j(t))$ is not the product of its marginals.
2. If $(Y_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}$ is a stationary Markov chain with transition matrix $K$ and stationary law $\pi$, and $\mathcal H_t$ is generated by $(Y_s)_{s\le t}$, then clause (i) holds for $i$ if and only if there are $\tau\ge1$ and $y$ with $\pi(y)>0$ such that $X_i$ is nonconstant on the support of $K^\tau(y,\cdot)$. The support patterns of the powers $K^\tau$ take finitely many values, so finitely many $\tau$ decide this.

Consequently, a stationary finite Markov perspective process on such a ladder exhibits structured novelty exactly when every $X_i$ is nonconstant on some $\tau$-step support from a stationary-positive state and some pair of perspectives is stochastically dependent; both conditions are read off from $(K,\pi)$. On a ladder lacking the identity or the terminal level, clause (iii) is an additional condition fixed by the registered coarse-grainings; Theorem P.2.5.1c attains it with the projection (P.2.5.1c.2).

*Proof.* For item 1, mutual information vanishes exactly for independent pairs, which gives the second equivalence. At $\ell_\top$ every coarse variable is constant, so $\mathcal I(\ell_\top)=0$, while $\mathcal I(\ell_{\mathrm f})=\sum_{i<j}I(X_i(t);X_j(t))$ is positive exactly under clause (ii). If (ii) holds, these two levels give distinct values. If (ii) fails, every pair is independent, coordinatewise functions of independent variables are independent, and $\mathcal I\equiv0$ on $\mathfrak L$, so (iii) fails.

For item 2, the Markov property and stationarity give
$$
H(X_i(t+\tau)\mid\mathcal H_t)=H(X_i(t+\tau)\mid Y_t)=\sum_y\pi(y)\,H\bigl(X_i(t+\tau)\mid Y_t=y\bigr),
$$
and the conditional law of $X_i(t+\tau)$ given $Y_t=y$ is the image of $K^\tau(y,\cdot)$ under the $i$th coordinate. That image has positive entropy exactly when it is not a point mass, that is, when $X_i$ is nonconstant on the support of $K^\tau(y,\cdot)$. The support pattern of $K^\tau$ is the $\tau$th Boolean power of the support pattern of $K$, and there are finitely many Boolean matrices of size $|\mathcal Y|$. ∎

<a id="definition-p251e-finite-partition-conditional-entropy-and-pair-information"></a>**Definition P.2.5.1e (Finite-Partition Conditional Entropy and Pair Information).**

Fix a probability space, an arbitrary family of standard-Borel-valued processes $X_i(t)$, and the actual complete history sigma-algebra $\mathcal H_t$. Finite, countable and arbitrary perspective index sets are allowed: an unordered-pair sum always means the supremum of its finite subsums. For every registered level $\ell$, the actual coarse variable is $Y_{i\ell}=c_{i\ell}(X_i(t))$, where every map is measurable with standard-Borel codomain. The levels need neither include identity/constant maps nor be nested. The history is not replaced by a finite window.

For a standard-Borel variable $X$ and sigma-algebra $\mathcal F$, define the partition-Shannon conditional entropy
$$
H_{\rm p}(X\mid\mathcal F)=\sup_\xi H(\xi(X)\mid\mathcal F),
\tag{P.2.5.1e.1}
$$
where $\xi$ ranges over finite measurable partitions. Ordinary finite/countable Shannon conditional entropy is recovered, with value in $[0,\infty]$. For a regular conditional distribution $K_\omega$ of $X$ given $\mathcal F$, the finite partition expression is
$$
H(\xi(X)\mid\mathcal F)=\mathbb E\sum_{A\in\xi}-K_\omega(A)\log K_\omega(A).
\tag{P.2.5.1e.2}
$$
This is the conditional-Shannon extension fixed at Definition P.2.5.1; differential entropy is treated separately in Proposition P.2.5.1i.

For any two standard-Borel variables put
$$
I(X;Y)=D(P_{XY}\Vert P_X\otimes P_Y).
\tag{P.2.5.1e.3}
$$
For finite partitions $\xi=(A_a)$ and $\eta=(B_b)$ write
$$
D_{\xi,\eta}(X,Y)=\sum_{a,b}p_{ab}\log\frac{p_{ab}}{p_a p_b},
\tag{P.2.5.1e.4}
$$
with zero terms interpreted as zero. If $p_{ab}>0$, its two marginals are positive, so this finite sum is well defined. These formulas use natural logarithms, as in Theorem P.2.5.1c.

<a id="theorem-p251f-complete-measurable-process-structured-novelty-classifier"></a>**Theorem P.2.5.1f (Complete Measurable-Process Structured-Novelty Classifier).** Choose for each outcome space a countable point-separating algebra that generates its Borel sigma-algebra, and let $\xi_n$ be the finite partition generated by its first $n$ members.

1. At each $t$, clause (i) with $H=H_{\rm p}$ holds for perspective $i$ exactly when some admitted lag $\tau>0$ and one algebra member $A$ satisfy
   $$
   \mathbb P\{0<K^{i,t,\tau}_\omega(A)<1\}>0.
   \tag{P.2.5.1f.1}
   $$
   Equivalently, the conditional future law $K^{i,t,\tau}_\omega$ fails to be Dirac on a positive-probability set. This condition is invariant under measurable outcome isomorphisms.

2. Clause (ii) holds exactly when some $i\ne j$ and algebra members $A,B$ satisfy
   $$
   P\{X_i(t)\in A,X_j(t)\in B\}\ne P\{X_i(t)\in A\}P\{X_j(t)\in B\}.
   \tag{P.2.5.1f.2}
   $$
   Thus positive dependence has a finite binary-partition witness, including when its total mutual information is infinite.

3. For each level define the directed set of all finite collections $F$ of perspective pairs and finite partitions for the two variables of each pair. Set
   $$
   b_\ell(F)=\sum_{(i,j)\in F}D_{\xi_{ij},\eta_{ij}}(Y_{i\ell},Y_{j\ell}),
   \qquad B_\ell=\sup_F b_\ell(F).
   \tag{P.2.5.1f.3}
   $$
   Then $B_\ell$ equals the correlation content $\mathcal I(\ell)$ of Definition P.2.5.1, in $[0,\infty]$. Clause (iii) holds exactly when there exist levels $\ell,m$, a nonnegative rational $r$, and a finite record $F_+$ such that
   $$
   b_m(F_+)>r,
   \qquad b_\ell(F)\le r\quad\hbox{for every finite record }F.
   \tag{P.2.5.1f.4}
   $$
   Consequently (P.2.5.1f.1) for every perspective, (P.2.5.1f.2) for some pair, and (P.2.5.1f.4) are a complete law-based classifier of Definition P.2.5.1 on this extension. The universal upper test in (P.2.5.1f.4) is retained; a finite search for lower witnesses is not a terminating decision algorithm.

4. If identity and constant levels are registered, clauses (ii) and (iii) are equivalent for every process above, with no finite-alphabet or Markov premise. If these levels are absent, criterion (P.2.5.1f.4) supplies the additional ladder predicate. A nonconstant ladder implies original pair dependence, by data processing.

**Proof.** A standard-Borel random variable has a regular conditional distribution given a sub-sigma-algebra. For each binary event the integrand $h(K(A))$ is nonnegative and vanishes precisely at $K(A)=0,1$. Thus (P.2.5.1f.1) implies positive entropy of that binary partition and hence (P.2.5.1e.1).

Conversely, suppose every member of the countable algebra has conditional probability zero or one almost surely. Remove the union of their null exceptional sets. At each remaining point, the probability measure $K_\omega$ is zero-one on the generating algebra. Such a probability on a standard-Borel space is Dirac: realize the space as a Borel subset of $\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ via a countable separating code. Every coordinate of the pushed-forward measure is almost surely a fixed bit; the countable intersection of those probability-one coordinate events is one singleton. That singleton has probability one and belongs to the embedded space. Hence $K_\omega$ is Dirac. Every finite partition in (P.2.5.1e.2) then has zero entropy. This proves both directions of item 1, including arbitrary conditioning histories. Isomorphisms transport the conditional kernel and preserve its Dirac/non-Dirac status.

For completeness, one fixed refining sequence $\xi_n$ suffices for (P.2.5.1e.1). If $\zeta$ is any finite measurable partition, the conditional probabilities of its cells given $\sigma(\xi_n(X))$ converge almost surely to their indicators by the bounded martingale theorem. Binary/finite entropy continuity and bounded convergence give $H(\zeta(X)\mid\xi_n(X))\to0$. The conditional entropy chain inequality yields
$$
H(\zeta(X)\mid\mathcal F)\le H(\xi_n(X)\mid\mathcal F)+H(\zeta(X)\mid\xi_n(X)).
$$
Taking limits and then the supremum over $\zeta$ proves $H_{\rm p}=\sup_n H(\xi_n(X)\mid\mathcal F)$.

For item 2, equality on every generating rectangle implies equality of the joint measure and product measure by the pi-lambda uniqueness theorem. If measures differ, some generating rectangle therefore differs; its binary quantizations are dependent and have strictly positive finite relative entropy. Conversely a differing rectangle forbids product form, and nonnegativity with the equality criterion for relative entropy gives positive $I$.

The finite-partition identity
$$
I(X;Y)=\sup_{\xi,\eta}D_{\xi,\eta}(X,Y)
\tag{P.2.5.1f.5}
$$
holds also at infinity. Here is a direct justification of the approximation step. For probability measures $P,Q$, the variational identity $D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_f\{\int f\,dP-\log\int e^f\,dQ\}$ holds over bounded measurable $f$: if $P\not\ll Q$, use $f=M1_A$ on a $P$-positive $Q$-null set; otherwise use the logarithm of the density clipped to $[-M,M]$, with truncation of its integrable negative part. The upper bound follows by normalizing $e^fQ$ and applying nonnegativity of relative entropy. On a product standard-Borel space, the increasing finite product partitions generated by the two countable algebras generate the whole product sigma-algebra. Conditional expectations approximate each bounded $f$ in $L^1(P+Q)$, with its uniform bound preserved. Hence both integrals in the variational expression converge. Maximizing over functions constant on a finite product partition gives its finite relative entropy by the same variational identity. This proves (P.2.5.1f.5), including singular measures and infinite divergence.

For a finite collection of pairs, the supremum of the sum is the sum of the separate suprema: choose a separate approximation within $\epsilon/|F|$ for every finite term, and approximate arbitrarily large values if a term is infinite. Taking the supremum over finite pair sets proves (P.2.5.1f.3). If $B_\ell<B_m$, the smaller value is finite. A rational $r$ can be chosen with $B_\ell\le r<B_m$. The supremum defining $B_m$ then supplies $F_+$ with $b_m(F_+)>r$, while all $b_\ell(F)\le r$. Conversely (P.2.5.1f.4) implies $B_\ell\le r<B_m$. This proves item 3 without subtracting infinities.

At a constant level every pair term is zero. At the identity level their sum is positive exactly when one pair is dependent. If all original pairs are independent, every coordinatewise coarse pair is independent and all levels have zero information. More generally data processing gives $I(c_i(X_i);c_j(X_j))\le I(X_i;X_j)$. These statements prove item 4. ∎

<a id="corollary-p251g-exact-nested-level-recovery-and-complete-history-limits"></a>**Corollary P.2.5.1g (Exact Nested-Level Recovery and Complete-History Limits).** Suppose a coarser pair is $(U,V)=(a(X),b(Y))$, with $I(X;Y)<\infty$. Then
$$
I(X;Y)-I(U;V)=\int D\bigl(P_{XY\mid u,v}\Vert P_{X\mid u}\otimes P_{Y\mid v}\bigr)\,P_{UV}(du,dv).
\tag{P.2.5.1g.1}
$$
The loss vanishes exactly when
$$
P_{XY}(dx,dy)=\int P_{X\mid u}(dx)P_{Y\mid v}(dy)P_{UV}(du,dv).
\tag{P.2.5.1g.2}
$$
Thus the two original variables can be recovered from the coarse pair by separate conditional kernels. For finitely many pairs with finite total information, equality of the total information between two nested levels holds exactly when (P.2.5.1g.2) holds for each pair.

*Proof.* Under the product comparison measure $P_X\otimes P_Y$, conditioning on $(a(X),b(Y))=(u,v)$ gives the product $P_{X\mid u}\otimes P_{Y\mid v}$. Apply the chain rule for relative entropy under the map $(X,Y)\mapsto(U,V)$. Finiteness permits the subtraction. The integral of nonnegative divergences is zero precisely when the conditional measures agree almost everywhere, which is (P.2.5.1g.2). Summing finitely many nonnegative losses proves the last claim. ∎

Infinite-information equality cannot replace this test. Let $Z$ have countably infinite Shannon entropy and let $B$ be an independent fair bit. For an explicit such $Z$, choose $P(J=j)=6/(\pi^2j^2)$, $j\ge1$, and, conditional on $J=j$, choose a uniform label among $2^j$ possibilities; set $Z$ equal to the pair. Then $H(Z)\ge\mathbb E[J]\log2=\infty$. For $X=Y=(Z,B)$, retain only $U=V=Z$. Both mutual informations are infinite, yet the conditional joint law of $(B,B)$ is not the product of two fair bits. Thus (P.2.5.1g.2) fails even though the extended numerical values are equal. Criterion (P.2.5.1f.4) correctly calls these two levels constant in the numerical sense of Definition P.2.5.1.

If the full history is generated modulo null sets by increasing finite sigma-algebras $\mathcal F_n$, then
$$
H_{\rm p}(X\mid\mathcal H_t)=\sup_m\inf_n H(\xi_m(X)\mid\mathcal F_n).
\tag{P.2.5.1g.3}
$$
For each fixed $m$, bounded martingale convergence and entropy continuity prove convergence of its conditional entropy down to the full-history value; Theorem P.2.5.1f then supplies the supremum. The order of operations matters. Let $X=\sum_{j\ge1}2^{-j}B_j$ for independent fair bits and $\mathcal F_n=\sigma(B_1,\ldots,B_n)$. The full history determines $X$, giving zero on the left. For every finite $n$, its residual conditional law is uniform on a nondegenerate dyadic interval, giving $H_{\rm p}(X\mid\mathcal F_n)=\infty$. Interchanging supremum and infimum would therefore give the false value infinity.

<a id="proposition-p251h-arbitrary-measurable-alphabet-extension"></a>**Proposition P.2.5.1h (Arbitrary-Measurable Alphabet Extension).**

Without the standard-Borel premise, the definitions (P.2.5.1e.1), (P.2.5.1e.3), (P.2.5.1f.3) using all finite measurable partitions still supply the finite-record rational-cut classifier, and entropy positivity is exactly the existence of some measurable event $A$ with $P(0<P(X\in A\mid\mathcal F)<1)>0$. To justify the partition identity without countability, fix $\nu=P+Q$ on the product sigma-algebra. The finite linear combinations of measurable rectangle indicators form an algebra containing constants and generating that sigma-algebra. Their $L^1(\nu)$ closure contains every bounded measurable function by the functional monotone-class theorem (bounded monotone limits converge in $L^1(\nu)$). A finite collection of rectangle indicators is constant on a finite product partition. Bounded clipping preserves this property and the $L^1$ approximation. The same variational argument used for (P.2.5.1f.5) therefore proves the identity as a directed supremum, without a fixed countable sequence. The Dirac-kernel and fixed countable-generator formulation additionally uses standard-Borel regularity.

<a id="proposition-p251i-reference-measure-relative-differential-branch"></a>**Proposition P.2.5.1i (Reference-Measure-Relative Differential Branch).**

If a continuous-outcome branch instead supplies a sigma-finite reference measure $\mu$, a conditional density $k_\omega=dK_\omega/d\mu$, and existence of the extended integral without an infinity-minus-infinity ambiguity, its differential predicate is
$$
h_\mu(X\mid\mathcal F)=-\mathbb E\int k_\omega\log k_\omega\,d\mu>0.
\tag{P.2.5.1i.1}
$$
Items 2–4 of the main theorem remain unchanged, while (P.2.5.1i.1), not the Dirac test, is clause (i). When its value is finite, replacing $\mu$ by $c\mu$, $c>0$, gives
$$
h_{c\mu}=h_\mu+\log c.
\tag{P.2.5.1i.2}
$$
Indeed the new density is $k/c$ and substitution proves the identity. Thus the positive, zero and negative cases are exactly $c>e^{-h_\mu}$, equality, and $c<e^{-h_\mu}$. A coordinate map that pushes the reference measure forward preserves (P.2.5.1i.1). Resetting the reference to Lebesgue measure in the new coordinate contributes the expected log Jacobian; in dimension $d$, scaling $X$ to $aX$ contributes $d\log a$.

For a one-dimensional independent uniform innovation on $[0,a]$, $h=\log a$, while (P.2.5.1e.1) is infinite for every $a>0$ and the conditional law is non-Dirac for every $a>0$. Hence the two extensions genuinely disagree about positivity. Definition P.2.5.1 selects (P.2.5.1e.1) for its structured-novelty predicate: the uncertainty test is invariant under measurable changes of outcome coordinates. Formula (P.2.5.1i.1) is the distinct reference-measure-relative comparison.

The finite-product-partition identity (P.2.5.1f.5) is also proved in (Polyanskiy and Wu 2025, Section 4.7); the proofs here include its extended-valued and complete-history cases.

<a id="construction-p251j-native-local-delayed-read-architecture-class"></a>**Construction P.2.5.1j (Native Local Delayed-Read Architecture Class).**

Use two local ports of the admitted finite Hilbert/instrument source with the positive unit, clock and primitive-service tariff of Definition C.6c.4a. Each port contains the same unchanged qualified P17 core from Theorem C.6c.P17a; the original core input, forecast, model, verification, timing and null-replacement interfaces remain fixed. The additional memory instrument acts on disjoint auxiliary factors and cannot read or overwrite that core. Tensoring the core's original source and each of its full original/null instrument words with the additional instrument preserves its qualification identity. Every core state, timer, support and source cost is in the common baseline below, rather than counted as an uncharged primitive. The association map sends receiver $i$’s delayed-read port, its output register and its service/record owner to the named qualified core $i$, for each cycle and every original/null core branch. The combined source instrument is the tensor extension of those original core instruments by the specified memory instrument; hence every original core outcome law and qualification test is preserved exactly. The augmented hardware $K(q)$ is a physical module containing that qualified core; its perspective is the core's, and the full module carrier carries no separate minimum-complexity or Definition-29 qualification. Definition P.2.5.1 consumes the assigned output processes of the two named perspectives.

The source generates a pair of independent fair symbols $(Z_t,N_t)$ within each integer cycle $t$. For each coin, allocate a fresh pure $|0\rangle$ source spin and a distinct fresh record spin, apply the admitted Hadamard pulse to the source, and apply the complete computational-basis record instrument. Its two branches have unnormalized maps $\rho\mapsto P_z\rho P_z\otimes|z\rangle\langle z|$ and sum to a trace-preserving map. On the specified source the branches have probability $1/2$. Both source and recorded outcome remain physically retained. The two preparations and instruments act on independent fresh factors and use input-independent controllers. This is exactly the pure-register/unitary/projective-record primitive class of Definition C.6c.4a, not a new supplied mixed-state primitive.

Future source factors may be allocated in their pure ready states, but remain unmeasured, independent of the complete retained past, and without an earlier access port. At the beginning of cycle $t$, the two new records are generated after the preceding cycle's complete history. Thus the complete exposed source/controller/core history does not contain the future symbols. A finite horizon $T$ uses $2T$ coin-source spins and $2T$ distinct coin-record spins, together with the additional output records and clock/controller inventory. Every one is charged, and stocks grow with $T$.

At port 1 the task is to return $X_1(t)=Z_t$ at its local delayed read. At port 2 the task is to return the complete pair $X_2(t)=(Z_t,N_t)$ at its independent local delayed read. The source labels are independent of every previous cycle and of every initial receiver resource. The input law gives all four pairs positive probability. Exact task success is required on every pair, with no abort/postselection branch.

The physical cut is between loading and reading. All source/provider/detector records and all previous output archives are isolated throughout the loading-to-read interval. The source is reopened only for the fixed return operation after both output records have been completed; it is then archived permanently. The complete label-bearing system crossing the read cut to receiver $i$ is $M_i=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes q_i}$. A read appliance may subsequently supply fresh pointer, meter and control factors in a fixed state $\sigma_{A_i}$, provided these factors have had no earlier interaction and are in product with the entire pre-read source and its references. Every initially correlated or input-dependent local work register, clock, old record, reference or appliance factor made available at read time is instead part of $M_i$ and counted in $q_i$. Mere independence of an appliance marginal is insufficient: a previously entangled appliance would violate the product requirement. There is no local side-input port after the cut. The read instruments act on $M_1$ and $M_2$ separately, and their outputs cannot condition each other. A shared resource is admitted only through its two retained local factors, each counted in the corresponding $M_i$. Input-dependent settings, arrival times or output clock changes are forbidden. Each admitted word has a public, input-independent schedule: it preserves every mandatory slot and may add separately paid extension intervals. Its completed read time can therefore be later, but cannot encode a current symbol. No common hard deadline or free use of a mandatory idle/hold interval is supplied.

These restrictions are instrument supports and isolation gates of this source. With read-time communication added, storing $Z$ at port 1 and $N$ at port 2 would give the homogeneous $(1,1)$-spin solution; local readout is therefore part of the physical task.

The allowed architectures range over all integers $q_1,q_2\ge0$, all finite source/auxiliary preparations independent of the current input, and all finite admitted local/global preparation words before the cut, followed by arbitrary local quantum instruments at the two read ports. Every extra retained accessible factor is counted. Additional primitive calls and their coefficients, controller, ready supplies, measurement outcomes, archives and clock slots are charged by the same positive tariff. The declared implementation grammar includes the fixed native source/ingress/read service below and arbitrary paid control extensions around its interfaces. It does not give an arbitrary matrix profile a free controller.

The physical module family is $K(q)$: the same unchanged qualified P17 core, $q$ identical reserved memory-spin units with their installation/ownership metadata, and the same typed programmable local connector/service machinery. Both modules have identical connector capabilities; the first task uses them for one nonconstant bit and the second task for two. Their different installed task words are external use records, not different connector hardware. Supplier distribution links and the fresh read appliances lie outside $K(q)$, have explicit common-source owners and costs, and cannot retain an additional accessible label across the read cut.

A module isomorphism preserves core fields, memory-unit factors, connector types and primitive capabilities, physical clock/unit conventions, and the complete support/resource records. The modules $K(q)$ and $K(q')$ are isomorphic exactly when $q=q'$: equality gives the factorwise map; inequality changes the counted number of the distinguished memory-unit factors and hence forbids such a map. Two-port hardware homogeneity means the modules are isomorphic; heterogeneity means they are not. Loaded local task programs may differ, as Remark P.2.5.1b permits. A response-null unused unit still has a physical support, an installation record and a holding interval. Deleting it from a response model does not delete its source cost. Task-response equivalence and this physical-module equivalence are kept separate.

<a id="theorem-p251k-all-size-local-quantum-feasibility-census"></a>**Theorem P.2.5.1k (All-Size Local Quantum Feasibility Census).** Every exact implementation on the fixed local delayed-read interface obeys $2^{q_1}\ge2$ and $2^{q_2}\ge4$. Conversely every pair satisfying these inequalities has an exact native realization. Hence the complete feasible dimension set is
$$
\{(q_1,q_2)\in\mathbb N_0^2:q_1\ge1,\ q_2\ge2\}.
\tag{P.2.5.1k.1}
$$

*Proof.* Condition on any common previous history with positive probability. The current source pair is still uniform and independent of that history. Let $\rho^{(1)}_z$ denote port 1's conditional state, averaged over $N$, and let $\rho^{(2)}_{zn}$ denote port 2's conditional state. These states include every local retained resource and can be arbitrary mixed states; they need not arise from product encoding.

The local read operation, including its fresh appliance, induces a POVM on $M_i$. Indeed, if $F_x$ is the total Heisenberg effect on $M_i\otimes A_i$, set
$$
E_x=\operatorname{Tr}_{A_i}[(I\otimes\sigma_{A_i}^{1/2})F_x(I\otimes\sigma_{A_i}^{1/2})].
$$
Positivity and $\sum_xF_x=I$ give $E_x\ge0$ and $\sum_xE_x=I$, while $\operatorname{Tr}[F_x(\rho\otimes\sigma_{A_i})]=\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho)$. The product-source premise applies even with all pre-read external references. Therefore fresh read machinery cannot enlarge the stored-label dimension. By contrast an initially entangled Bell-decoding appliance could transmit four labels through one delivered qubit and is explicitly excluded or counted at the cut.

Exact local decoding consequently gives POVMs $E^{(1)}_0,E^{(1)}_1$ and $E^{(2)}_{00},\ldots,E^{(2)}_{11}$ with
$$
\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho_y)=\delta_{xy}.
\tag{P.2.5.1k.2}
$$
If $0\le E\le I$ and $\operatorname{Tr}(E\rho)=1$, then the support of $\rho$ lies in the eigenvalue-one subspace of $E$: positivity gives $\operatorname{Tr}((I-E)\rho)=0$, hence $(I-E)^{1/2}\rho^{1/2}=0$. If the trace is zero, $E^{1/2}\rho^{1/2}=0$ and the support lies in its kernel. Equation (P.2.5.1k.2) therefore puts the support of each nonzero state in a subspace orthogonal to all other code-state supports. There are two such nonzero supports at port 1 and four at port 2. Their dimensions are each at least one, proving the lower bounds. Initial entanglement and global pre-cut operations do not affect this argument about the final local states. Neither does a variable-length internal code: the complete local Hilbert carrier at the fixed read cut must contain these orthogonal supports.

For sufficiency, initialize the memory spins in $|0\rangle$. Copy $Z$ into memory spin 1 at port 1; copy $Z,N$ into memory spins 1,2 at port 2. These are three full-support CNOT unitaries, defined on every computational basis state and therefore on every input superposition and reference. Extra memory spins retain their ready states. Measure the indicated spins in the computational basis at each local read. The full instrument includes every outcome. On the registered source all four pairs have probability $1/4$, and the two outputs are exactly $z$ and $(z,n)$. All surplus memory supports remain present. This proves (P.2.5.1k.1). ∎

At the minimal heterogeneous pair $(1,2)$, the two port-1 states and four port-2 states must be rank-one orthogonal states. Thus each minimal local code is a complete orthonormal basis. In particular the joint memory state conditional on $(z,n)$ is a product: its second marginal is pure, forcing product form, and its first is the corresponding pure state. Arbitrary unused-environment states remain with their supplier owners. This identifies the minimal exposed quantum code up to local unitaries and label permutations. Homogeneous minimizers have a larger unexposed local code fiber at port 1; no unsupported uniqueness of that fiber is claimed.

<a id="construction-p251l-literal-source-controller-and-complete-native-ledger"></a>**Construction P.2.5.1l (Literal Source, Controller and Complete Native Ledger).**

Use a common clock interval $\delta>0$, the source units $u_*,\tau_*$, and all positive rational tariff coefficients of Definition C.6c.4a. No new label-dependent acquisition or holding tariff is introduced. Every implementation preserves the same positive mandatory loading-to-read hold block, with fixed integer $L\ge1$; paid extension intervals may lengthen the actual delay. The native ledger below gives its literal duration. The local task asks for the exact output at the registered read service, without an additional hard deadline. The actual source has three ingress bit ports, one to the first receiver and two to the second. Their fixed native operations are the three CNOT copies just described. The delayed read ports copy those same three exposed bits to fresh pointer registers and apply the complete computational-basis meter. Source and pointer records, all failure/invalid inputs of optional extensions, and the final clock record are retained. The ingress, collection and meter interfaces, their actual service slots and their prices are identical across architectures; extra implementation words have positive incremental prices and cannot replace these physically specified interfaces by a free arbitrary matrix.

The canonical program contains no extra control word. It uses the fixed source distributor, two coin Hadamard pulses and two coin record services, three ingress CNOTs, the fixed hold, three egress CNOTs, three endpoint meter services, and the same three ingress CNOTs once more to return the memory to its ready state after the output has been fixed. Fixed routing from the common source to both receivers is completed before isolation and is included in the same baseline for every architecture. Every controlled inactive branch reserves its scheduled slot. The two cores each execute their unchanged qualification word once, before the first novelty cycle; their records remain retained throughout the finite horizon. The exact canonical counters below refer to these original-core executions. Every requested typed-null intervention is tensor-preserved as its own instrument word and carries the actual substituted primitive/call/action ledger, with the same reserved schedule when identity padding is specified. Preservation of each original/null response is not an assertion that different intervention words have identical pulse costs. The complete terminal source state, conditional on $(z,n)$, contains:

- unchanged original/null core records and their actual source states;
- the source records $(z,n)$ in their isolated supplier archive;
- every memory spin in $|0\rangle$ after the fixed return calls; immediately before readout the memory codewords are $z$ and $(z,n)$ with every surplus spin ready;
- the two local output records and the complete meter outcome record;
- the prescribed terminal controller/clock states.

There is no reset hidden at the endpoint. The fixed return calls uncopy the three stored bits using the still-retained source controls, after the receiver outputs are fixed. This returns every memory spin exactly to its ready state, while all source and output information remains in the charged archive. The next cycle reuses that returned memory and consumes fresh declared source/output/clock resources. A horizon $T$ uses $2T$ source spins and the full growing output/archive stock. Its canonical duration is the actual $W_T(n)$ computed below, depending on the horizon and reserved memory size; an extended word has its own additionally charged duration. Each memory support contributes its acquisition plus holding over that entire actual duration. No cyclic erasure of the growing source/output archive is claimed.

The full unitary action of each CNOT $U=U^*=U^{-1}$ can be supplied by the positive pulse
$$
H_U=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\delta}(I-U),\qquad 0\le s\le\delta,
\quad e^{-i\delta H_U/\hbar}=U.
\tag{P.2.5.1l.1}
$$
It has norm $\pi\hbar/\delta$ and integrated norm $\pi\hbar$. The independently driven switching schedule is part of the native service, as in the source conventions of Definitions C.6c.4a and Q.0.7t.5. With degenerate zero bare memory Hamiltonians, switch-on and switch-off mean work cancel exactly, because the pulse commutes with its propagator; their absolute values and the peak/action/clock reservations remain counted. For each of the first six canonical copy pulses, its input is a diagonal fair control and a ready target, giving $\langle U\rangle=1/2$, switch-on work $\pi\hbar/(4\delta)$ and absolute switching work $\pi\hbar/(2\delta)$. The same expectation $\langle U\rangle=1/2$ holds for each of the last three uncopy pulses, since the fair control and target are equal just before that pulse. Hence the nine-pulse subtotal is zero signed work and $9\pi\hbar/(2\delta)$ absolute switching work. For each coin Hadamard, $\langle0|H|0\rangle=1/\sqrt2$, so its absolute switching-work throughput is $(\pi\hbar/\delta)(1-1/\sqrt2)$ and its signed work is zero. The two-coin subtotal is twice this value. Source-distribution and record/meter services retain their separately supplied native work/resource values. No Landauer heat is inferred from a copy or from a zero signed-work total.

**Result and primitive boundary.**

This construction uses the fresh-pure-register, finite local pulse, projective record, descriptor-timed lane and finite driven-controller services of C.6c.4a. Its two calibrated cores are exactly the 75-bit cells of Theorem C.6c.P17a (parts H.2 and H.8) with the 21 additional source/scoring bits per cell stated below. The native source accepts an already expanded finite controller word, not a high-level program awaiting unpriced synthesis. A literal constructor installs the word by copying its rails. All physical source-word input, installed ROM and installation output remain in the paid finite experiment. The ideal service's initial pure-stock preparation and finite externally specified drive are the primitive boundary; they are not recursively manufactured by another copy of the experiment.

The source contract is a three-port star S--R1, S--R2 with one dedicated lane per edge, descriptor magnitude 1, fixed positive actuation time $\delta$ and lane service unit $\eta=2\delta$. Its fixed loading appliance applies three CNOTs, its fixed local read appliance applies three CNOTs and complete computational-basis record services, and its return appliance applies the same three source-controlled CNOTs after both local reads are complete. Additional paid words may be inserted at the named extension sockets but cannot overwrite the immutable appliance ROM or delete its delivered operations. This is an actually supplied finite native instrument contract. Both hardware classes use this one contract and price vector.

**Physical stocks.**

Fix $T,L\in\mathbb N$ with $T,L\ge1$, and write $n=q_1+q_2$. Qualification executes once; the memory task executes $T$ times with fresh coin/read/record banks. The $196+22T+n$ non-driver bits have these owners:

| Owner | Bits |
|---|---:|
| Two unchanged calibrated cells, including each 66-bit local ROM and three cursor bits |150|
| Four source qubits, four source records, F1,F2,X2, two terminal observation records, two four-bit score numerators per core |42|
| Task source qubits Z,N and their two retained records at S |$4T$|
| Three local read pointers and three local output records |$6T$|
| Supplier's nominated three-field carrier |3|
| Fixed descriptor-magnitude command bit $s=1$ |1|
| Six separate exact integer Q computation bits per cycle |$6T$|
| Six separate completion/meter records per cycle |$6T$|
| Receiver memory spins |$n$|

The source's complete classical command support is the shared magnitude bit, the indicated Q bit and the relevant controller state. Because the declared descriptor domain here is magnitude one, $Q=s^2=s$ on its one-bit representation; one CNOT $s\to Q$ executes the exact integer circuit on all one-bit inputs. The source accepts nonzero descriptor 1. Each later record of $Q=1$ also serves as the completion flag and the exact recorded metered lane value $q=1$. These roles share the same retained physical bit rather than being counted twice.

Every read pointer/record is an unexposed product $|0\rangle$ stock, with no earlier interaction. In particular it is in product with the entire pre-read source and every reference, which is stronger than input independence of its marginal law. The read controller states have a deterministic public trajectory, independent of input. No stored data from the source, a core or an earlier archive enters a local decoder.

**Actual finite event list.**

Each core contributes 30 data events: 24 unitaries (the 20 calibration gates of Theorem C.6c.P17a, part H.8, plus four Hadamards) and six complete record services. Its six local-cell cursor X operations are among those 20 gates. The H-plus-record coins are generated at the causal locations of Theorem C.6c.P17a, part H.2, after the corresponding forecast is frozen; no future coin is sampled into the complete past.

The task contributes the following 16 events, in order:

1. `H(Z), READ(Z->rZ), H(N), READ(N->rN)`.
2. `LINK-CNOT(Z,M11), LINK-CNOT(Z,M21), LINK-CNOT(N,M22)`.
3. After the registered hold: `CNOT(M11,p1), READ(p1->o1), CNOT(M21,p2), READ(p2->o2), CNOT(M22,p3), READ(p3->o3)`.
4. `LINK-CNOT(Z,M11), LINK-CNOT(Z,M21), LINK-CNOT(N,M22)`.

Each LINK event includes the source's full $\eta$ reservation and one projective record of its precomputed Q bit into its fresh completion/meter record. Thus each is one prescribed native two-port gate plus one counted record service. The records complete before the lane is released. The source controls remain in their owned live supplier bank until the three returns finish, and are archived afterwards; there is no archive feedback.

Run the two calibration blocks once. For each cycle, run six Q-computation CNOTs, then that cycle's task events. Insert $L\ge1$ completely inactive data-event cycles after the three loading events and before any read event. Define $E=60+T(22+L)$. This is the exact data-event count: $60$ core events plus $T$ repetitions of six descriptor computations, sixteen task events and $L$ idle events. Each fixed native event has a public time independent of the current labels $(z,n)$. Every four-input branch is retained. The task consumes fresh coins only after the complete prior-cycle history. The two post-qualification cores and their score/source records are retained and insulated; their ready-state qualification words are not replayed. Every later cycle reuses the three uncomputed memory bits and consumes fresh source/read banks, retaining all prior records.

**Local controllers, words and times.**

There are three independently installed local driven controllers, one at each port, with a common registered reference period. They are preinstalled and synchronized before the current coins are generated. No run-time controller message crosses ports: each has the entire fixed local word already installed. A two-port event is the separately paid named lane primitive.

Each controller has $E+1$ one-hot clock bits. It executes one data event (IDLE at ports not participating), then $X$ on its old clock bit, then $X$ on its next clock bit. There are $6E$ clock $X$ gates, $9E$ word-delivery events and $3E$ successive slot positions. The three local clock X operations in a slot occur in parallel. All actual data unitary operations other than those clock updates are serial.

A slot has duration $3\delta$: word delivery in its first $\delta$, pulse or record actuation in its second $\delta$, and reserved padding in its third $\delta$. A LINK gate starts after its word delivery and runs for $\delta$. Its lane remains busy for the following $\delta$; during that second service half the native projective Q-record service executes. Its record completes and the lane releases exactly at $\eta=2\delta$ from gate start, at the end of the data slot. No prefetch or simultaneous delivery/measurement is assumed. Each clock-X slot likewise has a delivery, actuation and padding interval. The run duration is $9E\delta$.

The local instruction format is a three-bit opcode with **four** padded addresses, the fourth needed to emit `LINK(control,target,Q,completion-record)` without hidden binding metadata. `X/CNOT/Toffoli/H/READ/IDLE` pad unused addresses with zero. The literal LINK word represents the already prescribed two-primitive lane/meter expansion above; it is not an arbitrary uncompiled profile. All addresses range over the $196+22T+n$ data bits and the $3(E+1)$ clock bits. Set

$$
a(n)=\max\{1,\lceil\log_2(196+22T+n+3(E+1))\rceil\},
\qquad R(n)=9E(3+4a(n)).
\tag{P.2.5.1l.2}
$$

$R$ is the exact number of logical bits in all three immutable runtime ROMs. Store each logical bit on two rails $(b,1-b)$. The supplied expanded-word input therefore uses $2R$ bits and its installed immutable copy uses another $2R$. The fixed drive service reads the first rail; the complementary rail has an explicit retained owner and is never credited as an extra task channel. It delivers exactly the stated $9E$ words. Dual rails make literal preparation independent of the input's Hamming weight.

The inventory input is the unary word $1^{q_1}0\,1^{q_2}0$, stored on two rails: $2(n+2)$ bits. Its length, not an arbitrary numeric value or the architecture label, is the support counter. Runtime pulse matrices are $X$, $H$, CNOT and Toffoli on their listed finite supports, tensored with the identity elsewhere. Their full computational-basis actions and unitarity certificates are those of Theorem C.6c.P17a, parts H.2 and H.4. This uses the local finite-matrix service of Definition C.6c.4a, not the dense whole-carrier coefficient expansion of Definition Q.0.7t.5.

**Installation and complete counters.**

Native fresh pure stocks are delivered at all three ports over one initial $\delta$ window. All zero stocks, including both copies of the word and every future source/read bit, are charged. The supplied literal finite preparation word loads exactly one rail per logical input bit, performs two CNOT copies per ROM bit, writes the two cell ROMs' 32 ones, initializes the three one-hot $c_0$ bits and writes the descriptor command bit. Its exact local-pulse count is

$$
P(n)=R+(n+2)+2R+32+3+1=3R+n+38.
\tag{P.2.5.1l.3}
$$

These are direct, supplied, timed native preparation calls under C.6c.4a's finite-driver service, not instructions read from an additional physical preparation tape. Each call owns one delivery/actuation/padding slot of duration $3\delta$, and all such calls are serial. The supplied native drive is distinct from the runtime word being installed: the latter starts zero and never programs its own preparation. No separate tape, ROM or parser is used for these direct preparation calls; their calls, clock slots, physical inputs/outputs and retained holding intervals are charged here once. The retained source input is the installation record: its two rails and the two output rails certify every copied bit. No compiler workspace or coefficient-generation register is used, since the input already is the expanded native list. Any derived or high-level descriptor is outside this literal-input source service unless its actual additional compilation is supplied and charged. The initial pure-stock/finite driven-preparation services are used directly as admitted source primitives.

For fixed $T,L$, write $W(n)=W_T(n)$ and suppress these fixed parameters in the other counters. The complete stock and elapsed time are

$$
B(n)=200+22T+3n+3(E+1)+4R(n),
\qquad W(n)=\delta[1+3P(n)+9E].
\tag{P.2.5.1l.4}
$$

All stocks are reserved from the start through the terminal time, so the exact bit-time is $I(n)=B(n)W(n)/\tau_*$. There is no early release. Both lanes are also reserved throughout that same window. Their total busy time is $12T\delta$, hence $I_0(n)=[2W(n)-12T\delta]/\tau_*$ and $E_{\rm lane}=2$. The metered link sum is $C_{\rm link}=6T$.

The complete native tariff coordinates are

$$
\begin{aligned}
G(n)&=P(n)+48+11T+6E,& J(n)&=12+11T,\\
K(n)&=3+P(n)+9E,& \Omega(n)&=3\pi\hbar/\delta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P.2.5.1l.5}
$$

$G$ counts local pulses: $48$ core pulses, $5T$ task-local pulses, $6T$ descriptor pulses, $6E$ clock pulses and $P$ preparation pulses. The $6T$ two-port gate pulses are counted in $C_{\rm link}$ and the generator record, rather than also being relabeled local pulses. $J$ counts $12$ core records, $5T$ task records and $6T$ link completion/meter records. $K$ counts the three initial pure-stock preparation clocks, each literal installation delivery/actuation slot, and the $9E$ local run slots. Initial zero-stock production is an owned source preparation, not erasure or recycling. Its bit count is $B$; initial nontrivial preparation pulses are exactly $P$.

Each Hermitian involution uses $H_U=\pi\hbar(I-U)/(2\delta)$. Its norm is $\pi\hbar/\delta$. The three parallel clock pulses are positive operators on disjoint factors; their sum has norm exactly $3\pi\hbar/\delta$. No other simultaneous Hamiltonian pulse raises that value. The action is exactly $\pi\hbar[P+48+17T+6E]$, counting the $6T$ link-gate pulses as well. The native record service has its declared finite instrument duration and tariff; it is not replaced by a hidden Hamiltonian implementation. No reset heat is inferred from these counters.

With the fixed source unit and positive tariff coefficients of C.6c.4a, the attained canonical value is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{V_T(n)}{u_*}
={}&2\alpha_E+\alpha_0\frac{2W(n)-12T\delta}{\tau_*}
 +\alpha_B B(n)+\alpha_I\frac{B(n)W(n)}{\tau_*}\\
&+\alpha_G[P(n)+48+11T+6E]+(12+11T)\alpha_J+6T\alpha_C\\
&+\alpha_K[3+P(n)+9E]+3\pi\alpha_\Omega\frac{\tau_*}{\delta}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P.2.5.1l.6}
$$

Every displayed $q$-dependent term is explicit. $R,P,B,W$ are nondecreasing in $n$, with $B(n+1)-B(n)\ge3$ and $P(n+1)-P(n)\ge1$. Therefore $V_T(n+1)>V_T(n)$ for every positive native price vector. Paid extensions preserve the native appliance prefix and add fresh stock/pulses/records/reserved intervals; their peak is at least the canonical peak because its three-clock slots are preserved. They therefore have $V\ge V_T(n)$. The empty extension attains $V_T(n)$.

The all-size feasibility theorem supplies $n\ge3$, attained at $(q_1,q_2)=(1,2)$. Homogeneity in the fixed $K(q)$ module family supplies $q_1=q_2\ge2$, hence $n\ge4$, attained at $(2,2)$. Thus the exact minima are $V_{\rm het}=V_T(3)$ and $V_{\rm hom}=V_T(4)$, with the exact gap given by the displayed formula and bounded below by $3u_*\alpha_B>0$. An affine-gap formula is unnecessary and is generally false when an address-width threshold is crossed.

**Hardware modules and exhaustive native extension rule.**

The separately owned source controllers, address machinery, coins, meters and fabrication/archive inputs are external appliances. The receiver module $K(q)$ consists of one unchanged 75-bit calibrated cell, $q$ ordered identical memory-spin/socket factors, and the same typed programmable connector capability at each socket. A named native two-port gate can address a nominated socket; a local read service can address a nominated socket with its fresh product pointer. The capabilities and their unit/duration maps do not depend on the task program. The core is insulated from memory/socket traffic. $K(q)$ has a literal core/ordered-factor/socket bijection with another $K(q)$; different $q$ have different physical memory-factor counts. External global address width $a$ is consequently not an unlisted part of $K(q)$. Both receiver appliances in any experiment use the same prescribed minimal address width $a$; surplus address bits or alternative descriptors are additional paid stock, not a lower-price alternative encoding.

The native supplied macro interface exposes extension sockets **between** immutable service blocks. An extension concatenates new paid time intervals and independently owned finite control words at those sockets. It has no access to an existing block's reserved intervals, fixed idle padding, immutable ROM or built-in clock pulses. In particular it cannot substitute its link traffic for pre-existing paid lane-idle time. These are the access and scheduling rules of the supplied instrument, fixed before choosing $q$ or testing an input, just as C.6c.4a's retained interface restricts its compiled macros.

Every old lane remains allocated through every inserted interval. If $k$ of the old lanes are used in a new interval of duration $d$ and the source has two old lanes, that interval contributes $(2-k)d\ge0$ to the old-lane idle integral. New lanes have their own nonnegative allocation/standby records. Old bit-time, ROM stock, mandatory calls and the three-clock peak remain. New stock, calls, records and clock slots have nonnegative counts. Thus the exact inherited tariff, coordinate by coordinate, dominates the displayed canonical value for the same $q$. Signed or absolute switching work is a separate retained physical record and is not added as an unproved monotone objective coordinate.

The task requires the stated mandatory isolation/hold interval and returns at the public completion slot of the submitted source word. Concatenated extensions may lengthen that delay; every additional interval is charged. A word's schedule is fixed independently of the current label, so this convention introduces no input-dependent arrival-time side channel. There is no common finite deadline imposed on words of unbounded finite length.

The literal address, word and preparation rules above give the following populated instance: $T=L=1$, $E=83$, $a=9$ and $R=29133$.

The exact positive gap in this populated instance is

$$
