All sampler, setting, forecast, comparison and consumed records have finite storage and verification. The common processor uses the same finite time envelope, calibrated clock and complete reserve for both schedules, by padding the inactive slots. The physical program grammar is the displayed immutable lookup service. It has one addressed bank per program and no arbitrary composition or randomized program input in its admissible program alphabet. The fixed prefix code assigns the two one-symbol words $0,1$ and admits no empty word. In particular the possible XOR processor from Theorem P.6.1b.8h is not a candidate in this particular compiler. Its ordinary forecast operations remain available in the proof of that theorem.

Add two labelled consumable banks $L,R$ with the same finite hardware, timing and ready stock in both programs. During the common program pulse, program $0$ activates one additional used-stock cell at $L$, and program $1$ activates one additional used-stock cell at $R$. A cell can be a fresh packet-and-fuel factor with a fixed controlled swap into a retained spent register. In both cases the pulse is a reversible controlled move between two distinct retained records, and its time and physical energy budget are the same. Retain the two labelled counts and the spent flags. With $h$ common uses of each bank the measured vector is $(h+1,h)$ in program $0$ and $(h,h+1)$ in program $1$. The labelled bank locations and their equal charge units are fixed by the comparison protocol. Each finite record is checked by the copied word and flag tests and enters the retained verification update, giving the finite dressings of Theorem P.6.2c. No raw charged operation is removed when changing the tariff below.

*Response and empirical-input maps.* The labelled protocol menu contains the two-trial response and its restrictions to the trial, forecast, error and resource records, with the same coordinate restriction on both candidates. The two-trial record is generated by the transition in Theorem P.6.1b.8h. For example with $Y_i=F_i\oplus E_i$ the law satisfies
$$
4\Pr(Y_1=0,F_2=1,Y_2=0)=(1-p)x_{00}.
$$
The probability on the left before multiplying by four is zero in program $0$ and $(1-p)/32$ in program $1$. Thus the two candidates have total variation distance at least $(1-p)/32$ even without the resource-count readout. The marked output and input conventions prohibit an interchange of the two verification records by a relabelling. The inverse on this response domain recovers $p$ and the chosen forecast table by (P.6.1b.8h.1). In particular distinct programs have distinct physical response classes and the map is onto the two realized laws with their stated restrictions. The finite response closure therefore has exactly two points, and by the fixed code each has minimal description length one.

The empirical-input map of this finite service sends an observed empirical two-trial law to the nearest of the two exact two-trial laws in total variation, with a tie reported when both have equal distance. If the source has one of the two laws and the empirical error is strictly smaller than $(1-p)/64$, this rule returns its physical program by the triangle inequality. The observed frequency of the displayed event alone also suffices when its absolute error is strictly less than that amount. Each empirical test refers to the fixed sampler, labelled output records and verified common clock. The same inference uses the full law if $p$ is an additional registered parameter, with the parameter stability bound of Theorem P.6.1b.8h.

*Tariffs and complete selector census.* For each fixed tariff, the two added resource coordinates are priced in the same positive cost unit. Use the same mismatch loss in both programs, counted on the actual later outcomes. Their common one-trial mismatch probability is $1/8+3p/8$ on both trials by Theorem P.6.1b.8h, so this loss agrees in the two cases. Both have zero constraint penalty on the registered finite domain and the same code cost. Every common apparatus, operation and raw use outside the two labelled increments is either fixed across candidates or already charged by the common measured vector. Thus for positive prices $w_L,w_R$ the cost difference on the two-point quotient is exactly
$$
V(q_0)-V(q_1)=w_L-w_R .
\tag{P.6.1b.8i.1}
$$
With $w_L=w_R=1$ both distinct response classes minimize, so there is no strict scalar or lexicographic separation on this fixed tariff. With $(w_L,w_R)=(1,2)$ the unique minimizer is $q_0$, and with $(w_L,w_R)=(2,1)$ it is $q_1$, each with gap one. The physical candidates, all retained non-cost responses and measured unweighted resource vectors are common to the two comparisons. The tariff maps are separately supplied positive prices on those same observables. If the price register itself is retained as an observable, its changed value is also a response of the enlarged comparison record.

This realizes the two-model cost pattern of Theorem P.14.1k.3 on an explicit finite predictive and verification service and the fixed-tariff tie on that same domain. The empirical rule and response maps have the stated finite protocol domain. A proof that both choices extend to models of every PU core axiom, or that this finite grammar exhausts the global physical candidates of Corollary P.14.1k.3.1, requires an additional admissibility theorem. $\square$

<a id="theorem-p61b8j"></a>

<a id="theorem-p61b8j-finite-physical-identification-of-repeated-quantum-instruments"></a>**Theorem P.6.1b.8j (Finite Physical Identification of Repeated Quantum Instruments).** Fix finite input and output Hilbert spaces $I,O$ with marked bases, a common positive clock step, and an exact supplied-port implementation contract as specified below. Fix a decidable binary prefix grammar of finite words. Each admitted code supplies an algebraic density matrix $\rho$ on a finite memory $M$ of dimension $d$ and an algebraic completely positive trace-preserving map $\mathcal T:\mathcal B(M\otimes I)\to\mathcal B(M\otimes O)$, used unchanged each step. The external protocols include arbitrary finite coherent adaptive interventions on the marked ports and external references, and every original output is retained in the experiment record. Each candidate also supplies a finite algebraic nonnegative cost of the declared source comparison. Then the following finite identification, exact selection, and empirical-input tests hold on this entire coded physical domain.

1. Use fixed physical density matrices $\{\sigma_i\}$ spanning the Hermitian operators on $I$ and effects $\{E_j\}$, $0\le E_j\le I_O$, spanning those on $O$. For two codes with memory dimensions $d_1,d_2$, equality of the probabilities of a sequence of positive binary outcomes using these bases through length $d_1^2+d_2^2-1$ is equivalent to equality of all finite adaptive port responses. This includes coherent interventions with an arbitrary finite reference. The bound yields a finite distinguishing experiment whenever the port responses differ.
2. Use the comparison objective $V(s)=\alpha|s|+A(s)$, with $\alpha>0$ algebraic and $A(s)\ge0$ the declared measured cost on code $s$. Compare response classes by the minimum over their representatives. Given any incumbent code with finite cost $U$, a terminating census gives the exact minimizing response classes and their attaining physical programs, and certifies a strict response gap when the minimizer is unique. It supplies a finite separating set of physical tests for every candidate that can attain cost at most $U$. This holds with no memory bound imposed in advance on the full language.
3. On that finite cost census, a certified error below half the minimum distinct response-vector separation identifies the occupied class, or rejects it under the error rule below. No finite testing depth works uniformly without a memory bound, even for equal-cost finite physical programs. No positive uniform response-separation margin follows even when the memory dimension is at most two.

*Physical grammar and equivalence.* Each program word is read into a fixed marked decoder and gives a finite classical pulse description and an exact algebraic channel recipe. One concrete exhaustive grammar encodes all finite ordered lists of rational polynomials with rational isolating intervals for real roots, using integer binary words with a length header. Decode complex entries as pairs of real algebraic numbers. Hermiticity, unit trace and positive semidefiniteness of the memory state, and the positive semidefiniteness and trace-preserving partial trace of the channel's Choi matrix are checked by exact algebraic arithmetic. The zero-dimensional memory encoding is rejected. Fixed supplied positive energy, time, and finite-stock tariffs complete this syntax. A code may have a longer pulse or larger stock than another. Both are accounted in its own cost. The cost comparison uses a declared finite accounting episode. Testing deeper response words uses a separate finite diagnostic episode with its own fresh supplies and clock debit.

To realize a decoded code, factor the positive Choi matrix to obtain a finite Kraus family and the corresponding isometry into the memory, output and a finite environment. Algebraic Cholesky elimination on its support gives such a factor using addition, multiplication, positive square roots and divisions by certified nonzero pivots. Extend the isometry, after padding the input and output workspaces to a common dimension, to a unitary by completing orthonormal bases. The same procedure prepares $\rho$ by a finite purification from ready stock. In the exact finite matrix-control branch, a prescribed finite unitary $U$ is implemented in its own positive clock interval by the bounded Hermitian spectral logarithm with norm at most $\pi$. A step interval of length $\tau>0$ uses norm at most $\pi\hbar/\tau$ for this pulse. Preparation, local measurement and archive release have their own positive intervals and finite bounds. Schedule fresh initialized workspace and environment for every step of the finite experiment. Preserve the consumed factors, copied outcomes, inactive slots and clock records. They are included in the source inventory, with a charged preparation, support, control and retention map. A returned output system or a readout record is an explicit port of that map. The unqueried internal memory, generator implementation and spent stock remain owned without becoming uncontrolled ports. This is the exact bounded matrix-control convention also used for source expressions in Definition K.6.6n. Approximate digital synthesis requires its own error budget.

Every code gives a finite recordable and verifiable protocol response, with its finite maintenance and update operations on each test horizon, as required by Theorem P.6.2c. The supplied contract allows finite repetition on fresh ready stock without a zero-cost infinite resource. Take the operational quotient by all marked port responses, including any verifier output that is actually exported. Pricing may use separately measured resource records as in Definition P.6.2a. If a particular comparison makes those records part of the response quotient, include them in the marked output alphabet and common instrumentation. The quotient here distinguishes any external experiment that distinguishes the resulting quantum instrument. Equality of the numerical cost alone gives no response identification. The physical domain consists of all admitted codes and their specified realizations in this grammar. Exact algebraic matrix entries are part of the admissibility condition for the terminating arithmetic statement.

*Finite port tests.* For a single marked preparation $\sigma_i$ and binary effect $E_j$, the memory map for a positive outcome is
$$
A_{ij}(X)=\operatorname{Tr}_O\!\left[(I_M\otimes E_j)\mathcal T(X\otimes\sigma_i)\right].
\tag{P.6.1b.8j.1}
$$
This is the unnormalized conditional state obtained by measuring the output and discarding it from the memory dynamics. It is completely positive because the partial trace permits insertion of the square root of $E_j$ on both sides. The effect $I_O-E_j$ gives the other outcome. Rank-one projectors onto the marked basis vectors and their normalized two-vector sums with phases $1$ or $i$ give the required real spanning sets of preparations and effects. They are exact finite algebraic recipes. Every finite list of positive-outcome tests gives the physically observed probability $\operatorname{Tr}(A_{i_kj_k}\cdots A_{i_1j_1}\rho)$, with no conditioning on a successful preparation. The clock and finite experiment horizon are fixed before the run.

For two codes work in the real vector space of pairs of Hermitian memory matrices, of dimension $D=d_1^2+d_2^2$. Put $x_0=(\rho_1,\rho_2)$, use the block diagonal maps $A_{ij}^{(1)}\oplus A_{ij}^{(2)}$, and take the final functional $\ell(X,Y)=\operatorname{Tr}X-\operatorname{Tr}Y$. The spans of all images of $x_0$ under words of length at most $k$ are nested. Once two successive spans agree, the earlier one is invariant under every letter, so no later span can grow. They start at dimension one and stabilize by length $D-1$. Thus vanishing of $\ell$ on the test words through length $D-1$ gives vanishing at every length. With algebraic entries Gaussian elimination constructs a reachable basis, retaining one actual test word for each independent basis vector. An exact nonzero evaluation of $\ell$ on such a word gives a distinguishing event. This is the finite linear-span test used for quantum finite-state machines (Wang et al. 2021).

At a given length the complete process output probabilities on product preparations and effects determine the whole marked process tensor. In detail, expanding each matrix unit on a port in the complex span of the corresponding Hermitian basis determines every entry of the iterated channel with memory initialized and finally traced. An external intervention with ancillary memory is a linear map on the joint port and ancillary matrix units. Its contribution to any final event is obtained by contracting the same iterated channel entries with those map entries, summing the internal ancillary indices. Intermediate classical decisions can be held in that ancillary register, so adaptivity is included in the contraction. Equality on the product tests therefore implies equality of every finite adaptive response, with or without a coherent reference. Conversely every product test is itself an admitted physical protocol. At each finite horizon all its coarse-grained readouts follow by the same linear contractions. This produces a well-defined faithful identification of the marked port-response quotient by the family of these finite laws, with each represented class supplied by an actual decoded source.

*Exact cost census and measured identification.* Enumerate all binary strings of length at most $L=\lfloor U/\alpha\rfloor$. Retain valid codes, apply the finite equivalence test, and take the minimum cost within each class. Every program of higher length costs at least $\alpha(L+1)>U$. Hence any class of cost at most $U$ appears with its true minimum, and the minimizing classes and programs are exactly those found by this enumeration. The minimum over representatives exists whenever a class has a valid finite-cost code, by the same finite-sublevel argument. Equality of algebraic cost words is decidable. If a single response class minimizes at cost $m$, the least positive difference to other classes among their retained representatives, together with $\alpha(L+1)-m$, supplies a strict response gap by taking their minimum. This is the exact coded selection of Theorem P.6.1b.8d, now evaluated on the supplied physical candidates and their actual response equivalence. The program may tie within its own response class.

For the finite census use all basis words through the maximum pairwise required depth and form a vector of their positive-outcome probabilities for every retained class. Let $\delta$ be the least positive sup-norm distance of distinct vectors. The exact census computes $\delta>0$ when there are at least two classes. With one class only its compatibility check is needed. An observed vector $\widehat v$ with certified sup-norm error at most $\epsilon<\delta/2$ has at most one class vector within $\epsilon$; report that class if present and rejection of the tested finite class if absent. Under the tested domain and the error certificate the true class is returned. The certificate can use actual independent finite copies of each experiment. If there are $J$ measured coordinates, $m_*$ independent repetitions per coordinate, and a deterministic implementation error at most $e<\epsilon$, Chebyshev's inequality and the union bound give failure probability at most $J/[4m_*(\epsilon-e)^2]$. All readouts use the declared input and effect coordinates and common clock. The empirical input selects no model component outside this fixed response comparison.

*No uniform depth or margin without the corresponding inputs.* For any $n\ge1$, use a finite deterministic memory counter with states $0,\ldots,n$, initialized to zero, with a saturated increment at each use. Two programs return zero until the increment first reaches $n$, and then return, respectively, zero or one. Both have exact algebraic channels on the same finite stock and can use one-bit prefix words and identical positive padded durations and tariffs. Their equal accounting records can be realized by executing a fixed output-copy circuit for both values on equal-energy registers. The two candidates have identical responses through depth $n-1$, including on every external intervention because their port channel ignores its input, and a different deterministic response at depth $n$. The marked horizon can be tested by repeating the same admitted port. For the margin claim take memory of dimension two and independent identical outputs of probability $p$ or $p+\eta$ on the same dyadic sampler class with $p$ interior. These response-distinct programs have a coordinate discrepancy at most $k|\eta|$ at depth $k$ by coupling the $k$ Bernoulli trials. Dyadic $\eta\ne0$ can tend to zero. Thus bounded memory supplies a depth bound but gives no strictly positive universal testing margin. The actual cost census and its exact class separation supply that margin. The theorem determines the declared physical and empirical maps on the exhaustive decoded port grammar. Identifying that grammar with the global PU candidate universe requires the global admission and exhaustiveness result. $\square$

<a id="definition-p61c1-finite-self-verifying-operational-presentation"></a>**Definition P.6.1c.1 (Finite Self-Verifying Operational Presentation).** A finite self-verifying operational presentation is a tuple
$$
\mathfrak T
=
(\mathsf S,\mathsf P,\Omega,E,U,V)
\tag{P.6.1c.1}
$$
where:

1. $\mathsf S$ is a finite state set or finite state category.

2. $\mathsf P$ is a finite protocol category with refinements, coarse-grainings, and pre/post-processing morphisms.

3. Each $P\in\mathsf P$ has a finite outcome set $\Omega_P$.

4. $E$ assigns finite expected outcome laws,
$$
E(s,P)\in\Delta(\Omega_P),
$$
naturally with respect to protocol coarse-graining.

5. $U$ assigns finite update kernels
$$
U_{P,o}:s\mapsto U(s,P,o)
$$
whenever outcome $o\in\Omega_P$ is obtained.

6. $V$ assigns a finite verification statistic comparing the expected law $E(s,P)$ with the realized outcome or realized coarse-grained outcome.

7. Let $\mathsf S_0$ be the finite state set, or the object set when $\mathsf S$ is a finite category, and let $q:\mathsf S_0\to\overline{\mathsf S}_0$ be the registered response-null quotient. For states with $q(s)=q(s')$, the retained expected laws and verification statistics agree, and every registered post-outcome update satisfies
   $$
   q_\#U_{P,o}(s)=q_\#U_{P,o}(s')
   $$
   whenever that outcome belongs to the retained update domain. All protocol and state-category maps respect this quotient. These are congruence and stochastic-lumpability conditions, not consequences of finiteness alone.

Two presentations $\mathfrak T$ and $\mathfrak T'$ are primitive-equivalent when an accepted identification of their quotient state sets makes their state-indexed protocol-response presheaves naturally isomorphic and intertwines their pushed-forward update and verification maps.

<a id="proposition-p61c1a-finite-presentations-without-update-congruence"></a>**Proposition P.6.1c.1a (Finite Presentations without Update Congruence).** Clause 7 of Definition P.6.1c.1 is independent of items 1–6. Let $\mathsf S_0=\{a,b,c\}$, let $\mathsf P$ consist of one protocol $P$ with its identity morphism and outcome set $\Omega_P=\{0,1\}$, and let $r(a)=r(b)=0$ and $r(c)=1$. Put $E(s,P)=\delta_{r(s)}$ and $V(s,P,o)=\mathbf 1[o\ne r(s)]$, and let the update after either outcome send $a\mapsto c$, $b\mapsto b$ and $c\mapsto c$. These data satisfy items 1–6. The quotient $q$ that identifies states with equal retained expected laws and verification statistics merges $a$ and $b$ and separates $c$, and
$$
q_\#U_{P,0}(a)=\delta_{q(c)}\ne\delta_{q(a)}=q_\#U_{P,0}(b),
\tag{P.6.1c.1a.1}
$$
so clause 7 fails. When the two-step protocol $P^{(2)}$, which reads, updates and reads again, is retained, its expected laws $\delta_{(0,1)}$ at $a$ and $\delta_{(0,0)}$ at $b$ separate the two states, the quotient becomes the identity and clause 7 holds. Update congruence is therefore a property of the retained protocol family, and admission to Definition P.6.1c.1 verifies it.

*Proof.* The state set, the protocol category and the outcome set are finite, $E$ assigns probability laws, the update assigns a map of $\mathsf S_0$ to each outcome, and $V$ compares the expected law with the realized outcome; the only protocol arrow is the identity, so naturality holds. This gives items 1–6. The states $a$ and $b$ have the expected law $\delta_0$ and the same verification statistic, while $c$ has $\delta_1$, so $q(a)=q(b)\ne q(c)$. The update sends $a$ to $c$ and $b$ to $b$, which gives (P.6.1c.1a.1). Under $P^{(2)}$ the outcome pair is $(r(s),r(U(s)))$, equal to $(0,1)$ at $a$, $(0,0)$ at $b$ and $(1,1)$ at $c$; the three expected laws are distinct, $q$ is injective, and clause 7 holds because its premise $q(s)=q(s')$ forces $s=s'$. ∎

<a id="definition-p61c2-predictive-normal-form"></a>**Definition P.6.1c.2 (Predictive Normal Form).** The predictive normal form of $\mathfrak T$ is the finite predictive-instantiation object
$$
\mathcal N_{\mathrm{pred}}(\mathfrak T)
=
(\mathsf P,\mathcal R_{\mathfrak T},U_{\mathfrak T},V_{\mathfrak T})
\tag{P.6.1c.2}
$$
where
$$
\mathcal R_{\mathfrak T}(P)(s)
=
E(s,P)
\tag{P.6.1c.3}
$$
and $\mathcal R_{\mathfrak T}$ denotes the family indexed by $s\in\mathsf S_0$ of protocol-response presheaves $P\mapsto E(s,P)$. The update and verification maps are the pushforwards of $U$ and $V$ to the registered response-null quotient, well-defined by clause 7 of Definition P.6.1c.1.

<a id="theorem-p61c3-primitive-equivalence-normal-form"></a>**Theorem P.6.1c.3 (Primitive-Equivalence Normal Form).** Every finite self-verifying operational presentation satisfying Definition P.6.1c.1, including its quotient-compatibility conditions, has a canonical predictive normal form up to the registered state identification and natural isomorphism. For presentations with accepted finite-cost PPI realizations on a separating protocol-complete branch, primitive-equivalence identifies them in the physical PPI quotient. Relation-first, process-first, computation-first, information-first, and prediction-first presentations therefore define the same registered operational primitive when their quotient state identification, state-indexed response presheaves, updates, and verification maps agree.

*Proof.* For each $s\in\mathsf S_0$, equation (P.6.1c.3) and the registered protocol naturality maps define a response presheaf. Taken together, they form the indexed functor
$$
\mathcal R_{\mathfrak T}:\mathsf P^{op}\longrightarrow(\mathsf{Prob}_{\mathrm{fin}})^{\mathsf S_0}.
$$
Clause 7 of Definition P.6.1c.1 makes the expected laws and verification statistics independent of a representative of each quotient state. Its equality of pushed-forward update kernels makes the quotient update law independent of that representative as well. These data construct $\mathcal N_{\mathrm{pred}}(\mathfrak T)$ up to the registered state identification and natural isomorphism. Finiteness alone would not prove this descent.

Primitive-equivalent presentations have matching state-indexed responses and intertwined quotient updates and verification maps, so they represent the same formal operational normal form by definition. When the accepted finite-cost PPI realizations and separating protocol-complete branch are also supplied, Theorem P.6.1b.3 applies to the retained response data; the independent update and verification intertwiners preserve the enriched normal form. Corollary P.6.1b.8 removes response-null presentation labels under its cost conditions. A difference in any retained response, update, or verification datum remains operationally distinct. ∎

<a id="corollary-p61c4-prediction-as-canonical-operational-form"></a>**Corollary P.6.1c.4 (Prediction as Canonical Operational Form).** Every finite presentation admitted by Definition P.6.1c.1, including its state-indexed responses and quotient-compatible update and verification maps, has the predictive normal form of Theorem P.6.1c.3. This is a formal representation statement; physical PPI identity additionally requires the realization and protocol hypotheses of that theorem.

*Proof.* Apply Theorem P.6.1c.3 to the presentation. The resulting object records exactly expected finite responses, update kernels, and verification statistics. That is the predictive normal form. ∎

### P.6.1d Finite Categorical-Unity Certificate Schedules

This subsection supplies the table-level schedules used by Definition 2.6a, Theorem 2.6b, Definition 2.6c, and Theorem 2.6d. Section 2.6 owns the response restrictions, classifier, completion predicates, and conclusions; the schedules below define their finite serializations and verification obligations.

<a id="definition-p61d1-registered-datum-table-and-audit-schedule"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.1 (Registered-Datum Table and Audit Schedule).** A datum of Definition 2.6a passes the registered-datum schedule exactly when the following finite tables and audits are present and accepted. Fix a finite protocol budget $B$, a declared exact decidable coefficient domain $\mathbb D_B$, and the six-element index set
$$
I_6
=
\{\mathsf t,\mathsf s,\mathsf e,\mathsf m,\mathsf f,\mathsf q\}
\tag{P.6.1d.1.1}
$$
for time, space, energy, matter, force, and charge. A registered finite categorical-unity datum $\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{CU},B}$ consists of the following exact finite data.

1. A finite source category $\mathsf S_B$ presents the admitted transformations of the predictive normal form, and a distinguished object $p_B\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathsf S_B)$ represents the frozen presentation $\mathfrak T$. Let $\mathsf P_B$ be the finite protocol category at budget $B$. A registered finite response-normal-form category $\mathsf{RNF}_B$ has objects
   $$
   X=(\mathcal R_X,U_X,V_X),
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.2}
   $$
   where $\mathcal R_X:\mathsf P_B^{op}\to\mathsf{Prob}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb D_B)$ is a normalized exact response presheaf, $U_X$ is its finite family of post-outcome update maps, and $V_X$ is its finite family of verification maps. A morphism in $\mathsf{RNF}_B$ is a natural transformation of response presheaves together with the registered state map that intertwines every update map and every verification map. All identity, composition, normalization, update-intertwining, and verification-intertwining equations are supplied as exact finite tables.

   The response-normal-form functor
   $$
   \mathcal Y_B:\mathsf S_B\longrightarrow\mathsf{RNF}_B
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.3}
   $$
   records these data, and the datum contains a checked isomorphism
   $$
   \zeta_B:
   \mathcal Y_B(p_B)
   \xRightarrow{\sim}
   \mathfrak P_0\!\restriction_B
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.4}
   $$
   to the budget-$B$ restriction of the canonical predictive normal form of Definition P.6.1c.2. Here $\mathfrak P_0\!\restriction_B$ denotes the object $(\mathcal R_{\mathfrak T}|_{\mathsf P_B},U_{\mathfrak T}|_{\mathsf P_B},V_{\mathfrak T}|_{\mathsf P_B})$ of $\mathsf{RNF}_B$; the protocol category $\mathsf P_B$ is its ambient indexing category rather than a fourth object field. Thus the response laws, pushed-forward updates, and verification maps are anchored jointly rather than identified from response probabilities alone.

2. For each $i\in I_6$, a registered inclusion
   $$
   j_i:\mathsf P_{i,B}\hookrightarrow\mathsf P_B
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.5}
   $$
   fixes the sector protocols. Restriction along $j_i$ acts on all three response-normal-form fields and gives a functor
   $$
   \widetilde R_i
   :=
   j_i^*\mathcal Y_B:
   \mathsf S_B\longrightarrow\mathsf{RNF}_{i,B},
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.6}
   $$
   where $\mathsf{RNF}_{i,B}$ is a registered finite response-normal-form category with exact object and morphism tables. Define $\mathsf R_{i,B}$ to be the full subcategory of $\mathsf{RNF}_{i,B}$ whose object set is
   $$
   \{\widetilde R_i(s):s\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathsf S_B)\}.
   $$
   The unique corestriction of $\widetilde R_i$ to this finite full image is denoted
   $$
   R_i:\mathsf S_B\longrightarrow\mathsf R_{i,B}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.7}
   $$
   Write
   $$
   \kappa_i:\mathsf R_{i,B}\hookrightarrow\mathsf{RNF}_{i,B}
   $$
   for the full-subcategory inclusion. Consequently, $R_i$ is fixed relative to the registered pair $(\mathcal Y_B,j_i)$; the inclusion $j_i$ is a frozen input of this finite classification.

   The semantic-label audit
   $$
   \mathfrak A_{\mathrm{sem},B}
   =
   \bigl(
   \{\lambda_i\}_{i\in I_6},
   \{\mathsf E_{i,B}\}_{i\in I_6},
   \pi_{\mathrm{sem}}
   \bigr)
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.8}
   $$
   assigns the six physical names bijectively, gives a decidable typed eligibility predicate $\mathsf E_{i,B}$ for each sector, and proves that the image of $j_i$ contains exactly the protocol objects and morphisms eligible under $\mathsf E_{i,B}$. For every sector and every protocol owner, $\pi_{\mathrm{sem}}$ records inclusion or a checked typed exclusion reason, verifies the operational type against the corresponding row of Section 2.6.1, and verifies that every label, predicate, and inclusion follows from the declared protocol semantics and typed eligibility rules without using a validation target as an input or selection criterion. Overlap of two sector protocol families is permitted only when it is recorded in the overlap inventory below. The audit licenses the registered sector interpretation; the accepted essential-preimage and PPI fields supply PPI physicalizability.

3. For each $i\in I_6$, a finite operational realization category $\mathsf O_{i,B}$, an enriched response-normal-form functor
   $$
   \rho_i:
   \mathsf O_{i,B}
   \longrightarrow
   \mathsf R_{i,B},
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.9}
   $$
   and a decidable natural-isomorphism-invariant predicate $\mathfrak B_i$ encode the category-specific PPI, domain, normalization, unit, source, and finite-cost gates listed in Section 2.6.1. The local-lift groupoid is
   $$
   \operatorname{Lift}_i(R_i)
   :=
   \left\{
   (F_i,\alpha_i):
   \begin{array}{l}
   F_i:\mathsf S_B\to\mathsf O_{i,B},\\
   \alpha_i:\rho_iF_i\Rightarrow R_i
   \text{ is a natural isomorphism},\\
   \mathfrak B_i(F_i)=1
   \end{array}
   \right\},
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.10}
   $$
   whose arrows $u:(F_i,\alpha_i)\to(F_i',\alpha_i')$ are natural isomorphisms $u:F_i\Rightarrow F_i'$ satisfying
   $$
   \alpha_i'\circ(\rho_i u)=\alpha_i.
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.11}
   $$

4. A finite overlap graph $G_B=(I_6,E_B)$ carries, for every edge $e=\{i,j\}$, a finite overlap category $\mathsf O_{e,B}$ and restriction functors
   $$
   r_{e,i}:\mathsf O_{i,B}\to\mathsf O_{e,B},
   \qquad
   r_{e,j}:\mathsf O_{j,B}\to\mathsf O_{e,B}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.12}
   $$
   Define the finite overlap-decorated groupoid $\mathscr A_B$ as follows. Its objects are tuples
   $$
   a
   =
   \bigl(
   (F_i,\alpha_i)_{i\in I_6},
   (\theta_e)_{e\in E_B}
   \bigr),
   \qquad
   \theta_e:
   r_{e,i}F_i
   \xRightarrow{\sim}
   r_{e,j}F_j,
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.13}
   $$
   and an arrow $a\to a'$ is a componentwise family of local-lift isomorphisms $(u_i)_{i\in I_6}$ satisfying, for every $e=\{i,j\}$,
   $$
   \theta_e'\circ(r_{e,i}u_i)
   =
   (r_{e,j}u_j)\circ\theta_e.
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.14}
   $$

   The overlap-eligibility inventory
   $$
   \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{ov},B}
   =
   \bigl(
   \Lambda_B,
   \{\mathsf E_\lambda^{\mathrm{ov}}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda_B},
   \pi_{\mathrm{ov}}
   \bigr)
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.15}
   $$
   contains a finite decidable predicate for every required edge, cycle, triple-overlap, unit, source-ownership, calibration, and higher coherence cell. The checked coverage proof $\pi_{\mathrm{ov}}$ classifies every overlap obligation generated by the six branch manifests exactly once as included or excluded with a typed reason, and every included predicate is invariant under arrows of $\mathscr A_B$.

   The compatible categorical-lift groupoid is the finite full subgroupoid
   $$
   \mathscr J_B
   :=
   \mathscr A_B
   \big|_{
   \left\{
   a:
   \mathsf E_\lambda^{\mathrm{ov}}(a)=1
   \text{ for every }\lambda\in\Lambda_B
   \right\}
   }.
   \tag{P.6.1d.1.16}
   $$
   Its components are compatible-lift natural-isomorphism classes. They are not identified with global physical response classes without the separate common-carrier response-equivalence data of Definition 2.6c.

Every category, functor, predicate, semantic assignment, coefficient, and equality test in $\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{CU},B}$ is supplied by a canonical finite serialization over $\mathbb D_B$. A submitted datum is **table-valid** exactly when its total decidable table checker verifies all types, identities, compositions, normalizations, intertwiners, eligibility predicates, and coverage proofs in this definition. Definition 2.6c assigns its accepted, failed, or pending status.

<a id="lemma-p61d2-enriched-full-faithfulness-fiber-criterion"></a>**Lemma P.6.1d.2 (Enriched Full-Faithfulness Fiber Criterion).** Let
$$
(\rho_i)_*^{\mathfrak B_i}:
[\mathsf S_B,\mathsf O_{i,B}]_{\mathfrak B_i}
\longrightarrow
[\mathsf S_B,\mathsf R_{i,B}]
\tag{P.6.1d.2.1}
$$
be postcomposition by $\rho_i$ on the full subcategory of $\mathfrak B_i$-admissible functors. Suppose an accepted proof establishes that $\rho_i$ is fully faithful on the operational realization subcategory containing every such image. Then $\operatorname{Lift}_i(R_i)$ is empty or equivalent to the terminal groupoid.

Theorem P.6.1b.3 supplies the response-presheaf part of this premise only when the datum identifies that realization subcategory with a full sector subcategory of $\mathsf{Inv}_{\mathrm{PPI}}/{\sim_{\mathrm{op}}}$, identifies the response-presheaf forgetful composite of $\rho_i$ with the corresponding restriction and corestriction of $\mathcal Y_{\mathrm{op}}$, and verifies the theorem's separating and protocol-complete hypotheses. The accepted enriched proof additionally supplies a typed forgetful functor
$$
\mathsf U_i:
\mathsf R_{i,B}
\longrightarrow
[\mathsf P_{i,B}^{op},\mathsf{Prob}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb D_B)]
\tag{P.6.1d.2.2}
$$
and proves that every response-presheaf morphism in the relevant image lifts uniquely to a $\rho_i$-morphism intertwining every registered update and verification map.

*Proof.* If $(F_i,\alpha_i)$ and $(F_i',\alpha_i')$ are two lifts, fullness gives a natural isomorphism $u:F_i\Rightarrow F_i'$ lifting $(\alpha_i')^{-1}\alpha_i$, and faithfulness makes it unique. Hence $\alpha_i'\circ(\rho_i u)=\alpha_i$, and the same faithfulness makes every lift automorphism the identity. Thus any nonempty fiber groupoid is equivalent to $\mathbf1$. The response-presheaf theorem supplies only the forgotten morphism; the additional enriched-lifting proof is exactly what transports and uniquely fixes the update and verification intertwiners. ∎

<a id="theorem-p61d3-exhaustive-compatible-lift-enumeration"></a>**Theorem P.6.1d.3 (Exhaustive Compatible-Lift Enumeration).** For a datum that passes Definition P.6.1d.1, the compatible-lift groupoid $\mathscr J_B$ is finite. Exhaustive enumeration computes its objects, arrows, components, complete isomorphism and non-isomorphism matrix between component representatives, and complete multiplication tables for every retained automorphism group. The result is exactly one of the four cases in Equation (2.6b.3).

*Proof.* The source, realization, response-normal-form, overlap, and protocol categories are finite. The naturality, branch-admissibility, overlap, eligibility, and higher-coherence predicates are decidable finite equations. Enumerating their solutions constructs the overlap-decorated groupoid and restricting to the objects that pass every audit predicate constructs its full compatible subgroupoid. Exhaustive arrow enumeration then computes connected components and automorphism groups, which determine exactly the four mutually exclusive cases of Equation (2.6b.3). ∎

<a id="definition-p61d4-trust-local-and-compatibility-schedules"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.4 (Trust, Local, and Compatibility Schedules).** The accepted trust, local, and compatibility schedules contain the following finite records and proof obligations.

1. The trust record
   $$
   \mathfrak T_{\mathrm{CU}}
   =
   \bigl(
   \iota_{\mathsf K},h_{\mathsf K},
   \Pi_{\mathsf K,\mathrm{tot}},\Pi_{\mathsf K,\mathrm{snd}},
   \iota_{\mathsf{Check}},h_{\mathsf{Check}},
   \Pi_{\mathsf{Check,tot}},\Pi_{\mathsf{Check,det}},
   \Pi_{\mathsf{Check,snd}},
   \mathsf A_{\log}
   \bigr)
   \tag{P.6.1d.4.1}
   $$
   fixes a versioned proof kernel, a versioned orchestration checker, their executable hashes, externally accepted kernel-totality and kernel-soundness results, checker totality, deterministic replay and correctness proofs, and a finite response-inert logical trust root. Kernel totality and soundness are external trust-root results; $\iota_{\mathsf K}$ checks every remaining proof object. The map $\iota_{\mathsf{Check}}$ computes coverage, status, and trace fields according to the acceptance predicates below. Let $\mathbb K_B$ be an exact decidable ordered field. The coefficient bridge is either the identity $\mathbb D_B=\mathbb K_B$ or a checked exact order-preserving embedding
   $$
   \jmath_B:\mathbb D_B\hookrightarrow\mathbb K_B
   \tag{P.6.1d.4.2}
   $$
   used by every response, probability, normalization, source-ownership, and cost table.

2. The local proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{loc}}$ verifies every finite source, response-normal-form, and realization-category table; every functor law; every response normalization; every branch predicate; every naturality square; every essential-image witness; and every finite-cost PPI dressing required by Definition 2.6a and Corollary P.6.1b.8b. The compatibility proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{comp}}$ verifies the exhaustive finite census of $\mathscr J_B$: all admissible local lifts, all admissible overlap maps, all eligibility and higher-coherence predicates, all lift isomorphisms, every component, and complete multiplication tables for every retained automorphism group. Distinct components are classified as distinct lift classes. A response-distinction label additionally requires a registered protocol that separates the components.

<a id="definition-p61d5-global-candidate-and-arrow-census"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.5 (Global Candidate and Arrow Census).**

The finite global-admissibility record is
   $$
   \mathfrak A_{\Omega,B}
   =
   \bigl(
   T_{\Omega,B},
   \mathsf P_{\Omega,B},k_B,
   \Sigma_{\Omega,B},L_{\Omega,B},
   \mathsf{Parse}_{\Omega,B}^{1},
   \mathsf{Code}_{\Omega,B}^{0},
   \mathsf{Code}_{\Omega,B}^{1},
   \mathsf G_{\Omega,B}^{0},
   \mathsf G_{\Omega,B}^{1},
   \operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{0},
   \operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{1},
   \mathsf{SemEqv}_{\Omega,B},
   \mathbf Y_{\Omega,B},
   (\sim_{s,p})_{s,p},
   Q_\Omega,\sim_\Omega,
   \mathscr L_{\Omega,B},
   \Pi_{\mathrm{gen}},\Pi_{\mathrm{arr}},
   \iota_{\Omega,B}
   \bigr).
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.1}
   $$
   Here $T_{\Omega,B}$ is a frozen typed finite-scope physical theory with explicit carrier, protocol, outcome, coefficient, and description bounds. Every accepted object code decodes to
   $$
   \omega
   =
   \bigl(
   \mathcal M_\omega,\mathfrak P_\omega,
   \mathsf O_{\Omega,\omega,B},
   \epsilon_\omega,\rho_{\Omega,\omega},
   (\pi_{i,\omega},\gamma_{i,\omega})_{i\in I_6},
   (\theta_{e,\omega})_{e\in E_B},
   \mathfrak D_\omega^{\mathrm{PPI}},C_\omega
   \bigr),
   \qquad
   C_\omega<+\infty,
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.2}
   $$
   where $\mathcal M_\omega\models T_{\Omega,B}$, $\mathsf P_{\Omega,B}$ is the finite global protocol category,
   $$
   \mathfrak P_\omega
   =
   (\mathcal N_\omega,\mathcal E_{N,\omega},V_\omega),
   \qquad
   \epsilon_\omega:
   \mathsf S_B\longrightarrow\mathsf O_{\Omega,\omega,B},
   \qquad
   \rho_{\Omega,\omega}:
   \mathsf O_{\Omega,\omega,B}
   \longrightarrow\mathsf{RNF}_{\Omega,B}
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.3}
   $$
   are one enriched PU carrier, its common realization functor, and its enriched global response-normal-form functor, where $\mathsf{RNF}_{\Omega,B}$ is the registered finite analogue of $\mathsf{RNF}_B$ on $\mathsf P_{\Omega,B}$. The inclusion $k_B:\mathsf P_B\hookrightarrow\mathsf P_{\Omega,B}$ and the sector functors $\pi_{i,\omega}:\mathsf O_{\Omega,\omega,B}\to\mathsf O_{i,B}$ carry checked natural isomorphisms
   $$
   k_B^*(\rho_{\Omega,\omega}\epsilon_\omega)
   \xRightarrow{\sim}
   \mathcal Y_B,
   \qquad
   \kappa_i\rho_i\pi_{i,\omega}\epsilon_\omega
   \xRightarrow[\ \gamma_{i,\omega}\ ]{\sim}
   j_i^*k_B^*(\rho_{\Omega,\omega}\epsilon_\omega)
   \xRightarrow{\sim}
   \kappa_iR_i,
   $$
   for all $i\in I_6$. The cells $\theta_{e,\omega}$ supply the overlap isomorphisms of (P.6.1d.1.13) and satisfy every predicate in the registered overlap inventory. Thus the six local lifts comprising $\operatorname{res}_B(\omega)$ factor through the same enriched carrier. The datum $\mathfrak D_\omega^{\mathrm{PPI}}$ is a checked finite-cost PPI dressing in the sense of Definitions P.6.2a and P.6.2b; it includes the physical protocol, finite record and verifier, cost, maintenance and update-use maps, and the intertwining proof for the complete response, update, and verification normal form. Define the complete global response-normal-form functor
   $$
   \mathbf Y_{\Omega,B}^{\omega}
   :=
   \rho_{\Omega,\omega}\epsilon_\omega:
   \mathsf S_B\longrightarrow\mathsf{RNF}_{\Omega,B}
   $$
   and, for $s\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathsf S_B)$ and $p\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathsf P_{\Omega,B})$, let
   $$
   \mathcal R_{\omega,s}(p)
   :=
   \mathcal R_{\mathbf Y_{\Omega,B}^{\omega}(s)}(p)
   \in
   \mathsf{Prob}_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb K_B),
   \qquad
   \sum_o\mathcal R_{\omega,s}(p)(o)=1.
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.4}
   $$
   Thus normalization is checked for every admitted source object and global protocol. For each pair $(s,p)$, the record also fixes an exact decidable equivalence relation $\sim_{s,p}$ on the corresponding normalized response laws and verifies reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity.

   Define the frozen PPI-filtered expanded-candidate class
   $$
   \operatorname{Cand}^{\mathrm{PPI}}_B(T_{\Omega,B})
   :=
   \left\{
   \omega\text{ of the form \emph{(P.6.1d.5.2)}}:
   \begin{array}{l}
   \mathcal M_\omega\models T_{\Omega,B},\ \omega\text{ lies within the registered}\\
   \text{carrier, protocol, coefficient, and description bounds, and}\\
   \omega\text{ passes every registered finite PPI gate}
   \end{array}
   \right\}.
   $$
   Isomorphism in this class means isomorphism of the complete registered tuple, including its carrier, protocols, PPI dressing, response, update, verification, overlap, unit, and cost data. The total generator $\mathsf G_{\Omega,B}^{0}$ enumerates the accepted object codes without duplication. The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{gen}}$ verifies every field in (P.6.1d.5.2)--(P.6.1d.5.4), proves that each decoded code belongs to $\operatorname{Cand}^{\mathrm{PPI}}_B(T_{\Omega,B})$, and proves the coverage statement
   $$
   \operatorname{Cand}^{\mathrm{PPI}}_B(T_{\Omega,B})/\cong
   \ =
   \operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{0}
   \bigl(
   \operatorname{im}\mathsf G_{\Omega,B}^{0}
   \bigr)/\cong .
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.5}
   $$
   The same proof verifies that every response law, update, verification, and finite PPI gate is invariant under the displayed expanded-candidate isomorphism. Thus the decoded representatives compute the corresponding candidate quotient, and coverage is a theorem of the frozen finite model language.

   The finite universe $\mathsf{Code}_{\Omega,B}^{1}$ is the canonical exhaustive census of every string over the frozen description alphabet, within the registered length bound, that the versioned total arrow parser accepts as a well-typed candidate PPI transformation. Independently of that syntax, let $\mathsf{SemEqv}_{\Omega,B}(\omega,\omega')$ be the exhaustive finite set obtained by enumerating every tuple of functions between the decoded finite carriers and retaining exactly those tuples that satisfy the complete PPI-dressing, response, update, verification, overlap, unit, inverse, and composition equations of $T_{\Omega,B}$. The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{arr}}$ verifies the syntax-coverage equality
   $$
   \mathsf{Code}_{\Omega,B}^{1}
   =
   \left\{
   s\in\Sigma_{\Omega,B}^{\le L_{\Omega,B}}:
   \mathsf{Parse}_{\Omega,B}^{1}(s)=1
   \right\}
   $$
   by an exhaustive census of the finite string universe. The total bounded generator $\mathsf G_{\Omega,B}^{1}(\omega,\omega')$ enumerates exactly the codes in that universe satisfying the admissibility equations of $T_{\Omega,B}$ for the ordered pair $\omega,\omega'$. Decoding is required to give a bijection
   $$
   \overline{\operatorname{dec}}_{\Omega,B}^{1}:
   \frac{
   \operatorname{im}
   \mathsf G_{\Omega,B}^{1}(\omega,\omega')
   }{={}_{\mathrm{code}}}
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
   \mathsf{SemEqv}_{\Omega,B}(\omega,\omega')
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.6}
   $$
   onto all semantic PPI equivalences in the frozen finite model class. Thus every such equivalence has a code, and two codes have the same decoded component maps exactly when they are $={}_{\mathrm{code}}$-equivalent. The objects of $\mathscr L_{\Omega,B}$ are the accepted code--decoding pairs
   $$
   \widehat\omega
   =
   (c_\omega,\omega),
   \qquad
   \omega=\operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{0}(c_\omega),
   $$
   and the hat is suppressed when the retained code is clear. The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{arr}}$ verifies the exhaustive classification of $\mathsf{Code}_{\Omega,B}^{1}$ into admissible and inadmissible codes with checked reasons, the groupoid laws, and bijections
   $$
   \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathscr L_{\Omega,B}}(\omega,\omega')
   \ \cong\
   \mathsf{SemEqv}_{\Omega,B}(\omega,\omega')
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.7}
   $$
   for every ordered pair. The same proof verifies total decoding, proves that $\operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{1}$ is constant exactly on $={}_{\mathrm{code}}$ and therefore descends injectively to the displayed quotient, and proves that no bounded canonical well-typed arrow string lies outside $\mathsf{Code}_{\Omega,B}^{1}$. It also proves
   $$
   \mathsf{SemEqv}_{\Omega,B}(\omega,\omega')\ne\varnothing
   \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   (\mathbf Y_{\Omega,B}^{\omega},\mathfrak D_\omega^{\mathrm{PPI}})
   \simeq_{\mathrm{PPI}}
   (\mathbf Y_{\Omega,B}^{\omega'},\mathfrak D_{\omega'}^{\mathrm{PPI}})
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.8}
   $$
   where $\simeq_{\mathrm{PPI}}$ means an isomorphism of the complete response, update, verification, overlap, unit, and dressing data on all retained global protocols. Hence the arrows exhaust the finite semantic PPI equivalences, including every retained automorphism. The semantic enumeration is independent of submitter-chosen syntax.

   Write
   $$
   (Q_\Omega/\!\sim_\Omega)_B
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.9}
   $$
   for the full subquotient of the registered ambient global-candidate quotient $Q_\Omega/\!\sim_\Omega$ used by Theorem P.14.1k.3 whose representatives satisfy every axiom of $T_{\Omega,B}$, every finite PPI gate in $\mathfrak D_\omega^{\mathrm{PPI}}$, and the carrier, protocol, coefficient, and description bounds. The equivalence relation $\sim_\Omega$ is registered independently of the finite code census and is checked to agree with the retained global PPI-equivalence semantics on this subquotient. The decoding-induced map is
   $$
   \iota_{\Omega,B}:
   \pi_0(\mathscr L_{\Omega,B})
   \longrightarrow
   (Q_\Omega/\!\sim_\Omega)_B,
   \qquad
   \iota_{\Omega,B}([\widehat\omega])
   =
   [\operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{0}(c_\omega)]_{\sim_\Omega}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.5.10}
   $$
   The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{gen}}$ verifies that this map is well defined, injective, and surjective, and that it commutes with restriction and with every claimed descended observable and PPI/PCE cost. Hence it is a bijection induced by the decoded physical candidates rather than an abstract cardinality match. The fixed-budget conclusion ranges over this exact subquotient. An unrestricted global-candidate conclusion requires a separately accepted exhaustive global-extension theorem.

<a id="definition-p61d6-restriction-and-essential-preimage-census"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.6 (Restriction and Essential-Preimage Census).**

The restriction functor
   $$
   \operatorname{res}_B:
   \mathscr L_{\Omega,B}
   \longrightarrow
   \mathscr J_B
   \tag{P.6.1d.6.1}
   $$
   is specified on every object and arrow and induces
   $$
   \overline{\operatorname{res}}_B:
   \pi_0(\mathscr L_{\Omega,B})
   \longrightarrow
   \pi_0(\mathscr J_B).
   $$
   The record also fixes the budget-$B$ compatible-tuple subspace $Q_{\mathrm{comp},B}$ of the $Q_{\mathrm{comp}}$ in the scope clause following Theorem P.14.1k.1, its registered restriction map
   $$
   \operatorname{res}^{P.14}_B:
   (Q_\Omega/\!\sim_\Omega)_B
   \longrightarrow
   Q_{\mathrm{comp},B},
   $$
   and a decoding-induced bijection
   $$
   \eta_B:
   \pi_0(\mathscr J_B)
   \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
   Q_{\mathrm{comp},B}.
   $$
   The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{res}}$ verifies functoriality, factorization through the six enriched sector lifts, every sector response, overlap, unit, calibration, and ownership equation, proves that $\eta_B$ preserves every sector coordinate and typed overlap cell, and verifies the commuting identity
   $$
   \eta_B\circ\overline{\operatorname{res}}_B
   =
   \operatorname{res}^{P.14}_B\circ\iota_{\Omega,B}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.6.2}
   $$
   For each representative $q$ of a component of $\mathscr J_B$, define the unframed essential preimage
   $$
   \mathscr E_q
   :=
   \mathscr L_{\Omega,B}
   \big|_{
   \{\omega:
   \operatorname{res}_B(\omega)\simeq q\}
   }.
   \tag{P.6.1d.6.3}
   $$
   This is the full subgroupoid on the displayed objects; a chosen isomorphism $\operatorname{res}_B(\omega)\simeq q$ remains an external membership witness. The record
   $$
   \mathfrak E_B
   =
   \{(\mathscr E_q,\Pi_{E,q})\}_{
   q\in\operatorname{Rep}\pi_0(\mathscr J_B)}
   \tag{P.6.1d.6.4}
   $$
   contains the exhaustive object, arrow, component, and automorphism census of every essential preimage.

<a id="definition-p61d7-exhaustive-source-audit"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.7 (Exhaustive Source Audit).**

The frozen source inventory is
   $$
   \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{src}}
   =
   \bigl(
   h_{\mathrm{src}},\mathsf E_{\mathrm{src}},
   \mathcal I_{\mathrm{src}},\pi_{\mathrm{cov}},
   \mathsf A_0,\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}},
   \mathcal Q_{\mathrm{src}},
   \mathsf{Cl}_{\mathrm{src}},
   \mathcal T_{\mathrm{src}},
   \Pi_{\mathrm{excl}}
   \bigr).
   \tag{P.6.1d.7.1}
   $$
   The source hash fixes the exact baseline. The typed eligibility rule $\mathsf E_{\mathrm{src}}$ ranges over every response-active protocol selection, sector-label map, source, operator, coefficient, normalization, unit map, calibration, branch premise, physical transformation, global-admissibility predicate, observable map, and cost term used anywhere in the certificate. It also visits every axiom and semantic clause of $T_{\Omega,B}$ and every branch of $\operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{0}$ and $\operatorname{dec}_{\Omega,B}^{1}$ as separate owners. The inventory $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{src}}$ classifies every eligible owner as included or excluded exactly once, with its source, type, status, and checked reason. The coverage proof $\pi_{\mathrm{cov}}$ proves that every owner actually consumed by a response-active certificate field is included exactly once, that every excluded owner is inapplicable in the frozen language or has a checked response-inertness proof, that no excluded owner is consumed by any constructor or proof, and that no eligible baseline owner is omitted.

   The finite seed set $\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{src}}$ contains the canonical typed serializations of the prohibited premise forms: a nominated sector lift, common carrier, source-exhaustion tag, selected minimizer, empirical outcome, or a literal equivalent under the registered source language. The finite typed transform grammar $\mathsf{Cl}_{\mathrm{src}}$ lists every admitted renaming, quotation, embedding, abbreviation, and constructor-literal transform. The canonical finite census $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{src}}$ is accompanied by $\Pi_{\mathrm{excl}}$, which proves that it contains $\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{src}}$, is closed under every transform in $\mathsf{Cl}_{\mathrm{src}}$, and gives a derivation of every member from a seed. Thus it is exactly the least closed set in the frozen finite serialization universe, and membership is terminating finite lookup.

   The finite directed graph $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{src}}$ contains every included owner and every derived response-active field. It is acyclic. Its leaves are partitioned into the exact predictive-base inventory $\mathsf A_0$, the response-inert logical trust root $\mathsf A_{\log}$, and the displayed independent sector premises $\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}}$. The base inventory is the canonical serialization of the registered predictive normal form and the explicitly named POP, PCE, and PPI premises admitted at this scope; it contains no sector lift, semantic target assignment, common-carrier witness, selected minimizer, or empirical comparison value.

   Every nonleaf vertex $v$ carries a registered total constructor
   $$
   g_v:
   \prod_{u\in\operatorname{Par}(v)}X_u
   \longrightarrow X_v
   \tag{P.6.1d.7.2}
   $$
   and a checked proof that its stored value is $g_v$ of its parent values. Every response-active literal occurring in constructor source or proof input is traced to a parent or promoted to an inventory leaf. The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{src}}$ verifies inventory coverage, constructor equations, topological rank, complete proof-dependency manifests, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{excl}}$. A desired lift, common carrier, source-exhaustion tag, selected minimizer, or empirical outcome may occur as a checked nonleaf output node. The canonical serialization of every leaf, constructor literal, and unproved premise must fail membership in $\mathcal T_{\mathrm{src}}$. The source status is
   $$
   \mathsf{base\mbox{-}exhausted}
   \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
   \mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}}=\varnothing
   \ \text{and every check in this item passes}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.7.3}
   $$
   Otherwise an accepted source audit is tagged $\mathsf{augmented}$ and lists every member of $\mathsf A_{\mathrm{ind}}$. Base exhaustion is relative to the frozen predictive presentation and leaves the premise status of every member of $\mathsf A_0$ unchanged.

<a id="definition-p61d8-no-double-counting-ownership-schedule"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.8 (No-Double-Counting Ownership Schedule).**

The no-double-counting record is
   $$
   \mathfrak W_B
   =
   \bigl(
   \mathbb K_B,W_B,\mathcal A_B,
   (P_a)_{a\in\mathcal A_B},
   \mathcal I_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{act}},
   \sim_{\mathrm{src}},\mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}},
   \operatorname{vec}_B,\operatorname{own}_B,
   L_{\mathrm{resp}},L_{\mathrm{cost}},
   \Pi_{\mathrm{own}}
   \bigr),
   \tag{P.6.1d.8.1}
   $$
   where $W_B$ is a finite-dimensional $\mathbb K_B$-contribution space and $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{act}}$ is the complete finite set of included response-active source rows from $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{src}}$. The exact decidable relation $\sim_{\mathrm{src}}$ identifies two rows exactly when their checked source semantics denote the same underlying contribution; every genuine partial intersection is split by a checked equalizer refinement before this relation is formed. The canonical contribution set is
   $$
   \mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}}
   :=
   \mathcal I_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{act}}/\!\sim_{\mathrm{src}},
   $$
   and its disjoint atomic cells are indexed by $\mathcal A_B$. The total maps
   $$
   \operatorname{vec}_B:
   \mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}}\to W_B,
   \qquad
   \operatorname{own}_B:
   \mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}}\to\mathcal A_B
   $$
   give each canonical contribution its stored vector and exactly one owner. The ownership projections obey
   $$
   P_a^2=P_a,\qquad
   P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad
   \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_B}P_a=I_{W_B}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.8.2}
   $$
   Let $\mathsf{Resp}^{\mathrm{lin}}_B$ be the registered finite $\mathbb K_B$-module of response contributions. The ledgers are typed linear maps
   $$
   L_{\mathrm{resp}}:W_B\to\mathsf{Resp}^{\mathrm{lin}}_B,
   \qquad
   L_{\mathrm{cost}}:W_B\to\mathbb K_B.
   $$
   The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{own}}$ exhaustively checks every pair of source rows, proves that $\sim_{\mathrm{src}}$ is an equivalence relation whose classes are exactly the common-source aliases after the declared equalizer refinements, proves that every active row maps to one class and every class has a row, and proves that $\operatorname{own}_B$ and $\operatorname{vec}_B$ cover every member of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}}$ exactly once. For each $c\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}}$ it checks
   $$
   P_a\operatorname{vec}_B(c)
   =
   \begin{cases}
   \operatorname{vec}_B(c),&\operatorname{own}_B(c)=a,\\
   0,&\operatorname{own}_B(c)\ne a.
   \end{cases}
   $$
   Writing $w_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{src}}}\operatorname{vec}_B(c)$, it verifies reconstruction by $w_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_aP_aw_{\mathrm{tot}}$, proves that the response and every asserted additive cost equal the corresponding sum of ledger images over the canonical atoms, and proves positivity and normalization of the assembled response law. A nonadditive cost is evaluated once on the assembled candidate.

<a id="definition-p61d9-observable-calibration-schedule"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.9 (Observable Calibration Schedule).**

The calibration record is
   $$
   \mathcal O_B
   =
   \bigl(
   (\mathcal V_{i,B},\mathcal O_{i,B})_{i\in I_6},
   \mathfrak U_B,\mathfrak N_B,
   \mathfrak C_B^{\mathrm{std}},
   \mathfrak R_B^{\mathrm{reg}},
   \mathfrak E_B^{\mathrm{err}},
   \Pi_{\mathrm{cal}}
   \bigr),
   $$
   where each $\mathcal V_{i,B}$ is an exact decidable value space and
   $$
   \mathcal O_{i,B}:
   \operatorname{Ob}(\mathscr L_{\Omega,B})
   \longrightarrow
   \mathcal V_{i,B}
   $$
   is the registered sector observable. The remaining fields give their unit maps, normalization conventions, calibration standards, regulator data, certified enclosures, and error laws. The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{cal}}$ verifies that every $\mathcal O_{i,B}$ is total on the declared global candidate class, normalized on its declared normalized domain, invariant on every arrow of $\mathscr L_{\Omega,B}$, and compatible with $\operatorname{res}_B$ and every registered overlap diagram. It also checks every typed unit-conversion square, calibration-standard identity, regulator-domain condition, enclosure inclusion, covariance or error-composition rule, and the source and overlap dependencies of those maps. Hence it induces the unique descended map
   $$
   \overline{\mathcal O}_{i,B}:
   \pi_0(\mathscr L_{\Omega,B})
   \longrightarrow
   \mathcal V_{i,B},
   \qquad
   \overline{\mathcal O}_{i,B}([\omega])
   =
   \mathcal O_{i,B}(\omega).
   $$
   Every retained rescaling or offset symmetry is either quotiented as response-null or fixed by an independently registered calibration. This includes time--energy rescaling, gauge-potential--charge rescaling, and absolute-energy offsets. Calibration definitions are independent of observed comparison values.

<a id="definition-p61d10-strict-selection-schedule"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.10 (Strict Selection Schedule).**

The selection field is either the token $\mathsf{unselected}$ or a tuple $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{sel}}$ of the following form:
   $$
   \mathfrak C_{\mathrm{sel}}
   =
   \bigl(
   \overline V_{\Omega,B},
   [\omega_*],g_{\Omega,B},
   \Pi_{\mathrm{desc}},\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}},
   \Pi_{\mathrm{tuple}}
   \bigr).
   \tag{P.6.1d.10.1}
   $$
   The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{desc}}$ verifies that the physical PPI/PCE cost is derived on $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{src}}$, fixed independently of comparison targets, invariant under every arrow of $\mathscr L_{\Omega,B}$, and therefore descends to
   $$
   \overline V_{\Omega,B}:
   \pi_0(\mathscr L_{\Omega,B})
   \longrightarrow
   \mathbb K_B\cup\{+\infty\}.
   \tag{P.6.1d.10.2}
   $$
   The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{sel}}$ compares every component in the exhaustive quotient, verifies finite attainment at $[\omega_*]$, and verifies
   $$
   g_{\Omega,B}
   :=
   \inf_{[\omega]\ne[\omega_*]}
   \bigl(
   \overline V_{\Omega,B}([\omega])
   -
   \overline V_{\Omega,B}([\omega_*])
   \bigr) >0,
   \tag{P.6.1d.10.3}
   $$
   with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, together with
   $$
   \overline{\operatorname{res}}_B([\omega_*])
   =
   [q_*].
   \tag{P.6.1d.10.4}
   $$
   The proof $\Pi_{\mathrm{tuple}}$ verifies
   $$
   \eta_B([q_*])=q_\bullet^*,
   $$
   where $q_\bullet^*$ is the selected compatible tuple of an accepted Theorem D.8.9c record, verifies its live sector statuses, and verifies that the accepted essential-preimage census contains $\omega_*\in\mathscr E_{q_*}$.

<a id="definition-p61d11-structural-independence-schedule"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.11 (Structural Independence Schedule).**

The independence field is the finite derivation dependency record of Convention P.14.1a.1 instantiated on the registered categorical-unity claim. It cites the source inventory and dependency proofs of Definition P.6.1d.7, the semantic check of Definition P.6.1d.11a, and the actual selection dependencies of Definition P.6.1d.10, including the eligible domain, cost and weights, normalization, calibration maps, and any tie rule. Let $h_{\mathrm{ind}}$ identify the exact serialized record for deterministic replay.

The checker traces every response-active choice to the declared base and independently supplied premises through typed, acyclic dependencies. A construction that uses a nominated lift, common carrier, selected representative, or empirical validation value as a decision input fails this schedule. Supplied physical assumptions retain their declared scope and status. Measurement data may enter the separately typed comparison calculation. They may also serve as explicitly declared calibration inputs in a claim whose status records that dependency.

<a id="definition-p61d11a-structural-independence-of-sector-interpretation"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.11a (Structural Independence of Sector Interpretation).**

For the registered finite category $B$, the interpretation record supplies the sector label map, the eligibility predicates $\mathsf E_{i,B}$, the induced inclusions $j_i$, and proofs of their typed definitions and exhaustive application as in Definition P.6.1d.5. Every response-active semantic choice must follow from the declared protocol types, rules, and premises, or have a checked proof that admissible alternatives induce equivalent responses. An unresolved, response-distinct interpretation remains an explicit branch choice. This check uses the semantic and source proofs and makes the admissible interpretation reproducible from its declared inputs.

<a id="definition-p61d12-continuum-status-hash-and-replay-schedules"></a>**Definition P.6.1d.12 (Continuum, Status, Hash, and Replay Schedules).**

The continuum field is either $\mathsf{not\mbox{-}claimed}$ or an accepted record $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{cont}}$ containing a directed family of finite-budget data and certificates, compatible bonding maps, commuting source and observable squares, a finite-PCE completion datum in the sense of Definition P.6.1b.5, quantitative convergence and remainder control, essential-image witnesses, PPI-physicalizable limiting morphisms, and a globally finite-cost representative as required by Theorem P.6.1b.6.

Let
$$
\mathcal K_{\mathrm{CU}}
=
\{
\mathsf{trust},\mathsf{datum},\mathsf{local},
\mathsf{compatibility},\mathsf{global},
\mathsf{restriction},\mathsf{source},
\mathsf{ownership},\mathsf{calibration},
\mathsf{selected\mbox{-}tuple},
\mathsf{cost\mbox{-}descent},
\mathsf{strict\mbox{-}selection},
\mathsf{independence},\mathsf{continuum}
\}
\cup
\{\mathsf E_q:
q\in\operatorname{Rep}\pi_0(\mathscr J_B)\}.
\tag{P.6.1d.12.1}
$$
The canonical payload $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{CU},B}^{\circ}$ contains the fields above but excludes the final hash, status vector, and checker output. The versioned total checker returns
$$
\mathsf{Check}_{\mathrm{CU}}
(\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{CU},B}^{\circ},h)
=
(\sigma_{\mathrm{CU}},\chi_{\mathrm{CU}}),
\qquad
\sigma_{\mathrm{CU}}(k)
\in

**P.6.3 A Case Study in Physical Instantiation: Outcome Records and Sharp Observables**

A measurement used for verification must produce a distinguishable record in a specified outcome alphabet $\Omega$. PPI requires a physical carrier for that record, while PCE compares carriers only after an encoding, a response criterion, and a cost functional have been specified. For finite $\Omega$, injective encodings exist into $\mathbb{R}$, $\mathbb{C}$, the integers, and finite bit strings. Consequently, distinguishability by itself does not select real numbers as a unique record language.

On the conditional complex-Hilbert branch, a sharp repeatable quantitative observable has additional structure. Assume that its possible retained values are real numbers $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$, that repeatability assigns mutually orthogonal outcome subspaces with projectors $\Pi_i$, and that the observable is represented linearly by
$$
A=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\Pi_i,
\qquad
\Pi_i^\dagger=\Pi_i,
\qquad
\Pi_i\Pi_j=\delta_{ij}\Pi_i.
$$
Then
$$
A^\dagger
=\sum_{i=1}^m\overline{\lambda_i}\Pi_i^\dagger
=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i\Pi_i
=A.
$$
Conversely, the finite-dimensional spectral theorem states that every Hermitian operator admits such a decomposition with real eigenvalues and orthogonal spectral projectors. Thus Hermiticity is equivalent to the stated sharp linear representation with real quantitative labels.

General quantum measurements are described by POVMs and need not be projective. Their outcome labels remain elements of an arbitrary registered alphabet. PPI/PCE can compare physical implementations of either a POVM or a sharp observable after the task and cost are specified; the Hermitian-observable representation additionally depends on the real-label, linearity, sharpness, and repeatability hypotheses above.

### P.6.4 Conditional Symmetry Selection by Efficiency

PCE supports a symmetry-selection statement on the following analytic branch. Let $X$ be a nonempty convex subset of a real Banach space, let a compact group $G$ act continuously and affinely on $X$, and let $\mu_G$ be normalized Haar measure. Assume that the finite-valued potential $V:X\to\mathbb R$ is convex, norm-lower-semicontinuous and $G$-invariant. For every $x\in X$, require the Bochner orbit average
$$
\bar x=\int_G g\cdot x\,d\mu_G(g)
$$
to belong to $X$. The continuous compact orbit is Bochner integrable. Finite measurable partitions of $G$ and representative orbit points give convex combinations $x_n\in X$ converging in norm to $\bar x$. Convexity and invariance give $V(x_n)\le V(x)$, and lower semicontinuity therefore yields
$$
V(\bar x)\le\liminf_{n\to\infty}V(x_n)\le V(x).
$$
For each $h\in G$, the partitions can simultaneously approximate the continuous maps $g\mapsto g\cdot x$ and $g\mapsto hg\cdot x$. Affinity identifies the second finite average with $h\cdot x_n$, continuity passes to its limit, and left Haar invariance gives
$$
h\cdot\bar x=\int_G hg\cdot x\,d\mu_G(g)=\bar x.
$$
Thus every admissible configuration has a $G$-invariant competitor of no greater cost. If a minimizer exists, averaging it produces an invariant minimizer. If $V$ is strictly convex, two distinct minimizers would have a midpoint of smaller cost; the minimizer is therefore unique and invariant.

Without convex feasibility, an invariant objective, and the orbit-average condition, resource optimization need not select a symmetric state. Symmetry-broken minima are compatible with a symmetric potential, and description complexity depends on the chosen representation and coding language. The electroweak value $\kappa_{EW}=38.5$, the flat-QFI branch, and other concrete symmetry comparisons therefore retain their separately stated response, calibration, admissible-class, and cost hypotheses.

### P.6.5.2 The Three Components

The entropy unification has three distinct components with different epistemic status:

**1. Landauer's Principle (Empirical Anchor)**

Landauer's principle provides the *physical content* of the logical-thermodynamic equivalence. It is an empirically confirmed principle (experimentally verified to within order unity of the theoretical bound) that can also be derived from applying the second law of thermodynamics to information-bearing degrees of freedom.

Landauer's principle is *incorporated* as the empirical bridge between logical and physical entropy; since it provides the physical basis for entropy unification, deriving it from the framework's axioms would be circular.

**2. PPI (Finite Physicalizability and Carrier Gate)**

The Principle of Physical Instantiation (Definition P.6.2) provides the carrier gate: every retained logical operation in the physical theory is represented by a finite physical process. It therefore prevents an abstract operation from bypassing the physical resource ledger, but it does not make every operation logically irreversible. Reversible embeddings and uncomputed ancillas may be implemented without an erasure heat floor.

Landauer accounting applies exactly when the physical process contains a registered cyclic many-to-one reset or overwrite. For an erased record $P$ with retained side record $R$, Theorem 31 gives $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}\ge H_q(P\mid R)$; the lower bound is positive only when that conditional entropy is positive. Thus PPI makes the reset theorem applicable to every physical reset meeting its hypotheses, while the reset certificate determines which operations incur the bound.

**3. Proposition E.2a and Theorems E.3 and E.6 (Operational Extension with Physical Bridges)**

The proved channel route is
$$
\text{completed binary reset-support certificate}
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{E.2a}}
C_{\max}\le\ln d_0-\ln2
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{E.3}}
N_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{\chi}{\eta\delta^2}\mathcal A+o(\mathcal A)
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{E.6\ saturation}}

=\frac{c^3\mathcal A}{4G_{\mathrm{op}}\hbar}+o(\mathcal A).

The leading Bekenstein--Hawking form follows only after independent records
verify $S_{\mathrm{rel}}=S_{BH}+o(\mathcal A)$ and $G_{\mathrm{op}}=G$.  The
local Clausius/Raychaudhuri branch is needed for the gravitational field
equation, not for the operational channel identity.

### P.6.5.4 Branch-Qualified Black-Hole Information Ledger

The unified entropy framework separates the black-hole information problem into structural no-deletion, exterior recovery, Page-purity, Page-entropy, and final-state layers with distinct hypotheses.

**Traditional Framing:** When matter falls into a black hole and the black hole subsequently evaporates via Hawking radiation, where does the information go? If the radiation is exactly thermal (carrying no information about the infallen matter), unitarity appears to be violated.

**PU Reframing:** Information and entropy are not separate substances but different operational descriptions of channel capacity across causal boundaries. The question "where does the information go?" presupposes that information is a conserved fluid that must flow somewhere. The framework replaces this picture with one of channel capacity reallocation.

**Four separate closure layers:**

1. **Operational boundary capacity is the proved channel quantity.** Theorems
   E.3 and E.6 give the saturated response entropy $S_{\mathrm{rel}}$ and
   operational coupling $G_{\mathrm{op}}$ on their stated branch.  Identifying
   this entropy with $S_{BH}$ and calibrating $G_{\mathrm{op}}=G$ are separate
   physical certificates.

2. **Infalling information is encoded.** On the finite retained-algebra branch of Theorem E.9.5e, an injective microscopic horizon update does not merge distinct retained finite-response classes. Recovery from the exterior coarse algebra additionally requires an accepted exterior-recovery sufficiency certificate $\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{hor},n}$ and is controlled by its certified error $\epsilon_n$.

3. **Evaporation transfers capacity.** On the macroscopic density and saturation branch of Theorem E.6, the retained boundary entropy satisfies $S_{\mathrm{rel}}/k_B=c^3\mathcal A_H/(4G_{\mathrm{op}}\hbar)+o(\mathcal A_H)$. Its budget tends to zero as $\mathcal A_H(t)\to0$ if the finite geometric bound $S_{\mathrm{rel}}/k_B\le C(\mathcal E_N(t))c_+(t)\mathcal A_H(t)/\delta(t)^2$ remains valid and the prefactor $C(\mathcal E_N(t))c_+(t)/\delta(t)^2$ stays uniformly bounded. Interpreting the changing tensor factors as transfer to radiation and horizon-radiation correlations additionally requires the closed retained-algebra and compatible-factorization hypotheses of Corollary E.9.5.2.

4. **Unitarity is preserved.** If the retained black-hole-plus-radiation algebra is closed and satisfies every finite-layer automorphism hypothesis of Theorem E.9.5 throughout evaporation, with the factorization required by Corollary E.9.5.2, the total fine-grained entropy is invariant. If the initial total state is pure and complete evaporation leaves a one-dimensional black-hole factor with no remnant or untracked sector, the final radiation state is pure.

**Technical restatement of Theorem K.3 (Page Curve).** *On a finite evaporation branch with $d_E(t)\ge2$ and $d_L(t)$, an accepted trace-coupled horizon entropy-continuity promotion certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{PageTV}}$ places the expected early-radiation von Neumann entropy within $\varepsilon_t\ln(d_E(t)-1)+h_2(\varepsilon_t)$ of the exact Haar Page average. Identifying the crossing with one half of the initial entropy additionally requires a conserved coarse entropy ledger. A zero final endpoint requires a pure initial closed state, a one-dimensional final black-hole factor, no remnant or untracked sector, and an exact endpoint or vanishing endpoint error.*

The Page-entropy conclusion is a trace-continuity-branch result. A bare accepted $t_{\mathrm{des}}=2$ moment-design certificate supplies only the Haar Page-purity law of Corollary K.3.1. Appendix K.3 supplies the separate design and trace-continuity gates.

## P.7 PU as a Transcendental Framework for Physics

Immanuel Kant's transcendental idealism sought to identify the *a priori* conditions for the possibility of human experience (e.g., space, time, causality) (Kant 1781). The PU framework can be seen as a generalization and operationalization of this project.

Instead of starting with human cognition, PU starts from registered predictive protocols and asks which operational, logical, and physical structures follow on specified realization branches. The Cogito and SPAP results constrain occurrence and diagonal self-prediction; Boolean closure, spacetime, quantum theory, and general relativity are reached only through the carrier, context, continuum, causal, thermodynamic, and observable certificates stated in their source theorems. Section P.7 therefore presents a branch-qualified transcendental programme.

### P.7.1 Resolution Programme for Wigner's Puzzle

The Principle of Physical Instantiation registers a bridge from an abstract operational requirement to a finite physical implementation. A PPI/PCE existence, optimality, or uniqueness conclusion requires a declared admissible comparison class, equivalence relation, cost functional, an existence or compactness/coercivity theorem, and the strict gap or rigidity needed for uniqueness. With those gates, the framework offers the following conditional explanation of why mathematical structures can recur in physics.

**Mathematics as Registered Predictive Structure**

Predictionism supplies one indubitable self-verifying occurrence through the Cogito. A general mathematical verification ledger requires additional closure data:

1. **Binary predicate.** Proposition A.0.1 supplies one retained binary predicate on its declared predictive encoding. It does not prove that every mathematical statement has an available, terminating, bivalent verifier.

2. **Boolean closure.** The identities
$$
V(\neg S)=1-V(S),\qquad
V(S_1\land S_2)=\min\{V(S_1),V(S_2)\},\qquad
V(S_1\lor S_2)=\max\{V(S_1),V(S_2)\}
$$
hold only when the registered statement class is closed under the indicated operations and the composite verifiers terminate with the declared semantics. Those closure and compositionality conditions are finite certificate entries, not consequences of a single Cogito occurrence.

3. **Universal computation.** Theorem A.0.1 and Corollary A.0.1 establish computation on the registered logical-structural route. Remark A.0.1b supplies a second, selected-rewrite interpreter using one duplicating rule, a retained term, a fixed root-restarted finite controller, and structural input and output maps. Its remaining Property R and physical realization premises are recorded separately.

On these branches, logic and computation are operational structures used by prediction. Each finite selection and observation is bounded; event existence quantifies over arbitrarily long iteration. The Predictive Universe framework treats spacetime as emergent finite-response structure rather than a fundamental substrate. Its causal and metric claims are carried by the intervention-response, latency, causal-diamond, regularity, and continuum certificates. A classical error-correcting code is a separate optional structural ledger.

Error correction may extend reliable transmission on a separately registered recovery branch; it is not constitutive of causal influence.

The Golay code is an independent optional recovery ledger and is not identified with spacetime.

<a id="thesis-p81-certificate-relative-spacetime-emergence"></a>**Thesis P.8.1 (Certificate-Relative Spacetime Emergence).** On the intersection of the independently registered dimensional, regularity, continuum, metric, causal-cone, clock, Lorentzian-signature, and physical-arrow branches, spacetime is represented as an effective finite-response geometry of the MPU network.
