4. During the exposure, environmental challenge points arrive as a Poisson process of mean $\nu$. Each point independently carries a mark $U_{c}$ uniform on $\{1,\dots,170\}$. A live compartment is killed by a challenge if $U_{c}\le 10$ for $G_{0}$ or $U_{c}\le 17$ for $G_{1}$. These thresholds are the exact finite-table implementation of $L_i/(1+L_i)$: $10/170=1/17$ and $17/170=1/10$.

The task is the same for both genomes. The score is the proper Brier rule on the full binary predictive simplex; the admissible phenotype class happens to contain only these two tables. The first action is not substituted for the forecast distribution when scoring. There is no feedback from viability or offspring counts into the forecast or loss definition.

The source uses $k_{\mathrm{PP}}=1$, so its registered expected-window predictive performance is exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{PP}_i &= 1/(1 + \mathbb{E}[L_i]) = 1/(1 + e_i^{2}), \\
\mathrm{PP}_0 &= 16/17, \qquad \mathrm{PP}_1 = 9/10.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
$$

The actual thinning probability is $1-\mathrm{PP}_i$. Because $L_{i}$ is constant on the task, neither an average-of-reciprocals substitution nor an accuracy/PP identification is used. A random-chance forecast 1/2 has performance 4/5, below both types, although that comparison is not needed for the weight theorem. We make no stronger viability-band or POP-optimality claim.

### 2.3 Complete operation and service ledger

The only admitted energy-consuming internal operations in a full parent cycle are:

| Stage | Operation | Type 0 debits | Type 1 debits | Byproduct during exposure |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Before exposure | Compartment/genome maintenance and expression preparation | 1 | 1 | A |
| Before exposure | Cue acquisition | 1 | 1 | A |
| Before exposure | Express the committed forecast table | 2 | 1 | A per debit |
| Before exposure | Forecast commitment and action gate | 1 | 1 | A |
| Before exposure | Delayed verification and challenge-gate installation | 1 | 1 | A |
| Before exposure | Reserved passive exposure service | 1 | 1 | A |
| Before exposure | Copy and prepare the two embryo slots | 2 | 2 | B per debit |
| After exposure, success or failure | Bounded-compartment cleanup/reset | 1 | 1 | None during this exposure |

Thus pre-exposure metabolic counts are $m=(7,6)$, embryo-copy counts are $b=(2,2)$, and post-exposure cleanup is one $E$. Reset is one finite-capacity padded batch primitive, valid for every admitted compartment configuration; it is not a per-survivor or per-waste-molecule cost. Any claim about a carrier with a different cleanup law would require a different ledger.

The environmental source/controller has a fixed per-parent service charge $C_{0}\ge 0$, plus $\epsilon_{c}\ge 0$ energy for every challenge mark emitted. It runs for the full $\tau$ even after death. It includes the fair-cue and 12-way action-source preparation, clocks, timing, control and finite-table maintenance. Non-challenge service is reserved/padded rather than stopped at death. The complete expected external charge is

$$
C_{\mathrm{env}} = C_0 + \epsilon_c \nu.
\tag{2}
$$

The entire challenge-source cost is counted, including harmless challenges and those emitted after death. Its random total has finite moments of every order and its expectation is common to the two types. It produces no internal A or B; no such equivalence is asserted. Passive source events do not require an uncharged internal evaluation or fresh forecast. The score gate is installed once, and a marked collision is a passive declared reaction. The source and controller costs are distinct from the task-value tariff $\Gamma$.

Every embryo is prepared before exposure, including embryos subsequently inactivated; both success and failure cleanup are charged. There is no successful-lineage-only accounting. The final readout is included in the reserved exposure/cleanup service. Storage is bounded and covered by maintenance, fixed-duration exposure service and reset. No latent physiological memory crosses generations.

The complete expected metabolic and reproductive ledger is therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{met}}(i) &= E(m_i + 1) + C_{\mathrm{env}}, \\
R_{\mathrm{rep}}(i) &= 2E, \\
V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(i) &= \Gamma, \qquad B(z) = z, \\
V_i &= R_{\mathrm{met}}(i) + R_{\mathrm{rep}}(i) + \Gamma(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$

The branch contains exactly the reactions, fuel debits and services just listed. Thus all admitted type-dependent energy terms are enumerated; all admitted external/failure/reset terms are included. There is no claim of enumerating unknown processes in actual biology. The expectation convention is explicit: V uses the whole-cycle expected ledger, not a pathwise equality between source energy and log viability.

## 3. The Definition-D.1f contract and response quotient

Let $X_B=\{\mathrm{cell}_0,\mathrm{cell}_1\}$ be the two complete prepared compartment specifications, including their genome, control tables and listed resources. All random source and reaction draws are outcomes, not extra persistent candidate coordinates.

Let the full retained one-generation response be

$$
O = (S, f_i(S), A_c, Y, L_i, H, D_0, D_1),
\tag{4}
$$

where $H$ is the end-of-exposure viability flag and $D_0,D_1$ are the viable child-template counts (zero through two). In the faithful branch $D_i=2H$ and $D_{1-i}=0$. Source/controller fuel counters are separately cost-typed records. The finite-resolution response does not claim to retain the unbounded Poisson source count. Its full expected service charge was accounted for in (2), so forgetting that environmental count does not forget a candidate-dependent cost.

The finite protocol category $P_{B}$ consists of the full protocol, its finitely many prefix/coordinate restrictions, the empty restriction, with an arrow from a restriction to each admitted refinement. Contravariance sends that arrow to the stochastic marginal projection from the refined response to its restriction. No unregistered adaptive requery, repair, earlier knowledge of Y, or environment port is allowed. Assign to each restriction the corresponding marginal of (4); the projections are stochastic maps. Coordinate deletion composes exactly, so these assignments constitute the response presheaf $R_{B}$. They are induced by the carrier operations above, not independently specified response tables.

For an especially elementary separating restriction, retain only $(S,A_c)$. Its four probabilities are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{type } 0 &: \{1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8\}, \\
\text{type } 1 &: \{1/6, 1/3, 1/3, 1/6\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
$$

These finite probability spaces are not isomorphic: an invertible stochastic map between finite probability spaces is a deterministic probability-preserving bijection, and the multisets of positive atomic masses differ. Therefore no natural isomorphism of the full response presheaves can identify $\mathrm{cell}_0$ and $\mathrm{cell}_1$. This argument does not rely on forbidding an arbitrary relabeling of a genome name. Numerical forecast and score labels are also fixed by the task.

Consequently $X_B/{\sim}_B$ has exactly two classes, and $i\to[\mathrm{cell}_i]$ is a bijection. Set

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_B &= \mathbb{R}_+^{3}, \\
r_B(\mathrm{cell}_i) &= (R_{\mathrm{met}}(i), R_{\mathrm{rep}}(i), \Gamma(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i)), \\
W_B &= \{(1,1,1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
$$

Every coordinate has energy units and is nonnegative. $K_{B}$ is closed, pointed and convex, and its dual interior is $\mathbb{R}_{>0}^3$. The chosen certificate belongs to that interior. Its scalarization is exactly $V_{i}$ in (3). Because the response classes are singleton classes of prepared specifications, $r_{B}$ and $V$ descend without a hidden minimization over implementations. Their quotient is finite, nonempty and compact, and $V$ is continuous. In particular a scalar minimum exists.

This proves the six D.1f fields and the descent actually required by P.8.9a.6. It does not invoke a stronger reconstruction theorem requiring every arbitrary natural transformation to have a biochemical implementation. Protocol-completeness at that stronger categorical level is not silently asserted.

## 4. Derived viable-descendant weights

<a id="theorem-p89a6n1-formal-physiological-realization"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.6n.1 (formal physiological realization).** On the carrier just defined, the exact expected viable-descendant weight is

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_i &= 2\exp[-\kappa\tau(m_i + 2) - \nu(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i)] \\
&= a \exp(-\lambda V_i), \\
a &= 2\exp(\lambda C), \qquad C = E + C_{\mathrm{env}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{7}
$$

All constants are independently registered source or operation parameters. In particular $a$ and $\lambda$ are branch-specific, and $\lambda V_i$ is dimensionless.

*Proof.* During exposure the number of metabolic byproducts is $m_{i}$ and the number of copying byproducts is two. Every byproduct has an independent exponential killing clock of rate $\kappa$. The probability that none rings before $\tau$ is $\exp[-\kappa\tau(m_i+2)]$. Independently, conditioning on $K$ challenge arrivals gives probability $\mathrm{PP}_i^K$ that no mark is fatal. The Poisson series gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k \ge 0} \exp(-\nu)\, \nu^{k}\, \mathrm{PP}_i^{k}/k! \\
&= \exp[-\nu(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i)].
\end{aligned}
$$

The survival probability $q_{i}$ is the product of these factors. Exactly two prepared embryo slots are released if the parent survives and none otherwise, so $\mathbb{E}[D_0+D_1]=2q_i$. By (3),

$$
V_i = E(m_i + 2) + C + \Gamma(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i).
$$

Using $\lambda E=\kappa\tau$ and $\lambda\Gamma=\nu$ yields (7). No inversion of measured or assumed $w$ occurs. The common post-exposure/source cost is retained in $V$ and creates the explicitly derived prefactor $a$. The prefactor need not be at most two; only the actual expected viable brood $2q_i$ is at most two. ∎

The theorem's essential source assumptions are transparent: independent per-byproduct killing clocks, their stated stoichiometric coupling to fuel debits, independent marked challenge arrivals, fixed brood, and the passive score-dependent challenge reaction. Changing any of these can destroy (7). POP/PCE alone does not infer them. Holding all operation costs and forecasts fixed while changing $\kappa$ or $\nu$ changes the life-cycle law; holding V fixed while changing copying errors changes descendants' types.

### Nonvacuous numerical branch

Take $\lambda=1/(20E)$, $\Gamma=30E$, hence $\nu=3/2$. Set $C_0=E/4$ and $\epsilon_c=E/2$, giving $C_{\mathrm{env}}=E$ and $C=2E$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_{\mathrm{met}} &= (9E, 8E), \qquad R_{\mathrm{rep}} = (2E, 2E), \\
V &= (217E/17, 13E), \qquad V_1 - V_0 = 4E/17 > 0, \\
q &= (\exp(-183/340), \exp(-11/20)), \\
a &= 2\exp(1/10).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$

Type 0 is strictly more expensive in metabolic energy but has sufficiently better source PP to have lower complete V and larger q. Removing the benefit/loss coordinate reverses the preferred type. Both cost and predictive performance are therefore nonvacuous parts of this comparison. The copies, failure handling and service charges are included even when common and order-neutral.

## 5. Response-faithful source-to-model maps

Define $J:I=\{0,1\}\to X_B/{\sim}_B$ by $J(i)=[\mathrm{cell}_i]$. Its inverse reads the two distinguished response classes (5); it does not require access to a hidden genome label. Both maps are total and bijective on the exact admitted class.

The carrier observation map $\pi$ reads the registers and viable embryo counts in (4). The mathematical protocol kernel $Q_{i}$ is the sequential composition of: fair $S$; the genome's deterministic $f_{i}$; the 12-way action gate; delayed $Y=S$; deterministic Brier verification; independent byproduct clocks and marked challenge gate; and the viable-embryo release rule. These are exactly the physical protocol stages specified in §2. For every retained restriction $P$ and every event $A$ in its finite response space,

$$
\Pr_{\mathrm{cell}_i}\{\pi_P \in A\} = Q_i^{P}(A).
\tag{9}
$$

*Proof.* The first five stage kernels agree entry by entry by their finite transition tables. Conditional no-death probability agrees by the clock/thinning calculation of Theorem P.8.9a.6n.1. The last stage is the deterministic release map. Multiplying the conditional kernels and summing over internal stages proves (9); marginalizing proves it for each restriction. Projection composition proves compatibility with every arrow of $P_{B}$. The distinguished masses (5) prove faithfulness. ∎

The resource map sends the actual admitted operation/source counters to their expected energy charges; the table and (2) prove that it equals $r_{B}$ after the registered task tariff is appended. This cost map is separate from the response map, but both come from the same compartment and source run. The mutation/copy map in §6 and population maps in §§7–8 extend the same commuting construction. No abstract identification of vector-space dimensions is used as a substitute for these maps.

## 6. Independently specified mutation generator

Let $u,v\ge 0$ have units inverse rescaled generation time. Declare a copying-error controller independent of all challenge/death/source draws. For a step $h\ge 0$ with $h\max(u,v)\le 1$, it applies to each embryo template the column-stochastic kernel

$$
M_h = I + hG, \qquad G = \begin{bmatrix} -u & v \\ u & -v \end{bmatrix}.
\tag{10}
$$

Specifically a $G_{0}$ template is copied as $G_{1}$ with probability hu, and a $G_{1}$ template as $G_{0}$ with probability hv; otherwise it is copied faithfully. For rational probabilities a single uniform finite word realizes these probabilities by thresholding. For general real probabilities the kernel is the separately declared ideal reaction instrument; the exact finite-word subbranch is already nonempty, for example rational u,v,h. Each prepared copy receives an independent error draw, including copies that will be inactivated. The copying operation is padded to its registered fixed E charge regardless of the draw. It is already included in the two embryo-copy debits.

Thus $G$ is derived as the exact derivative $(M_h-I)/h$ of the declared copying channel, has nonnegative off-diagonals and zero column sums, and is not derived from $V$. Taking $u=v=0$ gives the faithful/no-flux branch of Proposition P.8.9a.6. Taking positive $u,v$ activates an explicitly separate inheritance extension; the faithful-proposition hypothesis is not then asserted.

An alternative continuous-time template-error channel with those two reaction rates has $e^{hG}$ as its finite-step kernel, but it is a different source protocol. We use (10), not an unannounced replacement of I+hG by $e^{hG}$.

## 7. Exact finite brood law and expected-count selection

Let $n_{i}$ be the finite number of type-$i$ adults at generation start, with $N=\sum n_i$. Different parent compartments and their sources run independently. Let $S_i\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n_i,q_i)$ independently count viable parent broods. With faithful inheritance the next counts are $Z_i=2S_i$. With (10), every surviving brood has two independent child-template draws from $M_h$'s relevant column, conditional on its shared survival event.

The exact count probability-generating function is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[\prod_j z_j^{Z_j} \mid n] \\
&= \prod_i \Bigl[1 - q_i + q_i\Bigl(\sum_j M_{h,ji} z_j\Bigr)^{2}\Bigr]^{n_i}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
$$

It is normalized at $z=(1,1)$, has nonnegative coefficients, and contains the exact extinction probability

$$
\Pr(Z = 0 \mid n) = \prod_i (1 - q_i)^{n_i}.
\tag{12}
$$

There is no refill or retry in (11). Mutation draws of two siblings are independent conditional on survival; sibling viability is shared and correlated. Consequently multinomial offspring sampling cannot be substituted for (11).

The exact conditional mean is

$$
\mathbb{E}[Z \mid n] = M_h \operatorname{diag}(w)\, n.
\tag{13}
$$

In the faithful branch the deterministic expected-count recursion is therefore $N_i(t+1)=w_i N_i(t)$. This also holds for unconditional means of the independent branching process, by conditional expectation. Normalizing those means gives precisely

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_i(t+1) = {}&p_i(t) \exp(-\lambda V_i) \\
&/ \sum_j p_j(t) \exp(-\lambda V_j),
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
$$

and the source proposition's iterated formula and minimum-within-initial-support concentration follow. This is normalized expected count, not the expectation of a realized ratio.

For a direct denominator check, take one parent of each type. Conditional on at least one surviving brood,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[Z_0/(Z_0 + Z_1) \mid Z_0 + Z_1 > 0] \\
&= q_0(1 - q_1/2)/(q_0 + q_1 - q_0 q_1),
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$

whereas the normalized expected count is $q_0/(q_0+q_1)$. Their difference is

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_0 q_1(q_0 - q_1) \\
&/[2(q_0 + q_1)(q_0 + q_1 - q_0 q_1)],
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
$$

which is nonzero for (8). Equations (11)–(16) prevent a random-denominator normalization from being smuggled into the deterministic theorem.

## 8. Optional fixed-capacity regulation and a proved weak-exposure limit

This section is a **separate declared population protocol**, not a deduction from (11), and not needed for Theorem P.8.9a.6n.1. Its purpose is to connect the realized physiological branch to a concrete finite-population diffusion without assuming an iid exponential-weight sampler.

### 8.1 Actual regulator and its finite cost envelope

For every integer population size $N\ge\max(1,u,v)$, a generation starts with exactly $N$ adult templates. At the start it also copies an archive of their genome labels, retaining no older history. Each parent runs the preceding physiology with killing clock $\kappa/N$ and challenge mean $\nu/N$. In this regulated protocol the pre-exposure embryo-copy error controller of §6 is set to zero: both prepared embryo templates are faithful copies of their parental genome. The independent generator $G$ is activated only at the final output-copy step below. There is exactly one mutation stage. Let $S_{i}$ denote the number of viable broods and $K=\sum_i S_i$.

If $K>0$, the regulator draws N embryo templates independently with replacement from the 2K viable slots. If $K=0$, it instead draws N labels independently from the archive. Each chosen label is copied into one new adult template, with an independent error channel $M_{1/N}$. All parent compartments and their original embryo slots are then erased/reset in the parent cleanup stage already charged one E per parent. The separately added archive/control registers are also erased/reset. This explicit archive fallback closes the finite state space even on complete mortality; it is not a repeated attempt at selection.

The regulator is a finite source/control circuit for every $N$: scan all $N$ viability flags, keep their finite counts, and for each of exactly $N$ output slots use one uniform word in $\{0,\dots,L_N-1\}$, where $L_N=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,2N)$. Since both $2K$ and $N$ divide $L_{N}$, rank $\lfloor U d/L_N\rfloor$ is exactly uniform among $d$ available slots, for either $d=2K$ or the archive size $d=N$. This avoids an unbounded rejection sampler. For rational $u,v$, a second finite word implements $M_{1/N}$. All comparisons, lookup tables, archive writes, $N$ output-copy operations and resets have a fixed padded schedule at each $N$, including the fallback branch. Charge the complete additional finite source, table storage, archive/control schedule, output-copy energy and archive/control reset by $C_{\mathrm{reg}}(N)$ per population generation, whatever its finite size. This charge excludes the parent/original-embryo cleanup already owned by the one-$E$ parent ledger stage; no operation is charged twice. All embryo information needed for output copying is read before that cleanup. It need not be efficient or uniformly bounded in $N$.

$C_{\mathrm{reg}}(N)/N$ is a common per-input-parent service charge, so it does not change relative $V_{i}$. The regulator is physically outside the parent exposure compartment and generates no parental A or B. Its common ledger charge, like external service in §4, is included in the scalar ledger and accounted for by a common prefactor. There is no inference that this expensive finite implementation solves any complexity-budget optimization.

At weak exposure the environmental source charge is $C_{\mathrm{env}}(N)=C_0+\epsilon_c\nu/N$. Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
V_i^{(N)} = {}&E(m_i + 3) + C_{\mathrm{env}}(N) \\
&+ \Gamma(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i) + C_{\mathrm{reg}}(N)/N.
\end{aligned}
$$

This differs from (3) by a common scalar. With $C_N=E+C_{\mathrm{env}}(N)+C_{\mathrm{reg}}(N)/N$, the actual raw viability weights satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
2q_i^{(N)} &= 2\exp[(\lambda/N) C_N] \\
&\qquad \exp[-(\lambda/N) V_i^{(N)}], \\
q_i^{(N)} &= \exp(-d_i/N), \\
d_i &= \lambda[E(m_i + 2) + \Gamma(1 - \mathrm{PP}_i)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
$$

Even if the padded common charge grows with N, the equality and cancellation are exact. No mortality clock is attributed to external regulator service. The source comparisons and the limit concern the bounded relative $d_{i}$, not an unstated uniform bound on total implementation cost.

### 8.2 Exact regulated kernel

At $x=n/N$, draw independent $S_i\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n_i,q_i^{(N)})$. Put

$$
\begin{aligned}
y(S) &= S/K \text{ when } K > 0, \qquad y(0) = x, \\
\psi(S) &= M_{1/N}\, y(S).
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $X'=(1/N)\operatorname{Multinomial}(N,\psi(S))$ conditionally on $S$. Hence, for $z\in\Delta_{N}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_N(x,z) = {}&\sum_{s_0=0}^{n_0} \sum_{s_1=0}^{n_1} \\
&\Bigl[\prod_i \binom{n_i}{s_i} (q_i^{(N)})^{s_i} (1 - q_i^{(N)})^{n_i - s_i}\Bigr] \\
&[N!/\prod_j (Nz_j)!] \prod_j \psi_j(s)^{Nz_j}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$

This is normalized, contains the all-dead fallback, retains the random denominator, and has no hidden archive state: the archive is a deterministic copy of the current $n$ and is destroyed each generation. It is not equal at finite $N$ to $\operatorname{Multinomial}(N,M S_{\exp(-d/N)}(x))$.

### 8.3 Diffusion theorem and proof

<a id="theorem-p89a6n2"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.6n.2.** For fixed finite $d_{i}\ge 0$ and fixed $u,v\ge 0$, the chains (18), on the $N$-generation clock, converge from every initial law $X_0^N$ converging weakly to $X_{0}$ to the unique continuous diffusion with generator

$$
\begin{aligned}
L f(x) &= [Gx - \lambda C(x)V]\cdot\nabla f(x) \\
&\quad + (1/2)\, C(x) : \operatorname{Hess} f(x), \\
C(x) &= \operatorname{diag}(x) - x x^{T},
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
$$

where $V$ is the unscaled vector (3). Since $d=\lambda(V-C1)$, $C(x)d=\lambda C(x)V$. In coordinate $x=x_0$ this is

$$
\begin{aligned}
dX = {}&[v(1-X) - uX + \lambda(V_1 - V_0)X(1-X)]\,dt \\
&+ \sqrt{X(1-X)}\,dW.
\end{aligned}
\tag{20}
$$

The convergence is in Skorokhod J1 on every fixed finite time interval. Linear interpolants converge in the uniform-path topology in distribution. Boundaries are included; no artificial reflecting boundary is imposed.

*Proof of characteristics.* Let $D_i=n_i-S_i$ and $D=\sum_i D_i$ be the failed parent counts. Uniformly in $x$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E} D_i &= x_i d_i + O(N^{-1}), \\
\mathbb{E} \exp(tD) &\le \exp[d_{\max}(\exp(t) - 1)] \text{ for } t \ge 0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{21}
$$

The second inequality follows from $1-q_i\le d_i/N$ and multiplying Bernoulli moment-generating functions. Consequently all moments of $D$ are uniformly bounded, and the probability of $D>N/2$ decays faster than every inverse power of $N$ by using any fixed $t>0$. On $D\le N/2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
y - x &= (xD - D_{\mathrm{vector}})/(N - D), \\
y - x &= (xD - D_{\mathrm{vector}})/N + O(D^{2}/N^{2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{22}
$$

On the complementary event, including $D=N$, the difference is bounded. Thus, uniformly on the whole simplex lattice,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}(y - x) &= -C(x)d/N + O(N^{-2}), \\
\mathbb{E}\lVert y - x\rVert^{2} &= O(N^{-2}), \qquad \mathbb{E}\lVert y - x\rVert^{4} = O(N^{-4}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
$$

Multiplication by $M_{1/N}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}(\psi - x) &= [Gx - C(x)d]/N + O(N^{-2}), \\
\mathbb{E}\lVert \psi - x\rVert^{2} &= O(N^{-2}), \qquad \mathbb{E}\lVert \psi - x\rVert^{4} = O(N^{-4}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{24}
$$

For the independent final offspring sample, conditional mean is $\psi$, covariance is $C(\psi)/N$, and the fourth centered moment is $O(N^{-2})$ uniformly in $\psi$ (expand the sum of $N$ independent bounded centered one-hot variables; only index patterns without singleton indices remain). Smoothness of $C$ and (24) then give, with $\delta=X'-x$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
N \mathbb{E}\delta &\to Gx - C(x)d, \\
N \mathbb{E}[\delta\delta^{T}] &\to C(x), \\
N \mathbb{E}[\lVert\delta\rVert^{2}\, 1\{\lVert\delta\rVert > \epsilon\}] &\to 0
\end{aligned}
\tag{25}
$$

uniformly; the last statement follows from $\mathbb{E}\lVert\delta\rVert^4=O(N^{-2})$. Taylor's formula with a uniform Hessian modulus on the compact simplex proves convergence of discrete generators on $C^2$ tests to (19). Bounded drifts and scaled second moments give stopped-increment tightness; the fourth-moment bound makes the maximum jump vanish on a fixed $N$-scaled interval. Every limit is therefore continuous and solves the martingale problem (19), by the test-function martingale and generator convergence.

For completeness of the uniqueness step, the drift in (20) is Lipschitz on $[0,1]$. Extend it constantly past the endpoints and put $\sigma(x)=\sqrt{\pi(x)(1-\pi(x))}$ with $\pi$ clipping to $[0,1]$. Then $|\sigma(x)-\sigma(y)|^2\le|x-y|$. For two solutions with the same Brownian driver, the standard smooth absolute-value approximants with second derivative bounded by $2/(k|z|)$ give

$$
\mathbb{E} \phi_k(X_t - Y_t) \le L \int_0^t \mathbb{E}|X_s - Y_s|\, ds + t/k.
$$

Letting k increase and applying Gronwall proves pathwise uniqueness. Weak existence is already supplied by the compactness limit. The classical weak-existence/pathwise-uniqueness implication gives uniqueness in law. Therefore every subsequence has the same limit, proving full convergence. Vanishing jumps gives the linear-interpolation assertion. ∎

The general diffusion-approximation method and one-dimensional uniqueness implication are established probability results, not novelty claims. The new check here is for the actual survivor-then-regulation kernel (18), rather than importing multinomial normalized-selection moments into it. The same scaling must not be applied to fixed exposure: $q_{i}$ fixed away from one produces an order-one selection change and a different regime. This is a generation-count limit. Since the admitted regulator may grow with N, no fixed physical wall-clock scaling is asserted.

## 9. Acceptance boundaries and falsifiers

The construction proves a nonempty, source-typed realization component and a joined two-type diffusion. It does not classify every life cycle or provide recombination/diploid realization for this same two-template carrier. The separately proved tensor results remain inputs for those named mathematical classes. A future common-carrier lift must give its own copying/meiosis/role maps and cost closure rather than infer them from the present witness.

Concrete falsifiers within the declared class include: a hidden type-dependent service charge; a score not equal to the proper Brier loss of the committed forecast; revelation of Y before commitment; a byproduct count inconsistent with the fuel table; dependence among supposedly independent killing clocks; an uncharged retry or repair; omitting the all-dead case; replacing (18) with a normalized mean law; treating a source energy tariff as dissipated heat; or deriving G from V.

Changing the primitive carrier assumptions defines a different model and is not an empirical disproof of this conditional theorem. Conversely, explicitly naming those assumptions does not certify that a real biological system satisfies them. The realized formulas and the independent-input boundaries must remain together when this component is reviewed or integrated.

These supply the source-to-model maps and causal order. The theorem remains conditional on those explicitly declared carrier laws; it proves neither empirical occurrence nor arbitrary molecular synthesis feasibility.

 

 

### P.8.9a.5.2 Resolution of Evolutionary Puzzles

The PCE perspective resolves several classical puzzles:

**Puzzle 1: Why does complexity increase?**

*Standard view:* No clear thermodynamic driver; complexity increase appears contingent.

*PU resolution:* On a declared one-dimensional biological trait branch where $C$ obeys the complexity-adaptation dynamics of Definition 20, all remaining coordinates are held fixed or have been validly reduced, and the benefit map is the identity, the local direction of increasing complexity is selected exactly when

$$
\Gamma_0 \frac{\partial PP}{\partial C}
>
\lambda R'(C)+R'_I(C).
$$

This is the sign condition for that registered reduced dynamics. Changes in ecological interactions, resource constraints, inheritance, or the other coordinates of the generational ledger can reverse the sign, produce a plateau, or invalidate the one-dimensional reduction.

**Puzzle 2: Why is evolution "creative"?**

*Standard view:* Random mutation plus selection; creativity is illusory.

*PU resolution:* Appendix D supplies a stochastic-gradient model only on branches whose retained adaptation variables admit its drift, diffusion, regularity, and boundary data. When a biological scaling limit derives the drift and diffusion coefficients and identifies its effective potential with the registered generational PCE ledger, Equation D.8 gives a conditional exploration-and-selection model. Without that bridge, evolutionary novelty remains governed by the separately specified biological variation and inheritance kernels.

**Puzzle 3: Why convergent evolution?**

*Standard view:* Similar selective pressures lead to similar solutions.

*PU resolution:* On a biological model in which the compared lineages share a specified retained state space, the same PCE potential $V$, and the same attracting basin, Theorem D.5 gives low-noise concentration near potential minima only under its detailed-balance hypotheses; Theorem D.6.5b gives basin convergence only on its regular Morse--Smale branch. Theorem D.3 proves regularity of global minima under its own hypotheses. Convergent evolution is therefore a conditional application of an explicitly supplied biological landscape model.

**Puzzle 4: Why modularity and evolvability?**

*Standard view:* Modularity evolves because modular organisms evolve faster.

*PU resolution:* On a registered architectural comparison class, a modular candidate is PCE-favored only when its reduced cross-module propagation and adaptation costs lower the complete ledger of Definition D.1 after its interface, redundancy, coordination, and performance effects are included. PCE supplies the comparison rule. A modularity conclusion therefore requires an explicit response-preserving comparator and a strict total-potential inequality for the biological branch.

## P.8.9a.6 The Continuity of Life and Physical Law

The PU framework permits a branch-qualified comparison between physical code constructions and biological error-tolerant organization. The comparison records a common variational grammar where the relevant branch contracts exist:

**Table P.8.9a.3: Parallel Structure of Physical and Biological Codes**

| Property | Abstract Golay-code model | Life (Genetic) |
|----------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Block structure | $24$ binary coordinates | 3 nucleotides (codon) |
| Redundancy | a chosen systematic presentation has 12 message and 12 parity coordinates | 64 codons map redundantly to 20 amino acids plus termination |
| Rate / degeneracy | formal binary-linear rate $R=1/2$ | functional occupancy fraction $21/64\approx0.328$; information rate $\log_2 21/6\approx0.732$ |
| Error correction / tolerance | classical correction through weight 3 for a registered Hamming channel and decoder | point-mutation tolerance through wobble and chemical-neighborhood structure |
| Selection principle | retained mathematical code selection requires the rate gate and $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{dist}}$; physical realization is separate | normalized selection equals generational PCE reweighting only under Proposition P.8.9a.6 |

<a id="thesis-p89a2-continuity-of-organization"></a>**Thesis P.8.9a.2 (Continuity of Organization).** Physical code models and biological persistence models can instantiate the same branch-indexed PCE variational grammar when each domain supplies its own admissible state space, response quotient, cost ledger, and update law. This common grammar does not equate substrates, error channels, causal mechanisms, or functional roles. In the biological case, the exact theorem-level content is the conditional normalized-selection result of Proposition P.8.9a.6 and Theorem P.8.9a.6a.

The comparison extends the use of mathematical optimization language to the biological domain. Biological constitutive dynamics, inheritance kernels, environmental dependence, and empirical response maps remain independent inputs to the biological branch.

### P.8.9a.6.1 The Genetic Code as Evolved Error Tolerance

<a id="proposition-p89a2-ensemble-relative-genetic-code-error-tolerance"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.2 (Ensemble-Relative Genetic-Code Error Tolerance).** Under the random-code ensemble and translation-error-weighted efficiency score used by Freeland and Hurst (1998), the standard genetic code scores better than all but about one generated alternative in $10^6$.

*Evidence.* Quantitative analyses (Freeland and Hurst 1998; Novozhilov et al. 2007) support the following scoped statements:
1. The standard code has a low mutation/mistranslation cost under specified amino-acid cost functions
2. Synonymous and chemically related assignments contribute to that low score
3. The reported tail rank changes with the cost function, error weights, and admissible random-code ensemble

*Framework interpretation.* The random-code comparison is compatible with an evolutionary robustness hypothesis. Identifying its mechanism with PCE requires an independently specified evolutionary dynamics and a test against alternative mechanisms.

## P.8.9a.7 Consciousness Complexity in Biological Systems

The PU framework's treatment of consciousness provides a conditional extension of the error-correction perspective to neural systems. For biological aggregates with $C_{\mathrm{agg}}>C_{op}$, the threshold identifies the eligible aggregate class; nonzero Consciousness Complexity follows on Theorem 34's strict-improvement branch with a reachable Born reference, a lower-potential reachable non-Born context, Born-level minimality, operational representability, attainment, and asymptotic stability, together with Hypothesis 3's context-to-control realization.

### P.8.9a.7.1 The CC Threshold in Biology

<a id="definition-p89a4-biological-cc"></a>**Definition P.8.9a.4 (Biological CC).** Use the response-model extension and registered complexity units of Definition 31. For a biological system $S$, define the threshold response by
$$
\mathrm{CC}(S)=
\begin{cases}
0,&C_{\mathrm{agg}}\le C_{op},\\
\alpha_\infty\,\mathcal G\!\left((C_{\mathrm{agg}}-C_{op})/C_{\mathrm{scale}}\right),&C_{\mathrm{agg}}>C_{op}.
\end{cases}
$$
Here $C_{\mathrm{agg}}$ is the biological aggregate's registered complexity coordinate, $C_{op}$ is the operational threshold of Definition 13, and $C_{\mathrm{scale}}>0$ has the same units. The shape $\mathcal G:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]$ is right-continuous at $0$, satisfies $\mathcal G(0)=0$ and $\lim_{x\to\infty}\mathcal G(x)=1$, and has $\mathcal G'(x)\ge0$ and $\mathcal G''(x)\le0$ for $x>0$, as in Theorem 35. On the independently declared bounded-bias branch, $0\le\alpha_\infty\le\alpha_{CC,max}<1/2$. The piecewise definition evaluates $\mathcal G$ only on its declared domain.

The branch $\alpha_\infty=0$ is admissible and gives $\mathrm{CC}(S)=0$ at every aggregate complexity.

<a id="theorem-p89a7-emergence-of-biological-cc"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.7 (Emergence of Biological CC).** Let a biological MPU aggregate satisfy $C_{\mathrm{agg}}>C_{op}$ and Assumption 1's context-dependent ND-RID premise. On Theorem 34's strict-improvement branch, assume a reachable reference context $u_0$ with $P_{\mathrm{obs}}(\cdot\mid u_0)=P_{\mathrm{Born}}$; a reachable context $u_+$ with $V(u_+)<V(u_0)$ and $P_{\mathrm{obs}}(\cdot\mid u_+)\ne P_{\mathrm{Born}}$; $V(u)\ge V(u_0)$ for every reachable Born-realizing context; Definition 30's Hermitian-preserving, trace-annihilating complex-linear representation for every retained non-Born deviation; and an attained global minimum with an asymptotically stable minimizing attractor. If Hypothesis 3's separately nominated context-to-control realization is accepted for the biological system, then the resulting nonzero operational CC is realized as modulation of retained ND-RID probabilities through organized internal states.

*Mechanism.* On a biological branch satisfying the theorem above and an accepted Appendix L implementation package, including its carrier, source, coupling, target-response, coherence, noise, likelihood, continuity, compactness, stability, and cost-benefit records:
1. The biological aggregate maintains a registered context state $\text{context}_S$
2. A declared bioelectric, neural, or other physical carrier realizes the context-to-signal map
3. The accepted response map couples that signal to local ND-RID control parameters
4. The selected non-Born context produces the Definition 30 probability shift and has lower registered PCE potential than every Born-realizing context

### P.8.9a.7.2 Neural Systems and Predictive Processing

Predictive-processing models in neuroscience supply candidate neural variables for a PU bridge. Identifying a neural system with POP requires a registered task, score, cost ledger, forecast map, verifier, and update map:

<a id="proposition-p89a3-conditional-neural-to-pop-modeling-bridge"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.3 (Conditional Neural-to-POP Modeling Bridge).** Fix a neural dynamical model $\mathfrak N$ together with a registered task $\mathcal T$, admissible action set $\mathcal A$, outcome law, score $Q$, resource coordinate $C_P$, internal-state encoder $e$, forecast map $f$, verification map $v$, and update map $u$. Assume:

2. The performance functional computed from $Q$ is the registered $PP$ of that task.
3. The admissible-policy objective and resource constraint are exactly the POP objective and constraint of Axiom 1.

Then $\mathfrak N$ instantiates POP on that registered branch.

*Proof.* Assumption 1 supplies the required loop maps and capabilities. Assumption 2 identifies the optimized response functional with the registered PU performance, and assumption 3 identifies both the feasible set and objective with POP. Substitution therefore makes the neural policy problem identical to the registered POP problem. Without any one of these bridge assumptions, similarity of predictive-processing terminology does not establish PU implementation. ∎

*Candidate bridge coordinates:* predictive model $\mapsto M_t$; task-scored prediction error $\mapsto$ the registered $PP$ residual; precision $\mapsto$ a declared weighting coordinate; free energy $\mapsto$ a specified term of $V$ only after unit and sign matching; active inference $\mapsto$ a registered action-policy optimization only after the action and outcome maps are supplied. These arrows are modeling assignments certified by the proposition's hypotheses.

### P.8.9a.7.3 Bioelectric Codes and Morphogenetic CC

Bioelectric signaling supplies candidate observables for a morphogenetic aggregate bridge.

<a id="definition-p89a5-phenomenological-bioelectric-aggregate-coordinate"></a>**Definition P.8.9a.5 (Phenomenological Bioelectric Aggregate Coordinate).** For a declared family of gap-junction-coupled cellular-network models, define
$$
C_{\mathrm{agg}}^{\mathrm{bio}}(N,g)=C_0N^{\alpha(g)},
\qquad
\alpha(g)=1+\beta\tanh(g/g_c),
$$
where $N\ge1$ is an integer cell count, $C_0>0$ and $g_c>0$ are finite, and $\beta$ and the coupling coordinate $g$ are finite real numbers. The physiological state, network boundary, and response protocol specify the model domain. Report each parameter as a stipulated model input or as a calibration with its data and uncertainty. The formula defines a positive phenomenological coordinate for that domain.

<a id="proposition-p89a4-morphogenetic-bridge-obligations"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.4 (Morphogenetic Bridge Obligations).** The cited experiments provide evidence that bioelectric interventions can alter regeneration, ectopic organ formation, and error recovery. Calling those effects CC requires an additional bridge that maps the measured network state to $C_{\mathrm{agg}}$, verifies Theorem 34's strict-improvement and representability conditions, realizes Hypothesis 3's normalized response-active context-to-control map, and separates the claimed channel from ordinary electrophysiological and biochemical causation. `Goal-directedness`, `target morphology`, and `scale-free cognition` are interpretive labels until those records are supplied.

The attractor model below is therefore a conditional dynamical representation. It becomes a model of the biological system only after its state map, potential, dynamics, and observables are calibrated.

<a id="definition-p89a5a-morphogenetic-pce-potential"></a>**Definition P.8.9a.5a (Morphogenetic PCE Potential).** Let $X_{\mathrm{cell}}$ be the compact state space of a gap-junction-coupled cellular aggregate, including cellular positions, membrane-potential variables, gene-regulatory variables, and extracellular constraints at the resolution relevant to the developmental process. Let
$$
\pi_{\mathrm{morph}}:X_{\mathrm{cell}}\to\mathcal M
$$
map cellular states to coarse morphologies. Define the morphogenetic PCE potential
$$
V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)
=
V_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{cell}}(x)
+
V_{\mathrm{prop}}^{\mathrm{gap}}(x)
+
U_{\mathrm{viab}}(\pi_{\mathrm{morph}}(x))
-
V_{\mathrm{benefit}}^{\mathrm{form}}(\pi_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)).
\tag{P.8.9a.7.3.1}
$$
Here $V_{\mathrm{op}}^{\mathrm{cell}}$ is the metabolic and regulatory cost of maintaining the cellular state, $V_{\mathrm{prop}}^{\mathrm{gap}}$ is the propagation/coherence cost of maintaining bioelectric coordination across the coupled network, $V_{\mathrm{benefit}}^{\mathrm{form}}$ is the predictive benefit of a morphology that supports the aggregate's viability and action repertoire, and $U_{\mathrm{viab}}$ is a lower-semicontinuous viability penalty that is finite on admissible morphologies and diverges on morphologies outside the aggregate's viable developmental class. The role of $U_{\mathrm{viab}}$ is formally parallel to the cost potential $U_S$ of Definition P.16.3: it shapes trajectories through a constraint surface rather than through a positive stored template.

<a id="theorem-p89a7a-target-morphology-as-pce-attractor"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.7a (Target Morphology as PCE Attractor).** Suppose:

1. $X_{\mathrm{cell}}$ is a nonempty compact metrizable state space and $V_{\mathrm{morph}}:X_{\mathrm{cell}}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ is lower semicontinuous, finite on at least one state, and bounded below;
2. the reference measure $dx$ is a finite Borel measure on $X_{\mathrm{cell}}$, and, if $V_{\min}:=\min_{X_{\mathrm{cell}}}V_{\mathrm{morph}}$, then every sublevel set $\{x:V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)\le V_{\min}+\varepsilon\}$ with $\varepsilon>0$ has positive reference measure;
3. the detailed-balance stationary measures have Gibbs form
   $$
   \pi_\theta(dx)=Z_\theta^{-1}e^{-V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)/\theta}\,dx;
   \tag{P.8.9a.7.3.3}
   $$
4. for the deterministic conclusion, $B\subseteq X_{\mathrm{cell}}$ is a compact positively invariant basin identified homeomorphically with a compact subset of an open domain $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ for a specified finite $n$, $V_{\mathrm{morph}}|_B$ is the restriction of a $C^1$ function on $\Omega$ denoted by the same symbol, $G:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is continuous and symmetric positive semidefinite, and the vector field
   $$
   \dot x(t)=-G(x(t))\nabla V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x(t))
   \tag{P.8.9a.7.3.2}
   $$
   is locally Lipschitz and has a forward-complete solution for every initial state in $B$;
5. the largest invariant subset of
   $$
   \left\{x\in B:\nabla V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)^T G(x)\nabla V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)=0\right\}
   $$
   is contained in
   $$
   A_{\mathrm{morph}}:=\arg\min_{x\in X_{\mathrm{cell}}}V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x).
   \tag{P.8.9a.7.3.4}
   $$

Then:

(i) $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$ is a nonempty compact PCE-minimizing target set, and $\pi_{\mathrm{morph}}(A_{\mathrm{morph}})$ is the selected target morphology class.

(ii) For every open neighborhood $U\supset A_{\mathrm{morph}}$ there are constants $\Delta_U>0$ and $C_U<\infty$ such that
$$
\pi_\theta(X_{\mathrm{cell}}\setminus U)
\le
C_Ue^{-\Delta_U/\theta}
\tag{P.8.9a.7.3.5}
$$
for every $\theta>0$.

(iii) Every deterministic solution with initial state in $B$ satisfies
$$
\lim_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{dist}(x(t),A_{\mathrm{morph}})=0.
$$

*Proof.* Put $m=\inf_{x\in X_{\mathrm{cell}}}V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)$. The lower bound makes $m> -\infty$, and finiteness at one state makes $m<+\infty$. For $n\ge1$, let
$$
F_n=\left\{x\in X_{\mathrm{cell}}:V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)\le m+\frac1n\right\}.
$$
Each $F_n$ is nonempty by the definition of the infimum, closed by lower semicontinuity, and nested. Compactness gives $x_*\in\bigcap_{n\ge1}F_n$. Hence $V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x_*)\le m$, so $V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x_*)=m$. Thus $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$ is nonempty. It is the closed sublevel $\{V_{\mathrm{morph}}\le m\}$ of a compact space and is therefore compact. This proves (i).

For (ii), let $U$ be an open neighborhood of $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$. Choose a finite $\Delta_U^{(0)}>0$ such that
$$
V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)\ge V_{\min}+\Delta_U^{(0)}
\qquad (x\in X_{\mathrm{cell}}\setminus U).
$$
If the complement is empty, or the potential is $+\infty$ everywhere on it, any finite positive choice satisfies this inequality. Otherwise lower semicontinuity attains a finite minimum on the compact complement, and that minimum exceeds $V_{\min}$ because the complement contains no global minimizer. Its difference from $V_{\min}$ supplies the required choice. Since $dx(X_{\mathrm{cell}})<\infty$,
$$
\int_{X_{\mathrm{cell}}\setminus U}e^{-V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)/\theta}dx
\le dx(X_{\mathrm{cell}})e^{-(V_{\min}+\Delta_U^{(0)})/\theta}.
$$
Set $\varepsilon=\Delta_U^{(0)}/2$ and
$$
W_\varepsilon=\{x:V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x)\le V_{\min}+\varepsilon\}.
$$
Assumption 2 gives $dx(W_\varepsilon)>0$, and therefore
$$
0<
e^{-(V_{\min}+\varepsilon)/\theta}dx(W_\varepsilon)
\le Z_\theta
\le
e^{-V_{\min}/\theta}dx(X_{\mathrm{cell}})<\infty.
$$
Dividing the numerator bound by the lower bound for $Z_\theta$ yields
$$
\pi_\theta(X_{\mathrm{cell}}\setminus U)
\le
\frac{dx(X_{\mathrm{cell}})}{dx(W_\varepsilon)}
e^{-\Delta_U^{(0)}/(2\theta)}.
$$
Thus (P.8.9a.7.3.5) holds with $C_U=dx(X_{\mathrm{cell}})/dx(W_\varepsilon)$ and $\Delta_U=\Delta_U^{(0)}/2$.

For (iii), the chain rule and positive semidefiniteness give, along every solution in $B$,
$$
\frac{d}{dt}V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x(t))
=
-\nabla V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x(t))^TG(x(t))\nabla V_{\mathrm{morph}}(x(t))
\le0.
$$
The hypotheses of LaSalle's invariance principle (LaSalle 1960) are satisfied: the vector field is locally Lipschitz, $B$ is compact and positively invariant, solutions are forward complete, and $V_{\mathrm{morph}}\in C^1$ on $B$ with nonpositive orbital derivative. LaSalle's principle places the $\omega$-limit set of each solution in the largest invariant subset of the zero-derivative set, which is contained in $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$ by assumption 5. If the asserted distance did not tend to zero, there would be $\epsilon>0$ and times $t_n\to\infty$ with $\operatorname{dist}(x(t_n),A_{\mathrm{morph}})\ge\epsilon$. Compactness of $B$ would give a convergent subsequence with limit in the $\omega$-limit set and hence in $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$, contradicting continuity of the distance function. Therefore $\operatorname{dist}(x(t),A_{\mathrm{morph}})\to0$. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a7a1-no-local-template-requirement-on-the-certified-attractor-branch"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.7a.1 (No Local Template Requirement on the Certified Attractor Branch).** Assume all hypotheses of Theorem P.8.9a.7a. In particular, for stochastic concentration assume its finite reference measure and positive-volume sublevel conditions; for deterministic relaxation assume its $C^1$, local-Lipschitz, forward-complete, compact-positive-invariance, and LaSalle zero-set conditions. Then no additional localized register storing the final form is required. Perturbations remaining in the certified basin converge in distance to $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$; perturbations that alter gap-junction coupling, voltage-boundary conditions, or viability penalties can change $V_{\mathrm{morph}}$ and hence its minimizing set.

*Proof.* Operative Theorem P.8.9a.7a proves existence of the nonempty minimizing set and Gibbs concentration under its measure hypotheses. Under its deterministic hypotheses, LaSalle's invariance principle places every $\omega$-limit set in the largest invariant subset of the zero-dissipation set, which the theorem assumes is contained in $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$; therefore the distance to $A_{\mathrm{morph}}$ tends to zero. Neither argument introduces a variable that encodes a final morphology as a stored local template. Changing a registered coupling or penalty changes the potential and may consequently change its minimizing set. ∎

### P.8.9a.7.4 The Hierarchy of Biological Awareness

The following hierarchy is a research template: it pairs each candidate system with the independently measurable structure through which a CC test would proceed and with its current PU status.

**Table P.8.9a.4: Candidate Biological Systems for CC Tests**

| Candidate system | Independently measurable structure | PU status |
|------------------|------------------------------------|-----------|
| Single cell or cellular network | stimulus response and bioelectric coupling | candidate aggregate bridge |
| Neural circuit or brain region | task-scored prediction, control, and connectivity | candidate POP/context bridge |
| Integrated brain | behavioral and report-level integration measures | empirical integration data; not a CC certificate |

<a id="proposition-p89a5-admissible-graduated-cc-scaling-profile"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.5 (Admissible Graduated CC Scaling Profile).** On a Definition-31 scaling-model branch with independently selected $\alpha_\infty>0$, the representative $\mathcal G(x)=x/(1+x)$ is zero at threshold, increases monotonically for $x>0$, and approaches $1$ asymptotically. Hence the model CC approaches the supplied value $\alpha_\infty$. This algebraic profile neither selects $\alpha_\infty$, proves that a biological system realizes nonzero CC, nor explains phenomenal continuity; those require Theorem 34's realization package and separate empirical and interpretive bridges.

---

### P.8.9a.7.5 Self-Directed CTB and Contextual Physiological Bias

Placebo and nocebo effects motivate a candidate context-dependent physiological model on systems whose internal event channels are independently shown to be causally reachable. The interpolation below is a normalized model family. Estimating $\gamma_a(c)\mathrm{CC}(S)$ requires a likelihood whose calibration and selection dependencies are accounted for, an identified baseline and target direction, artifact controls, and evidence that ordinary conditioning and physiological pathways do not already exhaust the response. Open-label persistence is compatible with context engagement but does not identify the PU carrier or a nonzero CC contribution.

<a id="definition-p89a5b-internal-physiological-event-channel"></a>**Definition P.8.9a.5b (Internal Physiological Event Channel).** Let $S$ be a biological MPU aggregate with $C_{\mathrm{agg}}>C_{op}$. An internal physiological event channel of $S$ is a finite-outcome ND-RID event family
$$
a\in\mathcal A_S,\qquad \Omega_a=\{1,\dots,n_a\},
$$
whose outcome probabilities can be read at a coarse physiological level. Let
$$
p_a\in\Delta(\Omega_a)
$$
be the neutral baseline distribution of channel $a$ in the absence of the contextual intervention being tested.

<a id="definition-p89a5c-self-directed-ctb-channel"></a>**Definition P.8.9a.5c (Self-Directed CTB Channel).** Let $c$ be a context state of $S$, and suppose $c$ defines a target distribution
$$
q_a(c)\in\Delta(\Omega_a)
$$
for the internal channel $a$. Define the target contrast
$$
r_a(c):=\sup_{B\subseteq\Omega_a}|q_a(c,B)-p_a(B)|
=
\mathrm{TV}\bigl(q_a(c),p_a\bigr).
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.1}
$$
Let
$$
\gamma_a(c)\in[0,1]
$$
be the accessibility-fidelity coefficient of channel $a$ under context $c$, incorporating causal reach, context clarity, and the ability of the aggregate's organized state to couple to that channel. The self-directed CTB interpolation is admissible when
$$
\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S)\le r_a(c)
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.2}
$$
for nonzero $r_a(c)$. The observed internal distribution is then
$$
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c)
=
p_a
+
\frac{\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S)}{r_a(c)}
\bigl(q_a(c)-p_a\bigr),
\qquad r_a(c)>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.3}
$$
If $r_a(c)=0$ or $\gamma_a(c)=0$, set $p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c)=p_a$.

**Definition P.8.9a.5d (Placebo and Nocebo Context).**

A placebo context for channel $a$ is a finite intervention-context
$$
c_{\mathrm{pl}}
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.3a}
$$
such as an inert pill, clinical ritual, verbal report, expectation cue, conditioning signal, symbolic treatment frame, or practitioner interaction, satisfying:

1. $c_{\mathrm{pl}}$ has no direct active pharmacological or mechanical causal ingredient for channel $a$;
2. $c_{\mathrm{pl}}$ may nevertheless alter the physically instantiated context state of $S$:
$$
\mathrm{context}_S(t)\longrightarrow \mathrm{context}_S^{c_{\mathrm{pl}}}(t);
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.3b}
$$
3. the induced context enters Definition P.8.9a.5c through a target distribution $q_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})$ and accessibility-fidelity coefficient $\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})$.

A nocebo context is the same structure with an adverse or opposite target direction. Semantic content contributes to $c_{\mathrm{pl}}$ only through its physical instantiation in $\mathrm{context}_S(t)$.

<a id="theorem-p89a7b-self-directed-ctb-bound"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.7b (Self-Directed CTB Bound).** For every admissible self-directed CTB channel in Definition P.8.9a.5c:

(i) $p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c)$ is a normalized probability distribution.

(ii) For every event $B\subseteq\Omega_a$,
$$
\left|p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c,B)-p_a(B)\right|
\le
\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S).
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.4}
$$

(iii) If $\gamma_a(c)=0$, the context has no effect on channel $a$.

(iv) If $F_a:\Delta(\Omega_a)\to\mathbb R$ is $L_a$-Lipschitz in total variation, then
$$
\left|F_a(p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c))-F_a(p_a)\right|
\le
L_a\,\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S).
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.5}
$$

*Proof.* If $r_a(c)=0$ or $\gamma_a(c)=0$, the definition gives $p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c)=p_a$, so all claims are immediate. Assume $r_a(c)>0$ and define
$$
\eta_a(c):=\frac{\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S)}{r_a(c)}.
$$
By admissibility, $0\le\eta_a(c)\le1$. Equation (P.8.9a.7.5.3) becomes
$$
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c)=(1-\eta_a(c))p_a+\eta_a(c)q_a(c),
$$
a convex combination of two probability distributions. Hence it is normalized and nonnegative, proving (i).

For any $B\subseteq\Omega_a$,
$$
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c,B)-p_a(B)
=
\eta_a(c)\bigl(q_a(c,B)-p_a(B)\bigr).
$$
Taking absolute values and using the definition of $r_a(c)$,
$$
\left|p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c,B)-p_a(B)\right|
\le
\eta_a(c)r_a(c)
=
\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S),
$$
which proves (ii). Statement (iii) is the $\gamma_a(c)=0$ case already noted. For (iv), total variation gives
$$
\mathrm{TV}\bigl(p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c),p_a\bigr)
=
\sup_{B\subseteq\Omega_a}
\left|p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c,B)-p_a(B)\right|
\le
\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S).
$$
The Lipschitz condition then gives (P.8.9a.7.5.5). ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a7b1-coupling-dependent-specificity"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.7b.1 (Coupling-Dependent Specificity).** Within the admissible interpolation of Definition P.8.9a.5c, $\gamma_a(c)=0$ implies $p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c)=p_a$. For two channels with the same $\mathrm{CC}(S)>0$, nonzero target contrasts, and $0<\gamma_b(c)<\gamma_a(c)$, their maximal absolute event shifts have ratio $\gamma_a(c)/\gamma_b(c)$. A zero denominator has no such ratio.

*Proof.* For nonzero contrast, (P.8.9a.7.5.3) and the definition of $r_a(c)$ give $\mathrm{TV}(p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c),p_a)=\gamma_a(c)\mathrm{CC}(S)$. On a finite event space this total variation is the maximum absolute event shift. The positive common CC cancels in the ratio; the zero-coupling case follows directly from the definition. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a7b2-open-label-persistence"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.7b.2 (Open-Label Persistence).** Within the admissible self-directed CTB interpolation, explicit knowledge that a context has no direct pharmacological active ingredient does not force a shift to vanish. The full distribution shift vanishes exactly when $\mathrm{CC}(S)=0$, $\gamma_a(c)=0$, or $q_a(c)=p_a$. For an individual event, a zero target-event contrast is an additional zero-shift case.
If a disclosed context $c_{\mathrm{OL}}$ still satisfies
$$
\mathrm{CC}(S)>0,
\qquad
\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{OL}})>0,
\qquad
r_a(c_{\mathrm{OL}})>0,
$$
then the internal channel shift is nonzero for any event $B$ with
$$
q_a(c_{\mathrm{OL}},B)\ne p_a(B).
$$

*Proof.* By Definition P.8.9a.5c,
$$
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_{\mathrm{OL}},B)-p_a(B)
=
\frac{\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{OL}})\,\mathrm{CC}(S)}{r_a(c_{\mathrm{OL}})}
\bigl(q_a(c_{\mathrm{OL}},B)-p_a(B)\bigr).
$$
The right-hand side is nonzero exactly when $\mathrm{CC}(S)>0$, the accessibility-fidelity coefficient is nonzero, and the target contrast is nonzero for that event. No term in the expression requires propositional belief that the context contains a pharmacologically active ingredient. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a7b3-ritual-and-context-information-scaling"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.7b.3 (Ritual and Context-Information Scaling).** Suppose $\mathrm{CC}(S)>0$ and two admissible contexts $c_1,c_2$ have the same nonzero normalized target direction for channel $a$ and differ only in accessibility-fidelity coefficient, with
$$
0<\gamma_a(c_1)<\gamma_a(c_2).
$$
Their maximal absolute event shifts have ratio
$$
\frac{\gamma_a(c_2)}{\gamma_a(c_1)}.
$$

*Proof.* Equation (P.8.9a.7.5.3) gives $\mathrm{TV}(p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_i),p_a)=\gamma_a(c_i)\mathrm{CC}(S)$ for each nonzero target contrast. Total variation is attained by an event in the finite outcome space. Both shifts are positive, so division cancels the common CC and proves the ratio. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a7b4-nocebo-symmetry"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.7b.4 (Nocebo Symmetry).** Let $c_+$ and $c_-$ be two contexts for the same channel $a$ with equal accessibility-fidelity coefficient
$$
\gamma_a(c_+)=\gamma_a(c_-)
$$
and opposite target directions around the same baseline:
$$
q_a(c_+)-p_a=-(q_a(c_-)-p_a).
$$
Then
$$
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_+)-p_a
=
-\bigl(p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_-)-p_a\bigr).
$$

*Proof.* The target contrasts are equal, and the interpolation coefficients in (P.8.9a.7.5.3) are equal. Substituting the opposite target directions gives the sign reversal. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a7b5-context-channel-evidence-bound"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.7b.5 (Context-Channel Evidence Bound).** Let a placebo/nocebo dataset estimate an event shift $\widehat\Delta_a(B)$, with a justified artifact bound $B_{\mathrm{art}}$ satisfying the artifact controls of Definition 13.0a that apply to the evidence protocol. Suppose a statistical uncertainty certificate with valid coverage for the analysis and any data-dependent selection gives
$$
|\widehat\Delta_a(B)-\Delta_{\mathrm{tot}}(B)|\le B_{\mathrm{stat}}
$$
on the declared confidence event, and decompose the population shift as $\Delta_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta_{\mathrm{CTB}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{art}}$ with $|\Delta_{\mathrm{art}}|\le B_{\mathrm{art}}$. If the residual population effect is assigned to the admissible CTB channel, then, on that same confidence event,
$$
\gamma_a(c)\,\mathrm{CC}(S)
\ge
\max\{0,|\widehat\Delta_a(B)|-B_{\mathrm{art}}-B_{\mathrm{stat}}\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.6}
$$

*Proof.* The triangle inequality gives $|\Delta_{\mathrm{CTB}}|\ge\max\{0,|\widehat\Delta_a(B)|-B_{\mathrm{art}}-B_{\mathrm{stat}}\}$. Theorem P.8.9a.7b bounds the CTB event shift by $\gamma_a(c)\mathrm{CC}(S)$. Combining the inequalities proves the claim with the stated uncertainty coverage. ∎

**Corollary P.8.9a.7b.6 (Placebo and Nocebo as Bounded Context-Channel Effects).**

Let $c_{\mathrm{pl}}$ be a placebo or nocebo context for channel $a$ in the sense of Definition P.8.9a.5d. Then, for every event $B\subseteq\Omega_a$,
$$
\left|
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_{\mathrm{pl}},B)-p_a(B)
\right|
\le
\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})\mathrm{CC}(S).
\tag{P.8.9a.7.5.7}
$$
If $\mathrm{CC}(S)>0$, $r_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})>0$, $\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})>0$, and
$$
q_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}},B)\ne p_a(B),
$$
then the channel shift is nonzero on $B$. If $r_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})=0$, $\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})=0$, $\mathrm{CC}(S)=0$, or the event contrast vanishes, the context produces no shift on that event through the self-directed CTB channel.

*Proof.* This is Theorem P.8.9a.7b applied to the context $c_{\mathrm{pl}}$. When $r_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})>0$, Definition P.8.9a.5c gives
$$
p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_{\mathrm{pl}},B)-p_a(B)
=
\frac{\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})\mathrm{CC}(S)}{r_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})}
\bigl(q_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}},B)-p_a(B)\bigr).
$$
The right-hand side is nonzero exactly when $\mathrm{CC}(S)>0$, $\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})>0$, and the target event contrast is nonzero. If $r_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})=0$ or $\gamma_a(c_{\mathrm{pl}})=0$, Definition P.8.9a.5c sets $p_{a,\mathrm{obs}}(c_{\mathrm{pl}})=p_a$. If $\mathrm{CC}(S)=0$, the interpolation coefficient is zero, so the shift also vanishes. ∎

Within the stipulated interpolation, the upper bound scales with $\gamma_a(c)\mathrm{CC}(S)$ and disclosure need not set the model coefficient or target contrast to zero. This is an internal consequence of the definition; applying it to empirical placebo/nocebo effects requires the independently calibrated and artifact-controlled physical bridge stated above.

## P.8.9a.8 Connection to the Free Energy Principle

Friston's free energy principle (Friston 2010) proposes that biological systems minimize variational free energy. The PU framework reveals structural parallels between the two approaches.

### P.8.9a.8.1 Free Energy as an Inferential Restriction of PCE

<a id="theorem-p89a8-variational-free-energy-as-the-inferential-restriction-of-pce"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.8 (Variational Free Energy as the Inferential Restriction of PCE).** Fix a sensory-motor architecture and restrict the PCE potential
$$
V(x)=V_{op}(x)+V_{\mathrm{prop}}(x)-V_{\mathrm{benefit}}(x)+V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(x)
$$
to a branch on which only inferential state assignment varies and the propagation architecture and penalty contributions are constant. Let hidden states be $\theta$, observations be $o$, prior $p(\theta)$, likelihood $p(o\mid\theta)$, and recognition density $q(\theta)$, with densities taken relative to one registered reference measure. Require $q$ to give mass only where $p(\theta)p(o\mid\theta)>0$ and require $\ln(q/p)$ and $\ln p(o\mid\theta)$ to be $q$-integrable. Define the variable inferential restriction
$$
V^{\mathrm{inf}}_{\mathrm{PCE}}[q;o]
:=
D_{KL}\!\big[q(\theta)\,\|\,p(\theta)\big]
-\mathbb{E}_{q}\!\big[\ln p(o\mid \theta)\big].
$$
Then
$$
V^{\mathrm{inf}}_{\mathrm{PCE}}[q;o]
=
\mathbb{E}_{q}\!\big[\ln q(\theta)-\ln p(o,\theta)\big]
=
F[q;o].
$$
Hence, on the fixed-architecture inferential branch, the variable part of variational free-energy minimization is exactly PCE minimization.

*Proof.* Using $p(o,\theta)=p(o\mid\theta)p(\theta)$,
$$
\mathbb{E}_{q}[\ln q(\theta)-\ln p(o,\theta)]
=
\mathbb{E}_{q}[\ln q(\theta)-\ln p(\theta)-\ln p(o\mid\theta)]
=
D_{KL}[q\|p(\theta)]-\mathbb{E}_{q}[\ln p(o\mid\theta)].
$$
This is precisely $V^{\mathrm{inf}}_{\mathrm{PCE}}[q;o]$. Fixed propagation and penalty contributions add only constants on this restricted branch and therefore do not affect the minimizing $q$. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a81-thermodynamic-grounding-of-a-registered-inferential-reset"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.8.1 (Thermodynamic Grounding of a Registered Inferential Reset).** Let an implementation of the inferential branch contain a registered classical binary reset satisfying every hypothesis of Definition 28: the retained side record is unchanged, the register Hamiltonian is degenerate, the bath has temperature $T$, and cyclic isothermal control returns the register and controller Hamiltonians while retaining no additional copy of the erased record. Theorem 31 then gives $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}\ge H_q(P\mid R)$. If $H_q(P\mid R)\ge h_{\min}>0$, this heat floor is uniformly positive. An injective or reversibly uncomputed refinement need not incur this bound. Identifying the variational complexity $D_{KL}[q\|p]$ with a reset entropy or heat requires a separate quantitative implementation bridge.

*Remark: Scope of Exactness.* The equality above is an exact restricted-branch statement: it identifies the inferential subfunctional obtained after architecture, propagation, and penalty terms are fixed.

*Remark: Scope of Disagreement.* The equality above identifies a functional; it does not identify a global optimization problem. The full PCE objective is constrained by the registered Space of Becoming $\alpha<PP<\beta$ (Definition 8 and Axiom 3). Theorem 8 supplies the lower benchmark, Theorem 9 supplies the distinct excitation ceiling $\beta_0$, and Theorem 19 supplies the finite-complexity strict endpoint on its exact response-law branch. Theorems 10–11 exclude universal exact prediction on their diagonal classes but do not determine a system-independent scalar $\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$. Theorem 14's quantitative lower bound is available only on its registered reduction/cost certificate and transfers to $C_P$ only through the domination bridge.

Friston's variational free energy, taken as a local inferential objective, has no automatic identification with those PU branch constraints. For its posterior comparison, assume that the evidence $Z=p(o)=\int p(\theta)p(o\mid\theta)\,d\theta$ satisfies $0<Z<\infty$, with the integral taken against the registered reference measure. Put $q_*(\theta)=p(\theta)p(o\mid\theta)/Z$. For every recognition density admitted by Theorem P.8.9a.8,
$$
F[q;o]=D_{KL}[q\|q_*]-\ln Z\ge-\ln Z.
$$
This follows by substituting the definition of $q_*$; equality holds exactly when $q=q_*$ almost everywhere. If $q_*$ itself belongs to the admitted class, including its two integrability conditions, it attains the minimum $-\ln p(o)$ (Friston 2010). Otherwise this restricted problem need not attain that value. Any comparison with a perfect-prediction endpoint must separately identify the task, score, admissible class, and registered PU boundary. Standard active-inference formulations add prior preferences, expected free energy, and epistemic value (Friston et al. 2017); the equality of local functionals above does not make those policy terms identical to PU's branch certificates.

| Feature | Variational free-energy program | PCE / POP branch |
|:--------|:--------------------------------|:-----------------|
| Local inferential objective | $F[q;o]\ge-\ln p(o)$ on the finite-positive-evidence branch, with equality at an admitted exact posterior | $V^{\mathrm{inf}}_{\mathrm{PCE}}[q;o]$ on the constant-architecture equality branch |
| Registered lower benchmark | No PU-native value | $\alpha$ from Theorem 8 for the matched task and score |
| Excitation ceiling | No PU-native value | $\beta_0$ from Theorem 9 on its excitation-certificate branch |
| Response-law endpoint | No PU-native value | $\beta$ from Definition 8 and Theorem 19 on the exact response-law branch |
| Self-referential limitation | Not represented by the local functional | Class-level diagonal obstruction from Theorems 10–11; quantitative cost only under Theorem 14's certificate |
| Physical heat | Not fixed by the functional identity | Requires a separately registered reset and the hypotheses of Theorem 31 |

Thus the exact overlap is the restricted inferential functional. The global objectives, viability endpoints, diagonal classes, cost certificates, and physical ledgers remain distinct unless an explicit bridge identifies them.

<a id="remark-p89a81a-task-narrowing-and-a-registered-comparison"></a>**Remark P.8.9a.8.1a (Task Narrowing and a Registered Comparison).**

A registered task and score distinguish improved prediction from a change in what is being predicted. For a fixed evaluation task, a predictor earns a larger margin by improving its performance against the same benchmark. Restricting its observations or changing its training exposure earns credit through its performance on that evaluation task.

Comparisons across tasks require an additional rule. Write the performance and matched benchmark on task $T$ as $PP_T(S)$ and $\alpha_T$. For a registered task restriction $T\mapsto T'$ and its corresponding predictor transformation $S\mapsto S'$, immunity to improvement by restriction alone is the condition

$$
PP_{T'}(S')-\alpha_{T'}\le PP_T(S)-\alpha_T.
$$

One sufficient certificate is

$$
PP_{T'}(S')-PP_T(S)\le\alpha_{T'}-\alpha_T.
$$

Subtracting the benchmark change proves the margin inequality. A benchmark matched separately to each task makes the comparison explicit; the displayed certificate establishes its direction. A fixed evaluation task supplies a second route: task exposure may change while the score and benchmark used to assess improvement remain fixed.

The fixed-architecture inferential equality attributed to Theorem P.8.9a.8 can therefore coexist with a different architecture-selection objective. The architecture branch must specify its admissible comparisons, predictive score, and cost. The response law and the finite-complexity endpoint then determine the performance available at a given cost on that branch.
