#### 8.1 One sequence for stationarity, probe caps and resource moments

Here is an explicit common diagonal. Choose rational $h_{n}$ down to zero with $h_n\le h_1$, and choose $J_{n}$ so that $\sqrt{138}\,b(1-h_n)^{J_n}\le h_n^4$. Initialize at the floor and retain the state after $J_{n}$ updates. The rational-command precision can be chosen finer than $h_{n}^{3}$ if necessary so its total coupling error is $\le h_n^4$. These burn-in laws converge to $p_*$ and have the uniform (5/2)-moment bound (8a), with an arbitrarily small enlargement for rational commands. Hence their first and second moments converge to those of $p_*$.

For the tail proof put $R_n=l+h_n^{-1/4}$; this is only a proof partition, not a physical switch. Let $V_{n}$ be the deterministic maximum controller value over the $n$-th finite prefix and rational-command family. Choose the actual physical Poisson cap $M_{n}$ against $\Lambda_V=(V_n+d-l)/p$, at least

$$
M_n \ge \lceil 2e\Lambda_V + 8\log(1/h_n) \rceil,
$$

and increase it further until the $C^2$ bound in Section 8.2 passes. All controller states therefore use the same capped Poisson protocol; there is no discontinuity at $R_{n}$. A genuine overrun or random-table failure runs the two-base-unit probe only and marks the omitted extras. This always retains strict super-chance window performance, since the two-base completion probability is $1-(1-p)^2>0$.

For $\nu\le R_n$ the source-known Chernoff cap bound is at most $2^{-M_n}$ for sufficiently small $h_n$. On $\nu>R_n$ use the uniform (5/2)-moment bound: the probability is bounded by a constant times $R_n^{-5/2}$, and for $q_0=1,2$ the contribution of a $\nu^{q_0}$-growth active-resource observable is bounded by a constant times $R_n^{q_0-5/2}$. The capped $M$ is coupled below the full Poisson $M$ by replacing only overrun values by zero, so its first and second moments are dominated by those of the full probe. Installed maximum hardware and ROM capacity may be far larger than active usage and are separately charged as finite $n$-dependent baseline resources; no bounded-limit assertion applies to that installed inventory.

More precisely $\mathbb{E}[M|\nu]=\lambda(\nu)$ and $\mathbb{E}[M^{2}|\nu]=\lambda(\nu)^{2}+\lambda(\nu)$, where $\lambda(\nu)<(\nu+d-l)/p$. Thus both first and second copy-count moments converge along this same sequence. On the retained band, the discarded Poisson second moment is bounded by

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\Lambda_R^{2} \Pr[\operatorname{Pois}(\Lambda_R) \ge M_n - 1] \\
&\quad + \Lambda_R \Pr[\operatorname{Pois}(\Lambda_R) \ge M_n], \\
&\Lambda_R = (R_n + d - l)/p,
\end{aligned}
$$

by the Poisson factorial-moment identities, so it tends to zero with the chosen cap. The exact uncapped limiting moments are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_* K &= 2 + \int \lambda(\nu) p_*(\nu)\, d\nu, \\
\mathbb{E}_* K^{2} &= 4 + 5\int \lambda(\nu) p_*(\nu)\, d\nu \\
&\quad + \int \lambda(\nu)^{2} p_*(\nu)\, d\nu.
\end{aligned}
\tag{28}
$$

These are finite source-determined one-dimensional gamma-weighted integrals. The variable bank occupancy has $\mathbb{E}[N|\nu]=B_0\nu$ and $\mathbb{E}[N^{2}|\nu]=(B_0\nu)^{2}+\theta(1-\theta)$; full occupancy is $m_{\mathrm{bank}}=5+N$, so its moments are obtained by adding the displayed fixed five-cell baseline, so its first and second moments are controlled as well. Its bounded rounding variance is continuous as a function of $\nu$, including integer interfaces. For the limit,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}_* \nu &= (6b)\, \gamma(2,3)/\gamma(3,3), \\
\mathbb{E}_* \nu^{2} &= (6b)^{2}\, \gamma(1,3)/\gamma(3,3).
\end{aligned}
\tag{29}
$$

The state-dependent part of the expected completed total ledger is exactly $(P_0/2)\mathbb{E}_*(\nu-3b)^{2}$ plus the specified bounded performance term, with the constant ledger added separately. The padding alone also subtracts the baseline receipt and is not identified with that completed total. These finite state-dependent moments do not make the separate accelerated-source price or $L_{n}$ uniformly bounded.

All finite table-distribution errors, prepared-bit failures and cost-quantization errors are chosen after the finite deterministic maxima of the $n$-th experiment are known. If its maximum retained resource readout is $G_{n}$ and its maximum command count is $H_{n}$, choose the total failure/TV error $\le h_n^4/(1+G_n^{2}+H_n)$, and choose the work quantum so its cumulative error is $\le h_n^4$. Computability and finite caps make these choices finite and explicit. This prevents a vanishing response error from hiding an uncontrolled resource-moment error.

#### 8.2 C²-certified finite caps, tables and costs

This verifies finite PCE admission, including the increasing/convex physical-cost premise. Let $a=1-p$ and let the capped sampler replace $M>M_n$ by zero. Its failure-probability error relative to the ideal probe is

$$
\begin{aligned}
e(\lambda) &= a^{2} \mathbb{E}[g(M)], \\
g(m) &= 1_{m > M_n}(1 - a^{m}), \qquad M \sim \operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda).
\end{aligned}
$$

For any bounded $g$, termwise differentiation of the absolutely convergent Poisson series gives $d\,\mathbb{E}[g(M)]/d\lambda=\mathbb{E}[g(M+1)-g(M)]$ and the corresponding second difference for the second derivative. The supports of $g$, $\Delta g$ and $\Delta^{2}g$ are respectively $m\ge M_n+1$, $m\ge M_n$ and $m\ge M_n-1$, and their absolute bounds are 1,2,4. Hence, uniformly for $0\le\lambda\le\Lambda_V$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&|e| \le T_n, \quad |e_\lambda'| \le 2T_n, \quad |e_\lambda''| \le 4T_n, \\
&T_n = \Pr[\operatorname{Poisson}(\Lambda_V) \ge M_n - 1].
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
$$

Here $a^{2}\le 1$ has only enlarged the bounds. Since $\lambda'=\beta/(pP)\le L_1=\beta/(p\alpha)$ and $|\lambda''|\le L_2=\beta(\beta-\alpha)/(p\alpha^{2})$, its $\nu$ derivatives obey

$$
\begin{aligned}
|e_\nu'| &\le 2L_1 T_n, \\
|e_\nu''| &\le (4L_1^{2} + 2L_2)T_n.
\end{aligned}
\tag{31}
$$

The loss perturbation is $\Delta$ e. If E denotes the ideal mean loss, source-known bounds are

$$
\begin{aligned}
|E'| &\le E_1 = \Delta\beta/\alpha, \\
|E''| &\le E_2 = \Delta[(\beta/\alpha)^{2} + \beta(\beta - \alpha)/\alpha^{2}].
\end{aligned}
$$

Put $\delta_0=\Delta T_n$, $\delta_1=2\Delta L_1 T_n$, $\delta_2=\Delta(4L_1^{2}+2L_2)T_n$, and increase $M_{n}$ until $\delta_1\le 1$. For $P_{\mathrm{cap}}=1/(1+E+\Delta e)$, elementary differentiation, with every denominator $\ge 1$, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
|P_{\mathrm{cap}} - P| &\le \delta_0, \\
|P_{\mathrm{cap}}' - P'| &\le \delta_1 + 2E_1\delta_0, \\
|P_{\mathrm{cap}}'' - P''| &\le \delta_2 + (4E_1 + 2)\delta_1 \\
&\quad + (6E_1^{2} + 2E_2)\delta_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{32}
$$

All bounds tend to zero with the cap and are evaluated from source constants alone. Choose the cap until the last two are below

$$
\begin{aligned}
\epsilon_n = \min[{}&h_n^{4}, P_0(g - b)/(16\Gamma_0), \\
&P_0(1 - g)/(16\Gamma_0)].
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $T_{\mathrm{cap}}=\Gamma_0 P_{\mathrm{cap}}+(P_0/2)(\nu-3b)^2+L$, after subtraction of the same $R_{I}$, retains strict positive slope and curvature throughout the finite comparison interval $[l,V_n]$. The exact gradient cancellation continues to hold with $\mathrm{PP}_{\mathrm{cap}}$ on both sides of the cost completion.

For finite sampling tables and energy quanta, the reachable rational allocation grid is finite and computable. Let $\rho$ be $\min(1,\text{one third of its smallest positive spacing})$; a singleton grid can use $\rho=1$. The compactly supported $C^2$ function $\phi(u)=(1-u^{2})^3$ for $|u|\le 1$ and zero otherwise has $\phi(0)=1$, $\phi'(0)=0$ and a uniform bound 72 on its value and first two derivatives. Center disjoint translates $\phi((\nu-v)/\rho)$ at the distinct grid points $v$. If actual finite-table score values differ from $P_{\mathrm{cap}}(v)$ by at most $\delta$, adding those errors times the translates gives a $C^2$ interpolation through the actual values with value/first/second derivative errors at most $72\delta/\rho^{2}$. Its derivative at every grid point remains $P_{\mathrm{cap}}'(v)$, because $\phi'(0)=0$ and the supports are disjoint. The same construction applies to quantum-rounded cost values.

Choose table TV error and work quantum small enough that these $C^2$ errors, after their known score/cost conversion factors, are below $\epsilon_{n}$ and below one quarter of the remaining positive slope/curvature margins. The grid, its spacing, the source loss bound $\ln 4$ and finite cost maxima are all known before choosing the precision, so this is a finite constructive choice. The physical cost values are the common-node billed battery/resource values from Section 6, not independently rounded statewise padding values; the interpolation is exact on every physically reached state, increasing and strictly convex, and has the registered force at each grid point. Any remaining rational arithmetic error in that force is included in Section 7's update-error bound. The same source probability/error bounds also satisfy Section 8.1's resource-weighted failure budget by taking the smaller tolerance.

This closes the derivative gap left by value-only approximations: no unproved convexity of an arbitrary interpolant is assumed.

#### 8.3 Constructive precision order without a hidden sizing loop

First fix $h_n$, $J_n$ and the rational controller-command precision; this fixes the finite allocation grid, its minimum spacing, deterministic state maximum and probe cap. Choose a padding/reflexive energy quantum $q_{n}$ small enough for the $C^2$ margin and the cumulative quantization bound; the number of those billing transfers is fixed by $J_{n}$, not by later sampling precision. All fixed primitive prices can be represented on a common refinement of that quantum. These choices are held fixed in the following inner search.

Increase the probability-table precision $u$. On the fixed grid/cap, dyadic tables and their generation have polynomial space/gate bounds in $u$ (the finite set of computable exp/log/source constants is fixed). They use $O(u)$ bits per sampled row. Choose $O(u)$ R14 extractor attempts per bit, so the total source count and controller hardware are polynomial in $u$, while total table/extraction error is bounded by a fixed polynomial times $2^{-u}$. The constants may depend on this $n$-th experiment, but not on $u$.

For each u choose the least dyadic L passing the reservoir inequality, now including that precision's preparation/maintenance overhead. Since those overheads are polynomial in u and polynomial in log L, a polynomially large trial L in u passes; hence the least dyadic L, actual energy/resource-credit maxima and gate/cell/time counts are polynomially bounded in u. Resource values here use the fixed original energy/credit/time units, not the integer label Q obtained by dividing the same energy by a smaller quantum. All raw token counts remain recorded with their conversion $q_{n}$.

Therefore the weighted error test in Section 8.1 and the $C^2$ table test in Section 8.2 eventually pass: exponentially decaying probability error dominates every such fixed polynomial resource weight. Search $u$ until both pass and keep that complete finite record. This jointly determines precision, extraction supplies, reservoir size and resource maxima without assuming that precision-dependent hardware had already been fixed. It also prevents changing the allocation grid while estimating its nodal spacing.

There are three distinct limits, each with its own proof:

1. finite-prefix burn-in approaches $\pi_{h}$ with the explicit bound (7);
2. $h\to 0$ gives the reflected process and $\pi_h\to p_*$ by the reflected-process and stationary-limit claims;
3. finite randomization/state/probe caps and rational-command errors vanish with their displayed bounds.

They are not interchanged without control. A diagonal family chooses h first, then a burn-in satisfying (7), then finite approximation bounds tending to zero. Every member is finite; the limiting record is the exact diffusion and its response law. The invariant-law failure of the earlier copy-count chain is not used or hidden in this construction.

### P.8.9a.11.3 Scope, Epistemic Status, and Falsifiability

<a id="corollary-p89a117-unified-pce-signature-across-domains"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.11.7 (Unified PCE Signature Across Domains).** Any domain populated by adaptive predictive aggregates whose internal optimization is governed by PCE and whose near-equilibrium stochastic adaptation satisfies Hypothesis P.8.9a.11.4 exhibits the following signatures:

1. within each aggregate, value is concentrated disproportionately in a smaller fraction of the operational range (Theorem P.8.9a.11.2);
2. across aggregates, the stationary distribution of complexity excess has a Pareto upper tail with index $\zeta=1+2k/\sigma^2$ (Theorem P.8.9a.11.5);
3. across scale families with common shape $\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}>2$ and common scaled floor $a_{\min}$, the variance-mean relation has Taylor exponent $b=2$ (Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a);
4. in the small-noise regime with the interior-equilibrium separation required by Proposition P.8.9a.11.6, the local inequality scale is controlled by $\sigma^2/k$ through the lognormal approximation.

*Proof.* Theorem P.8.9a.11.2 proves item 1 for the within-aggregate operational-range profile. Hypothesis P.8.9a.11.4 supplies the near-equilibrium multiplicative stochastic dynamics required by Theorem P.8.9a.11.5; that theorem then gives the stationary Pareto tail and index $\zeta=1+2k/\sigma^2$, proving item 2. Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a computes $\operatorname{Var}(\nu)=(B_2/B_1^2)\mathbb E[\nu]^2$ at constant shape and scaled floor, proving item 3 with exponent $b=2$. Proposition P.8.9a.11.6 gives the local small-noise log-variance $\sigma^2/(2k)+O(\sigma^4/k^2)$ and the resulting Gini approximation, proving item 4. Each conclusion therefore has exactly the hypotheses stated in the corollary. ∎

<a id="remark-p89a112-universal-pattern-boundary"></a>**Remark P.8.9a.11.2 (Universal-Pattern Boundary).** The Pareto section supplies a common stationary heavy-tail mechanism under Hypothesis P.8.9a.11.4 and the exact fixed-shape variance-mean consequence of Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a. Other empirical signatures require additional domain hypotheses:

1. Proposition P.2.6.3d.2 gives an independent conditional Gibbs-log-cost route to Zipf-Mandelbrot statistics. Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 supplies a different route to Pareto tails through multiplicative adaptation. The two are compatible but neither eliminates the extra hypotheses of the other.
2. Approximate $1/f$ spectra arise in mixtures of uncorrelated exponential relaxation modes when the fluctuation-weighted relaxation-rate measure is approximately flat per logarithmic interval over a range sufficiently wider than the observed frequency window (Dutta and Horn 1981). This is a scale-mixture hypothesis, not a consequence of Equation (P.8.9a.11.1) by itself.
3. KWW/stretched-exponential or Mittag-Leffler relaxation requires an additional broad waiting-time, empirical KWW response kernel, or stable-subordination kernel (Scher and Montroll 1975; Williams and Watts 1970). Multiplicative PCE adaptation can motivate looking for such kernels, but does not fix them without a domain model.
4. Benford first-digit statistics follow from approximate equidistribution of logarithmic mantissas or scale-invariant sampling (Benford 1938). PCE scale invariance is relevant only after the mantissa-equidistribution condition is checked.
5. Biological distribution-network explanations of Kleiber-type metabolic scaling require additional model hypotheses. Under the space-filling, size-invariant terminal-unit, and transport-energy minimization assumptions of the cited branching-network model in three spatial dimensions, the model predicts $B\propto M^{3/4}$ (Kleiber 1932; West, Brown and Enquist 1997). PU supplies the $D_{\mathrm{space}}=3$ geometric background on the $D=4$ branch, but the biological network assumptions remain additional empirical structure rather than consequences of POP/PCE alone.
6. Criticality, avalanche exponents, and self-organized critical signatures require an additional mechanism placing the relevant system near a critical fixed point or critical manifold (Wilson 1971). PCE can supply an optimization pressure toward high-susceptibility operating points, but it does not by itself fix critical exponents or prove that a domain is tuned to criticality.
7. Log-periodic corrections require discrete scale invariance or complex scaling dimensions (Sornette 1998). Continuous PCE scale compression and the multiplicative population diffusion above do not by themselves introduce a preferred discrete scale ratio, so log-periodic modulation remains an additional domain hypothesis.

<a id="corollary-p89a118-tier-4-biological-fractal-status-boundary"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.11.8 (Tier-4 Biological-Fractal Status Boundary).** Biological fractal and allometric signatures are domain-model consequences only after a concrete biological transport or branching package is appended. Such a package must specify the network geometry, terminal-unit assumptions, dissipation functional, and empirical bridge from predictive complexity to biological throughput. Under those added hypotheses, PCE may act as the optimizing pressure over the biological network objective, but neither the fractal dimension nor the Kleiber exponent is fixed by POP/PCE alone.

*Proof.* Item 5 of Remark P.8.9a.11.2 isolates the biological distribution-network assumptions needed for Kleiber-type scaling and fractal-network signatures. Theorems P.8.9a.11.2 and P.8.9a.11.5 establish only the Law-of-Prediction concentration effect and the conditional multiplicative-noise Pareto tail. They contain no biological branching geometry, terminal-invariance condition, or metabolic transport law. Therefore any biological-fractal conclusion requires the stated domain package as an additional status-carrying input. ∎

**Epistemic Status.** Theorem P.8.9a.11.2 is an internal consequence of the Law of Prediction (Theorem 19). Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 is conditional on the Multiplicative PCE Noise Hypothesis, which is a modeling assumption about population-level fluctuations. Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a is an exact consequence of that stationary family under the fixed-shape and scaled-floor hypotheses. Proposition P.8.9a.11.6 is a local small-noise approximation.

**Falsification Conditions.** The PCE concentration signature admits the following tests:

1. *Within-system disproportion:* In a domain where the Law of Prediction's exponential saturation curve has been independently established, a stable equilibrium value-versus-effort curve violating $\rho(f;x^*)>f$ for some $f\in(0,1)$ contradicts Theorem P.8.9a.11.2.
2. *Tail index structure:* In a population where the effective mean-reversion rate $k$ and multiplicative noise amplitude $\sigma$ can be estimated, the measured upper-tail index should satisfy $\zeta=1+2k/\sigma^2$ within uncertainty if Hypothesis P.8.9a.11.4 applies.
3. *Fixed-shape Taylor scaling:* In a compared scale family satisfying the fixed-shape and scaled-floor hypotheses of Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a, the variance-mean exponent should be $b=2$ within uncertainty.
4. *Small-noise inequality scale:* In a small-noise population satisfying Hypothesis P.8.9a.11.4 and the interior-equilibrium separation of Proposition P.8.9a.11.6, the local lognormal Gini approximation obeys Equation (P.8.9a.11.6). A comparison with the full reflected stationary law also requires a quantitative approximation-error certificate.

These predictions distinguish the PCE-based account from purely phenomenological power-law fits by tying the tail index to adaptation-rate parameters that are independently measurable in principle.

**Relation to Holographic Saturation.** Both results are conditional optimization models. Theorem E.8.3.4 reaches boundary-utilization saturation only on its positive idle-cost, additive-utilization, monotone-benefit, and projected deterministic-dynamics branch; Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 yields a heavy tail only under multiplicative adaptation noise. Their shared concentration language is an analogy.

**Relation to Existing Theory.** The PU derivation recovers the structural form of Kesten-type multiplicative processes in the population model and the single-system concentration effect directly from exponential PCE saturation. Gibrat-style proportional fluctuations appear as the small-noise logarithmic approximation, Taylor's variance-mean law appears conditionally through Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a, and the Zipf-Mandelbrot template remains the separate Gibbs-log-cost route of Proposition P.2.6.3d.2. Preferential attachment, $1/f$ mixtures, KWW/stretched relaxations, Benford mantissas, criticality, log-periodic modulation, and Kleiber/fractal biological scaling are therefore related external mechanisms or conditional domain models rather than prerequisites for the PU Pareto derivation. Section P.8.9a.12 states the scale-pattern cases as dedicated conditional theorems by making each required domain hypothesis explicit.

## P.8.9a.12 Conditional Universal Patterns from PCE Scale Geometry

The preceding section separates the internal Pareto concentration theorem from population-level and domain-level hypotheses. This subsection records the corresponding conditional universal-pattern theorems. In each case PU supplies the shared PCE scale language, while the theorem states the additional cost, rank, phase, relaxation, discrete-scale, or biological-network condition needed for the named empirical pattern.

**Headline antecedent display.** Throughout this subsection, every named scale-pattern theorem has the structural form
$$
\mathrm{POP}\,\land\,\mathrm{PCE}
\,\land\,\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pattern}}
\;\Longrightarrow\;
\text{named scale pattern},
$$
where $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pattern}}$ is the explicit domain hypothesis named in each theorem: logarithmic ranked PCE cost (Zipf–Mandelbrot), multiplicative adaptation noise (Pareto), log-flat relaxation-rate measure ($1/f$), broad waiting-time or stable-subordination kernel (KWW), mantissa-equidistribution (Benford), discrete scale invariance (log-periodic), terminal-invariant space-filling biological transport (Kleiber), self-similar branching cascade with non-overlap (multifractal), or fixed-shape inverse-gamma family (Taylor). Removing $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{pattern}}$ from any of these antecedents removes the named conclusion. The conditional universal-pattern template is the precise discipline by which the framework relates to the empirical scaling literature without absorbing its named domain assumptions into POP/PCE.

**Definition P.8.9a.12.0c (Criticality-Tuning Certificate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}$).** A criticality-tuning certificate for a retained domain is a finite record with an outcome-independent specification
$$
\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}
=
(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{dom}},PP_{\mathrm{dom}},\theta_{\mathrm{ctrl}},\chi_{\mathrm{sus}},\mathcal M_{\mathrm{crit}},d_{\mathrm{crit}},\epsilon_{\mathrm{crit}},\mathcal U_{\mathrm{class}},\mathcal R_{\mathrm{FS}},\text{outcome-independence record}),
$$
where $\mathcal X_{\mathrm{dom}}$ is the retained domain state family, $PP_{\mathrm{dom}}$ is the predictive-performance observable, $\theta_{\mathrm{ctrl}}$ is the control coordinate, $\chi_{\mathrm{sus}}$ is the susceptibility or response-variance observable, $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the claimed critical manifold or fixed point, $d_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the distance-to-criticality functional defined on the declared domain, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the accepted residual window, $\mathcal U_{\mathrm{class}}$ records the universality-class data if critical exponents are claimed, and $\mathcal R_{\mathrm{FS}}$ records finite-size scaling, avalanche-window, or correlation-length tests. The domain, distance, and tolerance must have stated sources independent of the outcomes used to check them. The certificate supplies a domain-relative, finite-window claim beyond the viability band $\alpha<PP<\beta$.

**Proposition P.8.9a.12.0d (Marginal Predictability is Certificate-Gated Criticality).** POP, PCE, and Operational Viability alone do not prove that a domain is tuned to a critical point. If $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is accepted, then the domain may be reported as marginally predictable at the recorded resolution in the precise sense
$$
d_{\mathrm{crit}}(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{dom}},\mathcal M_{\mathrm{crit}})
\le
\epsilon_{\mathrm{crit}},
$$
and any scale-free exponents or avalanche laws inherit the universality-class and finite-size-scaling entries of the same certificate. Without $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}$, the correct PU statement is only that PCE can create pressure toward high-susceptibility operating points; it does not derive cosmological self-organized criticality, critical exponents, or edge-of-chaos tuning.

*Proof.* Remark P.8.9a.11.2 already separates criticality from the internal PCE Pareto and concentration theorems. A finite PCE optimization problem can have an isolated stable minimizer with finite susceptibility, so POP/PCE do not imply a divergent correlation length or a critical manifold. The additional entries of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}$ are exactly the missing data: a control coordinate, a distance-to-criticality functional, finite-size scaling, and a universality-class record when exponents are claimed. The displayed inequality is then the direct content of the accepted finite record. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a120e-populated-branching-entries-of-mathfrak-c_mathrmcrit"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.0e (Populated Branching Entries of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}$).** Register the formal state family $\mathcal X_{\mathrm{dom}}=\{\mathrm{GW}_\theta:\theta>0\}$ of Galton--Watson branching processes with one ancestor and Poisson offspring of mean $\theta$, the control coordinate $\theta_{\mathrm{ctrl}}=\theta$, the avalanche size $S$ (total progeny), the susceptibility $\chi_{\mathrm{sus}}(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta S$, the critical manifold $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{crit}}=\{\theta=1\}$ and the distance $d_{\mathrm{crit}}(\theta)=|\theta-1|$. Then:

1. $\chi_{\mathrm{sus}}(\theta)=1/(1-\theta)$ for $\theta<1$, and $\chi_{\mathrm{sus}}(\theta)=\infty$ for $\theta\ge1$.
2. For every $\theta>0$ and every integer $s\ge1$,
$$
\mathbb P_\theta(S=s)=\frac{e^{-\theta s}(\theta s)^{s-1}}{s!}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0e.1}
$$
3. *Finite-size scaling.* With $s_\xi(\theta):=1/(\theta-1-\ln\theta)$ for $\theta\ne1$,
$$
\mathbb P_\theta(S=s)=\theta^{-1}e^{-s/s_\xi(\theta)}\,\mathbb P_1(S=s),
\qquad
\lim_{\theta\to1}(\theta-1)^2s_\xi(\theta)=2.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0e.2}
$$
4. *Critical window.* For every integer $s\ge1$,
$$
\frac{e^{-1/(12s)}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,s^{3/2}}
<
\mathbb P_1(S=s)
<
\frac{e^{-1/(12s+1)}}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,s^{3/2}}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0e.3}
$$

Consequently the universality-class and finite-size-scaling entries of $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{crit}}$ on this family are the mean-field branching exponents $\tau_S=3/2$ for the avalanche-size law, $\gamma=1$ for $\chi_{\mathrm{sus}}=d_{\mathrm{crit}}^{-1}$ on $\theta<1$, and $1/\sigma=2$ for the cutoff $s_\xi\sim2d_{\mathrm{crit}}^{-2}$, each with the exact finite-window form above. The distance bound of Proposition P.8.9a.12.0d holds at $\theta$ exactly when $|\theta-1|\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{crit}}$. For every $\theta\ne1$ the finite-avalanche mass function (P.8.9a.12.0e.1) has the exponential cutoff $e^{-s/s_\xi(\theta)}$, and every member with $\theta<1$ has finite susceptibility. For $\theta\le1$ the finite sizes carry total mass $1$. For $\theta>1$ the size law also has the atom $\mathbb P_\theta(S=\infty)=1-\eta_\theta>0$, where $\eta_\theta\in(0,1)$ is the root of $\eta=e^{\theta(\eta-1)}$, and (P.8.9a.12.0e.1) sums to $\eta_\theta$ over $s\ge1$.

*Proof.* For item 1, the generation sizes satisfy $\mathbb EZ_{g+1}=\theta\,\mathbb EZ_g$ and $Z_0=1$, so $\mathbb EZ_g=\theta^g$; monotone convergence gives $\mathbb ES=\sum_g\theta^g$. For item 2, explore the tree depth first and let $\xi_i$ be the offspring number of the $i$-th explored individual; the $\xi_i$ are independent Poisson variables with mean $\theta$, the number of discovered but unexplored individuals after $i$ steps is $1+\sum_{l\le i}(\xi_l-1)$, and $S$ is the first $i$ at which this number vanishes. For integers $y_1,\ldots,y_s\ge-1$ with sum $-1$ and partial sums $\Sigma_k=y_1+\cdots+y_k$ ($1\le k\le s$), the rotation $(y_{j+1},\ldots,y_s,y_1,\ldots,y_j)$ with $1\le j\le s$ has all proper partial sums nonnegative exactly when $\Sigma_j<\Sigma_k$ for $k<j$ and $\Sigma_j\le\Sigma_k$ for $k>j$, that is, when $j$ is the first index at which $\min_k\Sigma_k$ is attained; hence exactly one rotation qualifies. The event $\{S=s\}$ is the event that $\sum_{l\le s}(\xi_l-1)=-1$ and the unrotated sequence ($j=s$) qualifies. Since the law of $(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_s)$ is invariant under rotation, averaging over the $s$ rotations gives
$$
\mathbb P_\theta(S=s)=\frac1s\,\mathbb P\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^s\xi_l=s-1\Bigr)=\frac1s\,e^{-\theta s}\frac{(\theta s)^{s-1}}{(s-1)!},
$$
which is (P.8.9a.12.0e.1). Item 3 follows by dividing (P.8.9a.12.0e.1) at $\theta$ by its value at $1$, which gives $\theta^{s-1}e^{-(\theta-1)s}=\theta^{-1}e^{-s(\theta-1-\ln\theta)}$, and from $\theta-1-\ln\theta=(\theta-1)^2/2+O(|\theta-1|^3)$. Item 4 follows from Robbins' bounds $\sqrt{2\pi}\,s^{s+1/2}e^{-s}e^{1/(12s+1)}<s!<\sqrt{2\pi}\,s^{s+1/2}e^{-s}e^{1/(12s)}$ applied to $\mathbb P_1(S=s)=e^{-s}s^{s-1}/s!$. The exponents follow from items 1, 3 and 4. The extinction probability $\mathbb P_\theta(S<\infty)$ is the smallest fixed point in $[0,1]$ of the offspring generating function $f_\theta(\eta)=e^{\theta(\eta-1)}$. Since $f_\theta$ is strictly convex with $f_\theta(0)>0$, $f_\theta(1)=1$ and $f_\theta'(1)=\theta$, that fixed point is $1$ for $\theta\le1$ and is the unique root $\eta_\theta\in(0,1)$ for $\theta>1$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a120f-predictive-selection-and-locked-critical-windows-for-a-branching-source"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.0f (Predictive Selection and Locked Critical Windows for a Branching Source).** Fix integers $K\ge M\ge3$. Register the control grid $\theta_j=j/M$, $1\le j\le M-1$, a fair hidden root bit $Z$, and an independent Poisson Galton–Watson source of mean $\theta_j$. Explore its ordered tree for at most $K$ nodes. Each active node supplies a fresh binary symmetric observation $Y_i=Z\oplus E_i$, with independent $\Pr(E_i=1)=1/4$. Offspring, root and noise sources are mutually independent. The predictor port receives the active count $n=\min(S,K)$ and its ordered noisy prefix; raw noise bits, the root, inactive observations and source workspace remain outside that port. After a forecast commits, a separate verifier releases the retained root and the actual squared score. All source/task data and the residual window $\epsilon_{\rm crit}=2/M$ are fixed before source outcomes.

Let
$$
 D_K=\prod_{n=1}^K\prod_{k=0}^n(3^k+3^{n-k}),\qquad
 \mathcal H_K=\{(n,y):1\le n\le K,\ y\in\{0,1\}^n\},\qquad
 L_K=|\mathcal H_K|=2^{K+1}-2.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.1}
$$
The full finite forecast class consists of all tables $F:\mathcal H_K\to\{0,1/D_K,\ldots,1\}$. Its proper task loss is $L_F=(F(n,Y)-Z)^2$, its window risk is $R(F)=\mathbb E L_F$, and its window performance is
$$
 PP_{\rm dom}=\frac1{1+R(F)}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.2}
$$
This is the $k_{PP}=1$ calibration of Definition 7 and Theorem 8 applied to expected proper loss. It is distinct from averaging the eventwise transform $1/(1+L_F)$. The physical class uses the exact finite source and the separately typed digital source below, with one fixed padded source/controller/lookup schedule in each class. Then:

1. **Complete predictor comparison and strict control selection.** For every supported history with $n$ observations and $k$ ones, the posterior and unique optimal table are
$$
 p_{n,k}=\frac{3^k}{3^k+3^{n-k}},\qquad F_*(n,y)=p_{n,\sum_i y_i}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.3}
$$
Every value is in the registered grid. The exact Bayes risk for $n$ observations is
$$
 R_n=\frac{3^n}{2\,4^n}\sum_{k=0}^n\frac{\binom nk}{3^k+3^{n-k}},\qquad
 R_1=\frac3{16},\quad R_2=\frac3{20},\quad R_n>R_{n+1}>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.4}
$$
Tree information, being independent of $Z$ and the noises, leaves this posterior unchanged. For any admitted table and either offspring law below,
$$
 R(F)=\mathbb E R_n+\mathbb E[(F(n,Y)-p_{n,\sum Y_i})^2].
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.5}
$$
Thus the complete table comparison selects $F_*$ on every supported history.

For the exact Poisson source put $R_j^P=\mathbb E_{\theta_j}R_{\min(S,K)}$ and $j_*=M-1$. Then, for every $j<j_*$,
$$
 R_j^P-R_{j_*}^P
 \ge\frac3{80}(e^{-\theta_j}-e^{-\theta_{j_*}}) >\frac1{80M}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.6}
$$
The complete control/table census therefore selects $(j_*,F_*)$, with $\theta_*=1-1/M$. The source task supplies the tuning pressure: its selected performance is greater than the matched constant-half predictor's $4/5$. Its critical distance is determined separately below, rather than inferred from this performance inequality.

2. **Exact finite Poisson-family realization.** For any $\theta>0$ and source interval $\tau_B>0$, take a $(K+1)$-level register with basis $|0\rangle,\ldots,|K\rangle$, initially $|0\rangle$. Its driven finite Markov source has jump operators
$$
 J_l=\sqrt{\theta/\tau_B}\,|l+1\rangle\langle l|\quad(0\le l<K),\qquad
 \mathcal L_\theta(\rho)=\sum_{l=0}^{K-1}\left[J_l\rho J_l^\dagger-\tfrac12\{J_l^\dagger J_l,\rho\}\right]
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.7}
$$
in its registered interaction picture. In an allocated $\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil$-bit register, embed these levels as codes $0,\ldots,K$ and extend all jumps and the ladder energy by zero on unused basis codes. The exact channel $e^{\tau_B\mathcal L_\theta}$ has the diagonal output law
$$
 p_l(\theta)=e^{-\theta}\theta^l/l!\quad(0\le l<K),\qquad
 p_K(\theta)=1-\sum_{l<K}p_l(\theta).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.8}
$$
The last symbol means at least $K$ Poisson offspring. Thus the source derives its probabilities from a specified finite generator, interval and initial state.

Each trial prepares a full bank of $m_B=K(M-1)$ independent source registers: $K$ at every grid rate, including unselected controls. Only the selected row feeds the queue. Starting at $Q_0=1$, slot $i$ is active if $Q_{i-1}>0$; at an active slot use its source symbol $C_i$ and set $Q_i=Q_{i-1}-1+C_i$, otherwise keep $Q_i=0$. The queue never exceeds $1+K(K-1)$. It produces the exact count $n=\min(S,K)$, active noisy prefix and final survivor flag $\mathbf1_{\{S>K\}}=\mathbf1_{\{Q_K>0\}}$. All $K$ noise pairs and every source-bank entry are generated on the same fixed schedule, including inactive slots. The predictor receives only its declared port. The complete source/queue/task records are retained and released after forecast commitment.

Censoring source symbols and tree exploration from a larger cutoff to a smaller one gives the corresponding smaller-window laws. Equivalently, independent unbounded Poisson offspring couple all these finite instruments. Their compatible finite-cylinder responses realize the family of Theorem P.8.9a.12.0e, including its finite-size and survival records. At each physical resolution the carrier and experiment remain finite.

3. **An exact fair-bit digital implementation and robust selection.** Put
$$
 \ell_M=\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil,\qquad \ell_K=\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil,\qquad
 b=16+(K+1)\ell_M+(K+2)\ell_K,\qquad J=2b+5.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.9}
$$
For each grid control compute the rational odd Taylor sum
$$
 L_j=\sum_{a=0}^{J}\frac{(-\theta_j)^a}{a!},\qquad
 n_{j,l}=\left\lfloor2^bL_j\frac{\theta_j^l}{l!}\right\rfloor\ (l<K),\qquad
 n_{j,K}=2^b-\sum_{l<K}n_{j,l},\qquad q_{j,l}=n_{j,l}/2^b.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.10}
$$
All counts are positive integers, and each row sums to $2^b$. A fresh $b$-bit integer and the cumulative counts sample this categorical law exactly. Prepare every row's $K$ draws, as in the exact bank. The queue now realizes the $K$-window of an actual bounded-offspring Galton–Watson law $q_j$; its last offspring value means exactly $K$ children. It is not relabeled as a Poisson offspring variable.

The full banks and every common decoded tree/task response have
$$
 d_{\rm TV}(P_j^P,P_j^D)\le\delta_B:=2(M-1)K^2 2^{-b}<\frac1{500M}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.11}
$$
Here the canonical decoded response contains source counts, queue/active history, prediction, delayed root, score and the locked logical fields. Both constructors output the identical typed pair $(\theta_j,\chi_P(\theta_j);q_j,\nu_j,\chi_D(q_j))$ and the same reference/digital window descriptors, computed from the same locked datum. Constructor-dependent physical source/energy/time descriptions lie outside this common logical projection and keep their own records. The predictor's information boundary is the same for both.

All digital input histories have positive probability. Their posterior is exactly (3), since the changed tree source is still independent of $Z$ and its noises. If $R_j^D$ is its Bayes risk, then
$$
 |R_j^D-R_j^P|\le\delta_B,\qquad
 R_j^D-R_{j_*}^D>\frac{17}{2000M}>\frac1{125M}\quad(j<j_*).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.12}
$$
Thus the actual digital source selects the same complete table and control. Its Bayes-control performance gap is greater than $1/(200M)$. No numerical risk oracle is needed by the selector: the proved control formula and the exact posterior formula give its finite integer program.

4. **Both criticality coordinates and finite-size records.** Preserve the exact Poisson record of Theorem P.8.9a.12.0e, with control $\theta$, critical manifold $\{\theta=1\}$, distance $d_P=|1-\theta|$, susceptibility $\chi_P=1/(1-\theta)$ on the subcritical branch, and its stated Poisson exponent and cutoff data. At the selected control,
$$
 d_P(\theta_*)=1/M<\epsilon_{\rm crit}=2/M.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.13}
$$
The digital record instead contains its actual offspring vector $q_j$ and mean $\nu_j=\sum_{l=0}^K lq_{j,l}<1$ at every grid control. Its ambient finite-support critical manifold is $\{q:\sum_l lq_l=1\}$ and its registered distance is $d_D(q)=|1-\sum_l lq_l|$. The selected actual source satisfies
$$
 \frac{499}{500M}\le1-\nu_{j_*}\le\frac3{2M}<\frac2M,
 \qquad
 \chi_D(q_{j_*})=\frac1{1-\nu_{j_*}}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.14}
$$
Hence the actual digital reproduction mean, as well as its ideal reference control, lies inside the same immutable residual window. The full-law susceptibility is distinguished from the bounded mean $\mathbb E\min(S,K)$ of one finite observation.

For any bounded-offspring law $q$ with generating polynomial $f_q(z)=\sum_{l=0}^Kq_lz^l$, its finite total-progeny probabilities are
$$
 \Pr_q(S=t)=\frac1t[z^{t-1}]f_q(z)^t\qquad(t\ge1).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.15}
$$
For the selected subcritical $q$ these sum to one. Its finite-size record uses these exact rational coefficients; for $t\le K$ and the overflow bin, its actual queue instrument realizes them and (11) controls their reference-Poisson discrepancy. The Poisson constants and exponents remain on the exact-family side of this map. The digital finite-window record consists of (15), the actual mean/distance/susceptibility and the displayed source error, with no assertion that its coefficients equal the Poisson Borel law.

5. **Forward lock and PCE ownership.** Before either source constructor evolves or prepares any root, offspring or noise outcome, setup installs the read-only tuple
$$
 \mathfrak D=(M,K,b,J,\{\theta_j\},\{q_j,\nu_j\},D_K,
 \text{task/score/port},\{d_P,d_D\},\epsilon_{\rm crit},
 \mathcal U_P,\mathcal R_P,\mathcal R_D,
 \text{clock/service data},\text{selection program}).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.16}
$$
The exact integer/rational fields occupy finite program registers; the clock, generator and service parameters are fixed apparatus constants with immutable type identifiers. Setup then writes a lock bit. Every runtime operation reads the locked registers as controls and writes only fresh targets. Root verification has its own output pointer, written after the forecast pointer. This is the finite source-level forward lock in Definition P.8.9a.12.0c: outcomes cannot alter the comparison class, performance calibration, criticality coordinates, window or finite-size record. Historical campaign receipts and acceptance remain a separate record.

For each physical constructor $\xi\in\{P,D\}$, take the complete finite configuration space $\mathcal X_\xi=\{1,\ldots,M-1\}\times\{0,1/D_K,\ldots,1\}^{\mathcal H_K}$. Retain a frozen run and an analytically selected run, with their finite coordinate restrictions. The frozen run uses its supplied control/table; the selected run uses $(j_*,F_*)$, retaining the originals. Both pay the same source-bank and program schedule. With fixed numerical output labels, the source/control/history/forecast response separates the supported configurations. Put
$$
 K_\xi=\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2,\qquad W_\xi=(0,\infty)^2,\qquad
 r_\xi(j,F)=(\Gamma_0 R_j^\xi(F),P_{\rm svc}^\xi),\qquad\Gamma_0>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.17}
$$
Here $\Gamma_0$ is a power-equivalent task tariff and the second coordinate is the common complete-run service power within that constructor. These are populated Definition-D.1f contracts. Their resource vectors descend to the finite response quotients, and every strictly positive scalarization uniquely selects $(j_*,F_*)$. The fixed grids, information port and padded service class are operative source premises; the theorem does not enlarge that comparison to supercritical controls or unrestricted hardware.

6. **Finite compilation, carrier and count record.** Let $\ell_J=\lceil\log_2(J+K+2)\rceil$, $u=\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil$, and reserve integer words of width
$$
 w=64[(K+1)^3+(J+K+1)(\ell_M+\ell_J+8)+b+M+K+64],\qquad B_w=256w^2.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.18}
$$
The elementary gate alphabet is retained-input NOT, AND, OR and XOR. Every integer add/subtract, multiply, comparison, bounded divide, fixed shift, word selection and bounded $M$-row selection is implemented with at most $B_w$ Boolean gates and padded to that number. Signed intermediates and unsigned counts have separate field types.

Setup computes (10) using the common integer denominator $M^J J!$, factorial and power tables, signed integer sums and divisions; it never compares a transcendental probability to a binary rounding boundary. It computes $D_K$, all posterior numerators $D_Kp_{n,k}$ and their complete table rows. The original input table is retained. Each forecast word is compared with $0\le A\le D_K$ and masked to zero before any prediction arithmetic if invalid; the original word and failure flag remain. The runtime control is checked by direct comparisons $1\le j\le M-1$ and replaced by $1$ on failure. The selected protocol installs $j_*=M-1$ and the compiled posterior table; the frozen protocol installs the sanitized original control/table. The source/grid/window datum and lock bit are written before source execution.

Use the following fixed word-operation reservations:
$$
\begin{split}
 Q_{\rm cfg}&=128(M+1)(J+K+1)+128(K+1)^2+64L_K(K+1),\\
 Q_{\rm dec}&=16m_B(K+1),\qquad Q_{\rm task}=64K+32,\\
 G_{\rm look}&=8L_Kw.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.19}
$$
The decoder reservation covers every bank entry in either constructor, including matching padded operations for the exact source. In the digital branch it computes a categorical symbol by comparing the $b$-bit source word with all $K$ cumulative thresholds and summing the accepting comparisons. In the exact branch it copies the ladder's count into a word, validates the count and executes the corresponding padding. A count outside $0,\ldots,K$ is retained with failure and masked to zero before the queue update.

Every task slot selects the active control's source row, updates the finite queue, copies its active flag and conditionally appends its noisy bit to the prefix. It updates the active count and a power-of-two counter. If $v$ is the active binary prefix, its table address is $2^n-2+v$. A complete retained-input equality/AND/OR lookup returns the corresponding $w$-bit forecast numerator in at most $G_{\rm look}$ Boolean gates. That numerator is copied to a fresh committed output, with a write-once commitment latch. No later gate or source operation targets that forecast or latch. Only then is the private root copied to the verifier output. Exact subtraction and squaring then give
$$
 T=(A-D_KZ)^2,\qquad L=T/D_K^2\in[0,1].
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.20}
$$
Thus the raw finite score alphabet itself is the verification response; no additional non-dyadic randomizer is assumed.

For $\xi=P,D$ the coin and retained-cell counts are
$$
\begin{split}
 C_P&=1+2K,\qquad C_D=1+2K+m_Bb,\\
 O&=m_Bw+(K+1)w+K(3w+2)+32w+8,\\
 G&=B_w(Q_{\rm cfg}+Q_{\rm dec}+Q_{\rm task})+G_{\rm look}+O,\\
 R_\xi&=128w+L_Kw+m_Bu+C_\xi+G+O.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.21}
$$
The output contains all source-bank counts and the $K+1$ integer counts of the active digital row, paired identically in both constructors; in each task slot, the selected offspring word, queue and active-prefix word, active flag and noisy bit; and a header/task reserve for the control, count, forecast, verified root, raw score, denominator, survivor flag, the same paired ideal/digital mean and susceptibility numerators/denominators in both constructors, critical-window data, lock and commitment labels, and the fixed aggregate failure status. Inactive noisy bits are withheld until after commitment. The original full forecast table occupies $L_Kw$ input cells. The source-ladder reserve is allocated in both formats, remaining ready in the digital constructor. Every source coin, gate output, masked/displaced word and final pointer copy has a separate cell. Unused reserved cells remain ready.

Each fair bit is prepared as $|+\rangle$ by a Hadamard pulse, retained privately throughout. Two noise bits give $E_i$ by AND, and XOR with the hidden root gives $Y_i$. The birth sources are the finite channels (7). Boolean gates extend reversibly by $|x,z\rangle\mapsto|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle$. The final public computational-basis projectors have identity on retained private workspace. Their fixed status fields contain the OR-aggregated table, control and source failure indicators; every individual row/source failure flag remains in private retained workspace. The resulting full finite instrument is normalized on its entire carrier. On its declared ready-input class, its decoded joint law is precisely the source/queue/noise/forecast/root/score law above. Orthogonal retained source words give the digital classical probabilities, while the exact source channels supply (8).

7. **Source, clock and energy ownership.** Both constructors prepare every control bank, including all unused entries. The setup duration $\tau_{\rm set}$ and charge $E_{\rm set}$ own the expanded hardwired gate schedule, wiring/control installation and input/table loading; $R_\xi$ counts the retained data cells. Fix positive ready/source/gate/readout times $\tau_r,\tau_c,\tau_g,\tau_m$, setup time $\tau_{\rm set}$, a birth interval $\tau_B$, a positive guard, and positive registered service charges $E_{\rm set},e_r,e_c,e_g,e_m,P_0,p_r,e_B,p_B,\varepsilon_B$. The exact birth ladder has physical energy observable $\varepsilon_B\sum_{l=0}^K l|l\rangle\langle l|$; its diagonal phase evolution commutes with the count operations, so (7) is its interaction-picture source. A raising jump supplies energy $\varepsilon_B$ to that retained source register. The source-service contract additionally charges $e_B+p_B\tau_B$ per driven channel for its controller/environment service. These are source-input and retained-energy transactions, with no reset-heat identification.

Define $\beta_K(\theta)=\sum_{l=0}^K l p_l(\theta)$ and the common expected exact-bank source charge
$$
 E_B=m_B(e_B+p_B\tau_B)+\varepsilon_B K\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\beta_K(\theta_j).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.22}
$$
The full random energy transfer is $\varepsilon_B$ times the sum of all bank counts; its law is independent of the selected control and forecast. The digital branch's source-bit preparation is charged through $C_De_c$. Fresh retained banks and records are owned for one complete cycle; closed reuse requires its own reset account.

With $I_P=1$, $I_D=0$, one sequential schedule is
$$
\begin{split}
 T_\xi={}&\tau_{\rm set}+R_\xi\tau_r+B_wQ_{\rm cfg}\tau_g
 +I_\xi m_B\tau_B+C_\xi\tau_c\\
 &+[B_w(Q_{\rm dec}+Q_{\rm task})+G_{\rm look}]\tau_g
 +O(\tau_g+\tau_m)+\tau_{\rm guard},\\
 E_\xi={}&E_{\rm set}+R_\xi e_r+C_\xi e_c+Ge_g+Oe_m+I_\xi E_B
 +(P_0+R_\xi p_r)T_\xi,\qquad P_{\rm svc}^\xi=E_\xi/T_\xi.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.23}
$$
Clock labels in each physical record use this constructor's fixed schedule. The logical response map used in (11) retains registered stage/commitment labels and keeps the two physical source-service descriptions separate. Here $E_\xi$ is the expected complete-run charge and $P_{\rm svc}^\xi$ its expected charge per fixed run time; in the exact branch the bank transfer is random before its expectation is taken. These expected charges are common across the complete candidate class within their constructor, including selection compilation, unused banks, inactive draws, score evaluation and readout. Equality of a Boolean gate count is not substituted for source heat or controller work: the driven-source and gate-service laws are explicit parts of this admitted physical class.

For each elementary unitary $U$, a duration-$\tau$ Hamiltonian $\pi\hbar(I-U)/(2\tau)$ implements its involution, with norm-action at most $\pi\hbar$. Hence Boolean and Hadamard operations contribute at most $\pi\hbar(G+C_\xi)$. The exact source's free ladder Hamiltonians add at most $m_BK\varepsilon_BT_P$. Its dissipative generators have the separate finite strength bound
$$
 \sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\sum_{i=1}^{K}\int_0^{\tau_B}\|\mathcal L_{\theta_j}\|_\diamond\,dt
 \le2K^2\sum_{j=1}^{M-1}\theta_j=K^2(M-1).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.24}
$$
The generator resource is not identified with Hamiltonian action. The finite open-source operators, clock and nonnegative service contract specify the formal source; empirical calibration and a microscopic bath model are not inferred from its endpoint statistics.

8. **Finite implementation and observation envelope.** Uniform source trace-distance and half-diamond gate/readout defects, including retained ancillas and all failed trials, add to a complete finite-word bound $\epsilon_\xi$. An arbitrary received score word is decoded by clipping $T/D_K^2$ to $[0,1]$ with the frozen denominator; its original word and flags remain. Thus its expected risk differs from the corresponding exact finite instrument by at most $\epsilon_\xi$, and the window-performance error is at most that value. For $A$ independent complete repetitions of a registered configuration and constructor,
$$
 \Pr\{|\overline L-R_j^\xi(F)|>\eta+\epsilon_\xi\}\le2e^{-2A\eta^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.0f.25}
$$
Mean/source identification and the critical-family entries remain those of the admitted independent source laws. A finite-word error alone does not assign a Galton–Watson critical manifold to an arbitrary correlated faulty source. Equations (11)–(15) provide the exact formal source and its digital transfer; measured repetitions and historical campaign acceptance have their own records.

*Proof.*
For a noisy word with $n$ symbols and $k$ ones, its likelihood under $Z=1$ is $3^k/4^n$ and under $Z=0$ is $3^{n-k}/4^n$. Equal prior weights prove (3). Tree/source information and the stopping count are independent of $Z$ and of the entire noise sequence, so neither selecting the first $n$ observations nor conditioning on the active tree changes this likelihood ratio. Every positive offspring law in the theorem supports each possible active length: a chain of $n-1$ one-child nodes followed by zero children gives every $n<K$, while a sufficiently large first family gives $n=K$. Both noise symbols have positive probability. Hence every table input is supported.

For a fixed history with posterior $p$, conditional squared risk is $p(1-p)+(F-p)^2$. Averaging proves (5), and the product defining $D_K$ makes every posterior exactly representable. Strict nonnegativity makes this table unique on the entire supported input class. A word with $k$ ones has marginal probability $(3^k+3^{n-k})/(2\,4^n)$ and posterior variance $3^n/(3^k+3^{n-k})^2$. Summing over its $\binom nk$ words proves (4), including the two displayed small risks.

After another noisy observation, a current posterior $p\in(0,1)$ takes values $3p/(1+2p)$ and $p/(3-2p)$ with probabilities $(1+2p)/4$ and $(3-2p)/4$. Its conditional variance is
$$
 \frac{4p^2(1-p)^2}{(1+2p)(3-2p)}>0.
$$
The conditional-variance decomposition thus gives $R_n-R_{n+1}>0$ for every finite $n$. This is a proper-score comparison, with no parity or hard-decision tie exception.

For $\theta'<\theta''$, couple offspring at every possible tree vertex by an independent Poisson increment of mean $\theta''-\theta'$. The smaller tree embeds in the larger, so its truncated active count is no larger. On the event that the smaller root has zero children and the increment has at least one, the first count is one and the second is at least two. Its probability is $e^{-\theta'}-e^{-\theta''}$. The strict risk decrease therefore proves the first inequality in (6). For $j<j_*$,
$$
 e^{-\theta_j}-e^{-\theta_*}
 =\int_{\theta_j}^{\theta_*}e^{-t}\,dt >\frac{\theta_* -\theta_j}{e}\ge\frac1{eM}.
$$
Since $e<3$, multiplying by $3/80$ gives the stated rational gap. Bayes risk is at most $R_1=3/16<1/4$, whereas the constant-half forecast has risk $1/4$ on the same root task. Equation (2) gives the super-chance performance claim. The optimization uses the full registered grid and every table, because (5) first removes every nonposterior table and (6) then compares every remaining control.

The finite generator (7) is of GKSL form, hence its finite-time maps are completely positive and trace preserving. On the diagonal subspace its populations satisfy
$$
 \dot p_0=-(\theta/\tau_B)p_0,\quad
 \dot p_l=(\theta/\tau_B)(p_{l-1}-p_l)\ (0<l<K),\quad
 \dot p_K=(\theta/\tau_B)p_{K-1}.
$$
Starting from $p_0(0)=1$, induction by an integrating factor gives $p_l(t)=e^{-\theta t/\tau_B}(\theta t/\tau_B)^l/l!$ for $l<K$, and normalization gives the last population. At $t=\tau_B$ this is exactly (8). Product initial states and channels make every source-bank entry independent. Tensoring the fresh root/noise inputs and the retained Boolean circuit gives the common source-to-task map on a finite carrier.

While active, each queue update increases the queue by at most $K-1$, proving its stated bound. If an offspring symbol is capped at $K$, then immediately after that step the queue is at least $K$. At most $K-i$ further explorations remain, each reducing it by at most one; consequently $Q_K>0$. The same conclusion holds for any unbounded Poisson offspring represented by that tail symbol. If no such symbol occurs, all active offspring values equal the true Poisson values. Therefore the first-zero time through $K$, the truncated active count and the terminal survivor flag are exact in both cases. This also proves across-cutoff compatibility by censoring independent underlying Poisson variables and ordered exploration. Physical source duration, carrier size and retained work remain resolution-indexed; the compatibility concerns the declared logical cylinder record.

For $0\le\theta\le1$, the odd alternating exponential sums increase to $e^{-\theta}$, and the degree-three lower sum is at least its value $1/3$ at $\theta=1$. Thus $1/3\le L_j\le e^{-\theta_j}$ and the alternating remainder is at most $1/(J+1)!<2^{-b}$. For $l<K$, its multiplication by $\theta_j^l/l!\le1$ preserves that error bound. Since $\theta_j\ge1/M$,
$$
 L_j\theta_j^l/l!\ge\frac1{3M^K K!}.
$$
The explicit choice of $b$ makes $2^b>6M^K K!$, so the downward-rounded count for every such bin is positive. The residual tail count is positive because the exact Poisson tail is positive and every earlier rounded probability is no larger than its exact value. This proves that (10) is a complete normalized positive integer source.

For each $l<K$, $0\le p_l-q_l<2^{1-b}$. All lost mass is placed in the final bin, hence
$$
 d_{\rm TV}(p,q)=\sum_{l<K}(p_l-q_l)<2K2^{-b}.
$$
There are $K(M-1)$ independent source-bank entries. Product coupling followed by the same queue, predictor and score decoder gives (11). To check its explicit last inequality, use $2^{\ell_M}\ge M+1$ and $2^{\ell_K}\ge K+1$: the resulting lower bound on $2^b$ exceeds $1000M(M-1)K^2$. The common root/noise law is unchanged. The bounded proper score then has expectation discrepancy at most $\delta_B$, uniformly over every table and control. Applying this at both Bayes controls in (6) gives
$$
 R_j^D-R_{j_*}^D>\frac1{80M}-\frac2{500M}=\frac{17}{2000M}>\frac1{125M}.
$$
Since the digital source is still independent of the root/noises, the exact same posterior table is optimal. For Bayes controls $R_j^D\le3/16$, and
$$
 \frac1{1+R_{j_*}^D}-\frac1{1+R_j^D}
 =\frac{R_j^D-R_{j_*}^D}{(1+R_j^D)(1+R_{j_*}^D)} >\frac{1/(125M)}{(19/16)^2}>\frac1{200M}.
$$
This proves robust strict control selection for the actual finite-bit source, not just its reference law.

Let $C\sim\mathrm{Poisson}(\theta)$ and $\mu_{\rm cap}=\mathbb E\min(C,K)$. Moving each deficit $p_l-q_l$ to bin $K$ gives
$$
 \nu=\mu_{\rm cap}+\sum_{l<K}(K-l)(p_l-q_l),\qquad
 0\le\nu-\mu_{\rm cap}\le Kd_{\rm TV}(p,q)\le\delta_B.
$$
For integers $x\ge K+1$, $(x-K)\le\binom{x}{K+1}$, because $\binom{x}{K+1}/(x-K)=\binom{x}{K}/(K+1)\ge1$. The Poisson factorial-moment identity, obtained directly by summing its series, therefore gives
$$
 0\le\theta-\mu_{\rm cap}=\mathbb E(C-K)_+
 \le\mathbb E\binom C{K+1}=\frac{\theta^{K+1}}{(K+1)!}
 \le\frac1{(K+1)!}\le\frac1{2M}.
$$
In particular $\nu_j\le\theta_j+\delta_B<1$ at every grid control, so each paired susceptibility header is well defined. At $\theta_*=1-1/M$, the upward digital correction is at most $1/(500M)$ and the downward truncation correction at most $1/(2M)$. This proves (14). For any offspring law of finite mean $\nu$, generation means are $\nu^g$, and Tonelli gives $\mathbb ES=\sum_{g\ge0}\nu^g$. Thus its susceptibility is $1/(1-\nu)$ when $\nu<1$ and infinite at or above one, validating the stated actual critical coordinate. At the selected control the source is strictly subcritical.

The cycle-rotation argument in Theorem P.8.9a.12.0e uses independence and exchangeability of offspring, not the Poisson formula itself. Apply it to $t$ iid samples from $q$: exactly one of the $t$ cyclic positions of a sequence with total offspring $t-1$ gives the proper nonnegative exploration before first extinction. Averaging over the rotations yields (15). When $\nu<1$, the probability a generation remains nonempty is at most its mean $\nu^g\to0$, so extinction occurs almost surely and the finite-size probabilities sum to one. For sizes through $K$, the queue's censoring proof makes this the exact measured finite-window law. The source coupling bounds its discrepancy from the ideal finite window. These are the digital finite-size entries; the exact Poisson expressions and exponents retain the separate premises already proved in .0e.

It remains to supply the operative lock, finite implementation and resources. The exact integer source table can be compiled without floating arithmetic. Precompute factorials through $J$, powers of $M$ through $J+K$ and powers of each $j$ through that range. With common denominator $M^J J!$, the numerator of $L_j$ is the alternating integer sum of $j^a M^{J-a}J!/a!$. Multiplication by $j^l$ and division by $M^l l!$, followed by the explicit factor $2^b$ and floor division, gives each integer source count. A cumulative sum gives every decoder threshold, including $2^b$. The source's actual mean numerator is $\sum_l l n_{j,l}$, so its digital mean and susceptibility are exact rational fields. These computations are finite and depend only on the locked source inputs.

Next precompute $3^0,\ldots,3^K$, all posterior denominator factors and their product $D_K$. Each selected forecast numerator is the exact division $D_K3^k/(3^k+3^{n-k})$. Enumerating every finite row $(n,y)$ and its popcount fills the selected table. Validation and masking of the original table are performed for every row in both protocols. The selected control is the explicit integer $M-1$; its correctness follows from the complete risk comparison (5)–(12), so the program uses neither an empirical optimizer nor an uncharged probability oracle. It performs the same compilation even in a frozen trial.

The source-factory reservations in (19) are conservative straight-line bounds. Powers and factorials cost linearly many word multiplications. Each exponential-sum term uses at most eight integer operations; each source probability, floor and threshold uses fewer than sixteen. The $128(M+1)(J+K+1)$ term covers these loops, headers, source mean and safe control selection. The $128(K+1)^2$ term covers posterior factors, the product and all distinct $(n,k)$ divisions. For a table row, fewer than $K+16$ operations count its bits, select its precomputed posterior value, validate and retain the original word, and choose the active frozen/selected entry. The $64L_K(K+1)$ reserve covers all rows and padding. All bound checks occur before the corresponding potentially large multiplication; invalid original inputs remain retained.

A digital categorical decoder compares its uniform input with the $K$ interior cumulative thresholds and counts how many thresholds it meets or exceeds. This is exactly the interval sampler, including equality at a boundary. Its primitive slots, copies and status handling fit within $16(K+1)$ word operations per bank entry. The exact constructor copies its count and executes the corresponding padded reservation. Each task slot then uses a bounded row selection, a source/queue comparison and update, active count, noise AND/XOR, conditional prefix and power-of-two updates, and retained output transfers. Fewer than sixty-four word operations suffice per slot. The remaining thirty-two slots cover the address, commitment, delayed root copy, score and final status.

For lookup, write the address in $K+1$ bits. Complement its input bits once, form an equality conjunction for every row address, and for each output bit AND every row's match with that table bit and OR the results. Its count is at most $(K+1)+L_KK+w(2L_K-1)<8L_Kw$. Invalid binary addresses have a retained flag and a safe zero output; ideal task inputs are always valid because the root is explored. The lookup transfers exactly one rational-grid forecast, then a distinct committed pointer is set. Only afterward is the root copied to the verifier. Thus all likelihood and proper-score calculations refer to an actual pre-verification forecast.

For arithmetic width, each posterior denominator is at most $2\,3^n<2^{2n+1}$. Summing these logarithmic bounds over all $(n,k)$ gives fewer than $2(K+1)^3$ bits for $D_K$, and its score square and auxiliary products fit within $8(K+1)^3$ bits. The source common denominator and every required integer product have fewer than $4(J+K+1)(\ell_M+\ell_J+8)+2b$ bits, including signed partial sums and multiplication by $2^b$. Queue, control, address and clock indices are smaller. The word width (18) contains all these bounds, the source means and resource-count metadata. The fixed compiler/control template fits in the input reserve; the expanded circuit and wiring belong to the setup service. Retained full adders, schoolbook multiplication, fixed-round division and word multiplexers each use fewer than $256w^2$ elementary Boolean gates. A bounded $M$-row selection uses at most $16Mw\le256w^2$ gates. Fresh ready-input padding makes every reservation explicit.

The output census (21) copies all $m_B$ bank words and the $K+1$ active digital source counts; three words and two bits per task slot; and a thirty-two-word/eight-bit task/header/status reserve. Its eight bits can hold lock, commitment, verification completion, survivor, protocol choice and the three OR-aggregated control/table/source failure indicators. Local failure flags remain retained privately, and their OR aggregation is included in the setup/decoder reservations. Source/format integers and rational numerator/denominator fields fit their assigned words. Fixed apparatus constants are referenced by their immutable type identifiers. Counting compilation, source decoding, task operations, lookup and final pointer copies gives $G$. Allocating original program/table inputs, the finite source bank, every fair coin, every Boolean output and every readout pointer gives $R_\xi$. Masked values, division remainders, old queues and original tables are already retained gate inputs or outputs, so no hidden erasure or workspace reuse is needed.

Read-only inputs are never gate targets after the lock. All runtime Boolean extensions retain their inputs and write fresh outputs. Source evolution acts on the separately allocated ready source factors and cannot write the locked bank. Noise and root information enter only the specified task fields. The compiler/source ordering therefore proves the outcome-independent forward lock, and the separate forecast/root pointers prove delayed verification. These statements establish a causal property of the constructed program; they do not manufacture a historical campaign receipt.

The zero extension on unused ladder codes preserves GKSL form and gives literal CPTP channels on the whole encoded source carrier. Each Hadamard and Boolean extension is unitary, and the complete final projectors sum to the identity on the public factors with private identity. Their composition is consequently a normalized finite instrument, including unsupported source counts and rejected programs as flagged outcomes. On the ready-input class the birth registers are diagonal with law (8), and orthogonal retained fair words give the exact digital and noise distributions. The deterministic queue and score computations give their complete joint law. This proves the formal source-to-response realization rather than assigning a probability label to unrelated qubits.

The entire source bank is generated before the selected row is used. Its state, jump-count distribution, duration and supplied energy are therefore the same over every control/table configuration. A raising jump increases the finite ladder energy by exactly $\varepsilon_B$; summing all counts gives the random bank transfer and its expectation (22). The fixed source-service overhead owns the controller/environment operation. Retaining those states carries their final energy forward; no heat equality is inferred from replacement or disposal. The digital source preparations have their separate counted service. Equation (23) then charges setup, every ready cell, all sources, Boolean operations, storage maintenance and readout once, including inactive and unused reservations. Physical time and source-generator data are explicit. For each source constructor these data make the service coordinate in (17) genuinely common, so strict positive scalarization leaves exactly the previously proved task-risk minimizer.

The elementary unitary Hamiltonian bound follows from the $\pm1$ eigenspaces of an involution. The finite ladder Hamiltonian has norm $K\varepsilon_B$ per register and hence the displayed whole-cycle bound. For a Lindblad jump $J$, its dissipator has diamond norm at most $2\|J\|^2$. Summing the $K$ jumps, $K$ source copies at each rate and all controls gives (24). This resource is kept separate from unitary action and the supplied-energy account.

Finally, trace-distance contraction and the telescoping uniform channel comparison give the complete finite-word implementation bound. The clipped score is a bounded deterministic observable, so its mean error is at most $\epsilon_\xi$. The map $R\mapsto(1+R)^{-1}$ is one-Lipschitz on $[0,1]$, giving the performance error. Hoeffding applied to independent complete bounded-score repetitions, followed by the implementation-bias triangle inequality, proves (25). None of these finite-word estimates changes the stipulated independent offspring family or transfers Poisson asymptotic constants to a different law. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a121-conditional-zipf-mandelbrot-law-from-logarithmic-pce-cost"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.1 (Conditional Zipf-Mandelbrot Law from Logarithmic PCE Cost).** Let $N\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$, let ranks be $r=1,\ldots,N$, and suppose the PCE activation weights are Gibbs weights
$$
p_r=Z_N^{-1}e^{-\beta E_r},
\qquad
\beta>0,
$$
with logarithmic ranked PCE cost
$$
E_r=E_0+\gamma\log(r+r_0),
\qquad
\gamma>0,
\qquad
r_0\ge0.
$$
Then
$$
p_r=
\frac{(r+r_0)^{-s}}
{\sum_{q=1}^N(q+r_0)^{-s}},
\qquad
s=\beta\gamma.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.1}
$$
For $N=\infty$, the normalizing constant is finite exactly when $s>1$. The exact Zipf exponent $s=1$ is therefore normalizable only on a finite ranked population, a truncated window, or a model with an additional upper cutoff.

*Proof.* Substituting the cost law into the Gibbs form gives
$$
e^{-\beta E_r}
=
e^{-\beta E_0}(r+r_0)^{-\beta\gamma}.
$$
The constant $e^{-\beta E_0}$ is independent of $r$ and is absorbed into $Z_N$, yielding (P.8.9a.12.1) with $s=\beta\gamma$. If $N<\infty$, the finite sum is positive and finite. If $N=\infty$, then $r+r_0$ is comparable to $r$ for large $r$, so
$$
\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}(r+r_0)^{-s}
$$
converges exactly when the $p$-series $\sum r^{-s}$ converges, namely when $s>1$. For $s=1$ the harmonic comparison diverges. ∎

<a id="convention-p89a121c-logarithm-base-in-the-ranked-cost"></a>**Convention P.8.9a.12.1c (Logarithm Base in the Ranked Cost).** In Theorem P.8.9a.12.1 and throughout this subsection, $\log$ in $E_r=E_0+\gamma\log(r+r_0)$ denotes the natural logarithm. Base-two logarithms are written $\log_2$.

<a id="remark-p89a121-coding-cost-reading-of-the-ranked-pce-cost"></a>**Remark P.8.9a.12.1 (Coding-Cost Reading of the Ranked PCE Cost).** Write
$$
Z_N=\sum_{q=1}^{N}(q+r_0)^{-s},
\qquad
p_r=\frac{(r+r_0)^{-s}}{Z_N},
\qquad
s=\beta\gamma,
$$
and let $\ell_r=-\log_2p_r$. Then
$$
\ell_r=\frac{s}{\ln2}\ln(r+r_0)+\log_2Z_N
=\frac{\beta}{\ln2}E_r+c,
\qquad
c=\log_2Z_N-\frac{\beta E_0}{\ln2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.1a}
$$
Thus $E_r$ is a positive affine reparametrization of the ideal information content of the rank index on this family.

*Proof.* Substitute the normalized weight into $-\log_2p_r$, then use $\ln(r+r_0)=(E_r-E_0)/\gamma$ and $s=\beta\gamma$. Since $\beta>0$, the affine slope is positive. ∎

The real-valued quantity $\ell_r$ is distinct from the integer-valued minimal-description envelope
$
D([R])=\min\{L_{\mathrm{desc}}(B):\mathcal R_B\simeq R\}
$
defined in the proof of Theorem P.6.1b.8a. The lengths $\lceil\ell_r\rceil$ satisfy the Kraft inequality because
$$
\sum_r2^{-\lceil\ell_r\rceil}\le\sum_r2^{-\ell_r}=1,
$$
so a prefix code with those lengths exists and has expected length smaller than $H(p)+1$ bit.

Under
$$
\beta=\frac1\mu,
\qquad
\gamma=a,
\qquad
E_0=b,
\qquad
r_0=V,
$$
Proposition P.2.6.3d.2 is the same Gibbs--log-cost template. This dictionary preserves the logarithmic-cost hypothesis. A numerical concentration ratio additionally requires registered parameter values and a population and likelihood model.

<a id="theorem-p89a122-rank-pareto-zipf-bridge"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.2 (Rank-Pareto Zipf Bridge).** Let $X$ be a positive population variable with Pareto upper survival law
$$
\mathbb P(X>x)=\left(\frac{x_0}{x}\right)^{\zeta},
\qquad
x\ge x_0>0,
\qquad
\zeta>0.
$$
For a population of size $N$, define the deterministic rank curve $x_r$ by the expected exceedance equation
$$
N\mathbb P(X>x_r)=r,
\qquad
1\le r\le N.
$$
Then
$$
x_r=x_0\left(\frac Nr\right)^{1/\zeta}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2}
$$
Thus a Pareto tail with survival exponent $\zeta$ induces a Zipf-type rank-size exponent $1/\zeta$. In particular, the multiplicative PCE adaptation tail of Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 gives the rank exponent
$$
\frac1{\zeta}
=
\frac1{1+2k/\sigma^2}.
$$

*Proof.* The defining equation gives
$$
N\left(\frac{x_0}{x_r}\right)^{\zeta}=r.
$$
Solving for $x_r$ gives
$$
\left(\frac{x_r}{x_0}\right)^{\zeta}=\frac Nr,
\qquad
x_r=x_0\left(\frac Nr\right)^{1/\zeta}.
$$
Substituting $\zeta=1+2k/\sigma^2$ from Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 gives the displayed PCE specialization. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a122a-disjoint-exponent-ranges-for-the-coding-and-growth-routes"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.12.2a (Disjoint Exponent Ranges for the Coding and Growth Routes).** Assume that the ranked activation weights of Theorem P.8.9a.12.1 are identified with the normalized rank-size shares of Theorem P.8.9a.12.2. On an unbounded rank population, normalizability of the coding route requires
$$
s=\beta\gamma\in(1,\infty),
$$
whereas the multiplicative-growth route of Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 gives
$$
\frac1\zeta=\frac1{1+2k/\sigma^2}\in(0,1)
\qquad(k,\sigma>0).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2a}
$$
The two exponents are therefore unequal on that branch. Their common boundary value is $1$, attained by neither route; $1/\zeta\uparrow1$ as $\sigma^2/k\to\infty$.

On a finite ranked population or a branch with an upper cutoff, the coding normalization imposes no condition $s>1$. Equality of the two exponents then holds exactly when
$$
\beta\gamma\left(1+\frac{2k}{\sigma^2}\right)=1.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2b}
$$

*Proof.* The series $\sum_{r\ge1}(r+r_0)^{-s}$ converges exactly for $s>1$. Since $2k/\sigma^2$ ranges over $(0,\infty)$, its reciprocal shift ranges over $(0,1)$. The finite-cutoff statement follows by algebraic rearrangement. ∎

An exact exponent equal to $1$ is incompatible with both unbounded mechanisms under these strict hypotheses. A measured interval containing $1$ leaves the interior exponents and finite-cutoff branches to be distinguished by the registered population and likelihood model.

<a id="theorem-p89a122c-rank-response-identification-criterion-and-finite-population-rank-bounds"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.2c (Rank-Response Identification Criterion and Finite-Population Rank Bounds).** Let $\beta,\gamma>0$, $r_0\ge0$, $s=\beta\gamma$, $\zeta>0$ and $t:=1/\zeta$. For $N\in\mathbb N$, and for $N=\infty$ when $s>1$, write $p_r^{(N)}$ for the weights (P.8.9a.12.1) and $Z_N:=\sum_{q=1}^N(q+r_0)^{-s}$; for finite $N$ write
$$
\pi_r^{(N)}:=\frac{x_r}{\sum_{q=1}^Nx_q}=\frac{r^{-t}}{\sum_{q=1}^Nq^{-t}}
\qquad(1\le r\le N)
$$
for the normalized rank-size shares of (P.8.9a.12.2).

1. *Identification.* For $N\ge3$, $p_r^{(N)}=\pi_r^{(N)}$ for every $r\le N$ exactly when $r_0=0$ and $\beta\gamma\zeta=1$. For $N=2$ the identity holds exactly when $s\ln[(2+r_0)/(1+r_0)]=t\ln2$. If $\zeta\ge1$, then $\pi_r^{(N)}\to0$ for every fixed $r$ as $N\to\infty$, so the growth route has no normalized rank law on an unbounded population.
2. *Normalization and cutoff.* For every finite $N$,
$$
\int_1^{N+1}(x+r_0)^{-s}\,dx\le Z_N\le(1+r_0)^{-s}+\int_1^N(x+r_0)^{-s}\,dx.
$$
If $s>1$, then
$$
\frac{(N+1+r_0)^{1-s}}{s-1}\le Z_\infty-Z_N\le\frac{(N+r_0)^{1-s}}{s-1},
\qquad
1\le\frac{p_r^{(N)}}{p_r^{(\infty)}}\le1+\frac{(N+r_0)^{1-s}}{(s-1)Z_N}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2c.1}
$$
3. *Finite-population rank response.* Let $\zeta>1$ and let $X_{(1)}\ge\cdots\ge X_{(N)}$ be the order statistics of $N$ independent copies of the Pareto law of Theorem P.8.9a.12.2. Then
$$
\mathbb EX_{(r)}=x_0\,\frac{\Gamma(N+1)\,\Gamma(r-t)}{\Gamma(N+1-t)\,\Gamma(r)},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2c.2}
$$
and
$$
\Bigl(\frac{N+1-t}{N}\Bigr)^{t}\Bigl(\frac{N+1-t}{N+1}\Bigr)^{1-t}\Bigl(\frac{r}{r-t}\Bigr)^{t}
\le
\frac{\mathbb EX_{(r)}}{x_r}
\le
\Bigl(\frac{N+1-t}{N}\Bigr)^{t}\frac{r}{r-t}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2c.3}
$$

Consequently, on a finite population with at least three ranks, identification of the coding and growth rank responses holds exactly when the exponent condition $\beta\gamma\zeta=1$, which is (P.8.9a.12.2b) at $\zeta=1+2k/\sigma^2$, and the offset condition $r_0=0$ both hold. The deterministic rank curve (P.8.9a.12.2) is the large-rank limit of the expected order statistics, with the explicit two-sided factor (P.8.9a.12.2c.3) at every finite rank.

*Proof.* For item 1, two normalized positive vectors coincide exactly when they are proportional, that is, when $g(y):=t\ln y-s\ln(y+r_0)$ takes one value at $y=1,\ldots,N$. If $N\ge3$, Rolle's theorem gives zeros of $g'(y)=t/y-s/(y+r_0)$ in $(1,2)$ and in $(2,3)$. The equation $g'(y)=0$ is $(s-t)y=tr_0$, which has at most one positive solution when $s\ne t$, and when $s=t$ has a solution only if $r_0=0$, in which case $g'\equiv0$. Two distinct zeros therefore force $s=t$ and $r_0=0$, and these conditions make the two vectors equal. For $N=2$ the single condition $g(1)=g(2)$ is the displayed equation. If $\zeta\ge1$, then $t\le1$ and $\sum_{q\le N}q^{-t}\ge\sum_{q\le N}q^{-1}\to\infty$, so each fixed share tends to $0$.

For item 2, $y\mapsto(y+r_0)^{-s}$ is positive and decreasing, so each summand lies between its integrals over the adjacent unit intervals; summation gives both displays, and $p_r^{(N)}/p_r^{(\infty)}=Z_\infty/Z_N=1+(Z_\infty-Z_N)/Z_N$.

For item 3, $X=x_0U^{-t}$ with $U$ uniform on $(0,1)$ has the Pareto law, and the $r$-th largest of $N$ copies is $x_0U_{(r)}^{-t}$, where the $r$-th smallest uniform $U_{(r)}$ has the $\mathrm{Beta}(r,N-r+1)$ law. Since $r-t>0$,
$$
\mathbb EU_{(r)}^{-t}=\frac{B(r-t,N-r+1)}{B(r,N-r+1)}=\frac{\Gamma(N+1)\Gamma(r-t)}{\Gamma(N+1-t)\Gamma(r)},
$$
which is (P.8.9a.12.2c.2). For $y>0$ and $0<h<1$, Hölder's inequality applied to $\Gamma(y+h)=\int_0^\infty(u^{y-1}e^{-u})^{1-h}(u^ye^{-u})^h\,du$ gives $\Gamma(y+h)\le y^h\Gamma(y)$; applying it at $(y+h,1-h)$ gives $\Gamma(y+1)\le(y+h)^{1-h}\Gamma(y+h)$. Hence
$$
y^h\Bigl(\frac{y}{y+h}\Bigr)^{1-h}\le\frac{\Gamma(y+h)}{\Gamma(y)}\le y^h .
$$
Taking $(y,h)=(N+1-t,t)$ and $(y,h)=(r-t,t)$ in
$$
\frac{\mathbb EX_{(r)}}{x_r}
=\frac{\Gamma(N+1)}{\Gamma(N+1-t)N^t}\cdot\frac{r^t\,\Gamma(r-t)}{\Gamma(r)}
$$
gives (P.8.9a.12.2c.3). Both bounds tend to $1$ as $r\to\infty$ with $r\le N$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a122d-pareto-ranks-from-a-renewal-amplitude-prediction-processor"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.2d (Pareto Ranks from a Renewal-Amplitude Prediction Processor).** Fix a source amplitude unit $v_0>0$, rates $\kappa,\lambda>0$ with $\lambda>2\kappa$, and an integer $d\ge1$. Rates are expressed in the registered nominal source clock. Write
$$
x_0=v_0^2,\qquad \zeta=\frac{\lambda}{2\kappa}>1,\qquad
M=2^d,\qquad \mathcal J=\{-M,\ldots,M\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.1}
$$
The source variable is a numerical task amplitude. Its ideal age $A_t$ increases at unit rate and resets to zero at independent Poisson rate $\lambda$; its amplitude is $V_t=v_0e^{\kappa A_t}$. At a registered sample, the current amplitude is copied into a committed task register. Configuration $j\in\mathcal J$ predicts $(j/M)V$ before a later independent fair sign $S$ generates the teacher $Y=SV$ from that same committed register. The source comparison uses the proper normalized loss
$$
L_j(S)=\frac{((j/M)V-Y)^2}{4V^2}
=\frac{(j-MS)^2}{4M^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.2}
$$
The numerical unit map, source coefficients, reset/multiply rule, candidate grid and future-sign task are fixed independently of ranked-response data. They define a clocked prediction processor, without an identification of its amplitude register with an electrostatic voltage. Its finite physical realizations are the retained qubit circuits below. Then:

1. **Selected observable and ideal source law.** Over the full $2M+1$ configurations,
$$
R(j)=\mathbb E L_j(S)=\frac14+\frac{j^2}{4M^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.3}
$$
Thus $j_*=0$ is the unique minimum, with gap $1/(4M^2)$. The selected *unnormalized* squared-error readout is the actual per-run value
$$
X=(0-Y)^2=V^2.
