\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.4}
$$
For a matched update from $j$ to zero, both forecasts precede the same sign. Its normalized realized gain is $[j^2-2jMS]/(4M^2)$, with mean $j^2/(4M^2)$; realized gains can be negative. The source's mean and symmetry, computed from its two equiprobable sign values, give the explicit constant selector zero.

The age transition kernel and its unique invariant law are
$$
P_t f(a)=e^{-\lambda t}f(a+t)+\int_0^t\lambda e^{-\lambda u}f(u)\,du,
\qquad \pi_A(da)=\lambda e^{-\lambda a}\,da.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.5}
$$
At stationarity the selected response therefore has
$$
\Pr(X>x)=(x_0/x)^\zeta\quad(x\ge x_0),\qquad
\mathbb EX=\mu_X=\frac{\zeta x_0}{\zeta-1}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.6}
$$
The deterministic expected-exceedance curve of a population of size $N$ is exactly $x_r=x_0(N/r)^{1/\zeta}$. For $N$ independent complete source replicas, their actual descending order statistics have the expectation (P.8.9a.12.2c.2) and its two-sided comparison (P.8.9a.12.2c.3). The sampled order statistics, the deterministic quantile curve and a normalized Gibbs rank law retain the distinct meanings in Theorem P.8.9a.12.2c.

2. **Warm-up and an exact finite physical source.** Initialize the ideal age at zero, run for nominal time $B>0$, and sample. Couple it to a stationary age $A\sim\mathrm{Exp}(\lambda)$ by the common last-reset history. Its final age and selected score are
$$
A_B=\min(A,B),\qquad X_B=\min(X,H_B),\qquad H_B=x_0e^{2\kappa B}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.7}
$$
The warm-up state-law total variation is $e^{-\lambda B}$ and
$$
\mathbb E(X-X_B)=D_B:=\frac{x_0}{\zeta-1}e^{-(\lambda-2\kappa)B}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.8}
$$
The finite implementation supplies this warm-up rather than requiring a stationary continuous random seed.

For the constructive source subclass take $\kappa/\lambda=a/c$ with positive integers $c>2a$. Fix integers $s,h\ge1$, $f\ge2$ and $K\ge1$, and set
$$
q=2^{-s},\qquad \delta=-\frac{\ln(1-q)}{\lambda},\qquad B=K\delta,
\qquad g=e^{\kappa\delta}=(1-q)^{-a/c},\qquad
P=\lfloor2^hg\rfloor.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.9}
$$
The integer $P$ is computed by bounded integer bisection on $2^h\le P<2^{h+1}$, using the exact test
$$
 P^c(2^s-1)^a\le2^{hc+sa}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.10}
$$
At each tick draw $s$ fresh fair bits; their all-zero event is the reset flag $E_l$. On fresh retained registers, execute
$$
 A_0^{\rm dig}=2^f,\qquad
 A_l^{\rm dig}=
 \begin{cases}
 2^f,&E_l=1,\\
 \lfloor P A_{l-1}^{\rm dig}/2^h\rfloor,&E_l=0,
 \end{cases}
 \quad (1\le l\le K).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.11}
$$
All old amplitudes, products, division remainders, fair bits and reset flags remain retained. The actual committed amplitude is $\widehat V=v_0 A_K^{\rm dig}/2^f$. The future teacher and squared scores are computed from this same integer, so the selected readout is exactly
$$
\widehat X=x_0\,(A_K^{\rm dig})^2/2^{2f}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.12}
$$
The exact finite source law sums the $2^{sK}$ fair words through (11); a flag history $e$ has probability $q^{\sum e_l}(1-q)^{K-\sum e_l}$. Its last-reset age in ticks is zero after a reset and otherwise increments by one. After $K$ ticks this age is $k$ with probability $q(1-q)^k$ for $0\le k<K$, and is $K$ with probability $(1-q)^K$. Formula (11), including rounding, determines the amplitude from that age. Flat intervals caused by finite precision are retained parts of this law.

3. **Full coupled response and mean-error certificate.** Couple each exact reset flag to the occupancy of a length-$\delta$ bin of the Poisson source. Distinct occupancies are independent and have probability $q$. The terminal grid age is $\delta\min(\lfloor A/\delta\rfloor,K)$, differing from $A_B$ by less than $\delta$ except at the harmless capped equality. Define
$$
\eta=2^{-h}+2^{1-f},\qquad
\epsilon=2\kappa\delta+2K\eta,\qquad
D=D_B+(1-e^{-\epsilon})\mu_X.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.13}
$$
The exact finite circuit and the ideal source have a coupling with
$$
 e^{-\epsilon}\min(X,H_B)\le\widehat X\le X_B\le X,
\qquad
W_1(\mathcal L(X),\mathcal L(\widehat X))
=\mathbb E(X-\widehat X)\le D.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.14}
$$
The same fair-sign coupling controls the teacher amplitudes and both matched raw squared scores; the normalized losses and their finite detector flags can be coupled exactly because (2) does not depend on amplitude. The source-to-circuit comparison retains the complete bin-occupancy history and nominal clock labels. Intrabin Poisson timestamps have been integrated into that registered projection.

For $x_0\le x<e^{-\epsilon}H_B$, the finite survival function obeys
$$
 e^{-\zeta\epsilon}(x_0/x)^\zeta
 \le\Pr(\widehat X>x)\le(x_0/x)^\zeta.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.15}
$$
Thus an actual finite-window survival response has a multiplicative envelope. The discrete finite output law and the continuous law in (6) are compared by (14)–(15) and the registered-bin metric below, rather than by their raw total variation.

For the explicit refinement $s=m$, $K=m2^m$, $h=f=3m$ with $m\ge1$, $B\ge m/\lambda$ and
$$
 \epsilon\le\frac{2\kappa}{\lambda}\,2^{1-m}+6m2^{-2m}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad D_B\le\frac{x_0}{\zeta-1}e^{-(1-1/\zeta)m}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.16}
$$
Hence these explicitly finite physical source laws converge in first Wasserstein distance to the owned Pareto response. Each resolution has its own complete clock and resource record; no uniform finite-cost continuum limit is imposed.

4. **Rank, bin and sampling records.** Use $N$ independent complete finite replicas and the product coupling in (14). Sort their selected scores in descending order with a fixed input-index tie rule. Then, for each $1\le r\le N$,
$$
 e^{-\epsilon}\min(X_{(r)},H_B)\le\widehat X_{(r)}\le X_{(r)},\qquad
0\le\mathbb EX_{(r)}-\mathbb E\widehat X_{(r)}\le ND.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.17}
$$
With probability at least $1-Ne^{-\lambda B}$, all ranks have $0\le\ln(X_{(r)}/\widehat X_{(r)})\le\epsilon$. For $0<u\le1$ define the finite generalized upper quantile by
$$
\widehat Q(u)=\inf\{x\ge x_0:\Pr(\widehat X>x)\le u\}.
$$
At $u=r/N$, its deterministic rank curve satisfies
$$
 e^{-\epsilon}\min(x_r,H_B)\le\widehat Q(r/N)\le x_r.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.18}
$$
Both the complete finite source probabilities and these generalized quantiles are certificate calculations obtained by summing the finite last-reset age law and the exact amplitude recurrence. The physical rank readout below is the sorted actual population; these analytic quantiles are not additional sampled outputs. Ties and stalls need no fictitious continuous interpolation.

For a preregistered bin partition with $b_0$ finite boundaries at or above $x_0$, use the same strict/right-closed convention in both responses. A population's complete binned word has a coupling error at most
$$
 N\left[e^{-\lambda B}+b_0(1-e^{-\zeta\epsilon})\right],
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.19}
$$
clipped to one. If sorted source identities are also retained in the compared response, add $\binom N2(1-e^{-\zeta\epsilon})$ for near-ties. This TV statement compares the registered binned-score projection, together with shared discrete sign, verifier, occupied-bin and nominal-clock labels; retained raw amplitudes use the value bounds above. Bin/rank labels, the complete unsorted records and the tie rule are all specified before sampling.

The population in (17) is random. For any registered rank set $\mathcal I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and $0<\rho<\min_{r\in\mathcal I}r/N$, the ideal independent population obeys, simultaneously except with probability $2|\mathcal I|e^{-2N\rho^2}$,
$$
 x_0\,[\min\{1,r/N+\rho\}]^{-1/\zeta}
 \le X_{(r)}\le x_0(r/N-\rho)^{-1/\zeta}
 \quad(r\in\mathcal I).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.20}
$$
Combining (17) with (20) gives the finite-source population band. These are independent-replica statements; successive samples from one renewal stream retain their dependence.

5. **Finite PCE branch and normalized realization.** At the chosen $(N,K,s,h,f,d,a,c)$ retain two complete protocols: the frozen run, where both committed forecasts are $j\widehat V/M$, and the selected run, where the preceding forecast is $j\widehat V/M$ and the active forecast is zero in every independent replica. Both forecasts precede the same later sign. Retain all finite coordinate restrictions of their whole-word outputs. On either protocol, let the two integer normalized-loss numerators be
$$
 T^\pm=(j^\pm-MS)^2\le4M^2,
\qquad Z^\pm=\mathbf1_{\{U^\pm<T^\pm\}},
\quad U^\pm\sim\mathrm{Unif}\{0,\ldots,4M^2-1\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.21}
$$
Each verifier uses $2d+2$ independent fair bits and a $2d+3$-bit threshold including the sentinel $4M^2$. The raw squared-error integers are $(A_K^{\rm dig})^2T^\pm$, with common task-unit decoder $x_0/(M^2 2^{2f})$. Conditional on the retained source and sign, the two loss flags have independent Bernoulli means $T^\pm/(4M^2)$. The complete response law is the product over replicas of the reset-history law, the fair sign and these two conditional Bernoulli kernels, with all integer, sort, setting and failure fields attached deterministically.

Take $\mathcal X_{\mathfrak B}=\mathcal J$, that finite protocol/restriction family, $K_{\mathfrak B}=\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$, $W_{\mathfrak B}=(0,\infty)^2$, and
$$
 r_{\mathfrak B}(j)=(\Gamma_0R(j),P_{\rm svc}),\qquad \Gamma_0>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.22}
$$
Here $\Gamma_0$ is a power-equivalent task tariff and $P_{\rm svc}$ is the common complete-run service power below. The response labels include the committed forecast integer, so the quotient separates the whole candidate grid; both resources descend to it. Every positive scalarization uniquely selects zero. The full source, teacher, score and rank records share one finite carrier. Its selected rank law is (12), with the controlled ideal identification (14)–(20).

6. **Explicit circuit and resource ownership.** Use signed or unsigned integer words as appropriate, with
$$
\begin{split}
 w&=32[K+f+d+c(h+1)+sa+N+s+h+16 ],\\
 B_w&=256w^2,\\
 Q_{\rm cfg}&=32(h+2)(c+8)+32(a+s+h+f+d+16),\\
 Q_{\rm init}&=16,\quad Q_{\rm tick}=32,\quad Q_{\rm obs}=64,\quad
 Q_{\rm sort}=8\binom N2.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.23}
$$
The elementary alphabet is retained-input NOT, AND, OR and XOR. Every word add/subtract, multiply, comparison, fixed shift, bounded integer divide or word selection uses a padded $B_w$ fresh-output Boolean-gate network. Setup computes (10), verifies the runtime forecast by direct comparisons $-M\le j\le M$, and replaces an invalid value by zero before multiplication, retaining the original and failure flag. All other displayed integer source parameters are fixed compilation inputs satisfying their stated inequalities.

Each replica first initializes its amplitude and age counter. Every tick draws its $s$ fair bits, computes the all-zero flag, performs the product and fixed shift in (11), retains the discarded remainder, and selects fresh reset or growth amplitude and age registers. All branches execute the same padded slots. After the last tick, both forecasts commit; the sign and both verifier words are then prepared. Exact integer arithmetic constructs the teacher, normalized and raw score fields and flags. A fixed descending bubble-sort network of $\binom N2$ adjacent compare/exchanges sorts the active raw-score integers and their input indices, exchanging only on strict inequality. Thus ties retain the fixed input order. Every displaced word remains in a fresh gate output or original register.

The complete coin, output, gate and retained-cell counts may be reserved as
$$
\begin{split}
 C_{\rm coin}&=N(sK+4d+5),\\
 O&=N(12w+4)+16w+1,\\
 G&=B_w[Q_{\rm cfg}+N(Q_{\rm init}+KQ_{\rm tick}+Q_{\rm obs})+Q_{\rm sort}]+O,\\
 R_{\rm bit}&=128w+C_{\rm coin}+G+O.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.24}
$$
The per-replica output words contain its index, original and active forecast integers, amplitude, signed teacher, two normalized-score numerators, two raw-score numerators, terminal age, sorted key and sorted source index. Its four bits retain the sign, two flags and admission information. The remaining output reserve contains source/precision/protocol headers and final status. The $128w$ input reserve contains source constants, controls and original forecast fields. Every coin, arithmetic/selection output and readout copy is a distinct owned cell; unused cells remain ready.

A source coin is prepared as $|+\rangle$ from a ready qubit by a Hadamard pulse, and its bit remains retained. Boolean primitives act as $|x,z\rangle\mapsto|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle$. These are finite unitary involutions. For such a primitive or a Hadamard, a duration-$\tau$ generator $H=\pi\hbar(I-U)/(2\tau)$ implements $U$ and has norm-action at most $\pi\hbar$. The final measurement acts on the $O$ public output cells, with identity on the retained private records, and includes every failure flag. It is a normalized instrument on the full finite carrier. Orthogonal retained coin words give precisely the complete classical response law described after (21), including the original fair bits as its dilation. Total source-plus-Boolean norm-action is at most $\pi\hbar(G+C_{\rm coin})$.

7. **Physical clock and implementation error.** Fix positive setup, ready, source, gate and readout times $\tau_{\rm set},\tau_r,\tau_c,\tau_g,\tau_m$, a guard $\tau_{\rm guard}>0$, and positive source-contract charges $E_{\rm set},e_r,e_c,e_g,e_m,P_0,p_r$. Sequential independent replicas have
$$
\begin{split}
T_{\rm prep}&=\tau_{\rm set}+R_{\rm bit}\tau_r+B_wQ_{\rm cfg}\tau_g,\\
\Delta_s&\ge s\tau_c+B_wQ_{\rm tick}\tau_g+\tau_{\rm guard},\\
T&=T_{\rm prep}+N[B_wQ_{\rm init}\tau_g+K\Delta_s+(4d+5)\tau_c+B_wQ_{\rm obs}\tau_g]
 +B_wQ_{\rm sort}\tau_g+O(\tau_g+\tau_m),\\
E&=E_{\rm set}+R_{\rm bit}e_r+C_{\rm coin}e_c+Ge_g+Oe_m
 +(P_0+R_{\rm bit}p_r)T,\qquad P_{\rm svc}=E/T.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.25}
$$
Setup includes the fixed circuit, wiring and controller preparation. The positive primitive service law is common across every candidate and both protocols. The nominal source tick $\delta$ and the physical service period $\Delta_s$ have this explicit ownership: $K\delta$ indexes the source model, while (25) is actual run time on the declared service class. The ideal comparison coefficients transported to physical tick labels are $(\kappa\delta/\Delta_s,\lambda\delta/\Delta_s)$, with invariant ratio $\lambda/(2\kappa)$; the exact finite reset probabilities and rounded gains retain (9)–(11). No claim identifies $\lambda$ with a fixed wall-time hazard while silently omitting circuit service. Public clock labels are registered indices and periods; residual physical timing errors have their own calibrated bounds.

Let $\epsilon_{\rm fin}$ bound the sum of source trace-distance and uniform half-diamond gate/readout errors, including retained ancillas and failure outcomes, clipped to one. It bounds total variation relative to the *exact finite* response instrument. For an arbitrary perturbed score word use its fixed decoder clipped to $[0,X_{\max}]$, where
$$
 X_{\max}=4x_0\,2^{2K}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.2d.26}
$$
bounds every ideal active squared loss in either protocol; retain the original word and all flags. Apply the same bounded decoder to each reported rank field, retaining every original sorted and unsorted word. For the implemented bounded reported rank $\widetilde X_{(r)}$, the resulting two-sided bound is $|\mathbb E\widetilde X_{(r)}-\mathbb EX_{(r)}|\le ND+X_{\max}\epsilon_{\rm fin}$; the ideal-to-finite one-sided ordering in (17) is not assigned to arbitrary implementation defects. Each compared finite binned-word TV bound acquires at most $\epsilon_{\rm fin}$. This preserves the finite-first-moment branch $\zeta>1$ without assuming an unproved variance bound or discarding failed trials.

*Proof.*
The independent fair sign has mean zero and second moment one. Expanding (2) proves (3), including its unique zero minimizer and exact adjacent-grid gap. At that configuration the teacher's actual square is $V^2$, proving the observable ownership (4). The matched gain formula follows before taking its expectation. Forecast commitment fixes its two operands before the sign; no realization replaces a future sample by an expected score.

If no reset occurs during a time interval of length $t$, the final age is $a+t$ and the event has probability $e^{-\lambda t}$. Otherwise the last reset has backward age $u\in(0,t)$ with density $\lambda e^{-\lambda u}$. This gives the normalized transition kernel (5). An exponential age followed by a fresh Poisson interval remains exponential, proving invariance. Two arbitrary initial ages driven by the same future resets agree after their first reset. Their law discrepancy is therefore at most $e^{-\lambda t}$, which proves uniqueness of the invariant law. The monotone change of variable $X=x_0e^{2\kappa A}$ yields (6), and integration of its survival function gives its first moment. All quantities needed for Theorem P.8.9a.12.2 and the finite-population part of Theorem P.8.9a.12.2c are now supplied by the actual selected task.

In a two-sided stationary reset history, either a reset occurs in the warm-up interval of length $B$ and both age constructions agree, or none occurs and the warm-up age is $B$ whereas the stationary age exceeds it. This is exactly the coupling (7). On $[0,B)$ both laws have the same exponential density; the remaining mass $e^{-\lambda B}$ is an atom at $B$ for the warm-up law and the continuous upper tail for the stationary law. Their total variation is therefore exactly that mass. Direct integration gives
$$
\mathbb E[(X-H_B)_+]
=\int_{H_B}^{\infty}(x_0/x)^\zeta\,dx
=\frac{x_0}{\zeta-1}e^{-(\lambda-2\kappa)B},
$$
proving (8). This uses the first-moment gate $\zeta>1$ and no second moment.

Since $q\le1/2$ and $a/c<1/2$, $1<g<\sqrt2<2$. Raising the gain comparison to the positive integer power $c$ gives exactly (10), so the bounded monotone bisection returns its largest admissible integer. In particular $P\ge2^h$. If $\gamma=P/2^h$, then $0\le g-\gamma<2^{-h}$ and
$$
0\le\ln(g/\gamma)\le(g-\gamma)/\gamma<2^{-h}.
$$
The all-zero test of $s$ retained fair bits has probability $q$ exactly, and independent fresh words give the complete flag-history law. An age of $k<K$ means its last reset was followed by precisely $k$ nonresets; age $K$ is the no-reset history. This proves its finite geometric-with-terminal-atom distribution. Even if distinct ages give the same rounded amplitude, their original histories remain retained.

For an integer $A\ge2^f$, the unrounded product $PA/2^h$ is at least $A$. Its floor is therefore at least $A$, so the fixed-point process never falls below its reset amplitude. Moreover,
$$
\lfloor\gamma A\rfloor\ge\gamma A(1-2^{-f}),\qquad
0\le\ln\frac{gA}{\lfloor\gamma A\rfloor}
\le2^{-h}-\ln(1-2^{-f})\le2^{-h}+2^{1-f}=\eta.
$$
The last inequality follows from $-\ln(1-u)\le2u$ for $0\le u\le1/2$. Iterating between the last reset and observation gives a log-amplitude deficit at most $K\eta$ relative to the unrounded geometric orbit. It also gives the pathwise upper bound by that orbit. A stall is an admitted exact integer update and obeys the same inequality.

Disjoint Poisson bins have independent occupancy probability $1-e^{-\lambda\delta}=q$, so their occupancies exactly realize the finite reset law. If the stationary age is $A<B$, its last occupied bin precedes the observation by $\delta\lfloor A/\delta\rfloor$; the omitted age is in $[0,\delta)$. If $A\ge B$, neither construction has a reset during warm-up and the ideal warm-up age and grid age both equal $B$. This establishes the terminal-age comparison and also couples every prefix of the finite source history to the corresponding occupied-bin projection. Squaring amplitudes doubles both log errors, giving the first inequality in (14). The coordinatewise order gives
$$
\mathbb E(X-\widehat X)
\le\mathbb E(X-X_B)+(1-e^{-\epsilon})\mathbb E X_B
\le D_B+(1-e^{-\epsilon})\mu_X.
$$
This monotone coupling attains the one-dimensional first Wasserstein distance, because its mean difference is a lower bound for the expected absolute difference under every coupling. Formula (14) follows. Using the same sign and verifier words preserves the normalized task response exactly; the unnormalized error at any other forecast has its known factor $(j/M-S)^2\le4$ multiplying the selected amplitude-square response.

If $x<e^{-\epsilon}H_B$, then $X>e^\epsilon x$ implies $e^{-\epsilon}\min(X,H_B)>x$, hence $\widehat X>x$. This proves the lower survival bound in (15); $\widehat X\le X$ gives the upper bound. For refinement, $q\le-\ln(1-q)\le q/(1-q)\le2q$, so $m2^m\delta\ge m/\lambda$ and $2\kappa\delta\le(2\kappa/\lambda)2^{1-m}$. The remaining term is $2m2^m(2^{-3m}+2^{1-3m})=6m2^{-2m}$. These facts prove (16) and convergence of the complete mean envelope.

Sorting is monotone in every coordinate. Apply it to the two componentwise bounds in (14); clipping at a common ceiling and multiplying by a positive constant commute with sorting. This gives the first part of (17). The sum of the nonnegative sorted differences equals the sum of the componentwise differences, so any single expected rank difference is at most $ND$. A union bound on the $N$ stationary ages exceeding $B$ proves the logarithmic-probability claim. Quantiles preserve stochastic order and commute with the same monotone clipping/scaling maps at $0<u<1$. At $u=1$, the source convention gives both lower-end quantiles $x_0$; the displayed inequality still holds. This proves (18), including discrete ties. The complete finite probabilities, or their sums over identical integer amplitudes, define the generalized quantile without an equality assumption for a discontinuous survival function.

For a bin boundary $b\ge x_0$, a downward log perturbation of size at most $\epsilon$ can cross it only when $X\in[b,be^\epsilon]$, apart from the warm-up tail event. Under the continuous ideal source this interval has probability $(x_0/b)^\zeta(1-e^{-\zeta\epsilon})\le1-e^{-\zeta\epsilon}$. A union over the registered boundaries and replicas proves (19); either consistent endpoint convention has the same bound because ideal endpoint masses vanish. The ideal log scores $\ln(X_i/x_0)$ are independent exponential variables of rate $\zeta$. Their pairwise difference has the two-sided exponential density $(\zeta/2)e^{-\zeta|u|}$, so a gap at most $\epsilon$ has probability $1-e^{-\zeta\epsilon}$. Outside those near-ties and the warm-up event, downward errors bounded by $\epsilon$ preserve every order. This gives the additional rank-identity term.

For the sampling band put $U_i=(x_0/X_i)^\zeta$. They are independent uniforms, and the $r$-th descending score corresponds to the $r$-th ascending uniform $U_{(r)}$. A lower deviation $U_{(r)}<r/N-\rho$ requires at least $r$ successes in $N$ independent Bernoulli trials of mean $r/N-\rho$. An upper deviation $U_{(r)}>r/N+\rho$ requires fewer than $r$ successes at the larger mean; if that threshold exceeds one, the event is empty. Hoeffding and a union over the registered rank set give the stated probability. Applying the decreasing function $x_0u^{-1/\zeta}$ proves (20), with the lower end truncated at the support floor. Combining this ideal population event with the deterministic coupling bounds gives its actual finite-source band.

Each integer score threshold in (21) lies between zero and $4M^2$. Exactly that many of its $4M^2$ equiprobable verifier words accept. Independent retained verifier words prove their conditional product kernel, including zero and unit losses. Combining it with the reset flags and independent later sign gives a normalized complete joint response. The source and scores remain on the same amplitude register: the raw error numerator is obtained by multiplying the actual squared amplitude by its actual normalized-error numerator. Both protocols retain the candidate labels, so Definition D.1f has the stated finite separating quotient. The strictly convex risk on its complete grid, together with the common service coordinate, proves the claimed PCE selection for every positive weighting.

We give the circuit details to check finiteness, arithmetic safety and the clock ledger. Repeated squaring or repeated integer multiplication computes the constant $(2^s-1)^a$; the chosen bound permits the latter's $a$ steps. Each of at most $h+2$ bisection rounds forms a midpoint, computes its $c$-th power, multiplies by that constant, compares to the fixed power of two and selects retained endpoints. Fewer than $c+16$ word operations suffice per round. Bounds checks, fixed constants, selector zero and safe forecast copies fit in the remaining $32(a+s+h+f+d+16)$ reserve. No runtime real logarithm or Poisson timestamp is required by this exact finite source; nominal $\delta$ is the separately registered clock formula (9).

A tick needs one all-zero comparison, one word multiplication, one fixed shift with its low-bit remainder retained, one reset/growth word selection, an incremented and reset-selected age counter, and index/control copies. Fewer than sixteen word slots suffice; $Q_{\rm tick}=32$ includes padding and retained transfers. The current input and all outputs have distinct cells. In the observation stage, both forecast descriptions commit before preparing the $4d+5$ fresh bits: one sign and two $(2d+2)$-bit verifier words. Multiplication by the sign gives the teacher; two subtract/square calculations give $T^\pm$; one amplitude square and two products give the raw scores; two comparisons give the flags. Transfers and the complete twelve-word record fit within the sixty-four observation slots. Initial amplitude/counter and forecast copies fit within sixteen initialization slots.

The fixed descending bubble-sort network has $\binom N2$ adjacent comparisons. Each compares the two keys and uses four word selections for their keys and indices. Its eight-slot reserve therefore suffices. A comparison exchanges only when the left key is strictly smaller, so equal keys preserve their input order. All previous arrays remain in the retained circuit history.

For width, $A_l^{\rm dig}\le2^f g^l<2^{f+l}$, and its product with $P$ has fewer than $f+K+h+2$ bits. Each raw score has fewer than $2(f+K)+2d+3$ bits. The root comparison has fewer than $c(h+1)+sa+2$ bits. Every age/index and unsigned/signed threshold fits well within $w$; the direct forecast bounds are checked before any multiply. The displayed word width exceeds these bounds by an ample fixed factor and contains the integer gate/resource metadata as well. Full adders, schoolbook multiplication and fixed-round long division give retained-bit circuits with quadratic gate count; comparisons, fixed shifts and multiplexed word selections have no larger count. As in the explicit circuits of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10d, fewer than $256w^2$ Boolean gates suffice for each operation. Ready-input padding makes the reservation exact. Source constants and the fixed algorithm/control template fit in the input reserve; the expanded gate circuit and its wiring are included in the setup contract.

There are $NsK$ reset coin bits and $N(4d+5)$ observation bits. The output fields have exactly the census stated after (24), with the header reserve covering the fixed source and format identifiers. Counting padded word gates and the final $O$ pointer copies gives $G$; allocating every coin, every gate output and each final readout cell separately gives $R_{\rm bit}$. Retained remainders and displaced reset amplitudes are already gate outputs, so no erasure or hidden workspace reuse is needed.

All declared elementary unitaries are involutions. The Hamiltonian formula applies zero phase on their $+1$ eigenspace and phase $-1$ on their $-1$ eigenspace, implementing them exactly. Hadamard-prepared source bits are retained throughout all controlled classical computations. Distinct source words thus remain orthogonal in private registers; tracing those registers at the final public measurement yields exactly the uniform source mixture and the classical word law. The projectors tensored with private identity sum to the full identity, proving instrument normalization for every carrier input, including failures. This also proves the norm-action bound.

The physical schedule in (25) owns every source preparation and Boolean slot, and all source-time ticks have their known physical period. The later sign preparation occurs after the relevant forecast commit inside the observation stage. Preparation, source calls, sorting, readout and the complete storage maintenance are charged once in the positive source service law. Equality of logical gate counts is not substituted for a physical switching-heat theorem. The source's numerical square has task units, while (25) is its physical energy account.

Finally, source trace-distance and uniform half-diamond errors telescope through the finite circuit, with private records treated as retained ancillas. Complete measurement cannot increase trace distance, so the exact finite word has the asserted total-variation envelope. The ideal score in either protocol is at most $4x_0g^{2K}<X_{\max}$, justifying the bounded decoder. Every reported clipped rank field lies in $[0,X_{\max}]$ and therefore has expectation error at most $X_{\max}\epsilon_{\rm fin}$. Any fixed binned or sorted-index readout contracts total variation. Combining this finite-to-implemented bound with the earlier continuous-to-finite value and bin bounds proves the final statement. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a123-conditional-1f-spectrum-from-log-flat-pce-relaxation-modes"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.3 (Conditional $1/f$ Spectrum from Log-Flat PCE Relaxation Modes).** Suppose an observed PCE-adapted aggregate has independent exponential relaxation modes whose unit-variance mode with relaxation rate $\lambda$ has two-sided spectrum
$$
S_{\lambda}(\omega)=\frac{2\lambda}{\lambda^2+\omega^2},
\qquad
\omega>0.
$$
Suppose further that, across the observed band, the relaxation-rate measure is logarithmically flat,
$$
d\mu(\lambda)=A\frac{d\lambda}{\lambda},
\qquad
A>0,
\qquad
\lambda\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}].
$$
Then the mixed spectrum is
$$
S(\omega)
=
\frac{2A}{\omega}
\left[
\arctan\left(\frac{\lambda_{\max}}{\omega}\right)
-
\arctan\left(\frac{\lambda_{\min}}{\omega}\right)
\right].
\tag{P.8.9a.12.3}
$$
In the intermediate window $\lambda_{\min}\ll\omega\ll\lambda_{\max}$,
$$
S(\omega)=\frac{\pi A}{\omega}
+
O\left(\frac{A\lambda_{\min}}{\omega^2}
+
\frac{A}{\lambda_{\max}}\right),
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4}
$$
with the explicit bound
$$
\left|S(\omega)-\frac{\pi A}{\omega}\right|
\le
\frac{2A}{\omega}
\left(
\frac{\lambda_{\min}}{\omega}
+
\frac{\omega}{\lambda_{\max}}
\right).
$$

*Proof.* The mixture spectrum is
$$
S(\omega)
=
\int_{\lambda_{\min}}^{\lambda_{\max}}
\frac{2\lambda}{\lambda^2+\omega^2}
A\frac{d\lambda}{\lambda}
=
2A\int_{\lambda_{\min}}^{\lambda_{\max}}
\frac{d\lambda}{\lambda^2+\omega^2}.
$$
Since
$$
\int\frac{d\lambda}{\lambda^2+\omega^2}
=
\frac1{\omega}\arctan\left(\frac{\lambda}{\omega}\right),
$$
Equation (P.8.9a.12.3) follows. Also
$$
0\le \arctan u\le u
\quad (u\ge0),
$$
and
$$
0\le \frac{\pi}{2}-\arctan v=\arctan(1/v)\le \frac1v
\quad (v>0).
$$
Therefore
$$
\left|
\arctan\left(\frac{\lambda_{\max}}{\omega}\right)
-
\arctan\left(\frac{\lambda_{\min}}{\omega}\right)
-
\frac{\pi}{2}
\right|
\le
\frac{\omega}{\lambda_{\max}}
+
\frac{\lambda_{\min}}{\omega}.
$$
Multiplying by $2A/\omega$ gives the stated bound and the asymptotic $1/\omega$ law. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a124-stretched-exponential-relaxation-from-stable-subordinated-pce-modes"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.4 (Stretched-Exponential Relaxation from Stable-Subordinated PCE Modes).** Let $0<\alpha\le1$ and $\tau>0$. Suppose a PCE relaxation observable is a positive mixture of exponential modes
$$
\Phi(t)=\int_0^{\infty}e^{-\lambda t}\,d\mu_{\alpha,\tau}(\lambda),
\qquad
t\ge0,
$$
where $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}$ is the probability measure whose Laplace transform is
$$
\int_0^{\infty}e^{-\lambda t}\,d\mu_{\alpha,\tau}(\lambda)
=
\exp[-(t/\tau)^{\alpha}].
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5}
$$
Then
$$
\Phi(t)=\exp[-(t/\tau)^{\alpha}].
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6}
$$
For $\alpha=1$ this reduces to ordinary exponential relaxation with rate $1/\tau$; for $0<\alpha<1$ it is the Kohlrausch-Williams-Watts stretched exponential.

*Proof.* For every $t\ge0$, the definition of the observable and the assumed Laplace-transform identity give
$$
\Phi(t)
=\int_0^\infty e^{-\lambda t}\,d\mu_{\alpha,\tau}(\lambda)
=\exp[-(t/\tau)^\alpha],
$$
which is (P.8.9a.12.6). If $\alpha=1$, this expression is $e^{-t/\tau}$, the ordinary exponential relaxation law with rate $1/\tau$. If $0<\alpha<1$, the same expression is, by definition, the Kohlrausch--Williams--Watts stretched exponential. No existence theorem for $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}$ is needed because existence and the transform identity are hypotheses of the theorem. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a124a-existence-exponent-range-and-finite-mode-realization-of-the-stable-relaxation-measure"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.4a (Existence, Exponent Range and Finite-Mode Realization of the Stable Relaxation Measure).** Let $\tau>0$ and $\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}(t):=\exp[-(t/\tau)^\alpha]$.

1. *Existence and uniqueness.* For $0<\alpha\le1$ there is exactly one Borel probability measure $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying (P.8.9a.12.5), and $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}(\{0\})=0$. For $\alpha=1$, $\mu_{1,\tau}=\delta_{1/\tau}$. For $\alpha=1/2$,
$$
d\mu_{1/2,\tau}(\lambda)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi\tau}}\,\lambda^{-3/2}e^{-1/(4\tau\lambda)}\,d\lambda,
\qquad
\mu_{1/2,\tau}([0,\lambda])=\operatorname{erfc}\bigl((4\tau\lambda)^{-1/2}\bigr).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4a.1}
$$
For $\alpha=2^{-j}$ with $j\ge1$, $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}$ is the law of $\tau^{-1}L_1L_2^{2}\cdots L_j^{2^{j-1}}$, where $L_1,\ldots,L_j$ are independent with law $\mu_{1/2,1}$.
2. *Exponent range.* For $\alpha>1$ no positive measure satisfies (P.8.9a.12.5).
3. *Tails.* For $0<\alpha<1$ and $x>0$,
$$
\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([0,x))\le\exp\!\left[-(1-\alpha)\alpha^{\alpha/(1-\alpha)}(\tau x)^{-\alpha/(1-\alpha)}\right],
\qquad
\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([x,\infty))\le\frac{(\tau x)^{-\alpha}}{1-e^{-1}}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4a.2}
$$
4. *Finite-mode realization.* Let $\lambda_i=\lambda_0q^i$ for $0\le i\le N$, with $\lambda_0>0$, $q>1$ and $N\ge1$, and put $w_0=\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([0,\lambda_1))$, $w_i=\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([\lambda_i,\lambda_{i+1}))$ for $1\le i<N$, and $w_N=\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([\lambda_N,\infty))$. The finite Markov relaxation in which an excited unit enters mode $i$ with probability $w_i$ and decays from it at rate $\lambda_i$ has survival function $\Phi_N(t)=\sum_{i=0}^Nw_ie^{-\lambda_it}$, and
$$
\sup_{t\ge0}\bigl|\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}(t)-\Phi_N(t)\bigr|
\le
\max\bigl\{\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([0,\lambda_0)),\ \delta(q)+\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([\lambda_N,\infty))\bigr\},
\qquad
\delta(q):=(1-q^{-1})\,q^{-1/(q-1)}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4a.3}
$$
For $0<\alpha<1$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, the choices $q=1+\varepsilon/2$,
$$
\lambda_0\le\tau^{-1}\Bigl[\frac{(1-\alpha)\alpha^{\alpha/(1-\alpha)}}{\ln(1/\varepsilon)}\Bigr]^{(1-\alpha)/\alpha},
\qquad
\lambda_0q^N\ge\tau^{-1}\Bigl[\frac{2}{(1-e^{-1})\varepsilon}\Bigr]^{1/\alpha},
$$
make the uniform error at most $\varepsilon$. A unit that decays at a random rate $\Lambda$ with law $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}$ has survival function exactly $\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}$.

*Proof.* For item 1, put $h(t)=(t/\tau)^\alpha$. For $0<\alpha\le1$, $(-1)^k\,d^k(t^{\alpha-1})/dt^k=(1-\alpha)(2-\alpha)\cdots(k-\alpha)t^{\alpha-1-k}\ge0$, so $h'$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$. For $g=e^{-h}$, the identity $g'=-h'g$ and Leibniz's rule give
$$
(-1)^{n+1}g^{(n+1)}=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk\bigl[(-1)^kh^{(k+1)}\bigr]\bigl[(-1)^{n-k}g^{(n-k)}\bigr],
$$
and induction on $n$ gives $(-1)^ng^{(n)}\ge0$ for every $n$. Thus $\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}$ is completely monotone on $(0,\infty)$, continuous on $[0,\infty)$ and equal to $1$ at $0$. Bernstein's theorem on completely monotone functions gives exactly one Borel probability measure on $[0,\infty)$ with Laplace transform $\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}$, and dominated convergence gives $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}(\{0\})=\lim_{t\to\infty}\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}(t)=0$. For $\alpha=1$ the transform of $\delta_{1/\tau}$ is $e^{-t/\tau}$. For $a,b>0$, the increasing substitution $u=\sqrt{b\lambda}-\sqrt{a/\lambda}$ of $(0,\infty)$ onto $\mathbb R$ satisfies $a/\lambda+b\lambda=u^2+2\sqrt{ab}$ and gives
$$
\int_0^\infty\bigl(\sqrt b\,\lambda^{-1/2}+\sqrt a\,\lambda^{-3/2}\bigr)e^{-a/\lambda-b\lambda}\,d\lambda=2\sqrt\pi\,e^{-2\sqrt{ab}}
$$
and the involution $\lambda\mapsto a/(b\lambda)$ shows that the two terms contribute equally. Hence $\int_0^\infty\lambda^{-3/2}e^{-a/\lambda-b\lambda}\,d\lambda=\sqrt{\pi/a}\,e^{-2\sqrt{ab}}$, and monotone convergence extends this to $b=0$. With $a=1/(4\tau)$ and $b=t$, the density in (P.8.9a.12.4a.1) has total mass $1$ and Laplace transform $e^{-\sqrt{t/\tau}}$. The substitution $y=(4\tau\lambda)^{-1/2}$ turns its distribution function into $(2/\sqrt\pi)\int_{(4\tau\lambda)^{-1/2}}^\infty e^{-y^2}\,dy$. For the dyadic case, let $S_j:=L_1L_2^2\cdots L_j^{2^{j-1}}$. Then $\mathbb Ee^{-tS_1}=e^{-t^{1/2}}$, and $S_{j+1}=L_1S_j'^2$ with $S_j'=L_2L_3^2\cdots L_{j+1}^{2^{j-1}}$ independent of $L_1$ and distributed as $S_j$. Conditioning on $S_j'$ gives $\mathbb E[e^{-tL_1S_j'^2}\mid S_j']=e^{-\sqrt t\,S_j'}$, so $\mathbb Ee^{-tS_{j+1}}=e^{-(\sqrt t)^{2^{-j}}}=e^{-t^{2^{-j-1}}}$. The variable $\tau^{-1}S_j$ therefore has transform $\Phi_{2^{-j},\tau}$, and uniqueness identifies its law with $\mu_{2^{-j},\tau}$.

For item 2, a positive representing measure makes $\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}''(t)=\int\lambda^2e^{-\lambda t}\,d\mu(\lambda)\ge0$ on $(0,\infty)$. For $\alpha>1$,
$$
\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}''(t)=\alpha\tau^{-\alpha}t^{\alpha-2}\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}(t)\bigl[\alpha(t/\tau)^\alpha-(\alpha-1)\bigr]<0
\qquad\text{for }0<(t/\tau)^\alpha<(\alpha-1)/\alpha .
$$

For item 3, $\mathbf 1\{\lambda<x\}\le e^{z(x-\lambda)}$ for $z>0$ gives $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([0,x))\le\exp[zx-(z/\tau)^\alpha]$, and minimization over $z$ gives the first bound. Also $1-e^{-\lambda/x}\ge(1-e^{-1})\mathbf 1\{\lambda\ge x\}$, so integration gives $\mu_{\alpha,\tau}([x,\infty))\le(1-\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}(1/x))/(1-e^{-1})$, and $1-e^{-y}\le y$ gives the second bound.

For item 4, the finite chain has survival function $\sum_iw_ie^{-\lambda_it}$ because the mode is drawn once and the exit time from mode $i$ is exponential with rate $\lambda_i$. Let $\varpi(\lambda)$ be $\lambda_0$ for $\lambda<\lambda_1$, $\lambda_i$ for $\lambda\in[\lambda_i,\lambda_{i+1})$ with $1\le i<N$, and $\lambda_N$ for $\lambda\ge\lambda_N$. Then $\Phi_N(t)=\int e^{-\varpi(\lambda)t}\,d\mu_{\alpha,\tau}(\lambda)$. The difference $e^{-\lambda t}-e^{-\varpi(\lambda)t}$ lies in $[0,1]$ for $\lambda<\lambda_0$, in $[-1,0]$ for $\lambda\ge\lambda_N$, and in $[-\delta(q),0]$ for $\lambda_0\le\lambda<\lambda_N$, because there $\varpi(\lambda)\le\lambda<q\varpi(\lambda)$ and $\sup_{y\ge0}(e^{-y}-e^{-qy})=\delta(q)$, attained at $y=\ln q/(q-1)$. Integration gives (P.8.9a.12.4a.3). For the stated choices, item 3 bounds the two tail masses by $\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon/2$, and $\delta(q)\le1-q^{-1}\le\varepsilon/2$. Finally, conditioning on $\Lambda$ gives survival probability $\mathbb Ee^{-\Lambda t}=\Phi_{\alpha,\tau}(t)$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a124b-source-derived-kww-relaxation-of-a-quenched-predictive-rc-memory"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.4b (Source-Derived KWW Relaxation of a Quenched Predictive RC Memory).** Consider the grounded, equal-teacher specialization of the predictive RC source of Theorem X.8k.6e. Its two positive feedback conductances have sum $G>0$, its forecast is the dimensionless capacitor voltage $x$, both held teachers are $0$, and the registered proper loss is $\mathrm{PE}(x,0)=x^2$, obtained by dividing the active loss of that source by its fixed positive value at $x=1$. The voltage unit is $V_0>0$. Preparation starts with a fresh zero-voltage capacitor and both feedback resistors disconnected. In a fixed interval $\tau_s>0$ an ideal controlled-current source sets $x_{\rm pre}(u)=u/\tau_s$ for $0\le u\le\tau_s$, with current $CV_0/\tau_s$ and work $W_{\rm prep}=CV_0^2/2$. It then disconnects the preparation supply, connects the feedback resistors and starts the relaxation clock at $x(0)=1$. Configuration/quench overhead is charged below. Ohm's law, the capacitor law and Kirchhoff balance give $C\dot x=-Gx$ while the held capacitance is positive. The optional teacher-to-teacher resistor has zero voltage on this task. The source includes the prescribed nonloading probes and isolated control/record ports below.

Fix a nonnegative integer controller depth $k$, a capacitance scale $C_0>0$, and the source laws
$$
Z_1,\ldots,Z_k\ \text{independent }N(0,1),\qquad
C=C_0\prod_{j=1}^k Z_j^{\,2^j}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.1}
$$
The empty product is $1$. On any coordinate-zero preparation, the total source map sets $C=C_0$; that set has probability zero under the displayed continuous law. The controller forms the indicated powers by repeated squaring and holds the resulting capacitance throughout the trial. The Gaussian preparation, controller depth, conductances, units, proper task and initial forecast are primitive design inputs. Neither a relaxation curve nor fitted $(\alpha,\tau)$ enters this controller. These are ideal analog source laws with finitely specified parameters; the continuous preparation permits unbounded capacitances and bandwidth. The finite capacitor-bank implementation is specified in item 4.

**Observation and service contract.** A trial additionally prepares one independent $U\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$ and retains it unchanged. A public query at time $t\ge0$ returns
$$
B(t)=\mathbf1\{U<x(t)^2\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.2}
$$
Every finite query word has a registered finite horizon $H>0$ and a maximum of $m\ge1$ increasing query times. A later time may depend on the retained earlier flags and on an exposed coarse mode label when specified. The public record contains registered nominal query-time labels, query indices and common release labels. Every primitive has a fixed source-independent service duration; preparation occupies a fixed padded interval $H_{\rm prep}>0$ before the common trial origin. All reserved cells and bank hardware are present from the start of that interval. A read uses a fixed delay $d_{\rm obs}>0$ for its sample, square, two comparisons and release, and every admitted fixed or adaptive read list places its next sample after the preceding release. The release delay includes a guard for the largest registered late-sampling residual plus the service pipeline. The finite horizon includes the last release. The actual physical sampling-time residual and the private controller timestamps are outside the public record. The precision comparison below retains identical public labels and release slots; exporting perturbed physical timestamps would define a different marked experiment. Each reserved slot uses the same nonloading sample, square, comparison and release schedule, including dummy operations when a branch makes fewer reads. The public threshold is prepared once; it is not redrawn at queries. The source permits no operation changing $C,G$, the teachers or the capacitor state during relaxation. Its preparation variables, $U$, raw voltage/loss values and energy records are retained in a private archive with no public or feedback return path.

Private task verification uses an independent fresh $W\sim\mathrm{Unif}(0,1)$ at each registered snapshot and records the bit $\mathbf1\{W<x^2\}$, together with the actual analog forecast/task record. Its Bernoulli parameter is the same proper expected loss $x^2$. The outcomes are fixed typed loss-bit labels, with label-preserving equality of response laws. This finite-outcome response law separates every $x\in[0,1]$; a realized bit is not identified with its expectation. This internal verification port and the public held-$U$ port have distinct source randomness, response cuts and records. In the finite-threshold implementation, mode/controller/clock/sensing errors are jointly bounded on their declared source range and their source dependence is retained.

Here is one complete finite-word service ledger for the admitted ideal apparatus. All coefficients in it are positive, finitely specified design tariffs fixed before responses. A Gaussian draw costs $e_G$, a uniform draw costs $e_U$, an arithmetic operation costs $e_a$, a comparison costs $e_c$, a nonloading voltage snapshot costs $e_v$, and a timed record release costs $e_o$. A fresh scalar/bit record allocation and its initialized write cost $e_r$; each allocated cell has maintenance power $p_r$. The private clock and isolated controller have power $p_0$. A held-capacitance configuration costs $e_s+e_C C/C_0$. The fixed infrastructure charge $e_s$ and controller power $p_0$ own the feedback resistors, isolation switches, sampler/controller housing and source interfaces. For a finite bank also charge $E_{\rm bank}=e_B\sum_{i=0}^N C_i/C_0$ and maintenance $P_{\rm bank}=p_B(N+1)$, with positive $e_B,p_B$, for all its capacitor/switch hardware, including unselected capacitors; those remain uncharged. For the continuous programmable-capacitance service set $E_{\rm bank}=P_{\rm bank}=0$ and include its housing in $e_s,p_0$. Preparation work $W_{\rm prep}$ is retained as capacitor inventory and accounted for separately below. Ideal hold, isolation and nonloading are constitutive entries: during discharge the capacitor has exactly the two resistor currents and no unrecorded control current. These positive service tariffs are charged to their isolated supplies; they are separate from capacitor energy and resistor heat.

For the finite bank of item 4 use its integer $N$, and for the continuous family use $N=0$ and dummy selector slots. Reserve
$$
A=\frac{k(k+3)}2+m+2,\qquad D=k+N+2m+2,\qquad
R=64+(k+m+2)+A+D+3(m+1)+2(N+1).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.3}
$$
The controller uses $\sum_{j=1}^k j$ squarings, $k$ product multiplications and one rate division; the $m+1$ verification snapshots use one square each. Thus $A$ arithmetic slots suffice. The $k$ coordinate-zero tests, one product-zero test, at most $N$ bin comparisons, and $2m+1$ public/private threshold comparisons fit in $D$ slots. The product-zero result controls the configured replacement $C_0$ before rate division; its switch routing is included in the configuration service. Pad unused slots. The $k+m+2$ random-source records hold the Gaussian draws, the public $U$ and $m+1$ private thresholds. The remaining record groups hold every arithmetic and comparison output, voltage snapshots, clock labels, public releases, the bank coefficient pairs $(\lambda_i,C_i)$ and up to $64$ fixed design/ledger scalars. The coefficient pairs are predeclared manufactured source records, charged by bank acquisition and initialized record allocation; no uncounted online grid generation is used. The energy record is the retained actual $C$, each sampled $x^2$, and the fixed unit factors, sufficient to reconstruct (11). Formula (3) does not charge or claim a separate online evaluation of all reconstructed energy values. Every overwritten scratch value, if a primitive uses scratch internally, is retained in that primitive's declared environment; the displayed interface records use fresh cells. There is no reset or closed-reuse step.

Define the external-service charge and its declared amortized power on this finite word by
$$
\begin{split}
E_{\rm svc}(C)&=e_s+e_C C/C_0+k e_G+(m+2)e_U+A e_a+D e_c
 +(m+1)(e_v+e_o)+R e_r+E_{\rm bank}+(p_0+Rp_r+P_{\rm bank})(H_{\rm prep}+H),\\
P_{\rm fix}(C)&=\frac{E_{\rm svc}(C)}{H}.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.4}
$$
The acquisition, configuration, representation, verification/processing, record and maintenance entries are therefore all supplied. The objective charges electrical dissipation once: $\int_0^H P_R(t)dt=W_{\rm prep}-E_C(H)$. The source balance is $E_{\rm svc}+W_{\rm prep}=E_{\rm svc}+Q_R(0,H)+E_C(H)$, where remaining capacitor energy is retained inventory, not a second consumed-energy charge. The displayed amortization is an accounting convention for a fixed prepared apparatus and reserved word; it is not its instantaneous electrical power. Additional source ports or state-dependent service costs require their own entries and alter the admitted branch. The exact formulas below hold on the stipulated ideal class. A finite-precision source supplies the independent residual entries in item 5.

Then the following statements hold.

1. **Actual predictive descent and the populated PCE branch.** For every prepared $C>0$,
$$
x_C(t)=e^{-Gt/C},\quad p_C(t):=\frac{\mathrm{PE}(x_C(t),0)}{\mathrm{PE}(1,0)}=e^{-\Lambda t},\quad
\Lambda=\frac{2G}{C},\quad
\mathrm{PE}(1,0)-\mathrm{PE}(x_C(t),0)=1-e^{-\Lambda t}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.5}
$$
The voltage and error rates differ by a factor two. Every positive finite interval strictly improves the fixed scored task along a nonzero trajectory.

For the fixed-$C$ configuration class $\mathcal X_C=[0,1]$, retain the single instantaneous internal binary verification protocol and its empty restriction. The response presheaf has outcome spaces $\{0,1\}$ and $\{*\}$, with the unique restriction map. The registered response equivalence preserves the numerical loss-bit labels, or equivalently the retained score observable; a bit-flip isomorphism is not an admitted equivalence. Its full nontrivial labeled law is $\mathrm{Bernoulli}(x^2)$, so equality implies $x=y$ and the response quotient is $[0,1]$ itself. Choose $K_C=\mathbb R_+^3$, $W_C=\{(1,1,1)\}$ and the resource vector
$$
r_C(x)=\bigl(GV_0^2x^2,\ \Gamma_0x^2,\ P_{\rm fix}(C)\bigr),\qquad \Gamma_0>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.6}
$$
The first entry is actual resistor power, the second is the independently registered task-value charge and the third is the complete fixed external-service amortization. In Definition 7's normalized score, $PP(x)=(1+\kappa_{\rm PE}x^2)^{-1}$ with fixed $\kappa_{\rm PE}>0$. The relative-to-perfect benefit $b(PP)=-(PP^{-1}-1)/\kappa_{\rm PE}=-x^2$ is increasing in $PP$ and lies in $[-1,0]$. Thus $\Gamma_0x^2$ is minus this benefit in the registered power-equivalent task units; it is not additional heat. This specifies a Definition-15/Definition-D.1f branch. Its scalarization and actual adaptation satisfy
$$
V_C(x)=P_{\rm fix}(C)+(GV_0^2+\Gamma_0)x^2,\qquad
\dot x=-M_C V_C'(x),\qquad
M_C=\frac{G}{2C(GV_0^2+\Gamma_0)}>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.7}
$$
The interval is invariant, $V_C$ has unique minimum $x=0$, and $\dot V_C=-M_C(V_C')^2<0$ for $x>0$. Each finite-$C$ trajectory converges to that minimum. This is a direct minimum and convergence proof for the stated branch; it invokes no additional global census or PCE-attractor clauses. The quenched $C$ and its source distribution are fixed task inputs in this comparison; optimizing among different preparation distributions is a separate comparison class. The branch uses the finite-outcome internal verification family. The public flag realization below uses its own retained family.

2. **Independently determined relaxation law.** The source (P.8.9a.12.4b.1) determines
$$
\alpha=2^{-k},\qquad \tau=\frac{C_0}{2^{2^k}G},\qquad
\Phi(t):=\mathbb E\,p_C(t)=\mathbb P\{B(t)=1\}=e^{-(t/\tau)^\alpha}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.8}
$$
Here $\tau$ has units of time. At depth zero the single rate is $2G/C_0$. At depth one the derived rate has density and distribution
$$
f_\Lambda(\lambda)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{\pi\tau}}\lambda^{-3/2}e^{-1/(4\tau\lambda)},\qquad
F_\Lambda(\lambda)=\operatorname{erfc}((4\tau\lambda)^{-1/2}).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.9}
$$
The mean normalized loss/power and the flag-survival frequency are distinct sample-level observables with the same expectation. The source law fixes which one is retained before a comparison. Its dyadic exponent is determined by controller depth; no inference of a generic non-dyadic physical exponent is part of this source family.

3. **Complete prepared-ensemble process realization and energy.** Set $T_*=-\log U/\Lambda$. Conditional on $\Lambda$, $T_*$ has exponential law of rate $\Lambda$, and $B(t)=\mathbf1\{t<T_*\}$. For a finite bank with mode $i$ and rate $\lambda_i$, the state $i$ while alive and an absorbing state $\dagger$ after exit has kernel
$$
K_s(i,i)=e^{-\lambda_i s},\quad K_s(i,\dagger)=1-e^{-\lambda_i s},\quad K_s(\dagger,\dagger)=1.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.10}
$$
The complete finite-word law is its normalized causal product with initial mode weights. An external immutable mode label may be retained as an additional mark through absorption. Unmarked binary histories are its postprocessing. Prefix restriction, common postprocessing and every finite noninvasive adaptive time-query policy on this retained history commute with the source map. For the continuous source the same conditional exponential law is mixed over its derived $\Lambda$; retaining only a coarse bin does not generally make that mixture a time-homogeneous finite-state chain.

This is a response-law realization under the specified prepared ensemble and protocol cut. Conditioning on the hidden $(C,U)$ gives a deterministic crossing time, and the capacitor continues its electrical relaxation after the public flag becomes zero. The chain represents the named relaxation-response process. Full analog-state, hidden-threshold or reset protocols require their own source response, and are outside this cut.

The actual discharge has zero boundary work and
$$
P_R(t\mid C)=GV_0^2 e^{-2Gt/C},\quad
E_C(t)=\frac{CV_0^2}{2}e^{-2Gt/C},\quad
Q_R(0,t\mid C)=\frac{CV_0^2}{2}(1-e^{-2Gt/C}),\quad
E_C(t)+Q_R(0,t\mid C)=E_C(0).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.11}
$$
In particular $P_R\le GV_0^2$. Put $n=2^k$ and $s=(t/\tau)^{1/n}$. The source moments and mean electrical ledger are
$$
\begin{split}
\mathbb EC&=C_0\prod_{j=1}^k(2^j-1)!!=C_0\frac{n!}{2^{n-1}},\qquad
\mathbb EC^2=C_0^2\prod_{j=1}^k(2^{j+1}-1)!!,\\
\mathbb E P_R(t)&=GV_0^2e^{-s},\qquad
\mathbb E E_C(t)=GV_0^2\tau n!\,e^{-s}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\frac{s^j}{j!},\\
\mathbb E Q_R(0,t)&=\mathbb E E_C(0)-\mathbb E E_C(t).
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.12}
$$
Every fixed depth has finite mean initial energy, total resistor heat and service charge (4). For $k\ge1$, arbitrarily small $C$ gives unbounded rate and infinite mean $\Lambda$, while arbitrarily large $C$ gives unbounded storage. The finite mean power and energy formulas do not impose a finite worst-case bandwidth or preparation cost on that ideal family. A finite bank has both positive minimum capacitance and finite maximum capacitance.

4. **Source-built finite bank, full-history remainder and energy remainder.** For $k\ge1$ use the geometric grid and bin map $\varpi$ of Theorem P.8.9a.12.4a, with $\lambda_i=\lambda_0q^i$, $q>1$, $0\le i\le N$, and build held capacitances $C_i=2G/\lambda_i$. The preparation controller draws the source Gaussians and selects the bin $I$ of its derived rate $\Lambda$; it then connects capacitor $C_I$. All source draws and comparisons, including both tails, are retained in the ledger. Its probabilities are the actual source-bin probabilities $w_i=\mathbb P(I=i)$, equal to the weights in that theorem. They are nonnegative and sum to one. At $k=1$ equation (9) gives every weight explicitly by differences of $\operatorname{erfc}$ values. At arbitrary finite depth the product Gaussian law and its total bin map give the probabilities without fitted relaxation inputs. At $k=0$ one capacitor realizes the exact ordinary exponential.

The bank and its public flag realize exactly the finite mode chain (10), with survival $\Phi_N(t)=\sum_iw_i e^{-\lambda_it}$. Put
$$
p_-=\mathbb P(\Lambda<\lambda_0),\quad p_+=\mathbb P(\Lambda\ge\lambda_N),\quad
\delta(q)=(1-q^{-1})q^{-1/(q-1)},\quad
\epsilon_{\rm curve}=\max\{p_-,\delta(q)+p_+\}.
$$
Then
$$
\sup_{t\ge0}|\Phi(t)-\Phi_N(t)|\le\epsilon_{\rm curve},\qquad
\operatorname{TV}\bigl(\mathcal L(I,T_*),\mathcal L(I,T_{*,N})\bigr)
\le\epsilon_{\rm path}:=\min\{1,p_-+p_++\delta(q)\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.13}
$$
The common mark $I$ is the same coarse source bin in both laws. The comparison does not export continuous $\Lambda$ from one source and a discrete rate from the other. Every retained finite or adaptive flagged history is a postprocessing of that marked lifetime, so it has the same total-variation bound. The two lifetime laws need not use the same threshold realization in a coupling that attains total variation.

For the source-coupled pair $C$ and $C_I=2G/\varpi(\Lambda)$, define
$$
D_C:=\frac{\lambda_0}{2G}\mathbb EC^2+(q-1)\mathbb EC+\frac{2G}{\lambda_N}.
$$
Then, uniformly over $t\ge0$,
$$
\mathbb E|C_I-C|\le D_C,\quad
|\mathbb E E_{C_I}(t)-\mathbb E E_C(t)|\le\frac{V_0^2D_C}{2},\quad
|\mathbb E Q_{R,I}(0,t)-\mathbb E Q_R(0,t)|\le\frac{V_0^2D_C}{2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.14}
$$
Mean power error is at most $GV_0^2\epsilon_{\rm curve}$. At a common service schedule, the mean configuration-charge discrepancy is at most $(e_C/C_0)D_C$; mean preparation-energy discrepancy has the first bound in (14). Sending $q\downarrow1$, $\lambda_0\downarrow0$ and $\lambda_N\uparrow\infty$ makes these bounds vanish. Thus a chosen finite bank carries explicit response, discharge-energy and selected-capacitor configuration remainders. Its separate bank acquisition, record and maintenance entries generally grow with resolution and are retained as actual costs; convergence or optimality of total apparatus cost is not inferred from these remainders.

5. **Finite implementation, clocks and sampling.** Fix a normalized nonnegative implemented mode law $\widetilde w$ and $\eta_w=\operatorname{TV}(\widetilde w,w)$. A finite Gaussian/controller representation maps every code, including zero, clipping and overflow, to a specified positive bank mode; its distributional/selection discrepancy is included in $\eta_w$. Tail trials are retained. Suppose each actual mode is a held positive one-pole source with $|G'/G-1|\le g<1$ and $|C_i'/C_i-1|\le c<1$. Set
$$
r_{\rm cal}=\max\!\left\{\frac{1+g}{1-c},\frac{1+c}{1-g}\right\},\qquad
\lambda'_{\max}=\lambda_N\frac{1+g}{1-c},\qquad \delta(1):=0.
$$
With an exact independent continuous threshold, the full marked-lifetime discrepancy from the ideal continuous source is at most $\epsilon_{\rm path}+\eta_w+\delta(r_{\rm cal})$, capped at $1$. For one-time mean response, replace $\epsilon_{\rm path}$ by $\epsilon_{\rm curve}$.

A finite threshold source has Kolmogorov discrepancy $\eta_U=\sup_{0\le u\le1}|\mathbb P(\widetilde U<u)-u|$, independently of the mode and trajectory; midpoint $b$-bit uniform thresholds have $\eta_U\le2^{-b-1}$. The one-time error gains $\eta_U$. A finite digital threshold has a discrete lifetime in each fixed mode and therefore does not have small total variation from a continuous lifetime. For a fixed list of $m$ read times, its complete monotone-flag history has total-variation discrepancy at most $m\eta_U$. For a general policy with at most $m$ binary reads, a bound $(2^m-1)\eta_U$ follows by counting distinct thresholds in its fixed decision tree; common external randomization can be conditioned on first. These finite-history bounds, rather than a continuous-path claim, are the finite-threshold route.

At one query, a clock perturbation bounded by $|t'-t|\le\eta_t$, a clipped voltage error at most $\eta_x$, and an additional normalized square/comparison threshold error at most $\eta_a$ give the threshold-value bound
$$
\eta_p=\lambda'_{\max}\eta_t+2\eta_x+\eta_a.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.15}
$$
Here both actual and nominal sample times are nonnegative; clock error may have either sign. Loading and constitutive residuals must either preserve the held one-pole assumption or enter an independently proved $\eta_p$ bound. When the threshold error is independent of $U$, an exact uniform threshold gives mismatch probability at most $\eta_p$; without that independence, the symmetric uncertainty-band bound $2\eta_p$ applies. For a finite threshold source it is safe to use $2\eta_p+2\eta_U$ per distinct decision-tree threshold. Multiplying by $m$ for a fixed list or by $2^m-1$ for a general depth-$m$ policy gives a complete union bound, capped at $1$. A latched or proved monotone implementation preserves absorption; otherwise the possible upward readout glitches belong to this finite-history defect. No statistical independence between separate calibration residuals is needed for these deterministic and union bounds.

For $r$ independent prepared trials and a fixed list of $m$ read times, either the bounded normalized analog losses or the public flags satisfy
$$
\mathbb P\!\left\{\max_{1\le j\le m}|\widehat\Phi_r(t_j)-\Phi_{\rm impl}(t_j)|>\eta\right\}
\le 2m e^{-2r\eta^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.4b.16}
$$
The source/implementation bias is added separately. A reused device or adaptively selected comparison time requires its actual dependence/selection record. A finite population of modes with counts $r_i$ has occupancy error $\eta_{\rm occ}=\frac12\sum_i|r_i/r-w_i|$; its mixture-response error is at most $\eta_{\rm occ}$ at all times. Largest-remainder allocation gives $\eta_{\rm occ}\le(N+1)/(2r)$. Every trial and every retained word receives fresh ready records or a separately charged reset contract. The displayed laws and bounds are formal predictions.

*Proof.* The grounded Kirchhoff equation has the unique solution (5), leaves $[0,1]$ invariant and gives the stated same-task gain. The binary verification law is injective because $x\mapsto x^2$ is injective on this interval. The positive orthant is a closed pointed cone with dual interior $\mathbb R_{>0}^3$. The supplied tuple therefore satisfies Definition D.1f; its compact quotient and continuous scalarization attain their unique minimum at zero. Differentiating (7) proves the exact physical gradient law and strict descent. The ledger (4) is constant in the live coordinate $x$ at fixed prepared $C$ and reserved word. Its acquisition/service amounts have their stated separate ownership, so differentiation discards no uncharged state-dependent port.

For the source law, if $Z\sim N(0,1)$ then $L=1/(2Z^2)$ has density $(2\sqrt\pi)^{-1}l^{-3/2}e^{-1/(4l)}$, by summing the two Gaussian change-of-variable branches. Theorem P.8.9a.12.4a identifies its transform as $e^{-\sqrt t}$. For $n=2^k$ and $k\ge1$,
$$
\Lambda=\frac{2G}{C_0}\prod_{j=1}^k Z_j^{-2^j}
=\frac{2^nG}{C_0}\,L_1 L_2^2\cdots L_k^{2^{k-1}}.
$$
The powers of two sum to $\sum_{j=1}^k2^{j-1}=n-1$. The independently prepared $L_j$ have exactly the dyadic product law proved in Theorem P.8.9a.12.4a, establishing (8). The depth-one Jacobian gives (9) directly. The zero-event convention changes no probability. This derivation begins with the Gaussian controller and the actual RC error; the positive stable measure is its proved image.

Since $-\log U$ has unit exponential law, (2) is exactly survival until $T_*$. Exponential memorylessness gives (10), including its absorbing row. For increasing deterministic times the probabilities of successive exits are differences of $e^{-\lambda_i t}$, and their sum with survival is one. Conditioning on successive retained prefixes proves the same causal response law under adaptive read times. An unchanged private source and common release schedule make the whole record a measurable function of its initial mark, lifetime and the common query policy. They prove the claimed prefix and postprocessing compatibility. Conditioning instead on the hidden threshold would change that retained experiment, which is why the prepared-ensemble qualification is necessary.

Multiplying $C\dot x=-Gx$ by $V_0^2x$ gives $\dot E_C=-GV_0^2x^2$, proving (11). Gaussian integration by parts gives $\mathbb E Z^{2a}=(2a-1)!!$. Independence gives both moments in (12). The identity $(2a-1)!!=(2a)!/(2^a a!)$ telescopes over $a=2^{j-1}$ and gives $\prod_{j=1}^k(2^j-1)!!=n!/2^{n-1}$. Conditional on $C$, $E_C(t)=\int_t^\infty P_R(u\mid C)du$. Tonelli and (8) give
$$
\mathbb E E_C(t)=GV_0^2\int_t^\infty e^{-(u/\tau)^{1/n}}du
=GV_0^2\tau n\int_s^\infty z^{n-1}e^{-z}dz.
$$
Repeated integration by parts yields (12), including $k=0$. At $t=0$ it agrees with $(V_0^2/2)\mathbb EC$. Also $\mathbb E Z^{-2}=\infty$; its positive independent factors give $\mathbb E\Lambda=\infty$ for every $k\ge1$. This is compatible with bounded resistor power, since the energy weight is proportional to $C$.

The bank implements its chosen held rate exactly by $C_i=2G/\lambda_i$ and the same independent-threshold operation. Its source-bin weights are exactly the stable-law weights by (8), so the first inequality of (13) is Theorem P.8.9a.12.4a. For rates $a$ and $ar$, $r>1$, the exponential densities cross once at $\log r/[a(r-1)]$. Integrating either positive density difference gives
$$
\operatorname{TV}(\mathrm{Exp}(a),\mathrm{Exp}(ar))
=e^{-\log r/(r-1)}-e^{-r\log r/(r-1)}=\delta(r).
$$
Equivalently $\delta(r)=\sup_{u\ge0}(e^{-u}-e^{-ru})$, so it is increasing in $r$. Interior grid rates differ by a ratio at most $q$; either tail costs at most one. Convexity of total variation under the common Gaussian/bin mixture proves the marked-lifetime bound. Data processing proves every stated history bound without identifying the same-$U$ coupling with a total-variation optimizer.

For $\Lambda<\lambda_0$, $|C-C_I|\le C\mathbf1\{C>2G/\lambda_0\}$; its expectation is at most $(\lambda_0/(2G))\mathbb EC^2$. In interior bins $C\le C_I<qC$. In the upper tail $0\le C_I-C\le2G/\lambda_N$. These give $\mathbb E|C_I-C|\le D_C$. With $a=2Gt$, both functions $C e^{-a/C}$ and $C(1-e^{-a/C})$ have derivative between zero and one: their derivatives are $e^{-a/C}(1+a/C)$ and $1-e^{-a/C}(1+a/C)$. They are therefore $1$-Lipschitz on $(0,\infty)$, proving (14) and the heat bound. The source's finite second moment makes the three cutoff limits valid.

The calibrated rate lies between $\lambda_i(1-g)/(1+c)$ and $\lambda_i(1+g)/(1-c)$. The exponential-density identity just proved supplies $\delta(r_{\rm cal})$; mode-law discrepancy contributes $\eta_w$ by mixture convexity. A one-time flag is a threshold event in $U$, giving $\eta_U$. For a fixed time list, the $m$ thresholds partition $(0,1)$ into at most $m+1$ monotone-history intervals. The sum of absolute interval-mass errors divided by two is at most $m\eta_U$. A depth-$m$ decision tree has at most $2^m-1$ threshold nodes; conditioning on the mode and external randomization and partitioning by all these thresholds gives the stated general bound. Discrete and continuous lifetimes have disjoint full-measure supports at a fixed finite bank, proving the full-path qualification.

The time derivative of $e^{-\lambda_i't}$ has magnitude at most $\lambda'_{\max}$, and $|x^2-y^2|\le2|x-y|$ for $x,y\in[0,1]$. These give (15). A shifted independent threshold interval has uniform mass at most its length; an arbitrary error within a symmetric band uses the twice-width bound. A threshold source of discrepancy $\eta_U$ adds at most $2\eta_U$ to an interval probability. Union over the specified list or decision tree supplies the history defect, including glitches. For each fixed read time, Hoeffding's bounded-variable inequality gives $2e^{-2r\eta^2}$; a union bound proves (16) without requiring independence between reads within one trial. Finally, any response in $[0,1]$ changes by at most the total variation of its mode weights. Largest-remainder allocation changes each weight by less than $1/r$, proving its occupancy bound. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a125-benford-mantissas-from-multiplicative-pce-phase-mixing"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.5 (Benford Mantissas from Multiplicative PCE Phase Mixing).** Fix an integer base $b\ge2$. Let $X>0$ and set
$$
Y=\{\log_b X\}\in[0,1),
$$
where $\{\cdot\}$ denotes fractional part. If $Y$ is uniform on $[0,1)$, then the first base-$b$ digit $D\in\{1,\ldots,b-1\}$ satisfies
$$
\mathbb P(D=d)=\log_b\left(1+\frac1d\right).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.7}
$$
Moreover, suppose a multiplicative PCE phase process has the form
$$
X_n=X_0\prod_{j=1}^n A_j,
\qquad
A_j>0,
$$
where the increments $Z_j=\log_b A_j\pmod1$ are independent and identically distributed on the circle $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$. If their common law $\nu$ satisfies
$$
|\widehat\nu(m)|<1
\qquad
\text{for every }m\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\},
$$
then
$$
\{\log_b X_n\}\Rightarrow \mathrm{Unif}[0,1)
$$
and the first-digit probabilities converge to (P.8.9a.12.7).

*Proof.* The event $D=d$ is exactly
$$
\log_b d\le \{\log_b X\}<\log_b(d+1),
$$
because numbers with first base-$b$ digit $d$ lie in intervals $[d b^m,(d+1)b^m)$ over integer $m$. If $Y$ is uniform, then
$$
\mathbb P(D=d)
=
\log_b(d+1)-\log_b d
=
\log_b\left(1+\frac1d\right).
$$

For the phase-mixing statement, let $\theta_n=\{\log_b X_n\}$. On $\mathbb T$,
$$
\theta_n=\theta_0+Z_1+\cdots+Z_n.
$$
Let $\mu_n$ be the law of $\theta_n$ and use the Fourier convention
$$
\widehat\mu_n(m)=\mathbb E\,e^{2\pi i m\theta_n},
\qquad
\widehat\nu(m)=\mathbb E\,e^{2\pi i m Z_1}.
$$
Fix $m\ne0$, set $F=e^{2\pi i m\theta_0}$, and let
$$
\mathcal G=\sigma(Z_j:j\ge1),\qquad
\mathcal G_r=\sigma(Z_1,\ldots,Z_r),\qquad
G=\mathbb E[F\mid\mathcal G],\qquad
G_r=\mathbb E[G\mid\mathcal G_r].
$$
Finite-coordinate functions are dense in $L^1(\mathcal G)$. If $H$ is $\mathcal G_{r_0}$-measurable, then for $r\ge r_0$ the $L^1$ contraction of conditional expectation gives $\|G-G_r\|_1\le2\|G-H\|_1$. Approximation therefore yields $\|G-G_r\|_1\to0$; also $|G_r|\le1$. For $n\ge r$, the phase sum is $\mathcal G$-measurable, and the increments after $r$ are independent of $\mathcal G_r$. Consequently
$$
\begin{aligned}
|\widehat\mu_n(m)|
&=\left|\mathbb E\!\left[G e^{2\pi i m\sum_{j=1}^{n}Z_j}\right]\right|\\
&\le \|G-G_r\|_1+
 \left|\mathbb E\!\left[G_r e^{2\pi i m\sum_{j=1}^{r}Z_j}\right]\right|
 |\widehat\nu(m)|^{n-r}\\
&\le \|G-G_r\|_1+|\widehat\nu(m)|^{n-r}.
\end{aligned}
$$
First letting $n\to\infty$ with $r$ held constant, and then letting $r\to\infty$, proves $\widehat\mu_n(m)\to0$. The coefficient for $m=0$ is $1$. Trigonometric polynomials are uniformly dense in the continuous functions on $\mathbb T$, so these limits imply weak convergence of $\mu_n$ to Haar measure, without an independence assumption on $\theta_0$. The digit intervals have boundary of Haar measure zero, so their probabilities converge to the Benford probabilities in (P.8.9a.12.7). ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a125a-forbidden-mode-criterion-and-finite-window-digit-certificate-for-multiplicative-phase-processes"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.5a (Forbidden-Mode Criterion and Finite-Window Digit Certificate for Multiplicative Phase Processes).** Keep the notation of Theorem P.8.9a.12.5, write $\theta_n=\{\log_bX_n\}$ with law $\mu_n$, and let $D_n$ be the first base-$b$ digit of $X_n$.

1. *Forbidden modes.* For $m\ne0$, $|\widehat\nu(m)|=1$ exactly when $mZ_1$ is almost surely constant modulo $1$, that is, when $\nu$ is carried by a coset of the cyclic subgroup $|m|^{-1}\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z$ of $\mathbb T$. If such an $m$ exists and $X_0$ is deterministic, then $|\widehat\mu_n(m)|=1$ for every $n$, and $\theta_n$ does not converge in law to $\mathrm{Unif}[0,1)$. Hence the phase-mixing condition of Theorem P.8.9a.12.5 is necessary and sufficient for Haar convergence from every deterministic initial value.
2. *Finite-window discrepancy.* Assume $X_0$ is independent of $(A_j)_{j\ge1}$ and $S_n:=\sum_{m\ne0}|\widehat\nu(m)|^n<\infty$. Then $\theta_n$ has a continuous density $g_n$ with $\sup|g_n-1|\le S_n$, and for every Borel set $I\subseteq[0,1)$ and every digit $d$,
$$
\bigl|\mathbb P(\theta_n\in I)-|I|\bigr|\le|I|\,S_n,
\qquad
\left|\mathbb P(D_n=d)-\log_b\!\Bigl(1+\frac1d\Bigr)\right|\le\log_b\!\Bigl(1+\frac1d\Bigr)S_n.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5a.1}
$$
The bound is uniform over the law of $X_0$, hence over every change of unit $X\mapsto cX$ with $c>0$.
3. *Registered lognormal class.* If $\ln A_j\sim N(\eta,s^2)$ with $s>0$, then $|\widehat\nu(m)|=\exp[-2\pi^2m^2s^2/(\ln b)^2]$ and
$$
S_n\le\frac{2q_n}{1-q_n},
\qquad
q_n:=\exp\!\left[-\frac{2\pi^2ns^2}{(\ln b)^2}\right].
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5a.2}
$$
This class contains the time-$\Delta$ skeleton $X_n=X_{n\Delta}$, $\Delta>0$, of every geometric Brownian motion $dX_t=\varrho X_t\,dt+\sigma X_t\,dW_t$ with $\sigma\ne0$ and $X_0>0$ independent of $W$, for which $ns^2=\sigma^2n\Delta$. For $b=10$, $ns^2\ge2.05$ makes the relative digit error in (P.8.9a.12.5a.1) smaller than $10^{-3}$.
4. *Sampling record.* For $M$ independent copies sampled at step $n$, the empirical first-digit frequencies $\widehat f_d$ satisfy
$$
\mathbb P\!\left(\max_{1\le d\le b-1}\Bigl|\widehat f_d-\log_b\!\Bigl(1+\frac1d\Bigr)\Bigr|\ge\epsilon+S_n\log_b2\right)\le2(b-1)e^{-2M\epsilon^2}.
$$

*Proof.* For item 1, put $W=e^{2\pi imZ_1}$, so $|W|=1$. If $|\mathbb EW|=1$, write $\omega=\mathbb EW$; then $\mathbb E\operatorname{Re}(\bar\omega W)=1$ while $\operatorname{Re}(\bar\omega W)\le1$ pointwise, so $\bar\omega W=1$ almost surely and $mZ_1$ is almost surely constant modulo $1$. The converse is immediate. For deterministic $X_0$, independence of the increments gives $\widehat\mu_n(m)=e^{2\pi im\theta_0}\widehat\nu(m)^n$, whose modulus is $1$. Since $x\mapsto e^{2\pi imx}$ is continuous on $\mathbb T$, weak convergence to Haar measure would force $\widehat\mu_n(m)\to0$.

For item 2, independence gives $\widehat\mu_n(m)=\widehat\mu_0(m)\widehat\nu(m)^n$, so $\sum_m|\widehat\mu_n(m)|\le1+S_n$. The series $g_n(x)=\sum_m\widehat\mu_n(m)e^{-2\pi imx}$ converges absolutely and uniformly to a continuous function with Fourier coefficients $\widehat\mu_n(m)$. Trigonometric polynomials are uniformly dense in the continuous functions on $\mathbb T$, so a finite measure is determined by its Fourier coefficients and $\mu_n=g_n\,dx$. Then $|g_n-1|\le\sum_{m\ne0}|\widehat\mu_n(m)|\le S_n$, and integration over $I$ gives the first bound. The event $D_n=d$ is $\theta_n\in[\log_bd,\log_b(d+1))$ by the proof of Theorem P.8.9a.12.5, which gives the second bound. A change of unit adds $\log_bc$ to $\theta_0$ and preserves both the independence and $|\widehat\mu_0(m)|\le1$.

For item 3, $\ln A_1/\ln b$ is Gaussian with variance $s^2/(\ln b)^2$, and the Gaussian characteristic function gives $|\widehat\nu(m)|=q_1^{m^2}$. Hence $|\widehat\nu(m)|^n=q_n^{m^2}\le q_n^{|m|}$, and summation of the geometric series gives (P.8.9a.12.5a.2). For the geometric Brownian motion, $\ln A_j=(\varrho-\sigma^2/2)\Delta+\sigma(W_{j\Delta}-W_{(j-1)\Delta})$ are independent Gaussian variables, independent of $X_0$, with variance $s^2=\sigma^2\Delta>0$. For $b=10$ and $ns^2\ge2.05$, $2q_n/(1-q_n)<10^{-3}$.

For item 4, Hoeffding's inequality gives $\mathbb P(|\widehat f_d-\mathbb P(D_n=d)|\ge\epsilon)\le2e^{-2M\epsilon^2}$ for each $d$, and a union bound over the $b-1$ digits together with (P.8.9a.12.5a.1) and $\log_b(1+1/d)\le\log_b2$ gives the display. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a125b-benford-response-of-a-clocked-gaussian-prediction-processor"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.5b (Benford Response of a Clocked Gaussian Prediction Processor).** Fix a clock period $\Delta>0$ compatible with the complete source/processor schedule below, dimensionless source variances $Q,R>0$, drift $\mu\in\mathbb R$ and initial estimate $m_0\in\mathbb R$. Admitted source inputs have finite effective descriptions and certified rational approximations. The displayed identities also specify the underlying all-real ideal law. The named domain is the following one-step log-prediction processor. Its ideal source has independent standard normal variables $Z_0,Z_1,V_1,Z_2,V_2,\ldots$ and the state/observation law
$$
\begin{split}
P&=\frac{\sqrt{Q^2+4QR}-Q}{2},\qquad S=P+Q+R,\qquad K=\frac{P+Q}{S},\qquad v=P+Q,\\
\theta_0&=m_0+\sqrt P Z_0,\qquad
\theta_n=\theta_{n-1}+\mu+\sqrt Q Z_n,\qquad
Y_n=\theta_n+\sqrt R V_n.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.1}
$$
The hidden variable $\theta_n$ is the logarithm of a positive source quantity in its registered reference unit. A source register advances $\theta_n$ and gives the observer $Y_n$ through the indicated independent-noise channel. The processor receives no other latent-state or source-noise port. It updates
$$
m_n^-=m_{n-1}+\mu,\qquad \xi_n=Y_n-m_n^-,\qquad
m_n=m_n^-+K\xi_n,
\qquad a_n=m_n+\mu.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.2}
$$
It commits the log-target forecast $a_n$ before the source generates $\theta_{n+1}$. The registered proper point-prediction loss is the dimensionless squared log error $\mathrm{PE}(a,\theta)=(a-\theta)^2$. At the next tick a private verifier receives the generated $\theta_{n+1}$, scores the committed forecasts and retains their sign bits $\mathbf1\{\theta_{n+1}\le a\}$. The teacher and score archives have no return path into the filter or its future noise sources. Expected risks below are evaluated under the supplied source law; no single realized score is identified with such an expectation.

The positive forecast observable is the conditional intensity mean
$$
X_n:=\mathbb E[e^{\theta_{n+1}}\mid Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]
=\exp\bigl(a_n+v/2\bigr).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.3}
$$
The processor represents it by $\ell_n=a_n+v/2$, rather than by an unbounded-amplitude voltage. The private task scores $a_n$ against the later log target; $X_n$ is the specified positive readout of the same predictive law. Fix an integer base $b\ge2$ and positive unit multiplier $u$ before the trial. The public port returns the first digit of $uX_n$ by
$$
\phi_n=\left\{\frac{\ell_n+\ln u}{\ln b}\right\},\qquad
D_n=1+\sum_{d=2}^{b-1}\mathbf1\{\phi_n\ge\log_b d\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.4}
$$
The sum is empty for $b=2$. The unit, base, step index, nominal clock labels, digit and any overflow flag are public. Source states, observations, innovations, raw log forecasts, proper scores and coefficient/resource records are private owned data. This public digit cut does not identify the complete apparatus with its mantissa process. Sampling and release slots are fixed before source draws; actual timing residuals stay private or enter an independently specified timing-response metric. Readout has no feedback or data-dependent scheduling path.

The parameters in (1), the observation/noise mechanism, proper task, clock and digit extractor are source inputs selected independently of measured digit frequencies. The stationary initial error is part of that preparation: an arbitrary initial error law does not have the exact innovations asserted below. The ideal law has continuous unbounded registers. Item 5 supplies a finite-bit circuit realization with complete response and task-risk remainders on every finite horizon.

1. **Actual forecast and populated gain-comparison branch.** Let $\mathcal F_n=\sigma(Y_1,\ldots,Y_n)$, with $m_0$ known. Then
$$
\theta_n\mid\mathcal F_n\sim N(m_n,P),\quad
\theta_{n+1}\mid\mathcal F_n\sim N(a_n,v),\quad
\xi_n\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}N(0,S),\quad
K^2S=Q.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.5}
$$
For the fixed new observation at step $n$, compare the same future target using
$$
a_n^-=m_{n-1}+2\mu,\qquad
 a_{n,g}=a_n^-+g\xi_n,\quad 0\le g\le1.
$$
The admitted configuration is the gain $g$ on this frozen input snapshot; every candidate uses the same reserved arithmetic/read/verification schedule. The conditional proper risk and finite labeled verification response are
$$
\mathcal R_n(g)=v+(g-K)^2\xi_n^2,\qquad
\mathbb P(\theta_{n+1}\le a_{n,g}\mid\mathcal F_n)
=\Phi_{\rm G}\!\left(\frac{(g-K)\xi_n}{\sqrt v}\right),
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.6}
$$
where $\Phi_{\rm G}$ is the standard normal distribution function. Retain the one sign-verification protocol and its empty restriction, with fixed numerical bit labels. Response equivalence preserves these labels and the registered forecast/teacher roles. If $\xi_n\ne0$, the response quotient is $[0,1]$; if $\xi_n=0$, all gains give the same forecast and the quotient is a singleton.

A Definition-D.1f contract uses $\mathcal X_n=[0,1]$, this finite protocol family, $K_n=\mathbb R_+^2$, $W_n=\{(1,1)\}$ and
$$
