r_n(g)=\bigl(\Gamma_0\mathcal R_n(g),\ P_{\rm svc}\bigr),\qquad
V_n(g)=\Gamma_0\mathcal R_n(g)+P_{\rm svc},\qquad \Gamma_0>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.7}
$$
Here $\Gamma_0$ is the independently registered power-equivalent task tariff and $P_{\rm svc}$ is the complete, gain-independent amortized service charge of the reserved source/processor word. Its complete ideal and finite circuit ledgers are given in item 5. The realized proper loss remains the squared error; the sign bit is its finite verification response, not that loss or its expectation. In Definition 7's score normalization, the registered benefit $-(PP^{-1}-1)/k_{PP}=-\mathrm{PE}$ gives (7) after conditional expectation. Task tariff is separate from physical service energy.

The actual update selects $g=K\in(0,1)$ and attains the unique response-class minimum. It also minimizes conditional log-MSE over every real point forecast. Its conditional and mean gains over the old forecast of this same future target are
$$
\mathcal R_n(0)-\mathcal R_n(K)=K^2\xi_n^2,\qquad
\mathbb E[\mathcal R_n(0)-\mathcal R_n(K)]=Q>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.8}
$$
The realized score difference is $(K\xi_n)^2+2K\xi_n(\theta_{n+1}-a_n)$ and can have either sign. This source performs a new conditional minimization at each tick. Incoming observations change $V_n$; a common decreasing global potential or a PCE-attractor limit is not inferred.

2. **Source-derived multiplicative class and finite digit law.** The actual positive readout satisfies
$$
X_n=X_0\prod_{j=1}^n A_j,\qquad
X_0=e^{m_0+\mu+v/2},\qquad
A_j=e^{\mu+K\xi_j},\qquad \ln A_j\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}N(\mu,Q).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.9}
$$
Consequently every nonzero Fourier mode of its base-$b$ increment has modulus
$$
|\widehat\nu(h)|=\exp[-2\pi^2h^2Q/(\ln b)^2]<1,
\qquad h\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}.
$$
Put
$$
q_n=\exp[-2\pi^2nQ/(\ln b)^2],\qquad
\varepsilon_n^{\rm mix}=\frac{2q_n}{1-q_n},\qquad
p_d=\log_b(1+1/d).
$$
Theorem P.8.9a.12.5a then gives a phase density bounded by $1+\varepsilon_n^{\rm mix}$ and
$$
|\mathbb P(D_n=d)-p_d|\le p_d\varepsilon_n^{\rm mix}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.10}
$$
These bounds are uniform over every fixed unit $u>0$ and every known $m_0$. The observation-noise variance $R$ affects the stationary error, gain and task risk; the multiplier log-variance is exactly the independently supplied process variance $Q$.

3. **Complete public response map and sampling ownership.** Conditional on $m_{n-1}$, the next log estimate is $m_{n-1}+\mu+\sqrt Q Z$ with a fresh standard normal $Z$. Thus the complete finite-word law of the phase process underlying the retained digit word is the circle convolution kernel with mean increment $\mu/\ln b$ and variance $Q/(\ln b)^2$, started from the phase of $uX_0$. The digit word is its deterministic interval postprocessing (4). The source-to-response map sends the actual recursion, source initialization and observation innovations to this kernel; it commutes with prefix restriction and common postprocessing. Selecting a subset of a previously registered finite digit word by its past public digits is also a postprocessing. Unit/base changes selected adaptively from hidden records are outside the declared protocol.

For $M$ independent trials, each freshly initialized by (1), sampled at a fixed registered step $n$, the empirical digit frequencies obey
$$
\mathbb P\!\left\{\max_d|\widehat f_d-p_d|\ge\eta+(\log_b2)\varepsilon_n^{\rm mix}\right\}
\le2(b-1)e^{-2M\eta^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.11}
$$
The count $M$ is a replica count, not the number of correlated observations along one trajectory. Every digit belongs to the registered mean-forecast readout, and every verification score belongs to the log-target task.

4. **Finite source and numerical response bounds.** Fix a finite horizon $N\ge1$ and generate source ticks through $N+1$ so every published forecast at steps $1,\ldots,N$ receives its later teacher. There are $d_N=2(N+1)+1$ standard-normal source draws, including the initial error and the deliberately retained final observation noise. Choose a rational grid in $[-L,L]$, containing both endpoints, with maximum gap $h_0>0$, and let its $J$ nearest-grid bins include both Gaussian tails in the endpoint bins. Let $p_j$ be their exact normal probabilities. A normalized dyadic table $\widetilde p_j=c_j/2^B$, with nonnegative integer counts summing to $2^B$, has a certified
$$
\eta_{\rm tab}=\frac12\sum_j|\widetilde p_j-p_j|.
$$
A $B$-bit fair word and a padded cumulative-table lookup generate one draw. The source probabilities are explicit differences of $\Phi_{\rm G}$ values; certified rational intervals and largest-remainder allocation construct a table of arbitrary prescribed accuracy. All zero and tail codes have specified retained outputs. No trial is removed or renormalized by its source value.

There is a joint construction with an ideal normal draw $Z$ such that, outside an event of probability at most
$$
\delta_0:=\min\{1,\eta_{\rm tab}+2e^{-L^2/2}\},
$$
the implemented draw $\widetilde Z$ obeys $|\widetilde Z-Z|\le h_0/2$. For the whole source word use $\delta_{\rm src}\le\min\{1,d_N\delta_0\}$. The clipped digital and continuous raw-source laws are not asserted to be close in full-path total variation; the following retained digit comparison uses this explicit value coupling.

Use certified positive finite-point coefficients with $0<K_-\le\widetilde K\le K_+<1$, $|\widetilde K-K|\le\eta_K$, and drift error at most $\eta_\mu$. Suppose the source circuit bounds the observation discrepancy by $|\widetilde Y_n-Y_n|\le E_Y$ and the initial estimate discrepancy by $E_0$, on the good coupling event. Let $B_\xi$ bound $|\xi_n|$ there and let $\rho_f$ bound the aggregate arithmetic residual in one implemented filter update. With $a=1-K_-$,
$$
E_n=a^nE_0+\frac{1-a^n}{K_-}
\bigl[(1-K_-)\eta_\mu+\eta_KB_\xi+K_+E_Y+\rho_f\bigr]
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.12}
$$
bounds $|\widetilde m_n-m_n|$.

These inputs can be populated directly from the finite source. Write $\eta_{\sqrt P},\eta_{\sqrt Q},\eta_{\sqrt R}$ for coefficient errors, and $\rho_0,\rho_\theta,\rho_Y$ for bounded aggregate source-arithmetic residuals. On the good event, put
$$
\begin{split}
E_{\theta,0}&=E_0+\sqrt P\,h_0/2+\eta_{\sqrt P}L+\rho_0,\\
e_\theta&=\eta_\mu+\sqrt Q\,h_0/2+\eta_{\sqrt Q}L+\rho_\theta,\\
E_Y&=E_{\theta,0}+(N+1)e_\theta+\sqrt R\,h_0/2+\eta_{\sqrt R}L+\rho_Y,\\
B_\theta&=|m_0|+\sqrt P L+(N+1)(|\mu|+\sqrt Q L),\\
B_Y&=B_\theta+\sqrt R L,\qquad
B_m=\max\{|m_0|,B_Y\}+(N+1)|\mu|,\qquad
B_\xi=B_Y+B_m+|\mu|.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.13}
$$
The grid draw itself lies in $[-L,L]$, which is why the coefficient-error terms use $L$. A signed fixed-point range chosen to contain these source/filter bounds, their certified residuals and every squared-score intermediate supplies a finite word width. Overflow is detected and returned as a retained abort at the common release slot. The stated bounded-code construction may choose its range from all digital codes and thereby make overflow impossible; a different implementation must add its certified overflow probability once to the word bound.

Let the computed unreduced phase be $\widetilde z_n=\widetilde c_b\widetilde m_n+\widetilde c_u$ plus error $\rho_\phi$, where the exact constants are $c_b=1/\ln b$ and $c_u=(\mu+v/2+\ln u)/\ln b$. If their errors are $\eta_b,\eta_u$, then the circle-distance phase error is bounded by
$$
\eta_n=|c_b|E_n+\eta_b(B_m+E_n)+\eta_u+\rho_\phi.
$$
Give every digit threshold error bound $\eta_{\rm cut}$. The complete implemented digit word, with identical public unit, index and nominal-time labels and retained aborts, then satisfies
$$
\operatorname{TV}(\mathcal L(\widetilde D_1,\ldots,\widetilde D_N),
\mathcal L(D_1,\ldots,D_N))
\le \varepsilon_{\rm word}:=
\min\!\left\{1,\delta_{\rm src}+\sum_{n=1}^N
2(b-1)(1+\varepsilon_n^{\rm mix})(\eta_n+\eta_{\rm cut})\right\},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.14}
$$
with any additional certified overflow probability added inside the minimum. An exact word has zero abort probability. Formula (14) therefore also controls aborts, rather than conditioning them away. Its one-step version can replace $\varepsilon_{\rm word}$ when only a fixed step is retained. Add that implementation bias to the threshold in (11) for independent digital trials.

5. **Finite task-risk and complete circuit resources.** The following risk statements choose ranges containing every value reachable from the bounded digital source and every admitted gain, so overflow is unreachable and arithmetic residual bounds hold globally. An implementation that can abort must first assign and bound its fallback forecast in $L^2$ before using these risk formulas. The digital source also has a global mean-square coupling. Since $|\widetilde Z|\le L$,
$$
\|\widetilde Z-Z\|_2^2\le h_0^2/4+\sqrt{8(L^4+3)\delta_0}=:e_Z^2.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.15}
$$
Replace $h_0/2$ by $e_Z$ in the source-error bounds (13), and replace $B_\xi$ by $\sqrt S$ in (12), interpreting the resulting $E^{(2)}$ quantities as $L^2$ bounds. For a selected implemented forecast and its generated future teacher, set
$$
\zeta_n=E_n^{(2)}+\eta_\mu+E_{\theta,n+1}^{(2)}+\rho_a,
$$
where $\rho_a$ is the forecast arithmetic residual and $E_{\theta,n+1}^{(2)}=E_{\theta,0}^{(2)}+(n+1)e_\theta^{(2)}$. Then
$$
\bigl|\mathbb E(\widetilde a_n-\widetilde\theta_{n+1})^2-v\bigr|
\le2\sqrt v\,\zeta_n+\zeta_n^2.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.16}
$$
For uniform comparison over a fixed grid of gains $g\in[0,1]$ represented exactly in the chosen format, use
$$
\zeta_n^*=E_{n-1}^{(2)}+2\eta_\mu+E_Y^{(2)}+\rho_a+E_{\theta,n+1}^{(2)},\qquad
\varepsilon_n^{\rm risk}=2\sqrt{v+S}\,\zeta_n^*+(\zeta_n^*)^2.
$$
The implemented and ideal unconditional gain risks differ by at most $\varepsilon_n^{\rm risk}$. Among a fixed finite grid of data-independent gains applied at this step after the common preceding filter, a nearest grid gain to $K$ therefore has actual finite-grid risk at most $2\varepsilon_n^{\rm risk}$ above the best fixed gain on that same grid. A general rounded gain has ideal excess $S(\widetilde K-K)^2$, or the conditional excess $(\widetilde K-K)^2\xi_n^2$ for exact inputs. These are approximation and finite-grid comparison statements; they do not assign exact Gaussian posterior optimality to arbitrary rounded hardware.

The expected values in (16) concern the exact mathematical loss of the encoded forecast and teacher. If a returned score word first rounds their difference with error at most $r_q$ and then rounds its square with the same bound, a bound $B_{\rm res}$ on the encoded residual gives
$$
\rho_{\rm score}=2B_{\rm res}r_q+r_q^2+r_q.
$$
Add $\rho_{\rm score}$ to the reported mean-risk bounds and to $\varepsilon_n^{\rm risk}$ when comparing rounded-score objectives. A returned subtraction of the two scores has the additional rounding error $r_q$.

The sign-verification records also have a finite response bound. On the good coupling event, let
$$
T_n^*=E_{n-1}+2\eta_\mu+E_Y+\eta_KB_\xi+\rho_a+E_{\theta,n+1}
$$
bound the residual discrepancy uniformly over matching gains in $[0,1]$, with the additional $\eta_KB_\xi$ term covering the actual selected-gain comparison $\widetilde K$ versus $K$. The ideal future residual has a conditional normal density bounded by $1/\sqrt{2\pi v}$. Thus one delayed sign can disagree with probability at most $\delta_{\rm src}+2T_n^*/\sqrt{2\pi v}$. For the two signs at every step, charge the source failure once and sum $4T_n^*/\sqrt{2\pi v}$. Adding that sum inside (14) controls the joint digit/sign word when those private sign records are retained. Finite digital sign kernels may have plateaus; the exact ideal sign-only quotient is not imposed on them.

For completeness, the ideal real-arithmetic reference also has an explicit finite-word interface ledger. Put $H=N+1$, let $A,D$ be (18), and reserve
$$
R_{\rm an}=64+b+d_N+A+D+9H+8.
$$
These are finitely many ideal scalar/bit coordinates, not a claim of finite digital capacity for arbitrary reals. With independently fixed positive setup, Gaussian-draw, arithmetic, comparison, phase-extraction, transfer/release, ready-coordinate and maintenance tariffs, define
$$
\begin{split}
E_{\rm ideal}&=E_{\rm set}^{\rm an}+d_Ne_G+A e_a+D e_c+H e_\phi
 +(8H+8)e_o+R_{\rm an}e_r^{\rm an}
 +(P_0^{\rm an}+R_{\rm an}p_r^{\rm an})T_{\rm tot},\\
P_{\rm svc}^{\rm an}&=E_{\rm ideal}/T_{\rm tot}.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.17}
$$
The record groups hold every primitive input/output, source/verification record, fixed coefficient and clock label; the setup term owns the apparatus and precompiled coefficient descriptions. Each primitive has its declared fixed duration, and $\Delta$ exceeds a padded block's full latency. These are the ideal source's stated service laws. The finite realization replaces them by the explicit bit/gate ledger below and retains the approximation bounds.

All finite resources are source-owned. Precompile the rational coefficient, digit-threshold, support-value and cumulative-count tables; charge their manufacture/compilation as a fixed setup entry, and charge every retained table bit. Each Gaussian draw consumes exactly $B$ fresh fair bits and one fixed-length lookup. Arithmetic uses a fixed signed $p$-bit format and a fixed rounding convention; comparisons and overflow handling are deterministic. A trial runs $N+1$ padded blocks. It retains every source draw, observation, innovation, forecast, delayed teacher/sign/score result, intermediate word, digit, abort flag and nominal release label. There is no archive reset or reuse.

One explicit straight-line block uses five add/multiply operations for $\theta_n,Y_n$, four for the filter prediction/innovation/update, three for the two same-target forecasts and positive-mean log readout, two for the unreduced phase, four for the two delayed squared-error scores and one for their realized difference. It also uses $b-2$ digit comparisons and at most $b-2$ additions to encode the digit, plus two delayed sign comparisons. The first block pads its unavailable prior verification with dummy values, and the last block keeps its unused new forecast/digit private while verifying step $N$. Initialization uses at most eight additional arithmetic operations. Hence
$$
A=(b+24)(N+1)+8,\qquad D=b(N+1)
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.18}
$$
arithmetic and numerical-comparison slots suffice. Modulo one in signed binary fixed point is extraction of the fractional bits; it is not an unbounded integer search.

For $p\ge2$, use retained-input fan-in-two AND, OR, XOR and NOT gates, each writing a fresh ready output bit. Pad a signed add/subtract/multiply/square operation, round-to-nearest-even logic, range detection and retained abort update to $64p^2$ gates, and a signed numerical comparison to $8p$ gates. A cumulative-table lookup uses at most
$$
L_{\rm tab}=16J(p+B+2)
$$
gates. Store $B+1$ bits for each cumulative count, including its possible value $2^B$, and $p$ bits for each support value. Phase extraction, the observer/teacher transfers, public copying and fixed labels fit in $16p$ additional gates per block and $16p$ at initialization. Thus one explicit padded realization has
$$
\begin{split}
G_{\rm tot}&=d_NL_{\rm tab}+64p^2A+8pD+16p(N+1)+16p,\\
R_{\rm bit}&=(64+b)p+J(p+B+1)+d_NB+G_{\rm tot}.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.19}
$$
The first record term reserves the design/ledger scalars and digit thresholds; every source-description field must fit its declared allocation. The remaining terms retain lookup tables, fresh source bits and every gate output, including displaced scratch data. The registered circuit has a fixed positive per-gate duration and per-coin duration. With per-coin and per-gate durations $\tau_{\rm coin},\tau_g>0$, choose
$$
\Delta\ge 2B\tau_{\rm coin}
 +\bigl[2L_{\rm tab}+64p^2(b+24)+8pb+16p\bigr]\tau_g
 +\tau_{\rm guard},\qquad \tau_{\rm guard}>0,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.20}
$$
and include the initial draw, initialization arithmetic, source/table preparation and initialized storage in the pre-origin schedule. All reserved cells are present and maintained throughout that schedule. The guard covers the registered delivery/clock residuals, so every forecast is actually committed before the next source tick. This gives identical public release labels for all source words and comparator gains. With $G_{\rm tot}$ such gate operations, $R_{\rm bit}$ initialized/retained bits, fixed positive setup energy $E_{\rm set}$, fresh-coin energy $e_{\rm coin}$, gate energy $e_g$, ready-bit energy $e_r$, controller power $P_0$ and per-bit maintenance $p_r$, the whole trial charge is
$$
E_{\rm trial}=E_{\rm set}+d_NB e_{\rm coin}+G_{\rm tot}e_g+R_{\rm bit}e_r
 +(P_0+R_{\rm bit}p_r)T_{\rm tot},\qquad
P_{\rm svc}=E_{\rm trial}/T_{\rm tot}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.21}
$$
Here $T_{\rm tot}$ includes padded preparation, all source/processing/verification slots and the final release. The constants are predeclared source tariffs, with units and source ports retained; they are not inferred from digit frequencies. Every gain comparator has the same allocated width and padded circuit. Selecting smaller error tolerances generally increases table, precision, timing and storage costs. The full run charge is used once: a collection of per-tick objectives uses their normalized average, rather than adding the complete service charge anew at every tick. Fixed per-gate energy and timing are properties of this registered circuit model, with separate residuals required for other hardware.

The finite carrier can be made explicit. Give each retained bit a two-dimensional basis register. A Boolean gate with inputs $x$ and a fresh target bit $z$ is the basis permutation
$$
U_f|x,z\rangle=|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.5b.22}
$$
It retains its inputs, satisfies $U_f^2=I$, and is implemented in duration $\tau_g$ by $H_f=\pi\hbar(I-U_f)/(2\tau_g)$. A fresh fair source bit has declared normalized state $(|0\rangle\langle0|+|1\rangle\langle1|)/2$, independent of every other source bit; deterministic records start in their specified basis states. Composition of these finite unitary gates and diagonal output instruments realizes exactly the finite digital word law, including every abort and private retained register. The output projectors sum to identity, so the full instrument is normalized. The wiring sends $Y_n$ to the filter and the delayed teacher to its separate verifier; neither the teacher archive nor future-source registers feed the filter. This is a finite carrier/instrument realization of the declared Boolean source, with $\|H_f\|\le\pi\hbar/\tau_g$ and total operator-norm action at most $\pi\hbar G_{\rm tot}$. The positive service energy in (21) is its separate controller/ready-source charge, not an identification with this action. The probability conclusions concern the supplied diagonal source preparation; arbitrary coherent inputs are not assigned its classical Gaussian-table law.

For every fixed $N,b,u$ and positive $Q,R$, the clipped range, table resolution/probabilities, fixed-point precision and a clock period sufficient for that circuit can be chosen so that (14) and (16) have any prescribed positive bounds. The reference source uses that same clock period; this is not a claim of arbitrarily accurate sequential computation at one hardware-limited period. The construction supplies a finite circuit and explicit remainders, while retaining the ideal source law as the reference model.

*Proof.* The positive root in (1) satisfies $P^2+QP=QR$, and therefore
$$
P=\frac{R(P+Q)}{P+Q+R},\qquad
(1-K)(P+Q)=KR,\qquad
\frac{(P+Q)^2}{P+Q+R}=Q.
$$
The prescribed initial error is centered Gaussian of variance $P$, independent of the known initial mean and future source noises. Suppose the posterior error $e_{n-1}=\theta_{n-1}-m_{n-1}$ is $N(0,P)$ and independent of $\mathcal F_{n-1}$. The prior error $h_n=e_{n-1}+\sqrt QZ_n$ is then $N(0,P+Q)$ and independent of that past. The innovation is $\xi_n=h_n+\sqrt RV_n$, while the new error is
$$
e_n=(1-K)h_n-K\sqrt RV_n.
$$
Their covariance is $(1-K)(P+Q)-KR=0$. Joint Gaussianity makes them independent. Direct variance calculation gives $\operatorname{Var}(e_n)=P$ and $\operatorname{Var}(\xi_n)=S$. Both variables are independent of the old observation history, and adjoining $Y_n=m_n^-+\xi_n$ proves the induction. The innovations are consequently independent with the same normal law. The last root identity gives $K^2S=Q$. The independent next process noise adds variance $Q$, proving the future conditional law in (5). Gaussian integration gives (3).

For any committed real forecast $a$, conditional expansion gives
$$
\mathbb E[(a-\theta_{n+1})^2\mid\mathcal F_n]=v+(a-a_n)^2.
$$
This proves its global unique minimum and, on the natural gain interval, (6)–(8). The normal distribution function is strictly increasing, so the fixed labeled sign-bit law separates gains unless $\xi_n=0$. The stated two-object protocol presheaf, orthant resource cone and positive scalarization therefore satisfy Definition D.1f. The risk descends to its exact quotient, which is compact; the selected response-class minimum is unique. Expanding the two realized squared errors around $\theta_{n+1}-a_n$ gives the displayed signed realized improvement. The formal objective is evaluated separately on each new observation; none of these calculations asserts monotone realized loss or a common fixed attractor.

The positive-mean log offset $\mu+v/2$ is constant. Consequently $\ln X_n-\ln X_{n-1}=m_n-m_{n-1}=\mu+K\xi_n$, proving (9). The characteristic function of this source-derived normal increment gives its nonzero Fourier moduli. Theorem P.8.9a.12.5a now applies with $s^2=Q$ and deterministic $X_0$, yielding (10) and its density bound. Independence of successive innovations proves the normalized product law of the complete log/phase word, not just its one-time marginal. The digit extractor is the stated deterministic map on each component; all prefix and postprocessing claims follow. Independent prepared replicas and the ordinary bounded-variable Hoeffding inequality give (11). Within-trajectory dependence has not been replaced by an iid replica assumption.

For the finite source, first couple $Z$ to its nearest clipped grid value. The error is at most $h_0/2$ on $|Z|\le L$. A maximal coupling of the resulting bin law $p$ and the dyadic law $\widetilde p$ fails with probability $\eta_{\rm tab}$. The normal tail bound $\mathbb P(|Z|>L)\le2e^{-L^2/2}$ proves $\delta_0$. Independent products and a union bound give $\delta_{\rm src}$. The source parameters and bin probabilities have certified computable intervals; approximating their finite probability vector and rounding to dyadic counts produces normalized tables with arbitrarily small $\eta_{\rm tab}$. For an exact finite probability vector, rounding down the $2^Bp_j$ and allocating the remaining counts to distinct bins gives coordinate discrepancy at most $2^{-B}$ and total variation at most $J2^{-B-1}$. Certified rational approximations add their own displayed probability discrepancy. Both tail masses stay in the finite vector.

Subtracting the exact and implemented filter recursions gives
$$
\widetilde m_n-m_n=(1-\widetilde K)(\widetilde m_{n-1}-m_{n-1})
 +(1-\widetilde K)(\widetilde\mu-\mu)
 +(\widetilde K-K)\xi_n+\widetilde K(\widetilde Y_n-Y_n)+r_n,
\qquad |r_n|\le\rho_f.
$$
Its geometric-series bound is (12). Applying the same triangle inequalities to the initial source, each source increment and each observation proves (13). The source bounds use $|Z_j|,|V_j|\le L$ on the good event. The filter is a convex combination of $m_{n-1}+\mu$ and $Y_n$, proving the supplied $B_m$ bound and hence $B_\xi$. Finite-point coefficient errors multiply the implemented grid draw, whose absolute value is always at most $L$.

Reduction modulo one cannot increase circle distance. The phase-error formula therefore follows by adding the estimate, coefficient, constant and arithmetic errors. A wrong digit on the good event requires the ideal phase to lie within $\eta_n+\eta_{\rm cut}$ of one of at most $b-1$ digit boundaries on the circle. This union has length at most $2(b-1)(\eta_n+\eta_{\rm cut})$, and the ideal phase density is at most $1+\varepsilon_n^{\rm mix}$. Union over the word, charging the common source failure once, proves (14). Total variation is bounded by disagreement probability under this explicit coupling. The result includes every abort outcome and identical public clock/unit marks. No conclusion about total variation of discrete versus continuous raw registers is needed.

For (15), the squared source error is at most $h_0^2/4$ on the good event and at most $(L+|Z|)^2$ elsewhere. Cauchy–Schwarz and
$$
\mathbb E(L+|Z|)^4\le8(L^4+\mathbb EZ^4)=8(L^4+3)
$$
prove the stated global bound. Minkowski's inequality propagates these $L^2$ errors through the linear source and filter recursions; the ideal innovation has norm $\sqrt S$. Global bounded-code arithmetic ranges justify the same residual bounds on the whole finite-source law. If $U= a_n-\theta_{n+1}$ and $\widetilde U=\widetilde a_n-\widetilde\theta_{n+1}$, then $\|U\|_2=\sqrt v$ and $\|\widetilde U-U\|_2\le\zeta_n$. The identity $\widetilde U^2-U^2=2U(\widetilde U-U)+(\widetilde U-U)^2$ proves (16). For a fixed candidate gain,
$$
a_{n,g}=(1-g)m_{n-1}+(2-g)\mu+gY_n,
$$
so its uniformly propagated error is bounded by $\zeta_n^*$. The ideal unconditional risk is $v+(g-K)^2S\le v+S$, giving $\varepsilon_n^{\rm risk}$. If all gain risks change by at most that amount, comparing an ideal grid minimizer to an actual grid minimizer uses the bound twice. This is an unconditional comparison of fixed gains after the common prior filter; it does not certify a conditional posterior optimum on every rounded observation history or a larger class of history-dependent selectors.

For the circuit census, the stated straight-line operations number $19+(b-2)$ per full block, below the reserved $b+24$; the two delayed signs and $b-2$ digit tests give exactly $b$ numerical comparisons. A ripple-carry addition uses at most $5p$ Boolean gates and signed subtraction at most $6p+1$. Schoolbook multiplication uses $p^2$ partial-product ANDs and at most $p-1$ widened $2p$ additions, bounded by $11p^2$ gates. Conditional sign handling, rounding, high-bit range detection, retained abort update and output selection can use at most $63p+2$ additional gates. For $p\ge2$, $11p^2+63p+2\le64p^2$; smaller arithmetic operations fit the same padded slot. A signed comparison uses the sign bits and a bitwise lexicographic test within $8p$ gates.

For lookup, compare the $B$-bit draw, padded by a leading zero, to every stored $(B+1)$-bit cumulative upper count. Adjacent comparison results form the one-hot bin indicators, including zero-count bins and the final sentinel $2^B$. Select the corresponding $p$-bit support word by AND/OR gates. The comparisons, one-hot logic and output selection fit in $16J(p+B+2)$ gates. Fixed-point fractional-bit extraction uses wiring/copy gates after the precompiled reciprocal multiplication. The $16p$ per-block reserve covers this extraction, observer and delayed-teacher copies, digit and fixed clock/index release copies; initialization has the same reserve. Every gate writes one new bit while retaining its inputs, giving (19) and the complete storage and charge (21). All stages are padded, including the initial/final dummy slots and the abort branch. A sufficiently long common period accommodates the selected finite circuit.

Finally, choose $L$ to make the finite union of normal tails small, then choose the grid, dyadic table and arithmetic precision to make the remaining bounds small. For the $L^2$ bound, enlarge $L$ slowly enough that $(L^4+3)\delta_0\to0$ while $h_0\to0$ and $\eta_{\rm tab}\to0$; the Gaussian tail permits this choice. Every fixed-horizon coefficient and density bound is finite. The recurrences therefore give $E_n,\eta_n,\zeta_n\to0$. Each choice has finite word width, table size, circuit, clock period and record supply, establishing the claimed finite implementation at the prescribed tolerances. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a126-log-periodic-corrections-from-discrete-scale-invariance"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.6 (Log-Periodic Corrections from Discrete Scale Invariance).** Let $\lambda>1$ and let $F:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be locally square-integrable. Suppose
$$
F(\lambda x)=\lambda^{\alpha}F(x)
\qquad
\text{for all }x>0
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8}
$$
for some $\alpha\in\mathbb R$. Then there is a period-one function $P$ such that
$$
F(x)=x^{\alpha}P\left(\frac{\log x}{\log\lambda}\right).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9}
$$
If $P$ has Fourier coefficients $c_m$, then in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on logarithmic scale,
$$
F(x)
=
x^{\alpha}
\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}
c_m
\exp\left(
\frac{2\pi i m\log x}{\log\lambda}
\right).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10}
$$
For real-valued $F$, $c_{-m}=\overline{c_m}$. If the first harmonic is the leading nonconstant mode, the leading log-periodic correction has the form
$$
F(x)
=
x^{\alpha}
\left[
c_0
+
2|c_1|
\cos\left(
\frac{2\pi\log x}{\log\lambda}
+
\phi
\right)
+
\cdots
\right],
\tag{P.8.9a.12.11}
$$
with $\phi=\arg c_1$. Near a critical point $x_c$, the same conclusion applies to the distance variable $y=|x-x_c|$ whenever the discrete scale covariance holds in $y$.

*Proof.* Define
$$
u=\frac{\log x}{\log\lambda},
\qquad
P(u)=\lambda^{-\alpha u}F(\lambda^u).
$$
Then
$$
P(u+1)
=
\lambda^{-\alpha(u+1)}F(\lambda^{u+1})
=
\lambda^{-\alpha u}\lambda^{-\alpha}F(\lambda\lambda^u).
$$
Using (P.8.9a.12.8),
$$
F(\lambda\lambda^u)=\lambda^{\alpha}F(\lambda^u),
$$
so $P(u+1)=P(u)$. Since $x=\lambda^u$, this gives
$$
F(x)=\lambda^{\alpha u}P(u)=x^{\alpha}P\left(\frac{\log x}{\log\lambda}\right).
$$
The Fourier series of the period-one function $P$ gives
$$
P(u)=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}c_m e^{2\pi i m u}
$$
in $L^2$ over one period, which yields (P.8.9a.12.10) after substituting $u=\log x/\log\lambda$. If $F$ is real-valued then $P$ is real-valued and its Fourier coefficients satisfy $c_{-m}=\overline{c_m}$. Combining the $m=1$ and $m=-1$ terms gives (P.8.9a.12.11). Replacing $x$ by $y=|x-x_c|$ gives the critical-point form. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a126a-exact-log-periodic-risk-of-a-dyadic-bernoulli-predictor"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.6a (Exact Log-Periodic Risk of a Dyadic Bernoulli Predictor).** Fix a Bernoulli source parameter $p\in(0,1)$ and put $q=p(1-p)$. Register the proper probability-forecast loss $\mathrm{PE}(a,y)=(a-y)^2$, with $a\in[0,1]$ and $y\in\{0,1\}$. The named source domain is the dyadically checkpointed predictor below. Its independently supplied source emits $Y_1,Y_2,\ldots$ with iid Bernoulli$(p)$ law. Its acquisition front end commits completed data banks at exactly $1,2,4,\ldots$ samples. Incomplete banks, source-preparation variables and all teacher/verification records have no input path into the predictor. The checkpoint architecture, proper task and source law are fixed before response evaluation.

For a finite horizon choose $J\ge0$, $K=2^J$, and generate $K+1$ source outcomes. At every acquisition index $1\le n\le K$, the most recent completed bank has size
$$
k(n)=2^{\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.1}
$$
The physical device receives finite integer indices. A real acquisition-budget label $x\ge1$ denotes the component $n=\lfloor x\rfloor$; it is a piecewise-constant mathematical label, not an arbitrary exact real register or an elapsed physical time. This device covers $1\le x<K+1$. Its clock and resource records have the horizon-indexed realization specified below.

**Calibrated predictor class.** For each completed bank size $k=2^j$, retain every table
$$
f:\{0,1\}^k\longrightarrow\{0,1/k,\ldots,1\},\qquad
r_z:=k f(z),\qquad
\sum_{|z|=s}r_z=s\binom{k}{s}\quad(0\le s\le k).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.2}
$$
Here $|z|$ is the count of ones. Universal unbiasedness over the Bernoulli parameter family is the registered design constraint; (2) is its exact finite certificate. Every candidate uses the same fixed-shape table lookup, data bank, verification circuit and padded service schedule. Table contents may vary; their allocated widths and executed resources do not. The source parameter $p$ is private to the source and its calibration record, and is not a predictor-table input.

The implemented selected table is
$$
f_k^*(z)=|z|/k,\qquad
A_n^+=\frac{1}{k(n)}\sum_{i=1}^{k(n)}Y_i.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.3}
$$
The before forecast is $A_n^-=A_{n-1}^+$ for $n\ge2$ and $A_1^-=A_1^+$. Both are committed before the source generates $Y_{n+1}$, and both are scored against that same next teacher. All forecast, teacher and score records are retained privately during the run. Final-only public readout returns the declared logical word after the last verification; no score, teacher or randomized-loss output returns to the predictor.

1. **Populated calibration and PCE minimum.** Condition (2) holds exactly when $\mathbb E_p f(Y_1,\ldots,Y_k)=p$ for every $p\in(0,1)$. It is also equivalent to calibration over all dyadic parameters, by the polynomial identity principle. The risk of every admitted table is
$$
\mathcal R_{p,k}(f):=\mathbb E_p(f(Y_1,\ldots,Y_k)-Y_{n+1})^2
=q\left(1+\frac1k\right)
 +\mathbb E_p\operatorname{Var}(f(Y_1,\ldots,Y_k)\mid S_k),
\qquad S_k=\sum_{i=1}^kY_i,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.4}
$$
for every $n\ge k$. Thus $f_k^*$ is the unique minimizing table for every $0<p<1$. The class contains three tables at $k=2$ and $2{,}144{,}975$ tables at $k=4$; it is not a singleton constraint.

For the tuple of all checkpoint tables, a Definition-D.1f contract retains one typed one-bit loss-verification protocol at each checkpoint, each evaluated under a fresh complete source trial, and the empty restrictions. Its response vector consists of Bernoulli kernels with parameters $\mathcal R_{p,2^j}(f_{2^j})$. Numerical loss-bit labels are fixed. Use the cone $\mathbb R_+^{J+2}$, resource vector
$$
r(\mathbf f)=\bigl(\Gamma_0\mathcal R_{p,1}(f_1),\ldots,
\Gamma_0\mathcal R_{p,K}(f_K),\ P_{\rm svc}\bigr),\qquad \Gamma_0>0,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.5}
$$
and positive dual weights $(1/(J+1),\ldots,1/(J+1),1)$. Here $\Gamma_0$ is a positive power-equivalent task tariff. The service charge $P_{\rm svc}$ is supplied in item 5 and is identical for every admitted tuple. Risks and cost descend to the stated finite response quotient. The selected tuple $\mathbf f^*$ is its unique minimum. In Definition 7's normalization, the registered benefit $-(PP^{-1}-1)/k_{PP}=-\mathrm{PE}$ produces this objective after expectation; the task tariff is separate from physical service energy.

A calibrated table on $k$ bits lifts to an admitted table on $2k$ bits by ignoring the last $k$ inputs. The actual next checkpoint therefore compares within the larger admitted class. For the selected processor,
$$
\mathbb E(\mathrm{PE}(A_n^-,Y_{n+1})-\mathrm{PE}(A_n^+,Y_{n+1}))
=\begin{cases}q/n,&n=2,4,8,\ldots,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.6}
$$
At a held step the two raw losses are literally equal. At a checkpoint the realized difference can have either sign; (6) is the same-target mean gain.

2. **Owned response, scale selection and harmonics.** Define the domain response by the expected excess proper risk
$$
F_p(x):=\mathbb E\,\mathrm{PE}(A_{\lfloor x\rfloor}^+,Y_{\lfloor x\rfloor+1})-q
=q\,2^{-\lfloor\log_2x\rfloor},\qquad x\ge1.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.7}
$$
The subtracted $q$ is the independently registered source variance. The raw proper loss is nonnegative; an individual baseline-subtracted score may be negative. No finite score observation is identified with $F_p$.

For every valid scale pair in a finite horizon, and on the compatible half-line response family,
$$
F_p(2x)=\tfrac12F_p(x),\qquad
F_p(x)=x^{-1}P_p(\log_2x),\qquad P_p(u)=q\,2^{\{u\}}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.8}
$$
The binary checkpoint rule selects $\lambda=2$, and the actual sample-mean variance selects $\alpha=-1$. The profile is bounded, nonconstant and period one, with its phase anchored by the first completed one-sample bank. With the Fourier convention of Theorem P.8.9a.12.6,
$$
c_m=\frac{q}{\ln2-2\pi i m},\qquad
c_0=\frac{q}{\ln2},\qquad
2|c_1|=\frac{2q}{\sqrt{(\ln2)^2+4\pi^2}},\qquad
\arg c_1=\arctan\frac{2\pi}{\ln2},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.9}
$$
and, for $M\ge1$,
$$
\left\|P_p-\sum_{|m|\le M}c_me^{2\pi imu}\right\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2
\le\frac{q^2}{2\pi^2M}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.10}
$$
The first harmonic is the largest nonconstant one. Fourier equality is in $L^2$; the specified checkpoint values remain the right-continuous values in (7)–(8).

3. **Exact finite source, proper-loss detector and complete word.** For an exact finite fair-bit source use $p=a/2^d$ with integers $d\ge1$ and $0<a<2^d$. Prepare $d$ fresh independent fair bits, interpret them as $U\in\{0,\ldots,2^d-1\}$ and write $Y=\mathbf1\{U<a\}$. Retain the draw and comparator records. This realizes the dyadic subfamily exactly. The statistical identities (4)–(10) hold for every Bernoulli parameter; exact bounded fair-bit preparation is asserted for the stated dyadic inputs.

Encode each committed forecast by the integer $B_n^\pm=K A_n^\pm\in\{0,\ldots,K\}$. At the next source tick compute and retain
$$
T_n^\pm=(B_n^\pm-KY_{n+1})^2\in\{0,\ldots,K^2\}.
$$
For each sign prepare a fresh independent $2J$-bit integer $V_n^\pm$ uniform on $\{0,\ldots,K^2-1\}$ and return the loss flag
$$
Z_n^\pm=\mathbf1\{V_n^\pm<T_n^\pm\},\qquad
\mathbb E[Z_n^\pm\mid B_n^\pm,Y_{n+1}]=T_n^\pm/K^2
=\mathrm{PE}(A_n^\pm,Y_{n+1}).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.11}
$$
The threshold register has at least $2J+1$ bits and includes the sentinel $K^2$. At $J=0$ the draw has zero bits, is the singleton value $0$, and the $0/1$ loss is returned exactly. The two flags need not equal their raw scores or each other on one trial.

The final logical word contains every $(n,k(n),A_n^-,A_n^+,Y_{n+1},T_n^-/K^2,T_n^+/K^2,Z_n^-,Z_n^+)$, with its index labels and the source-admission flag. Forecasts and raw scores are decoded rational values. For any admitted tuple, its complete law is obtained by assigning each source string $y_1,\ldots,y_{K+1}$ probability $p^{\sum y_i}(1-p)^{K+1-\sum y_i}$, deterministically computing its forecasts and raw losses $\ell_n^\pm$, and using the conditionally independent factors
$$
\prod_{n=1}^K\prod_{s\in\{-,+\}}
(\ell_n^s)^{z_n^s}(1-\ell_n^s)^{1-z_n^s}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.12}
$$
for the flags. At probabilities $0$ and $1$ this expression has its ordinary Bernoulli-kernel meaning. This supplies the entire normalized finite response, including correlations between acquisition indices. The table-to-word map is realized by the actual circuit, not by replacing its records with their expectations.

4. **Compatible finite horizons and registered observations.** Use the selected sample-mean tables at every horizon; more generally, admitted horizon tuples must agree as rational-valued functions on every overlapping checkpoint bank. Fix the same source parameter $p$ and couple these horizon devices to the same source sequence and to an independent infinite fair-bit tape for each pair $(n,\pm)$. For a forecast with checkpoint denominator $k=2^j$, the flag in any horizon $J\ge j$ depends only on the first $2j$ bits of its tape: the remaining bits cannot change the comparison to a threshold whose denominator is $k^2$. The rational forecast, teacher, raw score and flag prefixes are therefore pathwise compatible. They define the half-line response (7), and every finite restriction has the explicit finite implementation in item 5. The finite device asserts (8) exactly when both labels are in $[1,K+1)$.

This compatibility is the declared logical acquisition/forecast/verification projection. Physical clock periods, carrier sizes and service ledgers remain horizon-indexed data. Their complete raw time/cost records are not identified across different horizons. The $x<1$ continuation of the function in (7) is a mathematical extension if used in Theorem P.8.9a.12.6; the physical acquisition domain starts at one sample.

For $M$ independent complete replicas and the after-loss means $\widehat F(n)=M^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^M Z_{n,r}^+-q$,
$$
\mathbb P\!\left\{\max_{1\le n\le K}|\widehat F(n)-F_p(n)|>\eta\right\}
\le2K e^{-2M\eta^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.13}
$$
The same bound holds with the raw proper losses in place of their randomized flags. Independence is across complete replicas; budgets within one word are correlated. Observation-dependent stopping or budget selection needs its own registered sampling law. A simultaneous relative error $\varepsilon$ over the horizon is ensured by the sufficient sample size
$$
M\ge\frac{K^2}{2\varepsilon^2q^2}\ln\frac{2K}{\delta}
$$
for failure probability at most $\delta\in(0,1)$. These are source-law sampling predictions.

5. **Complete finite circuit, deadlines and resources.** Use the finite Boolean/fair-source carrier primitives of Theorem P.8.9a.12.5b. Choose an integer word width $w\ge4(K+d+J+16)$, increased when needed so every declared source-description or ledger field fits its separately typed allocation. Prediction/count/score fields are exact integers, with a signed score residual and unsigned nonnegative fields; no fixed-point rounding is used. The finite source parameters and positive service coefficients have their registered finite descriptions and units.

For each bank $k=2^j$, store $2^k$ table words encoding $Kf_k(z)$, its $k$ completed-data bits, and the $k+1$ target calibration sums $s\binom{k}{s}$. Before acquisition, a fixed-length checker verifies each table word is in $\{0,K/k,\ldots,K\}$, right-shifts to its numerator $r_z$, accumulates the count-layer sums and tests (2). Each invalid word is masked to zero in a sanitized lookup table before any arithmetic or runtime use; its original word and the admission-failure flag remain retained. The sanitized words are the mask-gate outputs already counted in (14) and (17). An invalid source threshold is similarly replaced by $1$ for the fixed $d\ge1$ comparator, with its failure retained. The source threshold is checked as well. No branch short-circuits the schedule, and failures remain output outcomes rather than being discarded. One padded gate bound is
$$
G_{\rm cfg}=32w+\sum_{j=0}^J\left[
2^{k_j}(64w^2+16w)+12w(k_j+1)\right],\qquad k_j=2^j.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.14}
$$
All admitted tuples pass. This checker and its source-independent calibration constants belong to the actual setup ledger.

A table lookup retains the $k$ complemented input bits, forms each of the $2^k$ address matches, and uses the matched row to select every output bit. With the table bits treated as inputs, a fixed gate census is
$$
L_k=k+2^k(k-1)+w(2^{k+1}-1).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.15}
$$
It applies equally to every table content. Unfilled completed-data banks contain fixed zeros; at acquisition $n=k_j$ the first $k_j$ front-end bits are copied into that bank, once. Every bank lookup executes in every padded stage, but only the most recent completed bank supplies the committed forecast. The partial front end and all unselected archives have no additional route into that forecast. At a checkpoint the before word is copied from the prior commitment; at the first step it equals the after word.

There are $K+1$ stages. Each prepares $d+4J$ fair bits, including two independent verifier draws even in the dummy first stage. It generates the current teacher, handles a completed-bank copy, runs all lookups, commits the active forecast when $n\le K$, and privately verifies the two forecasts from the preceding stage. The last stage verifies step $K$ and keeps its unused new forecast work as padding. Four signed integer subtraction/square slots and two loss comparisons suffice for verification. Using the $64w^2$ arithmetic and $8w$ comparison circuits of Theorem P.8.9a.12.5b, reserve
$$
G_{\rm step}=8(d+1)+\sum_{j=0}^J L_{k_j}
 +256w^2+16w+2K+32w.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.16}
$$
The $2K$ reserve covers completed-data copies and padding. The $32w$ reserve covers before/after commitments, teacher and score staging, counters, denominator/index labels and flag copies. The source comparator has width $d+1$. The schedule is unrolled at configuration time: the active-bank output and copy destinations at each stage are fixed wires in that compiled stage. No runtime multiplexer over the bank list is presumed in this reserve. All control choices are independent of source values, with no source-dependent branch latency.

Let the final output allocation have
$$
O=K(6w+3)+1
$$
bits for the six integer words $(n,k,B^-,B^+,T^-,T^+)$, the teacher and two loss flags at every index, and the admission flag. Copy these records into final readout pointers. A complete allocation and operation count are
$$
\begin{split}
M_{\rm coin}&=(K+1)(d+4J),\\
G_{\rm tot}&=G_{\rm cfg}+(K+1)G_{\rm step}+O,\\
R_{\rm bit}&=64w+w\sum_{j=0}^J(2^{k_j}+k_j+1)
 +(2K-1)+M_{\rm coin}+G_{\rm tot}+O.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.17}
$$
The allocation contains immutable program/calibration data, completed banks, every fresh source bit, all intermediate gate outputs, old forecasts, private verification records and output pointers. Unused reserved cells stay at their ready values. Scratch inputs and displaced values are retained; there is no reset or closed-reuse step.

Fix positive per-ready-bit, per-fair-bit, per-gate and per-output-bit durations $\tau_r,\tau_c,\tau_g,\tau_m$, setup time $\tau_{\rm set}$ and guard time $\tau_{\rm guard}$. Choose
$$
\begin{split}
\Delta_J&\ge(d+4J)\tau_c+G_{\rm step}\tau_g+\tau_{\rm guard},\\
T_{\rm prep}&=\tau_{\rm set}+R_{\rm bit}\tau_r+G_{\rm cfg}\tau_g,\\
T_{\rm tot}&=T_{\rm prep}+(K+1)\Delta_J+O(\tau_g+\tau_m).
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.18}
$$
The forecast at stage $n$ is committed before the next stage starts and before its next teacher is generated. All public readout follows final verification. The index-to-clock map, including guards and preparation, is part of this horizon's source record. It does not turn acquisition-budget scaling into an unregistered elapsed-time law.

With fixed positive setup energy $E_{\rm set}$, per-ready/source/gate/readout charges $e_r,e_c,e_g,e_m$, controller power $P_0$ and per-cell maintenance $p_r$, the registered source-service law is
$$
E_{\rm svc}=E_{\rm set}+R_{\rm bit}e_r+M_{\rm coin}e_c
 +G_{\rm tot}e_g+Oe_m+(P_0+R_{\rm bit}p_r)T_{\rm tot},\qquad
P_{\rm svc}=E_{\rm svc}/T_{\rm tot}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.19}
$$
All cells and hardware are present and maintained throughout the registered preparation and run. The primitive service contract makes these charges independent of data/table values; identical topology alone is not used as an assertion of identical switching heat in other hardware. The fixed setup entry owns the controller, source interfaces and precompiled descriptions. The PCE comparison in item 1 charges this whole-run amount once, through its normalized objective. Different horizon resources remain distinct.

Each Boolean gate has the retained-input unitary $|x,z\rangle\mapsto|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle$ of Theorem P.8.9a.12.5b, and is realized by $H_f=\pi\hbar(I-U_f)/(2\tau_g)$. The $R_{\rm bit}$ two-state registers supply a finite carrier. Fresh fair-bit preparations are normalized and independent, and all deterministic table/ready states have their declared basis values. Diagonal final-output projectors sum to identity; concatenation gives the complete normalized instrument, including rejected configurations. Its operator-norm gate action is at most $\pi\hbar G_{\rm tot}$; (19) is the separately owned service-energy record. On the admitted diagonal source it realizes the entire word law (12).

6. **Perturbation and observation envelope.** For a registered implementation, let the total prepared-source trace-distance discrepancy be at most $\varepsilon_{\rm src}$ and let the implemented gate/readout channels have half-diamond-norm discrepancies $\varepsilon_l$ from their registered ideal channels, uniformly including retained ancillas. The full observed word, with all flags and rejects retained, has total-variation discrepancy at most
$$
\varepsilon_J=\min\{1,\varepsilon_{\rm src}+\sum_l\varepsilon_l\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.6a.20}
$$
These are independently supplied source/implementation bounds. For an iid Bernoulli parameter error $|p'-p|\le\eta_p$, the source part may use $(K+1)\eta_p$ for the teacher word, together with the separately bounded verifier/ready preparations. An additional baseline-calibration error is at most $\eta_p$, since $|p'(1-p')-p(1-p)|\le|p'-p|$. Add the applicable bias to (13). The corresponding scaling defect is at most the response-error bound at $2x$ plus half that at $x$. This envelope preserves every failure outcome and does not convert absence of a populated implementation record into an empirical acceptance.

A concrete nonempty member uses $p=1/4$ from a two-bit threshold source. At checkpoint $k=4$, its expected proper loss is $15/64$, excess response is $3/64$, and mean proper improvement over the probability-$1/2$ baseline is $1/64$. Its true same-teacher gain at the $2$-to-$4$ checkpoint is $3/64$. Every datum and resource count above is finite at $J=2$; positive unit-scaled rational service coefficients give an explicit source packet without measured response inputs.

*Proof.* Let $\bar f_s$ be the mean of $f$ over strings of weight $s$. Unbiasedness is the polynomial identity
$$
\sum_{s=0}^k\binom{k}{s}\bar f_s p^s(1-p)^{k-s}=p
=\sum_{s=0}^k\binom{k}{s}\frac{s}{k}p^s(1-p)^{k-s}.
$$
The Bernstein coefficients are unique: after division by $(1-p)^k$ and substitution $t=p/(1-p)$, equality is an ordinary polynomial identity in $t>0$. Thus $\bar f_s=s/k$, which is exactly (2). Equality on all dyadic parameters gives the same identity because a polynomial vanishing on a dense set vanishes identically.

Given $S_k=s$, the training strings are uniform over that layer. Therefore $\mathbb E[f\mid S_k]=S_k/k$ and $\mathbb E f=p$. The independent next teacher contributes variance $q$, while total variance gives
$$
\operatorname{Var}_p f=\operatorname{Var}_p(S_k/k)
 +\mathbb E_p\operatorname{Var}(f\mid S_k)
=\frac qk+\mathbb E_p\operatorname{Var}(f\mid S_k).
$$
This proves (4). Every source string has positive probability when $0<p<1$. Equality forces every table entry in each layer to equal $s/k$, so the minimizer is unique. At $k=2$, the two interior numerator entries sum to $2$, giving three tables. At $k=4$, the layer counts are $1,35,1751,35,1$: the central count is the coefficient of $t^{12}$ in $(1+t+\cdots+t^4)^6$. Their product is $2{,}144{,}975$. These counts concern the exact finite class, before any observation.

The loss-verification construction (11) below gives the Bernoulli kernels used in the branch contract. Fixed numerical labels make their equality precisely equality of the corresponding risks. The resource vector is constant on this finite quotient, the orthant has the stated positive dual certificate, and the same physical cost applies to every table tuple. Each component is uniquely minimized by its sample-mean table; positive averaging gives the unique selected tuple. A $k$-table lifted to $2k$ inputs still has grid values in the larger grid and is unbiased for every parameter, so it satisfies the larger calibration constraints. For the actual means, at $n=2k$ the old risk against $Y_{2k+1}$ is $q(1+1/k)$ and the new risk is $q(1+1/(2k))$, proving (6). Held forecasts coincide exactly, hence so do their raw losses; their independent randomized flags have mean difference zero there.

The variance of $S_k/k$ is $q/k$. This proves (7), since $\lfloor\log_2\lfloor x\rfloor\rfloor=\lfloor\log_2x\rfloor$ for $x\ge1$. Adding one to this floor under $x\mapsto2x$ gives (8). The periodic profile is $q2^{u-\lfloor u\rfloor}$. Integrating over one period yields
$$
c_m=\int_0^1 q2^u e^{-2\pi imu}du
=q\,\frac{e^{\ln2-2\pi im}-1}{\ln2-2\pi im}
=\frac q{\ln2-2\pi im}.
$$
Its nonconstant coefficient magnitudes decrease with $|m|$, giving (9). Parseval gives the exact omitted squared norm
$$
2q^2\sum_{m>M}\frac1{(\ln2)^2+4\pi^2m^2}
\le\frac{q^2}{2\pi^2}\sum_{m>M}\frac1{m^2}
\le\frac{q^2}{2\pi^2M}.
$$
The bounded half-line profile has a unique period-one extension, so the same argument as in Theorem P.8.9a.12.10a applies the Fourier representation of Theorem P.8.9a.12.6 on its physical acquisition domain. It does not assign new experiments to $x<1$.

The dyadic source comparator has exactly $a$ accepting bit strings out of $2^d$, and fresh preparations make the successive teachers independent. Given an actual forecast and teacher, exactly $T_n^\pm$ of the $K^2$ verifier words accept. This proves (11), including the endpoints and $J=0$. Distinct verifier draws are independent conditional on the source word, so (12) follows. Summing its Bernoulli factors over all flags gives one, and summing the source factors gives one. The integer and rational record fields are deterministic functions of these data and the admitted tables. This proves the complete word law without a sample-to-expectation substitution.

For compatibility, write the forecast as $r/k$ with $k=2^j$ and the loss numerator as $h=(r-kY)^2$. At horizon $J\ge j$, its threshold is $h2^{2(J-j)}$. Decompose the longer verifier word into its first $2j$ bits $V_j$ and the remaining bits $W$:
$$
V_J=2^{2(J-j)}V_j+W,\qquad 0\le W<2^{2(J-j)}.
$$
Then $V_J<h2^{2(J-j)}$ exactly when $V_j<h$. This includes equality at the threshold and the deterministic $j=0$ case. Common source and verifier tapes therefore couple every retained logical prefix identically. Table and output integer widths may differ, but their registered rational decoders give the same forecasts and raw scores. The source construction supplies each finite restriction with its own clock and cost record. The relative error claim in item 4 follows from $F_p(n)\ge q/K$ and the absolute Hoeffding/union bound (13).

It remains to check that the implementation records are populated. Every table word is unsigned, and the grid check tests its range and its low $J-j$ zero bits. The decoded numerator has value at most $k$. The checker adds it to the accumulator for its precompiled address weight $s$ and compares the final sum to $s\binom{k}{s}$. Layer sums never exceed $k2^k$ on masked valid entries. The chosen word width contains these values, the score sentinel $K^2$, signed score residuals and all acquisition indices. A $64w^2$ padded adder, at most $16w$ range/divisibility/mask/flag gates per entry, and $12w$ final comparison/flag gates per layer give (14); the additional $32w$ includes the source-parameter checks. Invalid configurations set the retained flag and the fixed schedule continues.

For lookup, complementing the $k$ input bits costs $k$ retained-output gates. Each address match uses $k-1$ AND gates, with the one-input case interpreted as a wire. For each of the $w$ output bits, $2^k$ AND gates select row/table-bit pairs and $2^k-1$ OR gates combine them. This gives (15), even when some stored bits are zero. Every candidate has the same circuit, storage width and gate trace.

In a stage, the source uses an $8(d+1)$ comparator. At most one data bank becomes complete, and its at most $K$ bits are copied from the front end; the $2K$ reserve includes padding. Every lookup executes, with unfilled banks using their unchanged zero data. Four exact integer subtraction/square operations evaluate the two preceding losses, and two $8w$ comparisons evaluate their flags. The $32w$ reserve supplies the forecast, score, source-bit, flag, index and denominator transfers, including the initial and final dummy cases. These facts establish (16). The $K+1$ identical stage reservations and final $O$ pointer copies give $G_{\rm tot}$. The separate counts in (17) allocate all table/calibration constants, bank bits, source draws, gate outputs and readout records. Any overlapping logical use is assigned a distinct reserved cell if needed; unused allocated cells retain their specified ready values. Thus no hidden reset or discarded scratch information is needed.

All primitives are those of the already specified finite carrier class. The independent fair preparations and basis-state tables followed by retained-input basis permutations have the classical probabilities just computed. Their finite unitary implementation and final complete diagonal instrument prove the physical response map. Setup checks, source calls, all lookups, dummy paths and final readout appear in the explicit timing and energy counts. Equation (18) puts each active forecast before the next stage's source generation. Admission, controller, ready-state, readout and maintenance charges in (19) are common source-contract entries, not consequences inferred from equal logical gate counts. Increasing the horizon changes these actual resources, while preserving the defined logical response projection.

Finally, the telescoping channel comparison in trace norm adds the uniform source and half-diamond errors; diagonal measurement cannot increase trace distance. This proves (20) for the whole word. A maximal coupling of iid Bernoulli$(p)$ and Bernoulli$(p')$ samples fails with probability at most $(K+1)|p-p'|$ on the teacher word. The variance-baseline bound follows from the derivative $1-2p$, whose absolute value is at most one. Expectations of bounded loss flags change by at most the word's total variation. Applying the triangle inequality to $\widetilde F(2x)-\widetilde F(x)/2$ gives the stated scaling-defect envelope. These are conditional implementation bounds; their empirical inputs and independent campaign acceptance remain separately owned. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a127-conditional-kleiber-scaling-on-the-d_mathrmspace-3-biological-transport-branch"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.7 (Conditional Kleiber Scaling on the $D_{\mathrm{space}}=3$ Biological Transport Branch).** Consider an idealized terminal-invariant biological transport branch embedded in $D_{\mathrm{space}}=D$ spatial dimensions. Suppose the transport network has branching ratio $n>1$ and levels $k=0,\ldots,K$, with $N_k=n^k$ vessels at level $k$ and $N_K=n^K$ terminal service units. Assume:

1. terminal invariance: terminal length $l_K$ and terminal radius $r_K$ are independent of $K$, and each terminal unit supplies the same metabolic throughput;
2. space-filling geometry:
$$
l_k=l_K n^{(K-k)/D};
$$
3. area-preserving transport:
$$
N_k r_k^2=N_K r_K^2
\qquad
\text{for every }k;
$$
4. PCE-optimized biological resource allocation makes body mass proportional to total transport-network volume and metabolic rate proportional to terminal throughput:
$$
M\asymp V_{\mathrm{net}},
\qquad
B\asymp N_K.
$$

Then, as $K\to\infty$,
$$
B\asymp M^{D/(D+1)}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.12}
$$
On the PU branch with $D_{\mathrm{space}}=3$,
$$
B\asymp M^{3/4}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.13}
$$

*Proof.* The volume of level $k$ vessels is proportional to
$$
N_k r_k^2 l_k.
$$
By area preservation,
$$
N_k r_k^2=N_K r_K^2=n^K r_K^2.
$$
By space-filling geometry,
$$
l_k=l_K n^{(K-k)/D}.
$$
Therefore
$$
V_{\mathrm{net}}
\asymp
\sum_{k=0}^{K}N_k r_k^2l_k
=
r_K^2l_K n^K
\sum_{k=0}^{K} n^{(K-k)/D}.
$$
With $j=K-k$,
$$
\sum_{k=0}^{K} n^{(K-k)/D}
=
\sum_{j=0}^{K} n^{j/D}
=
\frac{n^{(K+1)/D}-1}{n^{1/D}-1}.
$$
Thus
$$
V_{\mathrm{net}}
\asymp
n^K n^{K/D}
=
(n^K)^{(D+1)/D}
=
N_K^{(D+1)/D},
$$
where the omitted multiplicative constants depend on $n,D,l_K,r_K$ but not on $K$. Since $M\asymp V_{\mathrm{net}}$ and $B\asymp N_K$,
$$
M\asymp B^{(D+1)/D},
$$
and hence
$$
B\asymp M^{D/(D+1)}.
$$
Setting $D=D_{\mathrm{space}}=3$ gives $B\asymp M^{3/4}$. ∎

<a id="proposition-p89a127a-finite-size-kleiber-window-and-areadissipation-ledger"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.12.7a (Finite-Size Kleiber Window and Area/Dissipation Ledger).** In Theorem P.8.9a.12.7, register assumption 4 as the exact ledger $M=\rho_MV_{\mathrm{net}}$ and $B=b_TN_K$ with constants $\rho_M,b_T>0$, where $V_{\mathrm{net}}=\pi\sum_{k=0}^KN_kr_k^2l_k$, and put $s_D:=D/(D+1)$ and $\eta_K:=n^{-(K+1)/D}$.

1. *Area-preserving ledger.* Under assumptions 1--3, for every $K\ge0$,
$$
B=b_T\,A_D^{-s_D}(1-\eta_K)^{-s_D}M^{s_D},
\qquad
A_D:=\frac{\rho_M\pi r_K^2l_K\,n^{1/D}}{n^{1/D}-1},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.7a.1}
$$
with $1\le(1-\eta_K)^{-s_D}\le(1-\eta_K)^{-1}$. For $0\le K_1<K_2$, the window exponent $b_{\mathrm{eff}}:=\ln(B_{K_2}/B_{K_1})/\ln(M_{K_2}/M_{K_1})$ satisfies
$$
0<s_D-b_{\mathrm{eff}}\le\frac{D^2\,\eta_{K_1}}{(D+1)^2(1-\eta_{K_1})(K_2-K_1)\ln n}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.7a.2}
$$
2. *Impedance ledger.* If every level-$k$ vessel has wave admittance $Y_k=\pi r_k^2/Z_0$ with a level-independent constant $Z_0>0$, the junction reflection coefficients $\Gamma_k=(Y_k-nY_{k+1})/(Y_k+nY_{k+1})$ vanish for every $k<K$ exactly when assumption 3 holds.
3. *Poiseuille dissipation ledger.* If instead, with terminal flow $Q_K>0$ fixed independently of $K$, as in assumption 1, and $Q_k=Q_KN_K/N_k$, the radii minimize the PCE transport cost
$$
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{tr}}(r_0,\ldots,r_K)=\sum_{k=0}^KN_k\left[\frac{8\mu_{\mathrm v}l_kQ_k^2}{\pi r_k^4}+\lambda_{\mathrm v}\pi r_k^2l_k\right]
$$
with viscosity $\mu_{\mathrm v}>0$ and volume price $\lambda_{\mathrm v}>0$, then the unique minimizer is $r_k=(16\mu_{\mathrm v}Q_k^2/(\pi^2\lambda_{\mathrm v}))^{1/6}$, so $r_k^3\propto Q_k$ and $N_kr_k^2=N_Kr_K^2n^{-(K-k)/3}$, which violates assumption 3 for $n>1$ and $K\ge1$. Under assumptions 1--2,
$$
M=\rho_M\pi r_K^2l_Kn^K\sum_{j=0}^Kn^{j(1/D-1/3)}.
$$
For $D=3$ this is $M=\rho_M\pi r_K^2l_KN_K(1+\log_nN_K)$, so $B=b_TM/[\rho_M\pi r_K^2l_K(1+\log_nN_K)]$ and $\ln B/\ln M\to1$. For $D<3$, $B\asymp M^{3D/(2D+3)}$, and for $D>3$, $B\asymp M$. In every dimension $D\ge1$ the exponent of this ledger differs from $D/(D+1)$.

*Proof.* For item 1, assumptions 1--3 give $N_kr_k^2l_k=n^Kr_K^2l_Kn^{(K-k)/D}$, and summing the geometric series gives $M=A_DN_K^{(D+1)/D}(1-\eta_K)$. Solving for $N_K$ gives (P.8.9a.12.7a.1), and $0<1-\eta_K<1$ with $0<s_D<1$ gives the bracket. For the window, put $\Lambda=(K_2-K_1)\ln n$ and $\varepsilon=\ln[(1-\eta_{K_2})/(1-\eta_{K_1})]$, which lies in $(0,-\ln(1-\eta_{K_1})]$ because $\eta_K$ decreases in $K$. Then $\ln(B_{K_2}/B_{K_1})=\Lambda$ and $\ln(M_{K_2}/M_{K_1})=\Lambda/s_D+\varepsilon$, so
$$
s_D-b_{\mathrm{eff}}=\frac{s_D\varepsilon}{\Lambda/s_D+\varepsilon}\in\Bigl(0,\frac{s_D^2\varepsilon}{\Lambda}\Bigr],
$$
and $-\ln(1-\eta)\le\eta/(1-\eta)$ gives (P.8.9a.12.7a.2).

For item 2, $\Gamma_k=0$ exactly when $Y_k=nY_{k+1}$, that is, $r_k^2=nr_{k+1}^2$, which is $N_kr_k^2=N_{k+1}r_{k+1}^2$.

For item 3, the cost is a sum of one-variable terms $g_k(r)=a_kr^{-4}+c_kr^2$ with $a_k=8\mu_{\mathrm v}N_kl_kQ_k^2/\pi$ and $c_k=\lambda_{\mathrm v}\pi N_kl_k$, both positive because $Q_K>0$. Each $g_k$ tends to $\infty$ at $0$ and at $\infty$ and has the single critical point $r^6=2a_k/c_k=16\mu_{\mathrm v}Q_k^2/(\pi^2\lambda_{\mathrm v})$, which is therefore its unique minimizer. Then $r_k=r_K(N_K/N_k)^{1/3}=r_Kn^{(K-k)/3}$, which gives $N_kr_k^2$ and, with $l_k=l_Kn^{(K-k)/D}$, the displayed sum with $j=K-k$. For $D=3$ every summand equals $1$. For $D<3$ the sum is comparable to $n^{K(1/D-1/3)}$, so $M\asymp N_K^{(2D+3)/(3D)}$, and for $D>3$ the sum converges, so $M\asymp N_K$. Since $B=b_TN_K$, these give the stated exponents, and $3D/(2D+3)=D/(D+1)$ would force $D=0$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a127b-finite-predictive-tubular-colony-realization-and-complete-transport-selection"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.7b (Finite Predictive Tubular-Colony Realization and Complete Transport Selection).** On the finite PBTC source defined below, the complexity-to-throughput map, recovery-complete impedance selector and component-corrected allometry have the following realization. All constants, source ports, physical hierarchy and finite geometric bounds are premises of this named organism model.

*Proof and source specification.*

### Colony realization

#### 1. Fixed domain and source inventory

Fix $n=8$, $D=3$, a finite integer $K_{\max}\ge 2$, and $K\in\{0,\dots,K_{\max}\}$. There are $N=8^K$ cells. For each $K$ choose a balanced embedded tree with level counts $8^k$ and segment lengths $l_k=l_T 2^{K-k}$. All cells have the same biochemical port specification and the same terminal area $A_T=\pi r_T^2$. All independently fixed parameters below are common across this family.

The pressure carrier is the positive linear long-wave metric-graph model in the carrier analysis below, section 1. Lumen density $\rho_{f}>0$ and effective compliance $\chi>0$ give $c_w=(\rho_f\chi)^{-1/2}$, $Z_0=\rho_f c_w$, $Y_k=A_k/Z_0$. Node pressures agree and flows sum. These are the constitutive equations of the formal domain, not conclusions about arbitrary viscous biological fluid. The tree has zero continuing viscous dissipation. Its root-entry adapter is independently dissipative, with fixed length $a>0$ and damping $\gamma>0$; the carrier analysis below, section 8 derives its transmission $\zeta=\exp(-2\gamma a/c_w)\in(0,1)$ and $d=\zeta^{-1}-1>0$. Every forward work input crosses this adapter. Root-side return recovery and cyclic storage are allowed without restriction beyond passivity. Additional distributed work-entry ports are a different source topology. Section 8 below retains the separate distributed positive-loss branch.

A terminal pulse has fixed zero-integral compactly supported pressure perturbation $p_T(t)$, support length $\delta<2 l_T/c_w$, and energy

$$
W_T=(A_T/Z_0) \int p_T(t)^2\, dt>0.
$$

For example $p_T(t)=p_0\, 16 s^2(1-s)^2(2s-1)$, $s=t/\delta\in[0,1]$, zero outside, with fixed $p_{0}>0$. The integral is $W_T=(A_T/Z_0)p_0^2\delta\,(128/3465)$. This specifies a receiver demand before any area is optimized. Fix $p_{0}$ small relative to the static pressure and the declared linear-response budget. Its absolute peak is at most $p_{0}$, and its integral is zero. Thus each pulse has zero net volume displacement; there is no unowned continuing lumen-fluid transport or static-pressure work. The actuator absorbs positive wave energy over its forward/backward cycle.

The source inventory is:

* lumen fluid and wall elastic energy, and a static pressure-preload store;
* finite membrane cells, cue and substrate ports, route register and verifier;
* nutrient chemical energy and material flux; separate maintenance and service reactions;
* one matched work receiver per cell and its fixed $W_{T}$ demand;
* a root pump with fixed chemical-to-wave efficiency $\eta$ in (0,1];
* junction switch/controller stocks, finite absorbing waste loads, clock and timing ports;
* finite one-time fabrication and assembly energy $E_{\mathrm{build}}$, and all retained component masses;
* output work, heat and labeled waste. No random realization seed is free when a specified microstate is constructed.

The objective compares radii in a closed convex logarithmic neighborhood X of exact matching, with 0 in its interior. It compares the same cells, task law, lengths, deadlines, pump efficiency, terminal pulse and biochemical performance. It does not compare arbitrary alternative organism architectures. Material and biochemical costs that do not change with x remain in the complete objective as constants.

#### 2. The terminal makes a forecast of a later substrate

At time $t_{c}$, cell $i$ receives a cue carrier with a fair bit $X_{i}$. The $X_{i}$ are independent. At $t_s>t_c$, after the route has been committed and while the cue is inaccessible to that route's decision input, a new service substrate arrives with label

$$
Y_i=X_i \oplus Z_i,
$$

where the $Z_{i}$ are independent $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\epsilon)$, $0<\epsilon<1/2$, independent of the cues. The future substrate is absent at the commitment time. The registered deadline is before any measurement of $Y_{i}$. The task is to select a catalytic route $R_{i}\in\{0,1\}$ that will extract useful service work from the later substrate. The full cue carrier remains in an owned holding compartment until the end of the cycle so that reset may be reversible; it cannot be reread after commitment to revise the forecast.

Conditional on $X_i=x$, the two future-label probabilities are $1-\epsilon$ and $\epsilon$. The unique optimal route is $R_i=x$, with success probability $1-\epsilon$. A route with no access to $X_{i}$ has success at most 1/2. Under the zero-regret task, every cue vector must produce its unique Bayes-optimal route vector. Hence any sufficient precommitment record distinguishes all $2^N$ cue vectors, and has capacity at least $N$ bits. A record $R=X$ attains this bound. The positive predictive value is the expected additional useful work $N\Delta_s(1/2-\epsilon)$ per cycle, where $\Delta_{s}>0$ is the independently specified service-substrate chemical energy.

This is prediction of a later, not-yet-present molecule. It is neither perfect universal prediction nor a claim that present-molecule recognition is itself forecasting. The nonzero $\epsilon$ also keeps the actual task score strictly below one.

#### 3. Cyclic biochemical source and energy/entropy ownership

Each cell is a membrane-enclosed finite-state biochemical service unit with two distinct nutrient ports.

1. A maintenance nutrient of chemical energy $\Delta_{m}>0$ is converted each cycle into a lower-energy waste molecule. Its energy supplies the fixed maintenance sink and the declared cyclic control overhead. The maintained variables are membrane integrity, available route catalyst, and empty receiver work register. These variables return to the same state after each cycle. $\Delta_{m}$ is fixed independently of $N$ and the geometric optimization.
2. A service substrate $M_{y}$ has energy $\Delta_{s}$ above its waste $W_{y}$. If committed route $r=y$, conversion transfers $\Delta_{s}$ to an output work packet. If $r\ne y$, conversion transfers the same energy to an owned heat/waste excitation. Both branches consume one service substrate, so the gross chemical conversion is $\Delta_{s}$ regardless of forecast outcome. The distinction is usable work, not an unaccounted change in fuel input.
3. The incoming cue carrier carries $X$ with equal internal energies. A reversible controlled-XOR sets the route $R=X$. After the service reaction, a reversible XOR computes the verification bit $V=R\oplus Y$. The verification outcome is copied to a labeled outgoing waste register; the verifier is uncomputed, and the route is uncomputed using the still-held cue. The cue exits labeled $X$. The cell's finite route and verifier stocks return to their blank states. The service waste carries $Y$ and the verification label $X\oplus Y$, a deterministic redundant record, so no new independent random seed is required.

These maps have a positive finite Hamiltonian implementation, not merely a truth-table energy label. On every finite reaction sector, a desired permutation U that is an involution and commutes with the bare Hamiltonian $H_{b}$ is generated by

$$
H_{\mathrm{gate}}=H_b + (\pi \hbar/(2 t_g))(I-U),
$$

during a fixed finite gate time $t_{g}$. The added term is positive semidefinite. Its propagator is $\exp(-i H_b t_g/\hbar)\, U$. Chemical conversion exchanges equal-total-energy configurations, e.g. $|M_y,\text{work}=0\rangle$ and $|W_y,\text{work}=\Delta_s\rangle$ on the matched branch, and $|M_y,\text{heat}=0\rangle$ and $|W_y,\text{heat}=\Delta_s\rangle$ on the unmatched branch. Route, cue and verifier XORs act within degenerate-energy sectors. Any needed finite permutation is a finite product of such swaps.

Switching the added term on and off is an owned work operation. Since U and $H_{b}$ commute and U is conserved during its pulse, its expectation is unchanged: switch-on work is exactly recovered at switch-off. The temporary nonnegative energy and control hardware remain in the resource stock. It is not a claim that all biological control costs vanish. The separately fixed maintenance conversion $\Delta_{m}$ covers any stipulated irreversible fixed per-cell operation, and an additional positive variable continuing cost is treated in section 8.

The matched receiver absorbs $W_{T}$ each cycle into a named membrane actuator/work-to-heat sink, returning its work register to blank. The nutrient pump and entry adapter supplying that pulse consume $W_T/(\eta\zeta)$ per cell at exact matching. Adapter heat is $d\,W_{T}$ and pump heat is $(\eta^{-1}-1)W_T/\zeta$. These sum with receiver work $W_{T}$ to the actual fuel input. Service work is exported or used by an independently specified load; unused service energy is heat. Cue and substrate label entropy exits through labeled matter ports. Per cell the incoming joint label entropy is $\ln 2+h(\epsilon)$, and the outgoing $(X,Y,X\oplus Y)$ has exactly the same entropy. No Landauer equality, free reset, or erasure of an unknown label is assumed.

The declared organism maintains bounded cellular organization by nutrient conversion, has a selective task with a future-dependent work benefit, and exports entropy and waste. Its service and maintenance components are physical parts of the model, not a relabeling of an acoustic resistor as a cell. Reproduction and evolution are outside this finite service-family claim.

#### 4. Repeated first-arrival service and finite clearing

At each cycle boundary the passive tree is quiescent and has no charged internal emitter/store. Source-side recovery stocks may be charged but inject only through the fixed root-entry adapter. These are actual retained initial/boundary conditions, not assumptions about an unrestricted architecture class. On the balanced tree all direct root-to-terminal paths have length $L_K=\sum_{k=0}^K l_k$. The pulse-width bound $\delta<2 l_T/c_w$ separates the direct pulse at every junction from every returning echo. At each junction, immediately after the trailing edge of its first direct pulse, an owned switch disconnects the star junction and terminates each incident segment in its own matched absorbing load. The switch occurs while the direct local field is zero and before any reflected wave can return. A load imposes the outgoing characteristic boundary condition and absorbs, rather than reflects, every later incoming wave.

After a port is switched, no wave can cross its junction again. Every remaining characteristic packet is therefore absorbed after traversing at most one additional complete segment. All fields are zero by

$$
t_{\mathrm{clear}} \le 2a/c_w + L_K/c_w + \delta + l_0/c_w.
$$

The extra $2a/c_w$ covers forward adapter passage and any returning root characteristic. A recovery competitor has to supply its own finite transfer/clearing schedule under the same service deadline; the universal net-work lower bound does not grant it free hidden initial energy.

Once all fields vanish, reconnecting the original zero-storage junctions costs no acoustic field energy. Switch controls are reversible finite-state cycles with their temporary stock and fixed maintenance cost already owned in section 3. The absorbed late-wave energy is a waste term, not useful cell delivery. No infinite echo tail is silently treated as a reset.

Choose the common cycle period $\tau$ greater than the maximum $t_{\mathrm{clear}}$ over $K\le K_{\max}$ plus the fixed biochemical gate schedule and cue/substrate delays. Inputs repeat only after clearance. A first-arrival pulse and every completing cell have a finite observable deadline, independently of radius optimization. At exact matching there are no echoes, so absorbing loads receive zero late-wave energy; they remain owned hardware and are probed by off-matching tests.

#### 5. Source-energy selection and the complete lifetime objective

Let $x_k=\ln(A_k/(8A_{k+1}))$ for $k<K$; $A_K=A_T$. As proved from wave energy balance in the carrier analysis below,

$$
W_{\mathrm{in}}(x)=N W_T F(x),\quad F(x)=\prod_{k<K} \cosh^2(x_k/2),
$$

and $\operatorname{Hess} F\ge I/2$. The first-pass cell service is exactly $N W_{T}$. The explicit clearing-load implementation disposes surplus $N W_T(F-1)$, and consumes $W_{\mathrm{in}}/(\eta\zeta)$. A recovery competitor may recover all surplus and reuse it at the source side. The recovery-complete theorem gives the strictly selecting lower bound $[N W_T+d N W_{T} F(x)]/\eta$, attained at matching. The tree source port and passive adapter are the same for every competitor. This avoids confusing launched energy with net consumed energy or double-counting delivered work as a second input.

For H completed cycles, the complete gross input-energy ledger is

$$
E_H(x)=E_{\mathrm{build}}(x)+H [N(\Delta_m+\Delta_s)+N W_T F(x)/(\eta \zeta)]+E_{\mathrm{fixed}},
$$

for the explicit clearing-load implementation. For arbitrary passive recovery competitors replace its last operating term by the lower bound $N W_T[1+d F(x)]/\eta$ and add the actual nonnegative recovery losses. Both objectives have the same unique long-run minimizer; the latter has the smaller strong-convexity constant.

where $E_{\mathrm{fixed}}$ is a nonnegative radius-independent setup stock. Positive transient gate stocks are in $E_{\mathrm{fixed}}$ or $E_{\mathrm{build}}$, with their recovered energy explicitly credited; no negative net gate cost is inserted. In this inviscid, non-ageing formal branch there is no radius-dependent continuing material-maintenance rate. The cells do continue to consume $\Delta_{m}$ every cycle.

A concrete construction ledger is

$$
E_{\mathrm{build}}(x)=a_V V(x)+\sum_{k<K} a_{J,k} \exp(3 S_k/2)+a_N N+a_J J+a_0,
$$

with nonnegative independently fixed fabrication-energy coefficients, $J=(N-1)/7$, $S_k=\sum_{j=k}^{K-1}x_j$ and $V=\sum_{k=0}^K N A_T l_k \exp(S_k)$. This represents positive bulk-material fabrication, finite junction fabrication, cellular/controller manufacture and assembly. Include the adapter fabrication energy $a_{\mathrm{adapter}}\, a A_0(x)$, another positive convex exponential, in $E_{\mathrm{build}}$. It is convex. It records a one-time cost, not a hidden continuing rate. A zero coefficient means that resource is supplied from a separately inventoried recoverable stock; component masses remain in section 6.

For every $H>0$ the normalized cost $E_H/H$ is strongly convex on $X$ and has a unique minimizer $x_{H}$. Since 0 is feasible, its variational inequality and strong monotonicity give

$$
\lVert x_H\rVert_2\le[2\eta\zeta/(H N W_T)]\,\lVert\nabla E_{\mathrm{build}}(0)\rVert_2.
$$

For the ideal fully recovered lower-envelope objective, replace $\eta\zeta$ by $\eta/d$. Arbitrary radius-dependent recovery hardware may change its finite-$H$ optimum and must keep its own construction term; the all-competitor long-run lower bound still strictly excludes every mismatched geometry.

This proof remains valid if $x_{H}$ lies on the physical-domain boundary: use $\nabla(E_H/H)(x_H)\cdot(0-x_H)\ge 0$. No false interior stationarity is assumed. Consequently $x_H\to 0$ with the displayed $O(1/H)$ bound, and all associated area and volume errors follow from $|S_k|\le\sqrt{K}\lVert x_H\rVert$.

The complete long-run average input energy is the actual limit

$$
\lim_{H\to\infty} E_H(x)/H = N(\Delta_m+\Delta_s)+N W_T F(x)/(\eta \zeta).
$$

Even when recovery is allowed, every competitor has long-run rate at least $N(\Delta_m+\Delta_s)+N W_T[1+d F(x)]/\eta$. Matching attains both at $N(\Delta_m+\Delta_s)+N W_T/(\eta\zeta)$.

Its unique minimizer on $X$ is $x=0$, derived from the source and independently fixed receivers. Thus the selected long-run geometry is $A_k=8 A_{k+1}$. Construction energy has been included and then amortized by a stated limit; it is not erased from a finite-$H$ optimum. This is an optimization conclusion, not a claim of evolutionary convergence. If a relaxation realization is wanted, projected gradient flow of this smooth strongly convex objective converges to its unique minimizer by the squared-distance differential inequality; its own finite actuator resources would belong to $E_{\mathrm{build}}$.

On the selected branch the actual gross metabolic input rate is exactly

$$
