B_K=b_T N,\quad b_T=(\Delta_m+\Delta_s+W_T/(\eta \zeta))/\tau.
$$

Every term is independently derived from an owned port. The forecast benefit is instead $N(1-\epsilon)\Delta_s/\tau$. Neither quantity is being defined as complexity. At finite $H$, the operating rate is $B_K(x_H)=[N(\Delta_m+\Delta_s)+N W_T F(x_H)/(\eta\zeta)]/\tau$, while fabrication is a separately reported amortized rate $E_{\mathrm{build}}/(H\tau)$. If a total lifetime rate is reported, it includes that latter term.

#### 6. Source-derived mass, wall stress and finite geometric domain

At the common pressure $P_{0}>0$, the wall has an independently fixed admissible hoop stress $\sigma_*>P_0+2p_0$. For a homogeneous thick cylindrical wall with outer radius $R=\beta r$, the elementary Lamé stress field is

$$
\sigma_r(s)=a-b/s^2,\quad \sigma_\theta(s)=a+b/s^2,
$$

$$
a=P r^2/(R^2-r^2),\quad b=P r^2 R^2/(R^2-r^2).
$$

It solves radial force balance, $\sigma_r(r)=-P$, $\sigma_r(R)=0$. Its maximum hoop stress is $P(R^2+r^2)/(R^2-r^2)$. Fix

$$
\beta^2=(\sigma_{*}+P_{\max})/(\sigma_{*}-P_{\max}),\quad P_{\max}=P_0+2p_0,
$$

so the admitted peak load exactly meets the fixed material stress budget. Beta is independent of size and level. Off-matching comparison pulses are restricted to the common small-response domain X so their pressure peaks remain below the same owned maximum; choose X small enough to use the strict factor-two pressure margin fixed above. The matching formula never changes to accommodate an optimized radius. Wall thickness is (beta-1)r, derived from pressure and stress, not chosen for the exponent.

With lumen and wall densities $\rho_f,\rho_w$, the retained straight-segment material mass is

$$
M_{\mathrm{tube}} = [\rho_f+\rho_w(\beta^2-1)] V = \rho_{\mathrm{eff}} V.
$$

The common compliance can be populated explicitly. For plane stress with Young modulus $E_{w}>0$ and Poisson ratio $\nu$ in [0,1/2), the Lamé displacement is

$$
u_r(s)=[(1-\nu)a s+(1+\nu)b/s]/E_w.
$$

Consequently the incremental lumen-area compliance is

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{wall}}=2[(1-\nu)+(1+\nu)\beta^2]/[E_w(\beta^2-1)].
$$

Choose the source $\chi=\chi_{\mathrm{fluid}}+\chi_{\mathrm{wall}}$, $\chi_{\mathrm{fluid}}>0$. It is independent of radius and level, so the actual material choice supplies the common wave admittance. This model is the declared one-dimensional long-wave constitutive branch; no unproved exact reduction of a general three-dimensional Navier-Stokes body is claimed.

The source adapter has a larger incident pulse. At matching its upstream perturbation is $p_T/\sqrt{\zeta}$; choose its independently rated pressure budget $P_{a,\max}=P_0+2p_0/\sqrt{\zeta}$ before optimizing $x$, then shrink $X$ to keep that strict margin. Fix a separate material stress $\sigma_a>P_{a,\max}$ and derive $\beta_a^2=(\sigma_a+P_{a,\max})/(\sigma_a-P_{a,\max})$. Its material density coefficient is $\rho_{\mathrm{adapter}}=\rho_f+\rho_{wa}(\beta_a^2-1)+\rho_{\mathrm{damp}}$, where $\rho_{\mathrm{damp}}\ge 0$ is the explicitly retained damping-medium mass per lumen volume. The adapter is not assigned the network's smaller pressure rating. To match the already fixed $\chi$ with finite elastic materials, choose any $\nu_{a}\in[0,1/2)$ and set

$$
E_a=2[(1-\nu_a)+(1+\nu_a)\beta_a^2]/[(\beta_a^2-1)\chi_{\mathrm{wall}}]>0.
$$

This makes the adapter's wall compliance equal $\chi_{\mathrm{wall}}$. Its fluid density is $\rho_{f}$, hence $Z_{0}$ is unchanged. These independently fixed material/source parameters do not depend on the area optimum or any fitted exponent.

Count all remaining components:

$$
M_K(x)=\rho_{\mathrm{eff}} V_K(x)+\rho_{\mathrm{adapter}} a A_0(x)+m_{\mathrm{cell}} N+m_{\mathrm{pump}} N+m_{\mathrm{node}} J+m_0+M_{\mathrm{junction}}(x),
$$

$$
M_{\mathrm{junction}}(x)=\sum_{k<K} c_{J,k} \exp(3S_k/2),
$$

where all masses are independently nonnegative, $m_{\mathrm{cell}}>0$, and $c_{J,k}$ are the actual chosen junction/control housing volumes times density at matching. Pump count $N$ comes from fixed per-terminal delivered pulse demand with fixed module output-work capacity $W_T/\zeta$ and fixed $\eta$; the $N$ modules feed the common root pressure port. Their total stock scales with delivered work capacity, not with a desired mass exponent. The cue and route registers, verifier and any colony-retained labeled holding records are explicitly included in $m_{\mathrm{cell}}=m_{\mathrm{biochemical}}+m_{\mathrm{holding}}+m_{\mathrm{register}}$. Labeled cue/waste holding inventories over one cycle are included in that same term once; exported material is not counted forever as body mass. The static preload and controller storage masses are included in the appropriate hardware terms.

The preparation factory is external to the organism mass observable. Give it a separate initial stock $M_{\mathrm{fac,in}}$ and final stock $M_{\mathrm{fac,out}}(K)$, plus exported fabrication waste $M_{\mathrm{fab,waste}}(K)$. The actual material balance is $M_{\mathrm{fac,in}}=M_K+M_{\mathrm{fac,out}}(K)+M_{\mathrm{fab,waste}}(K)$ on the declared nonrelativistic material ledger, with zero fabrication waste allowed for the explicit blank-body selection construction. Extracting a body reduces the factory stock; the unchanged initial full factory is never added again to $M_{K}$. The external program tape has its own recorded $N$-bit mass and endpoint label $x$. It is neither an unowned seed nor part of body mass unless physically retained in a cell, in which case it is included in $m_{\mathrm{holding}}$.

The factory's reusable capital, initial/final energy stores, the allocated prefabrication work of the selected blank body, and assembly work are external setup records. $E_{\mathrm{build}}$ charges that body's allocated fabrication/assembly expenditure once; $E_{\mathrm{fixed}}$ records the separately declared fixed setup charge with its actual recovery credits. Unused blank bodies and reusable tools remain in the final factory stock. Their full initial mass or energy is not silently consumed again on each cycle. Reporting a larger preparation-plus-body mass would give the different, explicitly available observable $M_K+M_{\mathrm{fac,out}}+M_{\mathrm{tape,out}}+M_{\mathrm{fab,waste}}$; it is not substituted into the organism's allometric extractor. This boundary choice is fixed for the whole compared family.

At $x=0$,

$$
V_K(0)=A_T l_T 8^K (2^{K+1}-1).
$$

Define the observed, source-derived correction

$$
a_K=[\rho_{\mathrm{adapter}} a N A_T+m_{\mathrm{cell}} N+m_{\mathrm{pump}} N+m_{\mathrm{node}} J+m_0+M_{\mathrm{junction}}(0)]/[\rho_{\mathrm{eff}} V_K(0)].
$$

Then $M_K=\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}V_K(0)(1+a_K)$, with $a_{K}\ge 0$ computed from actual components. This is an identity from mass summation, not a definition of body mass as tube volume. On the finite family, $a_K\le a_{\max}$ gives quantitative uniform $M/V$ bounds. For $K_1<K_2$, $\Lambda=(K_2-K_1)\ln 8$,

$$
b_{\mathrm{eff}} = \Lambda / \{ (4/3)\Lambda + \ln[(1-2^{-K_2-1})/(1-2^{-K_1-1})] + \ln[(1+a_{K_2})/(1+a_{K_1})] \}.
$$

The denominator must be positive; its exact measured/constructed component value is retained. If only a bounds are available, joint interval bounds are propagated before division. With finite-$H$ $x_{H}$, replace $\ln(1+a_K)$ by the full known logarithm $M_K(x_H)/(\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}V_K(0))$, and add $\ln[B_K(x_H)/(b_T N)]$ to the numerator. This yields an observable finite-size allometric prediction with all resources retained.

A finite embedding exists independently of the optimum: choose generic segment directions recursively with the prescribed positive lengths. In three dimensions nonincident line-segment intersections are a measure-zero condition on these finitely many direction choices; forbid collinear incident directions as well. The resulting finite nonincident compact segments and distinct nodes have positive minimum separation. Choose disjoint small junction neighborhoods, and then choose $r_{T}>0$ small enough that all thick tubes, junction housings and cells fit for every $K\le K_{\max}$ and every $x$ in a sufficiently small closed convex neighborhood $X$ of $0$. The finitely many inequalities can be checked in the geometric source record. This proves existence; a numerical embedding record would be needed for numerical dimensions.

The real slenderness constraint is retained:

$$
r_k/l_k=(r_T/l_T)8^{(K-k)/6},
$$

so $r/l\le\epsilon_{\mathrm{geom}}$ imposes $K\le 6\log_8(\epsilon_{\mathrm{geom}}l_T/r_T)$. The family is restricted to that cutoff. No infinite-$K$ physical embodiment follows. The infinite-$K$ allometric statement of Theorem P.8.9a.12.7 remains a mathematical asymptotic of its own ideal premises; this realization supplies a finite physical-model window and its full component-corrected extractor.

#### 7. Actual C_P bridge, with program semantics and random records

##### 7.1 Fixed physical program semantics

The original complexity is Section 2.4.1's minimum admissible program length for an individual microstate, not Shannon entropy of an ensemble and not the logarithm of a memory dimension. Use its explicitly admitted integer binary prefix-length branch. Fix a universal prefix machine U, one blank reference factory state, and the following physical constructor semantics before drawing any cue.

The finite factory has the largest required material/control stocks for $K\le K_{\max}$; its reference state contains no cue-dependent information. Its manufacture and material inventory are owned setup resources. At the specified precommitment slice, future noise labels $Z$ have not entered the colony. They are later incoming substrate-port records, not hidden constructor seeds. A target at a later slice that retains those independent noise outcomes would need their additional record cost. A fixed interpreter can assemble the selected finite tree, initialize its declared pressure and biochemical stocks, prepare a blank cell array, write a literal cue vector $x$ through the energy-degenerate cue XOR gates, and stop at the precommitment prediction slice. The substrate has not arrived. All material positions, model parameters, pulse profiles and gate schedules are fixed computable descriptions; no additional random seed is hidden in them. The target microstate $\mu_{K,x}$ is the actual retained colony at the precommitment slice, including its cue, route, verifier and holding stocks. The complete constructor certificate separately retains the external factory, program-tape and fabrication-waste endpoints just assigned in section 6. The physical program outputs the colony-state projection of that complete record; it never obtains $x$ from an unrecorded input. Its response-equivalence class retains every cell-indexed committed route and cue readout. Two different $x$ are therefore distinct responses, even if their ensemble laws agree.

A program consists of a fixed compiler/interpreter prefix of length $c_{U}$ (the actual chosen universal-machine encoding of this finite physical command constructor, retained as a machine-relative overhead), a self-delimiting size code for $K+1$, and exactly $8^K$ literal bits $x$. Use the Elias $\gamma$ code, of length

$$
h_{\mathrm{size}}(K)=2 \lfloor \log_2(K+1)\rfloor+1.
$$

After reading K the interpreter knows exactly how many literal bits to read. These complete words are prefix-free. The total constructor length is

$$
L_K=N+c_U+h_{\mathrm{size}}(K).
$$

Any other deterministic program producing the same target is allowed to compete; literal coding is an upper witness, not an artificial restriction excluding compressed strings. Nonhalting programs do not realize a target. Randomized constructors must include every seed/record necessary to realize that specified x; a short sampler describes the ensemble, not all individual deterministic target records for free.

The physical hierarchy is the original definition instantiated with this fixed PBTC source semantics: all stages require the declared positive carriers, finite admitted geometry, owned port transitions and finite resource/clock records; later stages may repeat these same exhausted constraints. Membership never mentions $C_{P}$. The displayed constructor directly obeys every source constraint, so it is a common full-constraint witness. This is a populated domain hierarchy, not an assertion that an unrelated unpopulated global PU hierarchy has been identified with it. If a consumer requires a particular global hierarchy hash instead, the additional baseline-identity/coverage map must be stated and checked; none is inferred from the capacity theorem.

##### 7.2 Prefix theorem and quantitative throughput bridge

Let $C_K(x)=C_P(\mu_{K,x})$ in that fixed source hierarchy, in bits. The common constructor gives $C_K(x)\le N+h_K$, $h_K=c_U+h_{\mathrm{size}}(K)$, for every $x$. Choose one shortest admissible program per distinct response $x$. These programs form a prefix-free set, so Kraft gives

$$
\sum_x 2^{-C_K(x)}\le 1.
$$

For uniform X, Jensen's inequality yields

$$
N \le \bar{C}_K := 2^{-N} \sum_x C_K(x) \le N+h_K.
$$

For every $s\ge 0$, the number of records with $C_K(x)<N-s$ is at most $2^{N-s}$, hence

$$
\Pr[C_K(X)<N-s] \le 2^{-s}.
$$

These are exact prefix bounds; no assertion that every particular cue vector is incompressible is made. In particular the all-zero record may have a much shorter program. The random ensemble itself has a description consisting of a size parameter and a sampling rule, generally $O(\log K)$; that is a different target object from $\mu_{K,x}$.

Combining the independently derived metabolic port law $B_K=b_T N$ with the independently derived program bounds gives the typed average bridge

$$
b_T (\bar{C}_K-h_K) \le B_K \le b_T \bar{C}_K,
$$

and, with probability at least $1-2^{-s}$, the individual-record bracket

$$
b_T [C_K(X)-h_K] \le B_K \le b_T [C_K(X)+s].
$$

A negative lower endpoint is replaced by zero. These relations retain actual compiler/size overhead; they do not equate program bits with joules. The conversion $b_{T}$ has units power per terminal and emerges from the chemical and wave ports. Multiplication by the one-bit-per-terminal task count is justified by the cue constructor and prefix theorem, not by naming throughput 'complexity'. If nats are desired, multiply complexity and overhead by ln2 and divide $b_{T}$ by ln2.

The theoretical $C_{P}$ observable is not claimed computable from a laboratory readout. Its actual readout protocol observes N, cue/route records and the physical fuel ports, and reports the proved uniform upper and distributional lower certificates. The finite record can also be checked for any displayed short program, but exhaustive minimality of arbitrary universal programs is not an experimental algorithm. The route capacity lower bound remains a separate operational certificate.

#### 8. Positive continuing losses and strict domain boundary

For viscosity $\mu_{v}>0$ or continuing material-maintenance coefficient $\lambda_{v}>0$, the complete objective includes the actual extra power

$$
R_\mu=\sum_{k=0}^K d_k \exp(-2 S_k),\quad d_k=8 \pi \mu_v 8^k l_k q_T^2/A_T^2,
$$

$\lambda_{v}$ V, for fixed actual terminal throughflow $q_{T}>0$. These are additional physical source ports, not terms that can be amortized away. This extension is exact for the displayed additive ledger, for example a separate owned mean-flow dissipative service and material-maintenance port alongside the declared wave channel. It is not a derivation of all viscous acoustic corrections to Navier–Stokes: putting viscosity into the same wave carrier can also alter propagation and must be rederived on that carrier. The source-selection theorem proves a unique minimizer and

$\lVert x^*\rVert\le(2/\alpha)\lVert\nabla J(0)\rVert$, $\alpha=N W_T/(\eta\zeta\tau)$ for the explicit dump implementation; $\alpha=d N W_T/(\eta\tau)$ for the ideal recovery lower envelope,

$$
\nabla J(0)_j=\sum_{k\le j}(\lambda_v v_k-2d_k).
$$

Exact matching requires $\lambda_v v_k=2d_k$ for every $k<K$. With $K\ge 2$ and $\mu_{v}>0$, the required ratios are proportional to $8^{k-K}$, so no common $\lambda_{v}$ can satisfy all levels. The adapter-supplied wave branch selects exact area preservation; the complete dissipative branch generally does not. The original accepted Poiseuille-only Murray law is preserved without modification.

#### 9. Retained observables and comparison quotient

The registered protocols are: indexed cue preparation/readout; route commitment before substrate arrival; service work and waste-label readout; maintenance and pump fuel-port calorimetry; first-arrival and late-load wave energies; pressure/flow probes on every segment; component mass inventory; and finite network lengths, areas and cell counts. Off-matching junction pulses identify each reflection coefficient; $\Gamma$ maps injectively to x by $x=2$ artanh $\Gamma$. Thus mismatched geometry is response-active, not quotient-null. Control hardware and late loads cannot be removed from the resource inventory merely because their matched-run net energy is zero: off-matching and gate-stock probes retain them.

Allowed relabelings are tree automorphisms applied simultaneously to cells, ports, cue inputs and output indices. The record-specific $C_{P}$ count uses the labeled task protocol, so it does not quotient $2^N$ records to only their Hamming weight. If labels are removed from the retained task, the prefix counting theorem must be recomputed for that coarser quotient and cannot be reused unchanged. No rescaling of mass, power or program cost is allowed to compensate an observed mismatch.

The finite source and probe definitions above populate an organism-model realization and a quantitative theoretical bridge. They do not claim an observed biological fit, an evolutionary mechanism, an infinite thin-tube body, or a statewise exact equality $C_P=N$. The finite-window domain, the specified hierarchy and the ideal constitutive carrier are premises of this realization.

### Carrier analysis

#### 1. Independently specified linear wave carrier

Fix a finite symmetric $n$-ary rooted tree with levels $0,\dots,K$, integer $n\ge 2$, $N_k=n^k$ and $N=n^K$ terminal receivers. Fix positive fluid density $\rho$, compressibility $\chi$, wave speed $c_w=(\rho\chi)^{-1/2}$, terminal area $A_{T}$ and lengths $l_k=l_T n^{(K-k)/D}$. Areas $A_{k}>0$ for $k<K$ are physical variables, not prescribed by the allometric exponent. On a straight uniform segment, the declared linear compressible-fluid carrier is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\rho\, \partial_t u &= -\partial_z p, \\
\chi\, \partial_t p &= -\partial_z u, \\
Q&=A_k u.
\end{aligned}
$$

Its positive energy and energy flux are

$$
\begin{aligned}
E_{\mathrm{segment}} &= (A_k/2) \int (\rho u^2+\chi p^2)\, dz, \\
\text{flux} &= p Q, \\
\partial_t\, \text{energy density} + \partial_z(p Q) &= 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

A right-going wave has $Q=Y_k p$, with $Y_k=A_k/Z_0$ and $Z_0=\rho c_w$. A left-going wave has $Q=-Y_k p$. This derives the level-independent characteristic admittance from the source equations; it is not inserted as a geometric optimization premise.

At a zero-storage junction, pressure is continuous and total flow is conserved. An incoming parent pulse $p_{\mathrm{in}}$, reflected pulse $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and identical child transmitted pulses $p_{\mathrm{tr}}$ therefore satisfy

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_{\mathrm{in}}+p_{\mathrm{ref}}&=p_{\mathrm{tr}}, \\
Y_k(p_{\mathrm{in}}-p_{\mathrm{ref}})&=nY_{k+1}p_{\mathrm{tr}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Solving gives $\Gamma_k=(Y_k-nY_{k+1})/(Y_k+nY_{k+1})$. The incident, reflected and total transmitted energies over the same pulse are proportional to $Y_k\int p_{\mathrm{in}}^{2}$, $Y_k\int p_{\mathrm{ref}}^{2}$ and $nY_{k+1}\int p_{\mathrm{tr}}^{2}$. Hence the exact first-pass reflected fraction is $\Gamma_{k}^{2}$ and the transmitted fraction is $1-\Gamma_k^{2}$. This is an actual energy identity on the positive wave carrier.

The finite receiver protocol starts from a quiescent tree, permits source injection only at the root, and retains the first outgoing wavefront and its prescribed reception window. Use a compact pulse of width $\delta<2\min_k l_k/c_w$, so no echo can enter its direct-arrival window. Later echoes are separately routed to owned absorbing loads; their stored energy and final disposal are recorded, not counted as useful first-arrival delivery. Matched terminal loads absorb the final first-pass pulse. On a balanced tree all root-to-terminal propagation lengths agree, and every terminal receives the same first-pass energy. An operating protocol and clearing time must be supplied before interpreting a repeated-cycle metabolic rate; the calculation below is the exact per-shot source cost.

#### 2. Exact source-energy selector

Let each terminal require a fixed first-arrival wave energy $W_{T}>0$, specified independently by its receiver. Define logarithmic mismatch coordinates

$$
x_k=\ln[A_k/(n A_{k+1})],\quad k=0,\dots,K-1.
$$

They are bijective with the positive area choices for fixed $A_{T}$:

$$
A_k=A_T n^{K-k} \exp(S_k),\quad S_k=\sum_{j=k}^{K-1} x_j,\quad S_K=0.
$$

Since $\Gamma_k=\tanh(x_k/2)$, the required root energy is exactly

$$
W_{\mathrm{in}}(x)=N W_T \prod_{k=0}^{K-1} \cosh^2(x_k/2).
$$

The transmitted first-pass energy is exactly N $W_{T}$. The difference is owned reflected/late-arrival energy, with no uncharged negative-energy source. Every factor is at least one; equality holds exactly when every $x_{k}=0$. Thus the unique global minimizer of the actual per-shot supplied energy is

$$
A_k=n A_{k+1},\quad \text{equivalently}\quad N_k A_k=N A_T.
$$

The source chooses area preservation because any mismatch requires strictly more incident energy to meet the same independently fixed receivers. Merely assigning a name to an impedance cost is unnecessary.

Put $F(x)=\prod\cosh^2(x_k/2)$. Its gradient is $F(x)\tanh(x_k/2)$, and its Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hess} F &= F\,[\operatorname{diag}(1/(2 \cosh^2(x_k/2))) + g g^{\mathsf T}], \\
g_k &= \tanh(x_k/2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Since $F/\cosh^2(x_k/2)\ge 1$, $\operatorname{Hess}F\ge I/2$ everywhere. The source objective is globally strongly convex. It is also coercive, so the displayed minimizer exists without a hidden compactness assumption.

#### 3. Complete positive-cost extension and exact matching obstruction

A complete biological operating objective need not equal the wave-energy term alone. Fix a declared cycle time $\tau>0$, terminal mean material flow $q_{T}>0$, positive viscosity $\mu_{v}$ if that ledger is present, and a material-maintenance price $\lambda_{v}\ge 0$. These parameters are independently owned physical inputs. Write $\alpha=N W_T/\tau$ and retain

$$
J(x)=\alpha F(x)+R_\mu(x)+\lambda_v V(x)+B_{\mathrm{base}},
$$

$$
V(x)=\sum_{k=0}^K v_k \exp(S_k),\quad v_k=N_k A_k^{*} l_k=N A_T l_k,
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
R_\mu(x)&=\sum_{k=0}^K d_k \exp(-2 S_k), \\
d_k&=8 \pi \mu_v N_k l_k q_T^2/A_T^2, \\
A_k^{*}&=A_T n^{K-k}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The expression for $R_{\mu}$ follows from the actual Poiseuille source power $8\pi\mu_v N_k l_k Q_k^2/A_k^2$ and the fixed terminal throughflow $Q_k=q_T n^{K-k}$. It is not a wave-reflection term and is not counted twice. A non-unit pump conversion efficiency can be absorbed into the separately fixed $d_{k}$. The maintenance term is an actual continuing cost only if the source record provides it; a one-time construction energy is instead a setup resource and does not silently become this rate.

This theorem is for the displayed additive source ledger. It is not a full viscous-acoustic propagation derivation; viscosity in the same wave carrier may also change its propagation losses. A separately owned mean-flow dissipative port and maintenance port realize the additive terms without that conflation.

Every additional exponential term is convex and nonnegative. Therefore J is coercive and globally alpha/2-strongly convex, and has a unique global minimizer x*. Its displacement from exact matching is bounded by

$$
\lVert x^*\rVert_2\le(2/\alpha)\lVert\nabla J(0)\rVert_2,
$$

$$
\nabla J(0)_j = \sum_{k=0}^{j} (\lambda_v v_k-2d_k).
$$

Proof: strong monotonicity of $\nabla J$, $\nabla J(x^*)=0$, and Cauchy-Schwarz give $(\alpha/2)\lVert x^*\rVert^2\le\lVert\nabla J(0)\rVert\,\lVert x^*\rVert$. This bound is a source-derived perturbation certificate, not a choice of geometry made to recover an exponent.

Exact area preservation is selected by this complete objective iff every displayed partial sum is zero. Equivalently,

$$
\lambda_v v_k=2d_k\quad\text{for every }k<K.
$$

For $\mu_{v}>0$, the required ratios are

$$
2d_k/v_k = 16 \pi \mu_v q_T^2 n^{k-K}/A_T^3.
$$

They differ with $k$. Consequently no single level-independent $\lambda_{v}$ makes exact matching optimal when $K\ge 2$, $n>1$ and $\mu_{v}>0$. With $\lambda_{v}=0$ and $\mu_{v}>0$ it is not optimal for any $K\ge 1$. With $\mu_{v}=0$ and $\lambda_{v}>0$ it is likewise not optimal. The wave-only branch $\mu_v=\lambda_v=0$ has the exact area-preserving optimum. $K=1$ permits one specially tuned balance, which must be retained as an independent source equality rather than silently assumed.

This does not contradict or replace the accepted Murray law. If the acoustic source term is removed, the original positive Poiseuille-plus-volume ledger has its independently proved cube-law minimizer. This theorem shows how a real acoustic receiver term changes that full optimization, and why adding a small omitted cost is not the same as proving exact matching.

#### 4. Quantitative transport and finite-window mass corrections

For any source-selected $x$ with $\lVert x\rVert_2\le\delta$, Cauchy-Schwarz gives $|S_k|\le\sqrt{K-k}\,\delta\le\sqrt{K}\,\delta$. Thus

$$
\exp(-\sqrt{K}\delta) V(0)\le V(x)\le \exp(\sqrt{K}\delta) V(0).
$$

The actual vessel radii have the corresponding half-log error. A retained construction ledger must additionally count walls, junctions, terminal tissues, receiver actuators, fluid inventory and pump/control resources. If the independently derived component sum has

$$
M_K=\rho_{\mathrm{eff}} V_K(0) \exp(e_K),\quad B_K=b_T N_K \exp(f_K),
$$

with certified bounds $|e_K|\le E_K$, $|f_K|\le F_K$, then every two-size logarithmic slope can be computed with those full joint bounds, rather than identifying $M$ with a vessel volume by definition. In particular, for $K_1<K_2$ let $\Lambda=(K_2-K_1)\ln n$ and let the accepted ideal mass logarithm be $D_0=\Lambda/s_D+\epsilon$ with $s_D=D/(D+1)$. The actual slope is

$$
b_{\mathrm{actual}}=(\Lambda+f_{K_2}-f_{K_1})/(D_0+e_{K_2}-e_{K_1}).
$$

A positive lower bound on the denominator is required before division. Its source-derived interval follows by monotonicity or exact interval arithmetic over the joint remainder set. Covariances are retained if the same physical parameters enter both e and f; independent marginal bands cannot silently replace that shared graph.

#### 5. Noncircular complexity/service primitive

A terminal throughput bridge must begin from a predictive task rather than define complexity from power. One explicit formal task has, at each of N terminal cells and each registered cycle, an independent fair binary substrate label $X_{i}$. The receiver must select the matching catalytic route before its deadline, with zero classification error. Any retained task state R from which all routes can be recovered satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
H(X_1,\dots,X_N \mid R)&=0, \\
I(X_1,\dots,X_N;R)&=N \ln 2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The lower bound is attained by the route register $R=(X_1,\dots,X_N)$. Thus the required predictive information is independently $C_{\mathrm{req}}=N\ln 2$ per batch. This is a source/task theorem, not a relabeling of $N$ times an energy rate.

A physical throughput map additionally needs the actual reaction and receiver implementation. A candidate reversible species-label transfer can keep the terminal catalyst cyclic while carrying $X_{i}$ into an outgoing waste label; then no unowned reset or Landauer equality is inferred. Independently specified fuel free energy, material flux, pulse actuation, control work and waste entropy must be added to derive the total metabolic B. The task theorem alone does not prove that a named organism performs this task, that every terminal consumes the same net fuel, or that supplied wave power equals metabolic rate.

#### 6. Finite geometric admission is a real gate

On the exact area-preserving branch in $D=3$,

$$
r_k/l_k=(r_T/l_T) n^{(K-k)/6}.
$$

Any declared uniform slender-vessel bound $r_k/l_k\le\epsilon$ therefore restricts the family to

$$
K\le 6 \log_n(\epsilon\, l_T/r_T).
$$

No fixed positive terminal radius/length can satisfy that bound for unbounded $K$. Junction volumes and tube packing also need ownership. A physically admitted finite size window can be constructed and checked, but the formal $K\to\infty$ exponent does not by itself prove an unbounded slender biological realization. This geometric condition is reported as an actual domain bound rather than being omitted from source accounting.

#### 8. Recovery-complete classification and a strictly dissipative source entry

The lossless launched-energy minimizer in section 2 is not, by itself, a net-consumed-work minimizer. Let $D=N W_T$ and $W=D F(x)$. If every excess $W-D$ is perfectly recovered and reused, the net work per service can be $D$ for every $x$. Thus a lossless recoverable source does not strictly select matching on a net-work objective. A mandatory absorbing boundary supplies the earlier per-shot objective, but a recovery competitor cannot be excluded without recording that boundary in the source class.

Here is a source whose strictness survives arbitrary allowed recovery. Fix one common root-entry adapter of length $a>0$ and damping $\gamma>0$, with the same area as the adjoining root segment. Its declared positive-energy equations are

$$
\rho (u_t+\gamma u)=-p_z,\quad \chi(p_t+\gamma p)=-u_z.
$$

The positive energy balance is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\partial_t [A(\rho u^2+\chi p^2)/2]+\partial_z(Apu) \\
&=-\gamma A(\rho u^2+\chi p^2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Both characteristics decay by $\exp(-\gamma a/c_w)$; their energy transmission is $\zeta=\exp(-2\gamma a/c_w)\in(0,1)$. The characteristic admittance remains $A/Z_0$, and the adapter is reflectionless when joined to a segment with that area. All forward source injections enter through this owned adapter; the comparison class has a single work-entry port and no distributed positive-energy injection sites. Any return energy may be recovered, stored and reused at the source side, with efficiency up to one; no recovery hardware is forbidden merely because it recovers resources. The adapter's damping heat is exported to the fixed-temperature waste bath and is not a free work source.

For one cyclic service, write $W$ for energy launched into the tree after the adapter, $D$ for terminal useful delivery, $R$ for energy recovered from the tree, and $Q\ge 0$ for all other tree/receiver waste. Conservation gives $W=D+R+Q$ when internal stocks return to their initial values. The adapter requires $W/\zeta$ input and dissipates $d W$, $d=\zeta^{-1}-1>0$. Consequently the external net work supplied satisfies

$$
W_{\mathrm{net}} \ge W/\zeta-R = D+Q+dW \ge D+d D F(x).
$$

The first-arrival constraint $W\ge D F(x)$ gives the last inequality even if extra pulses are allowed after the deadline. Root-side storage across cycles changes the finite-horizon identity only by its explicitly retained endpoint energy. A cyclic stock has zero endpoint difference; bounded stocks vanish after division by the number of cycles. A growing stock cannot be hidden in that limit. A store or actuator injecting energy downstream of the adapter changes the single-entry source topology and must be declared as a different carrier with its own source map; it is not a free recovery of the registered root input.

At $x=0$ a single direct pulse delivers $D$, has no reflections, and attains $W_{\mathrm{net}}=D/\zeta=D+dD$. Thus the lower bound is attained at matching, and every $x\ne 0$ has strictly greater net work even if all reflected energy is perfectly recovered. Extra nonnegative recovery/control costs cannot reverse this comparison. This proves global selection on the fixed single-entry source class without assuming that return energy is wasted.

If the chemical-to-work efficiency for net external replenishment is $\eta>0$, the minimal fuel input has lower bound $[D+dD F(x)]/\eta$, attained at matching. The independently specified positive damping, not an exponent fit or an exclusion of recovery, supplies strictness. If $\gamma=0$, then $d=0$ and this strict selector disappears, exactly as the lossless counterexample predicts. The adapter volume $aA_{0}$, wall mass and heat are additional owned source terms. At matching $aA_0=aNA_{T}$, so they are terminal-linear corrections, with no change of the accepted main network-volume calculation.

∎

<a id="corollary-p89a128-tier-4-biological-fractal-scaling"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.12.8 (Tier-4 Biological Fractal Scaling).** Let a biological morphology or transport subnetwork follow a branching rule with $n$ copies per scale step and length ratio $r\in(0,1)$. On a registered finite scale range, assume the box counts obey
$$
c_-n^m\le N(r^m)\le c_+n^m
$$
for constants $0<c_-\le c_+<\infty$. The branching exponent is
$$
D_f=\frac{\log n}{\log(1/r)}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.14}
$$
The finite-scale ratio $\log N(r^m)/\log(r^{-m})$ differs from $D_f$ by at most
$$
\frac{\max\{|\log c_-|,|\log c_+|\}}{m\log(1/r)}.
$$
An exact infinite-range Euclidean self-similar realization satisfying the corresponding non-overlap box-count estimates has box dimension $D_f$; an embedding in three-dimensional space requires $D_f\le3$. The biological conclusion depends on this appended branching and counting package.

*Proof.* Taking logarithms of the two count bounds and dividing by $m\log(1/r)>0$ gives the finite-scale error bound. If the same estimates hold for arbitrarily large $m$, their errors tend to zero and yield the box-dimension formula. A finite observed scale range supplies only the bounded-ratio statement. Ambient dimension bounds the exact infinite-range Euclidean box dimension. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a128a-finite-trisection-branching-predictive-colony-and-its-count-response-certificate"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.8a (Finite Trisection-Branching Predictive Colony and Its Count–Response Certificate).** A finite trisection-branching predictive colony (TBPC), defined below, realizes Corollary P.8.9a.12.8 on its complete terminal-cell morphology. Its branching number is two, its geometric ratio is one third, and its retained minimal-cover count is exactly $2^m$ throughout the registered scale window. Its biological service instrument gives a positive, spatially resolved response measure on the same cells. The ideal centroid carrier belongs to the strongly separated class of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10a; the positive-size cells have the same finite-window count with the explicit stability margin below.

*Source domain and construction.* Fix a finite $J_{\max}\ge2$ and integers $1\le J\le J_{\max}$. Choose one finite admissible cell module, a radius $a>0$ enclosing that module, and a terminal spacing parameter $L_T>2a$. Fix the common cell, material, port and clock parameters before generating cues or computing an exponent. The geometric architecture divides each occupied horizontal compartment into three equal compartments, leaves the middle one as a service separation, and branches to the first and third. This local architectural rule fixes the scale ratio; it is a premise of the named morphology, independent of its counting exponent. The biological unit is the membrane-enclosed predictive service cell of the colony realization, sections 2–3, in Theorem P.8.9a.12.7b. The construction below copies that cell's finite cue/route/verifier, maintenance, service and work-receiver mechanism. It has its own binary geometry and supply record; it does not import that theorem's eight-branch geometry or transport/allometry optimizer.

For $b\in\{0,1\}$, let
$$
f_b(x)=\frac{x+2b}{3},\qquad
q_w=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\frac{2w_i}{3^i},\qquad
I_w=[q_w,q_w+3^{-k}],\qquad |w|=k,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.1}
$$
with $q_{\varnothing}=0$. Put $L_J=L_T3^J$. The terminal cell labeled by $w\in\{0,1\}^J$ has center
$$
t_w=L_J(q_w,0,0).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.2}
$$
Its complete cell module is a nonempty compact body $S_w$ inside the closed ball of radius $a$ about $t_w$; its membrane cell, route stocks, finite local controls and receiver have positive finite mass and are included in this body. The source may choose identical solid enclosing capsules for all modules. The retained morphological support is
$$
S_J=\bigcup_{|w|=J}S_w,
\qquad
\nu_J=\sum_{|w|=J}\delta_{t_w},
\qquad
\mu_J=2^{-J}\nu_J.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.3}
$$
Thus $\nu_J$ is the counting measure of actual membrane-cell occurrences. The terminal-cell selection is fixed by the membrane/service-port identity before counting, includes every leaf of the binary tree, and retains the complete connecting structure in the source inventory. The connected tubes and the full positive-volume organism are separate geometric observables.

The entire connecting tree is explicit. For every $|w|=k<J$, place a junction at
$$
p_w=L_J(q_w+\tfrac12 3^{-k},3^{-k},0).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.4}
$$
For $k<J-1$, join $p_w$ to $p_{w0}$ and $p_{w1}$ by straight segments; for $k=J-1$, join it to $t_{w0}$ and $t_{w1}$. There are exactly $2^J-1$ junctions, $2^{J+1}-2$ segments and $2^J$ terminal cells. Every address has one root-to-cell path, and all segments belong to such a path. Internal segment lengths at depth $k<J-1$ are $\sqrt5L_J3^{-k-1}$; the two final lengths from each last junction are $3\sqrt5L_T/2$ and $\sqrt{37}L_T/2$. In particular the finite end closure is retained rather than treated as an exactly scaled copy of an internal edge. The total centerline length is
$$
\mathcal L_J=
2\sqrt5L_J\bigl[1-(2/3)^{J-1}\bigr]
+2^{J-2}L_T(3\sqrt5+\sqrt{37}).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.5}
$$
The first term is zero when $J=1$.

At a fixed depth, distinct prefixes have disjoint horizontal intervals separated by a positive gap. Edges from that depth stay in their own prefix interval and in the vertical band between that depth and the next. The two edges within a prefix meet only at their common parent. The final edges have the same properties in the last band. Hence nonincident segments are disjoint. Choose disjoint small junction neighborhoods, remove their interiors and the terminal-module interiors from the incident segments, and let $d_*>0$ be the minimum distance between distinct remaining compact segment pieces, over the finite family $J\le J_{\max}$. Take the tube outer radius smaller than $d_*/4$ and smaller than the finitely many local junction/port clearances. Incident tubes merge only inside their owned junctions or cell ports. These strict inequalities give a positive-radius physical-model realization; all coordinates and segment-distance tests are finite algebraic records. For an enlarged family the clearances and material inventory must be recomputed.

The root supplies each indexed cue and each receiver-work packet through this tree. A finite sequential address schedule visits every word $w$, routes its carriers along its unique path, deposits its cue at the cell, and returns the reusable routing registers and empty carriers. A junction implements the branch selected by the next address bit; it has two physically distinct outgoing ports, both retained in the schedule. To obtain a finite local implementation, subdivide each segment of length $\ell_e$ into $q_e=\lceil\ell_e/d_0\rceil$ links of length at most a fixed $d_0>0$. Use finite adjacent-carrier swap and controlled-swap gates on these links, with gate time $t_g\ge d_0/c_*$ for a declared carrier-speed bound $c_*>0$. The complete finite gate list is the concatenation, in lexicographic leaf order, of the forward route, terminal deposition and reverse route for each leaf; its length is a retained integer $G_J$. Empty-link, address and controller registers are owned stocks, not inputs carrying an uncharged cue. A common cycle time $\tau$ exceeds $\max_{J\le J_{\max}}G_Jt_g$ plus the fixed cue-commitment, substrate-arrival and biochemical schedule.

Every routing gate is an energy-preserving permutation of a finite classical orthogonal-state carrier. A transposition $U$ commuting with its nonnegative bare Hamiltonian $H_b$ has the positive gate realization
$$
H_{\mathrm{gate}}=H_b+\frac{\pi\hbar}{2t_g}(I-U),
\qquad
 e^{-iH_{\mathrm{gate}}t_g/\hbar}
 =e^{-iH_bt_g/\hbar}U.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.6}
$$
Finite permutations decompose into these transpositions. The controller and temporary gate-energy stocks are included, and the conserved gate term gives equal switch-on and recovered switch-off work. Any independently stipulated irreversible routing/control cost $e_r\ge0$ per listed gate is paid separately. Work carriers have states of energy zero and $W_T>0$ and are transferred by equal-energy swaps. The root produces one such packet per cell at fixed efficiency $\eta\in(0,1]$, retains the corresponding waste heat, and the cell's named receiver consumes $W_T$ in its actuator cycle. No shared acoustic-tree matching law is needed for this supply mechanism.

The source inventory comprises every cell and its local stocks; all segments, junction housings, carrier sites and routing/controller registers; root fuel/work conversion and waste loads; cue, service-substrate, maintenance-nutrient and labeled-waste ports; the clock, geometric and energy-readout instruments; positive temporary gate-energy stores; and finite fabrication/assembly resources. If tube material has mass per centerline length $\lambda_t>0$, the complete retained body mass is the actual sum
$$
M_J=2^Jm_{\mathrm{cell}}+\lambda_t\mathcal L_{\mathrm{straight},J}
+\sum_{|u|<J}m_{\mathrm{junction},u}
+\sum_e m_{\mathrm{carrier},e}+M_{\mathrm{root/control},J},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.7}
$$
where $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{straight},J}$ is the sum of segment lengths trimmed outside the already counted cell/junction housings. Junction/overlap volumes are assigned once; (P.8.9a.12.8a.5) is the separately retained untrimmed centerline length. Instruments external to the body and construction resources have their own initial/final stocks and are not added a second time to $M_J$. Finite fabrication energy $E_{\mathrm{build},J}$ is retained as a one-time charge. All masses and energies are finite on the declared family.

*Biological response instrument.* At each cycle the cell $w$ receives a fair cue bit $X_w$, commits $R_w=X_w$, and subsequently receives a service substrate labeled
$$
Y_w=X_w\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}Z_w,
\qquad Z_w\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\epsilon),
\qquad 0<\epsilon<\tfrac12.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.8}
$$
Cues and noises are independent over cells and cycles; they enter through the owned ports. The substrate is absent at commitment and the held cue cannot revise the committed route. A matched route converts the fixed substrate energy $\Delta_s>0$ into an output work packet, while an unmatched route converts it into owned heat/waste. Each cycle also consumes maintenance energy $\Delta_m>0$, pays for the receiver work, and restores membrane/route/verifier organization. The XOR verifier and the final cue/route uncomputation are exactly the finite cyclic operations in Theorem P.8.9a.12.7b: the outgoing labels are $(X_w,Y_w,X_w\mathbin{\mathrm{xor}}Y_w)$, whose entropy equals the incoming $\ln2+h(\epsilon)$. The port semantics thus retain the future-dependent task, waste labels and reset resources of the cell of Theorem P.8.9a.12.7b.

The actual per-cycle input and service-output records are
$$
E_{\mathrm{in},J}
=2^J(\Delta_m+\Delta_s+W_T/\eta)+e_rG_J,
\qquad
W_w=\Delta_s\mathbf1_{\{R_w=Y_w\}}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.9}
$$
Pump heat is $2^J(\eta^{-1}-1)W_T$, receiver consumption is $2^JW_T$, and maintenance, routing and unmatched service energy have their named sinks. Together with the matched output work these exhaust the input. A finite run of $H$ cycles additionally charges $E_{\mathrm{build},J}$ once; no amortization is needed for the geometric claim. The positive gate stocks remain in the resource record even when their recovered net switching work is zero.

For any set $A$ of terminal locations, the retained spatial service instrument records
$$
\mathcal W_J(A)=\sum_{t_w\in A}W_w,
\quad
\mathbb E\mathcal W_J(A)=\Delta_s(1-\epsilon)\nu_J(A),
\quad
\operatorname{Var}\mathcal W_J(A)
=\Delta_s^2\epsilon(1-\epsilon)\nu_J(A).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.10}
$$
The first equality is a sum of separately calibrated output-energy ports. The second and third follow from the independently specified substrate law. A cue-blind route has success probability at most $1/2$, so the optimal cue-aware instrument has positive expected excess useful work
$$
\Delta_s(\tfrac12-\epsilon)\nu_J(A)
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.11}
$$
per cycle. Conditional on either cue value, its matching route is the unique maximizer. Every cell is therefore response-active. The energy-to-count calibration $\mathbb E\mathcal W_J/[\Delta_s(1-\epsilon)]$ recovers $\nu_J$ on the full terminal-address algebra; it is a derived response map with energy units and a fixed physical calibration.

For a prefix $u$ of length $m\le J$, let $C_u$ denote the terminal modules with labels extending $u$. It has exactly $n_u=2^{J-m}$ cells. Its normalized expected service response is $\mu_J(C_u)=2^{-m}$. Over $H\ge1$ cycles, $\sum_{h=1}^H\mathcal W_{J,h}(C_u)/\Delta_s$ has the exact binomial law $\operatorname{Binomial}(Hn_u,1-\epsilon)$. In particular the empirical mean-power readout $\widehat P_u=(H\tau)^{-1}\sum_h\mathcal W_{J,h}(C_u)$ obeys, simultaneously for all $2^{J+1}-1$ prefixes, with probability at least $1-\alpha$,
$$
\left|\widehat P_u-\frac{\Delta_s(1-\epsilon)n_u}{\tau}\right|
\le\frac{\Delta_s}{\tau}
\sqrt{\frac{n_u}{2H}\ln\frac{2(2^{J+1}-1)}{\alpha}},
\qquad 0<\alpha<1.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.12}
$$
For the concentration bound, the logarithmic moment-generating function of a centered Bernoulli variable has value and derivative zero at the origin and second derivative at most $1/4$. It is therefore at most $t^2/8$. Multiplication over the $Hn_u$ independent trials and optimization of the exponential Markov bound give two-sided tail probability $2\exp[-2Hx^2/n_u]$ for a deviation $x$ of the cycle-averaged success count. Substitution of the displayed threshold and a union bound over all prefixes prove (P.8.9a.12.8a.12). Location/occupancy records remain separate from work records: a finite sequence of unsuccessful services is not treated as proof that a cell is absent.

*Counting theorem and proof.* Register the diameter-cover rule $N(s;S)$ of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10a and scales
$$
s_m=L_J3^{-m},\qquad 0\le m\le J,
\qquad \sigma=L_T-2a>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.13}
$$
For a prefix $u$ of length $m$, its leftmost terminal center is $L_Jq_u$ and its rightmost is $L_J[q_u+3^{-m}(1-3^{-(J-m)})]$. The diameter of its cell-module union is therefore at most
$$
s_m-L_T+2a=s_m-\sigma.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.14}
$$
Distinct depth-$m$ terminal-center groups have separation at least $s_m+L_T$: the smallest gap occurs between the two children of a common depth-$(m-1)$ prefix, and earlier separation is larger. Their cell-module unions consequently have separation at least $s_m+\sigma$. For $m\ge1$, every set of diameter less than $s_m+\sigma$ meets at most one of the $2^m$ nonempty groups; each group is itself a permissible covering set of diameter at most $s_m-\sigma$. Hence
$$
N(s;S_J)=2^m
\quad\text{for}\quad
s_m-\sigma\le s<s_m+\sigma,
\qquad 1\le m\le J,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.15}
$$
and $N(s_0;S_J)=1$. The same proof for the centroid set uses $a=0$. In particular
$$
N(s_m;S_J)=N(s_m;\operatorname{supp}\nu_J)=2^m,
\quad
\frac{\ln N(s_m;S_J)}{\ln(L_J/s_m)}
=\frac{\ln2}{\ln3}\quad(1\le m\le J).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.16}
$$
There is zero counting-exponent error at the registered scales. If each cell support is perturbed or localized with Hausdorff error at most $h\ge0$ and the scale threshold has absolute error at most $b\ge0$, the same counts remain certified whenever
$$
2h+b<\sigma.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.17}
$$
Indeed the within-group diameter increases by at most $2h$, the between-group gap decreases by at most $2h$, and the threshold stays strictly between them. If instead the reported logarithmic count has error at most $e_m$ and the reported denominator $\ln(L_J/s_m)$ has error at most $d_m<m\ln3$, then the reported exponent differs from $D_f=\ln2/\ln3$ by at most
$$
\frac{e_m+D_fd_m}{m\ln3-d_m}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.18}
$$
This follows by subtracting $D_f$ from $(m\ln2+\xi)/(m\ln3+\zeta)$ and using $|\xi|\le e_m$, $|\zeta|\le d_m$. The finite-window certificate therefore supplies both geometric and readout-error budgets.

Embed the maps (P.8.9a.12.8a.1) on the $x$ axis in $\mathbb R^3$ by $F_b(x,y,z)=(x+2b,y,z)/3$. Their attractor is the middle-third set on that axis, with first-level separation $1/3$. Since $0$ belongs to it,
$$
L_J^{-1}\operatorname{supp}\nu_J
=\{F_w(0,0,0):|w|=J\}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.8a.19}
$$
is exactly the finite terminal set in Theorem P.8.9a.12.10a. The infinite ideal centroid carrier has dimension $\ln2/\ln3<3$; the admitted physical source has finite $J_{\max}$. At resolutions below the terminal spacing the finite centroid count saturates, while positive-volume cell bodies have their ordinary small-scale dimension three. The connected tubular support has its own cover function. These are distinct declared observables, so none is substituted for the terminal-cell finite-window count.

The biological instrument reconstructs the same counting record in a response-faithful way. At every registered depth $m$, the terminal-address instrument yields exactly $2^m$ nonempty prefix response sectors; their module supports are separated by the just-proved gap, each is coverable by one set of diameter $s_m$, and no such set can combine two sectors. Equations (P.8.9a.12.8a.10)–(P.8.9a.12.8a.12) give each sector's actual work distribution and its positive expected response. Thus the geometry-to-cover and cell-to-work diagrams agree on the retained partition without equating a random single-cycle work value with an integer box count. Omitting a branch removes at least one leaf and one strictly positive expected response; changing a cell's address, location or service law changes a retained readout. Tree relabelings are allowed only when applied simultaneously to geometry, cue inputs, ports and output labels. Spatial rotations/translations and changes of units act covariantly; they cannot change the dimensionless scale ratio, hide a missing branch, or compensate an altered energy calibration. This proves the claimed morphology, realization and observable certificate. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a129-standalone-taylor-law-for-fixed-shape-pce-scale-families"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.9 (Standalone Taylor Law for Fixed-Shape PCE Scale Families).** Let $Y$ be a nonnegative random variable with
$$
0<\mu_Y:=\mathbb E[Y]<\infty,
\qquad
0<\sigma_Y^2:=\operatorname{Var}(Y)<\infty.
$$
Let a fixed-shape PCE scale family be given by
$$
X_a=aY,
\qquad
a>0.
$$
Then
$$
\mathbb E[X_a]=a\mu_Y,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(X_a)=a^2\sigma_Y^2,
$$
and consequently
$$
\operatorname{Var}(X_a)
=
\frac{\sigma_Y^2}{\mu_Y^2}\,\mathbb E[X_a]^2.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.15}
$$
Thus Taylor's variance-mean exponent is exactly $2$ on every fixed-shape scale family with finite nonzero mean and variance. Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a is the inverse-gamma PCE stationary-family specialization of this general scale-family theorem.

*Proof.* Linearity of expectation gives
$$
\mathbb E[X_a]=\mathbb E[aY]=a\mu_Y.
$$
Variance is homogeneous of degree two under deterministic scaling:
$$
\operatorname{Var}(X_a)=\operatorname{Var}(aY)=a^2\sigma_Y^2.
$$
Since $a=\mathbb E[X_a]/\mu_Y$, substitution gives
$$
\operatorname{Var}(X_a)
=
\left(\frac{\mathbb E[X_a]}{\mu_Y}\right)^2\sigma_Y^2
=
\frac{\sigma_Y^2}{\mu_Y^2}\,\mathbb E[X_a]^2.
$$
The exponent is therefore exactly $2$. Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a has common shape and common scaled floor, so its stationary laws differ only by the scale parameter $\beta_{\mathrm{st}}$ and are an instance of the present theorem. ∎

<a id="proposition-p89a129a-scaled-floor-stationary-family-response-offset-and-shape-drift-bound-for-the-taylor-law"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.12.9a (Scaled-Floor Stationary Family, Response Offset and Shape-Drift Bound for the Taylor Law).**

1. *Scaled-floor family.* Fix $k,\sigma,\kappa>0$, and for $m>0$ let $p_m$ be the stationary law of Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 with floor $\nu_{\min}=\kappa m$. Then $p_m$ is the law of $mY$ with $Y\sim p_1$. The family $\{p_m\}_{m>0}$ is therefore a fixed-shape scale family with common shape $\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}=1+2k/\sigma^2$ and common scaled floor $a_{\min}=2/(\sigma^2\kappa)$. Its variance is finite exactly when $2k>\sigma^2$, in which case
$$
\operatorname{Var}_{p_m}(\nu)=\frac{B_2}{B_1^2}\bigl(\mathbb E_{p_m}\nu\bigr)^2
\qquad(m>0)
$$
with the constants $B_1,B_2$ of Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a. When $2k\le\sigma^2$, every member has infinite variance.
2. *Response offset.* Let $X_a=aY$ ($a>0$) be a fixed-shape family as in Theorem P.8.9a.12.9, and let $R_a=u+wX_a$ with constants $u$ and $w\ne0$. Then
$$
\operatorname{Var}(R_a)=\frac{\sigma_Y^2}{\mu_Y^2}\bigl(\mathbb ER_a-u\bigr)^2,
\qquad
\frac{d\ln\operatorname{Var}(R_a)}{d\ln\mathbb ER_a}=\frac{2\,\mathbb ER_a}{\mathbb ER_a-u}
\quad(0<\mathbb ER_a\ne u).
$$
If $\mathbb ER_a>0$ and $\operatorname{Var}(R_a)=c\,(\mathbb ER_a)^b$ for all $a$ in an open interval, with constants $c>0$ and $b\in\mathbb R$, then $u=0$ and $b=2$.
3. *Shape drift.* For populations $j=1,\ldots,J$ with means $M_j>0$ and variances $V_j>0$, put $c_j:=V_j/M_j^2$ and $x_j:=\ln M_j$, not all equal. With equal-weight empirical moments $\operatorname{Cov}_J$ and $\operatorname{Var}_J$, the least-squares slope $\widehat b$ of $\ln V_j$ on $x_j$ satisfies
$$
\widehat b=2+\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_J(x,\ln c)}{\operatorname{Var}_J(x)},
\qquad
|\widehat b-2|\le\frac{\max_j\ln c_j-\min_j\ln c_j}{2\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_J(x)}}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9a.1}
$$
In particular $\widehat b=2$ on every finite family with a common coefficient.

*Proof.* For item 1, $p_m$ has density proportional to $\nu^{-\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}-1}e^{-2m/(\sigma^2\nu)}$ on $[\kappa m,\infty)$. The law of $mY$ has density proportional to $(\nu/m)^{-\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}-1}e^{-2m/(\sigma^2\nu)}$ on the same half-line, which is the same normalized density. The scaled floor is $\beta_{\mathrm{st}}/\nu_{\min}=(2m/\sigma^2)/(\kappa m)=2/(\sigma^2\kappa)$. Theorem P.8.9a.11.5 gives a finite second moment exactly when $\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}>2$, that is, $2k>\sigma^2$, and Corollary P.8.9a.11.5a then gives the displayed relation.

For item 2, $\mathbb ER_a=u+wa\mu_Y$ and $\operatorname{Var}(R_a)=w^2a^2\sigma_Y^2=(\sigma_Y^2/\mu_Y^2)(\mathbb ER_a-u)^2$, and the logarithmic derivative follows. As $a$ ranges over an open interval, $y=\mathbb ER_a$ ranges over an open subinterval of $(0,\infty)$, on which $(\sigma_Y^2/\mu_Y^2)(y-u)^2=cy^b$. Both sides are real-analytic on $(0,\infty)$, so the identity holds on all of $(0,\infty)$. If $u>0$, evaluation at $y=u$ gives $0=cu^b>0$. If $u<0$, the left side tends to $(\sigma_Y^2/\mu_Y^2)u^2>0$ as $y\downarrow0$, while $cy^b$ tends to $0$ for $b>0$ and to $\infty$ for $b<0$; for $b=0$ the left side would be constant, although its derivative $2(\sigma_Y^2/\mu_Y^2)(y-u)$ is positive. Hence $u=0$, and $(\sigma_Y^2/\mu_Y^2)y^2=cy^b$ on $(0,\infty)$ forces $b=2$.

For item 3, $\ln V_j=2x_j+\ln c_j$, and the least-squares slope is $\operatorname{Cov}_J(x,\ln V)/\operatorname{Var}_J(x)$, which gives the identity. The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality bounds the covariance by the product of the two standard deviations, and a variable with values in an interval of length $\ell$ has variance at most $\ell^2/4$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a129b-taylor-law-population-from-a-minimum-service-reserve-controller"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.9b (Taylor-Law Population from a Minimum-Service Reserve Controller).** The renewed-R14 source of Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b has the following population realization. An independently registered interruption-service contract selects a reserve proportional to its nominal demand. One common clock, source innovation, controller, cost ledger and calibrated excess instrument realize, on a nonempty open interval of demand inputs, the stationary family of Proposition P.8.9a.12.9a with
$$
k=\tau^{-1},\qquad \sigma=\tau^{-1/2},\qquad
\kappa=\frac{2\tau}{3},\qquad \nu_{\min}=\kappa m.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.1}
$$
The limiting excess readout has a common finite, positive squared coefficient of variation and hence Taylor exponent two. The finite-source sequence, its integer service contract, its actual baseline subtraction and its moment convergence are specified below.

*Proof.*

**1. Source, population interval and reserve-selection task.** Use the R14 completion probability $p$, the inherited physical clock $\tau$, the proper-score task, and the source grammar of Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. In particular
$$
b=-\ln(1-p),\quad 0<b<1,\quad g=\frac{1+b}{2},\quad
P(v)=\beta-(\beta-\alpha)e^{-v}.
$$
Every component remains an actual qualified R14 unit. Independent copies supply independent completion flags and task sources for distinct aggregates. Write $\mu=m\tau$, and set
$$
a=g-b>0,\quad d=\frac a4,\quad
K=[3b,3b+d],\quad I=(3b+d/4,3b+3d/4).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.2}
$$
The registered population has $\mu\in I$. The larger compact interval $K$ supplies common implementation and error bounds. Neither interval is obtained from population means, variances, tails or fitted exponents.

The external service specification uses occupied capacity cells of the same kind and unit preparation price as the bank in Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. A delivered cell is transferred to the task receiver, which retains its receipt. The quoted procurement task is to sustain the specified demand for an interruption lasting at most $\kappa=2\tau/3$, starting at a registered service epoch. During interruption the supplier is unavailable and a priority guard disables discretionary adaptation transfers. The cell stock then serves the demand alone. The procurement comparison holds the receiver, service demand, deadlines, bank maximum, clock, controller and all fixed apparatus constant; its variable is the guaranteed ready stock. Every feasible choice supplies the same requested service. The procurement tariff charges a strictly positive price per acquired occupied cell and a nonnegative holding price per occupied cell. Extra ready stock has no extra credited service benefit on this comparison. Thus the least feasible stock is the unique procurement minimizer. This contract fixes the lower-stock policy before the predictive controller is run. Normal-operation PCE subsequently optimizes allocation subject to that policy.

Here $m$ is a normalized flow with units $T^{-1}$. It is distinct from the number of aggregates. At finite bank scale $B$, the physical demanded cell flow is $Bm$ cells per unit time. The delivered service is occupied-cell capacity. Physical preparation, protected transfers and receiver storage use the inherited source primitives and their paid energy/resource budgets; occupancy is not treated as extractable work. Those unit prices and physical primitive specifications remain fixed as $B$ changes.

**2. Exact finite service and calibrated readout.** For an integer $q$ tending to infinity take $h=1/(3q)$ and use the clock interval $h\tau$ of Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. Choose the integer bank scale $B=B_q=(3q)^6$, so $B^{-1}=h^6\le h^4$. This choice is fixed before the probability-table and billing precision searches below. Choose fixed rational $u_-,u_+$, by certified approximation of the source constants, with $3b<u_-<3b+d/4$ and $3b+3d/4<u_+<3b+d$. Their positive gaps make this finite search terminate. Use the exactly enumerable parameter grid
$$
K_q=[u_-,u_+]\cap\{D/(Bh):D\in\mathbb N\}.
$$
For each $\mu\in I$ choose a nearest $\mu_q\in K_q$; for all sufficiently large $q$ this is possible and $|\mu_q-\mu|\le 1/(Bh)$. The same $B,h$, maximum bank size, command-word width, source schedule, probe cap and instrument are used for every grid member. All these maxima are selected using $K$.

Put $D=B\mu_qh\in\mathbb N$ and $H=2q$. In normal mode the supplier delivers $2D$ cells and the receiver consumes $D$ cells at each service epoch. The net contribution to normalized stock is therefore $D/B=\mu_qh$. An interruption is accepted at a ready epoch $t_0$, after that epoch's completed service. In interruption mode both incoming supply and discretionary adaptation transfers stop. The due debits are at $t_0+jh\tau$ for $j=1,\ldots,H$; there is no additional debit at $t_0$. Thus the registered maximum interruption contains exactly $H$ demanded debits, and the reserve problem is
$$
R\ge HD=B\frac{2\mu_q}{3}.
$$
Necessity follows by starting an interruption with stock $R$ and requesting all $H$ debits. Sufficiency follows because after $j\le H$ debits the stock is $R-jD\ge0$. The procurement rule in item 1 therefore selects exactly
$$
R_q(\mu_q)=HD,\qquad \ell(\mu_q):=R_q/B=2\mu_q/3=\kappa m_q.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.3}
$$
This is an integer service calculation, preceding every stationary calculation. A shorter interruption demands fewer debits. The onset signal, mode, debits, remaining stock, restoration supply and every service outcome are retained. Normal experiments run the uninterrupted registered mode; interruption experiments test the separate admission guarantee. These two mode records are not pooled or selected by their outcomes. During an interruption the capacity-dependent normal probe is suspended, pending probes retain their starting-state labels, and the two base R14 units retain their original forecast/verification task with its source-known positive margin. Its mode-labelled response is separately scored. The normal probe resumes only after paid refill restores $N\ge R_q$; its formula is never applied to a depleted interruption stock.

The stock is a bank of $N$ occupied cells with $N\ge R_q$ in normal ready states. A one-target gate changes at most one initially zero cell to occupied, so preparing $N$ occupied bank cells requires at least $N$ such operations, and $N$ NOT operations attain that count. Transfer from a ready supplier moves the preparation charge to its source receipt; it does not remove it. The bank therefore supplies an exact integer preparation-capacity calibration, with no single-cell rounding noise.

The finite apparatus has a separately metered fixed representation/preparation charge. Register its bit-credit conversion, and pad that fixed charge, with actual paid preparation operations, to a common value $H_q$ for all grid members. The padding, baseline meter and subtraction circuit are included before the value is fixed. The $m$ input has the same fixed-width representation for all grid members. Fixed apparatus is built for the common maximum; unused hardware remains charged. Let
$$
c_q=8+H_q,\qquad C_q=c_q+N,\qquad C_{s,q}=B,
\qquad Y_q=\frac{C_q-c_q}{B}=\frac NB.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.4}
$$
The admitted control-shell observable assigns eigenvalue $c_q+N$ to the retained stock-count word. Its baseline receipt is measured on the same source, and its instrument actually performs the displayed subtraction and division. The inactive empty shell at $K_0=3$ is retained as in Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. Thus $c_q$ is the registered operational proxy baseline; the theoretical component threshold and aggregate $C_P$ retain their original definitions. The fixed preparation charge has been included, not deleted. Acquisition, service, processing, update, maintenance, adaptation and mode-switching charges that vary with $m$, state or time are entered in the running ledger of item 4, rather than called a common baseline.

The effective scale $C_{s,q}=B_q$ is common across the population at each resolution. Its growth is an increase in actual bank size, service rate and resources. The unit cell price is unchanged. Equation (P.8.9a.12.9b.4) defines the single registered normalized response throughout that source sequence.

**3. Complete normal-mode update and source lift.** In the first half of each $h\tau$ interval run the same renewed R14 source with rate $28/(h\tau)$ as in Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. Its actual flag $B_j$ has probability $p$, independently at successive epochs. The second half contains the charged command arithmetic and bank transfers. Define
$$
Z_j=\frac{B_j-p}{\sqrt{p(1-p)}},\qquad
A_h=1-h+\sqrt h Z_j.
$$
Use the same mesh restriction that gives $A_h\ge1/2$. The ideal normal instruction is
$$
X_{j+1}=\max\{2\mu/3,A_hX_j+\mu h\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.5}
$$
For the actual integer bank, rationally approximate the two possible values of $A_h$ with error at most $h^3$ and round the commanded free stock upward to an integer. The final stock is the maximum of that integer and $R_q$. In normalized units the one-step difference from (P.8.9a.12.9b.5), at the same $\mu_q$, is at most
$$
h^3 X_j+B^{-1}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.6}
$$
The flags are still Bernoulli($p$); approximation affects their command arithmetic, not their source law.

Here is a source-level transfer order. Starting from $N$, first admit $2D$ supplier cells and deliver $D$ cells to the receiver. Compute the integer free target $F$ from the retained original $N$ and the flag. If $F<R_q$, admit the clamp supply $R_q-F$ before making the discretionary transfer. Then transfer the signed difference $F-(N+D)$: a positive difference draws prepared cells from its supplier, while a negative difference transfers occupied cells to its retained receiver. The final balance is $\max(R_q,F)$. Every intermediate admitted normal ready balance is at least $R_q$. An interruption accepted at the ready epoch has priority before the next interval's source and normal commands; the instrument records that epoch and uses the debit convention of item 2. Mid-command arrivals wait for that explicitly registered admission epoch. Restoration fills the bank to its reserve before normal service resumes, and retains and charges that transfer.

All suppliers and receivers have deterministic finite capacities for a fixed run length, because the innovation has two bounded values and the affine recurrence gives a computable deterministic stock bound. If $V$ bounds all final ready stocks and $D_{\max},R_{\max}$ bound the grid demands and reserves, the intermediate bank balances are bounded by $\max\{V+2D_{\max},V+D_{\max}+R_{\max}\}$. This includes the gross incoming transfer and clamp-before-withdrawal stage; the positive free target follows from $A_h\ge1/2$ and the stated small arithmetic error. The bank is sized to this enlarged bound, and supplies, receiver memories and arithmetic words are sized to their corresponding finite cumulative-transfer bounds before execution. Each cell transfer is a protected finite permutation; occupied-cell preparation uses the inherited paid primitives. The controller arithmetic and its case selection are finite classical maps with the diagonal hardware lift proved in Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. The gate, source and readout intertwiner therefore applies to every finite normal or interruption word. Its common source and calibrated clock fix $k=1/\tau$ and $\sigma=1/\sqrt\tau$ for every population member.

At stock $Y_q$ use Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's two-base-copy Poisson probe with
$$
\lambda(Y_q)=\{t(Y_q)-2b\}/p,
\qquad t(v)=v+\ln[P(v)/\alpha].
$$
It is nonnegative because $Y_q\ge2\mu_q/3\ge2b$. The stock and baseline-difference snapshot is read and time-stamped at the common registered terminal normal epoch. The probe freezes that starting value and label; its score arrives after its actual $14\tau$ service delay, while subsequent controller operations carry their own timestamps. The retained success/forecast selector, proper mean logarithmic loss and conditional response law are those of Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. The population statistic uses the labelled starting excess, with the separately owned delayed predictive score, rather than treating a probe loss or a later stock value as that excess. Hence
$$
PP(C_q)=\beta-(\beta-\alpha)
 \exp[-(C_q-c_q)/B]
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.7}
$$
on the ideal capped-probe limit, with Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's explicit finite cap/table/failure bounds on finite members. The receiver service and the predictive probe are different owned task ports. Every aggregate contains at least two qualified components, communicates their retained records through the same selector and implements this predictive model and the adaptive stock controller. Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's finite constructor and presentation-relative $C_P\ge8$ admission argument still apply after the added finite hardware; Definition 29 is instantiated on this declared source class.

**4. Common PCE ledger and uniform cost margins.** Keep Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's commensurate power unit $P_0=E_0/\tau$ and set
$$
\Gamma_0=\frac{P_0g e^{2b}}{\beta-\alpha},\qquad
T_\mu(v)=\Gamma_0P(v)+\frac{P_0}{2}(v-\mu)^2+L_q.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.8}
$$
For $\mu=3b+e\in K$ and $v\ge2\mu/3$,
$$
\frac{T_\mu'(2\mu/3)}{P_0}
 =g e^{-2e/3}-b-e/3
 \ge(g-b)-e\ge3a/4,
\qquad T_\mu''(v)\ge P_0(1-g)>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.9}
$$
The first inequality uses $e^{-x}\ge1-x$ and $(2g+1)/3\le1$. Thus the same benefit price and positive slope/curvature margins apply to the whole population interval. Put $v_-=2b$, $C_f=c_q+Bv_-$ and
$$
r_q=\frac{3P_0a C_f}{16B},\qquad
R_{I,q}(C)=r_q\ln(C/3),\qquad
R_{\mu,q}(C)=T_\mu((C-c_q)/B)-R_{I,q}(C).
$$
On the realized domain the derivative of $R_{I,q}$ with respect to $v$ is at most $3P_0a/16$. Hence $R_{\mu,q}$ has derivative at least $9P_0a/16$ in $v$, and strictly positive second derivative. Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's exponential extension below the realized floor supplies the full control-spectrum functional calculus.

The baseline running receipt includes every source copy and its renewal; all occupied-cell acquisition, storage and transfers; actual demand delivery and its receiver; leak/innovation/clamp receivers; bank preparation and counter readout; flag computation, protected records, selector and probe; clock and scheduled gate hardware; normal/interruption/restoration controller; and every update or reset. Initial stored cells and later withdrawals have separate balance records. Each preparation and withdrawal is charged once under the registered stock/flow convention. A reserve already held in the current $N$ is not acquired a second time under the reserve label. Its positive holding tariff is paid for the actual held stock. The procurement quote is the corresponding service-restricted comparison of item 1.

All normal and interruption receipts enter the source-exhausted finite resource record. The scalar PCE force and compensation below concern normal mode; the interruption procurement/service ledger directly charges its separately labelled operations. For each finite common apparatus, let $D_q$ bound the maximum actual baseline receipt rate over all grid members, states, mode records and service ticks. Choose $L_q$ above this bound, the reflexive transfer bound and the rounding margin. In normal mode implement Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's nonnegative common-node billing: at a frozen allocation node $v$, retain the realized baseline receipt, pay the registered reflexive transfer, then pay the nonnegative physical top-up that makes the total equal the rounded target $T_\mu(v)$. All supplies and receivers for these transfers are included in the baseline before their tables are constructed. The finite amount-transfer primitive and binary reservoir bookkeeping have the polynomial word-size bounds of Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b. A search of the same form $L\ge D_0+\operatorname{poly}(1+\log(1+L))$ terminates. The common fixed baseline receipt and the reflexive coefficient add polynomial word-size terms to this search. The grid and normalized controller update do not change when $L$ increases.

Use the actual finite probe score on both sides of the top-up. Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's derivative-controlled interpolation and resource-weighted failure precision search apply on the common finite grid, with the common positive margins (P.8.9a.12.9b.9). At each reached normal-mode node, the paid total and its registered scalar interpolation yield
$$
J_{\mu,q}(C)=\Gamma_0PP_q(C)-R_{\mathrm{total},\mu,q}(C)
 =-\frac{P_0}{2}\left(\frac{C-c_q}{B}-\mu\right)^2-L_q,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.10}
$$
up to the explicitly controlled command quantization. The mobility $B^2/(P_0\tau)$ gives normalized deterministic force $(\mu-v)/\tau$. Noise and clamping are the actual separately charged source commands of item 3. Thus Definition 15's six cost categories and the PCE force refer to the same implementation, while the reserve selector remains its prior service-procurement rule.

**5. One population process and moment limit.** First ignore the finite command rounding. At every mesh $h$, the exact kernel (P.8.9a.12.9b.5) obeys the pathwise identity
$$
X_j^{\mu}=\frac{\mu}{3b}X_j^{3b}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.11}
$$
when driven by the same innovation flags and started at the corresponding reserves. Consequently Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's contraction, stationary law, burn-in bound and reflected-process limit hold uniformly over $\mu\in K$, with constants multiplied by bounded powers of $\mu/(3b)$. In particular the exact mesh laws have uniformly bounded moments of order $5/2$, and their first and second stationary moments converge uniformly on $K$ to those of
$$
dX_t=(m-X_t/\tau)dt+X_t\,dW_t/\sqrt\tau+dL_t,
\qquad X_t\ge2m\tau/3.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.12}
$$
Uniformity follows directly from (P.8.9a.12.9b.11).

The finite integer source has the same limit, including its second moments. Here are explicit perturbation controls. Write $z=3X/\mu_q-2\ge0$. The exact standardized update, independently of $\mu_q$, is
$$
z^+=[z+h(1-z)+\sqrt h(z+2)Z]_+.
$$
Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b proves for $s=5/2$ and an explicit source constant $D_*$, after its stated mesh restriction,
$$
\mathbb E[(z^+)^s\mid z]\le(1-h/4)z^s+D_*h.
$$
The actual standardized update differs by at most $\varepsilon_q(1+z)$, where a common choice is
$$
\varepsilon_q=2h^3+\frac{1}{bB}.
$$
For small enough mesh, $|Z|$ is bounded and the exact update is at most $6(1+z)$; impose also $\varepsilon_q\le1$. The mean-value theorem and $(1+z)^s\le2^{s-1}(1+z^s)$ give
$$
\big|\widetilde z^{\,s}-(z^+)^s\big|
 \le A_*\varepsilon_q(1+z^s),
\qquad A_*=s\,7^{s-1}2^{s-1}.
$$
Choose the command precision and $B$ so $A_*\varepsilon_q\le h/8$. Then
$$
\mathbb E[\widetilde z^{\,s}\mid z]
 \le(1-h/8)z^s+(D_*+1/8)h.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.13}
$$
Iteration from the reserve proves a common $5/2$-moment bound for all finite burn-in lengths and all grid members. Every finite apparatus realizes the corresponding finite prefix exactly, with its supplies sized to the deterministic maximum; a finite bank cap is not inserted into the stochastic law before that prefix ends.

Synchronous coupling with the ideal kernel at $\mu_q$ gives, for a common constant $A$ and all burn-in lengths $J$,
$$
\mathbb E|\widetilde X_J-X_J^{\mu_q}|
 \le A\frac{h^3+B^{-1}}h.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.14}
$$
Indeed the exact update is $(1-h)$-contractive in mean, its one-step perturbation is bounded by (P.8.9a.12.9b.6), and (P.8.9a.12.9b.13) bounds the first moment uniformly; summing the resulting geometric series proves the estimate. The parameter error is at most $1/(Bh)$ and is transported by the exact scaling (P.8.9a.12.9b.11). Choose a common $J_q$ with $(1-h)^{J_q}\to0$. Then the finite-source laws at their registered terminal read time converge uniformly over the parameter grid to the intended stationary laws, and hence along $\mu_q\to\mu$ for every $\mu\in I$.

For completeness, this coupling also transports second moments rather than only distributions. The common $5/2$-moment bound gives
$$
\mathbb E[X^2\mathbf1_{X>M}]\le M^{-1/2}\mathbb E X^{5/2}.
$$
On $[0,M]$, the function $x\mapsto x^2$ is $2M$-Lipschitz. Apply (P.8.9a.12.9b.14), then let $M$ increase, to obtain uniform convergence of second moments. The same argument transports first moments. Finite table, extraction, probe and work-transfer approximations use Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's common source-known error bounds and its resource-weighted diagonal precision search; their retained failure outcomes have vanishing contribution to these moment and cost records. No failed experiment is removed or renormalized.

The reflected process convergence on each finite time interval follows from Theorem P.8.9a.11.6b's Skorokhod-map proof, the common coefficient and floor convergence, and the same stopped perturbation estimate. For any finite collection of population inputs, independent complete sources have factorized innovation laws, so their joint limit has independent Brownian drivers. This realizes the whole common source family, its stationary population measurements and its predictive response on one declared approximation scheme.

**6. The registered Taylor observable.** For every limiting population member, (P.8.9a.12.9b.12) has
$$
\alpha_{\rm st}=3,\qquad \beta_{\rm st}=2m\tau,
\qquad a_{\min}=3.
$$
The moment gate $2k>\sigma^2$ holds strictly. Proposition P.8.9a.12.9a therefore gives the same coefficient
$$
c_*=
\frac{\gamma(1,3)\gamma(3,3)}{\gamma(2,3)^2}-1>0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Var}(Y_m)=c_*\big(\mathbb E Y_m\big)^2,
\quad m\tau\in I.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.9b.15}
$$
Positivity follows from the nondegenerate positive stationary density, and finiteness from shape three. Equations (P.8.9a.12.9b.4), (P.8.9a.12.9b.13) and (P.8.9a.12.9b.14) identify $Y_m$ as the limit of the actual common baseline-difference instrument, with convergence of its mean and variance. Exact finite-bank power laws are replaced by the displayed controlled approximation errors. The raw proxy $C_q=c_q+BY_q$ retains its positive offset and the offset obstruction of Proposition P.8.9a.12.9a; the observed exponent-two coordinate is the registered complexity excess.

The construction has supplied the independent shape-fixing service policy, its qualified predictive aggregate family, all common coefficients and required moments, and its actual excess readout. Every finite source has finite charged resources. The growing banks, rates, supplies, baseline offsets and absolute cost constants belong to the stated source limit. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a1210-conditional-multifractal-cascade-spectrum-from-self-similar-pce-branching"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.10 (Conditional Multifractal Cascade Spectrum from Self-Similar PCE Branching).** *Consider a self-similar PCE-cascade branch whose probability measure $\mu$ is generated by $b\ge2$ contracting similarities of a Euclidean space, each with contraction ratio $1/r$, where $r>1$. Let the branch weights satisfy $p_i>0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^b p_i=1$. Assume strong separation: the images of the compact attractor under distinct first-level similarities are disjoint. Use the level-$n$ cylinder partition, with scale $\varepsilon=r^{-n}$, in the partition sum below. Its cells $B_i$ have positive mass and diameter proportional to $\varepsilon$.*

$$
Z_q(\varepsilon)
:=
\sum_{i:\,B_i\cap\mathrm{supp}(\mu)\neq\varnothing}
\mu(B_i)^q,
\qquad
q \in \mathbb{R},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.16}
$$

*and let the multifractal exponent function be*

$$
\tau(q)
:=
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0^+}
\frac{\log Z_q(\varepsilon)}{\log\varepsilon}
=
\frac{\log\!\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^b p_i^q\bigr)}{\log(1/r)}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.17}
$$

*Then:*

*1. (Singularity spectrum as Legendre transform.) The singularity spectrum*

$$
f(\alpha)
:=
\dim_{\mathrm H}
\Bigl\{
