x \in \mathrm{supp}(\mu)
:
\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0^+}
\frac{\log\mu(B_\varepsilon(x))}{\log\varepsilon}
=
\alpha
\Bigr\}
$$

*equals the Legendre transform of $\tau$:*

$$
f(\alpha)
=
\inf_{q \in \mathbb{R}}\bigl(q\alpha - \tau(q)\bigr).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.18}
$$

*2. (Large-deviation form.) Let $D_{\mathrm{eff}} := \log b/\log r$ be the box-counting dimension of $\mathrm{supp}(\mu)$, let $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_b)$ be the empirical branch frequencies along a length-$n$ path under the uniform branch-counting law, and let*

$$
I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\mathbf{x})
:=
\sum_{i=1}^b x_i \log(b\,x_i)
\tag{P.8.9a.12.19}
$$

*be the Cramer rate function for $\mathbf{x}$ relative to the uniform distribution. Define*

$$
\alpha(\mathbf{x})
:=
-\frac{1}{\log r}\sum_{i=1}^b x_i \log p_i.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.20}
$$

*Then for every $\alpha$ in the range of the map $\mathbf{x} \mapsto \alpha(\mathbf{x})$,*

$$
f(\alpha)
=
D_{\mathrm{eff}}
-
\frac{1}{\log r}
\inf\bigl\{\,I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\mathbf{x}) : \alpha(\mathbf{x}) = \alpha\bigr\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.21}
$$

*Proof.*

*Step 1 ($\tau(q)$ closed form).* By the non-overlap condition, the level-$n$ partition consists of $b^n$ disjoint boxes of diameter $r^{-n}$. The mass of the box reached by the path $(i_1, \dots, i_n)$ is $\prod_{j=1}^n p_{i_j}$. With $\varepsilon = r^{-n}$, the partition function evaluates to

$$
Z_q(r^{-n})
=
\sum_{(i_1,\dots,i_n)}\prod_{j=1}^n p_{i_j}^q
=
\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^b p_i^q\Bigr)^n.
$$

Therefore $\log Z_q(r^{-n}) = n \log\!\bigl(\sum_i p_i^q\bigr)$ and $\log(r^{-n}) = n\log(1/r)$, giving (P.8.9a.12.17) in the limit.

*Step 2 (Legendre transform.) Falconer [1997, Theorem 11.5] gives Equation (P.8.9a.12.18) for the Hausdorff singularity spectrum on the strong-separation similarity branch. Its attainable interval is $[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]$, where $\alpha_{\min}=\min_i(-\log p_i/\log r)$ and $\alpha_{\max}=\max_i(-\log p_i/\log r)$. When all weights are equal, this interval is a singleton and the spectrum is the Hausdorff dimension $\log b/\log r$ of the attractor.*

*Step 3 (LDP form.)* Let
$$
\Delta_b=
\left\{\mathbf x\in[0,1]^b:\sum_{i=1}^b x_i=1\right\},
\qquad
H(\mathbf x)=-\sum_{i=1}^b x_i\log x_i,
$$
with $0\log0=0$. If $\mathbf x$ is an $n$-type, so each $nx_i$ is an integer, every path of that type has mass $\prod_i p_i^{nx_i}$ and width $r^{-n}$. Hence its local exponent is
$$
\frac{n\sum_i x_i\log p_i}{-n\log r}
=
-\frac1{\log r}\sum_i x_i\log p_i
=
\alpha(\mathbf x).
$$
The method-of-types bounds (Cover and Thomas 2006) give
$$
(n+1)^{-b}e^{nH(\mathbf x)}
\le
\binom{n}{nx_1,\ldots,nx_b}
\le
e^{nH(\mathbf x)}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.21a}
$$
These inequalities also follow by applying Stirling's formula to the factorials; the logarithmic error is $O(\log n)$ uniformly over the at most $(n+1)^b$ possible types.

For $\delta>0$, let $N_{n,\delta}(\alpha)$ be the number of level-$n$ boxes whose type $\mathbf x$ satisfies $|\alpha(\mathbf x)-\alpha|\le\delta$. Summing (P.8.9a.12.21a) over all such types and using the bound $(n+1)^b$ on their number gives
$$
\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\lim_{n\to\infty}
\frac1n\log N_{n,\delta}(\alpha)
=
\sup\{H(\mathbf x):\mathbf x\in\Delta_b,\ \alpha(\mathbf x)=\alpha\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.21b}
$$
For the upper bound, compactness of $\Delta_b$ and continuity of $H$ and $\alpha$ imply that the supremum over the closed $\delta$-window decreases to the constrained supremum. For the lower bound, choose any feasible $\mathbf x$ and approximate it by $n$-types $\mathbf x^{(n)}\to\mathbf x$; continuity gives $\alpha(\mathbf x^{(n)})\to\alpha$ and $H(\mathbf x^{(n)})\to H(\mathbf x)$. Thus no uniqueness or interior assumption is used.

The count in (P.8.9a.12.21b), divided by $\log r$, is the cylinder-window spectrum. Step 2 identifies the Hausdorff spectrum with the Legendre transform, and the entropy-duality calculation below identifies that transform with the same constrained entropy maximum. Together these facts give
$$
f(\alpha)
=
\frac1{\log r}
\sup_{\alpha(\mathbf x)=\alpha}H(\mathbf x).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.21c}
$$
Moreover,
$$
I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\mathbf x)
=
\sum_i x_i\log(bx_i)
=
\log b-H(\mathbf x).
$$
Substitution into (P.8.9a.12.21c) yields
$$
f(\alpha)
=
\frac{\log b}{\log r}
-
\frac1{\log r}
\inf_{\alpha(\mathbf x)=\alpha}I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\mathbf x)
=
D_{\mathrm{eff}}
-
\frac1{\log r}
\inf_{\alpha(\mathbf x)=\alpha}I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\mathbf x),
$$
which is (P.8.9a.12.21).

It remains to verify agreement with (P.8.9a.12.18). For $q\in\mathbb R$, define
$$
x_i(q)=\frac{p_i^q}{\sum_jp_j^q}.
$$
For any $\mathbf x\in\Delta_b$, nonnegativity of relative entropy (Cover and Thomas 2006) gives
$$
0
\le
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathbf x\|\mathbf x(q))
=
-H(\mathbf x)-q\sum_i x_i\log p_i
+\log\!\left(\sum_jp_j^q\right).
$$
If $\alpha(\mathbf x)=\alpha$, then $\sum_i x_i\log p_i=-\alpha\log r$, and therefore
$$
\frac{H(\mathbf x)}{\log r}
\le
q\alpha+
\frac{\log(\sum_jp_j^q)}{\log r}
=
q\alpha-\tau(q).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.21d}
$$
For every exponent in the interior of the attainable interval, continuity of $q\mapsto\alpha(\mathbf x(q))$ supplies a $q$ with $\alpha(\mathbf x(q))=\alpha$, and equality holds in (P.8.9a.12.21d) because the relative entropy then vanishes. At either endpoint, take $q\to+\infty$ or $q\to-\infty$; the distributions $\mathbf x(q)$ converge to the entropy-maximizing distribution on the corresponding extremal-weight face, and continuity gives equality there as well. If all $p_i$ are equal, the attainable interval is a single point and equality follows directly from the uniform distribution. Consequently
$$
f(\alpha)
=
\inf_{q\in\mathbb R}\bigl(q\alpha-\tau(q)\bigr)
$$
for every attainable $\alpha$, including nonunique and endpoint cases. ∎

*Status.* Theorem P.8.9a.12.10 is an instance of the conditional universal-pattern template of Section P.8.9a.12: it derives the singularity spectrum of a self-similar PCE-cascade branch from explicit branching, weight, and non-overlap data. PCE may select among admissible cascade branches via the operational cost of the branching rule, but the selection of $b$, $r$, and $\{p_i\}$ requires additional domain hypotheses analogous to the network-geometry inputs of Theorem P.8.9a.12.7 and the discrete-scale-invariance input of Theorem P.8.9a.12.6. The relation $f(\alpha) = D_{\mathrm{eff}} - I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\alpha)/\log r$ is established here under the stated cascade hypotheses. It provides a conditional comparison with turbulence multifractal models (Frisch 1995, §8.5) and with the singularity-spectrum formalism of Halsey et al. [1986, §I, Eqs. (1.5), (1.8)–(1.11)]. PU supplies the conditional template; the empirical $f(\alpha)$ measurement is the direct test of the cascade hypothesis on each named domain.

*Falsification Conditions.* Within an independently validated PCE-cascade branch with measured branching parameters $(b, r, \{p_i\})$:

*1. an empirically resolved singularity spectrum $f_{\mathrm{obs}}(\alpha)$ that is not the Legendre transform of $\tau(q) = \log(\sum_i p_i^q)/\log(1/r)$ contradicts (P.8.9a.12.18);*

*2. an observed deviation between $f_{\mathrm{obs}}(\alpha)$ and $D_{\mathrm{eff}} - I_{\mathrm{unif}}(\mathbf{x}(\alpha))/\log r$ on the same branch contradicts (P.8.9a.12.21).*

*Each contradiction is conditional on the prior validation of the branching, scale-ratio, weight, and non-overlap hypotheses; absent that branch, the null result rejects the cascade hypothesis itself rather than the multifractal formalism.*

<a id="theorem-p89a1210a-exact-scale-covariance-of-strongly-separated-branching-sets"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.10a (Exact Scale Covariance of Strongly Separated Branching Sets).** In the notation of Corollary P.8.9a.12.8, let $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ with $n\ge2$ be similarities of $\mathbb R^d$ with common ratio $r\in(0,1)$, let $K$ be the nonempty compact set with $K=\bigcup_{i=1}^nf_i(K)$, and assume strong separation with gap
$$
\delta:=\min_{i\ne j}\operatorname{dist}\bigl(f_i(K),f_j(K)\bigr)>0.
$$
For a bounded set $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ and $\varepsilon>0$, let $N(\varepsilon;X)$ be the least number of sets of diameter at most $\varepsilon$ that cover $X$. Fix $x_0\in K$, put $T_0=\{x_0\}$ and $T_{j+1}=\bigcup_if_i(T_j)$, the terminal set of the level-$j$ branching, and write $D_f=\ln n/\ln(1/r)$.

1. *Covariance.* For $0<\varepsilon<\delta/r$ and $j\ge0$,
$$
N(r\varepsilon;K)=n\,N(\varepsilon;K),
\qquad
N(r\varepsilon;T_{j+1})=n\,N(\varepsilon;T_j).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10a.1}
$$
2. *Finite-window counts.* Let $m_0$ be the least integer $m\ge0$ with $r^{m+1}<\delta$, and put $c_K:=n^{-m_0}N(r^{m_0};K)$. Then $N(r^m;K)=c_Kn^m$ for every $m\ge m_0$, and $n^{m-m_0}\le N(r^m;T_j)\le c_Kn^m$ for $m_0\le m\le j+m_0$. Hence the box counts of Corollary P.8.9a.12.8 hold with $c_-=c_+=c_K$ on $K$ and with $(c_-,c_+)=(n^{-m_0},c_K)$ on the finite branching, and
$$
\frac{\ln N(r^m;K)}{\ln(r^{-m})}=D_f+\frac{\ln c_K}{m\ln(1/r)}
\qquad(m\ge\max(m_0,1)),
$$
so the box dimension of $K$ is $D_f$.
3. *Ambient gate.* Every bounded $X\subset\mathbb R^d$ with diameter $\Delta>0$ satisfies $N(\varepsilon;X)\le\lceil\sqrt d\,\Delta/\varepsilon\rceil^d$, and strong separation forces $D_f\le d$.
4. *Discrete scale invariance.* The response $F(x):=N(1/x;K)$ satisfies $F(x/r)=r^{-D_f}F(x)$ for $x>r/\delta$. Hence $F(x)=x^{D_f}P(\ln x/\ln(1/r))$ there, with $P$ periodic of period $1$ on $(\ln(r/\delta)/\ln(1/r),\infty)$ and $c_K/n\le P\le nc_K$ for $x\ge r^{-m_0}$; the expansion (P.8.9a.12.10) of Theorem P.8.9a.12.6 holds on this half-line with $\lambda=1/r$ and $\alpha=D_f$.

*Proof.* For item 1, a set of diameter at most $r\varepsilon<\delta$ meets at most one of the pieces $f_i(K)$. If $U_1,\ldots,U_N$ cover $K$ with diameters at most $\varepsilon$, the $nN$ sets $f_i(U_l)$ have diameters at most $r\varepsilon$ and cover $K$, so $N(r\varepsilon;K)\le nN(\varepsilon;K)$. Conversely, in a minimal cover of $K$ by sets of diameter at most $r\varepsilon$, the sets meeting $f_i(K)$ cover $f_i(K)$, and their images under the inverse similarity $f_i^{-1}$ have diameters at most $\varepsilon$ and cover $K$. Each piece therefore uses at least $N(\varepsilon;K)$ sets, and no set is counted for two pieces, so $N(r\varepsilon;K)\ge nN(\varepsilon;K)$. The same argument applies to $T_{j+1}=\bigcup_if_i(T_j)$ because $T_j\subseteq K$, so $f_i(T_j)\subseteq f_i(K)$.

For item 2, every scale $r^{m'}$ with $m'\ge m_0$ satisfies $r^{m'}<\delta/r$, so iterating item 1 from $r^{m_0}$ gives $N(r^m;K)=n^{m-m_0}N(r^{m_0};K)$ and $N(r^m;T_j)=n^{m-m_0}N(r^{m_0};T_{j-m+m_0})$. Since $\varnothing\ne T_{j-m+m_0}\subseteq K$, the last factor lies between $1$ and $N(r^{m_0};K)$. For $r^{m+1}\le\varepsilon\le r^m$ with $m\ge\max(m_0,1)$, monotonicity of $N$ in $\varepsilon$ places $\ln N(\varepsilon;K)/\ln(1/\varepsilon)$ between $(\ln c_K+m\ln n)/((m+1)\ln(1/r))$ and $(\ln c_K+(m+1)\ln n)/(m\ln(1/r))$, which both tend to $D_f$.

For item 3, a set of diameter $\Delta$ lies in a closed cube of side $\Delta$, which splits into $\lceil\sqrt d\,\Delta/\varepsilon\rceil^d$ subcubes of diameter at most $\varepsilon$. Strong separation with $n\ge2$ gives $\operatorname{diam}K>0$, and item 2 gives $c_Kn^m\le(\sqrt d\operatorname{diam}K+1)^dr^{-md}$ for every $m\ge m_0$. Thus $(nr^d)^m$ is bounded, so $nr^d\le1$, which is $D_f\le d$.

For item 4, put $\varepsilon=1/x$ in item 1, which gives $F(x/r)=nF(x)=r^{-D_f}F(x)$ for $x>r/\delta$. Then $P(u):=r^{D_fu}F(r^{-u})$ satisfies $P(u+1)=r^{D_f}r^{D_fu}F(r^{-u}/r)=r^{D_f}n\,P(u)=P(u)$ on the stated half-line, because $r^{D_f}=1/n$, and $F(x)=x^{D_f}P(\ln x/\ln(1/r))$ because $x^{D_f}=r^{-D_fu}$ at $x=r^{-u}$. For $x\in[r^{-m},r^{-m-1}]$ with $m\ge m_0$, item 2 and monotonicity give $c_Kn^m\le F(x)\le c_Kn^{m+1}$ and $n^m\le x^{D_f}\le n^{m+1}$, which bound $P$. Being bounded and measurable, $P$ is square-integrable over one period, and the Fourier argument of Theorem P.8.9a.12.6 applies on the half-line. ∎

<a id="corollary-p89a1210b-middle-third-branching-instance"></a>**Corollary P.8.9a.12.10b (Middle-Third Branching Instance).** Take $d=1$, $n=2$, $f_1(x)=x/3$ and $f_2(x)=x/3+2/3$. The attractor is the middle-third Cantor set $K_{1/3}$, with $\delta=1/3$ and $D_f=\ln2/\ln3$, and
$$
N(\varepsilon;K_{1/3})=2^{\lceil\log_3(1/\varepsilon)\rceil}\quad(0<\varepsilon<1),
\qquad
N(\varepsilon;K_{1/3})=1\quad(\varepsilon\ge1).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10b.1}
$$
Hence $F(x)=N(1/x;K_{1/3})$ satisfies $F(3x)=2F(x)$ for $x>1$, and $F(x)=x^{D_f}P(\log_3x)$ for $x>1$ with $P(u)=2^{\lceil u\rceil-u}$. The Fourier coefficients of $P$ and the leading data of (P.8.9a.12.11) are
$$
c_m=\frac1{\ln2+2\pi im},
\qquad
c_0=\frac1{\ln2},
\qquad
2|c_1|=\frac2{\sqrt{(\ln2)^2+4\pi^2}},
\qquad
\phi=\arg c_1=-\arctan\frac{2\pi}{\ln2},
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10b.2}
$$
so the relative first-harmonic amplitude is $2|c_1|/c_0=2\ln2/\sqrt{(\ln2)^2+4\pi^2}\approx0.2193$. The partial sums $P_M(u)=\sum_{|m|\le M}c_me^{2\pi imu}$ satisfy
$$
\|P-P_M\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2\le\frac1{2\pi^2M}
\qquad(M\ge1).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10b.3}
$$

*Proof.* The set $K_{1/3}$ lies in $[0,1]$ and contains $0$, $1/3$, $2/3$ and $1$, and $f_1(K_{1/3})\subseteq[0,1/3]$, $f_2(K_{1/3})\subseteq[2/3,1]$, so $\delta=1/3$ and $\delta/r=1$. For $\varepsilon\ge1$ one set covers $K_{1/3}$. For $1/3\le\varepsilon<1$, one set of diameter at most $\varepsilon$ cannot contain both $0$ and $1$, while $[0,1/3]$ and $[2/3,1]$ cover, so $N=2$. Item 1 of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10a gives $N(\varepsilon/3;K_{1/3})=2N(\varepsilon;K_{1/3})$ for $\varepsilon<1$, and induction over the intervals $[3^{-j},3^{-j+1})$ gives (P.8.9a.12.10b.1). For $x>1$, $F(x)=2^{\lceil u\rceil}$ with $u=\log_3x$, and $x^{D_f}=2^u$. Over one period,
$$
c_m=\int_0^12^{1-u}e^{-2\pi imu}\,du=2\,\frac{1-2^{-1}e^{-2\pi im}}{\ln2+2\pi im}=\frac1{\ln2+2\pi im}.
$$
Parseval's identity gives $\|P-P_M\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2=2\sum_{m>M}[(\ln2)^2+4\pi^2m^2]^{-1}\le(2\pi^2)^{-1}\sum_{m>M}m^{-2}\le(2\pi^2M)^{-1}$. ∎

<a id="proposition-p89a1210c-finite-window-mass-moment-and-spectrum-extractors-on-the-cylinder-partition"></a>**Proposition P.8.9a.12.10c (Finite-Window Mass, Moment and Spectrum Extractors on the Cylinder Partition).** In the setting of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10, with $b$ maps of contraction ratio $1/r$ and weights $p_1,\ldots,p_b$, let $N_n(\mathbf x)$ be the number of level-$n$ cylinders of type $\mathbf x$ for an $n$-type $\mathbf x\in\Delta_b$, and put $f_n(\mathbf x):=\ln N_n(\mathbf x)/(n\ln r)$.

1. For every $n\ge1$ and $q\in\mathbb R$, $\ln Z_q(r^{-n})/\ln(r^{-n})=\tau(q)$ exactly.
2. For every $n$-type $\mathbf x$, every cylinder of type $\mathbf x$ has mass $\prod_ip_i^{nx_i}$ and local exponent exactly $\alpha(\mathbf x)$ at scale $r^{-n}$, and
$$
0\le\frac{H(\mathbf x)}{\ln r}-f_n(\mathbf x)\le\frac{b\ln(n+1)}{n\ln r}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10c.1}
$$
3. If $b=2$ and $p_1\ne p_2$, then $\mathbf x\mapsto\alpha(\mathbf x)$ is injective on $\Delta_2$, $f(\alpha(\mathbf x))=H(\mathbf x)/\ln r$ for every $\mathbf x\in\Delta_2$, and
$$
0\le f(\alpha(\mathbf x))-f_n(\mathbf x)\le\frac{2\ln(n+1)}{n\ln r}
$$
for every $n$-type $\mathbf x$.

*Proof.* Item 1 is Step 1 of the proof of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10 at finite $n$: $Z_q(r^{-n})=(\sum_ip_i^q)^n$, so the ratio equals $\ln(\sum_ip_i^q)/\ln(1/r)=\tau(q)$ for every $n$. For item 2, a cylinder reached by a path of type $\mathbf x$ has mass $\prod_ip_i^{nx_i}$ and width $r^{-n}$, which gives the local exponent $\alpha(\mathbf x)$ as in Step 3 of that proof, and $N_n(\mathbf x)$ is the multinomial coefficient, so (P.8.9a.12.21a) gives (P.8.9a.12.10c.1). For item 3, $\alpha(x_1,1-x_1)=-[x_1\ln p_1+(1-x_1)\ln p_2]/\ln r$ is strictly monotone in $x_1$ when $p_1\ne p_2$, so each level set $\{\alpha(\mathbf x)=\alpha\}$ in $\Delta_2$ is a single point and (P.8.9a.12.21c) gives $f(\alpha(\mathbf x))=H(\mathbf x)/\ln r$; item 2 then gives the bound. ∎

<a id="theorem-p89a1210d-selected-ternary-predictive-cascade-and-complete-finite-window-spectrum"></a>**Theorem P.8.9a.12.10d (Selected Ternary Predictive Cascade and Complete Finite-Window Spectrum).** Fix a finite horizon $N\ge1$. The source is a categorical prediction processor with the following registered components. A three-bit uniform teacher word $U$ is decoded by
$$
t(U)=\begin{cases}1,&0\le U<4,\\2,&4\le U<7,\\3,&U=7.\end{cases}
\qquad
\mathcal A=\{A\in\{0,\ldots,8\}^3:A_1+A_2+A_3=8\},\qquad a=A/8.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.1}
$$
Successive teacher words are independent. The $45$ candidate configurations are the constant probability forecasts $a$, implemented by the same padded circuit. Each candidate also controls an independent three-bit address sampler: it returns $1$ on the first $A_1$ words, $2$ on the next $A_2$, and $3$ on the remaining $A_3$. The teacher decoder, the candidate grid, the proper loss
$$
L(a,Y)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^3(a_i-\mathbf1_{\{Y=i\}})^2,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.2}
$$
and the three address digits $(d_1,d_2,d_3)=(0,3,7)$ are fixed before calculating a spectrum. Forecast commitment precedes the fresh teacher and address draws. The address and teacher draws are independent, and neither returns to a future forecast input. All run records are retained through final readout.

The physical source class uses fresh finite fair preparations, retained-input Boolean gates, fixed-duration primitive slots and the positive service contract in item 6. Its geometric response is an exact rational address together with its cylinder label; a mechanical spatial placement device would carry its own calibration record. Then the following statements hold.

1. **Full comparison and actual selected update.** The teacher law and risk are
$$
p=(4,3,1)/8,\qquad
R(A)=\mathbb E_p L(A/8,Y)
=\frac{19}{64}+\frac{\|A-(4,3,1)\|_2^2}{128}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.3}
$$
Thus $A_*=(4,3,1)$ is the unique minimizer over all $45$ configurations, with strict gap $1/64$. A finite setup controller obtains the multiplicities $(4,3,1)$ by enumerating the eight entries of the registered teacher decoder. It evaluates $\sum_i c_i T_i(A)$ for each candidate, where $c_i$ is the obtained multiplicity and $T_i(A)=\sum_j(A_j-8\mathbf1_{\{i=j\}})^2$, and selects the least value, with a fixed lexicographic tie rule. This computes $A_*$ from the actual source description.

Retain two protocols at horizon $N$: a frozen-configuration run and a select-then-run experiment. In a frozen run every active and preceding forecast is $A/8$. In the selected run the first preceding forecast is $A/8$, the first active forecast is $A_*/8$, and all later preceding and active forecasts are $A_*/8$. Both forecasts at a stage are committed before the same teacher; the address sampler uses its active forecast. The realized first gain is $L(A/8,Y_1)-L(A_*/8,Y_1)$, and
$$
\mathbb E[\Delta PE_1]=\frac{\|A-A_*\|_2^2}{128};\qquad
\Delta PE_j=0\quad(j>1)
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.4}
$$
for raw scores in the selected run. Individual first gains can have either sign. Old configuration and controller records remain retained.

For Definition D.1f, take $\mathcal X_{\mathfrak B}=\mathcal A$ and retain these two protocols and their finitely many prefix and coordinate restrictions, with the numerical labels fixed. The responses include addresses, forecasts, teachers, both raw losses and both loss flags from item 2. The frozen first-address law recovers $a$, so this response quotient has exactly $45$ points. With
$$
K_{\mathfrak B}=\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2,\qquad
r_{\mathfrak B}(A)=(\Gamma_0R(A),P_{\rm svc}),\qquad
W_{\mathfrak B}=(0,\infty)^2,
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.5}
$$
where $\Gamma_0>0$ is a power-equivalent task tariff and $P_{\rm svc}>0$ is the common whole-run service power of item 6, every allowed scalarization selects $A_*$. The selected sampler is therefore a response-active consequence of the populated proper-task minimum on this complete finite configuration class.

2. **Complete finite word and separated address response.** At stage $j$, let $A_j^-$ and $A_j^+$ denote the preceding and active integer forecasts. Draw a teacher $Y_j$, an independent address symbol $I_j$ with law $A_j^+/8$, and independent seven-bit integers $V_j^-,V_j^+\in\{0,\ldots,127\}$. Store
$$
T_j^\pm=\sum_{i=1}^3(A_{j,i}^\pm-8\mathbf1_{\{Y_j=i\}})^2,\qquad
Z_j^\pm=\mathbf1_{\{V_j^\pm<T_j^\pm\}},\qquad
J_0=0,\quad J_j=8J_{j-1}+d_{I_j}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.6}
$$
The threshold is an eight-bit integer, including $128$. Thus $\mathbb E[Z_j^\pm\mid A_j^\pm,Y_j]=T_j^\pm/128=L(A_j^\pm/8,Y_j)$, including zero and unit losses. The dimensionless address, with its registered Euclidean numerical metric, is
$$
X_j=J_j/8^j=\sum_{h=1}^jd_{I_h}8^{-h}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.7}
$$
For either fixed protocol, the probability of an address/teacher/flag word is
$$
\prod_{j=1}^N\left[
\frac{A_{j,I_j}^+}{8}\,p_{Y_j}
\prod_{\sigma\in\{-,+\}}
\left(\frac{T_j^\sigma}{128}\right)^{Z_j^\sigma}
\left(1-\frac{T_j^\sigma}{128}\right)^{1-Z_j^\sigma}
\right],
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.8}
$$
with the Bernoulli endpoint factors interpreted by their normalized kernels. All other displayed fields, the protocol setting and the admission flag are deterministic retained fields. Formula (8) gives their joint law, including correlations caused by a common teacher. The private $20N$ fair bits and all computation outputs complete its dilation.

Let $f_i(x)=(x+d_i)/8$ on $[0,1]$ and let $K=\bigcup_i f_i(K)$ be the compact attractor. Its three first-level hull intervals are $[0,1/8]$, $[3/8,1/2]$ and $[7/8,1]$. Their exact minimum gap is $1/4$, since the endpoints $0,1$ belong to $K$. For a word $v=(i_1,\ldots,i_j)$, the retained cylinder label denotes $K_v=f_{i_1}\circ\cdots\circ f_{i_j}(K)$, whose hull is $[X_j,X_j+8^{-j}]$. In the selected run,
$$
\mu(K_v)=\prod_{h=1}^j p_{i_h},\qquad
b=3,\quad r=8,\quad
\tau(q)=-\frac{\ln[(1/2)^q+(3/8)^q+(1/8)^q]}{\ln8}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.9}
$$
The rational point $X_j$ is a retained representative of its cylinder. The cylinder coding, rather than an equality between a finite atomic point law and the infinite measure, supplies the finite response map. Common infinite independent fair tapes couple every logical prefix identically across horizon devices. Their separate widths, clock labels and costs remain horizon-indexed. The compatible cylinder measures give the stated infinite measure and the spectrum of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10.

3. **A complete spectrum window for every finite alphabet.** More generally, take the positive weights and separated carrier of Theorem P.8.9a.12.10 with any $b\ge2$. Define
$$
\ell_i=-\frac{\ln p_i}{\ln r},\qquad
\ell_- =\min_i\ell_i,\quad \ell_+=\max_i\ell_i,\quad
D=\ell_+-\ell_-,\qquad
\Omega_b(t)=\min\{\ln b,\ t\ln(eb/t)\},\quad\Omega_b(0)=0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.10}
$$
Here $0\le t\le1$. If not all levels coincide, let $g>0$ be their minimum distinct-value gap. For $\alpha\in[\ell_-,\ell_+]$, $n\ge1$ and $\delta\ge0$, let
$$
C_n(\alpha,\delta)
=\sum_{\substack{k_1+\cdots+k_b=n,\ k_i\ge0\\
|\sum_i(k_i/n)\ell_i-\alpha|\le\delta}}
\frac{n!}{k_1!\cdots k_b!},
\qquad
t_n=\min\{1,(b-1)/n\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.11}
$$
For every $\delta\ge Dt_n$, the count is positive and its observable $F_n=\ln C_n/(n\ln r)$ satisfies
$$
 f(\alpha)-\frac{\Omega_b(t_n)+b\ln(n+1)/n}{\ln r}
\ \le\ F_n(\alpha,\delta)\ \le\
 f(\alpha)+\frac{\Omega_b(\min\{1,\delta/g\})+b\ln(n+1)/n}{\ln r}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.12}
$$
This bound holds at endpoints and for repeated unequal weights. If all weights are equal, the attainable exponent is the singleton $\alpha_0=\ln b/\ln r$; at that query every window contains all $b^n$ words and $F_n=f(\alpha_0)=\ln b/\ln r$ exactly. For the selected ternary source,
$$
(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3)=\left(\frac13,1-\frac{\ln3}{\ln8},1\right),\qquad
D=\frac23,\qquad g=\frac{\ln(4/3)}{\ln8}>0.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.13}
$$
Consequently any windows with $\delta_n\downarrow0$ and $\delta_n\ge(2/3)t_n$ yield a uniform finite-window approximation to the full ternary spectrum, with both errors in (12) explicit. A single type entropy is not substituted for the maximum on its exponent fiber.

4. **Executable finite precision and observation.** Let rational levels $\widehat\ell_i$ obey $\max_i|\widehat\ell_i-\ell_i|\le\rho_\ell$, and let the registered rational query $\widehat\alpha$ obey $|\widehat\alpha-\alpha|\le\rho_\alpha$. Put $\rho=\rho_\ell+\rho_\alpha$. Define $\widehat C_n$ by the same integer sum as (11), using $|\sum_i(k_i/n)\widehat\ell_i-\widehat\alpha|\le\delta$. Then
$$
 C_n(\alpha,\delta-\rho)\le\widehat C_n\le C_n(\alpha,\delta+\rho)
 \quad(\delta\ge\rho).
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.14}
$$
If $\delta-\rho\ge Dt_n$, replace $F_n$ in (12) by $\ln\widehat C_n/(n\ln r)$ and $\delta$ in its upper bound by $\delta+\rho$. An output logarithm interval of radius $\epsilon_{\log}$ enlarges both bounds by that radius. Counts and all query/precision fields remain retained, including empty-window and invalid-query outcomes.

For the ternary source this extractor has a terminating rational implementation. Its fields describe the selected carrier $p$ in both protocols; the frozen protocol retains its separate address law $a$. Use a fixed integer precision $s\ge4$, dyadic levels and queries with denominator $2^s$, and $m=s+8$. The rational series
$$
 S_m(z)=2\sum_{h=0}^{m-1}\frac{z^{2h+1}}{2h+1},\qquad
0\le\ln\frac{1+z}{1-z}-S_m(z)
\le\frac{2z^{2m+1}}{(2m+1)(1-z^2)}
\quad(0\le z<1)
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.15}
$$
certifies $\ln2$ at $z=1/3$ and $\ln3$ at $z=1/2$. Interval division and dyadic rounding give all three $\widehat\ell_i$ with $\rho_\ell=2^{1-s}$. If their integer numerators are $L_i$, the query numerator is $a$ and its nonnegative window numerator is $d$, membership is the exact integer test $|\sum_i k_i L_i-na|\le nd$. Pascal addition gives every binomial coefficient through $N$, and each ternary type contributes $\binom n{k_1}\binom{n-k_1}{k_2}$. Thus the sum is a finite integer calculation, including window ties. For a positive count $C$, write $C=2^e u$, $1\le u<2$; use (15) at $z=(u-1)/(u+1)\le1/3$ and the same certified $\ln2$ to enclose $\ln C/(3n\ln2)$. Rounding the interval outward to denominator $2^s$ gives width at most $2^{2-s}$. The exact count accompanies it.

The law (8), rather than its predicted count alone, owns observation. For $M$ independent complete selected runs, the empirical frequency $\widehat\mu_v$ of every cylinder at a fixed level $n\le N$ obeys
$$
\Pr\left\{\max_{|v|=n}|\widehat\mu_v-\mu(K_v)|>\eta\right\}
\le2\,3^n e^{-2M\eta^2}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.16}
$$
On this event's complement, $0<\eta<8^{-n}$ gives every empirical cylinder exponent the error at most
$$
\rho_{\rm mass}=
\frac{-\ln(1-8^n\eta)}{n\ln8}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.17}
$$
The count of observed cylinder exponents in a registered window has the same sandwich with $\rho_{\rm mass}$ and the query error included. Such a frequency census uses all $3^n$ registered cylinder labels, and its replicate count is independently fixed. A pointwise sample of a few cylinders does not replace that census. The model-derived extractor (14), the sampling envelope (16)–(17), and measured empirical acceptance have these distinct inputs. Equations (19)–(21) bill one complete source run and its model-derived query; $M$ independent complete replicas carry $M$ such run ledgers, while the empirical frequency-census processor has its own separately registered ledger.

5. **Finite control, storage and complete instrument.** The construction admits the following explicit deliberately padded implementation. Fix a query depth $1\le n\le N$, $s\ge4$, and
$$
 w=64(N+s+16)^3,\qquad B_w=256w^2,\qquad
 Q_{\rm cfg}=2048,\quad Q_{\rm step}=128,\quad
 Q_{\rm ext}=32(N+1)^2+2048(s+8)+1024.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.18}
$$
The primitive alphabet is retained-input NOT, AND, OR and XOR on bit registers. Every word addition, subtraction, multiplication, comparison, bounded integer division, logical transfer, leading-bit scan or bounded $(N+1)$-row lookup is compiled into at most $B_w$ such gates and padded to exactly $B_w$ fresh-output gates. Signed operands and quotient/remainder outputs use separately typed $w$-bit fields. All arithmetic used below stays in range.

Setup first compares each original configuration word to the bounds $0\le A_i\le8$ and masks each failed field to zero before any sum. It then tests whether the sanitized sum is eight. It retains every original word and the admission flag, and replaces a failed tuple by $A_*$ before runtime arithmetic. It enumerates the eight teacher entries, all $45$ risk values and the selected tuple. The risk comparison and tie rule execute for every configuration and both protocol settings. The runtime query fields are validated by direct signed comparisons $-2^{s+2}\le a\le2^{s+2}$, $0\le d\le2^{s+2}$ and $1\le n\le N$, before absolute values, additions or products involving them. Failed fields and their flag are retained, and the query is replaced by $(a,d,n)=(2^s,2^s,1)$. The query precision and program horizon are compilation parameters.

Each stage commits its prescribed preceding and active vectors, draws twenty fair bits, applies the teacher and configurable address decoders, evaluates the six signed score residuals, six squares, four score additions, two flag comparisons, and the prefix address update, and records the indices, symbols and flags. Its $Q_{\rm step}$ slots include all transfers, conditional selections and padding. All control selections use the fixed protocol setting and stage index. Setup uses at most $Q_{\rm cfg}$ slots. After the stages, the extractor builds the Pascal table, evaluates every type in a fixed $(N+1)^2$ loop with inadmissible entries masked, and performs the certified rational logarithms and output rounding in at most $Q_{\rm ext}$ slots. An empty count is retained; the logarithm routine receives $\max(1,C)$ and an empty-window flag. Invalid and failure outcomes remain part of the instrument.

Reserve the output and full retained storage as
$$
\begin{split}
 O&=N(12w+4)+4w+1,\\
 G_{\rm tot}&=B_w(Q_{\rm cfg}+NQ_{\rm step}+Q_{\rm ext})+O,\\
 R_{\rm bit}&=128w+20N+G_{\rm tot}+O.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.19}
$$
At each stage the twelve output words contain its index, prefix integer, three preceding and three active numerators, teacher, address symbol and two score integers; the four bit fields retain the two flags, protocol and admission information. The remaining reserve contains the count, its two outward logarithm bounds, extractor status and necessary pointer copies. The $128w$ input reserve contains source/program constants, original configuration and query fields, and all static controls. Every fair draw, primitive gate output and final pointer copy has its own cell. Unused reserved cells remain ready.

For a Boolean primitive $f$ with its inputs retained, the extension $U_f:|x,z\rangle\mapsto|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle$ is a permutation involution. On the finite qubit carrier it is implemented in duration $\tau_g>0$ by
$$
H_f=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau_g}(I-U_f),\qquad
\int\|H_f\|\,dt\le\pi\hbar.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.20}
$$
The source calls prepare independent diagonal fair states. The final instrument measures the $O$ public output cells, including every public failure flag, with computational-basis projectors tensored with the identity on retained private workspace. Its nonselective sum is trace preserving on the full finite carrier; private source and workspace records remain in the unmeasured dilation. On the declared input class its public marginal is (8), with the exact deterministic extractor attached. Hence $\pi\hbar G_{\rm tot}$ bounds gate norm-action. Retained workspace supplies finite one-run execution; storage reuse has its own reset contract.

6. **Clock, service and implementation envelope.** Fix positive setup/ready/source/gate/readout durations $\tau_{\rm set},\tau_r,\tau_c,\tau_g,\tau_m$, a positive stage guard, and positive source-contract charges $E_{\rm set},e_r,e_c,e_g,e_m,P_0,p_r$. Use
$$
\begin{split}
T_{\rm prep}&=\tau_{\rm set}+R_{\rm bit}\tau_r+B_wQ_{\rm cfg}\tau_g,\\
\Delta_N&\ge20\tau_c+B_wQ_{\rm step}\tau_g+\tau_{\rm guard},\\
T_N&=T_{\rm prep}+N\Delta_N+B_wQ_{\rm ext}\tau_g+O(\tau_g+\tau_m),\\
E_N&=E_{\rm set}+R_{\rm bit}e_r+20Ne_c+G_{\rm tot}e_g+Oe_m
 +(P_0+R_{\rm bit}p_r)T_N,\qquad P_{\rm svc}=E_N/T_N.
\end{split}
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.21}
$$
The stage program puts forecast commitment before fresh source generation. Nominal stage and release labels are public; residual implementation timing has its separately registered bound and stays private in a comparison using those fixed labels. Preparation, controller, full retained storage, extraction, final readout and maintenance are charged. The common per-primitive service law fixes these physical costs over all configurations and both protocols; equality of a Boolean gate count alone is not used to infer switching heat.

For a uniform source trace-distance error $\epsilon_{\rm src}$ and uniform half-diamond primitive/readout errors $\epsilon_h$, including retained ancillas and all failure outcomes, the full word discrepancy obeys
$$
 d_{\rm TV}(\widetilde{\mathcal R},\mathcal R)
 \le\epsilon_N:=\min\{1,\epsilon_{\rm src}+\sum_h\epsilon_h\}.
\tag{P.8.9a.12.10d.22}
$$
Decode an observed score word by the bounded utility $\min\{1,\max\{0,T/128\}\}$, retaining its original integer and failure flags; this equals the raw loss on every ideal admitted run. Every cylinder probability and each mean of this bounded score or a loss flag differs by at most $\epsilon_N$. Replace $\eta$ by $\eta+\epsilon_N$ in the ideal-cylinder exponent bound after sampling iid implemented runs, provided that sum is below $8^{-n}$. The same complete timing/record cut is required in this comparison. The finite word error does not identify an arbitrary perturbed infinite-time process with the ideal cascade.

*Proof.*
There are $\binom{10}{2}=45$ integer compositions in (1). Decoder enumeration gives exactly four, three and one equiprobable teacher words. Expanding the proper loss gives, for every probability vector $a$,
$$
\mathbb E_p L(a,Y)
=\frac12\left(1-\|p\|_2^2+\|a-p\|_2^2\right).
$$
Here $\|p\|_2^2=26/64$, which proves (3). A nonzero integer vector $A-A_*$ with coordinate sum zero has squared norm at least two. The candidates $(3,4,1)$ and $(3,3,2)$ attain two, so the gap is exactly $1/64$. The setup objective $\sum_i c_iT_i(A)$ is $1024R(A)$, with denominator independent of the candidate. Its finite enumeration therefore implements the unique selected tuple. Replacing the decoder counts by any other nonnegative integer triple $C$ summing to eight replaces this minimum by $C$; the selector uses the source and score, without a spectrum input. Equation (4) compares the two forecasts against the same independent teacher. Once the first update has committed, the two subsequent raw forecasts coincide. For example, from $A=(3,3,2)$ the gain is negative when $Y=3$ and positive when $Y=1$, although its expectation is $1/64$.

The two finite protocols and their registered restrictions form a finite response presheaf. The one-symbol frozen address response has the distinct labels $0,3,7$ with probabilities $A_i/8$, and hence identifies the candidate. Risks and common service power consequently descend to its quotient. The cone and all positive scalarizations in (5) satisfy Definition D.1f. Their first coordinate has a strict unique minimum and the second is constant, which proves selection for every retained positive weighting. The service count includes selection computation in both protocols; protocol choice changes which retained tuple drives the sampler, with fixed-duration padding.

The maximum categorical score is one: $\|a-e_Y\|^2\le2$ on the probability simplex. Thus $0\le T\le128$, and exactly $T$ of the $128$ verifier words accept. Distinct draws are independent conditional on the teacher and forecasts, which gives (8). Summing both Bernoulli kernels, then the source factors at each stage, gives total probability one. The source-word refinement is obtained by retaining all twenty fair bits at every stage; all computations are deterministic functions of them and the original configuration. This proves the full finite word and its dilation, including the score correlations and sentinel cases.

Induction on the integer recursion proves (7). Composing the similarities in the chronological word order gives the cylinder hull $[X_j,X_j+8^{-j}]$. The two adjacent first-level hull gaps are $1/4$ and $3/8$; $0$ and $1$ belong to the attractor, so the smaller distance is attained. This establishes the strong-separation premise and injective infinite coding. In the selected protocol the active register is $A_*$ throughout, so independent address draws have law $p^{\otimes N}$. The cylinder mass in (9) and the common-tape prefix map follow. The unique product measure on infinite addresses pushes forward through the convergent digit series to the separated attractor. Theorems P.8.9a.12.10 and P.8.9a.12.10a therefore apply to that response carrier. Their finite partition calculation gives $Z_q(8^{-n})=(\sum_i p_i^q)^n$ for every real $q$, and (9) follows. Finite point representatives locate cylinders; the inverse-limit coding owns the infinite measure.

We prove the uniform window estimate directly. For distributions $x,y$ on $b$ symbols with total variation $t$, couple them with disagreement probability $t$. With disagreement indicator $E$, the conditional-entropy chain rule gives
$$
|H(x)-H(y)|\le H(E)+t\ln b
\le t\ln(e/t)+t\ln b.
$$
The first inequality follows from $H(X)-H(Y)\le H(X\mid Y)$ and its reverse, then conditioning on $E$; when $E=0$, the symbol is determined. Entropy also lies in $[0,\ln b]$. This proves the modulus $\Omega_b$, which is nondecreasing on $[0,1]$.

For the lower bound choose an entropy maximizer $x_*$ in the compact fiber $\ell\cdot x=\alpha$. Round its first $b-1$ coordinates downward to multiples of $1/n$ and assign the remainder to the last coordinate. The resulting type $x^{(n)}$ has total variation at most $\min\{1,(b-1)/n\}=t_n$. For any two probability vectors, the change of the mean of numbers in an interval of span $D$ is at most $D$ times total variation. Hence $|\ell\cdot x^{(n)}-\alpha|\le Dt_n$, and this type is included in the registered window. Proposition P.8.9a.12.10c and the entropy modulus give
$$

\ge nH(x_*)-n\Omega_b(t_n)-b\ln(n+1).
$$
The constrained entropy identity $H(x_*)=f(\alpha)\ln r$ proves the lower half of (12), as well as positivity of the count.

For the upper bound let $x$ be any included type and $\alpha'=\ell\cdot x$. If $\alpha'>\alpha$, let $F_-$ be the indices at level $\ell_-$. Choose a distribution $z$ on this face equal to the normalized restriction of $x$ there when its mass is positive, and arbitrary there otherwise. Set
$$

 u=\frac{\alpha'-\alpha}{\alpha'-\ell_-}.
$$
The denominator is positive and $0\le u\le1$. Then $\ell\cdot y=\alpha$ and
$$
 d_{\rm TV}(x,y)=u[1-x(F_-)]
 \le\frac{\alpha'-\alpha}{g},
$$
since $\alpha'-\ell_-\ge g[1-x(F_-)]$. The case $\alpha'<\alpha$ uses the maximum-level face and the same proof. Equality of the two means uses $y=x$. Thus $H(x)\le f(\alpha)\ln r+\Omega_b(\min\{1,\delta/g\})$. Every type contributes at most $e^{nH(x)}$, and there are at most $(n+1)^b$ types. Summing gives the upper half of (12). The proof treats endpoints and repeated extreme levels without a uniqueness assumption. When all levels are equal, every word is in the sole attainable fiber and its count is $b^n$.

For our source the three levels and span in (13) follow by logarithm arithmetic. Their successive gaps are $\ln(4/3)/\ln8$ and $\ln3/\ln8$; the first is smaller and positive. This lower bound can be used in a fully rational upper error certificate. Since $t_n\to0$, $\delta_n\to0$ and $\Omega_b$ is continuous at zero, both errors tend to zero uniformly over the complete attainable interval.

The coefficient/query error changes a type's distance from its queried center by at most $\rho_\ell+\rho_\alpha$. The two inclusions of type sets prove (14). Applying (12) at the two window widths gives its stated error bounds. No undecidable comparison of exact logarithmic boundary values is needed: the implemented dyadic window is an exact integer inequality, with uncertainty assigned by the sandwich.

To justify the rational implementation, integrate the nonnegative geometric series for $2/(1-z^2)$ from zero to $z$. Summing the tail and replacing every denominator by its first one gives (15). **Reference:** Theorem 23 (Section 7), Theorem Z.2 (Appendix Z, Section Z.3.3)

Assume the (O1)–(O3), (FC) realization class of Theorem 15; mutually perfectly distinguishable Hilbert representatives for its visited contexts; and Theorem Z.2's minimal-branch hypothesis that every admissible candidate with $d_0>8$ has an admissible eight-dimensional comparator in the same optimization class with the identical registered protocol-response family and identical non-support ledger entries, but strictly lower maintained-support cost. $$

*Proof.* Theorem 15 gives $N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}=8$ on the assumed (O1)–(O3), (FC) class. Perfectly distinguishable quantum states have pairwise orthogonal nonzero supports. Choosing one nonzero vector from each of the eight supports gives eight pairwise orthogonal, hence linearly independent, vectors, so $d_0\ge8$. The admissible eight-state comparator in Theorem Z.2 has the same registered response and strictly lower maintained-support cost, so no candidate with $d_0>8$ minimizes the total PCE potential on the minimal branch. Three structural constraints determine $d_0 = 8$ on the minimal branch:

3. **PCE minimality:** Under Theorem Z.2's registered same-response comparator and strict maintained-support cost, every $d_0>8$ representative is matched by a strictly cheaper eight-dimensional representative and is therefore excluded from the minimal branch.

Therefore the saturating minimal-branch value is $d_0 = 8$.

**Hurwitz coherence check.** Finite-dimensional unital real division algebras with a multiplicative norm are the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions or octonions, of dimensions 1, 2, 4, 8, respectively (Theorem Z.3). The value $d_0 = 8$ therefore also coincides with the maximal normed-division-algebra dimension. This is a secondary algebraic coherence check, not an independent upper-bound proof inside PU.

Hence $d_0=2a^2$ holds numerically on their conjunction. It is a consistency identity, not a second derivation from SPAP tensor structure and not a mutual-determination theorem. $\square$

**Epistemic Status:** Conditional framework theorem on the stated Theorem-15 Hilbert-carrier and Theorem-Z.2 minimality branch.

## P.13.2 The Interface Mode Structure

### Theorem P.13.5 (P.13 Interface-Branch QFI Mode Count)

**Reference:** Theorem Z.5 (Appendix Z, Section Z.7.2)

At the PCE-Attractor $\rho_0$, the number of QFI-active interface modes is:
$$M = 2ab = 24$$

The QFI metric on the interface subspace is isotropic.

*Proof.*

**Step 1 (Generator decomposition).** The $d_0^2 = 64$ generators of $\mathfrak{u}(8)$ decompose under the $a|b$ partition:

| Block | Dimension | QFI Status |
|-------|-----------|------------|
| AA | $a^2 = 4$ | Inactive: $(p_j - p_k)^2 = 0$ for $j,k \in A$ |
| BB | $b^2 = 36$ | Excluded: $p_j + p_k = 0$ for $j,k \in B$ (not in QFI sum) |
| AB + BA | $2ab = 24$ | Active: $p_j + p_k > 0$ and $(p_j - p_k)^2 > 0$ |

**Step 2 (QFI formula).** For $\rho = \sum_i p_i |i\rangle\langle i|$, the quantum Fisher information is [Braunstein & Caves 1994]: $$F_Q[\rho, G] = 2\sum_{i,j: p_i + p_j > 0} \frac{(p_i - p_j)^2}{p_i + p_j}|\langle i|G|j\rangle|^2$$

**Step 3 (Eigenvalues of $\rho_0$).**
- Active indices $A = \{1,2\}$: $p_j = 1/2$
- Inactive indices $B = \{3,...,8\}$: $p_k = 0$

**Step 4 (Interface contribution).** For $j \in A$, $k \in B$:
$$\frac{(p_j - p_k)^2}{p_j + p_k} = \frac{(1/2)^2}{1/2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

**Step 5 (Mode count).** There are $ab = 12$ complex pairs $(j,k)$ with $j \in A$, $k \in B$. Including both symmetric and antisymmetric real combinations:
$$M = 2 \times ab = 24$$

**Step 6 (Isotropy).** The isotropy group $H=S(U(a)\times U(b))$ acts on the interface space $V=\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbb C^b,\mathbb C^a)$ by $(A,B):X\mapsto AXB^{-1}$. This action has the same image as the full $U(a)\times U(b)$ action: multiplying both $A$ and $B$ by a common phase leaves $AXB^{-1}$ unchanged, and that phase can always be chosen to make the product of determinants one. On $V\cong\mathbb C^a\otimes(\mathbb C^b)^*$, the left and right unitary actions generate the matrix units in both factors, so their joint complex commutant consists only of scalars. The central phase subgroup acts by all complex phases on $V$; consequently an invariant real symmetric quadratic form is the real part of an invariant Hermitian form. Its associated self-adjoint intertwiner is therefore a real scalar multiple of the identity. Since the QFI metric is $H$-invariant (Petz 1996b), we have:
$$g_{\text{QFI}}|_{\text{interface}} = \lambda \cdot I_{24}$$

for some $\lambda > 0$. $\square$

### Theorem P.13.5a (Geometric Interpretation of Mode Count)

**Reference:** Theorem Z.6.3a (Appendix Z, Section Z.6.3)

The orbit of the PCE-Attractor state under unitary conjugation is:
$$
\mathcal{O}_{\rho_0} \cong U(d_0)/(U(a) \times U(b)) \cong \text{Gr}(a, d_0) = \text{Gr}(2,8)
$$

a compact Hermitian symmetric space with:
- Complex dimension: $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} = ab = 12$
- Real dimension: $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} = 2ab = 24 = M$

*Proof.* Write
$$
\rho_0 = \begin{pmatrix} \rho_a & 0 \\ 0 & 0_b \end{pmatrix},
$$
where $\rho_a=I_a/a$ has rank $a$ and the zero operator $0_b$ acts on a space of dimension $b=d_0-a$ but has rank zero. The two eigenspaces have eigenvalues $1/a$ and $0$. A unitary $U\in U(d_0)$ preserves $\rho_0$ under conjugation if and only if it preserves both eigenspaces. Therefore the isotropy subgroup is exactly the block-diagonal subgroup
$$
U(a)\times U(b) \subset U(d_0).
$$
Hence the conjugation orbit is the homogeneous space
$$
\mathcal O_{\rho_0} \cong U(d_0)/(U(a)\times U(b)).
$$

The orbit is naturally identified with the set of rank-$a$ orthogonal projectors, equivalently the set of $a$-dimensional complex subspaces of $\mathbb C^{d_0}$. That set is the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(a,d_0)$, giving
$$
\mathcal O_{\rho_0} \cong \mathrm{Gr}(a,d_0).
$$
For $a=2$ and $d_0=8$, this is $\mathrm{Gr}(2,8)$.

Finally,
$$
\dim_{\mathbb R} U(n)=n^2,
$$
so
$$
\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathcal O_{\rho_0}
=
d_0^2-a^2-b^2
=
(a+b)^2-a^2-b^2
=
2ab.
$$
Since the Grassmannian is a complex manifold, its complex dimension is half of its real dimension:
$$
\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathrm{Gr}(a,d_0)=ab.
$$
Substituting $a=2$ and $b=6$ gives $\dim_{\mathbb C}=12$ and $\dim_{\mathbb R}=24=M$. $\square$

**Epistemic Status:** Standard mathematical fact about Grassmannians.

## P.13.3 Multi-Constraint Convergence

### <a id="theorem-p136-convergence-at-m-24"></a>Theorem P.13.6 (Convergence at M = 24)

The value $M = 24$ satisfies multiple independent mathematical constraints:

| Constraint | Statement | Verification |
|------------|-----------|--------------|
| C1 (Algebraic) | $M = 2ab$ with $a + b = d_0$, $a = 2$ | $2 \times 2 \times 6 = 24$ ✓ |
| C2 (Geometric) | Kissing number $K(4) = 24$ | (Musin 2008) ✓ |
| C3 (Coding) | One coordinate-permutation equivalence class of binary linear $[24,12,8]$ codes exists; retained selection additionally requires $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{dist}}$ | (Pless 1968); Theorems Z.13 and Z.13b ✓ |
| C4 (Packing) | Optimal sphere packing in dimension 24 | (Cohn et al. 2017) ✓ |
| C5 (Unimodular) | Positive-definite even unimodular lattices require $\dim \equiv 0 \pmod{8}$; this does not select $M$ | (Zagier 2008, Proposition 12, p. 33) ✓ |
| C6 (Modular comparison only) | For $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$ and $\Delta=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}$, $\eta^{24}=\Delta$; this does not constrain $M$ | (Serre 1973, Ch. VII, §4.4, Thm. 6), after normalization conversion ✓ |

*Proof of individual constraints.*

**C1:** On the conjunction of Theorem P.13.4's active-kernel gates, Theorem Z.2's carrier comparator, and Theorem P.13.5's QFI tangent branch, $(a,b,M)=(2,6,24)$. The structural value $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ is one input to the active-kernel capacity gate, not a physical entropy cause of $M=24$.

**C2:** The kissing number $K(D)$ is the maximum number of non-overlapping unit spheres that can simultaneously touch a central unit sphere in $D$ dimensions. $K(4)=24$ (Musin 2008). For comparison: $K(3)=12$, $K(8)=240$, and standard bounds place $K(5)$ between $40$ and $44$ (Mittelmann and Vallentin 2010; Boyvalenkov et al. 2012).

**C3:** The extended binary Golay code $\mathcal G_{24}$ has parameters $[24,12,8]$, and every binary linear code with those parameters is coordinate-permutation equivalent to it (Pless 1968). This is a classification theorem; retained selection is the separate $\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{dist}}$ gate of Theorem Z.13b.

**C4:** The Leech lattice $\Lambda_{24}$ achieves optimal sphere packing density in 24 dimensions (Cohn et al. 2017).

**C5:** Positive-definite even unimodular lattices exist only in dimensions divisible by $8$ (Zagier 2008, Proposition 12, p. 33). The positive-definite hypothesis is the one used by the rank-$24$ lattice branch here.

**C6:** Put $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$, $\eta(\tau)=q^{1/24}\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)$, and define the normalized $\Delta(\tau)=q\prod_{n\ge1}(1-q^n)^{24}$. Then $\eta^{24}=\Delta$ by the product definitions. Serre uses a differently normalized discriminant: his Chapter VII, §4.4, Theorem 6 gives $\Delta_{\mathrm{Serre}}=(2\pi)^{12}\Delta$ (Serre 1973). His one-dimensional weight-12 cusp-space result supplies uniqueness once the leading $q$ coefficient is fixed to $1$. This identity is a modular-form comparison involving $24$, not a condition selecting the QFI mode count $M$. $\square$

<a id="remark-on-interpretation"></a>**Remark on Interpretation.** On the conjunction of Theorem Z.1's active-kernel branch and Theorem Z.2's carrier branch, $(a,b)=(2,6)$; Theorem Z.5 then gives $M=2ab=24$. The exponent $24$ in $\eta(\tau)^{24}=\Delta(\tau)$ is an independent modular-form fact. Identifying the QFI mode carrier with the modular-form construction, or PCE optimization with mathematical extremality, requires an explicit common-carrier bridge.

### Selection Principle P.13.7 (Fixed-Normalization Even-Lattice Admissibility)

On the $M=24$ lattice branch, let

with the positive-definite QFI metric of Theorem P.13.5. A lattice-carrier certificate consists of a full-rank discrete subgroup $\Lambda\subset V_{24}$ representing the retained vacuum-displacement labels and a positive length unit $\ell_{\mathrm{lat}}$ fixed before candidates are compared. Write

\qquad

$$
Candidate-dependent rescaling is not allowed. The even branch is the exact admissible class
$$

:=
\left\{

\ q_0(v)\in2\mathbb Z\ \text{for every }v\in\Lambda

*Argument.* If $\Lambda\in\mathcal A_{24}^{\mathrm{even}}$, then for every $v,w\in\Lambda$,

2\langle v,w\rangle_0
=

Hence $\langle v,w\rangle_0\in\mathbb Z$, so the even-norm condition also proves integrality in the same fixed normalization. This is an exact admissibility test. Neither QFI isotropy nor Theorem E.2's real-valued capacity bound supplies the lattice-carrier certificate or the condition $q_0(\Lambda)\subset2\mathbb Z$. $\square$

### Selection Principle P.13.8 (Fixed-Metric Unimodularity Certificate)

For $\Lambda\in\mathcal A_{24}^{\mathrm{even}}$, define the dual with respect to the same fixed inner product by
$$
\Lambda^*
:=
\{x\in V_{24}:\langle x,v\rangle_0\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }v\in\Lambda\}.
$$
Let $G_\Lambda=(\langle b_i,b_j\rangle_0)_{i,j=1}^{24}$ be the Gram matrix of any $\mathbb Z$-basis of $\Lambda$. The unimodular branch is
$$
\mathcal A_{24}^{\mathrm{EU}}
:=
\{\Lambda\in\mathcal A_{24}^{\mathrm{even}}:\det G_\Lambda=1\}.
$$

*Argument.* Evenness gives integrality by Selection Principle P.13.7, hence $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda^*$. Standard lattice duality gives
$$
[\Lambda^*:\Lambda]=\det G_\Lambda
=
\operatorname{covol}_0(\Lambda)^2.
$$
Therefore
$$
\det G_\Lambda=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
[\Lambda^*:\Lambda]=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Lambda=\Lambda^*.
$$
Thus self-duality is checked by one determinant in the fixed metric; it is not inferred from storing $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda^*$ as independent data. $\square$

**Epistemic Status:** Established lattice algebra. Membership in $\mathcal A_{24}^{\mathrm{EU}}$ is the registered even-unimodular branch certificate.

### Selection Principle P.13.9 (Finite Niemeier Gaussian-Cost Comparison)

Let

:=

be the set of isometry classes in the fixed positive-definite normalization. By the Niemeier classification, $\mathfrak N_{24}$ has exactly $24$ elements. Fix a registered $t>0$, put

u:=e^{2\pi i\tau}=e^{-2\pi t}\in(0,1),

and define

\Theta_\Lambda(\tau)
:=

The series converges absolutely. A Gaussian lattice-cost certificate is the exact restriction

of the descended PCE potential to $\mathfrak N_{24}$, where $V_0$ is class-independent and the equality includes every candidate-dependent lattice-sector term of Definition D.1. This is the Gaussian completely monotone pair cost appearing as a special case of Corollary R.4.2b.1.

=

Indeed, the $\theta$ series is a weight-$12$ modular form, the weight-$12$ space is spanned by $E_4^3$ and $\Delta$, and comparison of the coefficient of $u$ gives the displayed coefficient. Since

=
u\prod_{m=1}^{\infty}(1-u^m)^{24} >0,

the sign of every difference of Gaussian lattice costs is exactly the sign of the corresponding difference of root counts. Thus the ordering is independent of the registered values of $t>0$ and $\kappa_{\mathrm{lat}}>0$; no parameter is tuned to obtain the minimizer. $\square$

### Theorem P.13.10 (Unique Leech Minimizer on the Certified Niemeier Gaussian Branch)

**Reference:** Theorems R.4.6 and R.4.10 and Corollary R.4.2b.1 (Appendix R, Sections R.4.2.1.4, R.4.2.3, and R.4.2.4)

V_{\mathrm{lat}}([\Lambda])-V_{\mathrm{lat}}([\Lambda_{24}])

$$
\operatorname*{argmin}_{[\Lambda]\in\mathfrak N_{24}}
V_{\mathrm{lat}}([\Lambda])
=
\{[\Lambda_{24}]\}.
$$
Rootlessness is an output of the registered finite comparison, not an admissibility assumption. The selected lattice is even, unimodular, rootless, positive-definite, and rank $24$. $\square$

### Proposition P.13.6.1 (PCE-Attractor Scope and the Pure-Dilatation Obstruction)

$$

=x^\mu\partial_\mu\phi^*.
$$
The two-dimensional scale-to-conformal step used below therefore requires an independently stated exact-dilatation hypothesis for the two-dimensional theory.

*Proof.*

**Step 1 (Scope of the PCE minimum).** Definition D.1 defines
$$
V(x)=V_{op}(x)+V_{\mathrm{prop}}(x)-V_{\mathrm{benefit}}(x)+V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(x)
$$
on the complete admissible configuration space. Definition 15a requires this functional to attain its infimum and requires its quotient minimizer set to be a singleton. Since the minimization is constrained and may occur on the declared capacity boundary, these clauses do not imply an ambient equation $\nabla V=0$. Neither definition identifies $V$ with $S_{\mathrm{cont}}$ or supplies a transformation law for $S_{\mathrm{cont}}$ under spacetime dilatations.

**Step 2 (Virial stationarity).** Write $\phi^*_\varsigma(x)=\phi^*(\varsigma x)$. Theorem U.8a gives
$$
\left.\frac{d}{d\varsigma}S_{\mathrm{cont}}[\phi^*_\varsigma]\right|_{\varsigma=1}=0.
$$
This is first-variation stationarity along one curve and does not imply scale invariance or a Hessian zero mode.

**Step 3 (Exclusion of the exact critical family).** Set
$$
s=x^\mu\partial_\mu\phi^*.
$$
Theorem U.8c gives
$$
D^2S_{\mathrm{cont}}(\phi^*)[s,s]
=-4S_{\mathrm{kin}}(1)<0.
$$
Suppose that a smooth family of exact critical points with the displayed tangent existed. Theorem U.9 would give
$$
D^2S_{\mathrm{cont}}(\phi^*)[s,\eta]=0
$$
for every admissible test direction $\eta$. Taking $\eta=s$ contradicts the strict inequality. Hence no such family exists.

**Step 4 (Two-dimensional branch input).** The obstruction concerns the Definition U.4 action and the pure-coordinate tangent required by Theorem U.9. It makes no assertion about the weighted-conformal tangent of Proposition U.73 or about conformal critical points of other functionals. The exact dilatation invariance consumed by the two-dimensional scale-to-conformal argument is an independent hypothesis of Proposition P.13.6.2. $\square$

### Proposition P.13.6.2 (Conformal Structure on the Exact-Scale Two-Dimensional Boundary Branch)

Assume a two-dimensional local unitary theory with exact dilatation invariance, Poincaré invariance, a discrete non-negative spectrum of scaling dimensions, a conserved stress tensor whose virial current is improvable, and a chiral state-field correspondence satisfying the VOA vacuum, locality, translation, and grading axioms. On this branch, the vacuum chiral algebra is a vertex operator algebra.

*Proof.*

**Step 1 (Registered two-dimensional scale hypothesis).** Exact dilatation invariance of the two-dimensional theory is a hypothesis of this proposition. Proposition P.13.6.1 supplies no exact dilatation family, and its conclusion concerns the Definition U.4 continuum action rather than the two-dimensional theory assumed here. The conserved stress tensor has an improvable virial current by hypothesis; after improvement, $T^\mu_\mu=0$.

**Step 2 (Two-dimensional boundary branch).** On a separately certified $3+1$ Lorentzian conformal-boundary branch, assume that the relevant conformal boundary is three-dimensional. The two-dimensional boundary branch further assumes that the relevant CFT lives on a two-dimensional chiral slice: the worldsheet swept by string-like excitations, or equivalently, the Riemann surface on which modular transformations act. The 24 interface modes (Theorem P.13.5) provide the target-space degrees of freedom for this 2D structure. The identification of the QFI interface modes with the 2D chiral target-space coordinates is the content of this branch.

**Step 3 (Conditional local conformal structure).** By Step 1 the improved stress tensor has zero trace. In two-dimensional light-cone coordinates, its conservation and vanishing trace give $\partial_-T_{++}=0$ and $\partial_+T_{--}=0$, so the two stress components are chiral on this branch. The displayed Virasoro mode relation, $[L_m,L_n]=(m-n)L_{m+n}+\frac{c}{12}(m^3-m)\delta_{m+n,0}$, additionally uses the conformal-vector/OPE structure of the chiral VOA assumed in the proposition; it is not a consequence of scale invariance alone. This conditional argument does not invoke an exact Polchinski (1988) theorem statement.

**Step 4 (Registered chiral algebra).** The assumed chiral state-field correspondence obeys the VOA axioms, so its state space is a VOA. This conclusion is not inferred from dilation symmetry alone. $\square$

### Proposition P.13.6.3 (Central Charge on the Chiral 24-Boson Branch)

On the chiral 24-boson branch, in which each of the $M = 24$ QFI-active interface modes is realized as an independent chiral bosonic degree of freedom in the effective 2D theory of Proposition P.13.6.2, the central charge of the PCE-optimal CFT is:
$$c = M = 24.$$

*Proof.*

The assignment "each QFI mode $\mapsto$ one $c = 1$ chiral boson" is the branch rule; the mode count $M = 24$ is theorem-level (Theorem P.13.5).

$$c = M \times 1 = 24. \quad \square$$

<a id="remark-p13631-branch-dependence-of-the-scale-to-voa-chain"></a>**Remark P.13.6.3.1 (Branch Dependence of the Scale-to-VOA Chain).** The VOA endpoint $c = 24$ depends on three branch assumptions stated in Propositions P.13.6.2–P.13.6.3, with Proposition P.13.6.1 delimiting their functional scope:

### Proposition P.13.6.4 (Conditional PCE Comparison of Chiral and Full Realizations)

Assume the branches of Propositions P.13.6.2–P.13.6.3 and suppose that the admissible class contains a holomorphic chiral realization $V$ and a full-CFT realization $W$ satisfying
$$
V_{\mathrm{benefit}}(V)=V_{\mathrm{benefit}}(W),
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{prop}}(V)=V_{\mathrm{prop}}(W),
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(V)\le V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(W),
\qquad
V_{\mathrm{op}}(V)<V_{\mathrm{op}}(W).
$$
Then PCE selects $V$ over $W$ within this two-candidate comparison.

*Proof.* With the PCE potential of Definition D.1,
$$
V_{\mathrm{PCE}}=V_{\mathrm{op}}+V_{\mathrm{prop}}-V_{\mathrm{benefit}}+V_{\mathrm{penalty}},
$$
the two equalities and two inequalities give
$$
\begin{aligned}
V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(V)-V_{\mathrm{PCE}}(W)
&=V_{\mathrm{op}}(V)-V_{\mathrm{op}}(W)\\
&\quad+V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(V)-V_{\mathrm{penalty}}(W)<0.
\end{aligned}
$$
Therefore $V$ has the smaller PCE potential among the two candidates. The proposition does not assert a universal factor-of-two relation between full and chiral CFT data. ∎

### Proposition P.13.6.5 (Conditional Modular Consistency)

Assume that the effective two-dimensional theory is defined on a torus with modulus $\tau\in\mathbb H$, that physically equivalent descriptions are identified under the mapping-class action of $SL_2(\mathbb Z)$, and that its partition function is a scalar function on the resulting moduli space. Then
$$
Z(\gamma\tau)=Z(\tau)
\qquad
\text{for every }\gamma\in SL_2(\mathbb Z).
$$
For a VOA character, the same scalar conclusion requires a nonnegatively graded, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, holomorphic branch (one irreducible module up to isomorphism) on which the one-dimensional character representation has trivial multiplier.

*Proof.* The first three hypotheses say precisely that $Z$ descends from $\mathbb H$ to the quotient $\mathbb H/SL_2(\mathbb Z)$. Hence it is constant on every group orbit, which is the displayed invariance. For a nonnegatively graded, rational, $C_2$-cofinite VOA, Miyamoto's modular-invariance theorem (Miyamoto 2004b, Theorem 5.5) and its rational semisimple case give a finite-dimensional $SL_2(\mathbb Z)$-invariant span of ordinary irreducible characters. Holomorphicity makes this span one-dimensional; the additional trivial-multiplier hypothesis makes its character invariant rather than merely covariant by a phase. No map from the flag perspective space to torus moduli follows without the torus and mapping-class hypotheses stated above. ∎

### Proposition P.13.6.7 (Cylinder Shift and Finite-Size Excitation Gaps)

On the calibrated holomorphic cylinder branch, let
$$
H=\frac{2\pi\hbar v}{L}(L_0-c/24)+E_{\mathrm{common}}I,
\qquad v>0,\quad L>0.
\tag{P.13.6.7.1}
$$
For $c=24$ the vacuum exponent is $-1$ for every compared holomorphic candidate. This common scalar shift changes neither eigenvectors nor energy differences. It cannot resolve a degeneracy or open an excitation gap.

The Leech lattice VOA has first positive conformal weight $1$, and the Moonshine module has first positive conformal weight $2$. Their cylinder excitation gaps, at the same $v$ and $L$, are
$$
\operatorname{gap}(H_\Lambda)=\frac{2\pi\hbar v}{L},
\qquad
\operatorname{gap}(H_\natural)=\frac{4\pi\hbar v}{L}.
\tag{P.13.6.7.2}
$$
Both tend to zero as $L\to\infty$ at fixed $v$.

*Proof.* Replacing $H$ by $H+\alpha I$ replaces each eigenvalue by the same additive constant, leaving every eigenvalue difference and every eigenspace unchanged. Theorem P.13.14 gives twenty-four nonzero Leech weight-one currents, while its nonnegative integral grading has no weight strictly between $0$ and $1$. The Moonshine character of Theorem P.13.26 has zero weight-one coefficient and positive weight-two coefficient $196884$. Multiplication of these smallest positive weights by $2\pi\hbar v/L$ proves (P.13.6.7.2), and its limit is immediate. ∎

The Leech lattice-momentum norm gap and this full VOA excitation gap are different spectra: the Heisenberg currents remain at weight one in the lattice VOA. The involutive orbifold removes weight one on the stated Moonshine branch and doubles the finite-circumference gap. A uniform thermodynamic bulk gap is not furnished by either cylinder spectrum.

### Proposition P.13.6.8 (Equilibrium Current Test for the Chiral Source)

Consider an infinitely extended, isolated quasi-one-dimensional lattice system with finite-range interactions and uniformly bounded local Hamiltonian terms. Its transverse directions are compact; the net current is measured through a cut of the infinite system. Assume clustering Gibbs states and, for local observables with support separation $d$, a Kubo-pairing bound
$$
\left|\langle\!\langle A;B\rangle\!\rangle_\beta\right|
\le C_{A,B}(1+d)^{-1-\eta},\qquad \eta>0,
\tag{P.13.6.8.K}
$$
The decay exponent and constants are uniform over the translated local observables and bounded finite-range one-sided Hamiltonian deformations used in the no-current argument, throughout the same admitted equilibrium continuation. The associated linear responses are assumed to exist. Here
$$
\langle\!\langle A;B\rangle\!\rangle_\beta
=\frac1\beta\int_0^\beta\langle A_uB\rangle_\beta\,du
-\langle A\rangle_\beta\langle B\rangle_\beta,
\qquad A_u=e^{uH}Ae^{-uH},
$$
interpreted in finite volume and its admitted thermodynamic limit. Assume continuation to infinite temperature through that same equilibrium class with these bounds. The no-current theorem of Kapustin and Spodyneiko [Kapustin & Spodyneiko 2019, Sections “Lattice systems,” “Energy currents in lattice systems,” and “Applications”] gives zero net equilibrium energy current. Assume further that a response-preserving continuum limit identifies that microscopic energy current with the CFT stress-energy current. Such a source cannot realize a unitary CFT with $c_R\ne c_L$.

*Proof.* With restored physical units, the equilibrium CFT current is
$$
J_E(T)=\frac{\pi k_B^2T^2}{12\hbar}(c_R-c_L).
\tag{P.13.6.8.1}
$$
The no-current theorem makes its microscopic limit zero for $T>0$. The current identification therefore forces $c_R-c_L=0$. A holomorphic $c=24$ branch with orientation $(c_R,c_L)=(24,0)$ would instead give $J_E(T)=2\pi k_B^2T^2/\hbar\ne0$. Reversing orientation changes the sign and leaves the contradiction. ∎

This conclusion applies to the specified isolated microscopic source class and continuum-current identification. Proposition P.13.30b constructs a chiral conformal-net source on its stated mathematical domain; it does not assume the isolated bounded-term lattice realization excluded here. A higher-dimensional bulk/edge completion, compensating low-energy chirality, or another specified departure from the hypotheses is part of the nominated physical implementation. Its candidate-dependent resources enter the complete comparison in Proposition P.13.6.4 and Theorem P.13.28c.

Two separate checks distinguish spectral normalization from chirality. For a unitary periodic CFT with common propagation velocity $v$, vacuum conformal weights zero, and a correctly subtracted nonuniversal extensive ground energy,
$$
E_0(L)-e_\infty L
=-\frac{\pi\hbar v}{12L}(c_R+c_L)+o(L^{-1}),
\tag{P.13.6.8.2}
$$
whereas the corresponding infinite-line thermal branch has
$$
J_E(T)-J_E(0)
=\frac{\pi k_B^2T^2}{12\hbar}(c_R-c_L)+o(T^2).
\tag{P.13.6.8.3}
$$
For the exact CFT, (P.13.6.8.2) follows by evaluating
$$
H=\frac{2\pi\hbar v}{L}
\left(L_0+\overline L_0-\frac{c_R+c_L}{24}\right)
\tag{P.13.6.8.4}
$$
on its vacuum; the remainder records the admitted microscopic scaling limit. Equation (P.13.6.8.3) is the thermal current law (P.13.6.8.1) on that limit. The holomorphic $c=24$ branch has sum and oriented difference $(24,24)$; paired left/right $c=24$ sectors have $(48,0)$. Matching a finite-size vacuum coefficient alone therefore does not determine chirality. The energy subtraction, velocity, temperature, boundary conditions, current, and scaling limits in these checks belong to the same implementation.

Finally, for an integer-graded holomorphic character the transformation $\tau\mapsto\tau+1$ contributes the phase $e^{-2\pi ic/24}$. At $c=24$ it equals $1$, because every integer weight contributes $e^{2\pi in}=1$. This scalar torus multiplier does not change $c_R-c_L$. Scalar modular consistency in Proposition P.13.6.5 and the equilibrium-current source test above are distinct conditions.
