<a id="remark-p141m5-compression-trajectory-schema-for-an-accepted-registry-snapshot"></a>**Remark P.14.1m.5 (Compression-Trajectory Schema for an Accepted Registry Snapshot).** Let $\varnothing\ne\mathcal C^{(0)}$ be the finite set of records in a populated registry instance accepted by Algorithm P.14.1m.0. Registered recovery maps contain identities and are closed under composition. A syntactic record-count compression step chooses $A\subseteq\mathcal C$ with $|A|\ge2$ and replaces it by one fresh record $r_A\notin\mathcal C\setminus A$ carrying maps that recover every member of $A$, while preserving every accepted strict certificate and status assignment. Thus
$$
\mathcal C'=(\mathcal C\setminus A)\cup\{r_A\},
\qquad
\mu(\mathcal C):=|\mathcal C|,
\qquad
\mu(\mathcal C')=\mu(\mathcal C)-|A|+1<\mu(\mathcal C).
$$
Every maximal trajectory from $\mathcal C^{(0)}$ therefore terminates after at most $|\mathcal C^{(0)}|-1$ steps. Composable recovery maps ensure that each terminal record recovers the initial records below it. A current plural configuration admits a singleton compression only when an admissible fresh record recovers every record in that current configuration and preserves all accepted statuses. Recovery of the initial snapshot alone does not prove recovery of extra data introduced by intermediate records. Consequently a terminal configuration is singleton or admits no further registered compression step. This is a record-count theorem, not a decrease of information, Kolmogorov complexity, PCE cost, or physical resources; any such interpretation requires its own cost-decrease certificate. Candidate records already named in the manuscript include $\mathfrak L_{\mathrm{PU}}$, $\mathfrak Z_{\mathrm{PU}}$, $\mathfrak C_{\Omega}$ when its projection ledger is accepted, and the marked-arena package; their admissibility requires the declared current-record recovery certificate. The recurrent-ledger status of Theorem R.3.5e.3 and the open parent-source status of Remark R.3.5e.5 retain their separate domains.

*Proof.* Freshness of $r_A$ gives the displayed cardinality identity. Each step decreases the positive integer $\mu$ by at least one, so no trajectory contains more than $|\mathcal C^{(0)}|-1$ steps. Induction using identity and composable recovery maps recovers every initial record below each current record. Maximality gives the terminal alternatives. Status preservation is part of admissibility and creates no new physical postulate, strict certificate, operator, bridge condition, or acceptance gate. ∎

<a id="definition-p141m6-complete-alternative-artifact-status-datum"></a>**Definition P.14.1m.6 (Complete Alternative-Artifact Status Datum).** Let
$$
\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{PU}}
=(\mathcal V,\mathcal E,\kappa_{\mathcal V},\sigma,
\rho,\beta,\theta,\gamma,\delta,\zeta)
$$
be a registry accepted by Algorithm P.14.1m.0. Put
$$
\mathsf T_{\bot}
=
\{\bot_{\mathrm{unavailable}},\textsf{open},
\textsf{certificate-pending},\textsf{closed}\},
\qquad
\bot_{\mathrm{unavailable}}
\prec\textsf{open}
\prec\textsf{certificate-pending}
\prec\textsf{closed},
\tag{P.14.1m.6a}
$$
and write $\sqcap$ and $\sqcup$ for meet and join in this finite chain. The value $\bot_{\mathrm{unavailable}}$ records that no accepted artifact supports the vertex after the imposed change. Definition P.14.1m retains its three-element closure-status codomain; the bottom value belongs only to the counterfactual calculation.

A **complete alternative-artifact status datum** for this registry is a finite record
$$

=
(\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{PU}},\{\mathcal A(S)\}_{S\in\mathcal V},
\operatorname{par},u,\xi),
\tag{P.14.1m.6b}
$$
where $\mathcal A(S)$ is the finite nonempty set of every accepted proof-and-status artifact for $S$, $\operatorname{par}(a)\subseteq\mathcal V$ is the exact direct-parent set of artifact $a$, $u(a)\in\mathsf T_{\bot}\setminus\{\bot_{\mathrm{unavailable}}\}$ is the strongest local closure status justified by the artifact when all its direct parents are closed, and $\xi$ contains the source spans, source hashes, artifact hashes, proof objects, and checker records.

For an adopted, external, or otherwise parentless root, the source declaration together with its owning status record is its empty-parent artifact. This artifact records the root's source status and has no derivational parent.

The datum is accepted only when the finite checker verifies all of the following.

1. The registry, sources, artifacts, and proofs have one common frozen version and source snapshot.
2. For $a\in\mathcal A(S)$, every $R\in\operatorname{par}(a)$ has the parent-to-child edge $R\to S$. Conversely, every status-bearing edge into $S$ occurs in the direct-parent set of each artifact that uses it, and the union of the recorded artifact-parent relations is the status-bearing part of $\mathcal E$.

4. No accepted alternative artifact is omitted, and the original status is reconstructed exactly by

<a id="algorithm-p141m7-same-version-rejection-and-status-recalculation"></a>**Algorithm P.14.1m.7 (Same-Version Rejection and Status Recalculation).** Let $\mathfrak K$ be accepted, and let
$$
\eta:F\longrightarrow\mathsf T_{\bot},
\qquad
\eta(S)\preceq\sigma(S),
\tag{P.14.1m.7a}
$$
be a finite forced-status map whose value at every $S\in F$ is supplied by the accepted rejection, no-go, or status rule that owns the imposed change. Process $\mathcal V$ in a topological order of $\mathcal E$. For every artifact put
$$
q_\eta(a)
=
u(a)\sqcap
\bigsqcap_{R\in\operatorname{par}(a)}\sigma^\eta(R),
\tag{P.14.1m.7b}
$$
and define
$$
\sigma^\eta(S)
=
\begin{cases}
\eta(S),&S\in F,\\[1mm]
\displaystyle\bigsqcup_{a\in\mathcal A(S)}q_\eta(a),&S\notin F.
\end{cases}
\tag{P.14.1m.7c}
$$
The algorithm returns
$$
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{reaudit}}
=\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal E}(F),
\qquad
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{dem}}
=\{S:\sigma^\eta(S)\prec\sigma(S)\},
\qquad
\mathcal D_{\mathrm{drop}}
=\{S:\sigma^\eta(S)=\bot_{\mathrm{unavailable}}\}.
\tag{P.14.1m.7d}
$$
Here $\operatorname{Desc}_{\mathcal E}(F)$ is the reflexive descendant set of $F$ in the parent-to-child graph.
A surviving artifact with a weaker value contributes that weaker value to the join in (P.14.1m.7c), so the returned demotion set includes every surviving vertex whose strongest available status decreased.

<a id="theorem-p141m8-termination-exactness-and-alternative-artifact-preservation"></a>**Theorem P.14.1m.8 (Termination, Exactness, and Alternative-Artifact Preservation).** Algorithm P.14.1m.7 terminates and gives a unique map $\sigma^\eta$. For every vertex,

A registry snapshot that makes the recalculated status operative must delete the $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{drop}}$ vertices, update every affected $\rho$, $\beta$, $\theta$, $\gamma$, $\delta$, and $\zeta$ field, and pass Algorithm P.14.1m.0; Theorem P.14.1m.8 supplies the exact status calculation, while Algorithm P.14.1m.0 remains the acceptance gate for the resulting registry. ∎

```python
import json
from fractions import Fraction
from itertools import product
from math import comb

def native_component(reward, other, window, exponent, entropy_floor,
                     self_count, world_count, shared, world_overhead, budget,
                     mutation=None):
    q = Fraction(1, 64)
    f = sum(count * comb(weight, intersection) *
            comb(23 - weight, leader - intersection) *
            q ** (weight + leader - 2 * intersection) *
            (1 - q) ** (23 - weight - leader + 2 * intersection)
            for weight, count in ((7, 253), (11, 1288), (15, 506), (23, 1))
            for leader in range(4) for intersection in range(leader + 1))
    assert window > 0 and other >= 0 and reward > 2 * other / q
    assert 0 < f < 8855 * q ** 4 < q / 2
    gap = (reward * q / 2 - other) / window
    assert gap > 0
    assert exponent > 1 and entropy_floor > 0
    thermal = exponent * entropy_floor
    assert thermal > entropy_floor and world_overhead >= 0 and shared >= 0
    assert self_count >= 0 and world_count >= 0
    spent = shared + self_count + world_count * (thermal + world_overhead)
    assert spent <= budget

    domains = {'source': 3, 'decoded': 3, 'snapshot': 1, 'recovered': 1,
               'meter': 1, 'release': 2, 'forecast': 1, 'truth': 1,
               'world': 3}
    verifier = lambda x: (x[0] ^ x[1], x[0], 1 - x[1])
    edges = {
        ('source', 'decoded'): lambda x: (x[0] ^ x[1], x[1], x[2]),
        ('source', 'snapshot'): lambda x: (x[0],),
        ('source', 'forecast'): lambda x: (x[0] ^ x[1],),
        ('decoded', 'forecast'): lambda x: (x[0],),
        ('decoded', 'recovered'): lambda x: (x[0] ^ x[1],),
        ('snapshot', 'truth'): lambda x: x,
        ('recovered', 'truth'): lambda x: x,
        ('recovered', 'meter'): lambda x: x,
        ('meter', 'truth'): lambda x: x,
        ('meter', 'release'): lambda x: (x[0], 1),
        ('release', 'truth'): lambda x: (x[0],),
        ('source', 'world'): verifier,
        ('world', 'truth'): lambda x: (x[1],),
        ('world', 'forecast'): lambda x: (x[0],),
    }
    cells = {
        'forecast': (('source', 'forecast'), ('source', 'decoded', 'forecast')),
        'input': (('source', 'snapshot', 'truth'),
                  ('source', 'decoded', 'recovered', 'truth')),
        'commit': (('recovered', 'truth'), ('recovered', 'meter', 'truth')),
        'release': (('meter', 'truth'), ('meter', 'release', 'truth')),
        'world_forecast': (('source', 'world', 'forecast'), ('source', 'forecast')),
        'world_truth': (('source', 'world', 'truth'), ('source', 'snapshot', 'truth')),
    }
    if mutation == 'frame':
        edges['decoded', 'recovered'] = lambda x: (x[0],)
    if mutation == 'snapshot':
        edges['source', 'snapshot'] = lambda x: (1 - x[0],)
    if mutation == 'reverse':
        cells['commit'] = (('truth', 'recovered'), ('recovered', 'meter', 'truth'))
    if mutation == 'omit':
        del cells['commit']
    assert set(cells) == {'forecast', 'input', 'commit', 'release',
                          'world_forecast', 'world_truth'}
    marks = {'clock': 'common_source_service_address',
             'cut': 'exact_ready_terminal_forecast'}
    edge_marks = {edge: dict(marks) for edge in edges}
    if mutation == 'clock':
        edge_marks['meter', 'release']['clock'] = 'different_service_address'

    def route(path, word):
        for parent, child in zip(path, path[1:]):
            assert (parent, child) in edges and len(word) == domains[parent]
            assert edge_marks[parent, child] == marks
            word = edges[parent, child](word)
            assert len(word) == domains[child]
        return word

    tests = {}
    for name, (left, right) in cells.items():
        assert left[0] == right[0] and left[-1] == right[-1]
        tests[name] = []
        for word in product(range(2), repeat=domains[left[0]]):
            outputs = route(left, word), route(right, word)
            assert outputs[0] == outputs[1]
            tests[name].append([list(word), list(outputs[0])])

    def verify(report, meter, ready):
        if not ready:
            return ['failed_release', report]
        return [report, meter, int(report == meter)]

    joint = []
    for word in product(range(2), repeat=3):
        forecast, = route(('source', 'forecast'), word)
        truth, = route(('source', 'decoded', 'recovered', 'meter', 'release', 'truth'), word)
        world = verify(forecast, truth, 1)
        assert route(('source', 'world'), word) == tuple(world)
        assert route(('world', 'truth'), tuple(world)) == (word[0],)
        assert route(('world', 'forecast'), tuple(world)) == (word[0] ^ word[1],)
        assert world[-1] == 1 - word[1]
        assert verify(forecast, truth, 0) == ['failed_release', forecast]
        joint.append([list(word), world])

    fields = {
        'domains': domains,
        'edges': [list(edge) for edge in sorted(edges)],
        'edge_marks': [[list(edge), edge_marks[edge]] for edge in sorted(edges)],
        'edge_tables': [[list(edge),
                         [[list(word), list(route(edge, word))]
                          for word in product(range(2), repeat=domains[edge[0]])
                          if edge[0] != 'world' or word[2] == int(word[0] == word[1])]]
                        for edge in sorted(edges)],
        'cells': {key: [list(path) for path in value] for key, value in cells.items()},
        'marks': marks,
        'controls': {'link_gap': ['bound', str(gap)],
                     'reset_floor': ['bound', str(entropy_floor)],
                     'thermal_reserve': ['budget', str(thermal)]},
        'branch': {'q': str(q), 'qec_error': str(f), 'cost_bound': str(other),
                   'reward': str(reward), 'window': str(window),
                   'spent': str(spent), 'budget': str(budget),
                   'self_count': self_count, 'world_count': world_count},
        'comparisons': tests, 'joint': joint,
    }
    serialized = json.dumps(fields, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))
    assert json.loads(serialized) == fields
    return serialized
```

The six cell arrays contain thirty-six equalities, and the joint-verifier array contains eight additional complete comparisons. <a id="theorem-p141m11-reference-stable-quantum-link-overlap-on-the-native-registry"></a>**Theorem P.14.1m.11 (Reference-Stable Quantum Link Overlap on the Native Registry).** Retain the actual arbitrary-input LINK command of Theorem D.8.9c.25, its private independent classical Pauli flags, the joint syndrome and the calibrated one-use record. \tag{P.14.1m.11.1}

\tag{P.14.1m.11.2}

```python
from collections import Counter
from itertools import combinations, product
from math import comb

def verify_quantum_link(matrix, omit_phase=False):
    assert len(matrix) == 12
    assert all(len(row) == 12 and set(row) <= {'0', '1'} for row in matrix)
    extended = [int(row[::-1], 2) << 12 | (1 << i)
                for i, row in enumerate(matrix)]
    assert all((a & b).bit_count() % 2 == 0 for a, b in product(extended, repeat=2))
    shortened = [word >> 1 for word in extended[1:]]
    punctured = [word >> 1 for word in extended]

    def span(rows):
        words = [0]
        for row in rows:
            words += [word ^ row for word in words]
        assert len(words) == len(set(words))
        return set(words)

    def syndrome(word):
        return sum(((word & row).bit_count() % 2) << i
                   for i, row in enumerate(shortened))

    even = span(shortened)
    code = span(punctured)
    all_ones = (1 << 23) - 1
    assert len(even) == 2048 and len(code) == 4096
    assert all(syndrome(word) == 0 for word in code)
    assert even == {word for word in code if word.bit_count() % 2 == 0}
    assert code - even == {word ^ all_ones for word in even}
    leaders = {}
    for weight in range(4):
        for positions in combinations(range(23), weight):
            word = sum(1 << i for i in positions)
            label = syndrome(word)
            assert label not in leaders
            leaders[label] = word
    assert set(leaders) == set(range(2048))
    weights = Counter(word.bit_count() for word in code - even)
    assert weights == {7: 253, 11: 1288, 15: 506, 23: 1}
    assert (len(leaders) * len(code)) == (1 << 23)

    def image(a, b, unit):
        i, j, sign = unit
        return i ^ a, j ^ a, sign * (-1) ** (b * (i + j))

    comparisons = 0
    for a, b, i, j in product(range(2), repeat=4):
        source = (i, j, 1)
        decoded = image(a, b, source)
        correct = image(a, 0 if omit_phase else b, decoded)
        assert correct == source
        comparisons += 1
    witness = next(word for word in code - even if word.bit_count() == 7)
    assert leaders[syndrome(0)] == leaders[syndrome(witness)] == 0
    assert image(0, 0, (0, 0, 1)) == image(1, 0, (1, 1, 1))
    assert Counter(word.bit_count() for word in leaders.values()) == {
        weight: comb(23, weight) for weight in range(4)}
    return {'leaders': len(leaders), 'codewords': len(code),
            'supported_flag_pairs': (len(leaders) * len(code)) ** 2,
            'matrix_units': comparisons}
```

The executed input is the twelve ordered binary strings in the displayed matrix of Theorem Z.13c, with bit index zero at the left end of each string. The verification gives 2048 leaders, 4096 residual words and sixteen matrix-unit equalities, covering $2^{46}$ flag pairs by the proved product bijection. The omitted-phase test is rejected, and the zero-syndrome branch comparison gives the indistinguishable-input witness. The proof and computation check the full declared LINK overlap (P.14.1m.11.2) and its quantum continuation. Other registry semantic atoms and the common global-realizer record retain their separate tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-p141m12-certified-gibbs-heat-and-locked-source-controls-on-the-r14-engine"></a>**Theorem P.14.1m.12 (Certified Gibbs Heat and Locked Source Controls on the R14 Engine).** Use the actual countable bath and paid release of Theorem D.8.9c.27 with Gibbs exponent $s=2$. This supplies the numerical-origin, prescription-lock and residual-control components of Algorithm P.14.1m.0 for this R14 thermal payment and its input to the self/world account.

*Source law and signed comparison.* Use the normalized weight $w_n=(n+1)^{-2}/Z$, with $Z=\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-2}$. Set $j=n+1$ in (D.8.9c.27.3). The actual ready-lane transitions have ratios $(2j-1)/j$ and $2$. The two permit values are fair independently of the earlier records and the bath. It follows that
$$
\frac{Q_2}{u}=2E-\frac{E}{Z\ln2}S,
\qquad
S=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{-\ln(1-1/(2j))}{j^2}.
\tag{P.14.1m.12.1}
$$
Both $Z$ and $S$ are positive. The identity accounts for all thermally occupied basis inputs. The correction term subtracts from the pathwise reserve $2E$. Its sign does not depend on a heat reading. Since $S\ge\ln2$ and $Z\le2$, the reserve exceeds the actual heat by at least $E/2$. A converse lower bound strictly above the entropy floor follows from the relative-entropy term in (D.8.9c.27.3). Its simple finite witness is the output level-zero probability $w_0/2$, whereas the input probability there is $w_0$. This is a change of the normalized thermal distribution on the actual source. The paid reserve of $2E$ is a budget, and the enclosed heat and its error are derived bounds. The entropy floor $E$, the heat and the paid reserve are distinct controls in the same unit.

*Certified error bounds.* For a positive integer $N$ define $Z_N=\sum_{j=1}^N j^{-2}$ and $S_N=\sum_{j=1}^N-j^{-2}\ln(1-1/(2j))$. Integral comparison gives $0\le Z-Z_N\le 1/N$. For $0\le x\le1/2$, integration of $(1-x)^{-1}$ gives $-\ln(1-x)\le2x$, so $0\le S-S_N\le 1/(2N^2)$. The individual logarithms and $\ln2=-\ln(1-1/2)$ can be bounded by the positive power series
$$
L_m(x)=\sum_{k=1}^m\frac{x^k}{k},\qquad
L_m(x)\le -\ln(1-x)\le
L_m(x)+\frac{x^{m+1}}{(m+1)(1-x)}.
\tag{P.14.1m.12.2}
$$
The error inequality follows by replacing $k$ by $m+1$ in each denominator after the truncation. It applies uniformly to every term in $S_N$. There is also a direct rational acceleration that avoids evaluating $N$ separate logarithms. For $r\ge2$ use $\zeta_r=\sum_{j\ge1}j^{-r}$ and
$$
S=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\zeta_{k+2}}{k2^k},\qquad
0\le\zeta_r-\sum_{j=1}^{N}j^{-r}\le\frac{1}{(r-1)N^{r-1}}.
\tag{P.14.1m.12.3}
$$
The interchange is justified by the nonnegative series. Its tail after $m$ terms is at most $2^{1-m}/(m+1)$ since $\zeta_{k+2}\le2$ for all $k$. Computing (P.14.1m.12.3) with one cutoff for all powers, then dividing the positive bounds for $S,Z,\ln2$ in their correct directions in (P.14.1m.12.1), encloses the full heat. Taking $N,m$ to infinity proves convergence and termination of width-based refinement. The serialized endpoints are rounded outwards to a dyadic mesh at most $\epsilon/4$, so rounding adds at most $\epsilon/2$ to the enclosure width. Exact tuple serialization preserves those bounds. *Origin, lock and accounting records.* The branch identifier fixes the two returned-auxiliary gates, the ready-lane map (D.8.9c.27.2), the basis Hamiltonian proportional to $2\ln(n+1)$, the fair permit and the normalized Gibbs preparation.
```python
import json
from fractions import Fraction

def heat_certificate(frozen, submitted, epsilon):
    assert submitted == frozen and set(frozen) == {
        'branch', 'exponent', 'ready_lane', 'hamiltonian',
        'energy_unit', 'source_hashes'}
    assert frozen['branch'] == 'native_r14_countable_gibbs'
    assert frozen['exponent'] == 2
    assert frozen['ready_lane'] == 'double_index_fair_permit'
    assert frozen['hamiltonian'] == 'logarithmic_number_basis'
    assert frozen['source_hashes']
    unit = Fraction(frozen['energy_unit'])
    assert unit > 0 and epsilon > 0

    def rounded(value, direction):
        scale = 1
        while Fraction(1, scale) > epsilon / 4:
            scale *= 2
        numerator = (direction * value * scale).__floor__()
        return Fraction(direction * numerator, scale)

    def bound(n, m):
        z_lower = sum(Fraction(1, j * j) for j in range(1, n + 1))
        z_upper = z_lower + Fraction(1, n)
        log_lower = sum(Fraction(1, k * 2 ** k) for k in range(1, m + 1))
        log_upper = log_lower + Fraction(1, (m + 1) * 2 ** m)
        s_lower = s_upper = Fraction(0)
        for k in range(1, m + 1):
            power = k + 2
            base = sum(Fraction(1, j ** power) for j in range(1, n + 1))
            error = Fraction(1, (power - 1) * n ** (power - 1))
            coefficient = Fraction(1, k * 2 ** k)
            s_lower += coefficient * base
            s_upper += coefficient * (base + error)
        s_upper += Fraction(2, (m + 1) * 2 ** m)
        heat_lower = 2 * unit - unit * s_upper / (z_lower * log_lower)
        heat_upper = 2 * unit - unit * s_lower / (z_upper * log_upper)
        return max(unit, heat_lower), min(3 * unit / 2, heat_upper)

    n = m = 1
    while True:
        lower, upper = bound(n, m)
        lower, upper = rounded(lower, 1), rounded(upper, -1)
        assert lower <= upper
        if upper - lower <= epsilon:
            break
        n *= 2
        m += 2
    result = {
        'lock': frozen,
        'cutoffs': [n, m],
        'source_origins': ['ready_lane', 'hamiltonian', 'energy_unit'],
        'error_origins': ['gibbs_sum', 'log_series', 'positive_series_tail'],
        'heat': {'tag': 'residual', 'kind': 'bound',
                 'lower': str(lower), 'upper': str(upper)},
        'reserve': {'tag': 'budget', 'kind': 'budget', 'value': str(2 * unit)},
        'reserve_margin': {'tag': 'residual', 'kind': 'bound',
                           'lower': str(max(unit / 2, 2 * unit - upper))},
        'finite_bath_ready_error': {'tag': 'residual', 'kind': 'bound',
                                    'upper': str(Fraction(1, n))},
    }
    data = json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))
    assert json.loads(data) == result
    return data
```

The rational code verifies their numerical consequences. Execution at $E=1$ with requested widths $1/100$ and $1/1000$ gives $[329/256,331/256]$ and $[5293/4096,331/256]$, respectively, each with a certified reserve margin at least $181/256$. Changing any of the six declared lock fields is rejected. The heat control gives a complete numerical source and error record for the nominated thermal branch. Other engine inputs, a general spectral-ledger rule, the remaining registry predicates and full acceptance retain their own tests. $\square$

<a id="theorem-p141m14-joint-clock-and-verified-failure-overlap-on-the-r14-engine"></a>**Theorem P.14.1m.14 (Joint Clock and Verified-Failure Overlap on the R14 Engine).** Take the phased source of Theorem D.8.9c.29 and the private joint fault preparation of Theorem D.8.9c.30. If $\lambda$ is length on the time axis, then for every Borel pair $I,J$ the joint marked release measure is
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\Pr(t_j\in I,F_j=a,\ t_k\in J,F_k=b)\\
&\quad=\frac{\pi_{jk}(a,b)}{L}\,
\lambda\bigl([0,L)\cap(I-jL-d_e)\cap(J-kL-d_e)\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\tag{P.14.1m.14.1}
$$
The one-address measure is $\Pr(F_j=a)$ times the corresponding single shifted intersection length divided by $L$.
```python
import json
from fractions import Fraction
from math import comb

def checked_r14_pair(copies, period, delay, addresses, windows, exposure, both_fail):
    period, delay, q, both_fail = map(
        Fraction, (period, delay, exposure, both_fail))
    j, k = addresses
    if not (type(copies) is int and copies >= 4
            and type(j) is int and type(k) is int and 0 <= j < k < copies
            and period > delay > 0 and 0 < q <= Fraction(1, 64)):
        raise ValueError('invalid clock, address or protected exposure')
    left = [(Fraction(a), Fraction(b)) for a, b in windows]
    if len(left) != 2 or any(a > b for a, b in left):
        raise ValueError('invalid windows')

    r = Fraction(0)
    for i, multiplicity in ((7, 253), (11, 1288), (15, 506), (23, 1)):
        for weight in range(4):
            for meet in range(weight + 1):
                if weight - meet > 23 - i:
                    continue
                power = i + weight - 2 * meet
                r += (multiplicity * comb(i, meet) * comb(23 - i, weight - meet)
                      * q**power * (1 - q)**(23 - power))
    law = [1 - 2*r + both_fail, r - both_fail, r - both_fail, both_fail]
    if min(law) < 0 or sum(law) != 1:
        raise ValueError('joint verdict does not have a physical flag lift')

    offsets = [j * period + delay, k * period + delay]
    shifted = [(a - shift, b - shift) for (a, b), shift in zip(left, offsets)]
    a = max([Fraction(0)] + [pair[0] for pair in shifted])
    b = min([period] + [pair[1] for pair in shifted])
    engine = max(Fraction(0), b - a) / period

    cuts = {Fraction(0), period}
    cuts.update(point for pair in shifted for point in pair if 0 < point < period)
    cuts = sorted(cuts)
    verified = Fraction(0)
    for a, b in zip(cuts, cuts[1:]):
        midpoint = (a + b) / 2
        if all(lo <= midpoint + shift < hi
               for (lo, hi), shift in zip(left, offsets)):
            verified += (b - a) / period

    engine_values = [str(engine * probability) for probability in law]
    verified_values = [str(verified * probability) for probability in law]
    if engine_values != verified_values:
        raise ValueError('clock and verdict routes disagree')
    result = {
        'copies': copies,
        'addresses': [j, k],
        'windows': [[str(a), str(b)] for a, b in left],
        'period': str(period),
        'release_delay': str(delay),
        'exposure': str(q),
        'one_failure': str(r),
        'phase_mass': str(engine),
        'verdict_order': ['00', '01', '10', '11'],

    data = json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))
```

<a id="theorem-p141m15-shared-mass-log-residual-audit-on-the-saw1-threshold-source"></a>**Theorem P.14.1m.15 (Shared Mass-Log Residual Audit on the SAW1 Threshold Source).** On the common-mass calibration slice of Theorem X.9.6h.5b, the original determinant current and the installed log-mass actuator use one raw logarithm. Its complete contribution to the three threshold and three wavefunction coordinates has a certified rank-one joint interval, including the two relations among the threshold coordinates that cancel its error exactly. The verifier below executes the overlap and one-count residual checks on this source and rejects a split that treats the same evaluation error independently in the two physical components.

*Actual branches and common prescription.* Use the real-even mass row, its three reducing sectors of dimensions $(144,96,48)$, and the physical unit $Q$ of Theorem X.9.6h.5b. In the fixed positive calibration interval $999/1000\le\mu=m/Q\le1001/1000$, put $\ell=\log\mu^2$ and $F=(144,96,48)^{\mathsf T}\ell$. Keep the exact same mass row, native determinant orientation and finite-part prescription in the two component maps. The physical determinant map is $T_{\mathrm{det}}F$, and the actual precommitted actuator gives $(T_{\mathrm{full}}-T_{\mathrm{det}})F$, with the matrices from that theorem. Both consume the same $F$. The physical gauge-reference law cancels the cutoff contribution to this local calibration coefficient. Thus the two routes, from the mass row through the two physical components or directly through the complete Dynkin map, give
$$
\Delta=k\ell,\qquad Z=\mathbf1+k\ell/24,\qquad
k=(13824/5,2304,3456)^{\mathsf T}.
\tag{P.14.1m.15.1}
$$
In particular $5\Delta_1=6\Delta_2$ and $2\Delta_3=3\Delta_2$ for this projection. These equations hold for every input on the calibration slice and for the common mass-log error by linearity. A separately proved finite-precursor, controller or readout error remains in its own original category and can affect a contrast of the full physical output.

Let $\ell_*$ be one rational evaluation of the mass log, with error $e=\ell-\ell_*$ in a certified interval. The error vector in $(\Delta,Z)$ from that evaluation is exactly $e(k,k/24)$. This means the image of the one-dimensional source enclosure under the displayed map, with no assumption that each value of the interval is attained by the particular fixed input. It supplies one residual source and a jointly propagated bound. If an independently supplied stochastic model instead gives the common scalar error variance $v$, the contribution to the covariance is $v(k,k/24)(k,k/24)^{\mathsf T}$. A deterministic enclosure supplies no such variance by itself.

The two physical component directions for the threshold are $-c\mathbf1$ and $k+c\mathbf1$, where $c=1/(2\pi)>0$. The first identity follows by multiplying the actual determinant-current map by $(144,96,48)^{\mathsf T}$. If the errors were copied into independent scalars $e_1,e_2$ in the two components, the first threshold contrast would be $c(e_1-e_2)$ because $(5,-6,0)\cdot k=0$ and $(5,-6,0)\cdot\mathbf1=-1$. Hence a product of two nonsingleton error intervals does not preserve the common-source equation. This shows an actual acceptance-active difference in (C17) even where separate marginal error bounds are sound. The underlying physical determinant and actuator retain their own resources.

*Exact source check.* The prescribed inputs for the following finite check are the mass ratio, a positive number of logarithm terms, and one source binding independently read from the accepted proof span of Theorem X.9.6h.5b. The source binding names the same span for the single mass-log residual and its two consumers. The exact source-map identity is checked in the rational polynomial ring in the formal variable $c=1/(2\pi)$. No numerical evaluation of $\pi$ is needed for the cancellation. The checker evaluates the log once, using $z=(\mu-1)/(\mu+1)$ and
$$
\ell=4\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{2j+1}}{2j+1},\qquad
\left|\ell-4\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\frac{z^{2j+1}}{2j+1}\right|
\le
\frac{4|z|^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)(1-z^2)}.
\tag{P.14.1m.15.2}
$$
The identity follows by integrating the geometric series of $(1-z^2)^{-1}$ on the segment from zero to $z$. The tail uses $2j+1\ge2n+1$ for all omitted terms. It converges uniformly on this compact mass interval. The checker returns rational endpoints and the full joint direction. Its parser compares a submitted projection to the canonical recomputation from the independently supplied inputs. The two consumers use one residual identifier. A split identifier, different source hash or changed direction is rejected. The proof span is independently bound to its owning source before this local check. The arithmetic consumes that source proof.

```python
from fractions import Fraction
import json

def saw1_mass_log_projection(mass_ratio, terms, source_hash, submitted=None):
    mu = Fraction(mass_ratio)
    if not Fraction(999, 1000) <= mu <= Fraction(1001, 1000):
        raise ValueError('mass ratio outside the declared source')
    if type(terms) is not int or terms < 1:
        raise ValueError('positive term count required')
    if (len(source_hash) != 64
            or any(c not in '0123456789abcdef' for c in source_hash)):
        raise ValueError('invalid independently resolved proof hash')

    dimensions = (144, 96, 48)
    index = ((Fraction(2, 5), Fraction(3, 5), 0), (0, 1, 0), (1, 0, 0))
    k = tuple(24 * sum(x * d for x, d in zip(row, dimensions)) for row in index)
    det = tuple((0, -sum(row)) for row in index)
    actuator = tuple((coefficient, -linear) for coefficient, (_, linear) in zip(k, det))
    combined = tuple((a + c, b + d) for (a, b), (c, d) in zip(det, actuator))
    if combined != tuple((coefficient, 0) for coefficient in k):
        raise ValueError('native current paths do not agree')
    if 5*k[0] != 6*k[1] or 2*k[2] != 3*k[1]:
        raise ValueError('source contrast does not cancel')

    z = (mu - 1) / (mu + 1)
    midpoint = 4 * sum(z**(2*j + 1) / (2*j + 1) for j in range(terms))
    radius = 4 * abs(z)**(2*terms + 1) / ((2*terms + 1) * (1 - z*z))
    residual_id = 'saw1:common-mass-log'
    result = {
        'mass_ratio': str(mu),
        'terms': terms,
        'source_hash': source_hash,
        'residual': {
            'id': residual_id, 'tag': 'residual', 'kind': 'bound',
            'center': str(midpoint), 'radius': str(radius),
        },
        'component_uses': [
            {'component': 'determinant-current', 'residual': residual_id},
            {'component': 'log-mass-actuator', 'residual': residual_id},
        ],
        'delta_direction': [str(x) for x in k],
        'Z_direction': [str(Fraction(x) / 24) for x in k],
        'delta_intervals': [[str(x*(midpoint-radius)), str(x*(midpoint+radius))]
                            for x in k],
        'vanishing_delta_contrasts': [[5, -6, 0], [0, -3, 2]],
    }
    encoded = json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode()
    if json.loads(encoded) != result or (submitted is not None and submitted != encoded):
        raise ValueError('prescription, residual, overlap or codec mismatch')
    return encoded
```

The execution at $\mu=1$ returns exact zero residual width and zero threshold vector. At both ends of the declared calibration interval, the check uses positive radius and returns the same direction and exactly vanishing shared-error contrasts. Replacing one consumer's residual identifier, the bound tag or the source hash fails the canonical check. This verifies the specific shared numerical-origin and overlap records used by (C5), (C12), (C13), (C15), (C16), (C17), and the round trip for this projection. The other SAW1 controls and the corpus-wide normative tuple retain their respective tests. $\square$

<a id="convention-p141s-global-adopted-postulate-ledger"></a>**Convention P.14.1s (Global Adopted-Postulate Ledger).** Fix a versioned typed language $L_*$ and a source snapshot. The adopted-postulate ledger is a finite record whose entries have the form
$$
\mathfrak p
=
(\iota,\Sigma,\ell,s,\mathcal D,\mathcal B,\mathcal X,\chi),
\tag{P.14.1s.1}
$$
where $\iota$ is a stable identifier, $\Sigma\in\operatorname{Sent}(L_*)$ is the exact adopted statement, $\ell$ is its source file, line span, and source hash, $s\in\{\textsf{adopted},\textsf{proved},\textsf{refuted}\}$ is its status, $\mathcal D$ is its finite direct-dependency set, $\mathcal B$ is the finite set of consuming branches, $\mathcal X$ contains its independently stated evidence, falsifier, and any countermodel, and $\chi$ contains the cited proof, model, source, and checker hashes.

A populated ledger is accepted only when the following finite checks pass.

1. **Coverage and registry agreement.** Every source declaration carrying adopted-premise status in the frozen snapshot has exactly one entry. Its identifier is a vertex of the same snapshot of $\mathfrak G_{\mathrm{PU}}$; every dependency and every status-bearing consumer edge agrees with $\mathcal E$.
2. **Acyclicity.** The dependency graph on the entries is finite and acyclic. No consumer or descendant of $\mathfrak p$ occurs in a proof used to change the status of $\mathfrak p$.
3. **Certified deduplication.** The checker partitions entries only within one common frozen language, type convention, and branch context. It places two entries in the same block only when it accepts derivations of both $\Sigma\Rightarrow\Sigma'$ and $\Sigma'\Rightarrow\Sigma$, using neither entry as an undischarged premise and using no descendant of either entry. It then verifies reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity of the resulting relation and verifies every pairwise mutual-derivability certificate within each block. Entries lacking these certificates remain distinct. After item 4 is checked, a $\textsf{proved}$ or $\textsf{refuted}$ lifecycle tag propagates across its certified-equivalence block; incompatible proved/refuted tags reject the snapshot. Let $s([\mathfrak p])$ denote the resulting common block tag and write
   $$
   k_{\mathrm{total}}
   :=
   \left|
   \{[\mathfrak p]_{\sim_{\mathrm{cert}}}:s([\mathfrak p])=\textsf{adopted}\}
   \right|.
   \tag{P.14.1s.2}
   $$
4. **Discharge and refutation.** Status $\textsf{proved}$ requires a checked derivation of $\Sigma$ from closed non-descendant vertices. Status $\textsf{refuted}$ requires one of: a checked derivation of $\neg\Sigma$ from closed non-descendant vertices; an accepted empirical falsifier under $\Sigma$'s owning status rule; or, when $\Sigma$ is explicitly a universal mathematical assertion over a declared class, a checked counterexample together with a proof that the counterexample belongs to that class. A model of the declared dependencies that falsifies a general adopted premise records non-entailment under that premise set in $\mathcal X$ and leaves its lifecycle tag $\textsf{adopted}$. Every entry not meeting the stated proof or refutation rule remains $\textsf{adopted}$.
5. **Re-derivation record.** Every new accepted snapshot records, for each standing adopted entry, a declared finite proof search or derivation attempt, its input set, method, bound, and outcome. A successful checked proof invokes item 4. Exhaustion of a bounded search records only that bounded outcome and does not establish independence.

The field $s$ is a premise-lifecycle tag, distinct from the closure-status map $\sigma$ of Definition P.14.1m. A change to $s=\textsf{proved}$ or $s=\textsf{refuted}$ becomes operative only in a same-version registry snapshot that passes Algorithm P.14.1m.0 with the corresponding proof or no-go vertices and status propagation.

This ledger is an auxiliary projection of the strict-certificate registry. Its definition adopts no premise and changes no status until a populated record passes the stated checks.

| Registered values satisfy the joint constraints | On the conjunction of Theorem 15, Hilbert distinguishability, Theorem Z.2's same-class comparator, and Theorem Z.1's active-kernel gates, $(K_0,a,d_0)=(3,2,8)$ and hence $d_0=2a^2=2^{K_0}$; the Diophantine equality alone has other integer solutions |
| Several downstream values agree numerically | Evidence for a common-source hypothesis only after source independence, forward projection from one parent record, and overlap commutativity are proved |
| Agreement spans 5+ significant figures | Arithmetic precision of the comparison, not theorem status or causal origin |
| Same backbone inputs constrain several sectors | $\varepsilon_0,K_0$ organize the discrete backbone; every sector-specific output retains its branch, bridge, threshold, convention, model, residual, and certificate inputs |
| Standardized-residual display | Diagnostic only; no goodness-of-fit claim without a declared joint likelihood and covariance model |

The branch-level structural values $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ and $K_0=3$ avoid fitting those two backbone labels separately in each sector. Their recurrence is scientifically testable through the common-source and source-exhaustion ledgers.

### P.14.8 Summary

The framework's discrete core is fixed on its stated branch. Numerical applications in particle physics and cosmology retain their own models, calibrations, and evidential status.

**Technical ledger.**

$$\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
&\textbf{Structural theorem:} \quad \varepsilon_0=\ln2,\quad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}=H_q(P\mid R)+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{diss}}\ge H_q(P\mid R) \\[4pt]
&\textbf{Minimal SPAP core:} \quad K_0=3,\quad d_0\ge8,\quad d_0=8 \text{ on the minimal MPU branch} \\[4pt]

&\textbf{Status-carrying outputs:} \quad \alpha^{-1},D,\Lambda,v,\sin^2\theta_W^{(0)};\ m_H,\text{ CKM, PMNS, and }\eta_B\text{ remain conditional/certificate-gated} \\[4pt]
&\textbf{Experimental tests:} \quad \text{mixed-status rows are reported separately; no aggregate goodness-of-fit statistic is claimed} \\[4pt]
&\textbf{Conclusion:} \quad \text{the discrete backbone is theorem-level on its stated branch; downstream sectors retain their local bridge, certificate, or model status labels unless promoted by an accepted final spectral calibration datum}
\end{aligned}
}$$

A claim that a physical implementation approaches a thermodynamic optimum additionally requires its registered heat or work ledger, an admissible comparison class, and an attainment or saturation certificate.

### P.14.9 Meta-Theoretic Status and Comparative Adequacy

The status ledger above concerns object-level claims: assertions about physical reality or about the finite-response structures that generate physical predictions. The manuscript also contains meta-level claims about how physical frameworks are compared and how PU positions itself under that comparison. These two levels must remain separate.

**Convention P.14.9a (Object-Level / Meta-Level Separation).** A PU object-level claim is a finite-record assertion about a physical branch, response quotient, operator, sector value, or bridge map. Its manuscript status is assigned by Convention P.14.1a. A populated tuple satisfying Definition P.14.1m and Algorithm P.14.1m.0 has a mathematically accepted registry status. Calling that status **machine-audited** additionally requires a versioned executable verifier or proof kernel, a termination and soundness certificate for every invoked semantic predicate, the exact input artifact and cryptographic hash, and a recorded successful execution result. The schema template alone supplies none of these. A PU meta-level claim is a methodological assertion about the comparison criterion for theories, the role of compression in theory choice, or PU's own positioning under that criterion. Meta-level claims may be recorded in Appendix P, the discussion, or the conclusion, but they do not create new physical sectors, constants, operators, certificates, or validation rows.

**Definition P.14.9b (Structural Description Cost).** For a theory or framework $\mathcal T$ and empirical domain $\mathcal E$, let $K_{\mathcal E}(\mathcal T)$ denote the structural description cost of producing the predictions of $\mathcal T$ on $\mathcal E$ from the admitted initial data, boundary data, and observational protocols. Each comparison fixes one versioned structural-description language, decoder, admitted input and witness fields, and cost unit. If multiple encodings are admitted, the comparison supplies certified translation maps and their overhead and either proves that the reported ordering is invariant or labels the result as representation-relative. $K_{\mathcal E}$ is a methodological comparison proxy modeled on Kolmogorov description length, not a new physical observable. It is generally not computable exactly and is proxy-dependent in practice; comparisons using it must therefore state the shared domain $\mathcal E$ and the structural inputs counted. Description length, verifier runtime, thermodynamic dressing cost $C_X$, and registered bath heat remain distinct coordinates unless a physical implementation bridge relates them.

**Principle P.14.9c (Comparative K-Adequacy).** If two frameworks $\mathcal T_1$ and $\mathcal T_2$ are predictively adequate on a shared empirical domain $\mathcal E$, predictive overlap alone does not establish theoretical equivalence. On the shared domain, the framework with greater predictive yield per structural description cost, or with equal yield and lower $K_{\mathcal E}$, is the better compression of the same content. Coverage outside $\mathcal E$ can justify additional structure only when it supplies additional predictive yield on the enlarged domain.

<a id="theorem-p149c1-encoding-robust-k-adequacy-bounds"></a>**Theorem P.14.9c.1 (Encoding-Robust K-Adequacy Bounds).** Fix the shared domain $\mathcal E$ and two universal prefix-free description languages $U,V$. Suppose fixed translators give
$$
K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T)
\le
K_{\mathcal E}^V(\mathcal T)+c_{V\to U},
\qquad
K_{\mathcal E}^V(\mathcal T)
\le
K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T)+c_{U\to V}
\tag{P.14.9c.1a}
$$
for every compared framework, and set $C=\max\{c_{V\to U},c_{U\to V}\}$. Then
$$
\left|K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T)-K_{\mathcal E}^V(\mathcal T)\right|
\le C
\tag{P.14.9c.1b}
$$
and, for any pair $\mathcal T_1,\mathcal T_2$,
$$
\left|
\bigl(K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T_1)-K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T_2)\bigr)
-
\bigl(K_{\mathcal E}^V(\mathcal T_1)-K_{\mathcal E}^V(\mathcal T_2)\bigr)
\right|
\le2C.
\tag{P.14.9c.1c}
$$
Hence an equal-yield description advantage larger than $2C$ has the same sign in both languages.

Let $Y_{\mathcal E}(\mathcal T)\ge0$ be a language-independent predictive-yield functional and suppose $K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T)>C$. The score $S^V_{\mathcal E}=Y_{\mathcal E}/K_{\mathcal E}^V$ obeys
$$
\frac{Y_{\mathcal E}(\mathcal T)}
{K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T)+C}
\le
S^V_{\mathcal E}(\mathcal T)
\le
\frac{Y_{\mathcal E}(\mathcal T)}
{K_{\mathcal E}^U(\mathcal T)-C}.
\tag{P.14.9c.1d}
$$
Two such intervals being disjoint in one order certifies that order throughout the declared translator class. Overlapping intervals leave the ranking unresolved by the compiler bounds.

*Proof.* Each inequality in (P.14.9c.1a) rearranges to one side of (P.14.9c.1b). Applying the triangle inequality to the two theorywise differences gives (P.14.9c.1c), and a margin exceeding $2C$ cannot change sign. Positivity of the denominators reverses neither reciprocal bound, so substituting (P.14.9c.1b) into $Y_{\mathcal E}/K_{\mathcal E}^V$ gives (P.14.9c.1d). Disjoint score intervals fix the order for every value allowed by those bounds. When the intervals overlap, these translator bounds alone certify neither order; additional language-specific information is required. ∎

<a id="theorem-p149c2-a-populated-pu-and-quantum-description-and-yield-certificate"></a>**Theorem P.14.9c.2 (A Populated PU and Quantum Description and Yield Certificate).** The finite context-phase instrument of Theorem L.4.6c admits a complete formal comparison with its ordinary quantum-instrument description. The comparison has equal shortest prediction-description costs in each fixed language, a common positive formal yield, explicit constant-overhead translators and a response-error certificate.

1. **Shared source and protocol record.** Use the typed retained aggregate-context source of Theorem L.12.8b: orthogonal labels $|s_0\rangle,|s_1\rangle$, a retained source bit $R$, and the source-preserving controlled-$X$ encoder from $S$ into a fresh bit $C$. This source typing is the common admitted input of the comparison. Both descriptions consume the finite Hilbert/instrument branch, product ready preparations, unitary evolution and joint projective record service of Theorem L.4.6c. Register
   $$
   \mathcal D=\{(N,k,\mathbf b):N\in\{1,2\},\ k\in\{0,1,2\},\ \mathbf b\in\{0,1,2,3\}^N\},
   \quad
   \delta=\frac{k\pi}{2N},\quad \beta_i=\frac{b_i\pi}{12},
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.1}
   $$
   so $|\mathcal D|=60$. Every pulse and both primitive services have duration $\tau_0=1\,\mathrm s$, $\Omega=\delta/\tau_0$, and every free Hamiltonian vanishes on the registered strokes. The input basis is all four $|s_j,r\rangle$, $j,r\in\{0,1\}$; $C,M,Q_1,\ldots,Q_N,E_1,\ldots,E_N$ start in $|0\rangle$. The output order is $S,R,C,E_1,\ldots,E_N,Q_1,\ldots,Q_N,M$. The source/controller algebra $S,R,C$ remains with the source owner. The receiver algebra is $Q,E,M$. Its two registered endpoints are the target record $a$ and the noise-assisted record $(\xi,a)$, with $\xi\in\{0,1\}^N$ and $a\in\{0,1\}$. The complete quantum leaf is retained at either endpoint. All outcomes, including zero-probability ones, remain in the record.

   The shared resource record, in the units indicated, is
   $$
   n_q=2N+4,\quad n_p=4N+2,\quad n_{\mathrm{ready}}=n_{\mathrm{met}}=1,
   \quad \frac{T}{\tau_0}=4N+4,
   \quad \frac{A}{\pi\hbar}=3N+1+\frac{\sum_i b_i}{12}+\frac{k}{8}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.2}
   $$
   The ready and joint-record services are supplied primitive resources, and all registers are retained after this single use. The action $A$ is the pulse norm action of (L.4.6c.16). Its work, reset-heat and cyclic-reuse interpretations retain their separate implementation contracts. Each pulse has the Hamiltonian and positive duration specified in Theorem L.4.6c; in particular a Hermitian involution $U$ uses $\pi\hbar(I-U)/(2\tau_0)$, a noise rotation uses $\hbar\beta_iY/\tau_0$, and the phase pulse uses $\hbar\Omega(P_{1,C}-I_C/2)\sum_i Z_{Q_i}/2$.

   The comparison's physical domain is this source and ready-input class. Its full ready-input map on source matrix units, and its tensor extension by the identity on any spectator, are part of the formal certificate. Arbitrary initial states of the auxiliary registers are outside this protocol. The formal scoring prior is $q_{jr}=1/4$; its truth variable is the already retained source label $j$. The score is a mathematical functional of the channel, evaluated with that prior, and grants neither receiver endpoint access to $S,R,C$.

2. **Two finite descriptions of the same instrument.** The following algorithms specify the compared descriptions. Their inputs, branch premises and source/resource fields are exactly item 1. Their output is the outcome-labeled ready-input instrument and its common record, rather than a theory-name string.

   **PU description.** Set $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/96}$, $h=\cos(\pi/4)$, $\epsilon_\xi=(-1)^{\sum_i\xi_i}$, $\omega_{\mathbf b,\xi}=\prod_i (\cos\beta_i)^{1-\xi_i}(\sin\beta_i)^{\xi_i}$ and
   $$
   v_{j,\xi}=h\left(\zeta^{-6(2j-1)k}|0\rangle+
      \epsilon_\xi\zeta^{6(2j-1)k}|1\rangle\right),
   \qquad \Pi_a=\frac{I+(-1)^aY}{2}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.3}
   $$
   For each lexicographically ordered $(N,k,\mathbf b)$, source pair $(j,r)$ and leaf $(\xi,a)$, compute the column
   $$
   K_{\xi,a}|j,r\rangle=
   |s_j,r,j\rangle\otimes\omega_{\mathbf b,\xi}|\xi\rangle
   \otimes\Pi_av_{j,\xi}\otimes|0\rangle^{\otimes(N-1)}\otimes|a\rangle.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.4}
   $$
   The derivation capsule is the source-controlled eigenphase calculation, the GHZ preparation, independent noise amplitudes and their controlled phase signs, inverse fanout, and the actual $Y$-basis readout copy of Theorem L.4.6c. Specifically, the GHZ terms have generator eigenvalues $\pm N/2$, the source encoder gives $C=j$, and their phase factors are $e^{\mp iN(j-1/2)\delta/2}=\zeta^{\mp6(2j-1)k}$. Every noise-one bit changes the all-one term's sign, inverse fanout makes $Q_2,\ldots,Q_N$ zero, and the recorded readout applies $\Pi_a$. These finite identities derive (3)--(4) from the supplied Hamiltonians. Apply the serializer in item 3 to the columns and the resource record.

   **Quantum description.** Begin with each of the four source basis states and the stated ready factors. Multiply the following ordinary quantum gates on the full $2N+4$-qubit vector, in the displayed order: the source-to-$C$ controlled $X$; $H$ on $Q_1$; $\mathrm{CNOT}_{Q_1\to Q_i}$ for $i=2,\ldots,N$; $e^{-i\beta_iY_{E_i}}$ for $i=1,\ldots,N$; $e^{-i\delta(P_{1,C}-I_C/2)\sum_i Z_{Q_i}/2}$; $\mathrm{CZ}_{E_i,Q_i}$ for $i=1,\ldots,N$; the fanout gates in reverse order; and $\Pi_0\otimes I_M+\Pi_1\otimes X_M$. Project onto $E=\xi,M=a$ and retain every remaining factor. A local matrix acts by replacing the affected bit and summing its matrix entry times the input amplitude; a controlled $X$ permutes the target bit, a controlled $Z$ changes the sign exactly when both its bits equal one, and the phase on a computational string with $C=c$ and target Hamming weight $w$ is $\zeta^{-6(2c-1)k(N-2w)/N}$. This exponent is integral for both admitted $N$. Use $H=2^{-1/2}\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, $e^{-i\beta Y}=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}\cos\beta&-\sin\beta\\\sin\beta&\cos\beta\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ and $Y=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$. The derivation capsule is ordinary tensor-product unitary evolution followed by the complete orthogonal output projectors. Apply the same serializer to these independently multiplied columns and the resource record.

   Both algorithms terminate using exact arithmetic in
   $$
   F=\mathbb Q(\zeta)=\mathbb Q[z]/(z^{32}-z^{16}+1).
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.5}
   $$
   Their outcome maps agree on all sixteen source matrix units:
   $$
   \mathcal I^{PU}_{\xi,a}(|j,r\rangle\langle j',r'|)
   =\mathcal I^{QM}_{\xi,a}(|j,r\rangle\langle j',r'|)
   =K_{\xi,a}|j,r\rangle\langle j',r'|K_{\xi,a}^\dagger,
   \qquad \sum_{\xi,a}K_{\xi,a}^\dagger K_{\xi,a}=I_{SR}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.6}
   $$
   Thus equality includes the entire retained update, source coherences in the formal extension, every classical source mixture and spectator stability. The quantum comparator uses the same physically specified source, rather than a second output-probability table.

3. **Canonical prediction word and populated languages.** Fix $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/96}$ and $F=\mathbb Q[z]/(z^{32}-z^{16}+1)$ with $z$ embedded as $\zeta$. Use the computational order $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, $X=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, $Y=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$, $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $P_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, $i=z^{24}$ and $H=(z^{12}+z^{-12})\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)/2$. Set $I=\operatorname{diag}(1,1)$ and $\Pi_a=(I+(-1)^aY)/2$. Controlled $X$ flips its target exactly when its control is one; controlled $Z$ changes the sign exactly when both bits are one. Evaluate $\cos(t\pi/48)=(z^t+z^{-t})/2$ and $\sin(t\pi/48)=(z^t-z^{-t})/(2i)$ for integral $t$; the phase and noise exponents in this domain are integral. Use reduced rational coefficients, a positive denominator and the ordered basis $1,z,\ldots,z^{31}$ for $F$. Multiply polynomials and reduce every power $z^n$, $n\ge32$, by $z^n=z^{n-16}-z^{n-32}$, starting at the largest degree; conjugation sends $z$ to $z^{95}$. The embedding is the stated $\zeta$, and powers may first be reduced modulo $96$. This is a finite rational-arithmetic procedure. For each leaf form the Choi matrix
   $$
   J_{\xi,a}=|K_{\xi,a}\rangle\!\rangle\langle\!\langle K_{\xi,a}|,
   \qquad |K\rangle\!\rangle=\sum_{j,r}K|j,r\rangle\otimes|j,r\rangle.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.7}
   $$
   Its row and column bit tuples consist of the output bits followed by the two input bits. A field element is its ordered list of nonzero triples $[e,n,d]$ for coefficient $n/d$ at $z^e$; zero is the empty list. A matrix is its ordered list $[\mathrm{rowbits},\mathrm{columnbits},\mathrm{field\ element}]$ of nonzero entries. A leaf is $[\xi,a,J_{\xi,a}]$. A device record is the ten-element list
   $$
   [N,k,\mathbf b,2N+4,4N+2,1,1,4N+4,[a_A,d_A],\mathrm{leaves}],
   \quad \frac{a_A}{d_A}=3N+1+\frac{\sum_i b_i}{12}+\frac{k}{8}
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.8}
   $$
   in lowest terms. Order devices by $N,k,\mathbf b$, leaves by $\xi,a$, matrix entries by their row/column tuples, and field entries by exponent. The canonical word $R$ is the ASCII encoding of the nested list $[1,\mathrm{device\ records}]$: use `[` and `]`, commas, ordinary signed decimal integers, and no whitespace. This explicitly fixes every byte of a finite prediction word. Framework names, derivation traces and witness bytes are in the separately charged descriptions, outside $R$. Choi matrices remove Kraus-phase freedom.

   A query is a device key, leaf and input matrix unit. Parse the lists, select the indicated Choi block, and return its output matrix. The diagonal-input trace gives the conditional probability; summing leaves over $\xi$ gives the target endpoint, while retaining $\xi,a$ gives the assisted endpoint. Finite rational source mixtures and finite linear combinations of matrix units are evaluated by the same exact arithmetic. For the certified canonical word this is a total finite decoder on every registered query. Canonical validation checks all list lengths and ranges, sorted distinct indices, reduced rational coefficients, the exact device/leaf census and the generic normalization $\sum_{\xi,a,u}J_{\xi,a}[(u,\alpha),(u,\beta)]=\delta_{\alpha\beta}$ for the four input labels $\alpha,\beta$; a malformed record is rejected. This schema, query procedure and arithmetic constitute the common decoder record.

   For an integer $n\ge1$, let $\gamma(n)$ be $\lfloor\log_2n\rfloor$ zero bits followed by the ordinary binary representation of $n$. For a finite bit word $x$, put $E(x)=\gamma(|x|+1)x$; bytes are read most-significant bit first. Its framed length is
   $$
   \lambda(x)=|x|+2\lfloor\log_2(|x|+1)\rfloor+1.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.9}
   $$
   The generic universal prefix machine $W$ has a literal branch $W(0E(x))=x$ and a universal branch $W(1\gamma(e+1)p)=M_e(p)$, with no trailing data after a complete literal word. Fix the following effective enumeration of $M_e$. The $e$th finite bit string is the binary representation of $e+1$ with its first bit removed. Parse it as a gamma-framed finite Turing-machine table: state count, symbol count and transition count, followed by lexicographically ordered records $(q,s,q',s',d,o)$, each nonnegative integer encoded by $\gamma(v+1)$. State count is at least two, symbol count at least one; state $1$ is initial, state $0$ halts, symbol $0$ is blank. The work tape has cells indexed by $\mathbb Z$, initially blank, with the head at zero. Moves $d=0,1,2$ mean left, stay, right. Output codes $o=0,1,2,3$ mean no output, bit zero, bit one, separator. Each transition writes, moves, changes state and appends that output symbol. A missing transition halts. Invalid ranges, trailing bits or duplicate transition keys make an empty enumerator. Each separator ends the current output buffer; parse that buffer as exactly $E(p)E(x)$, discard malformed buffers, and clear it. This gives a computably enumerated graph of candidate pairs $(p,x)$. Retain such a pair exactly when $p$ is neither a prefix nor an extension, equality included, of a previously retained program. $M_e(p)$ is the unique retained output at $p$, when one appears. To execute it, simulate this finite-table enumerator until that acceptance; no negative halting decision is used. Every partial computable prefix machine occurs because its graph has such a finite-table enumerator and its distinct programs pass the prefix filter. Thus $W$ is a fully specified universal prefix machine, and every accepted $W$ word has at least two bits.

   Define two generic description languages by
   $$
   U(0p)=W(p),\quad U(10p)=V(p),
   \qquad V(00p)=W(p),\quad V(01p)=U(p),
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.10}
   $$
   with other forms undefined. Each wrapper call consumes bits, so its finite syntactic parsing terminates. The translators $p\mapsto01p$ from $U$ to $V$ and $p\mapsto10p$ from $V$ to $U$ add two bits. Both languages are prefix-free and universal. If $\kappa_A(x)$ is the shortest accepted $A$-program outputting $x$, then
   $$
   \kappa_U(x)=\kappa_W(x)+1\ge3,
   \qquad \kappa_V(x)=\kappa_W(x)+2=\kappa_U(x)+1.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.11}
   $$
   The precise shift belongs to these two frozen languages; equality of two theories' shortest descriptions of the same semantic word holds in every fixed language.

4. **Complete description costs and encoding bounds.** Charge the full literal common source record of item 1 and the full decoder/schema/language record of item 3. More precisely, let $c_0$ and $c_1$ be the UTF-8 byte words of those numbered items, including their item text through the next numbered item and excluding that next item, and measure their bits by the preceding byte convention. Their shared charge is $D=\lambda(c_0)+\lambda(c_1)$. These words are supplied in the theorem; hashes are checks on them, rather than substitutes for their contents. Let $d_{PU}$ and $d_{QM}$ be the respective literal **PU description** and **Quantum description** paragraphs in item 2, including their displayed formula or algorithm and derivation capsule, ending immediately before the next bold description or the paragraph beginning “Both algorithms”. The two populated, representation-relative description-package costs are

The canonical Choi word has $1244722$ ASCII bytes, hence $n=9957776$ bits; its literal $U$ and $V$ program lengths are $9957825$ and $9957826$ bits.

   The exact algebraic arithmetic and lookup rules are in $c_1$; no native PU or QM probability oracle is an instruction. Independent executable renderings may add a declared implementation library and witness transcript to their own source-byte packages. The costs in (12) concern the complete formal algorithms and their stated premises. Physical pulse resources remain (2), and description length is measured in bits.

   On this formal shared domain use Definition P.14.9b's semantic shortest-description choice
   $$
   K_{\mathcal E}^{A}(\mathcal T)=D+\min\{|p|:A(p)=R_{\mathcal T}\},
   \qquad A\in\{U,V\},\quad \mathcal T\in\{PU,QM\}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.13}

   The canonical response compiler of item 3 gives $R_{PU}=R_{QM}=R$. Hence the two sets minimized in (13) are identical in each language. If $n=|R|$ in bits and $L=2+\lambda(R)$, the literal words $00E(R)$ for $U$ and $000E(R)$ for $V$ give
   $$
   \begin{aligned}
   K_{\mathcal E}^{U}(PU)&=K_{\mathcal E}^{U}(QM)=:K,\qquad D+3\le K\le D+L,\\

   The translator constants in Theorem P.14.9c.1 are $c_{U\to V}=c_{V\to U}=2$, and $K>2$. The registered two-theory description difference is zero in either language; its encoding-change difference is zero as well. Different values of the explicit package costs (12) are description-relative upper-level accounting data. The equality in (14) follows from semantic equality and requires no computation of the shortest program.

5. **Language-independent formal yield and response robustness.** For each device in $\mathcal D$ give both endpoints weight $1/2$, use the uniform prior on $j,r$, and retain the exact common response law as the formal benchmark. A theory reports the posterior forecast $f(j=1\mid y)$ computed from its endpoint law and that prior; assign $f=1/2$ on a zero-probability outcome. For any reported forecast define the nonnegative yield
   $$
   Y_{\mathcal E}(\mathcal T)=\max\left\{0,\frac14-
     \frac1{120}\sum_{d\in\mathcal D}\sum_{e\in\{\mathrm{target},\mathrm{joint}\}}
       \mathbb E_{P_{d,e}}\bigl[(f_{\mathcal T,d,e}(y)-j)^2\bigr]\right\}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.15}
   $$
   Here $P_{d,e}$ is the frozen formal source/response law, including $j$, rather than an observed frequency table. The source labels remain absent from the receiver's forecast argument. The constant forecast $1/2$ has loss $1/4$. This definition is independent of language and nonnegative for every forecast, including an inaccurate one.

   Put $s_k=\sin(k\pi/4)$ and $m_{\mathbf b}=\prod_i\cos(b_i\pi/6)$. The exact posterior at the target endpoint is $[1+(-1)^a m_{\mathbf b}s_k]/2$ for $j=1$. At the joint endpoint it is $[1+(-1)^a\epsilon_\xi s_k]/2$ whenever $w_\xi>0$. Both descriptions therefore attain the benchmark Bayes risks. Their endpoint gains and common yield are
   $$
   G_{d,\mathrm{target}}=\frac{m_{\mathbf b}^2s_k^2}{4},\qquad
   G_{d,\mathrm{joint}}=\frac{s_k^2}{4},\qquad
   Y_{\mathcal E}(PU)=Y_{\mathcal E}(QM)=\frac{13}{160}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.16}
   $$
   In particular their description-normalized scores are equal within each language. With $Y=13/160$, explicit score enclosures are
   $$
   \frac{Y}{D+L}\le S^U_{\mathcal E}(PU)=S^U_{\mathcal E}(QM)\le\frac{Y}{D+3},
   \qquad
   \frac{Y}{D+L+1}\le S^V_{\mathcal E}(PU)=S^V_{\mathcal E}(QM)\le\frac{Y}{D+4}.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.17}
   $$
   The more general translator enclosure (P.14.9c.1d), with $C=2$, also applies at the actual unknown $K$.

   Suppose an approximate description supplies, on every benchmark device/endpoint, a normalized joint law $Q_{d,e}$ of the same $(j,y)$ alphabet with $\operatorname{TV}(Q_{d,e},P_{d,e})\le\varepsilon$, and uses a Bayes posterior for $Q_{d,e}$. A zero-mass $Q$ outcome again uses $1/2$. If its reported posterior lies in $[0,1]$ and differs from that Bayes posterior by at most $\rho$ pointwise and the scoring law has total-variation error at most $\eta$ from $P_{d,e}$, its resulting clipped yield satisfies
   $$
   \left|\widetilde Y-Y\right|\le 2\varepsilon+2\rho+\eta=:\Delta_Y.
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.18}
   $$
   In the exact-scoring, exact-reporting case it lies in $[\max(0,Y-2\varepsilon),Y]$. For each of the four prepared inputs, impose $\tfrac12\|\bigoplus_{\xi,a}(\widetilde{\mathcal I}_{\xi,a}-\mathcal I_{\xi,a})(|j,r\rangle\langle j,r|)\|_1\le\varepsilon$ on the complete outcome-labeled classical–quantum output. This direct-sum bound implies the endpoint-law bound after the common prior and registered coarse-graining. If the new description also supplies its own positive cost interval $[\ell,u]$, then its score lies in
   $$
   \left[\frac{\max(0,Y-\Delta_Y)}u,
          \frac{\min(1/4,Y+\Delta_Y)}\ell\right].
   \tag{P.14.9c.2.19}
   $$
   The cost interval belongs to that description. Response closeness supplies the numerator bound; the denominator uses that description's separately supplied cost record.

*Proof.* There are $3(4+16)=60$ devices, all with the admitted finite ready/source preparations. The source-controlled generator gives the two eigenphases stated in item 2. Expanding each noise rotation, multiplying the controlled signs and decoding fanout gives (3)--(4). The quantum description performs those same physical operations by direct matrix multiplication, so each of its four source columns equals (4), including every coherent noise amplitude and retained label. This is equality before taking probabilities. Its projectors sum to the identity, and all preceding operations are unitary, hence the sum of Kraus adjoint products is $I_{SR}$. Matrix-unit extension proves (6), and tensoring the equal maps by the spectator identity preserves equality. Counting the operations and their norm actions gives (2), with $N\delta/4=k\pi/8$ and $\sum_i\beta_i=\pi\sum_i b_i/12$.

The $96$th cyclotomic polynomial is $z^{32}-z^{16}+1$: substituting $x=z^{16}$ gives $x^2-x+1$, whose roots are primitive sixth roots; its roots $z$ have order $96$, and the degree is $\varphi(96)=32$. Consequently the displayed power basis is independent, rational reduction is unique, and all Hadamard, noise, phase and readout entries lie in $F$. Formula (7) then produces unique outcome Choi matrices, independent of a Kraus global phase. The finite ordering and decimal serializer define one finite word $R$ for each description. Equality (6) makes those words equal. The query procedure is finite parsing and finite exact arithmetic on that word; its matrix-unit blocks recover the entire admitted instrument, and their traces and sums recover both endpoints.

The code $\gamma$ is prefix-free because its initial zero count fixes the length of the following binary word. Thus $E$ is prefix-free and has length (9). For each enumerator the retained programs form a prefix-free set by construction. If a given partial computable machine already has prefix-free domain, an enumerator for its graph emits all and only its successful pairs, and the filter retains one copy of every pair. Finite-table machines can enumerate a computable machine's graph by dovetailing its executions on finite inputs and framing each finite successful output; the work-tape conventions permit these finite simulations and output operations. The universal branch of $W$ therefore simulates every prefix machine with the constant prefix $1\gamma(e+1)$, while its literal branch supplies a total finite-output witness for every word. The two branches are disjoint and prefix-free. Their minimum lengths are two, as asserted.

Every accepted $U$ or $V$ description has a finite wrapper path ending at $W$. Paths from $U$ have length at least one, attained by its direct zero prefix. Paths from $V$ have length at least two, attained by its direct double-zero prefix. Taking minima over the same $W$ outputs proves (11); the two translated descriptions directly invoke the opposite language and add exactly two bits. Prefix-freeness follows by reading the disjoint wrapper prefixes until the prefix-free $W$ word. The common charge $D$ is identical for both languages and both theories. Their successful program sets for the common response word are identical in each language, proving the two theorywise equalities in (14). Prepending the direct language prefix to the literal $W$ word gives the stated upper bounds. The lower bounds and the exact shift follow from (11). Substituting these positive denominator bounds gives (17), and Theorem P.14.9c.1 applies with the explicit translator constants.

For the yield, (4) gives $p_j(\xi,a)=w_\xi[1+(-1)^a\epsilon_\xi(2j-1)s_k]/2$. Summing over $\xi$ gives the target response. Under the fair $j$ prior the target marginal of $a$ is $1/2$, and the joint marginal is $w_\xi/2$. Bayes' rule gives the posteriors in item 5 on positive-mass outcomes. Their deviations from $1/2$ have magnitudes $|m_{\mathbf b}s_k|/2$ and $|s_k|/2$. Conditional squared-loss minimization gives risk $\mathbb E[p(1-p)]$, so the baseline-relative gains are (16). Zero-mass noise outcomes contribute zero and their declared total forecast causes no change.

The mean of $s_k^2$ over $k=0,1,2$ is $1/2$. The four values of $\cos^2(b\pi/6)$ are $1,3/4,1/4,0$, with mean $1/2$. Thus the mean of $m_{\mathbf b}^2$ is $1/2$ on the twelve $N=1$ devices and $1/4$ on the forty-eight $N=2$ devices; its mean on all sixty devices is $(12/2+48/4)/60=3/10$. The configuration-averaged, endpoint-averaged gain is $\tfrac18\cdot\tfrac12\cdot(1+3/10)=13/160$. It is positive, so clipping does not alter either exact yield.

For robustness write $L_P(f)$ for expected squared loss under $P$. The loss lies in $[0,1]$, hence $|L_P(f)-L_Q(f)|\le\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)$. If $f_P,f_Q$ are Bayes rules, then
$$
0\le L_P(f_Q)-L_P(f_P)
\le L_Q(f_Q)+\varepsilon-L_Q(f_P)+\varepsilon
\le2\varepsilon.
$$
This also covers zero-mass outcomes under $Q$, since any forecast there is Bayes-optimal for $Q$. For forecasts in $[0,1]$, changing the forecast by at most $\rho$ changes squared loss by at most $2\rho$. A scoring-law change costs at most $\eta$. Averaging over the fixed finite weights preserves those bounds, and $x\mapsto\max(0,1/4-x)$ is one-Lipschitz. This proves (18) and its sharper one-sided case. The yield always lies in $[0,1/4]$, so division by the separately supplied positive cost interval gives (19). ∎

**Remark P.14.9d (Application to PU).** PU is bound by Principle P.14.9c. It cannot dismiss quantum mechanics, general relativity, the Standard Model, or any alternative framework merely by reproducing their predictions. On a shared domain, PU must either derive with lower explicit structural input what the competitor postulates, or supply additional predictive yield that justifies any additional structure. This is the methodological reading of the input-output economy statement in Section 14.6.8.

**Observation P.14.9e (Bet-Criterion Coherence).** PU's substantive framework bet is that physical reality is most efficiently modeled as predictive activity under finite-resource constraints. Principle P.14.9c evaluates theories by predictive yield per structural description cost. Thus, if PU wins the comparative $K_{\mathcal E}$ test on a domain, the criterion would have selected a framework whose subject matter is the same kind of activity that the criterion measures. This is a structural coherence between criterion and framework content; the comparison itself remains empirical and relative to competing frameworks.

**Convention P.14.9f (Conservative Status of the Meta-Theoretic Layer).** The meta-theoretic layer is methodological. It does not add a branch, close a certificate, promote a model-level row, modify the strict-certificate registry, or change any status in Convention P.14.1k. Rejection or alteration of the meta-theoretic layer would not by itself affect any object-level theorem. Conversely, acceptance of the meta-theoretic layer cannot repair a failed physical prediction or fill a missing certificate.

<a id="definition-p149g-response-completeness-global-lift-completeness-and-empirical-realization-identification"></a>**Definition P.14.9g (Response Completeness, Global-Lift Completeness, and Empirical Realization Identification).** Let $T$ be a theory in a language $L$, let $\operatorname{Mod}(T)$ be its model class, and let $\mathfrak P$ be a fixed family of finite registered protocols. For each $P\in\mathfrak P$, let $\mathcal R_P(\mathcal M)$ be the normalized response law of model $\mathcal M$, with a registered equivalence relation $\sim_P$. A numerical tolerance may be used only after taking its transitive closure or otherwise proving reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity; pairwise distance below a tolerance is not automatically an equivalence relation. Define
$$
\mathcal M\sim_{\mathrm{resp}}\mathcal N
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal R_P(\mathcal M)\sim_P\mathcal R_P(\mathcal N)
\quad\text{for every }P\in\mathfrak P.
\tag{P.14.9g.1}
$$
The theory is **mathematically response-complete** on $\mathfrak P$ when $\operatorname{Mod}(T)\ne\varnothing$, every $\mathcal R_P$ is total and normalized on $\operatorname{Mod}(T)$, and
$$
\left|\operatorname{Mod}(T)/\!\sim_{\mathrm{resp}}\right|=1.
\tag{P.14.9g.2}
$$

For the compatible tuple $q_\bullet$ and restriction map of the scope clause following Theorem P.14.1k.1, **global-lift completeness** means
$$
\operatorname{res}^{-1}(q_\bullet)
=
\{[\omega_*]\}
\tag{P.14.9g.3}
$$
in the declared global response quotient. **Empirical realization identification** is a separate finite record consisting of calibrated protocol implementations, unit maps, sampling and covariance laws, residual intervals and applicable stopping rules, and observed response data used to test membership in the response class of $[\omega_*]$. The record identifies calibration, selection, and evaluation data and uses the evidence protocol of Definition 13.0d. The selected class and physical PCE functional have their own derivation dependencies.

<a id="theorem-p149h-formal-core-realization-non-entailment"></a>**Theorem P.14.9h (Formal-Core Realization Non-Entailment).** Let $T$ be any classical theory with ordinary two-valued model semantics in a language $L$, and let $A_{\mathrm{real}}$ be a fresh zero-ary predicate in the expanded language $L^+=L\cup\{A_{\mathrm{real}}\}$, read as “the selected PU response class is instantiated as the realized physical universe.” Then exactly one of the following holds:

1. $\operatorname{Mod}(T)=\varnothing$, in which case $T$ supplies no candidate realization; or
2. $\operatorname{Mod}(T)\ne\varnothing$, in which case, when $T$ is read as an $L^+$-theory,
   $$
   T\not\models A_{\mathrm{real}},
   \qquad
   T\not\models\neg A_{\mathrm{real}}.
   \tag{P.14.9h.1}
   $$

Consequently, a satisfiable formal core whose axioms do not contain a realization statement cannot derive its own external actuality. Mathematical response completeness, a unique PCE minimizer, and global-lift completeness do not alter this result.

*Proof.* If $T$ has no model, the first case holds. Otherwise choose $\mathcal M\models T$. Because $A_{\mathrm{real}}$ is fresh and no sentence of $T$ constrains it, $\mathcal M$ has an $L^+$-expansion $\mathcal M^+$ in which $A_{\mathrm{real}}$ is true and another expansion $\mathcal M^-$ in which it is false. Both reducts satisfy every sentence of $T$. Hence $A_{\mathrm{real}}$ fails in one model of $T$ and $\neg A_{\mathrm{real}}$ fails in another, proving (P.14.9h.1). Conditions on response quotients or minimizers are $L$-statements and therefore do not distinguish the two expansions. ∎

<a id="corollary-p149i-maximum-noncircular-pu-completion-target"></a>**Corollary P.14.9i (Maximum Noncircular PU Completion Target).** For a declared scope, PU proves mathematical response completeness only after the following independently checkable gates are discharged:

1. a versioned typed language $L$, exact theory $T_{\mathrm{PU}}\subseteq\operatorname{Sent}(L)$, model semantics, a fixed carrier or foundational-universe convention making the models a set up to $L$-isomorphism, a finite protocol family $\mathfrak P$, and, for every $P$, a fixed finite outcome space $\Omega_P$, response codomain $\Delta(\Omega_P)$, and proved equivalence relation $\sim_P$ are specified independently of the validation data;
2. at least one $L$-structure satisfying every axiom of $T_{\mathrm{PU}}$ is constructed;
3. every registered response map $\mathcal R_P$ is defined and proved total and normalized on every member of $\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{PU}})$; and
4. every two models of $T_{\mathrm{PU}}$ are proved response-equivalent on every $P\in\mathfrak P$:
   $$
   \forall\mathcal M,\mathcal N\in\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{PU}}),\qquad
   \mathcal M\sim_{\mathrm{resp}}\mathcal N.
   $$
   Because item 1 makes the quotient a set and item 2 makes it nonempty, this is equivalent to
   $$
   \left|\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{PU}})/\!\sim_{\mathrm{resp}}\right|=1.
   $$

A single constructed model discharges nonemptiness only; it does not discharge the universal comparison in item 4. Corollary P.14.1k.3.1 may identify a unique PCE-selected candidate, but a unique minimizer alone does not exclude response-distinct nonminimizing models. PU proves global-lift completeness only after it constructs the global restriction map and proves separately that the selected fiber is nonempty and injective modulo global response equivalence. When both results and a structurally justified observable registry are accepted, all PU models lie in one joint registered response class. This still does not prove $A_{\mathrm{real}}$. Identification with observed physical records is an empirical realization-identification result. Violation of an exact consequence or hard-support bound falsifies the tested realization class; a statistical-tail event triggers rejection under the specified evidence rule at its justified error level. Adding $A_{\mathrm{real}}$ as an axiom is a realization postulate; defining the global candidate class, cost, or protocols from the observed target is circular and is excluded by Remark P.14.1k.3.2.

*Proof.* Items 1–4 unpack Definition P.14.9g. Item 2 establishes only $\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{PU}})\ne\varnothing$; item 4 supplies the distinct universal statement needed for a singleton quotient. Corollary P.14.1k.3.1 contributes the selected-minimizer conclusion under its hypotheses but contains no universal quantifier identifying every model with that minimizer. Equation (P.14.9g.3) similarly requires both an ambient witness and uniqueness of its response class. The non-entailment conclusion is Theorem P.14.9h. The empirical statements follow from the derivation-dependency and no-validation-import clauses of a populated accepted registry. ∎
