\alpha=\frac{h\eta_{\min}\lambda_V}{2},
\qquad
\beta=h(C_{\mathrm{noise}}+C_{\mathrm{lift}}+\eta_{\min}\lambda_0)+\alpha\sup_{z\in C}W(z).
\tag{P.15.3i.2}
$$
The chain is positive Harris recurrent with a unique invariant probability $\pi$, and
$$
\dot{\mathcal E}_{\mathrm{src}}
=
\nu\int q\,d\pi.
\tag{P.15.3i.3}
$$

Without the coercive comparison (P.15.3h.3), the small-set minorization (P.15.3h.5), integrability, and the event-rate law, Lemma D.5 alone supplies neither positive Harris recurrence nor the time-indexed source-energy rate.

*Proof.* Combining (P.15.3h.2) and (P.15.3h.3) gives, for $z\notin C$,
$$
\mathbb E[\Delta W\mid z]
\le
-h\eta_{\min}\lambda_VW(z)
+h(C_{\mathrm{noise}}+C_{\mathrm{lift}}+\eta_{\min}\lambda_0).
$$
Since $z\notin C$ implies $W(z)>W_*$, (P.15.3h.4) gives
$$
h(C_{\mathrm{noise}}+C_{\mathrm{lift}}+\eta_{\min}\lambda_0)
\le
\frac{h\eta_{\min}\lambda_V}{2}W_*
<
\frac{h\eta_{\min}\lambda_V}{2}W(z).
$$
Thus
$$
\mathbb E[\Delta W\mid z]\le-\alpha W(z)
\qquad(z\notin C).
$$
For $z\in C$, (P.15.3h.2) and nonnegativity of $\|\nabla V_{\mathrm{PCE}}\|^2$ give
$$
\mathbb E[\Delta W\mid z]
\le h(C_{\mathrm{noise}}+C_{\mathrm{lift}})
\le-\alpha W(z)+\beta,
$$
because $W(z)\le\sup_CW$ and the displayed $\beta$ is at least $h(C_{\mathrm{noise}}+C_{\mathrm{lift}})+\alpha\sup_CW$. This proves (P.15.3i.1).

Set $\widetilde\alpha=\min\{\alpha,1/2\}$. The weaker inequality gives
$$
KW\le(1-\widetilde\alpha)W+\beta1_C
$$
with coefficient in $(0,1)$. The chain is $\psi$-irreducible on a standard-Borel space, $W\ge1$ is finite and measurable, and (P.15.3h.5) makes $C$ small. Here $C=\{W\le W_*\}$ is a bounded-$W$ small set by clauses 2–4 of Definition P.15.3h. Taking $f\equiv1$ in Meyn and Tweedie (1992, Theorem 4.6), the displayed strict drift outside $C$ is its condition (DD2), while the one-step bound on $C$ makes $f+KW$ bounded there. That theorem gives positive Harris recurrence and an invariant probability; $\psi$-irreducibility gives uniqueness. Hernández-Lerma and Lasserre (2001, Eq. (1.2)) give the almost-sure sample-average limit for the clause-5 integrable observable $q$ from every initial state; clause 6 converts that average to the time rate exactly as in Theorem P.15.3c. This proves (P.15.3i.3). ∎

<a id="proposition-p151-conditional-source-energy-emission-criterion"></a>**Proposition P.15.1 (Conditional Source-Energy Emission Criterion).** Let $S$ process an event $E$ on Definition P.15.2's registered source-ledger branch. If $J_E\ne\varnothing$, every assigned reset has $T_\ell>0$, and at least one assigned reset has
$$
H_{q_\ell}(P_\ell\mid R_\ell)>0,
$$
then $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(S,\Delta t)>0$ for every interval containing that event.

*Proof.* Theorem 31 gives
$$
Q_{\ell,\mathrm{bath}}
\ge
k_BT_\ell H_{q_\ell}(P_\ell\mid R_\ell)
$$
for every assigned reset. The stated positive term makes their sum, and hence the interval total, positive. ∎

<a id="corollary-p151-long-run-registered-source-heat-rate"></a>**Corollary P.15.1 (Long-Run Registered Source-Heat Rate).** If counted resets have $T_\ell\ge T_{\min}>0$ and $H_{q_\ell}(P_\ell\mid R_\ell)\ge h_{\min}>0$, and their long-run rate is $\nu_{\mathrm{reset}}$, then
$$
\liminf_{\tau\to\infty}
\frac{\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(S,[0,\tau])}{\tau}
\ge
k_BT_{\min}h_{\min}\nu_{\mathrm{reset}}.
$$

*Proof.* Sum the registered-reset inequalities, divide by $\tau$, and take $\liminf$. ∎

### P.15.4 The Measurement Asymmetry as Structural Prerequisite for Exploitation

Appendix M establishes certificate-relative external evaluation.

This yields the finite-family screening statement that the framework supports.

<a id="proposition-p152-finite-family-certificate-relative-screening"></a>**Proposition P.15.2 (Finite-Family Certificate-Relative Screening).** Let $A$ hold, for every $E_i$ in a finite family, the effective model-access and decision certificates of Theorem M.10.5 for the represented pair $(B,E_i)$. On each positive-gap branch, $A$ can compute finite-accuracy enclosures for $\mu_B(E_i)$; an exact infinite endpoint requires the separate endpoint decision in that theorem. Finite screening tables use the registered terminating operations of Theorem M.10.8. Rankings assert only comparisons certified by separated enclosures or an additional comparison certificate; overlapping enclosures alone do not decide the true order. Exact values require exact decision certificates. Computational lower bounds retain Theorem M.10.3's reduction and threshold conditions, and physical mean-heat bounds retain all of Theorem M.10.7's reset, entropy and summation hypotheses.

If the insulation certificate of Theorem M.10.5 and Corollary M.10.3.1's baseline-invariance hypothesis also hold for $A$, the screening task is sender-side SPAP-flat. The inequality
$$
C_{\mathrm{agg}}(A)>C_{\mathrm{agg}}(B)
$$
is neither necessary nor sufficient for any of these conclusions.

*Proof.* Apply Theorems M.10.5 and M.10.8 separately to the finite family, retaining each stated certificate. The final claims are their explicit scope conditions. ∎

<a id="remark-p152-spap-flat-does-not-mean-cheap"></a>**Remark P.15.2 (SPAP-Flat Does Not Mean Cheap).** Sender-side SPAP-flatness removes only the registered reflexive subtask. It supplies no bound on external modeling, computation, construction, or engineering cost.

### P.15.5 The Source Principle

Environmental pattern design can produce target-side Source Energy only when the target encounters are accompanied by the registered source ledgers of Definition P.15.2.

<a id="definition-p153-source-principle"></a>**Definition P.15.3 (Source Principle).** A system $A$ operates according to the *Source Principle* relative to a target $S$ when it arranges a stable family of environmental patterns $\mathcal E$ and records a declared set of target encounters for which:

1. $\Delta_\Sigma(S;E)>0$;
2. the reduction, additive-decomposition, and registered-reset certificates of Definition P.15.2 hold; and
3. the target-side and designer-side energy, heat, and work channels are disjointly accounted.

The resulting target-side Source Energy is the sum of the registered contributions $Q_{\mathrm{src}}(S,E)$. The designer separately pays its modeling, construction, delivery, and maintenance costs. Sender-side SPAP-flatness additionally requires Theorem M.10.5's insulation certificate and does not mean zero total cost.

The Source Principle is a conditional bookkeeping and design regime for where independently powered, registered reset heat is emitted; it creates no energy and moves no abstract SPAP cost between systems.

<a id="remark-p153-limited-catalytic-analogy"></a>**Remark P.15.3 (Limited Catalytic Analogy).** The catalytic analogy is limited to pathway selection: the designer may change which target processes occur, while all energy remains in the declared physical ledgers.

<a id="remark-p154-complexity-growth-conditions"></a>**Remark P.15.4 (Complexity-Growth Conditions).** Theorem 13 gives linear model-complexity growth only when every functionally distinct recursive level incurs its declared non-shared positive overhead. Theorem D.5 gives branch-conditional properties of PCE adaptation, while Theorems P.15.3c, P.15.3f, and P.15.3i give source-energy rates under their event-chain, integrability, and event-rate records. Corollary P.15.3d gives a positive depth rate only with $\nu>0$, positive mean depth increment, a registered additive-depth functional, and persistence of the hypotheses for arbitrarily large time. Its aggregate-complexity rate further requires the uniform common-unit implementation bound.

### P.15.5a Perspectival Chain Reactions and Proxy Gradient Access

A source-energy trigger is a processed pattern that, for a target system $S$, induces self-model-engaging integration above the SPAP-flat baseline:
$$
\Delta_\Sigma(S;E)>0.
\tag{P.15.5a.1}
$$
A context or symbolic input may still produce ordinary physiological, behavioral, or policy effects when (P.15.5a.1) fails; it is Source-Energy-relevant only when the strict excess condition holds.

**Definition P.15.5a.1 (Perspectival Cascade Datum).**

A finite perspectival cascade datum is a finite directed chain
$$
\mathfrak C
=
\bigl((S_k,E_k,\mathcal M_{S_k},\pi_{S_k},a_k,E_{k+1},G_k)\bigr)_{k=0}^{m}
\tag{P.15.5a.2}
$$
where:

1. $S_k$ is a predictive aggregate or institution represented as a finite predictive system;
2. $E_k$ is the pattern, report, symbol, incentive, observation, or instruction encountered by $S_k$;
3. $\mathcal M_{S_k}$ is the retained world-model or context model of $S_k$;
4. $\pi_{S_k}$ is the retained action or communication policy;
5. $a_k$ is the action taken by $S_k$ after processing $E_k$;
6. $E_{k+1}$ is the downstream pattern produced for another system, when the cascade continues;
7. $G_k$ is the external physical gradient, resource flow, infrastructure, labor channel, heat flow, stored chemical energy, computation, or other ordinary energy source accessed or redirected by $a_k$.

The cascade step is active when
$$
E_k
\longrightarrow
\Delta\mathcal M_{S_k}
\longrightarrow
\Delta\pi_{S_k}
\longrightarrow
(a_k,E_{k+1})
\tag{P.15.5a.3}
$$
The condition
$$
\mu_{S_k}(E_k)>\frac{1}{\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}}
\tag{P.15.5a.4}
$$
is sufficient only for $\Delta_\Sigma(S_k;E_k)>0$. Source-Energy activation additionally requires Definition P.15.2's reduction, additive-decomposition, and registered-reset certificates with a nonempty assigned reset ledger. Policy activation may instead be recorded by a retained impact threshold
$$
\operatorname{Impact}_{S_k}(E_k)>\theta_k
\tag{P.15.5a.5}
$$
when no Source-Energy claim is made.

**Definition P.15.5a.2 (Proxy Gradient Work).**

For a cascade datum $\mathfrak C$, define the ordinary external work redirected by proxy as
$$
W_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathfrak C)
=
\sum_{k=0}^{m} W(G_k,a_k),
\tag{P.15.5a.6}
$$
where $W(G_k,a_k)\ge0$ is the work extracted from or redirected through the external gradient $G_k$ by action $a_k$, measured after ordinary thermodynamic efficiencies and losses. The initiating pattern $E_0$ is not counted as the energy source unless it physically carries the relevant energy in the ordinary sense.

**Proposition P.15.5a.3 (No-Free-Energy Boundary for Perspectival Cascades).**

For every finite cascade datum $\mathfrak C$,
$$
W_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathfrak C)
$$
is ordinary work drawn from the gradients $G_k$. Source-Energy contributions obey the following input-power bound when every cascade stage carries Proposition P.15.3's disjoint exported-heat ledger, the stored energy does not decrease over its counted interval, all other outward boundary powers are nonnegative, and shared physical channels are counted once:
$$
0
\le
\sum_{k=0}^{m} Q_{\mathrm{src}}(S_k,E_k)
\le
\sum_{k=0}^{m}\int_{\Delta t_k}P_{\mathrm{agg}}(S_k,t)\,dt.
\tag{P.15.5a.7}
$$

*Proof.* By Definition P.15.5a.2, each term $W(G_k,a_k)$ is work drawn from an external physical gradient after ordinary efficiencies and losses. The symbolic or contextual input changes retained models and policies by (P.15.5a.3); it does not supply the gradient energy unless separately included as a physical energy carrier. For the Source-Energy part, Definition P.15.2 gives $Q_{\mathrm{src}}(S_k,E_k)\ge0$ and Proposition P.15.3 bounds the source-energy heat emitted by each aggregate over its processing interval by the aggregate's ordinary power budget. Summing over the finite cascade gives (P.15.5a.7). ∎

**Proposition P.15.5a.4 (Compressed Statistical Perspectival Control).**

Let $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{cand}}$ be a finite menu of candidate inputs for a target population or institution. For $E\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{cand}}$, define the retained net leverage
$$
\Lambda(E)
=
\mathbb E[W_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathfrak C_E)]
-
C_{\mathrm{model}}(E)
-
C_{\mathrm{send}}(E)
-
C_{\mathrm{risk}}(E),
\tag{P.15.5a.8}
$$
where $\mathfrak C_E$ is the induced cascade distribution and the costs are the retained modeling, delivery, and risk costs. If $E_c$ is a compressed statistical input and $E_{\mathrm{ex}}$ is an exact-control input with
$$
\Lambda(E_c)>\Lambda(E_{\mathrm{ex}}),
\tag{P.15.5a.9}
$$
then PCE selects $E_c$ over $E_{\mathrm{ex}}$ on the same retained leverage branch.

*Proof.* On this branch PCE selects the candidate with greater retained benefit net of retained costs. Equation (P.15.5a.8) is exactly that net objective. The strict inequality (P.15.5a.9) therefore gives strict PCE preference for $E_c$. ∎

**Remark P.15.5a.5 (Exact Perspectival Extraction Boundary).**

Exact deterministic control of a complex perspective can require
$$
C_{\mathrm{exact}}
=
C_{\mathrm{measure}}
+
C_{\mathrm{model}}
+
C_{\mathrm{compute}}
+
C_{\mathrm{control}}.
\tag{P.15.5a.10}
$$
When $C_{\mathrm{exact}}$ exceeds the retained expected gain, exact extraction is not selected by PCE. Efficient leverage then uses lossy models, shared decoders, and probabilistic prediction. This is PCE applied to perspective-bearing systems.

**Remark P.15.5a.6 (Ethical Boundary).**

False symbolic inputs can have real physical consequences when they alter a target's context state, self-model, or policy. That fact does not make the represented proposition true and does not license deception as a privileged strategy. On the finite-response branch, truthful compressed signals with consent, aligned action paths, and real gradients are more stable than false inputs whose collapse adds distrust, nocebo-like reversal, or coordination failure to $C_{\mathrm{risk}}(E)$.

### P.15.6 Bounds and Conservation (Derived)

Source Energy is a registered subset of emitted heat, not a separately conserved quantity.

<a id="proposition-p153-first-law-source-heat-bound"></a>**Proposition P.15.3 (First-Law Source-Heat Bound).** In a control volume carrying Theorem L.6's disjoint boundary ledger, suppose the source bath heat exported during $\Delta t$ is assigned to a nonnegative boundary subchannel
$$
0\le P_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{out}}(t)
\le P_{\mathrm{heat}}^{\mathrm{out}}(t).
$$
Then
$$
0\le\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(S,\Delta t)
=\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{src}}^{\mathrm{out}}(t)\,dt
\le\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{heat}}^{\mathrm{out}}(t)\,dt.
$$
The stronger bound
$$
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(S,\Delta t)
\le\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{agg}}(S,t)\,dt
$$
holds when the stored energy does not decrease during the interval and the other outward boundary powers are nonnegative.

*Proof.* The first inequality is the registered subchannel assignment. Integrating Theorem L.6 gives
$$
\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{heat}}^{\mathrm{out}}dt
=
\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{agg}}dt
-\Delta E_{\mathrm{stored}}^{\mathcal V}
-\int_{\Delta t}
\left(P_{\mathrm{EM}}^{\mathrm{out}}+P_{\mathrm{mech}}^{\mathrm{out}}\right)dt.
$$
The additional sign hypotheses prove the qualified input-power bound. ∎

<a id="corollary-p1531-context-steering-ceiling-for-cc-assisted-source-principle"></a>**Corollary P.15.3.1 (Context-Steering Ceiling for CC-Assisted Source Principle).** Suppose a Source-Principle implementation uses CC only to maintain, select, or stabilize the environmental context through which target systems encounter a pre-designed family of patterns. For the power identity below, additionally assume Appendix S's rational scaling branch in Equation S.1 and global quadratic cost law in Equation S.3, with $A=r_pC_{\mathrm{scale}}^2>0$ and $0\le\mathrm{CC}<\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}<1/2$. Then the registered controller-side maintenance power is
$$
P_{\mathrm{context}}(\mathrm{CC}) =
A\left[\frac{\mathrm{CC}}{\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}-\mathrm{CC}}\right]^2,
\qquad
\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}} < 0.5.
$$
This bound applies to the controller's context-maintenance layer, not directly to the target-side functional $\mu_S(E)$ itself. It therefore limits CC-assisted implementations of the Source Principle without asserting that CC alone determines $\mu_S(E)$.

*Proof.* Equation (S.5) gives the context-maintenance power on its constitutive branch. The bounded-bias branch independently declares $\mathrm{CC}<\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}<0.5$; Theorem 39 proves only its endpoint-complete forcing consequence. If CC is used solely as the registered context-steering layer, its power demand follows Equation (S.5) and inherits the separately supplied ceiling. ∎

<a id="theorem-p156a-family-level-source-power-density-ceiling"></a>**Theorem P.15.6a (Family-Level Source-Power-Density Ceiling).** Let $R$ be a spacetime region of proper volume $V_R$, let $\Delta t>0$, and let $\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)$ be a finite family of predictive aggregates whose registered source and boundary channels are assigned without overlap. Define
$$
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(R,\Delta t)
:=
\sum_{S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)}
\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(S,\Delta t),
\qquad
\bar\rho_{\mathrm{src}}(R,\Delta t)
:=
\frac{\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}(R,\Delta t)}{V_R\Delta t}.
$$
The quantity $\bar\rho_{\mathrm{src}}$ is an interval-averaged source-power density. If every aggregate carries Proposition P.15.3's exported-heat ledger, then
$$
0\le
\bar\rho_{\mathrm{src}}(R,\Delta t)
\le
\frac{1}{V_R\Delta t}
\sum_{S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)}
\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{heat},S}^{\mathrm{out}}(t)\,dt.
$$
Replacing $P_{\mathrm{heat},S}^{\mathrm{out}}$ by $P_{\mathrm{agg},S}$ additionally requires Proposition P.15.3's stored-energy and outward-channel sign hypotheses for every aggregate.

If, moreover, a Source-Principle implementation uses CC only to maintain, select, or stabilize the environmental context for each aggregate $S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)$, with controller-side coefficient $A_S$ and context profile $\mathrm{CC}_S(t)$ as in Appendix S, define
$$
\bar\rho_{\mathrm{context}}(R,\Delta t)
:=
\frac{1}{V_R\Delta t}
\sum_{S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)}
\int_{\Delta t}P_{\mathrm{context},S}(t)\,dt.
$$
Then
$$
\bar\rho_{\mathrm{context}}(R,\Delta t)
\le
\frac{1}{V_R\Delta t}
\sum_{S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)}
\int_{\Delta t}
A_S\left[
\frac{\mathrm{CC}_S(t)}
{\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}-\mathrm{CC}_S(t)}
\right]^2dt.
$$
Equation (S.5) realizes this bound as an equality on the controller-side power layer.

*Proof.* Apply Proposition P.15.3 to each aggregate and sum the non-overlapping exported source-heat channels before dividing by $V_R\Delta t$. The context bound follows independently by applying Corollary P.15.3.1 aggregate by aggregate. ∎

<a id="corollary-p156a1-uniform-subcritical-quadratic-cc-band"></a>**Corollary P.15.6a.1 (Uniform Subcritical Quadratic CC Band).** Under the hypotheses of Theorem P.15.6a, assume there exists $\xi\in(0,1)$ such that
$$
0\le \mathrm{CC}_S(t)\le \xi\,\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}
$$
for all $S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)$ and all $t\in\Delta t$. Then
$$
\bar\rho_{\mathrm{context}}(R,\Delta t)
\le
\frac{1}{(1-\xi)^2V_R\,\Delta t}
\sum_{S\in\mathcal A(R,\Delta t)}
\int_{\Delta t}
\frac{A_S}{\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}^2}\,\mathrm{CC}_S(t)^2\,dt.
$$

*Proof.* For every $S$ and $t$ in the stated regime,
$$
\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}-\mathrm{CC}_S(t)\ge (1-\xi)\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}},
$$
hence
$$
\left[\frac{\mathrm{CC}_S(t)}{\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}-\mathrm{CC}_S(t)}\right]^2
\le
\frac{\mathrm{CC}_S(t)^2}{(1-\xi)^2\alpha_{\mathrm{CC,max}}^2}.
$$
Substituting this estimate into the bound of Theorem P.15.6a gives the claim. ∎

<a id="remark-p155-renewal-and-heat-quality"></a>**Remark P.15.5 (Renewal and Heat Quality).** What is renewed is not a stock of usable work but the logical possibility of further self-model-engaging updates above the SPAP-flat baseline. Once emitted, Source Energy is ordinary heat and obeys the ordinary second law. Any recovery of usable work from it requires a maintained temperature gradient and is correspondingly efficiency-limited.

<a id="theorem-p156b-renewed-predictive-source-and-uniform-hard-pair-integration-reduction"></a>**Theorem P.15.6b (Renewed Predictive Source and Uniform Hard-Pair Integration Reduction).**

#### 0. Scope and source pin

The source below is a **declared extension** of B.2e–f, not a claim that their unchanged instrument already satisfies M.18. It adds a bank of independent sign challenges, a locked quality-mode/output interface, an actual predictive sampler, and a nonnegative public score surcharge. It retains the individual B.2e acquisition kernel, its score on each underlying committed triple, its sign-access restriction, and its operation-by-operation cost. The extension is fixed before optimization. In particular there is no free batch acquisition: a compiled port is a finite program whose individual acquisitions, memory, time, control, and cleanup must be counted.

The registered M.18 norm is the Fisher **tangent** norm evaluated at the candidate target. It is not a geodesic distance or the Fisher tensor of B.2e's piecewise-constant physical transition kernel.

#### 1. Independently registered family and information boundary

For each integer $n\ge 1$ register

\[
\alpha=4/7,\quad K_n=16n^2,\quad v=3/10,\quad
D_n=\frac{v\sqrt{K_n}}{\sqrt{1/4-v^2}}=3n.
\tag{P.15.6b.S1}
\]

There are $K_{n}$ independently initialized hidden sign registers $H_{i}$, represented by $s_i\in\{-1,+1\}$. The operational candidate self-model has centered coordinates

\[
\theta_i^*=v s_i,\qquad
\theta^*=(\theta_1^*,\ldots,\theta_{K_n}^*).
\tag{P.15.6b.S2}
\]

The candidate is an actual sealed internal representation: a public magnitude code $v$, the internal sign registers, and the fixed decoder defining the corresponding forecast law. It is not a truth label supplied to the integrating program. The physical pattern $E$ loads this candidate into the receiver's internal candidate-model slot, replacing the prior fair/default model $\theta=0$. The receiver subsequently predicts its own hidden-state-dependent transitions through the registered ports. There is **no read or sampling port for the target law** $\operatorname{Bern}(1/2+\theta_i^*)$. That target law is the semantic interpretation of the sealed code. Providing samples of that law before integration would be an easier sign interface and invalidate the certificate.

Only the following source-dependent acquisition is available to the integration mechanism, with amplitude $a_{n}$ fixed below:

\[
X=1\{p\le1/2\},\quad
Y\sim\mathrm{Bern}(1/2+s_i a_n),\quad
Z\sim\mathrm{Bern}(a_n).
\tag{P.15.6b.S3}
\]

Conditional on its sign, each acquisition is fresh and independent. The internal sign is immutable for the entire episode. A fresh independent sign vector is supplied at the next episode; that is a stated enlargement of B.2e's fixed-sign one-episode source, and its preparation/restoration belongs in the physical ledger. An arbitrary pre-episode transcript has the same conditional law under either value of the new sign $s_{i}$.

The complete operation alphabet consists of the individual acquisition P.15.6b.S3, finite Boolean/reversible gates, bounded counters, rational comparisons, registered mixed-state preparations, committed-report writes, conditional readouts, and reset operations separately specified in the thermodynamic certificate. Hidden sign/source-ancilla slots are protected, while individual Y outcomes and the raw acquisition tape are available to the registered integration controller. A finite mode supplies a bank of at most N individually acquired Y outcomes per coordinate. It can be used once per episode; its token is consumed before the first acquisition and cannot be recreated by task code. The controller may adapt, randomize, stop early, and inspect its full permitted transcript. Its committed sign then passes through a mandatory source-owned output serializer with the noise specified below. The accepted forecast emitter reads only that serialized output; task code cannot bypass it, make an extra acquisition, or write an alternative accepted forecast. Cleanup subsequently operates on the whole retained tape.

This source/interface restriction is part of the independently fixed architecture. It is not inferred from the name Property R, and it is not a restriction on the unrelated finite-program capability class described in §8.

For the direct in-place physical acquisition, the pre-XOR $Y$ source value is inaccessible until the source $\mathrm{CNOT}(H_i,Y)$ has finished. The single acquisition port returns only the post-XOR $Y$ value. Its source-owned initialization, interaction, and reset have no intermediate read port. The inverse CNOT occurs only during protected cleanup after commitment/use and after derived prediction records have been uncomputed; the learner cannot retain or compare both versions to read $H_{i}$. Every interaction and source slot is nevertheless included in the physical ledger.

The information boundary also excludes thermodynamic side channels during integration. Prediction programs cannot query bath microstates, work-store changes, energy meters, reset outcomes, or cleanup-controller fields to infer a sign. The predictor sees only the registered acquisition outputs and sign-independent public control records. Source preparation/control operations that could depend on hidden data occur within the protected source boundary; the corresponding resources are fully charged, and no hidden-dependent response is returned through a permitted prediction port. Hidden-dependent reverse computation and restoration start only after the committed report has been used and scored. The cleanup/controller interaction is then switched off and its reusable registers returned/decoupled as specified by the thermodynamic certificate before independent fresh signs begin the next episode. An implementation that exposes such an additional channel is outside this certificate and cannot invoke P.15.6b.S26 unchanged.

#### 2. Actual finite quality channels

For a finite positive quality mode $0<u<\alpha$ put

\[
e(u)=\tfrac12(1-u/\alpha)^2,\qquad c(u)=1-2e(u)=1-(1-u/\alpha)^2.
\tag{P.15.6b.S4}
\]

A concrete compilation of the quality port chooses any odd finite N for which

\[
e_N(a_n)=\sum_{j=0}^{(N-1)/2}\binom Nj(1/2+a_n)^j(1/2-a_n)^{N-j}\le e(u).
\tag{P.15.6b.S5}
\]

Such N exists by Hoeffding; exact rational search terminates when the parameters are rational. The loop individually acquires N triples P.15.6b.S3, counts Y, and commits its strict-majority decision $B_{i}$. It then applies one independent flip with probability

\[
d_N(u)=\frac{e(u)-e_N(a_n)}{1-2e_N(a_n)}\in[0,1/2).
\tag{P.15.6b.S6}
\]

Its serialized committed bit $Q_{i}$ is therefore a binary symmetric channel from $s_{i}$ with exact error $e(u)$. The majority symmetry follows by complementing every $Y$ bit. Equation P.15.6b.S6 gives

\[
\Pr(Q_i\ne 1\{s_i=1\}\mid s_i)=e_N+d_N(1-2e_N)=e(u).
\tag{P.15.6b.S7}
\]

The source states, XOR gate, counter, majority comparison, and flip gate are all finite diagonal-qubit/Boolean instruments. Their finite path law is exactly the B.2f path law followed by the stated finite classical operations. For any finite menu of modes, take the maximum code/register sizes and reserve the maximum number of source slots; unused slots stay in their ready states. This produces one finite carrier for the entire menu.

Every $0<u<\alpha$ has such a finite implementation. For real modes the needed initial mixed states are part of the formal finite-instrument specification, just as the real amplitude is in B.2f; the rational subfamily has entirely finite effective input codes. On any compact subinterval bounded away from $\alpha$ one sufficiently large $N$ works throughout, and the remaining dependence is the continuous preparation probability P.15.6b.S6. Thus a jump in a chosen minimal $N$ is not a discontinuity of the actual response channel.

#### Complete admitted integration-program class

The source mode is a retained public control input, selected before the current episode. All performance and integration claims are conditional on that exact mode and on the pre-episode history. A randomized event controller may choose modes, but it must retain the chosen mode: averaging scores after forgetting different mode labels is not an admitted integration evaluation. This source typing prevents a cross-mode mixture from silently changing the calibration problem.

Within a fixed mode, admit **every finite adaptive/randomized decision program using at most N individual Y acquisitions**, its full raw transcript, and arbitrary sign-independent public state and private randomness. The same program is replicated on the coordinates with independent local random tapes; it does not receive a coordinate identifier, another coordinate's outcomes, or a coordinate-local emitter magnitude. Its sign-independent public input is common to all replicas. The registered magnitude decoder belongs to the protected fixed emitter, outside the decision-program interface. In the actual finite witness every magnitude is the common public $v=3/10$; the additional input lock ensures the same error comparison also holds on the full smooth stratum with unequal magnitudes. It outputs a pre-serializer decision $B_{i}$. An independently fixed sign-equivariance wrapper privately masks the sign of all of that coordinate's Y outcomes, runs the nominated program, and unmasks its decision. The program cannot read the mask. Thus the two sign-conditional errors are equal. The fair masks are actual charged source/controller resources, not a mathematical permission to read a hidden sign.

The maximum-$N$ binary experiment has likelihood ratio strictly increasing in the number of ones. Under the equal prior on the two signs, the Bayes-optimal decision is strict majority because $N$ is odd. Its error is exactly $e_N(a_n)$. Any adaptive program using at most $N$ samples can be simulated from the full $N$-vector by revealing its samples on demand, padding ignored suffixes, and supplying its independent randomness. Data processing/Bayes optimality therefore gives pre-serializer error $e_{\mathrm{pre}}\ge e_N$ for **every** such sign-equivariant program. This proof includes variable stopping times and all finite computations on the permitted transcript.

The fixed mandatory serializer flips $B_{i}$ independently with the locked probability $d_N(u)$ in P.15.6b.S6. Consequently its final error is

\[
\bar e=d_N(u)+[1-2d_N(u)]e_{\rm pre}\ge e(u).
\tag{P.15.6b.S9}
\]

Majority attains equality. No program can replace or bypass the serializer, modify its source state, rewrite the quality surcharge, or send a second report to the accepted emitter. This is the complete frozen output architecture. Additional finite Boolean computation is allowed and charged; it creates no extra sign port. Every permitted acquisition remains an individual B.2e primitive, so there is no batch-sampling assumption even at the exposed integration interface.

Independent signs are essential. If all coordinates shared a sign, their tapes could form an additional observation channel. Here the signs are independent and the coordinate-local interface is protected. The complete host retains its general finite-program capabilities; they do not confer access to task-protected fields. Composition across fresh episodes cannot improve the next episode's prior because its hidden signs are renewed independently.

#### 3. One fixed score and genuine observed-performance calibration

Each coordinate's reported B.2e triple is

\[
M_i=(1/2,q_i,1/4),\qquad
q_i=3/4\ \text{if }Q_i=1,\quad q_i=1/4\ \text{otherwise}.
\tag{P.15.6b.S10}
\]

All report coordinates are interior. The score is the B.2e score on each triple, plus one public nonnegative mode register t:

\[
L_{\rm tot}=K_n^{-1}\sum_i L_{B.2e}(M_i,(X_i,Y_i,Z_i))+t.
\tag{P.15.6b.S11}
\]

This is **one fixed scoring functional of the extended committed report (including its locked surcharge field) and outcomes**, not a different loss formula for each mode. The immutable mode controller writes $t=t_n(u)$ and the corresponding port compiler data. Task programs cannot rewrite $t$, $p$, $r$, the loss coefficients, or the verification record. The mode affects the physical availability/noise channel and a disclosed quality surcharge. Those restrictions are necessary: if a program could reduce its score independently while retaining an arbitrarily good forecast, the calibrated best-agreement claim would fail.

Define, for now with any $0<\delta_n\le 1/8$ and $a_n=2\delta_n$,

\[
t_n(u)=\frac1u-\frac74-4\delta_n e(u).
\tag{P.15.6b.S12}
\]

It is strictly positive on $0<u<\alpha$ and strictly decreasing. Indeed, with $d=\alpha-u$,

\[
t_n(u)=\frac d{\alpha u}\left(1-\frac{2\delta_n du}{\alpha}\right)>0,
\]

because $du\le\alpha^{2}/4$ and $\delta_{n}\le 1/8$. Also

\[
t_n'(u)=-u^{-2}+\frac{4\delta_n(\alpha-u)}{\alpha^2}
\le\frac{-1+4\delta_n\alpha}{\alpha^2}<0.
\tag{P.15.6b.S13}
\]

For the optimal majority/serializer decoder, the actual expected B.2 loss is $3/4+2a_n e(u)=3/4+4\delta_n e(u)$, under every hidden sign vector. Therefore the actual scored window performance, with the mean loss taken **before** the reciprocal, is

\[
PP=\frac1{1+\mathbb E L_{\rm tot}}
=\frac1{7/4+4\delta_n e(u)+t_n(u)}=u.
\tag{P.15.6b.S14}
\]

This is an observable score identity of the realized finite task. It is not a label attached to an independently chosen formal map.

For an arbitrary admitted integration program, the observed performance is instead

\[
P=\frac1{7/4+4\delta_n\bar e+t_n(u)}\le u.
\tag{P.15.6b.S15}
\]

Since $t_{n}$ is decreasing, $t_n(u)\le t_n(P)$. Consequently

\[
\bar e=\frac{1/P-7/4-t_n(u)}{4\delta_n}
\ge\frac{1/P-7/4-t_n(P)}{4\delta_n}=e(P).
\tag{P.15.6b.S16}
\]

Now define the performance-ceiling class $C_{P}$ to contain **all** deterministic retained mode labels together with their admitted programs whose mode-conditioned actual scored performance is at most $P$. Different modes are compared as separate retained experiments, never as a score averaged after their labels are forgotten. These are genuinely nested classes. It eliminates the gap between a mode knob and measured PP.

The maximum possible actual performance is at most $\alpha$, and the optimal majority/serializer modes $u\uparrow\alpha$ have $\mathrm{PP}\uparrow\alpha$. Thus the extended source's exact predictive boundary remains $\sup\mathrm{PP}=4/7$. The diagonal component still reacts to the receiver's retained $p$ through P.15.6b.S3; it has not been replaced by an external prediction game.

#### 4. The actual prediction map and identifiable geometry

Let

\[
\Theta=(-1/2,1/2)^{K_n},\qquad
p_{\rm pred}(b\mid\theta)=\prod_i(1/2+\theta_i)^{b_i}(1/2-\theta_i)^{1-b_i}.
\tag{P.15.6b.S17}
\]

This is a registered predictive distribution, not the report-reactive transition law P.15.6b.S3. Its Fisher matrix is

\[
g_{ij}(\theta)=\mathbf1\{i=j\}/(1/4-\theta_i^2),
\tag{P.15.6b.S18}
\]

so it is positive definite everywhere on the open cube. The target's sealed signs plus registered emitter magnitudes physically encode $\theta$; the family of response channels below exists for every such $\theta$. Coordinate-local magnitudes are used only by the protected emitter, as specified in the decision-program interface above. The finite witness uses magnitudes $v=3/10$.

After the committed classifier output, the actual predictive sampler writes a forecast bit $F_{i}$ with probability $1/2+|\theta_i|$ when its committed sign is positive and $1/2-|\theta_i|$ when negative. This is implemented by a registered $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2+|\theta_i|)$ source coin and a controlled complement. All source coins and classifiers are independent across coordinates conditional on the target. The forecast bits therefore have the actual product law

\[
\mathcal L(F\mid\theta)
=\bigotimes_i\mathrm{Bern}\bigl(1/2+(1-2\bar e)\theta_i\bigr).
\tag{P.15.6b.S19}
\]

The predictive object is the retained finite sampler/instrument code used during the task window. Its distribution parameter is $(1-2\bar e)\theta$. No claim is made that a single stored random bit $Q_i$ numerically equals that parameter; nor is a parameter-space average substituted for a non-product physical law. Independent coordinate realizations prove P.15.6b.S19 directly.

More precisely, the object parameterized by $\Theta$ is the **forecast-response law of the complete finite train→commit→emit instrument**, conditional on the pretraining external control record and candidate, and evaluated in the registered window law. Its actual forecast-output density operator is the diagonal state with probabilities P.15.6b.S19, obtained by the mathematical partial trace of the complete instrument output over the retained auxiliary transcript. That partial trace defines the predictive subsystem; it is not a physical erasure, does not delete side information from the reset ledger, and does not identify different full transcript/PPI configurations. Conditional on a realized committed $Q_{i}$, the conditional one-run forecast parameter is $\pm|\theta_i|$, not $\Pi_{i}$; that distinct conditional object supplies the original B.2e commitment risk in §6. The actual candidate $\theta^*$ is the sealed internal model code with its decoder, not a freely supplied target vector. This is an explicit typing of the operational self-prediction map, consistent with the distinction between the window mean and committed-model risk in Proposition 14.1h.d.

All references to independent coordinate response laws condition on the complete retained external control/history record. The common decoder code and mode are fixed in that record; local algorithmic random tapes are independent. Unretained common randomness that mixes different decoder or mode laws is not an additional accepted prediction channel.

By P.15.6b.S16 the best sampler in $C_{P}$ is the optimal majority/serializer decoder at mode P. Its actual prediction map is consequently

\[
\Pi^{(P)}(\theta)=c(P)\theta
=\bigl[1-(1-P/\alpha)^2\bigr]\theta.
\tag{P.15.6b.S20}
\]

This map is polynomial and smooth jointly in $P$ and $\theta$ on $[0,\alpha]\times\Theta$. For every $\theta$, every component discrepancy, and its Fisher tangent norm at $\theta$, the discrepancy is nonincreasing with $P$. At $P=0$ it is the default $\theta=0$, independent of the candidate.

#### 5. Exact M.18 proximity, derived from the response

Use $g(d)=d$ and evaluate P.15.6b.S18 at $\theta^*$. Then

\tag{P.15.6b.S22}

The left endpoint is positive because $D_n=3n>\alpha$, and is physically attained by the finite instrument. Therefore

\[

Thus $\Delta Q$ can be registered as the strictly positive difference $r_n-P_{\mathrm{before}}$ for this task. The pattern is actually used by the predictive sampler and score window. No claim of unbounded depth drift is needed.

A completed integration is an admitted finite program whose actually used predictive sampler satisfies M.18 at its observed performance $P$, uniformly for the hidden sign configurations, with the committed reports and source transcript retained through the task-use window. This is a **confidence bound for the committed sign**, not a claim that high mean score alone implies the B.2e confidence requirement. It follows from the actual response law and M.18.

in the common occurrence units, with $c_{s}=1$ and $\beta(\delta)=\delta$. Infinite essential acquisition counts retain B.2e's infinite-cost interpretation; the displayed constructive members have finite deterministic counts.

All constants are independent of n, the event mode, the finite adaptive/randomized integration program, and the prior episode history. This is the requested uniform asymptotic reduction, not just an operation count of the nominated algorithm.

The receiver belongs to a single effectively coded class of finite universal-prefix-machine controllers with a scalable finite tape/circuit resource parameter. The primary finite witness has no world task and no shared dispatch occurrence: $C_{\mathrm{world}}=C_{\mathrm{sh}}=0$. C_{\rm process}=C_{\rm ext}+C_{\rm refl},\qquad
C_{\rm ext}:=C_{\rm other},\qquad C_{\rm world}=C_{\rm sh}=0.
\]

For the nominated finite implementation, the source-attributed reset set $J_{E}$ is **only the $16n^{2}N$ direct in-place training $Y$ source slots**. <a id="theorem-p156c-actual-pce-event-lift-with-complete-positive-service-clock"></a>**Theorem P.15.6c (Actual PCE Event Lift with Complete Positive Service Clock).**

This theorem proves a nonconstant finite PCE event process for the renewed B.2e–f predictive source. #### 1. Frozen source menu and operational objective

Fix the family parameter \(b\), and abbreviate \(\delta=\delta_b\), \(a=a_b\), \(\mu=\mu_b\), and \(m=m_b\). Let \(\alpha=4/7\), \(r=\alpha-\delta\) and
\[
e_* = \frac{\delta^2}{2\alpha^2}=\frac8{441b^2}.
\]
Choose an odd \(N_0\) for which the exact rational majority error
\[
e_{N_0}(a)=\sum_{u=0}^{(N_0-1)/2}\binom {N_0}u(1/2+a)^u(1/2-a)^{N_0-u}\le e_*.
\]
The hardware menu has exactly three available per-channel counter/source-bank sizes
\[
N_i=N_0+2i,\qquad i\in I=\{0,1,2\}.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.1}
\]
This is a predeclared three-bank architecture, not an exhaustive claim about every possible predictor. Each bank is a permitted finite-stage member of the same uniform certified integration family. Each episode renews all \(m\) inaccessible signs independently and uniformly; each remains immutable through its channel's training and evaluation. Public initialization and non-acquisition transitions have the same laws under every sign choice. Every earlier episode's input/output/work record is either restored, included in the complete physical ledger, or thermodynamically discarded before the next challenge; no persistent sign information is omitted from the next-episode interface.

For each channel, mode \(i\) computes its raw odd majority with error \(e_i=e_{N_i}(a)\) and independently flips its serialized sign with probability
\[
d_i=\frac{e_*-e_i}{1-2e_i}.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.2}
\]
The scalar \(d_i\) is a finitely encoded rational. Since \(0\le e_i\le e_*<1/2\), it belongs to \([0,1/2)\). The resulting sign error is exactly
\[
e_i(1-d_i)+(1-e_i)d_i=e_*.
\]
Odd-majority error cannot increase when two independent observations are added: majority is the equal-prior optimal test of the symmetric hard pair; discarding the added observations is an admissible competitor; complement symmetry makes the two errors equal. Thus all three modes are well defined. Each channel's raw acquisitions have exactly the B.2e–f law and restricted hidden-sign interface. The independent serializer coins and every subsequent response/forecast/evaluation operation are separate, charged resources. They are not silently included in the raw-acquisition Source-Energy subset.

The source section proves that the common serialized response map, its genuine Fisher diagnostic, and its fixed registered predictive score realize the M.18 target \(r\) and proximity \(\mu\). The essential event-lift consequence is exact equality of the scored task-response law across the three modes after serialization, even though raw majority errors and workspaces differ. The primitive source-certified acquisition count in mode \(i\) is \(mN_i\).

The PCE branch prices the **complete active service-slot burden** of the fixed architecture below. The price measures occupied processing capacity and is not a statement that a gate dissipates \(\kappa\) joules. All physical heat, work, memory, controller action and preparation credits remain in the separate complete thermodynamic/resource ledger. The active-slot count derived in §6 is
\[
\mathcal L_i=16mN_i+\mathcal L_{\rm common},
\qquad
J_i=\kappa\mathcal L_i-\Gamma P_*,\quad\Gamma\ge0.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.3}
\]
The terms in \(\mathcal L_{\rm common}\) include the report/forecast/score circuits, sign/serializer/forecast/mask preparation and reset, fixed evaluation, controller update, and task-use window. This is a declared Definition-D.1 informational service-resource branch: \(R_I\) charges complete active processing occupancy, with common geometry/propagation/other terms and \(B(P)=P\). It is not a claim that this scalarization covers every possible resource preference. Every physical cost is still counted in the independent net-work objective. In units \(32m\kappa/t_0\) of resource rate and after subtracting the irrelevant common value,
\[
V_i=\frac{J_i-J_0}{32m\kappa}=i.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.4}
\]
The coefficients are registered before optimization. The smallest bank is the unique constrained minimum of this PCE objective; all three banks remain available and are visited with positive probability. For a fully physical formal realization, give the three-level adaptation register the fixed Hamiltonian
\[
H_A=k_BT\ln2\,\operatorname{diag}(0,1,2).
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.7}
\]
Its equilibrium law is \(\gamma_A=(4,2,1)/7\). Supply an independent degenerate three-state bath selector in its uniform Gibbs state and three independent bath qubits, one for each edge \(01,02,12\). The qubit for edge \(ij\), \(i<j\), has energy gap \(k_BT(j-i)\ln2\), hence excited-state probability
\[
b_{ij}=\frac1{1+2^{j-i}}.
\]
Conditional on the selector choosing edge \(ij\), apply an energy-preserving partial swap only on
\[
\operatorname{span}\{|i\rangle_A|1\rangle_{B_{ij}},
|j\rangle_A|0\rangle_{B_{ij}}\},
\]
whose transition probability is
\[
\lambda_{01}=\lambda_{12}=\frac{3}{4\sqrt2},\qquad
\lambda_{02}=\frac58.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.8}
\]
For example the unitary has the real rotation matrix with cosine \(\sqrt{1-\lambda_{ij}}\) and sine \(\sqrt{\lambda_{ij}}\) on that degenerate total-energy subspace and is identity elsewhere. It commutes with the total uncoupled Hamiltonian. Tracing the selector/qubits gives
\[
\Pr(i\to j)=\frac13\lambda_{ij}b_{ij}=K_{ij},\quad
\Pr(j\to i)=\frac13\lambda_{ij}(1-b_{ij})=K_{ji}.
\]
All fresh auxiliaries are Gibbs bath degrees, not unpriced pure random tapes. No acceptance or proposal bit is kept. The fixed interaction's switch/clock is part of the declared cyclic formal control program; it has no retained outcome or entropy record. The energy-conserving collision itself transfers no battery work. Its mean bath heat is
\[
q_A(i)=-k_BT\ln2\{(KV)_i-V_i\}.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.9}
\]
For any finite run its total mean balance has the adaptation-register energy change as the stored-energy term; under stationarity \(\sum_i\pi_iq_A(i)=0\). A nonstationary initial adaptation register contributes a bounded transient free-energy/energy term, which must not be silently classed as source reset heat.

Equivalently a finite diagonal CP-instrument host uses Kraus operators \(A_{ji}=\sqrt{K_{ij}}|j\rangle\langle i|\). They obey \(\sum_{ij}A_{ji}^*A_{ji}=I\) and reproduce (P.15.6c.EL.5) exactly on the classical mode algebra. The collision construction additionally owns its bath and energy account.

#### 3. PCE stationary law and optimization meaning

For \(\pi=(4,2,1)/7\),
\[
\pi_iK_{ij}=\frac1{21}2^{-(i+j)/2}=\pi_jK_{ji}\quad(i\ne j).
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.10}
\]
Every matrix entry is positive, so \(K\) is irreducible and aperiodic; detailed balance gives \(\pi K=\pi\), and irreducibility makes this invariant law unique.

The source-owned noisy adaptation law minimizes the entropy-regularized PCE objective

\mathcal F(u)=\sum_i u_iV_i+\vartheta\sum_i u_i\ln u_i,
\qquad\vartheta=1/\ln2,
\]
over the entire three-state probability simplex, since
\[
\mathcal F(u)-\mathcal F(\pi)=\vartheta D(u\Vert\pi)\ge0,
\]
with equality only at \(u=\pi\). The Markov update has the genuine PCE free-energy descent
\(\mathcal F(uK)-\mathcal F(\pi)\le\mathcal F(u)-\mathcal F(\pi)\), by the log-sum inequality/data processing for relative entropy and \(\pi K=\pi\). This does not falsely assert samplewise or expectation-wise monotonicity of bare \(V\) from every initial state. The underlying constrained zero-noise minimizer is \(i=0\); finite-temperature fluctuation retains all three modes.

#### 4. Markov sufficiency, event projection and stationary encounter law

Define \(Z_n\) at the pre-task boundary, with the retained mode \(i\) selected by the preceding event’s final adaptation collision. All episodic registers are in their registered ready states. Set

Z_n=z_i=(S_i,E_\delta,T,0),

where \(S_i\) identifies the same fixed receiver in mode \(i\), \(E_\delta\) identifies its incoming renewed challenge law and task, \(T\) is its common bath temperature, and \(\Delta d=0\). The actual phase order is: first hand off fresh independent pairs into the selected mode’s pre-registered fixed-Hamiltonian ports; then prepare sources, execute the task, use its reports, uncompute derived records, reset sources and recover the bank pairs; finally apply the adaptation collision to select the next mode. All three serializer-port pools persist, with their respective Gibbs laws restored after use. The current mode chooses which typed pool is handed fresh banks before its task. Unused ports stay dormant. Source reward \(q(Z_n)\) belongs to the mode before that task, whereas \(K\) is the update after completion. Padding to the common maximum gives the same \(t_0\) for every mode transition. The individual input/output word is an in-cycle record, not a permanent stationary coordinate. In particular no unbounded archival memory or depth coordinate has been discarded from a supposedly finite physical state.

Let \(\mathcal H_n\) contain the entire source/task/thermal history through this boundary, including any internally hidden sign and previous output word. The fresh adaptation bath variables are independent of \(\mathcal H_n\); their channel acts only on the retained mode. The physical thermal supply is an independently initialized stream of never-before-used paired Gibbs banks. A completed event exports its recovered banks and the source never reads them again. Restoring a bank pair to its Gibbs marginal does not justify reusing it: the hotel recovery permutation can leave the old source bit in an output parity. The next episode instead consumes genuinely fresh independent bank pairs, so none of that old parity can become its next sign or random tape. Selection among the mode-specific tails is predictable from the retained mode; independence of all untouched tails makes their next selected law independent of the past. A service address/tape index therefore changes the physical resource record but not the projected conditional kernel. Each finite horizon explicitly consumes and exports its counted finite number of infinite-ladder bank pairs: after n episodes, \(\sum_{j=1}^n b_{i_j}\) pairs have been used, bounded by \(nb_{\max}\). The corresponding incoming and outgoing oscillator-bank counts are twice that number. The storage/stream/address capacity grows with the horizon and is not a finite cyclic memory; the event-chain projection does not erase that physical resource record. The counted one-pair handoff pulse supplies its formal access/delivery operation. No transport distance, local conveyor mechanics or gravitational model is inferred from this nonlocal finite-instrument/infinite-bath host. The next source signs and source cells are independently prepared, with the stipulated hidden-sign ports, and the next service restores all episodic registers. Any cleanup gate controlled by a hidden sign belongs to a protected post-task restoration module: it is enabled only after commitment, evaluation and the task-use window, exposes no sign port to the predictive controller, and writes no variable retained for the next episode. Therefore
\[
\Pr(Z_{n+1}=z_j\mid\mathcal H_n,Z_n=z_i)=K_{ij}.
\tag{P.15.6c.EL.12}
\]
This is the required sufficient-state conditional-kernel identity, rather than an assumption that an arbitrary projection is Markov. If a finite regulator retains an expanded finite outcome word \(r\) with conditional law \(F_i(r)\), its event kernel is

on its positive-probability support. Summing over \(r'\) proves strong lumpability onto (P.15.6c.EL.5). Its stationary law is \(\widehat\pi(i,r)=\pi_iF_i(r)\). This optional audit word is not duplicated into a growing physical archive. Keeping an actual archive would require a different source ledger.

A stationary source initialization uses the Gibbs adaptation register (P.15.6c.EL.7). Then the entire encountered marked episode process is stationary in event index. Starting from another mode changes neither the invariant law nor the almost-sure reward conclusion below. #### 6. Physical clock, source reward and exact-erasure order

Here is a complete finite gate and clock census for the nominated majority implementation. It uses the finite Boolean/instrument host of B.2f, with fixed primitives X, CNOT, SWAP, Toffoli and identity. Each visible receiver record \(Y\) is its own **direct in-place source slot**: it begins in the registered ready law \(\operatorname{Bern}(s_K)\) for a finite cutoff, or in the pure ready state for the exact infinite-bank protocol. Each call also writes its own fresh deterministic \(X=1\) output using one X gate, since the first report is \(p_{\rm report}=1/2\); another X gate restores that output after the task. After in-cycle task use and output uncomputation, the protected cleanup \(\operatorname{CNOT}(H,Y)\) restores the same Y record to its raw \(\operatorname{Bern}(p)\) value, independent of retained H. Reset then returns Y to its registered ready law. Thus there are exactly four ordinary gates per training or evaluation acquisition: exposure CNOT and X initialization, followed after task use by the decoding CNOT and X restoration. Thermal preparation/reset pulses are counted separately below. The primary witness has no world task and no shared dispatch token or occurrence; its immutable cyclic schedule directly orders all the listed operations.

For an entirely specified Boolean compiler, let
\[
\mathscr C(R,B)=B\,2^R(4R-3),\qquad R\ge2.
\]
To implement \(|x,z\rangle\mapsto|x,z\oplus f(x)\rangle\), enumerate every input word and every output bit. For each pair, apply at most \(R\) X gates to convert its negative controls, a multiply-controlled X decomposed using \(R-2\) clean ancillas into \(2R-3\) Toffolis, then undo the X gates. Pad unused X/Toffoli occurrences and zero truth-table entries with identities. This gives exactly \(4R-3\) registered primitive slots per pair and restores every scratch ancilla. It is an explicit finite generative circuit, even when its size is enormous. The fixed truth-table description/generation and ROM storage are part of source construction, not an uncharged runtime arithmetic oracle; its hardware and pure scratch are retained unchanged, and their finite initial preparation is separately charged. The count is deliberately very loose and makes no optimal-circuit claim.

Let \(N_{\max}=N_0+4\),
\[
R_Q=mN_{\max}+2m+2,\quad B_J=\lceil\log_2(2m+1)\rceil,

The report circuit inputs only the maximum visible training-Y bank, the \(m\) protected equivariance masks, \(m\) serializer coins and two public mode bits. Its Boolean function is explicitly: mask each selected mode's first \(N_i\) Y bits, take their strict majority, unmask that decision, then XOR the mode's serializer coin. It writes \(m\) committed signs. Unused source-bank positions are ignored. Hidden signs are not circuit inputs. The invalid public mode code 11 writes zero, completing its truth table. Forecast outputs obey \(F=A\oplus(1-Q)\), with \(A\sim\operatorname{Bern}(4/5)\); their forward/inverse circuit uses \(6m\) gates. The score circuit inputs only \(m\) committed signs, \(m\) fresh evaluation-Y bits and \(m\) evaluation-Z bits, and writes

The source's fixed score decoder uses the public surcharge and \(L_{\rm tot}=1/4+J/m+t\). Both truth-table circuits are run forward and then backwards after the task-use window. Nothing in this schedule replaces the committed model after seeing its evaluation outcome.

Consequently the active nonthermal gate count and stochastic-slot count in mode \(i\) are

The final +1 is the actual adaptation collision; every individual X-record preparation/restoration is already included in the four-gate acquisition count. The strong law follows from the finite irreducible chain and the deterministic count law. <a id="theorem-p156d-complete-same-record-reset-and-attained-global-recovery-optimum"></a>**Theorem P.15.6d (Complete Same-Record Reset and Attained Global Recovery Optimum).**

#### Result and scope

This certificate supplies positive-conditional-entropy resets and complete recovery for the registered B.2e/B.2f source family. It contains an exact countable-Gibbs-bath realization, finite-dimensional approximants with exact predictive responses, all resource and heat formulas, and an attained global zero-net-work optimum for a fixed nontrivial task workload. The same physical acquisition records are reset; no unrelated random-bit erasures or heater are appended.

The exact branch uses countably many bath energy levels and infinite-bandwidth addressing. Its logical registers and auxiliary are finite, its bath entropies and all polynomial energy moments are finite, and its interaction pulses have bounded operator norm and finite duration. It is not a finite-level laboratory eraser. Unlike a bare ready-channel limit, it has a genuine joint unitary. Finite regulators have an explicitly imperfect ready state, with controlled entropy and heat convergence.

Source attribution uses the M.18/B.2.1 reduction and additive excess-reflexive identification proved in Theorem P.15.6b. The thermodynamic proof establishes the separate physical bridge; it does not infer it from proximity. In the exact formulas below, the selected reset has a strictly positive excess dissipation term, and the addressable spent banks permit its recovery.

#### 1. Frozen source, same physical records, and complete side information

For a source amplitude \(a\), prepare a sealed sign \(H\sim\operatorname{Bern}(1/2)\), and independent acquisition slots with raw laws \(E_s\sim\operatorname{Bern}(p)\), \(Z_s\sim\operatorname{Bern}(a)\), where \(p=1/2+a\). Here $E_{s}$ names the pre-XOR random value, not an additional physical register. A single acquisition XORs \(H\) into the physical raw slot and exposes it as \(Y_s\). Thus \(Y_s=E_s\oplus H\), with the exact B.2e response law. The sign is immutable during the task; the learner has no direct sign or batch interface. The pre-XOR physical slot is sealed inside the acquisition module until the single-call output is delivered. The post-task decoder/reset has no intermediate read port and runs only after commitment/use and returned learner workspaces. Observing both a pre-XOR and post-XOR value is expressly inadmissible, since it would reveal H immediately. Each next event receives genuinely fresh independent source banks, hence genuinely renewed signs.

There is **no second retained $E$ copy and no $E$ staging register** in the primary in-place realization. The physical $Y$ register starts in its registered ready law, is prepared directly to $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)$, is XORed with $H$ for acquisition, is decoded after cleanup, and is reset to that same ready law. The reset owner is the receiver acquisition slot itself. At finite $K$ the ready law is $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(s_K)$; on the exact countable branch it is pure zero. No pure-target SWAP is used or omitted.

A copied implementation of B.2f must instead explicitly remove its redundant E copy by \(E\leftarrow E\oplus Y\oplus H\), a reversible two-CNOT operation, before claiming positive conditional acquisition entropy. Otherwise \(H(Y\mid E,H)=0\), and no positive entropy floor is available.

The learned report is committed, retained, and genuinely used during its registered task-use window. The forecast is sampled and the evaluation score is generated. All report, counter, serializer-output, forecast-output, deterministic X, score and scratch records are then uncomputed using the retained raw samples. Public program/constant registers are unchanged; pure workspaces return exactly pure and decoupled. No output archive is exported or silently destroyed. An external retained report changes the contract and would require a different conditional entropy ledger.

After this cleanup the source module decodes each physical acquisition slot by \(Y_s\leftarrow Y_s\oplus H\). The same receiver record now contains the independent raw Bernoulli bit. It is this record that is reset. Its complete retained context includes the mode, amplitude, public challenge/program, sealed signs, every other stochastic slot, returned workspaces, and independent external data. This is the information that physically survives unchanged through the reset, after derived records have been uncomputed. It does not include a fictional transcript retaining the current erased value. Renewal may also be conditioned on the history before the current episode, because the episode receives independent fresh banks. Therefore
\[
\Pr(P_s=1\mid R_s)=p,
\qquad H(P_s\mid R_s)=h(p)\ge h(3/4)>0.
\tag{P.15.6d.T1}
\]
No copied record or surviving derived statistic determines \(P_s\). Other registered stochastic slots have their own independent conditional laws \(\operatorname{Bern}(t)\). Signs are reset after decoding the response slots. A single pure catalyst bit used below is initially independent and returns exactly pure after every primitive.

Each mode's fixed-Hamiltonian bath species is part of an initially independent product supply. The retained mode selects which banks are used; the unused banks remain unchanged. In particular the bath is not secretly prepared in a mode-correlated Gibbs state. All event banks are new independent cells from that supply. A transparent common carrier reserves the full three mode menus separately: \(2(768+832+896)=4992\) Gibbs bath cells per prospective event, of which at most \(2\cdot896=1792\) are acted on. At finite regulator $K=16$ each cell has dimension 32. All unselected cells remain untouched; the supply, storage and initial thermal-energy inventory counts all 4992 cells, not merely the active maximum. This oversized but explicit source-bank inventory is fixed before mode selection. Each prospective event additionally receives one fresh Gibbs qutrit selector and three fresh Gibbs qubits for the adaptation collision. Thus the total installed event inventory is 4996 bath cells, with at most 1796 cells used during an event, including adaptation. The cells have heterogeneous dimensions: at the finite regulator, the 4992 source-bank cells each have dimension 32, the selector has dimension 3, and the three adaptation qubits each have dimension 2. The already counted single adaptation pulse directly addresses that event’s never-before-used four-cell bundle under the declared nonlocal, deterministic clock-indexed schedule. This primitive asserts no separate loading or transport operation; adding a local transport mechanism would require its own resource and clock account. The source-bank recovery optimum does not consume these four adaptation cells or change the fixed adaptation policy.

#### 2. Exact countable-bath preparation and reset

Let \(P,A\) be degenerate qubits, with \(A=0\) the pure cyclic catalyst. Let a bath have basis \(n\in\mathbb N_0\). Define selfadjoint involutions \(T_1,T_2\) by
\[
T_1:|p,n,0\rangle\longleftrightarrow|0,2n+p,1\rangle,
\quad T_1|1,n,1\rangle=|1,n,1\rangle,
\]
\[
T_2|0,n,a\rangle=|0,n,1-a\rangle,
\quad T_2|1,n,a\rangle=|1,n,a\rangle.
\tag{P.15.6d.T2}
\]
The exchanges of \(T_1\) are disjoint and cover the entire \(A=0\) and \(P=0,A=1\) sectors. Put \(U=T_2T_1\). Then
\[
U|p,n,0\rangle=|0,2n+p,0\rangle,
\qquad
U^*|0,k,0\rangle=|k\bmod2,\lfloor k/2\rfloor,0\rangle.
\tag{P.15.6d.T3}
\]
Both factors permute a complete orthonormal basis, so U is a genuine unitary on the entire Hilbert space. The pure cyclic auxiliary and infinite-dimensional bath distinguish this from a finite-rank impossible reset. It is not a non-surjective unilateral shift disguised as a unitary.

Fix \(r=1/2\) for the entire source architecture. For a slot law \(t\in(0,1)\), write \(w_0=1-t,w_1=t\),
\[
\gamma_n=2^{-n-1},\qquad
q_t(2n+b)=2^{-n-1}w_b.
\tag{P.15.6d.T4}
\]
Both are faithful Gibbs states at the same \(T>0\), for example under
\[
H_\gamma(n)=k_BT(n+1)\ln2,
\qquad
H_{q_t}(n)=-k_BT\ln q_t(n).
\tag{P.15.6d.T5}
\]
These Hamiltonians are selfadjoint and bounded below; their partition functions are one under this harmless energy-zero convention. The distributions have geometric tails. Thus all entropy, mean-energy and polynomial energy-moment terms below are finite.

#### Claim P.15.6d.1 (Exact Positive-Entropy Source Slot)

Supply separate independent preparation and reset banks, initially \(q_t\) on \(H_{q_t}\) and \(\gamma\) on \(H_\gamma\).

1. Apply \(U^*\) to a ready source slot \(P=0\), the preparation bank and \(A=0\). This produces exactly independent \(P\sim\operatorname{Bern}(t)\), preparation-bank law \(\gamma\), and \(A=0\).
2. Run and use the actual reversible task, then uncompute all derived records and sign XORs. The same physical source slot again has its raw independent Bernoulli law.
3. Apply U to that slot, the fresh reset bank and \(A=0\). The source slot returns exactly to \(P=0\); the reset bank has law \(q_t\); the catalyst is exactly \(A=0\) and uncorrelated with everything.

Use bath heat positive into the bank and work positive supplied by cyclic external control. With \(h(t)=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t)\),
\[
\frac{Q_\uparrow(t)}{k_BT}=(1+t)\ln2
=h(t)+D(q_t\Vert\gamma)>0,
\tag{P.15.6d.T6}
\]
\[
\frac{Q_\downarrow(t)}{k_BT}
=-h(t)+D(\gamma\Vert q_t)
=-\frac23\ln2-\frac23\ln(1-t)-\frac13\ln t-h(t).
\tag{P.15.6d.T7}
\]
The initial reset bath is independent of all non-bath degrees. The record Hamiltonian is degenerate. Every auxiliary is returned exactly and all entropy terms are finite. Consequently this is the complete Definition-28 reset contract, not an imperfect-reset inequality.

**Proof.** In the preparation bank write its index as \(2a+b\). Under (P.15.6d.T4), a and b are independent with laws \(\gamma\) and Bernoulli(t). Equation (P.15.6d.T3) returns b to the source and a to the bank. At reset an independent bath index c becomes \(2c+b\), proving all endpoint product-state claims. Its number increment is \(c+b\); since \(\mathbb E c=1\), the mean heat is (P.15.6d.T6). The reset bath entropy grows by exactly \(h(t)\). The Gibbs relative-entropy identity therefore yields \(Q_\uparrow/(k_BT)=h(t)+D(q_t\Vert\gamma)\). The preparation entropy change is \(-h(t)\), giving (P.15.6d.T7). Directly splitting the geometric law into even and odd indices, with parity probabilities \(2/3,1/3\), gives the last displayed expression. All sums converge geometrically. \(\square\)

For the source acquisition record \(t=p\), (P.15.6d.T1) and (P.15.6d.T6) show that the actual reset heat is positive and at least \(k_BT h(p)\). It is **not** assigned equality with the Landauer lower bound.

#### 3. Exact finite regulators, including all endpoint laws

The countable primitive has a finite-dimensional response/heat-consistent approximation. For integer \(K\ge1\), set
\[
\gamma_K(n)=\frac{2^{-n}}{\sum_{j=0}^{K-1}2^{-j}},\quad 0\le n<K,
\qquad s_K=\frac{2^{-K}}{1+2^{-K}}.
\]
Use bath dimension \(2K\), laws
\[
\gamma_{2K}(n),\qquad
q_{t,K}(2a+b)=\gamma_K(a)w_b,
\quad 0\le a<K,
\tag{P.15.6d.T8}
\]
and ready source law Bernoulli(\(s_K\)). Both finite bath laws are strictly positive Gibbs states for \(-k_BT\log\gamma_{2K}\) and \(-k_BT\log q_{t,K}\).

The finite permutation
\[
U_K(p,n)=\left(\left\lfloor\frac nK\right\rfloor,
2(n\bmod K)+p\right),
\qquad
U_K^{-1}(u,m)=(m\bmod2,\lfloor m/2\rfloor+Ku)
\tag{P.15.6d.T9}
\]
acts on \(\{0,1\}\times\{0,\ldots,2K-1\}\). Prepare with \(U_K^{-1}\), reset with \(U_K\). The preparation sends
\[
\operatorname{Bern}(s_K)\otimes q_{t,K}
\longmapsto\operatorname{Bern}(t)\otimes\gamma_{2K},
\]
and reset sends
\[
\operatorname{Bern}(t)\otimes\gamma_{2K}
\longmapsto\operatorname{Bern}(s_K)\otimes q_{t,K},
\tag{P.15.6d.T10}
\]
with independence at both endpoints. Thus the B.2 source law is exact for every finite K, including source renewal. Logical/scratch pure catalysts remain pure; the stochastic slots alone have the imperfect ready law.

Indeed \(\gamma_{2K}(a+Ku)=\gamma_K(a)\operatorname{Bern}_{s_K}(u)\), so (P.15.6d.T10) follows by a direct product factorization. No finite exact-erasure claim is made. The finite reset heat is exactly
\[
\frac{Q_{\uparrow,K}(t)}{k_BT}
=\ln2\left[1+t-\frac{2K2^{-K}}{1-2^{-2K}}\right],
\tag{P.15.6d.T11}
\]
\[
\frac{Q_{\uparrow,K}}{k_BT}
=h(t)-h(s_K)+D(q_{t,K}\Vert\gamma_{2K}),
\quad
\frac{Q_{\downarrow,K}}{k_BT}
=h(s_K)-h(t)+D(\gamma_{2K}\Vert q_{t,K}).
\tag{P.15.6d.T12}
\]
To prove (P.15.6d.T11), the truncated geometric mean is \(m_K=1-K2^{-K}/(1-2^{-K})\); the input bath mean is \(m_K+Ks_K\), and the output mean is \(2m_K+t\).

The exact reset endpoint, entropy and heat converge:
\[
\|\rho_{s_K}-|0\rangle\langle0|\|_1=2s_K\to0,
\quad h(s_K)\to0,
\]
\[
|Q_{\uparrow,K}(t)-Q_\uparrow(t)|
=k_BT\ln2\,\frac{2K2^{-K}}{1-2^{-2K}}\to0.
\tag{P.15.6d.T13}
\]
The heat error is independent of t. For any finite event menu with at most \(J_{\max}\) assigned source resets, multiply that error by \(J_{\max}\) for uniform event-reward convergence. The countable U is a separately supplied exact unitary, not an unsupported assertion that the finite matrices have a particular global unitary limit.

The finite permutation uses the two-involution auxiliary implementation specified in Theorem P.15.6e. Its fixed two-pulse preparation and reset counts agree with the physical clock in Theorem P.15.6c. No noisy source slot is treated as a pure computational target.

#### 4. Safe finite-duration control and every ideal resource

Use the cyclic externally driven Hamiltonian convention already admitted in manuscript Theorem 7.6r. A finite quantum work battery which remains exactly uncorrelated during every fluctuating stroke is **not** inferred from this convention. If such a battery is requested it needs a separate implementation/limit. The complete exact source-plus-recovery cycle below has zero total bare-energy change on every classical trajectory, a stronger endpoint closure statement than cancellation of mean costs.

For each involution \(T_j\), put \(G_j=\frac\pi2(I-T_j)\). In a stroke of duration \(\tau>0\), native Hamiltonian \(H_0\), and
\[
f(s)=6s(\tau-s)/\tau^3,
\quad V_j(s)=\hbar f(s)e^{-iH_0s/\hbar}G_j e^{iH_0s/\hbar},
\tag{P.15.6d.T14}
\]
the interaction-picture propagator is \(e^{-iF(s)G_j}\), \(F(s)=\int_0^sf\), and the endpoint is \(e^{-iH_0\tau/\hbar}T_j\). Native phases do not affect these diagonal classical laws. The coupling is zero at endpoints and
\[
\|V_j(s)\|\le3\pi\hbar/(2\tau),\qquad
\int_0^\tau\|V_j(s)\|\,ds\le\pi\hbar.
\tag{P.15.6d.T15}
\]
Because each partial pulse is a linear combination of I and \(T_j\), it only visits the paired number levels \(n\) and \(2n+p\), or swaps two bath numbers at recovery. All initial geometric moments remain finite throughout. Thus mean work is the finite bare-energy change, including all switching, with no uncontrolled intermediate-energy logarithm or cancellation of an unbounded native Hamiltonian.

An exact preparation or reset uses two such pulses; bank recovery uses one. A whole two-pulse operation may be assigned one duration if its two pulse durations are explicitly halved. The event clock must include all of them.

| Resource | Registered account |
|---|---|
| Raw acquisitions, signs, masks, calibration, diagnostics | Each is an actual named stochastic slot with its own preparation, reset and bank-recovery strokes |
| Pure workspaces/program/constants | Finite static resources; reversible computation and exact return; not consumed entropy sinks |
| Reset catalyst A | One initially pure qubit, reused sequentially; returned exactly pure/decoupled after every exact primitive |
| Exact bath | Countably infinite levels; finite Gibbs entropy and all polynomial moments; two fresh bath cells per active stochastic slot |
| Finite regulator | Two \(2K\)-level Gibbs cells per active slot, common ready probability \(s_K\), exact source responses |
| Control | Explicit cyclic interaction-picture pulses, bounded norm/action at any fixed duration; infinite resonant frequency bandwidth and infinitely many addressed pairs in exact branch |
| Controller/clock | Prescribed external pulse schedule, all durations included; no finite autonomous clock realization claimed |
| Work | Signed cyclic-drive work integrals equal actual bare-energy changes; no unpriced finite battery assumption |
| Source-bank renewal | New independent banks every event and fixed-H independent banks for every mode; finite-horizon supply grows linearly with completed events |
| Returned banks | Recovered to their original Gibbs product law; not reused as the next event's purported fresh randomness |
| Output/archive | Used inside the event and uncomputed; no free permanently exported record |
| PCE mode | Separate stored-energy and thermal adaptation entries; never assigned to acquisition-source reset heat |

The fresh-bank restriction is essential. Under the exact complete cycle, an initial preparation index \(2a+b\) and reset index c become \(2c+b\) and a. The preparation bank still carries the old parity b after recovery. Reusing it would reproduce the old random bit even though its marginal law is Gibbs. Our independent event-bank supply prevents this repeated-learning loophole. Its energy/entropy inputs and outputs are explicitly thermal resources; a marginal state identity alone is never a renewal certificate.

#### 5. Complete frozen recovery class and attained global optimum

Fix a mode and its nontrivial finite task workload before optimization. Every admitted source completes the prescribed acquisitions, committed-report task and use window; doing nothing is inadmissible. Freeze its bath species, sign/read restrictions, available source slots and timing convention.

The recovery class receives **all spent preparation and reset banks only after task commitment, use, cleanup and reset**, individually addressable and with their actual joint law. It has no pre-commit communication or bank/work-telemetry port to the learner. It includes every collective, coherent, adaptive or randomized protocol using those banks, any independent Gibbs ancillas at the same T, and any finite controller or auxiliary returned jointly to its initial state and decoupled. All measurement records must be restored. The supplied banks must return to their original Gibbs states. Every admitted protocol has finite entropy and mean-energy terms in the registered balance; any additional limit must justify convergence of those terms and exact resource closure. The work convention is the same cyclic external control. There is no consumed purity, chemical reservoir, extra record, temperature gradient or nonequilibrium catalyst. This is a complete physical interface class, not a retrospective list of selected engines. The objective is expected gross work per prescribed event; the larger source-plus-recovery comparison subtracts every source/preparation/controller/reset cost.

#### Claim P.15.6d.2 (Exact Global Recovery Maximum)

For one exact source slot, the spent banks are the independent product \(\gamma\) on \(H_{q_t}\) and \(q_t\) on \(H_\gamma\). Their initial product was \(q_t\) on \(H_{q_t}\) and \(\gamma\) on \(H_\gamma\). A single whole-bank SWAP restores the latter exactly. Its work output is
\[
W_{\mathrm{rec}}(t)=Q_\uparrow(t)+Q_\downarrow(t)
=k_BT C(t),
\]
\[
C(t)=D(q_t\Vert\gamma)+D(\gamma\Vert q_t)
=(t+\tfrac13)\ln2+(t-\tfrac13)\ln\frac t{1-t}>0.
\tag{P.15.6d.T16}
\]
It is the global **maximum** over the entire recovery class, attained at finite registered service duration on the stated infinite-bandwidth branch. For finite K the same SWAP attains
\[
W_{\mathrm{rec},K}(t)=k_BT\{D(q_{t,K}\Vert\gamma_{2K})+D(\gamma_{2K}\Vert q_{t,K})\}.
\tag{P.15.6d.T17}
\]
For any finite collection of slots the maxima add because their complete joint spent-bank state is product. Over the whole cyclic same-temperature source-plus-recovery class with the fixed workload,
\[
\max \mathbb E W_{\mathrm{net,out}}=0,
\tag{P.15.6d.T18}
\]
attained by these source/reset/SWAP protocols. The exact pure-ready branch attains zero pathwise; each finite regulator attains zero in the registered mean-work convention.

**Proof.** The Gibbs variational identity is
\[
F_T(\rho)-F_T(\gamma_H)=k_BT D(\rho\Vert\gamma_H).
\]
For arbitrary initially independent Gibbs baths and a global unitary,
\[
\beta Q_B=-\Delta S_{\mathrm{nonbath}}+
I(\mathrm{nonbath}:B)' +D(\rho'_B\Vert\gamma_B).
\tag{P.15.6d.T19}
\]
Including every controller, memory and catalyst, the first law and (P.15.6d.T19) bound work extracted from the spent banks by their total nonequilibrium free energy. Since they exchange their populations as independent factors, their total entropy change relative to their initial Gibbs product is zero. Their energy/free-energy excess is exactly (P.15.6d.T16) or (P.15.6d.T17). SWAP restores the Gibbs product and extracts exactly that amount, proving the global bound and its attainer. Collective operations and feedback cannot evade a bound on the full joint state; restored auxiliary records supply no additional entropy sink.

For the complete cycle, all non-bath resources return to their initial state, so (P.15.6d.T19) gives net work at most zero. Our source supplies \(Q_\uparrow+Q_\downarrow\) and recovers exactly the same amount. On the exact branch, initial indices \(A=2a+b,B=c\) become \(A'=2c+b,B'=a\); by (P.15.6d.T5) the total bare energy depends on \(a+c\) and the unchanged parity b, so its change is exactly zero on each trajectory. \(\square\)

This recovery uses the *nonequilibrium bank states and their known Hamiltonians*. It does not convert equilibrated heat from a single-temperature port into net work. If the bank interface were replaced by an equilibrated macroscopic bath alone, the recovery maximum would be zero. A maintained gradient or unpriced correlation supply is a different class. No Carnot or quasistatic-equality argument is used here, and no finite-bandwidth hardware inference is made.

#### 6. Locked source list, heat table, and energy ownership

The source bridge registers
\[
a=32/147,\quad p=211/294,\quad K_{\mathrm{coord}}=16,
\quad N=(21,23,25).
\]
For each N,
\[
e_N=\sum_{k=0}^{(N-1)/2}\binom{N}{ k}p^k(1-p)^{N-k},
\quad d_N=\frac{8/441-e_N}{1-2e_N}\in(0,1/2).
\]
The calibrated majority error is exactly \(8/441\). The complete slot ledger, including a fresh evaluation triple, is:

| Role | Bernoulli parameter | Count | Reset owner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Hidden signs | 1/2 | 16 | Challenge renewal |
| Equivariance masks | 1/2 | 16 | Controller/source overhead |
| Training receiver E/Y records | p | 16N | Certified excess integration only after bridge |

Thus

b_N=16(2N+6)=(768,832,896),\qquad |J_N|=16N=(336,368,400).
\]
Only \(J_N\) is source-assigned. Its exact actual heat is
\[
q_N=k_BT\,16N(1+p)\ln2,
\tag{P.15.6d.T20}
\]
while its conditional entropy floor is \(16N h(p)\). These are different quantities.

For the complete mode-\(N\) list \(\mathscr T_N\),
\[
Q_{\mathrm{reset,all},N}=k_BT\ln2\sum_{t\in\mathscr T_N}(1+t),
\]
\[
W_{\mathrm{source,in},N}=W_{\mathrm{rec},N}=k_BT\sum_{t\in\mathscr T_N}C(t),
\quad Q_{\mathrm{prepare},N}=W_{\mathrm{source,in},N}-Q_{\mathrm{reset,all},N}.
\tag{P.15.6d.T21}
\]
All sums include multiplicities. The recovery tagged to the certified source subset alone is \(W_{\mathrm{rec},J_N}=k_BT\,16N C(p)\), with its own preparation-work term; the larger total in (P.15.6d.T21) also includes every overhead bank. Thus gross source-attributed recovery is not confused with gross recovery from the whole apparatus. The finite table uses (P.15.6d.T11),(P.15.6d.T12),(P.15.6d.T17) instead.

Numerical displays are diagnostics; the defining formulas and rational-log intervals are the certificate:

| 21 | 768 | 4040/7 | 400.044944208883 |

For invariant law \(\pi=(4,2,1)/7\),
