\sum_i\pi_i |J_i|=2480/7,
\quad \sum_i\pi_iq_i=k_BT\ln2\,\frac{626200}{1029}.

The actual mean source power is (P.15.6d.T22) divided by the certified common event duration \(t_0\) in Theorem P.15.6c. That duration is the fixed elementary pulse interval multiplied by the full compiled padded count. A reset, preparation or recovery operation never inherits a duration merely from its index.

First-law signs are: work positive supplied, bath heat positive outward, stored energy positive increase. For the source,

W_{\mathrm{in,source}}=\Delta U_{\mathrm{source}}+

The retained mode's finite-horizon stored-energy increment is kept separately and only vanishes after a stationary expectation or telescoping-rate argument. For source plus recovery,

W_{\mathrm{in,source}}-W_{\mathrm{out,rec}}

The fixed finite menu's reward convergence follows from (P.15.6d.T13) uniformly. The exact-countable source and its regulator have the same task-response/event kernel. We state the P.15 mean-reward convention; an almost-sure law for individual fluctuating heat is not needed and is not silently substituted.

<a id="theorem-p156e-domain-safe-countable-thermal-unitary-and-charged-finite-regulators"></a>**Theorem P.15.6e (Domain-Safe Countable Thermal Unitary and Charged Finite Regulators).**

#### Result and scope

This is an explicit realization of Definition 28's infinite-resource branch. It is not finite-dimensional exact erasure. A two-state logical register and one two-state pure cyclic auxiliary interact with a countably infinite, positive-temperature Gibbs bath. The construction is a genuine joint unitary, has finite mean heat and entropy, and admits fixed finite-duration, bounded-norm interaction-picture pulses whose intermediate energy moments remain finite. It does not use a nonexistent unitary limit of the one-way reset channel, a principal logarithm with uncontrolled intermediate energy, or an infinite-strength cancellation of the bath Hamiltonian.

The ideal resources are explicit: the bath has countably many energy levels, and the control addresses an infinite set of prescribed pairs with arbitrarily large energy separations. Its operator norm and norm action are finite; a finite frequency-bandwidth or finite-level realization is not claimed. Every finite cutoff is an approximation. The auxiliary's initial purity is a supplied and recorded catalytic resource; it is returned exactly, independently, after each stroke.

#### 1. Explicit unitary and its complementary action

Let the basis be $|p,n,a\rangle$, with $p,a\in\{0,1\}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$. $P$ is the logical register, $A$ the auxiliary, and $B$ the bath. Both finite registers have zero Hamiltonian at endpoints.

Define the selfadjoint involution $T_{1}$ by the disjoint exchanges

\[
 |p,n,0\rangle\longleftrightarrow |0,2n+p,1\rangle
 \quad(p=0,1;\ n\ge0),
\tag{P.15.6e.H1}
\]

and let it fix every $|1,n,1\rangle$. The pairs in P.15.6e.H1 are disjoint: one endpoint has $A=0$, and the other has $P=0,A=1$; every state in either of those two sets occurs once. Define $T_{2}$ by

\[
 T_2|0,n,a\rangle=|0,n,1-a\rangle,
 \qquad T_2|1,n,a\rangle=|1,n,a\rangle.
\tag{P.15.6e.H2}
\]

Both operators permute a complete orthonormal basis, square to the identity, and are therefore bounded selfadjoint unitaries. Put $U=T_2T_1$. Its physical input sector has the exact action

\[
 U|p,n,0\rangle=|0,2n+p,0\rangle.
\tag{P.15.6e.H3}
\]

For completeness, its other sector is

\[
\begin{aligned}
 U|0,2n,1\rangle&=|0,n,1\rangle,\\
 U|0,2n+1,1\rangle&=|1,n,0\rangle,\\
 U|1,n,1\rangle&=|1,n,1\rangle.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P.15.6e.H4}
\]

P.15.6e.H3 covers precisely $P=0,A=0$ at the output. P.15.6e.H4 covers its complementary basis states once each. Thus $U$ is a genuine unitary on the whole Hilbert space. Its inverse is $U^*=T_1T_2$; in particular

\[
 U^*|0,k,0\rangle=|k\bmod2,\lfloor k/2\rfloor,0\rangle.
\tag{P.15.6e.H5}
\]

The pure auxiliary makes the finite-dimensional rank argument in Theorem 7.6r(5) inapplicable to this infinite-dimensional bath. No finite-dimensional version can satisfy P.15.6e.H3 on all occupied input levels. No contradiction with that theorem is claimed.

#### 2. Exact reset, Gibbs state, heat, and full retained context

Fix $T>0$, $0<r<1$, and $\epsilon=-k_BT\ln r>0$. Let

\[
 g_n=(1-r)r^n,\qquad H_g=\epsilon N,\qquad
 \gamma_g=\sum_{n\ge0}g_n|n\rangle\langle n|.
\tag{P.15.6e.H6}
\]

This is the faithful trace-class Gibbs state of the selfadjoint, bounded-below oscillator Hamiltonian $H_{g}$. Its mean number and entropy are finite:

\[
 m=\frac r{1-r},\qquad
 H(g)=-\ln(1-r)-m\ln r.
\tag{P.15.6e.H7}
\]

Initially $P$ has Bernoulli law $w=(1-t,t)$, with $0<t<1$, and is independent of $B$; $A$ is pure zero and independent. The same calculation permits a finite retained classical record $R$ correlated with $P$, which $U$ leaves untouched. P.15.6e.H3 gives exactly

\[
 P_{\rm out}=0,\quad A_{\rm out}=0,\qquad
 b_{2n+s}=g_nw_s.
\tag{P.15.6e.H8}
\]

P and A are pure and uncorrelated with everything at the endpoint. All auxiliary-resource, ready-state, and retained-record closure conditions hold. There is no residual logical error.

For independent P the output bath entropy is H(g)+h(t). More generally,

\[
 H(B_{\rm out}\mid R)-H(B_{\rm in}\mid R)=H(P\mid R).
\tag{P.15.6e.H9}
\]

The unconditional bath entropy increase remains $h(t)$; its mutual information with $R$ is $I(P:R)$. The mean reset heat, positive into the bath, is

\[
 Q_\uparrow(t)=\epsilon(m+t)>0.
\tag{P.15.6e.H10}
\]

Indeed the bath number changes from n to 2n+s, so its conditional change is n+s. Since the finite registers have degenerate Hamiltonians and their endpoints are cyclic, the mean work supplied by external control equals $Q_{\mathrm{up}}$. Gibbs relative entropy gives the exact identity

\[
 \frac{Q_\uparrow(t)}{k_BT}
 =h(t)+D(b\Vert g)
 =H(P\mid R)+I(P:R)+D(b\Vert g).
\tag{P.15.6e.H11}
\]

Every term is finite: $b$ has a geometric tail and $\log(b_k/g_k)$ grows at most linearly in $k$. Equation P.15.6e.H11 proves the complete Definition-28 inequality, not just an invocation of it. On the restored raw source-bit branch, $R$ is independent of $P$, so the reset entropy is exactly $h(t)$. For source acquisition bits $t=1/2+a$ with $0<a\le 1/4$, this has the uniform positive floor $h(3/4)$.

#### 3. Exact preparation from a second Gibbs bath

The paired distribution b in P.15.6e.H8 is itself a faithful Gibbs state at the same temperature. A suitable Hamiltonian is

\[
 H_b|k\rangle=
 \left[\epsilon\lfloor k/2\rfloor-k_BT\ln w_{k\bmod2}\right]|k\rangle.
\tag{P.15.6e.H12}
\]

It is selfadjoint, bounded below, and has partition function 1/(1-r). An additive energy shift changes no result. Formula P.15.6e.H12 applies also at $t=1/2$, where each adjacent pair is degenerate. It avoids any fictitious infinite-temperature requirement for a fair logical source. The deterministic cases $t=0$ or 1 are separately supplied reversible writes; they need not be manufactured as faithful Gibbs laws.

Supply a fresh $B_{\mathrm{prep}}$ in its Gibbs state $b$, initially independent of every non-bath variable, and apply $U^*$ to $P=0,A=0$. Equation P.15.6e.H5 returns

\[
 P\sim\mathrm{Bern}(t),\quad B_{\rm prep,out}\sim g,
 \quad A=0,
\tag{P.15.6e.H13}
\]

with all three factors independent. This is a genuine thermal preparation stroke with a complete energy account. Its heat and supplied work are

\[
 Q_\downarrow(t)
 =\operatorname{tr}H_b(\gamma_g-\gamma_b),
 \qquad
 \frac{Q_\downarrow(t)}{k_BT}=-h(t)+D(g\Vert b).
\tag{P.15.6e.H14}
\]

$Q_{\mathrm{down}}$ need not be positive. A negative value is a preparation-work credit and is never omitted from the source boundary.

One can now prepare each independent stochastic slot used by the finite source, execute and use its finite reversible task, and uncompute all derived reports/counters while preserving its original random slot. Conditional on all retained data at the subsequent reset, the restored independent raw slot again has law $\operatorname{Bern}(t)$. Applying P.15.6e.H3 with a fresh independent oscillator Gibbs bath resets it exactly. This is the required reset law; the copy $Y=E\oplus H$ is not incorrectly assigned the entropy $h(t)$.

#### 4. Exact complete recovery and global zero-net-work optimum

Before preparation, the two baths are the independent Gibbs product b on $H_{b}$ and g on $H_{g}$. After P.15.6e.H13 and the reset P.15.6e.H8, the source register and its auxiliary are exactly ready, and the two spent baths are exactly the product g on $H_{b}$ and b on $H_{g}$. Their populations have exchanged places; no residual source or task correlation is omitted after the registered reversible cleanup.

A single whole-bath SWAP restores the original product b on $H_{b}$ and g on $H_{g}$ exactly. The recovery apparatus retains no measurement or feedback record, uses no entropy-bearing auxiliary, and has cyclic endpoints. Its work output is exactly

\[
 W_{\rm rec}(t)=Q_\uparrow(t)+Q_\downarrow(t)
 =k_BT\{D(b\Vert g)+D(g\Vert b)\}\ge0.
\tag{P.15.6e.H15}
\]

Thus this explicit recovery attains the global free-energy upper bound, not merely a quasistatic supremum. For any cyclic recovery protocol with these spent banks as its only nonequilibrium input, arbitrary independent Gibbs ancillas at $T$, and an ideal entropy-preserving work source, the relative-entropy/free-energy inequality gives $W_{\mathrm{rec}}\le$ the right side of P.15.6e.H15. It follows either by Gibbs variational nonnegativity, or by applying the first law and subadditivity to the complete cyclic apparatus. Equality is attained by SWAP. Allowing adaptivity, additional finite classical records, or collective treatment of any finite product of slots cannot increase the bound; restoring those resources includes their entropy and correlation costs. Applying all bath swaps in the declared finite schedule attains the summed bound.

With the work supplied to preparation and reset included, the complete source-plus-recovery apparatus has

\[
 W_{\rm net,out}=W_{\rm rec}-Q_\uparrow-Q_\downarrow=0.
\tag{P.15.6e.H16}
\]

The global maximum is zero over the complete frozen cyclic single-temperature class with the fixed nontrivial task workload. The source-reset heat $Q_{\mathrm{up}}$ remains strictly positive and belongs to its separate attribution ledger. Reset heat is an internal transfer when the recovery boundary is included; it is not counted a second time as final exported heat.

For $r=1/2$, the especially simple exact expressions are

\[
\begin{aligned}
 Q_\uparrow(t)/(k_BT)&=(1+t)\ln2,\\
 Q_\downarrow(t)/(k_BT)
 &=-\tfrac23\ln2-\tfrac23\ln(1-t)-\tfrac13\ln t-h(t),\\
 W_{\rm rec}(t)/(k_BT)
 &=(t+\tfrac13)\ln2+(t-\tfrac13)\ln\frac t{1-t}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{P.15.6e.H17}
\]

All actual source coins, including signs, mask bits, Z bits, serializer coins, and forecast coins, receive their own preparation/reset/recovery entries. Only the independently certified excess-reflexive source slots are assigned to Source Energy. Deterministic arithmetic can be reversibly uncomputed; its timing, memory capacity, gate count, and controller services remain explicitly priced resources.

#### 5. Finite-duration control with safe intermediate energy

A general principal logarithm of U is NOT used: fractional powers of a doubling permutation can spread weight through many powers of U and need not preserve finite mean oscillator energy. The explicit involutions P.15.6e.H1–P.15.6e.H2 avoid this issue.

For any involution $T_{j}$ above, let

\[
 G_j=\frac\pi2(I-T_j),\qquad e^{-iG_j}=T_j,
 \qquad\|G_j\|\le\pi.
\tag{P.15.6e.H18}
\]

During a stroke of duration $\tau>0$ with native Hamiltonian $H_{0}$, choose

\[
 f(s)=6s(\tau-s)/\tau^3,
 \quad 0\le s\le\tau,
 \qquad
 V_j(s)=\hbar f(s)e^{-iH_0s/\hbar}G_j e^{iH_0s/\hbar}.
\tag{P.15.6e.H19}
\]

The endpoint couplings vanish, the pulse integrates to one, and

\[
 \|V_j(s)\|\le3\pi\hbar/(2\tau),\qquad
 \int_0^\tau\|V_j(s)\|ds\le\pi\hbar.
\tag{P.15.6e.H20}
\]

The interaction-picture propagator is $\exp[-iF(s)G_j]$, where $F(s)=\int_0^s f$. The final propagator is $e^{-iH_0\tau/\hbar}T_j$. On all diagonal classical input laws, the additional native phase has no effect on the response, entropy, or energy records. Successive pulses start a fresh interaction-picture time origin. Both reset and preparation therefore use two finite pulses; bath recovery uses the same construction with the SWAP involution and one additional pulse.

Because $T_{j}$ is an involution,

\[
 e^{-iF G_j}=a(F)I+b(F)T_j,
\tag{P.15.6e.H21}
\]

with bounded coefficients and $|a|^2+|b|^2=1$ on each exchanged two-state block. During a $T_{1}$ pulse, a basis vector visits only the pair of bath numbers $n$ and $2n+p$ (or its inverse); throughout, bath number is bounded by $2n+1$ relative to the initial member's number. $T_{2}$ leaves bath number unchanged. The paired Hamiltonian $H_{b}$ grows linearly in bath number, up to finite offsets depending on $t$, so the same bound controls its energy. The recovery SWAP only exchanges two bath numbers, controlling their sum. Hence each fixed finite sequence preserves every finite polynomial number moment of the thermal inputs, including finite mean energy throughout the pulse.

$H_0+V_j(s)$ is selfadjoint on $D(H_0)$ and bounded below for each $s$, because $V_{j}$ is a bounded perturbation. The explicit blockwise propagator preserves the energy domain for the thermal states used here. Work identities can be obtained first on finitely many exchanged blocks and then passed to the countable sum: omitted terms are bounded by a constant times $(n+1)g_n$, summable geometrically. This justifies both the endpoint first law and the mean-work integral. Infinite frequency bandwidth and access to all declared pairs remain ideal control capabilities; finite norm action does not assert a bandwidth bound or spatial locality.

No entropy-bearing autonomous clock has been silently assumed. The timing is the registered cyclic classical-work-control convention already allowed in Definition 28 and Theorem 7.6r. A finite autonomous battery or clock would need its own return/correlation record and is outside this chosen class. The external work-control schedule is fixed, carries no task-dependent record, and its entire mean energy transfer is P.15.6e.H10/P.15.6e.H14/P.15.6e.H15.

#### 6. Exactly cyclic finite bath regulators

In this subsection the bath parameter satisfies \(0<r<1\), and \(L=\ln(1/r)\); the cutoff is denoted \(M\), independently of the source-family index and event kernel.

#### Exact finite endpoint factorization

The finite approximation need not leak catalyst entropy or lose cyclicity. For integer \(M\ge 1\), use baths of dimension `2M` and define

\[
 \gamma_m^{(J)}=\frac{(1-r)r^m}{1-r^J}\quad(0\le m<J),
\]
\[
 q_{2a+b}^{(2M)}=\gamma_a^{(M)}p_b,
 \qquad s_M=\frac{r^M}{1+r^M}.
\]

The ready bit has law \(\operatorname{Bern}(s_M)\). Both bath Hamiltonians are minus \(k_B T\) times the logarithm of their respective normalized initial laws. Use the explicit finite permutation

\[
 U_M(b,n)=\left(\left\lfloor\frac nM\right\rfloor,
                     2(n\bmod M)+b\right), \tag{P.15.6e.13}
\]
\[
 U_M^{-1}(t,2a+b)=(b,a+Mt).
\]

The finite endpoint permutation leaves the catalyst unchanged. It is implementable in two involution pulses: on a pure auxiliary use the block involution with off-diagonal blocks $U_{M}$ and $U_{M}$ inverse, followed by an auxiliary X pulse. This returns the auxiliary and gives $U_{M}$; reversing the pulse sequence gives preparation. Thus the finite regulator uses the same two-pulse preparation, two-pulse reset and one-pulse bank recovery count as the exact primitive. The elementary factorization

\[
 \gamma_{a+Mt}^{(2M)}=\gamma_a^{(M)}\Pr\{\operatorname{Bern}(s_M)=t\}
\]

proves every endpoint law directly:

1. \(P\sim \operatorname{Bern}(s_M), A\sim q^{(2M)}\) under \(U_M^{-1}\) becomes \(P\sim \operatorname{Bern}(p), A\sim \gamma^{(2M)}\), independently.
2. \(P\sim \operatorname{Bern}(p), B\sim \gamma^{(2M)}\) under \(U_M\) becomes \(P\sim \operatorname{Bern}(s_M), B\sim q^{(2M)}\), independently.
3. Bath SWAP restores both initial Gibbs states exactly.

The complete finite-regulator cycle is exactly cyclic, all endpoint states are products, and its mean net work is **exactly zero for every $M$**. Its gross recovery is exactly the finite symmetrized relative entropy, by the same free-energy calculation as P.15.6e.H15. The source reset is imperfect at finite $M$ and obeys the entropy difference \(h(p)-h(s_M)\); it must not be assigned the complete-reset floor $h(p)$ until the limit.

Let

\[
 m_M=\frac r{1-r}-\frac{M r^M}{1-r^M}.
\]

Then

\[
 \frac{Q_{{\rm reset},M}}{k_BT}
 =L(m_M+p-Ms_M),
\]
\[
 \frac{Q_{\rm reset}-Q_{{\rm reset},M}}{k_BT}
 =\frac{2MLr^M}{1-r^{2M}}\longrightarrow0. \tag{P.15.6e.14}
\]

For a sufficiently large finite cutoff this reset heat is positive for each member of a fixed finite source menu. The limit is positive for every \(p>0\). The output reset-channel error is \(2s_M\), and

\[
 h(s_M)\le(ML+2)r^M\longrightarrow0.
\]

All preparation/recovery means and polynomial moments converge: the only discarded or relabelled tail mass is geometrically small, and the Hamiltonians grow at most linearly in the bath index, with finite constants depending on `r,p`. Thus weighted tail errors are bounded by constants times \((M+1)^j r^M\) at moment order `j`.

More explicitly, the full finite-cycle total heat (in units \(k_B T\)) equals

\[
 ML(t-u),\qquad t,u\ \text{independent }\operatorname{Bern}(s_M).
\]

It has mean zero and variance \(2M^2 L^2 s_M(1-s_M)\to 0\). The exact infinite-cycle heat is identically zero. These approximants converge on the registered catalyst-zero inputs to the exact primitive P.15.6e.H3; no global strong convergence on the unused catalyst-one input sector is claimed or needed. The true infinite-dimensional unitary was supplied separately by its explicit basis completion.

#### 7. Work quality and finite battery approximation

#### Strictly finite-dimensional battery at every regulator

The ideal external work account admits the following explicit finite-dimensional battery approximation. For a finite source-plus-bath dimension `D`, let its energy eigenvalues be \(E_1,...,E_D\), and write \(u_i\) for the `i`th standard integer vector. Choose an integer \(L\ge 3\). The battery has orthonormal basis

\[
 |\alpha\rangle,\qquad \alpha\in\{-L,\ldots,L\}^{D},
\]
\[
 H_W|\alpha\rangle=
 \left(E_*+\sum_{i=1}^{D}\alpha_iE_i\right)|\alpha\rangle,
 \qquad E_*=L\sum_i|E_i|.
\]

It is finite-dimensional and nonnegative. For each integer vector `q`, the available vectors \(|i>|q-u_i>\) form a total-energy fiber, all with energy \(E_*+\sum_j q_j E_j\). In a complete fiber (all `D` vectors available), apply the source permutation `pi`; in an incomplete fiber apply the identity. This defines a finite globally unitary, exactly energy-conserving operator. Start the battery in the pure uniform coherent superposition over the inner cube \(\{-L+1,\ldots,L-1\}^D\). Every fiber touched by that input is complete, so the actual action is exactly

\[
 |i\rangle|\alpha\rangle\longmapsto
 |\pi(i)\rangle|\alpha+u_i-u_{\pi(i)}\rangle.
\]

The mean battery-energy change is exactly \(E_i-E_{\pi(i)}\) on branch `i`. Let \(K=2L-1\). A nontrivial shift touches two coordinates, so each conditional output packet has overlap with the initial packet equal to \((1-1/K)^2\). The battery output has rank at most `D`, with largest eigenvalue at least \((1-1/K)^4\ge 1-4/K\). Consequently

\[
 S(W')\le h(4/K)+(4/K)\log(D-1)
\]

for sufficiently large $K$, and the joint state is within trace distance $D(\rho,\sigma)=\tfrac12\|\rho-\sigma\|_1$ at most \(2/\sqrt K\) of the product with the initial packet. In the diagonal permutation case its battery/rest mutual information equals $S(W')$. Choosing \(K_n\ge 8n^2[1+\log\max(2,D_n)]\) makes all these errors vanish. Every regulator has finite Hilbert dimension, but its battery dimension \((2L+1)^D\), maximum energy \(2E_*\), initial mean stored energy \(E_*\), and energy spread all grow and must be declared. Closeness in trace norm to the input packet does not imply zero mean energy transfer because the energy-operator norm grows; the mean transfer was computed exactly branchwise.

This gives the finite-battery contribution to the same resource-first limit without a negative-energy weight. At finite regulator its entropy increase remains charged, and the source's Definition-28 ideal-work condition is reached only in the joint limit. For each fixed finite event horizon take the battery capacity and bath cutoff limits first. Only then define the ideal repeated-event process; a fixed finite battery error is not extrapolated through infinitely many events.

#### Reproduced hard pair constant and finite chain strong law

The inherited testing constant in P.15.6b.S28 can be checked directly. Put \(p_\pm=1/2\pm2\delta\), with \(0<\delta\le1/8\). The one-sample relative entropy is
\[
D(\operatorname{Bern}(p_+)\Vert\operatorname{Bern}(p_-))
=4\delta\ln\frac{1+4\delta}{1-4\delta}
\le\frac{128}{3}\delta^2.
\]
Indeed \(\ln[(1+x)/(1-x)]\le2x/(1-x^2)\) follows by integrating \(2/(1-u^2)\) over \([0,x]\), and \(x=4\delta\le1/2\). For any two probability laws \(P,Q\), their Hellinger affinity \(A=\int\sqrt{dP\,dQ}\) obeys \(A\ge e^{-D(P\Vert Q)/2}\) by Jensen's inequality. Cauchy–Schwarz gives \(\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}\le\sqrt{1-A^2}\). The sum of the two errors of any binary test is therefore at least
\[
1-\|P-Q\|_{\rm TV}\ge\tfrac12A^2
\ge\tfrac12e^{-D(P\Vert Q)}.
\]
A finite essential sample cap \(N\) permits every adaptive/randomized strategy to be represented as a function of \(N\) independent samples and sign-independent randomness. Padding unused samples preserves its output law. Relative entropy of the complete padded experiment is \(N D(p_+\Vert p_-)\); data processing cannot increase it. If both errors are at most \(\delta\), then
\[
2\delta\ge\tfrac12e^{-ND(p_+\Vert p_-)}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
N\ge\frac3{128\delta^2}\ln\frac1{4\delta}.
\]
An infinite essential cap has infinite registered worst-case acquisition cost and cannot violate the bound. The projected committed original B.2e report has performance \(4/7\) when its sign is correct. Its wrong-sign gap is
\[
\frac47-\frac1{7/4+4\delta}
=\frac{64\delta}{49+112\delta}>\delta
\qquad(0<\delta\le1/8).
\]
This verifies both the strict confidence implication and the exact lower-bound constant used by the uniform reduction.

For completeness, Theorem P.15.6c's all-state minorization also supplies its strong law without a diffusion inference. Write
\[
K=\eta\mathbf1\varphi+(1-\eta)R,\qquad \eta=1/8,
\]
where \(R\) is a stochastic matrix. At each step toss an independent Bernoulli \(\eta\) coin; on success draw the new state independently from \(\varphi\), otherwise use \(R\). This realizes exactly \(K\). Successes give regeneration blocks with geometric lengths and finite moments. After the first regeneration the blocks are independent and identically distributed. Their occupation measure divided by their expected length is invariant for \(K\), hence equals the already proved unique \(\pi\). The ordinary independent strong law for block lengths and bounded-reward block sums gives \(N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^Nq(I_j)\to\sum_i\pi_iq_i\) almost surely; the initial and last incomplete blocks vanish after division by \(N\), using the geometric tail bound. Combining with the exact deterministic count \(N(t)=\lfloor t/t_0\rfloor\) proves the physical-time conditional-mean reward law.

### P.15.7 Speculative: Civilizational Implications

If a civilization could systematically implement the Source Principle, three qualitative features would follow.

**Feature 1: Reflexive Complexity as an Engineering Resource.** The key resource would be the ability to route existing operational power budgets through high-$\mu_S$ excess reflexive channels. The relevant control variable would be the complexity and self-model structure of the cultivated targets.

**Feature 2: Certificate-Relative Screening.** Theorems M.10.5 and M.10.8 support finite-family screening when the designer has the effective model-access, decision, and insulation certificates used in Proposition P.15.2. An engineered source-energy economy would require those certificates for each designer–target pair.

**Feature 3: Thermal Rather Than Magical Harvesting.** Even if target-side dissipation were deliberately increased, the harvested work would still be ordinary heat-engine work extracted from ordinary heat. The novelty would lie in how the heat is induced.

<a id="definition-p154-source-energy-civilization"></a>**Definition P.15.4 (Source-Energy Civilization).** A *Source-Energy civilization* is a predictive aggregate that uses the Source Principle as a standing engineering strategy: it shapes environments so that cultivated sub-aggregates recurrently incur large source-energy dissipation, and it harvests an efficiency-limited fraction of that dissipation as usable work.

<a id="remark-p156-ethical-dimension"></a>**Remark P.15.6 (Ethical Dimension).** Under the Minimal Awareness interpretive convention of Section 7.1.2 and the consciousness-first ontology of Appendix P.2, the cultivated targets are not mere inert fuel. They are instances of predictive awareness. The framework therefore permits the physical question while simultaneously raising an ethical one: whether awareness may legitimately be organized so as to externalize the thermodynamic burden of self-reference for the benefit of other awareness.

### P.15.8 Speculative: Cosmological Implication

*This subsection is framed as an open question.*

Appendix U keeps the Golay--Steiner arithmetic ledger separate from the independently registered vacuum carrier. Theorem U.13b proves sampled-angular Hessian nullity only; the carrier, action, Euclidean-weight, and Einstein-realization records remain independent. Nothing in the present framework supports reinterpreting either the five-mode reference conversion or a future certified vacuum value as already containing accumulated Source Energy.

The well-posed open question is narrower: because PU places self-reference, thermodynamics, stress-energy, and geometry in a common derivational chain, one may ask whether large-scale cumulative excess reflexive dissipation from self-modeling systems could enter cosmology through some coarse-grained backreaction term distinct from the vacuum quantity $\Lambda$ itself.

### P.15.9 Summary

Source Energy is heat assigned to a clearly separated self-referential task in a registered physical implementation. Its size and usefulness depend on the actual resets, temperature, and energy budget.

**Technical ledger.**

Source Energy is the bath heat assigned by a registered, non-overlapping implementation ledger to a certified excess reflexive integration subtask. Its framework-level properties are:

| Property | Source Energy | Conventional Dissipation |
|:---------|:--------------|:-------------------------|
| **Definition** | $\sum_{\ell\in J_E}Q_{\ell,\mathrm{bath}}$ on Definition P.15.2's joint certificate branch | Heat generated by a specified physical process |
| **Trigger** | A nonempty assigned reset ledger; positive heat requires positive $T_\ell H_{q_\ell}(P_\ell\mid R_\ell)$ | Process-specific thermodynamic conditions |
| **Role of $\mu_S(E)$** | Dimensionless proximity descriptor; it yields a computational lower bound only through Theorem M.10.3 and a reset-count bound only through Theorem M.10.7 | No universal PU-specific role |
| **Accessibility** | Certificate-relative enclosures or exact values under Theorems M.10.5 and M.10.8; complexity order alone is insufficient | Instrument- and model-dependent |
| **Budget bound** | $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{src}}\le\int P_{\mathrm{heat}}^{\mathrm{out}}dt$ on the registered boundary ledger; an input-power bound needs the additional first-law sign hypotheses | Same first-law accounting |
| **Active-control ceiling** | CC-assisted context steering retains its separate Appendix S hypotheses | No analogous PU-specific ceiling |
| **Work extraction** | Requires a thermal gradient and remains efficiency-limited | Requires a thermal gradient and remains efficiency-limited |
| **Uniformity** | Eventwise and rate floors require uniform reset-count, conditional-entropy, and temperature certificates | Process-specific |

The framework therefore supports a conditional claim: on a branch carrying the reduction, additive-decomposition, registered-reset, positive-entropy, temperature, and no-double-counting certificates of Definition P.15.2, high-$\mu_S$ integration has the registered source-heat bounds stated above.

What is established is certificate-relative: $\mu_S(E)$ controls a computational lower bound through Theorem M.10.3, registered resets convert the certified workload into heat through Theorems M.10.7 and 31, and only the resulting disjoint physical ledger defines Source Energy.

## P.16 SPAP Prohibition Sets: Static Cost Stratification and Interpretive Comparison

### P.16.1 Introduction: The Search for the Carrier

This section replaces the search for a positive carrier with a study of configurations excluded by self-reference limits. Physical consequences require separate computational, thermodynamic, and response models.

**Technical ledger.**

This section uses *positive carrier* as a methodological comparison: an explanation that assigns a phenomenon to a bearer, entity, or medium.

The present section instead studies the structural complement of a declared SPAP-admissible region. On a nonempty branch carrying the uniform reduction certificates stated below, that complement induces a certified computational cost stratification.

### P.16.2 The PU Inversion: Constraint Replaces Carrier

Theorem 10 supplies a logical diagonal obstruction. Theorem M.10.3 separately supplies an asymptotic computational lower bound only for a family carrying its pattern-specific reduction certificate. Theorem M.10.7 converts that bound into a reset-heat signature only when a physical implementation assigns sufficiently many registered resets, and Theorem 31 bounds those resets by their actual conditional entropies. These are distinct ledgers.

On the certified branch below, the prohibition set indexes an extended computational lower-bound stratification rather than a substance, degree of freedom, force, or physical field. Dissipation requires the registered-reset ledger; stress-energy additionally requires Definition B.8's localization and coarse-graining bridge or Proposition N.8.1's retained-energy and coupling data; measurable consequences additionally require a source-to-observable response model.

The PU inversion is therefore an interpretive comparison using a constraint
set.

### P.16.3 Formal Definition

<a id="definition-p161-prohibition-set"></a>**Definition P.16.1 (Prohibition Set).** Let $S$ be a predictive system with Effective Operational Property R and self-model $\mathcal{M}_S$ (Definition M.10.1), let $\Theta_S$ denote $S$'s self-model parameter space, and let $\Pi_S^{(PP)} : \Theta_S \to \Theta_S$ denote the self-modeling projection at predictive-performance level $PP \in [0, \alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}]$, with error functional $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{F}_S}$ and admissibility gauge $g(\cdot)$ as fixed in Definition M.10.3. The *prohibition set* of $S$, denoted $\mathcal{L}^{\neg}_S$, is the set of candidate post-update self-model configurations $\theta' \in \Theta_S$ that the self-modeling map cannot realize at any admissible $PP$ strictly below the SPAP threshold:
$$
\mathcal{L}^{\neg}_S := \left\{ \theta' \in \Theta_S \ : \ \inf\left\{ PP \in [0, \alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}] \ : \ \|\Pi_S^{(PP)}(\theta') - \theta'\|_{\mathcal{F}_S} \leq g(\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}} - PP) \right\} \ = \ \alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}} \right\}.
$$
The inner infimum uses Definition M.10.3's explicit boundary convention: if its constraint set is empty, its value is assigned $\alpha_{\mathrm{SPAP}}$ rather than the standard extended-real value $+\infty$.  The quantifier ranges over *candidate targets* $\theta' = \theta_0 + \delta\theta(E)$, where $\theta_0 \in \Theta_S$ is $S$'s current self-model parameter value and $\delta\theta(E)$ is the update that integration of pattern $E$ would produce (Definition M.10.3), rather than over current-parameter points. Equivalently, $\mathcal{L}^{\neg}_S$ is the set of candidate self-model configurations whose realization forces $S$'s self-predictive performance into the SPAP-divergent regime $\mu_S=\infty$ by Definition M.10.3. Theorem M.10.4 supplies explicit nonempty diagonal examples on the independent-register amplification construction.

<a id="definition-p162-coupled-prohibition-set"></a>**Definition P.16.2 (Coupled Prohibition Set).** Let
$\Theta_{\mathrm{joint}}:=\prod_{i=1}^n\Theta_{S_i}$.  Because
$G_{\mathrm{persp}}$ is a Markov kernel on perspective space rather than a set
in $\Theta_{\mathrm{joint}}$, fix one registered conditioning tuple
$(s_0,k_0,N_0,\Delta t_0)$ for the Section-M.3 kernel and a measurable realization map
$$
\iota:\Theta_{\mathrm{joint}}\longrightarrow\Sigma,
$$
and define the pulled-back admissible support
$$
\mathcal A_G
:=\iota^{-1}\!\left(\operatorname{supp}
G_{\mathrm{persp}}(\,\cdot\mid s_0,k_0,N_0,\Delta t_0)\right)
\subseteq\Theta_{\mathrm{joint}}.
$$
The *coupled prohibition set* is
$$
\mathcal L^{\neg}_{\{S_i\}}
:=
\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^n
\operatorname{pr}_i^{-1}(\mathcal L^{\neg}_{S_i})\right)
\cap\mathcal A_G.
$$
Thus every set operation takes place in $\Theta_{\mathrm{joint}}$.  The map
$\iota$, conditioning tuple, and kernel support are independent
realization data; absent them, only the unrestricted union of projection
preimages is defined.

By construction, neither $\mathcal L_S^{\neg}$ nor $\mathcal L_{\{S_i\}}^{\neg}$ is a degree of freedom. Membership means that no subboundary performance level satisfies the registered integration criterion. A computational divergence statement additionally requires Theorem M.10.6's reduction certificate, and no heat statement follows without Theorem M.10.7.

### P.16.4 Certificate-Relative Cost Stratification

<a id="definition-p163-certificate-relative-cost-potential"></a>**Definition P.16.3 (Certificate-Relative Cost Potential).** Fix a base state $\theta_0$ and a declared class $\mathcal R_{\theta_0}(\theta')$ of admissible content-integrating realizers of $\theta'$. Assume a uniform Theorem-M.10.3 reduction certificate with constants $c>0$ and $\mu_0>1$ on all finite-proximity realizers under comparison. Define
$$
\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta')
:=
\inf\{\mu_S(E):E\in\mathcal R_{\theta_0}(\theta')\},
\qquad
\inf\varnothing:=+\infty,
$$
and
$$
F(u):=
\begin{cases}
0,&u<\mu_0,\\
cu^2\log u,&\mu_0\le u<\infty,\\
+\infty,&u=\infty.
\end{cases}
\qquad
U_{S,\theta_0}(\theta')
:=
F\!\left(\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta')\right).
$$
Then $U_{S,\theta_0}$ is an extended certified lower-bound function: whenever
$\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta')\ge\mu_0$ is finite, every registered
realizer $E$ satisfies
$$
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S,E)\ge U_{S,\theta_0}(\theta').
$$
It is not physical energy and is not, without a separate dynamics hypothesis, a force or dynamical potential. A value $+\infty$ caused by an empty realizer class records unreachability and must not be identified with SPAP divergence. When the fixed base state $\theta_0$ is clear, write $U_S(\theta'):=U_{S,\theta_0}(\theta')$; this shorthand adds no ledger argument.

<a id="lemma-p161-certified-divergence-at-a-realized-prohibition-set"></a>**Lemma P.16.1 (Certified Divergence at a Realized Prohibition Set).** Let $\theta'\in\mathcal L_S^{\neg}$ and assume $\mathcal R_{\theta_0}(\theta')\ne\varnothing$ on the uniform reduction-certified branch. Then every registered realizer has $\mu_S(E)=\infty$, so
$$
U_{S,\theta_0}(\theta')=+\infty.
$$
Along any sequence with finite
$$
\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k)\ge\mu_0,
\qquad
\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k)\to\infty,
$$
one has
$$
U_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k)
=
c\log\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k)\,
\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k)^2
\longrightarrow\infty.
$$
Here $U_{S,\theta_0}=+\infty$ is an extended boundary-obstruction marker, not the inequality $C_{\mathrm{integrate}}\ge+\infty$.  Theorem M.10.6 excludes the corresponding uniformly finite completed-integration branch, while the displayed finite-proximity sequence supplies genuine finite lower bounds tending to infinity.  No infinite heat is assigned to an aborted run.

*Proof.* Definition P.16.1 gives $\mu_S(E)=\infty$ for every realizer of a prohibited target. For the finite sequence, every realizer has
$$
\mu_S(E)\ge\underline\mu_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k).
$$
Monotonicity of $u^2\log u$ on $u>1$ and the uniform Theorem-M.10.3 bound give
$$
C_{\mathrm{integrate}}(S,E)\ge U_{S,\theta_0}(\theta'_k).
$$
Theorem M.10.6 supplies the completed-integration scope at the boundary. ∎

<a id="theorem-p161-static-constraint-cost-stratification"></a>**Theorem P.16.1 (Static Constraint-Cost Stratification).** Let $S$ have a nonempty realized prohibition branch satisfying Definition P.16.3 and Lemma P.16.1. Then $U_S$ supplies the declared computational lower-bound stratification. If one fixed viable comparison class carries an accepted objective decomposition in which $U_S$ is a monotone nonnegative summand, a candidate with larger $U_S$ has a correspondingly larger contribution to that static objective. This conclusion specifies neither dynamics nor a trajectory-selection law; the following thermodynamic statement requires its separate reset certificate.

*Step 1 (Computational effect).* Lemma P.16.1 gives the certified super-level stratification. It asserts neither smoothness nor a pointwise gradient.

*Step 2 (Conditional thermodynamic effect).* If Theorem M.10.7 additionally assigns registered resets with
$$
H_{q_j}(P_j\mid R_j)\ge h_{\min}>0,
$$
then
$$
\frac{\Delta S_{\mathrm{bath}}}{k_B}
\ge
\sum_jH_{q_j}(P_j\mid R_j)
\ge
h_{\min}n_{\mathrm{reset}}.
$$
A stress-energy term follows only with Definition B.8's local energy-density, support, and coarse-graining data or Proposition N.8.1's retained fraction and separate coupling map. No measurable response follows until a source-to-observable model is supplied.

*Step 3 (Static objective order).* Under the explicit PCE-objective hypothesis,
a candidate with a larger certified $U_S$ contribution has the corresponding
larger declared objective contribution inside the same viable comparison
class.  This comparison does not specify an update rule, transition kernel,
initial distribution, or selection law.

Thus the theorem establishes a conditional computational cost stratification
and, when the Step-2 reset certificate is added, a conditional heat lower
bound.  It establishes no trajectory bias or avoidance.  The prohibition set
is a subset of candidate-configuration space, not a positive carrier. ∎

<a id="remark-p161-negative-space-interpretation"></a>**Remark P.16.1 (Negative-Space Interpretation).** On Theorem P.16.1's branch,
the prohibition set records targets with no admitted completed realizer and the
associated certified cost stratification.  Calling this negative space
“causal” is justified only after a separate dynamics certificate maps the
objective comparison to an observable response.

### P.16.5 Static Ledger Separation and Joint-Objective Exclusion

The single-system result below is an information theorem: two full ledgers can induce opposite nominated objective orders while presenting the same deliberative record. The coupled-system result excludes sequences approaching a prohibition set from a declared joint-objective minimizing sequence. Neither theorem specifies an evolution law, transition probability, or actual trajectory; those require an independent dynamics certificate.

<a id="theorem-p162-retained-record-nonreconstructability-of-objective-order"></a>**Theorem P.16.2 (Retained-Record Nonreconstructability of Objective Order).** Let $S$ satisfy Theorem P.16.1 and let $r_{\mathcal D}$ be the retained-record map from the full cost-and-trajectory ledger to a registered deliberative subprocess $\mathcal D_S$. Assume there are two admissible full ledgers $\ell_0,\ell_1$ such that
$$
r_{\mathcal D}(\ell_0)=r_{\mathcal D}(\ell_1)
$$
but their certified cost comparisons or resulting PCE deflections differ. Then $\mathcal D_S$ cannot reconstruct from its retained record which of those full-ledger comparisons governs the trajectory, while the registered PCE dynamics may still respond to the full ledger.

*Proof.* Equal retained records make every reconstruction based only on $r_{\mathcal D}$ return the same answer on $\ell_0$ and $\ell_1$, whereas the certified full-ledger answer differs. Such a reconstruction is therefore wrong on at least one witness. Theorem P.16.1 supplies the full-ledger cost response on its branch; Proposition 15 is not used and supplies only reset heat. $\square$

<a id="proposition-p162-joint-objective-exclusion-near-prohibition-sets"></a>**Proposition P.16.2 (Joint-Objective Exclusion Near Prohibition Sets).** Let $\{S_1,\dots,S_n\}$ be a finite collection of Property-R aggregates on a shared branch satisfying every invoked hypothesis of Theorems P.16.1, O.2, and M.6.1. On one declared viable comparison class
$$
\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal A_G,
$$
fix one registered common objective unit and positive dimensionless weights $w_i>0$, and assume that the joint PCE objective has the source-exhaustive decomposition
$$
J_{\mathrm{joint}}(\theta'_1,\ldots,\theta'_n)
=
\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{rel}}}w_iU_{S_i}(\theta'_i)
+R(\theta'_1,\ldots,\theta'_n),
\tag{P.16.2b}
$$
where $R\ge-C$ on $\mathcal C$ for one finite $C$, and that $\mathcal C$ contains a feasible comparator $z_0$ with $J_{\mathrm{joint}}(z_0)<\infty$.  Each $U_{S_i}=+\infty$ boundary marker is explicitly adopted here as an extended-objective hard constraint; it is not inferred to be a physical cost inequality. Then no minimizing sequence for $J_{\mathrm{joint}}$ can approach a realized individual prohibition set through finite-proximity points while any relevant $U_{S_i}$ diverges and all the other summands remain nonnegative.

*Proof.* Along such a sequence, Theorem P.16.1 gives $U_{S_i}\to+\infty$ for at least one relevant factor. The other $U_{S_j}$ are nonnegative by Definition P.16.3, and (P.16.2b) gives
$$
J_{\mathrm{joint}}
\ge
w_iU_{S_i}-C
\longrightarrow+\infty.
$$
The feasible comparator has finite objective, so the sequence cannot be minimizing. The common unit and weights make the sum meaningful. Theorems O.2 and M.6.1 supply only the separately certified substrate and correlation branch; the exhaustive objective decomposition, normalization, lower bound, and comparator are the independent cross-sector compatibility gates. $\square$

<a id="remark-p162-objective-exclusion-is-not-dynamical-exclusion"></a>**Remark P.16.2 (Objective Exclusion Is Not Dynamical Exclusion).** Proposition P.16.2 proves that a sequence whose relevant individual cost diverges cannot minimize the declared source-exhaustive joint objective when the remainder has the certified lower bound and a finite comparator exists. Kernel-support exclusion still requires Hypothesis 14.5.8, while an actual transition claim requires a separately registered dynamics and selection law.

<a id="corollary-p161-joint-minimizing-sequence-exclusion"></a>**Corollary P.16.1 (Joint Minimizing-Sequence Exclusion).** Under Proposition
P.16.2's source-exhaustive decomposition, common-unit and positive-weight
normalization, uniform lower bound, and finite-comparator hypotheses, no
joint-objective minimizing sequence can approach a realized individual
prohibition set along a subsequence on which a relevant $U_{S_i}$ diverges.
This conclusion introduces no dynamical state variable; the fixed joint-ledger
objects remain independent coupling data. It is an objective-level exclusion
only; support exclusion requires Hypothesis 14.5.8, and trajectory avoidance
requires an independent dynamics certificate.

*Proof.* Proposition P.16.2 gives
$J_{\mathrm{joint}}\ge w_iU_{S_i}-C\to+\infty$ because $w_i>0$, whereas the
registered comparator has finite objective. Hence the sequence cannot be
minimizing. None of these inequalities specifies a transition law or the
support of a dynamical kernel. ∎

<a id="theorem-p163-finite-kernel-classification-of-prohibition-access"></a>**Theorem P.16.3 (Finite-Kernel Classification of Prohibition Access).** Let $\Theta$ be a finite retained candidate-configuration set carrying a static cost $U:\Theta\to[0,+\infty]$, for instance the restriction of $U_{S,\theta_0}$ of Definition P.16.3, and put
$$
P:=U^{-1}(+\infty),
\qquad
A:=\Theta\setminus P,
$$
both assumed nonempty. By Lemma P.16.1, $P$ contains every realized prohibited target in $\Theta$. Let $K$ be a Markov kernel on $\Theta$ with chain $(X_n)_{n\ge0}$. Then:

1. *Access.* $\mathbb P_x(X_n\in P\text{ for some }n\ge1)=0$ for every $x\in A$ if and only if $K(x,y)=0$ for all $x\in A$ and $y\in P$.
2. *Invariant mass.* Every stationary law $\pi$ of $K$ satisfies $\pi(P)=0$ if and only if every closed communicating class of $K$ lies in $A$. When the access condition of item 1 holds, each communicating class lies in $A$ or in $P$, and the criterion reads: no closed communicating class lies in $P$.
3. *Cost-compatible kernels.* The access condition of item 1 holds for every kernel in each of the following classes: (K1) cost-nonincreasing kernels, $K(x,y)>0\Rightarrow U(y)\le U(x)$; (K2) expected-cost-nonincreasing kernels, $\sum_yK(x,y)U(y)\le U(x)$ for every $x\in A$, with $0\cdot(+\infty)=0$; (K3) kernels reversible for a Gibbs weight $\pi_\beta(x)\propto e^{-\beta U(x)}$ with $\beta>0$ and $e^{-\infty}:=0$. Class (K1) is contained in (K2).
4. *Rows on $P$ are free.* Each of (K1), (K2) and (K3) contains a kernel whose stationary laws all vanish on $P$ and a kernel with a stationary law of mass one on $P$.

Thus cost compatibility of type (K1)–(K3) forces zero dynamic access from $A$ to $P$, while zero invariant mass on $P$ holds exactly when, in addition, no closed communicating class lies in $P$, for instance when every configuration in $P$ has a positive-probability path into $A$.

*Proof.* For item 1, if $K(x,y)=0$ for all $x\in A$ and $y\in P$, then $K(x,A)=1$ for $x\in A$, and induction on $n$ gives $\mathbb P_x(X_n\in A)=1$ for every $n$. Conversely, $K(x,y)>0$ with $x\in A$ and $y\in P$ gives $\mathbb P_x(X_1\in P)\ge K(x,y)>0$.

For item 2, on a finite state space every stationary law vanishes off the union of the closed communicating classes, each closed class $C$ carries a unique stationary law $\pi_C$, $\pi_C$ is strictly positive on $C$, and the stationary laws of $K$ are exactly the convex combinations of the $\pi_C$ (Levin and Peres 2017). Hence $\pi(P)=0$ for every stationary $\pi$ if and only if $\pi_C(P)=0$ for every closed $C$, that is, if and only if every closed $C$ is disjoint from $P$. Under the access condition, $A$ is closed under $K$, so a communicating class meeting both $A$ and $P$ would contain a path from $A$ to $P$; each class therefore lies in $A$ or in $P$.

For item 3, let $x\in A$. In class (K2), a transition $K(x,y)>0$ with $y\in P$ would give $\sum_{y'}K(x,y')U(y')=+\infty>U(x)$. Every kernel in (K1) satisfies $\sum_yK(x,y)U(y)\le U(x)$ because each successor has cost at most $U(x)$. In class (K3), $\pi_\beta(x)>0$ and $\pi_\beta(y)=0$ for $y\in P$, so detailed balance $\pi_\beta(x)K(x,y)=\pi_\beta(y)K(y,x)=0$ forces $K(x,y)=0$.

For item 4, fix $x_*\in\operatorname{argmin}_AU$ and $p\in P$. The kernel $K_*(x,\cdot):=\delta_{x_*}$ lies in (K1), hence in (K2); every configuration leads to the absorbing point $x_*$, so $\delta_{x_*}$ is its unique stationary law. For (K3), let
$$
K_\beta(x,y):=|\Theta|^{-1}\min\{1,\pi_\beta(y)/\pi_\beta(x)\}\quad(y\ne x),
\qquad
K_\beta(x,x):=1-\sum_{y\ne x}K_\beta(x,y),
$$
with the ratio set equal to $1$ when $\pi_\beta(x)=0$. Then $\pi_\beta(x)K_\beta(x,y)=|\Theta|^{-1}\min\{\pi_\beta(x),\pi_\beta(y)\}$ is symmetric, $K_\beta$ is irreducible on $A$, and every $x\in P$ moves to each point of $A$ with probability $|\Theta|^{-1}>0$. Its only closed class is $A$, so $\pi_\beta$ is its unique stationary law and $\pi_\beta(P)=0$. The identity kernel lies in (K1), (K2) and (K3) and has the stationary law $\delta_p$, of mass one on $P$; so does the kernel that agrees with $K_\beta$ on $A$ and is absorbing on $P$, which is again $\pi_\beta$-reversible. ∎
