*Proof.* Reflexivity is inserted by the Reflexivity clause. Transitivity is closed by the same-perspective Transitivity clause at the fixed point. ∎

<a id="definition-p16b26-labeled-proof-system"></a>**Definition P.16b.2.6 (Labeled Proof System).**

Let $E_p(s,u,a,c)$ denote the judgment
$$
(s,u,a,c)\in R_p^\star.
$$
The proof rules are:

1. **Base:** if $(s,u,a,c)\in R_p^\circ$, infer $E_p(s,u,a,c)$;
2. **Refl:** infer $E_p(s,s,a,a)$;
3. **Trans:** from $E_p(s,t,a,b)$ and $E_p(t,u,b,c)$, infer $E_p(s,u,a,c)$;
4. **CPA:** from $E_p(s,t,a,b)$, $E_q(t,u,b,c)$, and $\mathrm{CPA}_p(q,u)=1$, infer $E_p(s,u,a,c)$.

<a id="theorem-p16b27-soundness-and-completeness-of-labeled-proofs"></a>**Theorem P.16b.2.7 (Soundness and Completeness of Labeled Proofs).**

For every $p,s,u,a,c$,
$$
\vdash E_p(s,u,a,c)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(s,u,a,c)\in R_p^\star.
$$

*Proof.* Soundness follows by induction on proof height. Base and Refl match the Seed and Reflexivity clauses. Trans and CPA match the closure clauses defining $T$. Therefore every derivable judgment appears at some finite stage and hence in $R^\star$.

For completeness, suppose $(s,u,a,c)\in R_p^\star$. By Theorem P.16b.2.4, the tuple appears in some finite stage $R_p^{(n)}$. Induct on the least such $n$. Each tuple introduced at stage $n+1$ is introduced by one of the four defining clauses of $T$. The corresponding proof rule derives it from premises that appeared at earlier stages. The induction hypothesis supplies derivations of those premises. Thus the tuple is derivable. ∎

<a id="definition-p16b28-borel-registered-perspective-layer"></a>**Definition P.16b.2.8 (Borel-Registered Perspective Layer).**

A perspective layer is *Borel-registered* when $P$ and $V$ are standard Borel spaces and the global seed and guard sets
$$
\mathsf B^\circ
:=
\left\{
(p,s,u,a,c)\in P^3\times V^2:
(s,u,a,c)\in R_p^\circ
\right\},
$$
$$
\mathsf C
:=
\left\{
(p,q,u)\in P^3:
\mathrm{CPA}_p(q,u)=1
\right\}
$$
are Borel. Register Borel probability measures $\nu$ on $P$ and $\mu_V$ on $V$, and let
$$
\lambda
:=
\overline{\nu^{\otimes2}\otimes\mu_V^{\otimes2}}
$$
denote the completion of their product on
$$
Z:=P^2\times V^2.
$$
The closure operator remains exactly the Seed, Reflexivity, Transitivity, and CPA operator of Definition P.16b.2.3; no substitution rule is added.

<a id="theorem-p16b29-analyticity-of-the-borel-registered-closure"></a>**Theorem P.16b.2.9 (Analyticity of the Borel-Registered Closure).**

On a Borel-registered perspective layer, the global closed relation
$$
\mathsf R^\star
:=
\left\{
(p,s,u,a,c)\in P^3\times V^2:
(s,u,a,c)\in R_p^\star
\right\}
$$
is analytic. Consequently, for every $p\in P$, the closure profile
$$
\mathsf R_p
:=
\left\{
(s,u,a,c)\in Z:
(p,s,u,a,c)\in\mathsf R^\star
\right\}
$$
is analytic and therefore $\lambda$-measurable.

*Proof.* Write $\mathsf R^{(n)}$ for the global form of the $n$-th Kleene stage. The seed set is Borel by Definition P.16b.2.8, and the reflexive set
$$
\{(p,s,s,a,a):p,s\in P,\ a\in V\}
$$
is Borel because equality is Borel on a standard Borel space. Suppose $\mathsf R^{(n)}$ is analytic. A Transitivity conclusion is obtained by taking two coordinate pullbacks of $\mathsf R^{(n)}$, intersecting them on their common middle perspective and value, and projecting away those middle variables. A CPA conclusion is obtained in the same way after intersecting with the Borel guard set $\mathsf C$ and retaining the validating-perspective coordinate of the left premise. Analytic sets are closed under Borel pullback, finite intersection, and projection. Hence $\mathsf R^{(n+1)}$ is analytic. The countable union
$$
\mathsf R^\star=\bigcup_{n<\omega}\mathsf R^{(n)}
$$
is analytic. Sections of analytic subsets of standard Borel products are analytic, and analytic sets are universally measurable, hence measurable in the completed product measure $\lambda$. ∎

Theorem P.16b.2.4 and Theorem P.16b.2.7 already apply to arbitrary sets $P$ and $V$. The Borel registration adds measurability.

---

### P.16b.3 Finite-Support Paradox Containment

<a id="definition-p16b31-finite-support-configuration"></a>**Definition P.16b.3.1 (Finite-Support Configuration).**

A perspective configuration has finite support if there are finite sets
$$
S_P\subseteq P,
\qquad
S_V\subseteq V
$$
such that:

1. all non-reflexive seeds lie in
$$
S_P\times S_P\times S_V\times S_V;
$$

2. if $\mathrm{CPA}_p(q,u)=1$, then
$$
p,q,u\in S_P.
$$

Let
$$
\mathrm{NonRefl}:=D\setminus\{(s,s,a,a):s\in P,
 a\in V\}.
$$

<a id="theorem-p16b32-no-explosion-under-finite-support"></a>**Theorem P.16b.3.2 (No Explosion Under Finite Support).**

In a finite-support configuration,
$$
R_p^\star\cap\mathrm{NonRefl}
\subseteq
S_P\times S_P\times S_V\times S_V
$$
for every $p\in P$.

Thus a paradox-shaped cycle does not derive arbitrary non-reflexive judgments outside the finite supported domain.

*Proof.* Induct on the finite stages $R^{(n)}$.

At stage $1$, the only non-reflexive tuples are base seeds, and by hypothesis all such seeds are supported.

Assume the result at stage $n$. A new non-reflexive tuple at stage $n+1$ can arise only by Trans or CPA. For Trans, both premises are supported by the induction hypothesis unless one premise is reflexive. If one premise is reflexive, the conclusion equals the other premise and remains supported. If both are non-reflexive, the composed endpoints and values are already in $S_P$ and $S_V$.

For CPA, the guard condition ensures the validating and target perspectives involved in the imported step are in $S_P$. The local and imported premises are supported by the induction hypothesis unless reflexive, and reflexive premises do not introduce new values or perspectives. Therefore the conclusion remains supported.

Taking the union over all finite stages preserves the inclusion. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16b32a-containment-from-supported-seeds"></a>**Corollary P.16b.3.2a (Containment from Supported Seeds).** For the closure of Definition P.16b.2.3, let finite sets $S_P\subseteq P$ and $S_V\subseteq V$ contain every non-reflexive seed:
$$
R_p^\circ\cap\mathrm{NonRefl}
\subseteq S_P\times S_P\times S_V\times S_V
\qquad(p\in P).
$$
Then
$$
R_p^\star\cap\mathrm{NonRefl}
\subseteq S_P\times S_P\times S_V\times S_V
\qquad(p\in P),
$$
without a support restriction on the CPA guards or on the validating perspective $p$.

*Proof.* Induct on derivations. A seed is reflexive or supported by hypothesis; a reflexivity step is reflexive. For a transitivity or adoption step with premises $(s,t,a,b)$ and $(t,u,b,c)$, if the first premise is reflexive, the conclusion equals the second premise. If the second is reflexive, the conclusion equals the first. If both are supported, then $s,u\in S_P$ and $a,c\in S_V$, so the conclusion is supported. The guard does not add an endpoint or a value. Theorem P.16b.2.7 identifies these finite derivations with the least closure. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16b33-paradox-as-local-cycle-rather-than-global-explosion"></a>**Corollary P.16b.3.3 (Paradox as Local Cycle Rather Than Global Explosion).**

A role-sensitive or perspective-sensitive self-reference cycle may exist inside the supported substructure without forcing every judgment in $D$.

*Proof.* Theorem P.16b.3.2 bounds every non-reflexive derived judgment by the finite supported set. Since $D$ may contain values and perspectives outside that set, arbitrary judgments outside it are not derivable. ∎

---

### P.16b.4 Process Typing and Local Classicality

<a id="definition-p16b41-prop-and-proc-types"></a>**Definition P.16b.4.1 (Prop and Proc Types).**

Let $E$ be an expression evaluated at perspective $p$.

$E$ is **Prop-typed** at $p$ when all admissible evaluation sequences converge to the same Boolean value, independent of initial condition and evaluation strategy.

$E$ is **Proc-typed** at $p$ when this fails: the evaluation oscillates, diverges, depends on an initial condition, depends on strategy, or requires non-well-founded context update.

The local truth predicate $\tau_p(E)$ is defined only for Prop-typed expressions.

<a id="theorem-p16b42-local-classicality-of-value-compositional-prop-typed-expressions"></a>**Theorem P.16b.4.2 (Local Classicality of Value-Compositional Prop-Typed Expressions).**

At a fixed perspective $p$, assume the local Boolean language is value-compositional: the connectives $\neg$, $\wedge$, $\vee$, and $\to$ are interpreted extensionally by the usual truth tables on settled Boolean values and do not introduce additional evaluation dynamics. Then the Prop-typed expressions form a classical Boolean algebra under the usual Boolean connectives, after quotienting expressions by equality of local Boolean value.

*Proof.* Each Prop-typed expression has a unique Boolean value in $\{0,1\}$ at $p$. By the value-compositional branch hypothesis, the value of $\neg E$, $E\wedge F$, $E\vee F$, and $E\to F$ is obtained by the ordinary Boolean truth tables on those unique values, and the resulting expressions remain Prop-typed at the quotient level. Since the quotient identifies expressions with the same value, the quotient algebra has exactly the usual Boolean operations on $\{0,1\}$. Hence all classical Boolean laws hold locally on the value-compositional Prop-typed quotient. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16b43-liar-pattern-expressions-are-not-prop-typed-on-the-unstratified-branch"></a>**Corollary P.16b.4.3 (Liar-Pattern Expressions Are Not Prop-Typed on the Unstratified Branch).**

On the unstratified branch requiring one role-insensitive value for a negating reflexive expression, the Liar pattern is Proc-typed rather than Prop-typed.

*Proof.* By Theorem P.16b.1.3, the unstratified collapsed Liar equation has no Boolean solution. Therefore there is no unique Boolean value to assign. By Definition P.16b.4.1, it is not Prop-typed. ∎

<a id="remark-p16b44-decidability-boundary"></a>**Remark P.16b.4.4 (Decidability Boundary).**

On finite bounded-evaluation branches, Prop/Proc typing can be checked by finite convergence analysis. In unrestricted languages with arbitrary self-reference and syntax-quantification, Prop/Proc classification need not be decidable.

---

### P.16b.5 Holonomy and Global-Section Obstruction

<a id="definition-p16b51-finite-signed-logical-atlas"></a>**Definition P.16b.5.1 (Finite Signed Logical Atlas).**

A finite signed logical atlas consists of:

1. a finite set of vantages $\mathcal V$;
2. for each $i\in\mathcal V$, a local Boolean valuation domain;
3. for each overlap edge $(i,j)$ and shared atom $a$, a sign
$$
s_{ij}(a)\in\{+1,-1\}.
$$

A local valuation assigns
$$
v_i(a)\in\{+1,-1\}.
$$
Edge compatibility is
$$
v_i(a)=s_{ij}(a)v_j(a).
\tag{P.16b.5.1}
$$

For a cycle
$$
\gamma=i_0i_1\cdots i_ki_0,
$$
define holonomy
$$
H_\gamma(a)=\prod_{r=0}^k s_{i_ri_{r+1}}(a).
\tag{P.16b.5.2}
$$

<a id="theorem-p16b52-flatness-and-compatibility-criterion"></a>**Theorem P.16b.5.2 (Flatness-and-Compatibility Criterion).**

On a connected finite signed atlas, a global section for atom $a$ exists if and only if:

1. every cycle has trivial holonomy,
$$
H_\gamma(a)=+1;
$$

2. local valuations are edgewise compatible,
$$
v_i(a)=s_{ij}(a)v_j(a)
$$
on every overlap edge.

*Proof.* If a global section exists, transporting the value around any closed cycle must return the same value. Transport around $\gamma$ multiplies the value by $H_\gamma(a)$. Therefore $H_\gamma(a)=+1$. Edge compatibility is the definition of local restrictions agreeing on overlaps.

Conversely, choose a root vantage $i_0$ and assign a value at $i_0$. For any other vantage $j$, define the value at $j$ by transporting along a path from $i_0$ to $j$. Trivial holonomy makes this path-independent, because two paths from $i_0$ to $j$ form a cycle when one is reversed. Edge compatibility ensures the transported values agree with local overlap data. Hence the local valuations glue to a global section. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16b53-global-curvature-without-local-contradiction"></a>**Corollary P.16b.5.3 (Global Curvature Without Local Contradiction).**

A signed atlas may be locally classical at every vantage and still lack a global section because of nontrivial holonomy.

*Proof.* Local classicality concerns Boolean evaluation inside each vantage. Theorem P.16b.5.2 shows that global gluing additionally requires trivial cycle holonomy. A cycle with $H_\gamma(a)=-1$ obstructs the global section while leaving each local Boolean algebra intact. ∎

---

### P.16b.6 Cogito-Centered Perspective Geometry

<a id="definition-p16b61-evidential-perspective-space"></a>**Definition P.16b.6.1 (Evidential Perspective Space).**

Let $(V_C,\mathcal F,\nu)$ be a probability space of contents. A graded evidential perspective is a measurable function
$$
p:V_C\to[0,1].
$$
Let $\mathcal P\subseteq L^1(V_C,\nu)$ be a lattice of such functions closed under pointwise essential suprema and infima.

Fix a measurable set
$$
I\in\mathcal F
$$
representing minimal presence-as-experiencing, and assume
$$
\mathbf 1_I\in\mathcal P.
$$
Equivalently, the retained evidential-perspective branch is closed under adjoining the minimal presence indicator.

Define the self-evidence operator
$$
\mathrm{SE}(p)=\max\{p,\mathbf 1_I\}.
\tag{P.16b.6.1}
$$

<a id="theorem-p16b62-cogito-as-least-self-evidence-fixed-point"></a>**Theorem P.16b.6.2 (Cogito as Least Self-Evidence Fixed Point).**

The operator $\mathrm{SE}$ is a closure operator on $\mathcal P$. Its least fixed point is
$$
p^\ast=\mathbf 1_I.
$$

*Proof.* Since $\mathbf 1_I\in\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal P$ is closed under pointwise essential suprema, $\mathrm{SE}$ is a well-defined map $\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$. The operator is extensive because
$$
p\le \max\{p,\mathbf 1_I\}.
$$
It is monotone because $p\le q$ implies
$$
\max\{p,\mathbf 1_I\}\le\max\{q,\mathbf 1_I\}.
$$
It is idempotent because
$$
\mathrm{SE}(\mathrm{SE}(p))
=
\max\{\max(p,\mathbf 1_I),\mathbf 1_I\}
=
\max\{p,\mathbf 1_I\}
=
\mathrm{SE}(p).
$$
Thus $\mathrm{SE}$ is a closure operator.

A fixed point satisfies
$$
p=\max\{p,\mathbf 1_I\},
$$
which holds exactly when $p\ge\mathbf 1_I$ almost everywhere. The least such element is $\mathbf 1_I$. ∎

<a id="definition-p16b63-perspective-metric-and-cogito-radius"></a>**Definition P.16b.6.3 (Perspective Metric and Cogito Radius).**

Define
$$
\Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,q)=\int_{V_C}|p(v)-q(v)|\,d\nu(v).
\tag{P.16b.6.2}
$$
After quotienting by equality almost everywhere, this is a metric. The cogito radius is
$$
r_P(p)=\Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,p^\ast).
\tag{P.16b.6.3}
$$

<a id="theorem-p16b64-cogito-radius-is-1-lipschitz"></a>**Theorem P.16b.6.4 (Cogito Radius Is 1-Lipschitz).**

For all $p,q\in\mathcal P$,
$$
|r_P(p)-r_P(q)|\le \Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,q).
$$

*Proof.* The triangle inequality gives
$$
\Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,p^\ast)
\le
\Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,q)+\Delta_{\mathcal P}(q,p^\ast).
$$
Thus
$$
r_P(p)-r_P(q)\le\Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,q).
$$
Interchanging $p$ and $q$ gives
$$
r_P(q)-r_P(p)\le\Delta_{\mathcal P}(p,q).
$$
Combining the two inequalities proves the claim. ∎

<a id="definition-p16b65-cogito-origin-separating-branch"></a>**Definition P.16b.6.5 (Cogito-Origin Separating Branch).**

A content profile chart
$$
\mathcal P_S(c)=(\Delta Q_S(c),\mu_S(c),\sigma_S(c))
$$
is normalized and separating at the origin on a retained content class $\mathcal E$ when it is invariant under $\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S$ on $\mathcal E$, satisfies
$$
c\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S\psi_C
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal P_S(c)=(0,0,0),
$$
and satisfies
$$
\mathcal P_S(c)=(0,0,0)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
c\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S\psi_C
$$
for all $c\in\mathcal E$, where $\psi_C$ is the cogito content and $\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S$ is operational response equivalence.

<a id="theorem-p16b66-unique-zero-on-the-separating-origin-branch"></a>**Theorem P.16b.6.6 (Unique Zero on the Separating-Origin Branch).**

Define the evaluation cost
$$
E_S(c)=
\sqrt{
 w_Q\Delta Q_S(c)^2+w_\mu\mu_S(c)^2+w_\sigma\sigma_S(c)^2
}
\tag{P.16b.6.4}
$$
with strictly positive weights. On the cogito-origin separating branch,
$$
E_S(c)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
c\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S\psi_C.
$$

*Proof.* If $c\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S\psi_C$, then the profile agrees with the cogito profile on the branch, so $\mathcal P_S(c)=(0,0,0)$ and $E_S(c)=0$.

Conversely, if $E_S(c)=0$, then every term in (P.16b.6.4) is nonnegative and each weight is positive. Therefore
$$
\Delta Q_S(c)=\mu_S(c)=\sigma_S(c)=0.
$$
By the separating-origin hypothesis, this implies
$$
c\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S\psi_C.
$$
∎

<a id="remark-p16b67-boundary-of-the-cogito-zero-claim"></a>**Remark P.16b.6.7 (Boundary of the Cogito Zero Claim).**

Without the separating-origin branch, $E_S(c)=0$ proves only that the chosen finite profile chart assigns zero to $c$. The separating condition is the load-bearing hypothesis.

---

### P.16b.7 Predictive Role-Position Equivalence

<a id="definition-p16b71-operational-response-presheaf-of-a-content"></a>**Definition P.16b.7.1 (Operational Response Presheaf of a Content).**

Let $S$ be a knowledge system with retained protocol category $\mathsf P_S$. For content $c$, define its operational response presheaf
$$
\mathcal R_c^S:\mathsf P_S^{op}\to\mathbf{Set}
$$
or, on probabilistic branches,
$$
\mathcal R_c^S:\mathsf P_S^{op}\to\mathbf{Prob}_{\mathrm{fin}}.
$$
For a protocol $P\in\mathsf P_S$, $\mathcal R_c^S(P)$ is the finite response produced when $S$ engages content $c$ under $P$.

<a id="definition-p16b72-predictive-function-space"></a>**Definition P.16b.7.2 (Predictive-Function Space).**

Define operational equivalence by
$$
c_1\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S c_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal R_{c_1}^S\cong\mathcal R_{c_2}^S
$$
by natural isomorphism of response presheaves.

The predictive-function space is the quotient
$$
\mathcal F_S:=\mathsf{Cont}_S/\equiv_{\mathrm{op}}^S.
$$
The position map is
$$
\pi_S:\mathsf{Cont}_S\to\mathcal F_S,
\qquad
\pi_S(c)=[c]_{\mathrm{op}}.
$$

<a id="definition-p16b73-predictive-role"></a>**Definition P.16b.7.3 (Predictive Role).**

The predictive role of $c$ for $S$ is
$$
\operatorname{Role}_S(c):=[\mathcal R_c^S]_{\cong}.
$$

<a id="theorem-p16b74-quotient-formula-for-predictive-role-and-position"></a>**Theorem P.16b.7.4 (Quotient Formula for Predictive Role and Position).**

For every retained content item $c$,
$$
\pi_S(c)=[c]_{\mathrm{op}}=[\mathcal R_c^S]_{\cong}=\operatorname{Role}_S(c).
$$
Thus qualitative predictive role and quantitative position in $\mathcal F_S$ are the same operational invariant expressed in two vocabularies.

*Proof.* By Definition P.16b.7.2, $\pi_S(c)$ is the equivalence class of $c$ under natural-isomorphism equivalence of operational response presheaves. Therefore
$$
\pi_S(c)=[\mathcal R_c^S]_{\cong}.
$$
By Definition P.16b.7.3, the right-hand side is $\operatorname{Role}_S(c)$. Hence all displayed quantities are identical in the quotient. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16b75-finite-profiles-are-descriptors-not-complete-identities"></a>**Corollary P.16b.7.5 (Finite Profiles Are Descriptors, Not Complete Identities).**

A finite profile such as
$$
(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)
$$
is a finite descriptor on the part of $\mathcal F_S$ where it is defined. Equality of profile coordinates implies equality of predictive role only on a separating-profile branch. The term *coordinate chart* is reserved for a map proved to be an injective local parametrization on a registered topological domain.

*Proof.* A point of $\mathcal F_S$ is a response-presheaf equivalence class. A finite descriptor need not separate distinct classes. Therefore equality of descriptor values is weaker than role-position equality unless injectivity on the retained class has been proved. ∎

---

### P.16b.8 Triadic Description-Arity

<a id="definition-p16b81-spap-role-set"></a>**Definition P.16b.8.1 (SPAP Role Set).**

The SPAP role set is
$$
\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SPAP}}=\{\Phi,\Pi,\Gamma\},
$$
where:

1. $\Phi$ is the state role;
2. $\Pi$ is the prediction role;
3. $\Gamma$ is the control/comparison role.

The SPAP register notation $(\phi,p,c)$ realizes these roles. A full SPAP role implementation is a typed register with projections onto all three sorts and an admissible update map whose domain contains the ordered pair consisting of a present state and a stored prediction and whose codomain contains the comparison/update channel. The update involution is an operation inside the role system, not a fourth role.

<a id="theorem-p16b82-three-role-necessity"></a>**Theorem P.16b.8.2 (Three-Role Necessity).**

The SPAP architecture requires all three roles $\Phi$, $\Pi$, and $\Gamma$. No two-role subsystem implements the full SPAP cycle.

*Proof.* Work in the typed signature of Definition P.16b.8.1. A full implementation must type every occurrence of the SPAP cycle: the realized state term, the stored prediction term, and the comparison/update term. If $\Phi$ is removed, the state term has no sort, so the comparison map has no current-state argument. If $\Pi$ is removed, the prediction term has no sort, so there is no stored target against which the current state can be compared. If $\Gamma$ is removed, the comparison/update codomain has no sort, so the ordered cycle cannot feed an error or control value back into the next predictive step. In each two-role reduct, at least one required typed occurrence is undefined, hence the reduct cannot implement the full SPAP cycle. Conversely, the triple $(\phi,p,c)$ supplies one value in each required sort, and the update involution is an internal operation on those sorts. Therefore three roles are necessary and sufficient for the typed SPAP role architecture. ∎

<a id="definition-p16b83-description-lenses"></a>**Definition P.16b.8.3 (Description Lenses).**

The semantic-extension ledger uses three primitive description lenses:

1. **Operational/categorical lens $\mathsf C$:** finite protocol identity, response presheaves, operational quotienting, branch predicates, and categorical role structure.

2. **Geometric/topological lens $\mathsf G$:** connections, holonomy, curvature, signed atlases, shape, transport, and metric geometry.

3. **Measure-theoretic/dynamical lens $\mathsf M$:** probability measures, Markov kernels, entropy, cost, convergence, and quantitative profiles.

<a id="definition-p16b84-description-arity-of-a-finite-ledger"></a>**Definition P.16b.8.4 (Description-Arity of a Finite Ledger).**

For a finite theorem ledger $\mathcal L$, let $\operatorname{Req}(T)$ be the subset of $\{\mathsf C,\mathsf G,\mathsf M\}$ used essentially in the proof of $T$. Define
$$
\operatorname{descArity}(\mathcal L)
=
\min\left\{|S|:S\subseteq\{\mathsf C,\mathsf G,\mathsf M\},
\ \operatorname{Req}(T)\subseteq S\text{ for every }T\in\mathcal L\right\}.
$$

<a id="branch-condition-p16b84a-primitive-lens-independence"></a>**Branch Condition P.16b.8.4a (Primitive-Lens Independence).**

On the typed non-collapse branch, the three lenses $\mathsf C$, $\mathsf G$, and $\mathsf M$ are treated as primitive description lenses. No one of the three is definitionally eliminable into the other two while preserving the theorem statements of the retained ledger. In particular, response-presheaf quotienting, signed holonomy/transport, and measure-defined metric or dynamical data remain typed separately.

<a id="theorem-p16b85-three-lens-minimality-of-the-semantic-ledger"></a>**Theorem P.16b.8.5 (Three-Lens Minimality of the Semantic Ledger).**

Let $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sem}}$ be the finite ledger consisting of Theorems P.16b.1.3, P.16b.2.4, P.16b.3.2, P.16b.4.2, P.16b.5.2, P.16b.6.2, P.16b.6.4, P.16b.7.4, P.16b.8.2, P.16b.9.5, P.16b.10.3, P.16b.10.4, and P.16b.10.6. On the typed non-collapse branch with Primitive-Lens Independence,
$$
\operatorname{descArity}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sem}})=3.
$$

*Proof.* Every listed theorem uses only the three lenses $\mathsf C$, $\mathsf G$, and $\mathsf M$, so $\operatorname{descArity}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sem}})\le3$.

No two-lens cover suffices. Theorem P.16b.7.4 requires response presheaves and operational quotienting, so $\mathsf C$ is essential. Theorem P.16b.5.2 requires signed transport around cycles and holonomy, so $\mathsf G$ is essential. Theorem P.16b.6.4 requires an $L^1$ integral metric and the triangle inequality for a measure-defined distance, so $\mathsf M$ is essential. By Branch Condition P.16b.8.4a, none of these three primitive sorts is definitionally eliminable by the other two on the retained branch. Therefore every cover must contain all three lenses, giving $\operatorname{descArity}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{sem}})\ge3$.

Combining the two inequalities yields equality. ∎

<a id="remark-p16b85a-branch-conditional-status-of-descarity-3"></a>**Remark P.16b.8.5a (Branch-Conditional Status of descArity = 3).** Theorem P.16b.8.5 is a conditional theorem on the typed non-collapse branch with Primitive-Lens Independence (Branch Condition P.16b.8.4a). Alternative formal foundations in which one of $\mathsf C$, $\mathsf G$, or $\mathsf M$ is definitionally encoded inside the other two — for example, a purely categorical encoding that internalizes measure data as enriched homs, or a purely measure-theoretic encoding that reconstructs categorical quotients from $\sigma$-algebras — supply alternative branches on which descArity may be strictly less than three for the same ledger.

<a id="corollary-p16b86-role-compatible-lens-map"></a>**Corollary P.16b.8.6 (Role-Compatible Lens Map).**

The map
$$
\Theta(\mathsf C)=\Phi,
\qquad
\Theta(\mathsf M)=\Pi,
\qquad
\Theta(\mathsf G)=\Gamma
$$
is role-compatible: operational identity supplies the state role, measure/dynamics supplies predictive law, and geometry supplies comparison/transport.

*Proof.* $\mathsf C$ decides what counts as the retained object or state, matching $\Phi$. $\mathsf M$ supplies probability, cost, and dynamics for prediction, matching $\Pi$. $\mathsf G$ supplies transport and comparison across positions, matching $\Gamma$. The three source lenses and three target roles are both necessary by Theorem P.16b.8.5 and Theorem P.16b.8.2. ∎

### P.16b.9 Predictive Models, Shape, and Compression

<a id="definition-p16b91-predictive-model-presentation"></a>**Definition P.16b.9.1 (Predictive Model Presentation).**

A predictive model presentation for a knowledge system $S$ is a tuple
$$
\mathcal M_S=(\mathcal C_S,\mathcal R_S,\ell_S,\mu_S,\mathrm{Pred}_S)
$$
where:

1. $\mathcal C_S$ is a finite or locally finite typed concept/protocol category;
2. $\mathcal R_S$ is a response presheaf on $\mathcal C_S$;
3. $\ell_S$ is a description and traversal cost;
4. $\mu_S$ is a query distribution;
5. $\mathrm{Pred}_S$ is the prediction operation obtained by finite diagram evaluation, path traversal, or morphism composition.

The signal cost is
$$
SC(\mathcal M_S)=
\operatorname{CodeLength}(\mathcal C_S,\mathcal R_S,\ell_S,\mathrm{Pred}_S)
+
\mathbb E_{q\sim\mu_S}\left[\ell_S(\mathrm{PredPath}(q))\right].
$$

The meaning potential is
$$
MP(\mathcal M_S)=
\mathbb E_{q\sim\mu_S}\left[\operatorname{Adeq}(\mathrm{Pred}_S(q),q)\right].
$$

<a id="definition-p16b91a-budget-restriction-query-to-role-allocation-and-occupancy"></a>**Definition P.16b.9.1a (Budget Restriction, Query-to-Role Allocation, and Occupancy).**

Fix a finite predictive budget $B$ in the sense of Definition P.16d.0.1 and a registered protocol embedding
$$
\iota_B:\mathsf P_B\hookrightarrow\mathsf P_S.
$$
Let $T_B:\mathsf P_B^{op}\to\mathbf{Resp}$ be a registered finite or compact response presheaf. For every arrow $f:P'\to P$ in $\mathsf P_B$, require the coarse-graining and tolerance maps to satisfy the naturality identity
$$
T_B(f)\circ\vartheta_{B,P}\circ(q_{B,P})_*
=
\vartheta_{B,P'}\circ(q_{B,P'})_*
\circ\mathcal R_c^S(\iota_B f)
\tag{P.16b.9.1a}
$$
on every response law used below. On a deterministic branch, a response is first identified with its Dirac law. A set-valued response lacking a registered probability-law or deterministic embedding is outside this budget restriction rather than being pushed forward implicitly.

Define $\mathsf{Cont}_{S,B}$ to be the retained contents $c\in\mathsf{Cont}_S$ for which every response law in (P.16b.9.1a) is defined and the displayed naturality identities hold. For $c\in\mathsf{Cont}_{S,B}$, define the budget-level response presheaf by
$$
\mathcal R_c^{S,B}(P)
:=
\vartheta_{B,P}\!\left((q_{B,P})_*\mathcal R_c^S(\iota_B P)\right),
\qquad
\mathcal R_c^{S,B}(f):=T_B(f).
$$
Put
$$
c\equiv_B^S c'
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal R_c^{S,B}\cong\mathcal R_{c'}^{S,B},
$$
$$
\mathcal F_{S,B}:=\mathsf{Cont}_{S,B}/{\equiv_B^S},
\qquad
\operatorname{Role}_{S,B}(c):=[c]_{\equiv_B^S}.
\tag{P.16b.9.1b}
$$
This is a budget-level role quotient. Equality in the full role space $\mathcal F_S$ descends to equality in $\mathcal F_{S,B}$ only when the registered restriction and tolerance maps are equivariant under the corresponding full natural isomorphism.

Let $\mathsf Q_{S,B}$ be a nonempty retained query family equipped with a registered probability law $\mu_{S,B}$ obtained by restriction and normalization of $\mu_S$, or supplied directly when that restriction has zero mass. Require every evaluated adequacy integrand to be measurable and integrable. For a presentation $\mathcal M$ on this branch, set
$$
MP_B(\mathcal M)
:=
\int_{\mathsf Q_{S,B}}
\operatorname{Adeq}(\operatorname{Pred}_{\mathcal M}(q),q)
\,d\mu_{S,B}(q),
$$
$$
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE},B}(\mathcal M)
:=
SC_B(\mathcal M)-\lambda MP_B(\mathcal M),
$$
where $SC_B$ is the complete signal cost evaluated in the units and over the horizon fixed by $B$. Let
$$
\varnothing\ne\mathcal F_{S,B}^{\mathrm{act}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{S,B}
$$
be the finite set of predictive roles available to the retained prediction paths.

A query-to-role allocation kernel is a registered Markov kernel
$$
\kappa_{S,B}:\mathsf Q_{S,B}\longrightarrow
\Delta(\mathcal F_{S,B}^{\mathrm{act}})
$$
defined on the quotient roles themselves and satisfying
$$
\kappa_{S,B}(\mathfrak r\mid q)>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\text{the registered evaluation path for }q\text{ uses }\mathfrak r
$$
for $\mu_{S,B}$-almost every $q$. Its role-occupancy law is
$$
\nu_{S,B}(\mathfrak r)
=
\int_{\mathsf Q_{S,B}}
\kappa_{S,B}(\mathfrak r\mid q)\,d\mu_{S,B}(q).
\tag{P.16b.9.1c}
$$
Every coordinate $q\mapsto\kappa_{S,B}(\mathfrak r\mid q)$ is measurable. Fractional allocation records shared participation of several quotient roles in one prediction path. Because the kernel is registered on $\mathcal F_{S,B}^{\mathrm{act}}$, it cannot depend on a choice of content representative. Query frequency alone is not a role-occupancy law.

<a id="theorem-p16b92-finite-resource-compression-necessity"></a>**Theorem P.16b.9.2 (Finite-Resource Compression Necessity).**

Fix a nonempty task family $Q\subseteq\mathsf Q_{S,B}$, a preregistered adequacy threshold $a_0$, and a finite presentation-cost cap $b_S\ge0$ in the units of $SC_B$. Let $\mathfrak A(Q,a_0)$ be the registered admissible presentations satisfying the task and adequacy requirement. Assume a finite presentation-grammar certificate proves the exhaustive disjoint normal-form decomposition
$$
\mathfrak A(Q,a_0)
=
\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{enum}}(Q,a_0)
\,\dot\cup\,
\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{shared}}(Q,a_0).
\tag{P.16b.9.2a}
$$
Here an enumerative presentation stores the retained task responses independently and contains no rule, relation, program, or composition node shared by two distinct retained query paths. A shared-structure presentation contains at least one such node used by two distinct retained query paths. Define
$$
K_{\mathrm{enum}}(Q,a_0)
:=
\inf_{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{enum}}(Q,a_0)}
SC_B(\mathcal M),
\qquad
\inf\varnothing:=+\infty.
\tag{P.16b.9.2b}
$$
Call $S$ viable on this registered task branch at cap $b_S$ exactly when there exists $\mathcal M\in\mathfrak A(Q,a_0)$ with
$$
SC_B(\mathcal M)\le b_S.
\tag{P.16b.9.2c}
$$
If
$$
K_{\mathrm{enum}}(Q,a_0)>b_S
$$
and $S$ is viable in the sense of (P.16b.9.2c), then at least one cap-feasible shared-structure presentation exists, and every cap-feasible member of $\mathfrak A(Q,a_0)$ belongs to $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{shared}}(Q,a_0)$.

*Proof.* Viability supplies a presentation $\mathcal M$ with $SC_B(\mathcal M)\le b_S$. If $\mathcal M$ were enumerative, Equation (P.16b.9.2b) would give
$$
K_{\mathrm{enum}}(Q,a_0)
\le SC_B(\mathcal M)
\le b_S,
$$
contrary to the strict hypothesis. The exhaustive normal-form certificate (P.16b.9.2a) therefore places $\mathcal M$ in $\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{shared}}(Q,a_0)$. The same argument applies to every cap-feasible presentation. ∎

The scalar cap $b_S$ is presentation-cost branch data. Identifying it with $C_P(S)$ requires a separate unit and domination bridge proving that the same complete presentation cost is bounded by, or equals, $C_P(S)$. Without that bridge, finite $C_P(S)$ alone does not imply (P.16b.9.2c).

<a id="remark-p16b92a-complete-cost-and-a-shared-sensory-presentation"></a>**Remark P.16b.9.2a (Complete Cost and a Shared Sensory Presentation).**

The shared-node theorem evaluates a presentation through its complete registered signal cost. That cost includes its description and the query-weighted traversal expectation

$$
\mathbb E_{q\sim\mu_S}[\ell_S(\mathrm{PredPath}(q))].
$$

A shared node can shorten the description while increasing traversal cost. Its admissibility depends on the sum charged by Definition P.16b.9.1 under the registered query law $\mu_S$. The presentation cap $b_S$ controls this sum.

A two-channel sensory predictor illustrates the construction. Let two independently variable input coordinates represent sweetness and acidity, and let the retained task include a joint assessment such as ripeness. The predictor may route both coordinates through a shared intermediate response used by several retained queries. On a task whose best adequate enumerative presentation costs more than $b_S$, and for which an adequate presentation within $b_S$ exists, the shared-node theorem requires structure shared across query paths. The example identifies the task, its inputs, and the economy the theorem measures.

The externally weighted graphs of Definition P.2.6.3d represent a separate coarse-graining. Relating their weights to the registered traversal cost requires an explicit unit and response map.

**Finite presentation example.** Register two independent input coordinates $x,y\in\{0,\ldots,15\}$ and two equally weighted queries $q_1(x,y)=x+y$, $q_2(x,y)=2(x+y)$ with exact adequacy. In the registered table-or-shared-program grammar, the enumerative normal form stores two independent 256-entry tables with five and six bits per entry, respectively. Its description therefore costs $256(5+6)=2816$ bits before traversal charges. A shared program stores one addition node and one doubling node; a registered encoding of at most 128 bits and a traversal charge of at most 16 bits gives complete cost at most 144 bits. At cap $b_S=200$ bits, the shared program is viable and every enumerative presentation exceeds the cap. Theorem P.16b.9.2 consequently forces sharing on this declared grammar. Enlarging the grammar requires recertifying its normal forms and enumerative lower bound.

<a id="theorem-p16b93-pce-selection-of-equal-adequacy-compression"></a>**Theorem P.16b.9.3 (PCE Selection of Equal-Adequacy Compression).**

On the PCE presentation branch, define
$$
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\mathcal M_S)=SC(\mathcal M_S)-\lambda MP(\mathcal M_S),
\qquad
\lambda>0.
$$
If
$$
MP(\mathcal M_1)=MP(\mathcal M_2)
$$
and
$$
SC(\mathcal M_1)<SC(\mathcal M_2),
$$
then PCE strictly selects $\mathcal M_1$ over $\mathcal M_2$.

*Proof.* Subtract the two objective values:
$$
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\mathcal M_1)-\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\mathcal M_2)
=
SC(\mathcal M_1)-SC(\mathcal M_2)
-
\lambda(MP(\mathcal M_1)-MP(\mathcal M_2)).
$$
The meaning potentials are equal, so the second term vanishes. The signal-cost difference is negative. Hence
$$
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\mathcal M_1)<\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE}}(\mathcal M_2).
$$
∎

<a id="theorem-p16b93a-occupancy-controlled-pairwise-deletion-bound"></a>**Theorem P.16b.9.3a (Occupancy-Controlled Pairwise Deletion Bound).**

The law $\nu_{S,B}$ of Definition P.16b.9.1a is a probability measure on $\mathcal F_{S,B}^{\mathrm{act}}$ and is independent of the retained content representative used for a predictive role.

Fix $\mathfrak r\in\mathcal F_{S,B}^{\mathrm{act}}$ and two feasible presentations $\mathcal M$ and $\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r}$ on the same registered comparison branch, where the latter removes $\mathfrak r$ while keeping the query law, protocol family, adequacy functional, tolerances, and PCE parameter $\lambda$ fixed. Suppose that for $\mu_{S,B}$-almost every $q$,
$$
0
\le
\operatorname{Adeq}(\operatorname{Pred}_{\mathcal M}(q),q)
-
\operatorname{Adeq}(\operatorname{Pred}_{\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r}}(q),q)
\le
L_{\mathfrak r}\kappa_{S,B}(\mathfrak r\mid q)
\tag{P.16b.9.3a}
$$
for a finite constant $L_{\mathfrak r}\ge0$. Then
$$
0
\le
MP_B(\mathcal M)-MP_B(\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r})
\le
L_{\mathfrak r}\nu_{S,B}(\mathfrak r).
\tag{P.16b.9.3b}
$$
If, in addition,
$$
c_{\mathfrak r}
:=
SC_B(\mathcal M)-SC_B(\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r})>0,
$$
then the PCE objective strictly prefers $\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r}$ whenever
$$
c_{\mathfrak r}
>
\lambda L_{\mathfrak r}\nu_{S,B}(\mathfrak r).
\tag{P.16b.9.3c}
$$
This is a sufficient pairwise comparison, not a uniqueness claim for the global PCE minimizer.

*Proof.* For every $q$, the Markov-kernel normalization gives
$$
\sum_{\mathfrak r\in\mathcal F_{S,B}^{\mathrm{act}}}
\kappa_{S,B}(\mathfrak r\mid q)=1.
$$
The active role set is finite, so integration and summation commute and yield
$$
\sum_{\mathfrak r}\nu_{S,B}(\mathfrak r)
=
\int_{\mathsf Q_{S,B}}1\,d\mu_{S,B}=1.
$$
The kernel is indexed by quotient points of $\mathcal F_{S,B}$, so changing a content representative within the same budget-level natural-isomorphism class changes neither $\kappa_{S,B}$ nor $\nu_{S,B}$.

Integrating (P.16b.9.3a) against $\mu_{S,B}$ gives (P.16b.9.3b) by the definition of $MP_B$ and Equation (P.16b.9.1c). Put
$$
\Delta MP_B
=
MP_B(\mathcal M)-MP_B(\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r}).
$$
The objective change under deletion is
$$
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE},B}(\mathcal M^{-\mathfrak r})
-
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{PCE},B}(\mathcal M)
=
-c_{\mathfrak r}+\lambda\Delta MP_B.
$$
By (P.16b.9.3b), this is at most
$$
-c_{\mathfrak r}
+
\lambda L_{\mathfrak r}\nu_{S,B}(\mathfrak r),
$$
which is strictly negative under (P.16b.9.3c). ∎

<a id="remark-p16b93d-scope-of-occupancy"></a>**Remark P.16b.9.3d (Scope of Occupancy).** Occupancy is not engagement depth, abstraction level, importance, or retention priority. It affects a PCE comparison only through an explicit adequacy envelope such as (P.16b.9.3a), together with the complete cost difference on one fixed branch.

<a id="definition-p16b94-exact-shape"></a>**Definition P.16b.9.4 (Exact Shape).**

A model region $A$ is a finite retained subdiagram of $\mathcal C_S$ with restricted response presheaf and cost data. Two regions $A$ and $B$ have the same exact shape when there is a typed isomorphism
$$
\varphi:A\to B
$$
preserving relation types, incidence, composition, relevant cost data, and response presheaves:
$$
\mathcal R_A\cong\varphi^*\mathcal R_B.
$$

<a id="theorem-p16b95-operational-shape-recognition"></a>**Theorem P.16b.9.5 (Operational Shape Recognition).**

Exact shape recognition is the registration of a typed subdiagram isomorphism together with natural isomorphism of restricted response presheaves. Approximate shape recognition is the same structure with bounded response discrepancy over a retained test family.

*Proof.* By Definition P.16b.9.4, exact shape consists exactly of a typed isomorphism preserving diagram structure and a natural isomorphism of response presheaves. Recognizing exact shape therefore amounts to detecting those data. If exact equality is replaced by a finite test family and discrepancy bound, the same proof gives approximate shape recognition with the stated tolerance. ∎

---

### P.16b.10 Decompression and Creative Transfer

<a id="definition-p16b101-structural-content-and-annotation-content"></a>**Definition P.16b.10.1 (Structural Content and Annotation Content).**

For a model region $A$, the structural content $\operatorname{Str}(A)$ is the set of true statements about $A$ expressible purely in its retained relational, categorical, geometric, and response-presheaf language. Truth is evaluated in the registered structure; expressibility alone does not place a statement in $\operatorname{Str}(A)$.

The annotation content $\operatorname{Ann}(A)$ is the set of non-structural associations accumulated from prior use, including domain interpretations, empirical associations, heuristics, and qualitative expectations.

<a id="definition-p16b102-decompression-along-a-shape-match"></a>**Definition P.16b.10.2 (Decompression Along a Shape Match).**

Given a shape match
$$
\varphi:A\dashrightarrow B,
$$
decompression produces:

1. transported structural consequences $\varphi_*\operatorname{Str}(A)$;
2. transferred hypotheses $\varphi_?\operatorname{Ann}(A)$;
3. tests in $B$ for the transferred hypotheses.

<a id="theorem-p16b103-structural-decompression-is-sound"></a>**Theorem P.16b.10.3 (Structural Decompression Is Sound).**

If
$$
\varphi:A\to B
$$
is an exact shape isomorphism, then every structural statement in $\operatorname{Str}(A)$ transports to a true corresponding structural statement in $\operatorname{Str}(B)$.

*Proof.* A structural statement is written only in the language preserved by the exact shape isomorphism: typed relations, incidence, composition, response-presheaf structure, and retained cost relations. Isomorphisms preserve truth of all statements in the preserved language. Therefore any $\sigma\in\operatorname{Str}(A)$ has a corresponding transported statement $\varphi_*\sigma$ true in $B$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p16b104-annotation-transfer-is-hypothesis-generation"></a>**Theorem P.16b.10.4 (Annotation Transfer Is Hypothesis Generation).**

If
$$
\alpha\in\operatorname{Ann}(A),
$$
then $\varphi_?\alpha$ has hypothesis status in $B$ unless $\alpha$ is independently shown to be structural.

*Proof.* Annotation content may depend on domain-specific facts, empirical history, or contextual interpretation not preserved by shape isomorphism. Therefore shape matching alone does not guarantee its truth in $B$. It can be carried forward only as a testable hypothesis. If it is later proven to depend solely on structure preserved by $\varphi$, it belongs to $\operatorname{Str}(A)$ and Theorem P.16b.10.3 applies. ∎

<a id="definition-p16b105-intuitive-creative-episode"></a>**Definition P.16b.10.5 (Intuitive Creative Episode).**

An intuitive creative episode is a tuple
$$
\mathcal E=(A,B,\varphi,\mathcal O)
$$
where:

1. $A$ is a prior model region;
2. $B$ is a target model region;
3. $\varphi:A\dashrightarrow B$ is an exact or approximate shape match;
4. $\mathcal O=\operatorname{Decomp}_\varphi(A\to B)$ is the decompressed output.

<a id="theorem-p16b106-soundness-of-the-creativity-algorithm"></a>**Theorem P.16b.10.6 (Soundness of the Creativity Algorithm).**

For every intuitive creative episode:

1. exact structural outputs are theorem-level consequences of the shape match;
2. approximate structural outputs require an explicit retained discrepancy metric and a stated stability modulus for the transported statement;
3. annotation outputs are hypotheses requiring testing;
4. any output lacking one of these statuses is not licensed by the algorithm.

*Proof.* Item 1 is Theorem P.16b.10.3. For item 2, an approximate match is not an isomorphism, so truth is not preserved by invariance alone. A quantitative conclusion is licensed only after specifying a discrepancy metric $d$ on the retained test family and a modulus $\omega_\sigma$ for the transported structural statement $\sigma$, so that a match with discrepancy at most $\epsilon$ yields an error bound at most $\omega_\sigma(\epsilon)$. Without $d$ and $\omega_\sigma$, there is no well-defined theorem-level error statement. Item 3 is Theorem P.16b.10.4. Definition P.16b.10.2 lists only transported structural consequences, transferred hypotheses, and tests; hence any output lacking one of these statuses is not licensed by the decompression operation. ∎

<a id="proposition-p16b106a-bare-decompression-admits-zero-novelty-episodes"></a>**Proposition P.16b.10.6a (Bare Decompression Admits Zero-Novelty Episodes).** Shape recognition followed by decompression is not sufficient for genuine new content. Let $A=B$ be the same finite retained model region, let $\varphi=\operatorname{id}_A$, let $\operatorname{Ann}(A)=\varnothing$, and suppose every member of $\operatorname{Str}(A)$ is already retained in $B$. Then $\varphi$ is an exact shape match and Definition P.16b.10.2 executes, but
$$
\operatorname{Decomp}_{\varphi}(A\to B)
\subseteq
\operatorname{Str}(B)
\tag{P.16b.10.6a.1}
$$
adds no content to the target model. A sufficiency claim therefore requires an additional novelty predicate and a proof that the decompressed output lies outside the target's prior retained closure.

*Proof.* The identity preserves every typed relation, response, and cost, so Theorem P.16b.9.5 recognizes the shape and Theorem P.16b.10.3 transports each structural statement to itself. There are no annotations to generate hypotheses. By hypothesis every transported statement is already retained in $B$, proving (P.16b.10.6a.1) and the zero-novelty conclusion. ∎

The following conjecture has the opposite implication direction: it asks whether every genuinely creative output admits a shape-and-decompression representation. Proposition P.16b.10.6a leaves that representation-exhaustiveness direction open.

<a id="conjecture-p16b107-representation-exhaustiveness-for-intuitive-structural-creativity"></a>**Conjecture P.16b.10.7 (Representation Exhaustiveness for Intuitive Structural Creativity).**

Every instance of intuitive structural creativity that produces genuine new content in a predictive model can be represented as shape recognition followed by decompression.

Formally, for every such output $\mathcal O$, there exist model regions $A,B$ and a correspondence $\varphi:A\dashrightarrow B$ such that
$$
\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Decomp}_\varphi(A\to B).
$$

This is a conjecture.

<a id="theorem-p16b107a-exact-match-classification-of-representation-exhaustiveness"></a>**Theorem P.16b.10.7a (Exact-Match Classification of Representation Exhaustiveness).**

Fix a predictive model presentation with a finite set $\mathcal R$ of retained model regions, a target region $B\in\mathcal R$, and write $\operatorname{Ret}(B)$ for the prior retained closure of the target named in Proposition P.16b.10.6a. Call an output $\mathcal O$ *new for $B$* when $\mathcal O\ne\varnothing$ and $\mathcal O\cap\operatorname{Ret}(B)=\varnothing$. Restrict correspondences to exact shape isomorphisms (Definition P.16b.9.4), and call a representation $\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Decomp}_\varphi(A\to B)$ a *transfer representation* when $A\in\mathcal R\setminus\{B\}$. Then:

1. *Identity representation.* Every $\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Str}(B)$ satisfies
$$
\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Decomp}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(B\to B).
$$
The displayed condition of Conjecture P.16b.10.7 therefore holds for every structural output, new for $B$ or not.
2. *Transfer representation.* A nonempty $\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Str}(B)$ has a transfer representation exactly when $\mathcal R\setminus\{B\}$ contains a region with the same exact shape as $B$. For every exact shape isomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, $\varphi_*\operatorname{Str}(A)=\operatorname{Str}(B)$.
3. *Statements outside the structural content.* For $A\in\mathcal R$ and an exact shape isomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, an output satisfies $\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Decomp}_\varphi(A\to B)$ exactly when $\mathcal O\setminus\operatorname{Str}(B)$ is contained in the transferred hypotheses $\varphi_?\operatorname{Ann}(A)$ together with their tests in $B$.
4. *Countermodel.* If $\mathcal R=\{B\}$, $\operatorname{Ann}(B)=\varnothing$ and $\operatorname{Ret}(B)=\varnothing$, and $B$ is a finite typed diagram with $\operatorname{Str}(B)\ne\varnothing$, then every nonempty $\mathcal O\subseteq\operatorname{Str}(B)$ is new for $B$, has the identity representation and has no transfer representation, and no output containing a statement outside $\operatorname{Str}(B)$ has an exact representation.

On the exact-match class, Conjecture P.16b.10.7 in its displayed form is thus satisfied by every structural output through the identity match, its transfer-restricted strengthening holds exactly for targets with a distinct isomorphic prior region, and an output with statements outside $\operatorname{Str}(B)$ is represented through an exact match $\varphi$ exactly when those statements are transferred prior annotations along $\varphi$ or their tests.

*Proof.* For item 1, the identity of $B$ preserves every typed relation, incidence, composition, cost datum and response presheaf, so it is an exact shape isomorphism, and Definition P.16b.10.2 places $\mathrm{id}_{B*}\operatorname{Str}(B)=\operatorname{Str}(B)$ in the decompression. For item 2, Theorem P.16b.10.3 applied to $\varphi$ and to $\varphi^{-1}$ gives $\varphi_*\operatorname{Str}(A)\subseteq\operatorname{Str}(B)$ and $(\varphi^{-1})_*\operatorname{Str}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{Str}(A)$; transport along $\varphi^{-1}$ followed by transport along $\varphi$ is the identity on statements about $B$, so $\varphi_*\operatorname{Str}(A)=\operatorname{Str}(B)$. A transfer representation of a nonempty structural output therefore exists exactly when some $A\ne B$ in $\mathcal R$ admits an exact shape isomorphism onto $B$. For item 3, item 2 gives $\varphi_*\operatorname{Str}(A)=\operatorname{Str}(B)$, so $\operatorname{Decomp}_\varphi(A\to B)$ is the union of $\operatorname{Str}(B)$, the transferred hypotheses $\varphi_?\operatorname{Ann}(A)$ and their tests by Definition P.16b.10.2, and $\mathcal O$ lies in this union exactly when its part outside $\operatorname{Str}(B)$ lies in the last two components. For item 4, $\operatorname{Ret}(B)=\varnothing$ makes every nonempty output new, item 1 supplies the identity representation, $\mathcal R\setminus\{B\}=\varnothing$ excludes transfer by item 2, and $\operatorname{Ann}(B)=\varnothing$ leaves no transferred hypotheses and no tests, so item 3 excludes every statement outside $\operatorname{Str}(B)$. ∎

<a id="theorem-p16b107d-complete-semantic-approximate-transfer-classification"></a>**Theorem P.16b.10.7d (Complete Semantic Approximate-Transfer Classification).**

The following registered source/status, discrepancy, novelty and actual-record interface gives the complete semantic classification, with its numbered lemmas and theorems.

#### 1. Purpose and admission interface

The result below classifies a registered approximate-transfer problem semantically. It does not assert that the truth theory of an arbitrary retained language is decidable. The exact classification of Theorem P.16b.10.7a likewise quantifies over all output sets without a universal decision algorithm. Effective tree, polyhedral and semialgebraic procedures are specializations that compute the semantic invariants, rather than extra requirements imposed on every retained language.

Fix a predictive presentation and a target region $B$ as in P.16b.9.1 and 9.4. Retain its actual typed relations, category, response-presheaf data, costs, source contents and access cut. Let $M$ be the complete set of admitted correspondences from distinct retained prior regions $A_{m}$ to $B$. It is a set, not necessarily finite. A finite region list alone does not imply a finite correspondence list for arbitrary response objects. The identity representation of P.16b.10.7a is kept separate: $M$ is the transfer branch and $A_m\ne B$.

An admitted record consists of the following data, fixed independently of the output query.

1. **Prior and semantics.** The independently registered prior retained closure $R_{B}$ of P.16b.10.7a is preserved as a set of assertions. A nonempty source-independent target comparison prior $P$ and an interpreted truth set $T_{\sigma}$ in $P$ for each retained assertion are also registered. In general $R_{B}$ is not replaced by every semantic truth on $P$. Only on an explicitly registered entailment-prior branch, with $R_B=\{\sigma:P\text{ is contained in }T_\sigma\}$ established for the retained language, may novelty be computed by prior-model counterexamples. Existing target-only retained information must not be omitted from $R_{B}$ merely to make an assertion appear new. The prior and its relationship to $R_{B}$ are fixed independently of the output query.
2. **Source-content lineage.** For each $m$, the retained true structural premises of $A_{m}$ and their typed source-to-target transport are registered. A target assertion may enter the structural candidate catalogue $L_{m}$ only with an identified source premise and transport/weakening template. This includes exact consequences of the preserved relational/category/cost skeleton and quantitative assertions about identified transported response observables. Quantitative templates include the source calibration and statement-specific stability datum of P.16b.10.6. For example, a retained source bound on $F_{A}$ transports to bounds on the corresponding $F_{B}$, with the registered calibration and discrepancy error. The catalogue is fixed before the requested output and does not consist of whichever assertions happen to be true on the chosen target comparison. An independently constrained target fact, with no source-content lineage, is not decompression merely because it is robust.
3. **Statuses.** Uncalibrated annotations and their tests have the separate hypothesis/test statuses of P.16b.10.4. They are not silently included in the theorem-level structural catalogue. A registered Boolean assertion can be treated as a robust truth claim using the erosion criterion below, but its indicator is not automatically assigned a vanishing global modulus. The exact status and the relevant numeric observable or local truth-margin certificate must be supplied.
4. **Coupled comparison.** For each $m$, a set $H_{m}$ of full source/target/calibration/nuisance records is independently registered. Its target projection lies in $P$. Its source coordinates satisfy the admitted source premises, and its fixed categorical, relational, cost and calibration constraints are preserved. Coupled/nonrectangular, nonlinear, nonclosed, noncompact and infinite-dimensional sets are allowed. $H_{m}$ can be empty. It may not be enlarged to a product of its marginal projections. It does not depend on the scalar discrepancy radius $r$ considered below.
5. **Retained discrepancy.** Original-owner applications must supply the explicit registered discrepancy metric on retained test responses required by P.16b.10.6, with its induced pullback pseudometric handled as below; an arbitrary scalar cost is not a substitute for that metric. Each $z\in H_{m}$ has a finite nonnegative discrepancy $D_m(z)$, computed from that metric using the declared retained tests after the typed transport. The abstract cutoff lemma itself remains valid for any finite nonnegative scalar $D$, but that greater generality does not waive the original metric admission. In a standard metric presentation $D_m(z)=d(\pi_A(\mathrm{source}(z)),\pi_B(\mathrm{target}(z)))$, where $d$ is the registered response metric. If observations do not separate full semantic records, this is a pseudometric on those records, and the zero-fiber requirement in Section 4 applies. No change of tests or metric is implicit.
6. **Actual application.** Nonemptiness is class population, not actual membership. Applying a class conclusion to the actual target requires an independent certificate that the actual source/target/calibration record belongs to $H_{m}$ and has $D_{m}$ at most the applied radius. This certificate is not inferred from existence of some comparison record.

The catalogue in item 2 fixes source premises, source-to-target readout/formula identities, and permitted weakening templates; it must not be defined as the assertions whose target conclusions are already certified. Its source-truth and independent stability premises can be checked semantically without assuming robust target truth. The exact comparison geometry below then decides which of those candidate conclusions are robust. A particular restricted proof system may impose an additional radius-dependent license, such as $a\le l-\omega(r)$; in that case its certified radius set must be intersected explicitly with the intervals below. It is not silently a fixed-catalogue premise, and an arbitrary radius-dependent license can destroy the one-interval conclusion. Monotone margin licenses add their corresponding endpoint-aware upper cut.

The catalogue in item 2 is an admission interface, not a proposed universal proof search. It can be specified semantically by the transported source content of P.16b.10.2, or by a complete declared effective calculus in a computational application. An incomplete selected catalogue classifies that selected catalogue and must not be described as all original retained content. This distinction is necessary to avoid using a robustness theorem as an unsupported source-provenance theorem.

Write $K_m(r)=\{z\in H_{m}:D_m(z)\le r\}$, for finite $r\ge 0$. A **licensed robust structural transfer** of a nonempty output $O$ uses one common $m$, has $O$ contained in $L_{m}$ with its admitted statuses and stability data, has $K_m(r)$ nonempty, and makes every member of $O$ true at every target in $K_m(r)$. It is **new** exactly when $O$ intersects $R_{B}$ trivially, the novelty convention of P.16b.10.7a. This retains the distinction between a conjunction listed as one assertion and its conjuncts listed as separate assertions.

##### Maximal semantic source branch and its exact scope

For the original semantic language, take the **full** source-content input $S_m=\operatorname{Str}(A_m)$, not a chosen finite fragment. Let $\tau_{m}$ be the typed syntactic transport of its retained relation, category, cost and response/test symbols along the correspondence. Syntactic transport does not assert that a transported formula is true at $B$. Form a provenance record for each transported source premise, preserving its original premise and status; for quantitative content, retain the identified source/target numerical observable, any stated source bound, the admitted calibration, and the statement-specific error template. Numerical weakening may instantiate a target bound from a source bound and an independently certified error, while exact transported skeleton consequences retain their exact status. The source-free relation “is already true at $B$” is not an operation of this construction.

Define $L_m^{\max}$ as the target formulas/templates in these provenance records before testing target truth, retaining the template parameters and guards. Include every source structural premise and every error/status template admitted by P.16b.10.2 and 10.6; do not discard a template merely because its target truth, stability or robustness later fails. Guards such as $a\le l-\omega(r)$ are explicit conditions on the template's parameters, not a truth oracle. A requested radius-dependent output is instantiated first; Theorem P.16b.10.7d.1 then classifies each fixed requested output, while the guard is intersected separately as stated above.

<a id="lemma-p16b107d0-coverage-of-the-original-source-status-interface"></a>**Lemma P.16b.10.7d.0 (coverage of the original source-status interface).** An output has structural source lineage under the original decompression operation for m exactly when it has one of the provenance records just constructed. A record provides candidate lineage, not automatic theorem-level target truth. Its exact/error status is licensed precisely after the retained-metric and corresponding error requirements of P.16b.10.6, together with any explicit template guards, hold.

**Proof.** By P.16b.10.2, a structural output of decompression comes from transported true retained source structural content. Its source formula therefore belongs to $S_{m}$, and its typed formula/readout transport and any admitted error weakening give one of the records in the full construction. P.16b.10.6 requires exactly the additional metric/error status data, so no originally licensed structural output is discarded. Conversely, a provenance record names a member of $\operatorname{Str}(A_m)$ and its typed transport, rather than a target fact inferred without source lineage. This is a candidate structural output of P.16b.10.2. Exact preserved consequences use P.16b.10.3; response-dependent approximate conclusions must satisfy P.16b.10.6 and their recorded guards. Prior to those tests the record remains a candidate and does not assert the conclusion. These two inclusions establish equality of the source-lineage domains, not an assumption of representation or robust truth. ∎

This is a semantic coverage lemma over the source's existing true content, as in the exact theorem's use of $\operatorname{Str}(A)$. It does not produce missing source truth certificates or decide an arbitrary theory. Using all source content here avoids restricting the general theorem to a selected affine/Boolean syntax. A selected effective proof calculus supplies the same original domain only if its completeness for that domain is proved; otherwise its result remains the stated fragment. Missing source truth or calibration in an actual application remains a failed original premise.

For annotations and tests, register separately $\mathrm{HYP}_m=\tau_{m,?}(\operatorname{Ann}(A_m))$ and $\mathrm{TEST}_m$ as the registered tests for those hypotheses. These are source-identified, status-tagged output catalogues. Their membership is not a claim that the annotation is true. A mixed output is represented via one $m$ exactly when its structural part passes the structural criterion and every hypothesis/test part belongs to the corresponding catalogue. Statuses are metadata and preserve the original assertion identity used for novelty. Merely relabeling a retained assertion as a hypothesis or test does not make it new. If the original registered language already distinguishes status-qualified assertions, use that same pre-existing identity convention consistently in $R_{B}$. Novelty uses that original closure and identity convention. The same common-match quantifier is retained across all parts; a hypothesis cannot silently be reclassified as a structural theorem. If a task has no structural part, class population and the required actual-match admission still apply, but the empty structural part contributes no bad records. The complete output must remain nonempty for novelty.

#### 2. Exact radius normal form, including nonattained boundaries

For any subset S of $H_{m}$ define its distance floor

$$
a(S) = \inf\{D_m(z) : z \in S\}, \quad \text{with } \inf(\emptyset) = +\infty,
$$

and its finite-floor attainment flag

$$
e(S) = \mathrm{true} \text{ iff } a(S) < +\infty \text{ and some } z \in S \text{ has } D_m(z) = a(S).
$$

For an output O define its bad-record set

$$
\mathrm{Bad}_m(O) = \{z \in H_m : \text{some } \sigma \in O \text{ is false at } \mathrm{target}(z)\}.
$$

Put $p_m=a(H_m)$, $u_m=e(H_m)$, $b_m(O)=a(\mathrm{Bad}_m(O))$, and $v_m(O)=e(\mathrm{Bad}_m(O))$. These are geometric invariants of registered source/target records and interpreted truth sets. They do not assert the existence of a representation.

##### Theorem P.16b.10.7d.1: complete interval classification

Suppose O is a fixed nonempty candidate output with source-content lineage for m. Then its populated comparison-robust radii for this match are exactly

$$
I_m(O) = \mathrm{Pop}_m \cap \mathrm{Safe}_m(O),
$$

where, for finite $r\ge 0$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
&r \in \mathrm{Pop}_m \text{ iff } r > p_m, \text{ or } r = p_m \text{ and } u_m = \mathrm{true}; \\
&r \in \mathrm{Safe}_m(O) \text{ iff } r < b_m(O), \text{ or } r = b_m(O) \text{ and } v_m(O) = \mathrm{false}.
\end{aligned}
$$

When $H_{m}$ is empty, $\mathrm{Pop}_m$ is empty. When $\mathrm{Bad}_m(O)$ is empty, $b_m(O)=+\infty$ and $\mathrm{Safe}_m(O)$ is every finite nonnegative radius. Thus $\mathrm{Pop}_m$ is an upper interval with an explicitly open or closed lower endpoint, and $\mathrm{Safe}_m(O)$ is a lower interval with an explicitly open or closed upper endpoint. Their intersection is one possibly empty interval. Restricting a registered radius budget further simply intersects this interval with that budget.

Let $J_m(O)$ be the radius set on which the independently registered source/error/status template guards for this candidate hold. These are the stated source-bound, calibration, numerical-error and status rules, not a predicate that assumes robust target truth. If admission is radius-independent throughout the declared range, $J_{m}$ is that entire range. All new licensed robust transfer radii are exactly

$$
\bigcup_{m \,:\, O \subseteq L_m} [I_m(O) \cap J_m(O)],
$$

provided O intersects $R_{B}$ trivially; otherwise there are no new-output radii. The same m must serve every assertion. If the $J_{m}$ guards are the full radius range or intervals, a finite admitted correspondence census gives a finite union of intervals. More general guard sets remain explicitly intersected and need not preserve that normal form. With an arbitrary set of matches the displayed union is set-indexed; no finite-union or effective-decision claim is made.

For an actual-record certificate $z_{\mathrm{actual},m}\in H_{m}$, the radii at which this particular actual record is covered are obtained by additionally intersecting $I_m(O)\cap J_m(O)$ with $[D_m(z_{\mathrm{actual},m}),+\infty)$. An uncertified actual record cannot be used in this intersection.

###### Proof

For any nonempty $S$, no point has distance below $a(S)$. A point at distance $a(S)$ exists exactly when $e(S)$ is true. At every $r>a(S)$, the defining property of the infimum supplies a point $z\in S$ with $D_m(z)<r$: otherwise $r$ would be a larger lower bound. Applying these facts first to $H_{m}$ gives $\mathrm{Pop}_m$. Applying them to $\mathrm{Bad}_m(O)$ and negating the existence of a bad point at distance at most $r$ gives $\mathrm{Safe}_m(O)$. The empty-set conventions give the stated exceptions.

The target of every point of $K_m(r)$ satisfies every output precisely when there is no member of $\mathrm{Bad}_m(O)$ at distance at most $r$. One common match therefore yields the population/robustness intersection already computed. Its independent source/status guards contribute $J_{m}$, and existentially choosing that common match gives the displayed union. Novelty is evaluated solely in the independently retained closure $R_{B}$; class population and actual-record membership are separate predicates. No compactness, convexity, decidability or attainment premise was used. ∎

##### Exact obstruction and witness branches

For every proposed match and finite radius, a failed classification has a precise cause:

- missing source lineage or missing required status/stability admission;
- no population: $r<p_m$, or $r=p_m$ with unattained population floor, or $H_{m}$ empty;
- an actual bad comparison: $r>b_m(O)$, or $r=b_m(O)$ with attained bad floor;
- or, independently, failure of novelty for some output assertion.

In the bad-comparison branch, the proof supplies existence of a full admitted $z$ with $D_m(z)\le r$ and one false output. At an attained boundary it is a minimizing bad record; above the boundary it follows from the infimum property and need not minimize anything. A computational specialization may compute that witness; this semantic theorem does not pretend that existence is a terminating extraction algorithm for an arbitrary language. Different matches and different assertions may have different counterexamples. No simultaneous bad record is demanded.

If O is infinite, its bad set is the union over all its assertions. Its floor is the infimum over their floors, but its attainment flag must be computed for that union. It cannot be copied from any one assertion. For example, individually attained bad floors 1/n have union floor 0 that is not attained. Robustness then holds at radius 0 and fails at every positive radius, assuming population at 0. The theorem covers this case without a false closed endpoint.

##### Corollary P.16b.10.7d.1a: metric erosion and arbitrary coupled fibers

Assume in this corollary that $D_{m}$ is exactly the displayed metric distance of the source/target response pair. If additional nuisance coordinates change the discrepancy, retain them as part of the source/target record rather than existentially forgetting their effect. On that common response/semantic space, for any target set T and target admission set Q define

$$
E_r^{Q}(T) = \{x : \text{there is no } y \in Q \setminus T \text{ with } d(x,y) \le r\}.
$$

Equivalently this is the complement of the radius-$r$ existential dilation of $Q\setminus T$. If the comparison is rectangular, $H_m=S_m\times P$, robust truth of $\sigma$ holds exactly when $S_{m}$ is contained in $E_r^P(T_\sigma)$, with population still checked separately.

For a coupled comparison, use its actual fiber $Q_{m,s}=\{t:(s,t,\dots)\text{ is admitted}\}$, including the nuisance-coordinate existential quantifier. Robust truth holds exactly when every admitted source $s$ belongs to $E_r^{Q_{m,s}}(T_\sigma)$. This is not permission to replace $Q_{m,s}$ by a common marginal projection. The scalar cutoff in Theorem P.16b.10.7d.1 is the distance from the entire admitted relation to its falsifying part and automatically preserves these fibers.

Proof: expand the existential condition defining the complement; it is precisely an admitted source/target pair within radius r that falsifies the assertion. ∎

##### Radius-dependent records

The interval theorem requires radius-independent $H_{m}$ and metric-ball truncation. An independently radius-dependent or nonnested family of admission constraints must retain its full graph {(r,z): z admitted at r}; it need not produce an interval of valid radii. The set-based classification applies at each registered radius, but no single lower/upper cutoff is asserted. A single already registered comparison at radius r0 can use its fixed nonmetric constraints as $H_{m}$ and be evaluated at r0. A response relation whose substantive constraints genuinely change with r cannot be relabeled as fixed merely to apply this corollary.

#### 3. Numerical thresholds and exact endpoint rules

Suppose a registered source-to-target observable $F$ has been admitted under the stability and lineage interface. At fixed $r$ with $K_m(r)$ nonempty, let

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_m &= \inf\{F(\mathrm{target}(z)) : z \in K_m(r)\}, \\
U_m &= \sup\{F(\mathrm{target}(z)) : z \in K_m(r)\},
\end{aligned}
$$

and record whether each finite extremum is attained. Define $L_0,U_0$ analogously on $P$. Extended values are permitted; real output thresholds are finite.

##### Theorem P.16b.10.7d.2: complete threshold classification

A weak lower assertion $F\ge a$ is robust exactly when $a\le L_m$. A weak upper assertion $F\le b$ is robust exactly when $b\ge U_m$. A strict lower assertion $F>a$ is robust exactly when $a<L_m$, or $a=L_m$ with the infimum unattained. A strict upper assertion $F<b$ is robust exactly when $b>U_m$, or $b=U_m$ with the supremum unattained.

Replace the match subscripts with $0$ to obtain exact prior-model entailment. On the entailment-prior branch $R_B=\{\sigma:P\text{ is contained in }T_\sigma\}$, negating those tests gives novelty, including the strict-boundary cases. For a different registered $R_{B}$, novelty remains literal nonmembership in $R_{B}$ and no general threshold-interval formula for novelty is asserted. On that entailment-prior branch, all individually novel weak lower thresholds lie in $(L_0,L_m]$, and all individually novel weak upper thresholds lie in $[U_m,U_0)$. For any fixed list of such output literals, take the product of its intervals for one common match, then the union over matches; never reverse that order. Finite Boolean formulas retain their actual truth sets and are classified by Theorem P.16b.10.7d.1; independent coordinate extrema alone do not in general decide a disjunction.

Proof: a weak lower bound holds at every point precisely when its threshold is a lower bound of the value set; the greatest lower bound is $L_{m}$. For a strict assertion, equality at the infimum fails exactly if that value is achieved. The upper cases reverse signs. Prior entailment is the same argument on the independent prior. ∎

This theorem computes comparison truth and, on its stated prior branch, novelty. Licensed transfer additionally retains the source-lineage and template-guard conditions; a threshold box alone does not eliminate them. These formulas are not limited to affine scores, polyhedral uncertainty, finite probability alphabets or tabular syntax. The price of that generality is semantic extrema rather than a promise that every such extremum is computable. For effectively specified compact semialgebraic data they become a quantifier-elimination problem; the categorical polyhedral packet computes them by finite rational primal/dual certificates.

#### 4. Exact stability classification and its obstructions

Let $X$ be a nonempty full registered semantic record space relevant to a transported observable $F:X\to\mathbb{R}$. Let $\pi:X\to Y$ be its retained response map into a metric space $(Y,d_Y)$, and put $d_X(x,y)=d_Y(\pi(x),\pi(y))$. The map need not be injective. Define the extended sharp oscillation

$$
\omega_F(r) = \sup\{|F(x) - F(y)| : x, y \in X,\ d_X(x,y) \le r\},
$$

with the supremum at least zero. This is a semantic invariant, not an assumed regularity claim.

##### Theorem P.16b.10.7d.3: universal stability/zero-fiber alternative

1. $\omega_{F}$ is the least nonnegative nondecreasing pointwise error envelope for all compared pairs. Every valid envelope $h$ obeys $h(r)\ge\omega_F(r)$. It is finite on a registered radius range exactly when these oscillations are uniformly bounded there.
2. $\omega_F(r)$ tends to zero as $r$ decreases to zero exactly when $F$ is uniformly continuous for the pseudometric $d_{X}$. Consequently a finite vanishing modulus exists on the registered radius range exactly when this uniform-continuity condition and finite oscillations on that range both hold. Bounded observables automatically satisfy the latter condition.
3. A vanishing modulus forces $F$ to be constant on every zero-distance fiber. If two records have identical retained responses but different $F$ values, their positive difference is a zero-radius obstruction. $F$ then cannot be transported with a vanishing error based only on those retained tests.
4. If zero-fiber constancy holds, $F$ factors uniquely as a function $\bar{F}$ on $\pi(X)$. A vanishing modulus exists exactly when this factored function is uniformly continuous (and its oscillations on the required range are finite). Thus constancy on fibers alone is not sufficient on an arbitrary domain.
5. If $X$ is compact Hausdorff, $\pi$ is continuous into the metric space $Y$ and $F$ is continuous, all oscillation maxima are attained and $\omega_{F}$ is finite. In that case a vanishing modulus exists if and only if $F$ is constant on the fibers of $\pi$. This compact specialization is a sufficient structural setting for deciding the general alternative, not an additional universal gate on P21.

###### Proof

Every pair at distance at most $r$ is bounded by any envelope $h(r)$, so their supremum is bounded by $h(r)$. The supremum itself bounds every such pair and is monotone as the feasible pair sets grow. For item 2, a vanishing $\omega$ implies uniform continuity directly. Conversely, uniform continuity supplies for every $\eta>0$ a $\delta>0$ such that $d_X<\delta$ implies $|F(x)-F(y)|<\eta$. For every $r<\delta$ the corresponding supremum is at most $\eta$, proving its vanishing limit. Finite values on the full registered range are an independent requirement when $F$ is unbounded.

At zero distance the pair remains admissible at every positive radius. Its difference is therefore bounded by a modulus tending to zero, proving item 3. Constancy on fibers gives the unique well-defined factorization $\bar{F}(\pi(x))=F(x)$, and the metric comparisons and value differences in the image are exactly those in $X$, proving item 4.

For item 5, each pair set $\{d_X\le r\}$ is a nonempty closed subset of compact $X\times X$ and the continuous absolute difference attains a finite maximum. The continuous surjection $\pi:X\to\pi(X)$ is a quotient map because its domain is compact and its image is Hausdorff. A fiber-constant continuous $F$ therefore descends to a continuous $\bar{F}$ on compact metric $\pi(X)$; that function is uniformly continuous. Alternatively, decreasing compact pair sets show $\lim_{r\downarrow 0}\omega_F(r)=\omega_F(0)$. At radius zero, $\omega$ is zero exactly when the fiber differences vanish. ∎

##### Explicit negative certificates

Beyond the zero-fiber obstruction, failure of vanishing continuity is certified by an $\eta>0$ and pairs $x_n,y_n$ with $d_X(x_n,y_n)\le 1/n$ but $|F(x_n)-F(y_n)|\ge\eta$. Conversely such a sequence forbids every vanishing modulus. This follows by selecting pairs from failure of uniform continuity, with a harmless fixed reduction in $\eta$ if a supremum is unattained. Failure of finite oscillation at some registered radius is witnessed by pairs with unbounded differences at that radius.

The compact continuity assumptions matter. On $X=(0,1]$ with ordinary distance, the bounded continuous $F(x)=\sin(1/x)$ is fiber-constant but is not uniformly continuous. On compact $X=[0,1]$, $\pi$ the identity and $F=1_{x=0}$, fibers are singletons but discontinuity again prevents a vanishing modulus. These are separate, exact obstruction classes.

##### Boolean truth and local margins

For a truth set T, the indicator's sharp oscillation is either zero or one: it is one exactly when a true and false record lie within radius r. Its global modulus vanishes if and only if the two truth classes have positive metric separation, or one class is empty. At the critical separation radius, the jump occurs exactly if the cross-class distance infimum is attained. Arbitrary Boolean truth therefore does not acquire a vanishing modulus merely because the underlying numerical observables have one.

A particular source or source-comparison class may nevertheless have a positive distance from the falsifying set. Theorem P.16b.10.7d.1 supplies its exact local robustness window, including its endpoint. A locally constant zero-error truth guarantee inside that window is legitimate; a global continuity claim about all Boolean truth is not. For numerical inequalities one can use the registered numerical modulus and a strict margin, or the sharper exact comparison geometry. For example $F(\mathrm{source})\ge a+\omega_F(r)$ suffices for the weak target assertion $F\ge a$. Exact sharp transfer in a coupled comparison may be better than this uniform sufficient bound and is decided by Theorems P.16b.10.7d.1–P.16b.10.7d.2.

##### Calibration and composition
