W(1^e0q)=D_e(q).
\]

The prefixes $1^e0$ are prefix-free, as are the domains of $D_{e}$, so $W$ has prefix-free domain. It simulates $D_{e}$ with the constant overhead $e+1$. This establishes optimal prefix universality. The indexing convention and enumeration are fixed once before selecting semantic examples.

For the normalized $U_*$, the tags 0, 10 and 1100 are prefix-incomparable. Thus its domain remains prefix-free, and

K_{U_*}(y)\le 4+K_W(y).

still hold. The upper bound uses the unchanged literal constructor $100\operatorname{enc}(w_S)$. The finite hierarchy, physical decoder and all operational circuits are unchanged. The short-program census remains valid because it covers lengths at most three.

It validates that all addressed registers exist, all targets/controls are distinct where required, all write targets meet their primitive's initialization contract, and all omitted records remain in the named archive. ### Ideal host, physical primitives, and complete state

For \(N\) addressed payload bits allocate \(n=\max(2,N)\) 75-bit cells, for total cell Hilbert space \((\mathbb C^{2^{75}})^{\otimes n}\). Include any separately listed source, clock or controller registers in \(N\) if they occupy payload bits; if declared as other carriers, list them separately rather than silently omitting them. All cell adaptive cores are retained. The physical carrier count is therefore \(75n\), not \(N\); this includes every cell's own adaptive core, forecasts, ROM and cursor. Factory loading adds exactly \(16n\) X operations for the identical local ROMs. The unexercised cores require no outcome inputs, while each exercised core receives its owned finite environmental input/source records. Computational initial payloads are zero; an initial bit equal to one is written by an X gate and counted once. The incoming seed/guard extension \(E\) is an owned basis-encoded physical record. Its monotone OR-writing/validation circuit belongs to the update schedule; it is not semantic permission magically entering hardware.

The ideal law set supplies exactly the addressed gates

\(\operatorname X:z\mapsto z\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}1\),
\(\operatorname{CNOT}:(a,z)\mapsto(a,z\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}a)\),
\[
\operatorname{Toffoli}:(a,b,z)\mapsto(a,b,z\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}ab)
\]

Each is a permutation on the computational basis and therefore an exact unitary on the finite tensor-product Hilbert space. Circuit composition is exact. On basis inputs, copying uses CNOT into a fresh zero target and retains the source. It is not cloning of an unknown quantum state. Primitive AND uses Toffoli into zero. Primitive NOT-into-fresh uses CNOT then X. OR-into-fresh uses two CNOTs and one Toffoli because \(a\lor b=a\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}b\mathbin{\mathrm{XOR}}ab\).

A finite pulse realization is explicit. Each named gate obeys \(U=U^\dagger=U^{-1}\). For a registered positive gate-actuation duration \(\tau_g\), set
\[
H_U=\frac{\pi\hbar}{2\tau_g}(I-U).
\]
Its eigenvalues are zero and \(\pi\hbar/\tau_g\), so it is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the finite registered gate support, with \(\|H_U\|\le\pi\hbar/\tau_g\), and
\[
\exp(-iH_U\tau_g/\hbar)=U.
\]
This proves the stipulated ideal unitary has a finite driven pulse realization. Endpoint data Hamiltonians are registered as degenerate. The finite drive, input purity and pulse switching remain owned source/controller resources; neither a zero-work claim nor a heat floor follows from this matrix construction.

Basis readouts use the normalized instrument \(\mathcal I_z(\rho)=P_z\rho P_z\), with its classical result copied into a fresh archive. The summed instrument is trace preserving, and on registered basis states it is nondemolition with probability-one correct record. A fair basis coin preparation is explicitly a registered diagonal instrument; its output distribution is intentional, while computational gate/readout error is zero. All conditional single-run states, coin records and forecasts remain distinct from their predictive marginal. Keep one physical perspective \(s_0\), the fixed computational ONB, with normalized identity perspective kernel \(G(s^{\prime}\mid s_0,\ldots)=\mathbf1_{s^{\prime}=s_0}\). These are direct instances of Definition 27's finite instrument rule. No \(\mathfrak C_{act}\), context-triggered actualization, or non-Born claim is made.

The full retained state includes code, input, old and new closure/model versions, every DNF intermediate, proof/trace data, transaction outputs, coins, complete source/controller records and insulated core state. Only an explicitly named response decoder may discard those coordinates mathematically when defining a forecast marginal. Different physical histories are not identified because their marginals coincide.

### Uniform arbitrary bounded-program simulation

Fix a coded deterministic TM \(e\), input-length bound \(r\), and step bound \(T\). A tape segment of length \(h=r+2T+1\) suffices, with the input beginning \(T\) cells from the left boundary. Let \(k\) be its finite state count and \(a\) its alphabet size, each at least two and including a halt state/blank convention. A configuration uses

\[
\ell=\lceil\log_2k\rceil+\lceil\log_2h\rceil+h\lceil\log_2a\rceil
\]

bits: state, head index and tape symbols. Extend the next-step function \(F_e\) to all \(2^\ell\) bitstrings by self-loops on invalid encodings, halted configurations and any transition trying to exit the bounded segment. Such exits cannot occur in the first \(T\) transitions of an admitted input. A directly executed parser reads the finite transition table, current symbol and head, writes the indicated symbol, changes state and moves the head. Thus \(F_e\) is obtained from transition semantics, not from a table of desired answers.

The following uniform algorithm compiles one layer. For every \(\ell\)-bit configuration evaluate that one transition rule. For each output bit \(j\), let \(a_j\) be the number of input configurations on which that bit is one. Generate its disjunctive normal form. First make and retain \(\ell\) complement wires, each using CNOT then X. Each minterm uses one copied literal and \(\ell-1\) fresh-target Toffolis, hence exactly \(\ell\) gates and \(\ell\) fresh wires. Combine its \(a_j\) terms with \(a_j-1\) fresh-target ORs when \(a_j>0\); when \(a_j=0\), allocate one zero output. No old wire is overwritten or freed.

Write \(A=\sum_j a_j\) and \(b=|\{j:a_j>0\}|\). One layer uses exactly

\(G_{\mathrm{layer}}=2\ell+\ell A+3(A-b)\) gates,

\(W_{\mathrm{layer}}=\ell+\ell A+(A-b)+(\ell-b)\) fresh bits.

The formula covers constant-zero outputs. It assumes \(\ell\ge1\), which this encoding guarantees. \(A\le\ell2^\ell\), so both numbers are finite. Append \(T\) independently typed layers, retaining the original and all intermediate configurations. The simulation uses \(TG_{\mathrm{layer}}\) gates and \(\ell+TW_{\mathrm{layer}}\) configuration/workspace bits, plus the explicitly retained program/input metadata and controller. The result is the exact first \(T\) transitions, with halting states held fixed. Induction on layers proves the all-instance claim. Exponential compilation cost is admitted and charged; no efficiency theorem is asserted.

**A fixed programmable receiver for each resource bound.** To make program capability literal on the same receiver, rather than changing its wiring for each nominated program, also register the universal bounded variant. Fix a program-record width \(B\), maximum state/alphabet/tape bounds, and \(T\) before use. Its immutable gate list computes the single total Boolean map \(F(e,c)\) obtained by decoding the retained \(B\)-bit program record \(e\), then performing exactly the transition-table step above on configuration \(c\). Invalid program/state encodings self-loop under the fixed decoder convention; their original program/state records remain available to the finite validity predicate. Valid shorter program records carry their declared length and zero padding. Code bits remain unchanged and are reused as inputs to every layer. This is a direct bounded universal interpreter with input program data; its circuit is generated once from the bounds, not from the final answer or a later semantic example.

For input width \(q=B+\ell\), output width \(\ell\), and minterm counts \(a_j\) now taken over all \(2^q\) program/configuration words, the identical construction gives exact layer counts
\[
G_{\rm univ}=2q+qA+3(A-b),\qquad
W_{\rm univ}=q+qA+(A-b)+(\ell-b).
\]
The initial program record uses \(B\) separately retained bits. The total is \(TG_{\rm univ}\) gates and \(B+\ell+TW_{\rm univ}\) program/configuration/work bits. Since \(A\le\ell2^q\), finite bounds can be allocated before loading \(e\). Taking larger finite \(B,T\) yields the scalable receiver family required by the task. The specialized six-bit circuits actually executed below are efficient finite subprogram witnesses on this same ideal host; the universal variant supplies the stronger fixed-hardware capability analytically. Nothing relies on the four-program test language being universal.

This is a uniform compiler for every program and specified finite bound, as in actual Theorem A.0.1. One fixed finite instance has only its declared capacity. The unbounded family supplies arbitrary finite bounds. The code-generation/initialization work is separately part of the finite source budget. The compiler enumerates \(2^\ell\) configurations, runs one bounded table lookup on each, and writes the listed finite gate and wire records. No oracle or precomputed output table is used.

Finite representations use \(\operatorname{code}(w)=2^{|w|}+\sum_iw_i2^i\); an arithmetically coded tuple records program, input, bound and trace. PA represents the finite one-step relation. A finite output/trace predicate is compiled by the same Boolean construction, or by compiling a terminating TM for it at its declared bound. Logical memory is the retained configuration/scratch array. NAND/AND/OR/NOT and finite composition are supplied by the exact primitive embeddings above. These prove all finite subcapacities used by A.0.1 on this protocol depth, with error zero.

### Diagonal wrapper and actual finite execution

Fix a program \(e\) and its declared simulation bound \(T\). A uniform syntactic constructor \(d(e,T)\) encodes the program: write the word \(d(e,T)\) to its input tape, simulate \(e\) on that word for \(T\) steps, and, if the nominated binary report has appeared, copy and complement it into the wrapper's output; otherwise output a separately retained timeout flag. The constructor is finite: it serializes its fixed template together with \(e,T\); the program reconstructs that same serialization from its embedded parameters. No halting decision or assertion that every predictor answers within \(T\) is made. Compile this finite simulation and the predicate/report test by the preceding construction. A retained Boolean complement costs two gates and one fresh bit; overwriting the report is unnecessary.

For a directly executable nonvacuity check, use the four-program finite sublanguage with two-bit opcodes COPY, NOT, ZERO, ONE. Each reads its first input bit, writes respectively that bit, its complement, zero, or one, then halts after moving right. The ordinary code is `0||e`; its diagonal-wrapper code is `1||e`. The three code bits are loaded as the actual tape input. The wrapper executes the nominated predictor on that exact wrapper code for two padded transitions and retains the report and its complement. These are internal simulated-program DATA codes, not the original physical-constructor codes of \(U_*\): the internal word `111`, for example, need not be an admissible constructor program. Both type conventions are fixed before semantic examples. The small witness language is only a tested subclass; the previous uniform proof supplies arbitrary bounded programs.

The checker below compiles the actual total next-configuration function on six bits (halt, two head bits, three tape bits). It enumerates all 64 configurations for each of the four programs, applies the reversible primitive schedule, checks the exact successor and unchanged input, executes the two-layer traces, and checks the self-code wrapper. In addition, it constructs one immutable eight-input/six-output circuit for the combined map \(F(e,c)\), with two variable opcode bits and six configuration bits, and executes that same circuit on all 256 inputs. It verifies the successor and retention of both program and old configuration, without recompiling between opcodes. That single variable-program circuit has exactly 9,502 gates, 7,778 fresh bits and 7,786 total bits, with output minterm counts \((192,128,160,128,128,128)\). Its trace verification is exact Boolean arithmetic, and its calibration is exact rational arithmetic.

Actual output is in the verification appendix. The largest specialized diagonal-wrapper payload computation has 4,022 gates and 3,143 configuration/workspace bits, plus two retained opcode bits. Its output complement and all stage records are included in those counts. This excludes only separately itemized input-loading, source, full controller and insulated-core overhead; those are added by the ledger below. Thus a numerical demonstration is not misreported as the total physical device.

### Time, memory, initialization and source ownership ledger

Let the assembled payload schedule contain \(G_X,G_C,G_T\) X/CNOT/Toffoli gates, \(G=G_X+G_C+G_T\); include input loading, semantic closure compiler, program simulation, proof/probe processing and diagonal complement in these totals. Let \(N_{data}\) count all live and retained payload bits, including the complete input/program records, every scratch/old buffer, coins and outputs, with separate flags for their initial states. No variable is reclaimed merely because a later decoder does not use it. Its insulated-core/controller overhead is \(74\max(2,N_{data}+N_{\mathrm{control}})\) when global controls are represented in payload cells.

The selected implementation is a driven serial schedule with fully counted clock changes. For a data-gate list of length \(G\), allocate \(G+1\) one-hot clock bits, prepare \(c_0=1\) with one X, and after each data gate \(j\) apply X to \(c_j\) and then X to \(c_{j+1}\). This is exactly \(2G\) clock X gates, leaving \(c_G=1\). Every update is an invertible X; no clock record is erased. The complete execution schedule therefore has \(3G\) primitive slots and duration \(3G\tau\), with the one initial clock-preparation X and all other preparation slots listed separately. \(G\tau\) is only the data-path duration, not the reported complete run time. Here \(\tau=\tau_{\mathrm{read}}+\tau_g>0\) is the complete addressed slot, including its finite instruction-delivery interval and gate actuation; choose positive \(\tau_{\mathrm{read}},\tau_g\). Delivery events are separately counted resource occurrences within these slots, not additional uncounted sequential delays. These durations are registered branch data, not energy-derived speed limits.

The finite owned ROM stores this complete \(3G\)-instruction driven sequence. With \(B\) data bits and \(G+1\) clock bits its padded address width is \(a=\lceil\log_2(B+G+1)\rceil\), and the ROM uses exactly \(3G(2+3a)\) bits under the two-bit-opcode/three-address convention. The ROM is immutable. Its read-and-drive source supplies exactly \(3G\) registered finite instruction-delivery events; these are explicit controller/source operations, distinct from the gate tally. The clock is the only mutable indexing record and its physical X gates are included above. The schedule is driven, not an asserted autonomous perpetual controller. ROM loading costs exactly its Hamming weight in X writes; source preparation/maintenance and instruction-delivery slots are part of the owned finite controller resource vector.

All clock/source states and old source records are retained. A driver that uses further mutable memory must add that memory and its specified update operations; this witness uses the fixed finite sequence source just defined. Definition 27 permits this registered finite control instrument without a claim about an unmanufactured lower-level controller design.

Resource cost is the finite vector of initialized cells, classical program/controller bits, owned coin/source records, primitive counts, retained bit-time, and duration. The code-generation algorithm also has finite recorded input, output and transition count, and can itself be compiled through the same bounded simulation once its terminating trace length is fixed. This does not require any computation to occur for free or use an infinite precision real. It is not a claim of optimal resource consumption, zero work, or zero heat. The complete retained-register branch uses no irreversible scratch reset and invokes neither Definition 28 nor Theorem 31.

### A complete common finite bound for the assembled two-epoch receiver

The following conservative bound is deliberately larger than the exact subcircuit counts, to include every operational subsystem rather than silently dropping output or state-observation work. Let

\[
n=|P|,\quad m=|V|,\quad k=nm,\quad d=k^2,\quad N=nd,\quad G_{\rm guard}=n^3,
\]

and let the closure certificate have fixed selector width \(J=3+k+nk\). Thus its proof-table size is always \(B_\Pi=N^2(J+1)\). Put \(B_{\rm copy}=N+G_{\rm guard}+B_\Pi\). This is the number of bits/CNOTs needed for each external appliance's separate raw-configuration and proof copy.

Let \(H_c,W_c\) be the certified compiler's gate count and complete wire count, and \(H_v,W_v\) the independent simultaneous-root validator's gate count and fresh-workspace count. Their actual formulas from the closure component are

\[
H_c=N^2(12+7k+8nk),\qquad W_c=2N+G_{\rm guard}+2+N^2(6+4k+5nk),
\]
\[
H_v=N^2(47+14k+15nk)+d-1,\qquad W_v=N^2(22+7k+8nk)+d-1.
\]

For one epoch the operational program can use two full independent validators, one local and one external, even though each appliance needs only its assigned coordinates. Per coordinate it allocates both fair source bits and retained coin outcomes, rejection/decision bits, the two-bit rational forecast plus its journal copy, an input payload of width \(w\ge1\), selected/committed payload, acknowledgement, the full external report copy, current-state estimate, the observation-update copy, and the four-bit Brier numerator. The specified primitive counts are at most: two gates for forecast encoding, one for any extra root conjunction, three for noise/decision, \(w+1\) for payload/ack, \(w+1\) for state-estimate copying, \(w+1\) for full external report copying, and three for the Brier score. Separate journal/epoch/status copies and the observation-update copy fit within the deliberately loose allowance of \(64(w+1)\) gates and fresh/input bits per coordinate. Constants, two fair preparations and their records also fit that wire allowance. Retained raw configurations and old versions are charged separately below.

Thus two complete pre/post epochs, one physical monotone OR event, the capability program, and one local adaptive calibration execution are covered by

\[
H_{\rm data}\le 2H_c+3(N+G_{\rm guard})+4H_v+2B_{\rm copy}
+128d(w+1)+H_{\rm cap}+12,
\]
\[
B_{\rm data}\le 2W_c+3(N+G_{\rm guard})+4(W_v+2)+2B_{\rm copy}
+128d(w+1)+B_{\rm cap}+B_{\rm program}+32.
\]

Here \(H_{\rm cap},B_{\rm cap}\) are the exact capability simulation counts; \(B_{\rm program}\) contains its retained code/parameters. The 32-bit reserve includes the finite calibration source/outcomes and epoch flags. Any additional scored probe repetition receives another separately allocated epoch term. These are upper bounds, not equalities: \(W_c\) already contains its configuration input, so the displayed bound intentionally double-allocates some source banks. A more economical exact alias-aware count is permissible but unnecessary. All proof references alias the compiler's retained certificate; the extra copy is only for the physically external appliance.

For a completely specified implementation, concatenate the finite subprograms and their explicit interface-copy/score instructions, then read \(H_{\rm actual}\) and \(B_{\rm actual}\) off the resulting list. The inequalities prove in advance that this list and its complete memory fit a finite bound for all family sizes. Include the seed/guard input mask in the \(3(N+G_{\rm guard})\) bank allowance; retain the old configuration, new configuration and mask. Keep external apparatus outside the boundary of S for self/external semantics, but include its separate memory, source and operations in this common experiment ledger.

Global controller ROM and one-hot clock use the exact \(3H_{\rm actual}\)-slot construction above: \(H_{\rm actual}+1\) clock bits and \(3H_{\rm actual}(2+3\lceil\log_2(B_{\rm actual}+H_{\rm actual}+1)\rceil)\) ROM bits. Allocate one payload cell per needed data/control bit in its declared location. At most four additional padding cells suffice to enforce a minimum of two cells on each of S and the external appliance. The entire experiment therefore has the finite cell-carrier upper bound \(75(B_{\rm actual}+B_{\rm control}+4)\), plus any separately declared source carriers. Each cell has its own fully counted adaptive core/controller. Input loading costs exactly the Hamming weight of the ready basis-input/ROM bitstring in X gates; global/local ROM loading, coin preparations and their finite drive sources are explicitly preparation costs. Runtime is the sum of the stated gate slots, diagonal-instrument slots and controller slots at their registered finite durations. No gate count is substituted for a thermodynamic energy unit.

### Physical-pattern scope of Definition 1

The seed/guard event is a finite basis-encoded physical input, read through its registered finite update instrument and code. The complete compiler proves that it is processable within the allocated resource bound. For a pattern that changes at least one scored Bernoulli transaction coordinate from the pre-event forecast \(1/4\) to the true post-event forecast \(3/4\), Brier excess risk of the old forecast is \((3/4-1/4)^2=1/4\) per changed coordinate; exact updated forecasting therefore gives strictly positive event-conditional quality gain. Normalize by the number of scored coordinates when using mean Brier loss. This validates Definition 1's functional criterion on nonzero registered examples with positive event probability, because the transaction mechanism is the independently fixed operational probe constructed in P.16b.12.4j. Closure-idempotent events need not be information-bearing; no false claim of positive gain for every input is made.

All capability results are on the declared ideal finite formal physical branch. Error zero is exact in its laws. Noisy manufacture, arbitrary cross-perspective physical equivalence and sustained operation without renewed workspace remain outside this certificate's scope rather than hidden premises of its finite realization.

## P.16b.12.4i Uniform proof closure compiler and independent verifier

### Scope and inherited facts

This component supplies an actual finite, reversible, retained-scratch implementation of the semantic closure and its proof-carrying readout. It does not independently assert Effective Operational Property R or that a selected coordinate is physically self-referential; those receiver/model obligations are supplied by P.16b.12.4h and P.16b.12.4j. The semantic correctness being implemented is that of Definitions P.16b.2.1–P.16b.2.3 and P.16b.2.6, Theorems P.16b.2.4 and P.16b.2.7, and Corollary P.16b.2.5. Firewall invariance and the linear factorization classification remain exactly Theorems P.16b.12.4d and P.16b.12.4g. In particular, no guard bit is itself a physical record-sharing certificate.

Let nonempty finite perspective and value sets be enumerated as $P=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and $V=\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$; set $k=nm,\ d=k^2,\ N=nd=n^3m^2,\ G=n^3,\ J=3+k+nk$. A labeled vertex $i=(s,a)$ has integer code $sm+a$. Relation entry $(r,i,j)$, with $i=(s,a)$, $j=(u,c)$, has index $rd+ik+j$; this is the manuscript tuple $(s,u,a,c)$ in evaluator $r$. A raw configuration $C$ consists of exactly $N$ seed bits $B$ and $G$ guard bits $g$, with $g(r,q,u)$ in lexicographic order. The nominated perspective $p$ is fixed before examples. All $2^{N+G}$ configurations, and all bitwise-monotone extensions of them, are admitted. There is no dependence of this registration on a desired firewall example.

### Proposition P.16b.12.4i.1: the exact synchronous iteration and its stopping bound

Write $T_C$ for the source operator and define the implemented operator

$$
F_C(X)=X\cup T_C(X),\qquad X_0=0,\qquad X_{h+1}=F_C(X_h).
$$

Every rule in a round reads only $X_h$. Old and new are separately typed banks. A completed new bank becomes the read-only old view for the next round; preceding banks and their scratch are retained and never overwritten. In particular, an in-place rule scan is not being equated to a synchronous round.

$F_C$ is monotone and inflationary. Its chain has at most $N$ strict increases, since there are $N$ possible evaluator/tuple entries. If a step is not strict, that state is fixed. Otherwise $N$ strict steps have filled every possible entry, which is also fixed. Thus $X_N=X_{N+1}$. For completeness, this implementation also agrees stage by stage with the bottom-started Kleene iteration of $T_C$: monotonicity gives $T_C^h(0)\subseteq T_C^{h+1}(0)$, and induction therefore gives $F_C^h(0)=T_C^h(0)$. Consequently $X_N=R^\star(C)$. Alternatively, $X_N$ is $T_C$-prefixed, the entire $F$-chain lies below $R^\star(C)$, and leastness of $R^\star(C)$ gives the opposite inclusion. Both arguments apply to every $n,m$ and every $C$.

$N$ rounds are a uniform safe bound, not an assertion that every input needs $N$ rounds. The protocol executes exactly $N$ even when convergence occurs earlier; its duration is input independent. A closure stage is not a physical time unit.

### Proposition P.16b.12.4i.2: uniform gate generator and exact size

For a fixed output node $(h+1,r,i,j)$, the generator creates candidates in the following fixed priority order:

1. COPY: $X_h(r,i,j)$.
2. BASE: $B(r,i,j)$.
3. REFL: the constant $\mathbf1_{\{i=j\}}$.
4. TRANS, one for each $t\in\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$: $X_h(r,i,t)\wedge X_h(r,t,j)$.
5. CPA, in lexicographic $(q,t)$ order: $X_h(r,i,t)\wedge X_h(q,t,j)\wedge g(r,q,\lfloor j/m\rfloor)$.

There are $J$ candidates. TRANS uses $k$ binary ANDs; CPA uses $2nk$ binary ANDs. A left-associated OR of all candidates produces the new relation bit, with $J-1$ OR gates. The bare Boolean circuit therefore has exactly

$$
N^2(2+2k+3nk)
$$

binary gates. The order of all gate operations is fixed: increasing stage, evaluator, source vertex, target vertex, then the displayed candidate order and left-associated OR order. Its description is produced by these bounded nested loops for arbitrary finite $n,m$; a table of outputs for input configurations is never supplied.

For physical basis-state execution, allocate each intermediate destination freshly as $\lvert0\rangle$. Implement $\operatorname{AND}(a,b)$ by $\operatorname{Toffoli}(a,b,\mathrm{target})$, $\operatorname{OR}(a,b)$ by $\operatorname{CNOT}(a,\mathrm{target})$, $\operatorname{CNOT}(b,\mathrm{target})$, $\operatorname{Toffoli}(a,b,\mathrm{target})$, $\operatorname{NOT}(a)$ by $X(\mathrm{target})$, $\operatorname{CNOT}(a,\mathrm{target})$, and $\operatorname{XOR}(a,b)$ by two CNOTs. Every operation is a unitary permutation of a finite computational basis. If two AND controls name the same wire, replace that Toffoli by a single CNOT. This avoids an illegal repeated-control gate without changing the count. In the OR construction coincident controls give three CNOTs, also correct. No gate target aliases a source wire.

The bare retained-scratch circuit has $H_{\mathrm{bare}}=N^2(6+4k+5nk)$ elementary gates and $W_{\mathrm{bare}}=2N+G+2+N^2(2+2k+3nk)$ bits, including raw configuration, $N$ initially-zero old bits and supplied $\lvert0\rangle,\lvert1\rangle$ constants. A $\lvert1\rangle$ resource is explicit here; if instead obtained from a supplied $\lvert0\rangle$, add one X gate. Basis preparation, transfer of input records, a timing controller and the rest of the receiver are not silently counted as zero-size parts of $W_{\mathrm{bare}}$.

### Proposition P.16b.12.4i.3: canonical bounded proof provenance

The actual receiver uses the following certified version, rather than merely the bare closure circuit. At each node, let $c_0,\ldots,c_{J-1}$ be its candidate bits and let $v_j=c_0\vee\cdots\vee c_j$. Retain the first-true selector bits

$$
s_0=c_0,\qquad s_j=c_j\wedge\neg v_{j-1}\quad(j\ge1).
$$

The same prefix values already occur in the closure's OR chain. For each $j\ge1$, the selector adds one NOT and one AND: exactly three elementary gates and two fresh bits. $s_0$ aliases its already retained candidate. The node presence bit is $v_{J-1}$. A present node has exactly one selector; an absent node has none.

The certificate has $N^2$ potential nodes $(h,r,i,j),\ 1\le h\le N$, each read out as presence plus $J$ selectors. Rule tags, tuple labels, premise addresses and guard addresses are fixed by their stage/node/slot positions; they are not externally supplied truth tables. All premises have stage $h-1$. The $h=0$ table is identically zero. COPY refers to the same preceding tuple, BASE to the raw seed bit, REFL to $i=j$, TRANS to its two preceding same-evaluator nodes, and CPA to its two preceding nodes and the nominated raw guard bit. A COPY chain can be deleted to obtain a proof solely in the source's Base/Refl/Trans/CPA rules. These are bounded DAG certificates, not necessarily exponentially expanded proof trees: there are at most $N^2$ occupied nodes and dependency depth at most $N$.

For any $C$, first-true selection is deterministic, so the complete basis-state transcript and certificate $\Pi(C)$ are canonical for the registered schedule and fresh ancillas. An induction over $h$ proves soundness of every present node. Conversely, the presence bits are the closure iteration already proved complete, so every member of $R^\star(C)$ has a present final node and a finite source proof. This is a computational realization of the accepted soundness/completeness theorem.

The exact certified counts are

$$
\begin{aligned} H_{\mathrm{cert}}&=N^2(12+7k+8nk),\\ W_{\mathrm{cert}}&=2N+G+2+N^2(6+4k+5nk).\end{aligned}
$$

The derivation per node is $a=k+2nk$ AND candidates, $3(J-1)$ OR elementary gates, and $3(J-1)$ selector elementary gates. Fresh bits per node are $a+(J-1)+2(J-1)=6+4k+5nk$. These totals retain every intermediate bit, including every earlier old/new stage. Certificate fields are read-only views into those wires; merely naming the fields does not allocate a duplicate physical certificate.

### Proposition P.16b.12.4i.4: an independent sound physical proof verifier

The verifier receives $C$ and a candidate certificate with the fixed node layout. For each node it computes rule availability from $C$ and the presence bits at the preceding stage, using the same *local source rules*, not a stored correct answer. Let $\mathrm{seen}=\mathrm{bad}=0$ at the start of the node. For each supplied selector $s$ and associated availability $a$, it performs

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathrm{conflict}&=\mathrm{seen}\wedge s,\\ \mathrm{bad}&\leftarrow\mathrm{bad}\vee\mathrm{conflict},\\ \mathrm{seen}&\leftarrow\mathrm{seen}\vee s,\\ \mathrm{bad}&\leftarrow\mathrm{bad}\vee(s\wedge\neg a).\end{aligned}
$$

At node end it sets $\mathrm{bad}\leftarrow\mathrm{bad}\vee(\mathrm{presence}\oplus\mathrm{seen})$, and $\mathrm{valid}_{\mathrm{node}}=\neg\mathrm{bad}$. Let $\mathrm{Valid}$ be the AND of all $\mathrm{valid}_{\mathrm{node}}$ bits. The nominated verified judgment bit is

$$
K_{r,x}=\mathrm{Valid}\wedge\mathrm{presence}_{N,r,x}.
$$

If $K_{r,x}=1$, the table has exactly one available justification for each present node, so induction in stage yields a valid source proof for the root. Unsupported REFL, unavailable premises/guards, contradictory one-hot selectors and malformed claimed presence are rejected. A completely absent proof returns $K=0$, even if the statement could be proved by a different certificate. The verifier is a proof validator, not an oracle for nonderivability.

On the registered compiler-produced certificate $\Pi(C)$, $\mathrm{Valid}=1$ and

$$
K_{r,x}(C,\Pi(C))=\mathbf1_{\{x\in R_r^\star(C)\}}
$$

for every $C$, $r$ and $x$. This is the all-instance verifier/closure interface consumed by the actual operational plant. The fact that incomplete arbitrary certificates may return zero does not weaken this identity on the admitted compiler branch.

For a single root, the reversible retained-scratch verifier has exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}H_{\mathrm{ver}}&=N^2(47+14k+15nk),\\ W_{\mathrm{ver,fresh}}&=N^2(22+7k+8nk).\end{aligned}
$$

gates and fresh bits, in addition to its input references and the two constant wires. Indeed, each node uses $a=k+2nk$ candidate gates/bits, 13 elementary gates and six fresh bits per selector, then seven gates/three bits for the final XOR, OR and NOT. The global validity AND uses $N^2-1$ gates, and the root AND uses one. For simultaneous $d=k^2$ roots of the nominated evaluator, share $\mathrm{Valid}$ and add $d-1$ elementary AND gates and $d-1$ fresh bits to these single-root totals. The code also compiles this independent verifier gate by gate and exhaustively executes it on the two smallest registered finite families.

### Proposition P.16b.12.4i.5: actual update channel and the semantic commuting square

Encode a monotone physical event $E$ by a basis record of $N+G$ additional seed/permission bits $e$. With the old $C$ retained, produce a fresh $C'=C\vee e$ bank using $N+G$ independent reversible OR constructions. This costs exactly $3(N+G)$ elementary gates and $N+G$ fresh output bits. The event record $e$ is an owned input resource, not a discarded catalyst. It may include ones already present in $C$. Every finite monotone extension is represented this way, for example by $e=C'\setminus C$.

Apply the certified compiler to $C'$ with fresh retained workspace. Keep the old configuration, event, old transcript/model and all new workspace. Let $U_E$ denote this finite composed basis-state channel. Let $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{rel}}$ and $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{proof}}$ read the new closure bank and its canonical proof view. Then, for every admitted $C$ and $E$,

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{rel}}\bigl(U_E(\operatorname{Enc}(C))\bigr)&=R^\star(C\vee e),\\ \operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{proof}}\bigl(U_E(\operatorname{Enc}(C))\bigr)&=\Pi(C\vee e),\\ K_{r,x}\bigl(C\vee e,\Pi(C\vee e)\bigr)&=\mathbf1_{\{x\in R_r^\star(C\vee e)\}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\operatorname{Enc}(C)$ includes the canonical pre-event compiled configuration, for which $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{rel}}=R^\star(C)$. The identities follow first from the bitwise OR channel and then from Propositions C1–C4. This proves a response-faithful semantic computation on the whole finite class. It asserts equality of decoded readouts, not equality of complete physical microstates before and after an event; all additional histories and workspaces remain distinct retained records. It supplies exactly the closure/provenance side of the full model-realization square. When the operational instrument derives its model readout as $\theta_x=\tfrac14+\tfrac12 K_{p,x}$, that instrument's proof immediately yields $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{model}}\bigl(U_E\operatorname{Enc}(C)\bigr)=\theta\bigl(R^\star(C\vee e)\bigr)$.

CPA indices here are registers/evaluator labels inside the single declared receiver. No statement that they are independently actualized physical perspectives is needed or made by this compiler. A separate physical cross-perspective interpretation would require the proposition-specific certificates of M.6.2 and is not supplied merely by $g(r,q,u)=1$.

### Timing, control and retained resources

Choose a positive duration $\tau$ for each registered ideal X, CNOT and Toffoli primitive, and execute the explicit gate list serially. The closure data path takes exactly $H_{\mathrm{cert}}\tau$; OR-updating and recompiling takes $[3(N+G)+H_{\mathrm{cert}}]\tau$ before subsequent model/verifier/probe operations. These are registered logical-protocol clock statements, not physical speed limits. Every stage costs $N(12+7k+8nk)$ such ticks; the number $N$ of closure stages was not substituted for elapsed time.

A literal finite control registration is available if desired: store the gate list in read-only control memory, requiring at most $H\bigl(2+3\lceil\log_2 W\rceil\bigr)$ bits for $H$ instructions and $W$ data wires, plus a program-counter range $\{0,\ldots,H\}$. The gate-list executor/clock is part of the hosting receiver's bounded interpreter/control account. The listed $H,W$ counts describe the compiled data path and are not a claim that the control hardware has no cost. Alternatively, augment a completely scheduled finite circuit with a one-hot history clock of $H+1$ supplied basis bits, initially $h_0=1$ and every other clock bit zero. After logical gate $j$, apply X to $h_j$ and $h_{j+1}$. The resulting fully explicit augmented list has $3H$ elementary pulses, $H+1$ extra clock bits, duration $3H\tau$, and its clock marks the completed gate at every macro-boundary. The scheduler is fixed by that finite list. The receiver may use either declared convention, but must not mix their time totals.

No scratch is erased, no retained history is identified with a marginal forecast, and no heat/reset bound is asserted. For a fixed finite number of authorized events, allocate this finite input/ancilla/clock budget per event in advance; indefinite reuse without reset is not claimed.

### Exact nonvacuity and falsification examples

Fix $P=\{p,t,u\}$, $V=\{a,b,c\}$, all distinct as displayed, and nominate evaluator $p$. Let $x=(p,u,a,c)$ and $y=(t,u,b,c)$. In all examples the standard physical predictive decoder is $\theta_z=\tfrac14+\tfrac12\mathbf1_{\{z\in R_p^\star\}}$, and the Fisher norm is evaluated at the *pre-event* model. Every newly inserted nonreflexive coordinate then has pre-event probability $1/4$ and Fisher weight $16/3$.

**Protected external change.** Start with every seed and guard zero. Every component closure is the identity relation on the $k=9$ labeled vertices. Adjoin only $y$ to $B_p$. The $p$-closure adds exactly $y$; all other components are unchanged. The explicit firewall is $I_p=\{y\},\ I_r=\varnothing\ (r\ne p)$. The candidate $R^\star\cup I$ is closed: $y$ composes only with its endpoint identities, since $(t,b)\ne(u,c)$, and no guards are enabled. Thus $T'(R^\star\cup I)=R^\star\cup I$ and $I_p\cap Q_p=\varnothing$. The actual model increment is $\tfrac12 e_y$, with nonzero external squared norm $4/3$, zero self increment and $\sigma=0$. This is not a vacuous zero-total-update example.

**Required guard-only leakage.** Initially $B_p=\{(p,t,a,b)\},\ B_t=\{(t,u,b,c)\}$, with all other seeds and all guards zero. Enable only $g(p,t,u)=1$. The $p$-closure gains exactly $x$ and $y$: $x$ follows by CPA from the two given seeds, and $y$ follows by CPA from the $p$-evaluator identity $(t,t,b,b)$ and the $t$-evaluator seed. The proposed final relation, identities plus $(p,t,a,b),x,y$ in $p$, identities plus the original seed in $t$, and identities in $u$, is closed. The only new nonidentity composition in $p$ is $(p,t,a,b)\circ y=x$; the sole enabled guard has no other nonidentity imported premise. Therefore no omitted tuple can appear. Only $x$ is self-indexed. The actual increment is $\tfrac12(e_x+e_y)$, with self squared norm $4/3$, total squared norm $8/3$, and $\sigma^2=\tfrac12$, hence $\sigma=1/\sqrt2$. This preserves both new tuples required by P.16b.12.4g, rather than reporting only the self leak.

**Different faulty coupling.** Keep the same valid semantic compiler and protected extension, but change the *physical predictive coupling* to

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta_{\mathrm{bad}}(R)&=\tfrac14\mathbf1+\tfrac12b+\tfrac18 b_y e_x,\\ L_{\mathrm{bad}}&=\tfrac12 I+\tfrac18 e_xe_y^{\mathsf T}.\end{aligned}
$$

where $b=\mathbf1_{R_p}$. Every coordinate stays strictly between zero and one on all configurations: the $x$ coordinate lies in $\{1/4,3/8,3/4,7/8\}$. It is finitely realizable, for example by three fair bits at $x$ and threshold count $2+4b_x+b_y$ of eight outcomes. Thus this is a genuine alternative coupling, not a formally impossible tangent perturbation. The protected seed insertion $y$ leaves semantic self sectors equal but yields $\Delta\theta_{\mathrm{bad}}=\tfrac12e_y+\tfrac18e_x$. At the initial model, squared self norm is $1/12$, total squared norm is $17/12$ and $\sigma^2=\tfrac1{17}$. Since $\operatorname{pr}_{\mathrm{self}}L_{\mathrm{bad}}e_y=\tfrac18e_x\ne0$, the accepted factorization criterion fails exactly as it should. This is not a counterexample to the theorem when its zero-column premise holds.

## P.16b.12.4j Operational self model and response faithful instrument

### Result and precise scope

This construction supplies the missing semantic-to-operational bridge on an explicit ideal finite logical receiver family. It is an operational implementation, rather than a conditional assertion that some unspecified physical bridge would suffice. Its ideal physical premises are exact finite computational-basis Boolean gates, ready finite registers, independently prepared specified diagonal ancillas, and the finite Hilbert/Born instrument convention. The host capability and original-complexity registration are supplied by P.16b.12.4h on this **same** family. No noisy unprotected MPU, universal physical exhaustiveness, global complexity minimum, SPAP-proximity bound, heat floor, reset cycle, or cross-perspective equivalence is asserted here.

The self-model has a declared operational scope: the receiver's own validation-controlled transaction service, its local transaction states, their predicted outcomes, their accuracy, and their finite transition law. It also forecasts a physically separate external transaction appliance. It is not a complete predictor of every compiler, audit, forecast-memory, or random-source microstate. Such states remain explicit and retained. Equality of the nominated prospective transaction response does not identify complete physical states. This is the same kind of scope restriction used whenever an internal operational model represents selected system states and dynamics; it does not stipulate that a complete controller state is unchanged under a firewall.

All evaluator labels are semantic namespaces inside one classical proof processor. The distinguished endpoint label $p$ is wired to its local transaction service. Other endpoint labels name a separate external test appliance's endpoint ports. These labels are not declared to be distinct Appendix-M physical perspectives. The common computational basis and common physical registration context are fixed before configurations and examples are chosen.

### 1. Frozen architecture and variable inputs

Fix finite nonempty sets $P,V$, a nominated $p\in P,\qquad D=P\times P\times V\times V,\qquad d=|D|$, and a finite event/probe horizon. Choose a fixed order of each finite set. A tuple $x=(s,u,a,c)$ is a request to execute a sandbox transaction taking a record with type $(s,a)$ to a record with type $(u,c)$. The architecture contains these disjoint physical subsystems:

1. **Receiver S:** seed/guard input archive, synchronous proof compiler, complete retained compiler workspace, independent proof verifier, predictive-model registers, a controller, an accuracy ledger, and its own local transaction source/destination/acknowledgment registers.
2. **External appliance W:** a physically disjoint set of transaction source/destination/acknowledgment registers, a copy of the proof-validation circuit, and ready report registers. W has no authority to change S's local transaction latches. It can transmit its retained basis report through the registered copying circuit below.
3. **Owned inputs and sources:** ready basis registers, the finitely many event cards, and two independent fresh fair classical bits per transaction per probe. These belong to the finite execution ledger. They are not free repeatedly reusable supplies.

The routing map is physically frozen as follows:

- If $u=p$, the transaction writes a fresh local destination/import register of S on the accepted branch.
- If $s=p\quad\text{and}\quad u\ne p$, it reads a prepared local source card and writes S's outgoing-commit register and an outgoing payload card on the accepted branch.
- If both endpoints equal $p$, the local loopback path is used.
- If neither endpoint equals $p$, W performs the transaction between its external endpoint cards and S receives only W's retained report.

Thus $x\in Q_p$ if and only if the targeted transaction has a local endpoint and its nominated actuation/commit feature is in S's own service. For $x\notin Q_p$, the targeted actuation feature is in W, outside S. This is an operational, independently fixed incidence test: replacing the model's names does not move the gates or registers. In particular, merely storing a forecast of W's state inside S does not make W's transaction an event of S's own service.

Each tuple and probe uses its own ready sandbox card, destination, and acknowledgment latch. Consequently two coordinate probes do not compete for a mutable queue or overwrite the same destination. This allocation, not an independence assumption about a shared queue, makes the parallel product law below true. A finite serial implementation probes these independent cards in the fixed tuple order. The content of the request is the fixed type encoding of $x$; it is not an input lookup table of desired forecast probabilities.

For each ready transaction, a nonzero valid payload code $\operatorname{payload}(x)$ is present on its source card, and the destination and acknowledgment are initially zero. The accepted branch applies controlled basis copies of this code and sets the acknowledgment. The rejected branch leaves those destination/acknowledgment registers ready. The source is retained in either branch. All payload bits, source ownership, and target ownership are fixed by the architecture and tuple type. This is a real finite import/update operation on the admitted sandbox, not an unrelated random light appended to a graph.

The **semantic configuration** $C=(B,G)$ is the complete array of seed and guard bits. A monotone input event $E=(B_{\rm add},G_{\rm add})$ is a basis-encoded physical card; the updated configuration is $C'=C\lor E$, entrywise. The event carries permission/seed bits, not a precomputed model or response table. Arbitrary finite configurations and every such event are admitted. Nonmonotone changes, malformed codes, exhausted ready-register allocations, and arbitrary hostile edits to internal model or proof storage are outside the commuting theorem; the latter are used only as explicitly identified diagnostic interventions.

### 2. Semantic compiler and independent operational validator

Write $\operatorname{Comp}(C)=(R(C),\Pi(C),H(C))$ for the actual bounded synchronous compiler, with full retained trace $H$. Its proved contract is:

- $R(C)=R_C^\star$ in every evaluator component;
- every present final entry has a finite Base/Refl/Trans/CPA proof against the original raw configuration C;
- the fixed finite schedule terminates;
- $\Pi(C)$ is selected deterministically by a fixed rule priority and index order.

A concrete provenance interface compatible with the synchronous inflationary compiler is the following. Put $k=|P||V|\quad\text{and}\quad N=|P|k^2$. There are $N^2$ stage-entry nodes $(h,r,i,j),\qquad 1\le h\le N$, with a presence bit and $J=3+k+|P|k$ one-hot rule-selector bits. Slots are ordered COPY, BASE, REFL, then the $k$ TRANS choices, then the $|P|k$ CPA choices. All premise addresses are fixed by the indices and point to stage $h-1$; stage zero is absent. COPY only retains a previously established judgment. BASE checks the corresponding raw input seed, REFL checks endpoint/value equality, TRANS checks its two prior-stage premises, and CPA additionally checks its specific raw guard. The compiler chooses the first true candidate; metadata is not supplied as an answer table. COPY nodes can be eliminated to recover the manuscript's four-rule proof system.

The operational validator $V(C,\Pi)$ is a separate circuit. At every node it recomputes rule candidates from C and the supplied preceding-stage presence bits, checks that the selector is either absent with absent presence or exactly one supported rule with present presence, and ANDs all node-validity bits into $\operatorname{Valid}$. For a requested final root $(p,x)$, it returns

$$
K_x=\operatorname{Valid}\wedge\operatorname{presence}_{N,p,x}.
$$

The circuit never reads the model register. It has no gate controlled by a forecast probability. A successful node validates only earlier nodes, so induction on stage proves soundness of every present validated root. On canonical compiler output all node tests succeed, and completeness of the compiler yields

$$
K_x(C,\Pi(C))=\mathbf1_{R_{C,p}^\star}(x).
$$

The independent verifier need not establish maximality for an arbitrary externally supplied partial proof. Completeness in this equality comes from the compiler contract on the admitted canonical ready states; soundness comes from the verifier. The theorem does not silently extend this equivalence to arbitrary corrupted proofs. Its independent program and access separation ensure that the actual service validates a proof of the requested transaction, rather than accepting a displayed forecast as authorization.

For an external transaction, ordinary CNOT copies of raw configuration and provenance are supplied to W's identical verifier. Its basis input is exactly the same canonical C and $\Pi$, so its returned K has the same value. This is not a semantic CPA import across physical perspectives. CPA is evaluated inside the classical compiler/verifier as one proof rule with raw guard data.

The complete compiler's proof and resource ledger establish the all-size closure statement. The operational results below use that proved finite computation, not an independent least-fixed-point oracle.

### 3. Actual noisy transaction service

For each tuple x the relevant local or external verifier first computes $K_x$. Only after the forecast is recorded, the controller reads fresh independent fair bits $A_x,B_x$ and computes

$$
N_x=A_x\wedge B_x,
$$

$$
Z_x=K_x\oplus N_x.
$$

The physical actuator applies the accepted transaction branch exactly when $Z_x=1$. In particular, $Z_x$ sets the appropriate local or external acknowledgment and controls the payload copying gates described in Section 1. The bit $N_x$ is registered deliberate fault injection in a transaction-validation test, so even an invalid request can produce a false acceptance with probability 1/4. The sandbox makes that event a precisely specified, harmless test operation. It is not represented as a proof that the invalid request was semantically valid. Both $K_x\quad\text{and}\quad Z_x$ are retained, permitting the validity decision, fault, and action outcome to be distinguished.

The source bits are part of the instrument, not execution faults. Boolean/proof execution error on the ideal host is zero. The accuracy of the noisy operational decision is separately $\Pr(Z_x=K_x)=\frac34$.

Let $b_x=\mathbf1_{R_{C,p}^\star}(x)$. The independent verifier theorem gives $K_x=b_x$, and direct enumeration of the four equiprobable coin pairs gives

$$
\Pr(Z_x=1\mid C,\text{canonical ready state, fixed probe})=\frac14+\frac12b_x.
$$

For $b=0$, only $(A,B)=(1,1)$ accepts. For $b=1$, the other three pairs accept. Distinct coordinates have separate coins and latches; hence

$$
\Pr(Z=z\mid C,\mathrm{ready})=\prod_{x\in D}\theta_x(C)^{z_x}(1-\theta_x(C))^{1-z_x},
$$

where

$$
\theta_x(C)=\frac14+\frac12\mathbf1_{R_{C,p}^\star}(x).
$$

A single realized bit Z is an outcome, not a probability and not a semantic judgment. Nor is the record of one successful random action evidence that the corresponding closure bit is one.

#### 3.1 Finite instrument and complete retained output

For a fixed ready configuration, each of the $4^d$ complete coin strings $\omega=(A,B)$ has probability $4^{-d}$. Let $F(C,\Pi,M,\omega)$ denote the finite deterministic execution that checks proofs, computes K,N,Z, operates the typed payload latches, copies external reports, calculates accuracy records, and appends all gates' scratch and control records. It retains the input rather than overwriting it. A reversible Boolean implementation maps a ready basis vector to a distinct basis vector containing that input and the computed records. Denote the resulting isometry on the ready input space by $W_omega$. The instrument with coin record $\omega$ has Kraus operator

$$
J_\omega=2^{-d}W_\omega.
$$

Since $W_\omega^\dagger W_\omega=I$ on that space and there are $4^d$ records,

$$
\sum_\omega J_\omega^\dagger J_\omega=I.
$$

The instrument is completely positive and normalized. It is implemented by preparing $2d$ owned fair diagonal bits and the finite controlled NOT/CNOT/Toffoli circuit, retaining the bits and its scratch. A total channel can act as a retained reject/invalid-state branch outside the declared ready space. No claim about coherent unknown input copying is needed.

The full post-probe state is the diagonal joint state

$$
\rho_{\rm full}(C,M)=4^{-d}\sum_{\omega}|C,\Pi,H,M,\omega,F(C,\Pi,M,\omega)\rangle\langle C,\Pi,H,M,\omega,F(C,\Pi,M,\omega)|,
$$

with the deterministic fixed header and source registers included in each basis record. The notation uses a complete deterministic execution record; it does not trace away hidden garbage to make a unitary computation appear irreversible. At the time of prediction $\omega$ is future random input. It is retained after the probe; it is not retroactively conditioned on when assigning the prospective forecast.

The nominated response is the distribution of the actual transaction acknowledgment vector Z, equivalently the corresponding physical committed-payload feature at each typed endpoint. Summing the displayed full state over all coin and audit records with the same Z derives exactly the product law above. These records remain present for a full-response or resource comparison even though they are marginalized in this particular predictive task.

#### 3.2 External report retention and correlation

An external acknowledgment basis bit z in W is copied to a ready S report bit by

$$
|z\rangle_W|0\rangle_{\rm report}\longmapsto|z\rangle_W|z\rangle_{\rm report}.
$$

For an arbitrary diagonal acknowledgment law, the resulting joint state is

$$
\sum_z p_z|z,z\rangle\langle z,z|.
$$

Consequently report disagreement has probability zero, the original acknowledgment is unchanged, and both records are retained. The same bitwise circuit copies the finite basis payload, configuration, and provenance records used by the external appliance. Its copying gate cost and ready targets belong to the ledger. This statement is about a specified classical basis record; on a coherent superposition CNOT correlates registers and does not clone an unknown state. All these records are registered in one fixed physical context. No inference of a definite record at a distinct actualization perspective is made, so no M.6.2 cross-perspective import certificate is invoked or implied.

#### 3.3 Separation from an ornamental output emitter

Three verifiable properties distinguish this implementation from appending an arbitrary Bernoulli lamp:

1. K is the result of checking the request's semantic derivation against physical raw seed/guard inputs, not a forecast-register read.
2. Z selects a typed payload operation of the receiver's own transaction service or the physically separate external service. The acknowledged destination/source states change exactly on the selected branch.
3. Intervening on the forecast register alone while holding C,Pi and source preparations fixed does **not** change the K,Z,or payload law. Conversely, changing a seed/guard event while freezing the old forecast can change the actual transaction law. The latter incurs the strictly positive excess Brier risk calculated below.

These are circuit-access and response identities, not interpretations assigned after computing a desired Fisher split.

### 4. The receiver's internal operational model

At each ready epoch S stores a model header containing the fixed endpoint/subsystem map, validity/fault/actuation distinctions, the transaction transition program, the source-noise calibration, the proper-score program, and its physical computational-basis convention. It also stores an active exact forecast word for each x,

$$
t_x=1+2b_x\in \{1,3\},\qquad \theta_x=t_x/4.
$$

The forecast word is written by the compiler-output/model encoder. The independent operational verifier and actuator do not read it. S's decoder uses the header and these words as an internal model of the registered service. The model represents:

- **Own states.** For $x$ incident to $p$ it represents the local source/destination/commit state, the validated request bit $K_{x}$, the phase `ready -> verified -> acted -> scored`, and the resulting payload/acknowledgment distribution. Every own transaction has an explicitly represented target state. Registers for another transaction are allocated separately. On working code points $b_x=2\theta_x-\frac12$ recovers the validated local permission from the forecast, and the model also has its retained proof/configuration explanation.
- **Predictions.** Its pre-noise prediction for the actual own acknowledgment is $\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\theta_x)$. It predicts $W$'s transaction outcomes in the complementary coordinates and uses the proved report-copy channel to forecast their sensor reports.
- **Accuracy.** It represents $\Pr(Z_x=K_x)=\frac34$, its expected calibrated Brier loss $\theta_x(1-\theta_x)=3/16$, and the exact observed post-probe score $(Z_x-t_x/4)^2$. The last is computed as the integer $(4Z_x-t_x)^2$ with denominator 16 and retained alongside the pre-outcome forecast. No realized outcome is used to define its earlier prediction.
- **Dynamics.** Its transition program maps ready typed transaction state to the verified state, then to the two actuation branches with probabilities $\theta_{x}$ and $1-\theta_x$, followed by exact score and report updates. For example the distribution of the physical local destination/commit pair is $(1-\theta_x)\delta_{(0,0)}+\theta_x\delta_{(\operatorname{payload}(x),1)}$. This is the actual channel's restriction to that subsystem. The epoch-update program is $C'=C\lor E$, followed by the compiled proof/model replacement. Its full $C$/proof trace is retained as conditioning/explanatory data.

On the fixed classical perspectival registration, the header additionally represents the common computational context $s_0$ and the relevant diagonal density operator. The local service's predicted post-probe density operator is explicitly

$$
\rho_{\rm local}(\theta)=\bigotimes_{x\in Q_p}\left[(1-\theta_x)|\mathrm{ready}_x\rangle\langle\mathrm{ready}_x|+\theta_x|\mathrm{committed}_x\rangle\langle\mathrm{committed}_x|\right],
$$

where these two orthogonal basis states contain the named local payload/commit target states. The model header also gives the corresponding finite formula for the complete joint instrument state in Section 3.1 with its retained conditioning records. There is no pure-state vector assigned to a mixed marginal, no imported alternate observer's actualization, and no claim to predict the hidden future coin string.

The model contains a **current-state estimate register** for every retained own transaction slot. Before the nominated comparison that estimate and the physical slot are both ready. After actuation, a registered basis-copy observation writes the observed payload/acknowledgment into a fresh current-state estimate, appends the realized Brier score, and changes the model's phase to `scored`. This is an actual outcome-conditioned internal-model update: the next retained hold/read query for that slot is predicted as its observed state with probability one, whereas the pre-observation forecast assigns its two possible states probabilities $\theta_{x}$ and $1-\theta_x$. The finite predictive loop therefore records a prior prediction, verifies it against an actual operation, evaluates its accuracy, and updates its current-state representation. It does not merely print a probability and discard the result.

There are three distinct times. At t0 and t1, immediately before and after the semantic event computation, the **same unused transaction bank** is ready, its current-state estimates remain ready, and its past accuracy/state history is preserved unchanged. The event channel does not actuate that bank. At t2, the separately invoked probe uses that bank, records its outcomes and scores, and performs the current-state-estimate update just described. The M.10.2 displacement for E compares the t0/t1 predictive chart. It does not silently include the later t2 observation/update in the same $\theta$ displacement. A later challenge uses another preallocated bank; no reset is assumed. Endpoint flags are read at `ready` at both comparison snapshots; transient compiler phases are retained in the full transcript but are not current target states at either snapshot.

The changing statistical parameter at t0/t1 is $\theta$. The header's programs, response variables, physical subsystem meanings, current target-state estimates and past accuracy records are fixed across that comparison. C,proofs, past scores, scratch, and clocks are retained data; they are not extra unidentified coordinates smuggled into the Fisher chart. A firewall therefore protects the nominated own transaction-prediction component. It does not claim that S's memory of external configuration data, its compilation activity, or its archive is unaffected. An operational self-model can represent these own transaction states and dynamics without being an omniscient model of every internal variable.

#### 4.1 Positive predictive quality and physical information

Use summed Brier loss $L(q,z)=\sum_x (z_x-q_x)^2$ and quality $Q=-L$; a normalized average divides all results by d. For a true product law with marginal vector $\theta'$,

$$
\mathbb E_{\theta'}[L(q,Z)]=\sum_x\left[\theta_x'(1-\theta_x')+(q_x-\theta_x')^2\right].
$$

This follows by expanding the square coordinate by coordinate; product independence is not needed for this particular expectation. Updating a frozen old forecast $\theta$ to the correct post-event forecast $\theta'$ improves quality by

$$
\Delta Q(E)=\sum_x (\theta'_x-\theta_x)^2.
$$

For a monotone closure extension with $m=|R_p^{\star\prime}\setminus R_p^\star|$, the actual model update gives $\Delta Q=m/4$. Thus every admitted event that changes the nominated closure response has strictly positive event-conditional predictive improvement for relevant actual transaction outcomes. In either example below m is positive. If closure is unchanged, the event remains physically processable but this task has no positive new-information claim for it.

For a matched chance forecast $q_{x}=1/2$, the correctly calibrated model has Brier improvement $1/16$ per coordinate over chance. This verifies that the service's forecast task has genuine predictive performance independently of selecting an extension. A task distribution assigning positive mass, for example one half, to the chosen extension card and otherwise to a null card makes the event's Definition-1 functional potential explicit. Applying the update only on that event gives zero additional loss on the null branch and positive unconditional improvement as well. The input pattern is the physical basis card, its content is the seed/guard extension, and its useful regularity is the change in actual validation-controlled transaction law.

### 5. Identifiable open Fisher stratum and physically typed splitting

The statistical model family is

$$
p_\theta(z)=\prod_x\theta_x^{z_x}(1-\theta_x)^{1-z_x},\qquad \Theta=(0,1)^D.
$$

Its open statistical chart is not an assertion that a finite bit register exactly names every real number. The actual encoder uses the finite rational points with entries 1/4 or 3/4. The open family also has a concrete physical interpretation: keep a working closure bit $K_{x}$ fixed and vary the independent fault ancilla's calibrated flip probability $\epsilon_{x}$ in $(0,1)$. Then

$\theta_x=\epsilon_x$ if $K_{x}=0$, and $\theta_x=1-\epsilon_x$ if $K_{x}=1$.

This is a smooth coordinatewise bijection between open calibration parameters and $\Theta$ on the fixed discrete branch. A diagonal qubit state $\operatorname{diag}(1-\epsilon_x,\epsilon_x)$ and an XOR implements that law; at the nominated $\epsilon=1/4$ it is realized exactly by the two fair-coin AND circuit already specified. This calibration chart introduces no uncountable program-description requirement and is not used to alter the finite rational working encoder. It supplies the identifiable open stratum around every retained point with a physical channel interpretation.

The effect selecting $Z_x=1$, equivalently the actual acknowledged payload at the relevant endpoint, satisfies $\Pr_\theta(Z_x=1)=\theta_x$. Thus the family is identifiable, and the same readout separates a newly admitted transaction's parameters 1/4 and 3/4 by probability difference 1/2. A single trial is not asserted to distinguish these overlapping distributions with certainty; identifiability is a statement about the distribution.

The score component is

$$
\partial_x\log p_\theta(Z)=\frac{Z_x-\theta_x}{\theta_x(1-\theta_x)}.
$$

It has mean zero, variance $1/[\theta_x(1-\theta_x)]$, and is independent of the other score components. Hence

$$
g_{xy}(\theta)=\frac{\delta_{xy}}{\theta_x(1-\theta_x)}.
$$

For a nonzero v, $g_\theta(v,v)=\sum_x\frac{v_x^2}{\theta_x(1-\theta_x)}>0$. This proves positive definiteness throughout $\Theta$ without a pseudometric or quotient of singular directions.

Register the tangent subspaces by the pre-existing endpoint actuator ownership:

$$
T^{(\mathrm{self})}=\operatorname{span}\{e_x:x\in Q_p\},\qquad T^{(\mathrm{ext})}=\operatorname{span}\{e_x:x\notin Q_p\}.
$$

Their supports are disjoint, so their cross Fisher product vanishes at every $\theta$. Their direct sum is the entire tangent space, and the orthogonal self projection retains exactly local-transaction coordinates. This is the Fisher metric of the nominated prospective acknowledgment distribution. It is not asserted equal to the Fisher information of every fully retained coin/proof/audit register; those registers are different operational questions with their own full responses.

Every update is represented by the affine-chart displacement theta'-theta in $T_\theta\Theta$, with all norms and projections evaluated at the **pre-update** point $\theta$. This is the manuscript's finite-update convention, not a geodesic distance. The straight segment between any two encoded working points remains in $\Theta$.

### 6. Exact encoder, update channel, decoder, and commuting theorem

Let $\operatorname{Enc}(C)$ be the ready physical state containing raw $C$, the actual compiler output $R(C)$, $\Pi(C)$, all deterministic compiler history, fixed header, active forecast words $t(C)$, and the preallocated remaining ready resources. If the common host has a previous finite history, include it unchanged; $\operatorname{Enc}$ can carry this history as an extra argument. Let $U_{E}$ be the finite physical channel that:

1. reads and archives the basis event E and the old active configuration/forecast, leaving the same designated unused transaction bank, its ready current-state estimates, and all past accuracy records untouched;
2. writes $C'=C\lor E$ in fresh registers;
3. runs the complete actual compiler on C';
4. writes fresh forecast words $t'_x=1+2 R(C')_{p,x}$;
5. advances the active-ready pointer while retaining all old/new workspace, sources, proofs, forecast words, event, and controller history.

These are basis-state computations implemented with retained inputs and fresh scratch. The update produces a new ready epoch referring to that same untouched designated transaction bank; it does not yet draw the next probe's coins or change any current transaction-state estimate. In particular its model decoder is deterministic on the admitted input even though the subsequent prospective response is stochastic.

Define $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{closure}}$ to read the active final relation and $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{proof}}$ to read its active provenance. Define $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{model}}$ to return the rational vector $t/4$. Define $\operatorname{Resp}$ to be the actual prospective transaction law from the probe instrument, marginalizing the complete retained record as in Section 3.1. The prediction decoder and the physical response map are separate maps.

**Theorem (all-instance response-faithful realization).** For every finite nonempty $P,V$, every nominated $p$, every finite configuration $C$, and every monotone event $E$ that fits the registered finite horizon/resources, let $C'=C\lor E$ and let $R^\star=R_C^\star,\qquad R^{\star\prime}=R_{C'}^\star$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Dec}_{\rm closure}(\operatorname{Enc}(C))=R^\star,
$$

$$
\operatorname{Dec}_{\rm closure}(U_E(\operatorname{Enc}(C)))=R^{\star\prime},
$$

$$
\operatorname{Dec}_{\rm model}(\operatorname{Enc}(C))=\theta(R^\star),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Dec}_{\rm model}(U_E(\operatorname{Enc}(C)))=\theta(R^{\star\prime}),
$$

$$
\operatorname{Resp}(\operatorname{Enc}(C))=p_{\theta(R^\star)},
$$

$$
\operatorname{Resp}(U_E(\operatorname{Enc}(C)))=p_{\theta(R^{\star\prime})}.
$$

Every active present closure entry has the corresponding sound decoded proof, and the independent validator gives $K_x=\mathbf1_{R_p^\star}(x)$ before and $K_x'=\mathbf1_{R_p^{\star\prime}}(x)$ after the event. All equalities remain true for any allowed prior retained history, because the active-slot selector and fresh ready-resource allocation prevent old scratch and probe outcomes from controlling the new computation.

*Proof.* The compiler's stage induction and finite stabilization proof apply to arbitrary raw finite C and to C'. They establish the two closure equalities and canonical proof validity. The model encoder computes $t=1+2b$ from the active p-component bit and divides by four on readout; therefore it gives exactly the two specified $\theta$ vectors. The independent validator's proof induction returns the same active bits. Its circuit does not read the forecast. The explicit four-coin-case calculation and disjoint-source factorization then give each prospective response equality. The finite update schedule retains old data and computes on fresh active registers, so no history affects these implications. These are identities for every input and every coin outcome in the declared finite class, not only expectation-level properties established by sampling. ∎

The commuting diagrams can equivalently be written

$$
C\xrightarrow{\ C\mapsto C\lor E\ }C'\xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{Cl}\ }R^{\star\prime}\xrightarrow{\ \theta\ }\theta(R^{\star\prime}),
$$

$$
C\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Enc}}\rho_C\xrightarrow{U_E}\rho_{C,E}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Dec}_{\rm model}}\theta(R^{\star\prime}),
$$

with $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{closure}}/\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{proof}}$ supplying the corresponding closure/provenance diagram and $\operatorname{Resp}$ supplying the actual-response diagram. The semantic arrows are implemented by the indicated finite physical programs.

#### 6.1 Exact response equivalence and its limits

Two ready states are equivalent for the nominated predictive task precisely when they induce the same conditional prospective acknowledgment law for the fixed standardized probe, after conditioning on the ready epoch and fixed request labels. On the admitted class this is equivalent to equality of $\theta$, and to equality of the p closure component, because the marginal readouts identify $\theta$ and the 1/4/3/4 code identifies that component.

This is a task-specific response equivalence, not equality of complete states or of all outputs. Two raw configurations may have the same closure but different seed/guard/proof/history records. Their task response laws can agree while $\operatorname{Dec}_{\mathrm{raw}}$ or a proof/audit readout separates them perfectly. Even $U_E(\operatorname{Enc}(C))$ and a newly prepared $\operatorname{Enc}(C')$ need not be equal microstates, since the former retains $C,E$ and its history. The theorem asserts the decoded and response identities, not a false whole-state equality. Complete comparisons retain all omitted records and all owned resources.

#### 6.2 Complete retained response equivalence

Fix the registered finite horizon and let \(\mathfrak P_H\) contain the joint computational-basis readout of every named retained register, its coordinate readouts, all nominated update/probe compositions within that horizon, and the recorded resource readout. This includes raw configuration and event cards, all closure/proof stages, forecasts and journals, source coins, payloads, acknowledgments, reports, state estimates, scores, controller/clock records, and the charged input/workspace/operation ledger. Define
\[
\rho\equiv_{\rm full}\widetilde\rho
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Law}_\rho(\pi)=\operatorname{Law}_{\widetilde\rho}(\pi)
\text{ for every }\pi\in\mathfrak P_H,
\quad\text{with equal registered resource ledgers}.
\]
On the admitted diagonal retained-state class, the complete joint basis readout separates distinct diagonal density operators. On conditional single-run basis states, it separates every different retained bitstring. No equality of forecasts can erase a history, coin, proof, source, or cost difference under this equivalence.

The prospective transaction-task quotient is the separately named projection
\[
[\rho]_{\equiv_{\rm full}}\longmapsto
\operatorname{Law}_\rho(Z\mid\text{ready epoch and fixed request labels}).
\]
It is well-defined because the transaction probe belongs to \(\mathfrak P_H\), and it is generally noninjective. For example, recording an additional already-reflexive seed changes the raw input/archive readout without changing the closure or prospective transaction law. The Fisher tensor belongs to this projected predictive family. The complete-response equivalence and its resource ledger are retained alongside it throughout the realization theorem.

### 7. Derived maps and firewall transport

From the just-proved physical decoder/response identities, the actual nominated model change is

$$
\Delta M_S(E)=\theta(R^{\star\prime})-\theta(R^\star)=\frac12\left(\mathbf1_{R_p^{\star\prime}}-\mathbf1_{R_p^\star}\right).
$$

Thus define the populated map

$$
\Delta\Phi_S(R,R')=\frac12(\mathbf1_{R_p'}-\mathbf1_{R_p}).
$$

This is derived from the implemented model encoding and actual verified transaction response. It is not chosen first and enforced by directly driving a random emitter from a model label. It is the linear map $L=(1/2)I$ on closure differences.

For self sectors $A=R_p^\star\cap Q_p,\qquad A'=R_p^{\star\prime}\cap Q_p$, the physically typed Fisher projection gives

$$
\operatorname{pr}_{\rm self}\Delta M_S(E)=\frac12(\mathbf1_{A'}-\mathbf1_A).
$$

Consequently the populated factor map is

$$
\Psi_S(A,A')=\frac12(\mathbf1_{A'}-\mathbf1_A),
$$

viewed as a vector supported on $Q_{p}$. It satisfies $\Psi_S(A,A)=0$ for every retained sector and is additive on composable extensions. The factorization holds for every finite configuration and every admitted monotone event, including external changes that propagate through arbitrarily many closure stages. It makes no assumption that new guards have external targets.

Since every external nonreflexive column of $(1/2)I$ projects to zero, this realized map also satisfies the already-proved classification theorem P.16b.12.4g.2. The classification and negative leakage theorem are preserved; the new result supplies their previously missing operational population.

If $I$ is a fixed-point firewall certificate, the manuscript's exact criterion gives $A'=A$. The physical result is therefore

$$
\Delta M_S^{(\mathrm{self})}(E)=0,\qquad \sigma_S(E)=0.
$$

It means that all prospective own transaction marginal probabilities, and hence their whole product law and represented transition kernels, are unchanged. It does not mean that their individual new random outputs coincide with an earlier run, that no calculation occurred, that the full transcript is unchanged, or that heat is zero. No SPAP-proximity value is asserted without the separately required default-model condition.

### 8. Nonvacuity, exact calculations, and falsification

#### 8.1 Protected nonzero external change

Take P containing distinct p,t,u, take V containing a,c, and let $y=(t,u,a,c)$ be nonreflexive. Start with no seeds and no guards. Every component's closure is exactly the reflexive identity relation. Add just the seed y in evaluator p. The updated p closure adds exactly y: composition with reflexive entries returns y and y cannot compose with itself because its labeled endpoints differ; all guards remain zero. The other components do not change.

Set $I_p=\{y\}$ and all other $I_r=\varnothing$. Then $R^\star\cup I=R^{\star\prime}$ is a fixed point and $I_p\cap Q_p=\varnothing$, an explicit firewall certificate. The actual external appliance's y acceptance probability changes from 1/4 to 3/4. No own local transaction law changes. The populated update is $(1/2)e_y$, so the total squared pre-update Fisher norm is $(1/4)/(3/16)=4/3$, the self norm is zero, $\sigma$ is zero, and the Brier improvement is 1/4. This protects a genuine nonzero physical external response.

#### 8.2 Guard-only self leakage

Use the manuscript's fixed example with $P=\{p,t,u\}$, $V=\{a,b,c\}$, original seed $(p,t,a,b)$ at evaluator $p$, seed $(t,u,b,c)$ at evaluator $t$, and all guards zero. Enable only $\mathrm{CPA}'_p(t,u)=1$. The two newly derived $p$ tuples are

$$
x=(p,u,a,c)\quad\text{and}\quad y=(t,u,b,c).
$$

The first follows by the original p edge and evaluator-t edge. The second follows by the p reflexive edge at $(t,b)$ and the evaluator-t edge. The reflexive entries together with the original p edge and these two new edges are closed: the only new nontrivial same-evaluator composition returns x, and the only enabled CPA premise returns x or y. Thus there are exactly these two new p tuples.

The local outgoing route x and the external route y both change actual acceptance probability from 1/4 to 3/4. Hence

$$
\Delta M=(1/2)e_x+(1/2)e_y,
$$

$$
\|\Delta M^{(\mathrm{self})}\|_{\rm pre}^2=4/3,
$$

$$
\|\Delta M^{(\mathrm{ext})}\|_{\rm pre}^2=4/3,
$$

$$
\|\Delta M\|_{\rm pre}^2=8/3,
$$

$$
\sigma=1/\sqrt2.
$$

The positive Brier improvement is 1/2. Although the guard target u is not p, it changes an actual local transaction probability through closure composition. The example therefore retains both the semantic obstruction and its operational response witness.

#### 8.3 Different faulty coupling, with real self disturbance
