### P.16b.15b Semantic Satiation and the Predictive Use of Meaning

Repeating a familiar word can produce a temporary state in which its sound or written form remains recognizable while its meaning feels less immediately available. This effect, semantic satiation, separates three quantities that a predictive account keeps apart: the physical recurrence of a symbol, access to its meaning, and the usefulness of that meaning for the current task. Its processing locus is an empirical question: perceptual adaptation, changes in word-to-meaning access and semantic effects have received different support across tasks (Pilotti et al. 1997; Tian and Huber 2010; Ströberg et al. 2017).

PU proposes that repeated, predictable tokens can cease to justify the same degree of active semantic engagement when their meaning adds little to the current task, while the word keeps its learned meaning and remains available for another task. Definition P.16b.15b.1 fixes the comparison, Proposition P.16b.15b.2 gives its PCE criterion, Hypothesis P.16b.15b.3 posits the allocation response together with a candidate law, and Protocol P.16b.15b.5 tests that law.

<a id="definition-p16b15b1-task-relative-semantic-comparison"></a>**Definition P.16b.15b.1 (Task-Relative Semantic Comparison).**

Fix a finite experimental horizon, an observer, a stimulus and task law, a history $h_t$, a predictive scoring rule, a feasible policy menu, and a complete resource-cost convention. Compare two feasible processing policies on those same data:

* $a_0$, which supports the registered form-recognition task with less active access to semantic relations;
* $a_1$, which additionally recruits the registered semantic relations for the task.

Both policies act on the same stored word and concept; they differ in active processing. Let $Q_t(a)$ be the expected predictive score under policy $a$, conditioned on $h_t$ and evaluated on the declared outcome law. Let $C_t(a)$ include the activation, maintenance, switching, inhibition and later reactivation costs over the same horizon. Register the tradeoff coefficient $\lambda>0$, converting score units into cost units, and define
$$
G_t:=Q_t(a_1)-Q_t(a_0),
\qquad
\Delta C_t:=C_t(a_1)-C_t(a_0),
\qquad
V_t:=\lambda G_t-\Delta C_t.
\tag{P.16b.15b.1}
$$
Here $G_t$ is the incremental task benefit of semantic access. It differs from the learning increment $\Delta Q$ of one prediction-update cycle, from sensory surprise and from prediction error. The scoring rule, admissible policies, horizon, cost units and $\lambda$ are registered independently of the effect being explained. The sign of $\Delta C_t$ is measured: a policy with less active processing need not have lower complete cost.

<a id="proposition-p16b15b2-pairwise-allocation-criterion"></a>**Proposition P.16b.15b.2 (Pairwise Allocation Criterion).**

On the comparison of Definition P.16b.15b.1, let the PCE objective be
$$
F_t(a)=C_t(a)-\lambda Q_t(a).
\tag{P.16b.15b.2}
$$
Then $a_0$ has strictly lower objective than $a_1$ exactly when $V_t<0$, $a_1$ has strictly lower objective exactly when $V_t>0$, and the two tie at $V_t=0$. In particular, when $\Delta C_t>0$, a positive incremental benefit with $\lambda G_t<\Delta C_t$ favors $a_0$.

*Proof.* Direct subtraction gives $F_t(a_1)-F_t(a_0)=\Delta C_t-\lambda G_t=-V_t$. ∎

Proposition P.16b.15b.2 is the pairwise comparison of Theorem P.16b.9.3 without its equal-meaning-potential hypothesis, applied to two registered processing policies. Whether observers allocate access according to $V_t$ is the content of Hypothesis P.16b.15b.3.

<a id="hypothesis-p16b15b3-reversible-semantic-access-allocation"></a>**Hypothesis P.16b.15b.3 (Reversible Semantic-Access Allocation).**

On a registered class of repetition tasks, observers adjust active semantic access partly in response to the incremental benefit and complete cost in (P.16b.15b.1). Repetition without a continuing semantic requirement can lower $V_t$, and a later task that makes the meaning useful can raise it; the dependence of $G_t$ and $\Delta C_t$ on task structure is calibrated independently of the access measurements (Protocol P.16b.15b.5). One minimal candidate law is
$$
g_{t+1}=(1-\eta)g_t+
\eta\,\sigma(\beta V_t),
\qquad
\sigma(x)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-x}},
\quad 0<\eta\le1,\quad\beta>0,
\tag{P.16b.15b.3}
$$
where $g_t\in[0,1]$ is a latent semantic-access allocation variable and each update indexes one registered trial. Each update is a convex combination of $g_t$ and $\sigma(\beta V_t)\in(0,1)$, so $g_t$ stays in $[0,1]$. The coefficient $\beta$ has reciprocal cost units, so $\beta V_t$ is dimensionless.

*Status.* Equation (P.16b.15b.3) is a phenomenological law posited in addition to Proposition P.16b.15b.2: minimizing (P.16b.15b.2) selects one policy, while the finite-$\beta$ target of (P.16b.15b.3) permits intermediate allocation when one policy is strictly preferred. A separately registered measurement relation connects $g_t$ to behavioral or neural responses. The parameters and the measurement relation are estimated on training or calibration data and tested on held-out conditions.

For fixed $V$, (P.16b.15b.3) gives
$$
g_{t+k}-\sigma(\beta V)
=(1-\eta)^k\bigl(g_t-\sigma(\beta V)\bigr),
\qquad k\ge0.
\tag{P.16b.15b.4}
$$
Thus, if repetition lowers $V$ so that $\sigma(\beta V)<g_t$, the law predicts a monotone decline of access, geometric for $0<\eta<1$ and complete at the next update for $\eta=1$; if useful semantic context raises the target above the current allocation, it predicts a monotone recovery. Both predictions follow from (P.16b.15b.3) together with the specified change of $V$. Throughout, the law allows continued semantic processing and nonzero prediction error, and the stored semantic representation is unchanged.

<a id="remark-p16b15b4-information-surprise-and-the-quotient-of-theorem-82"></a>**Remark P.16b.15b.4 (Information, Surprise and the Quotient of Theorem 8.2).**

Definition 1 measures information by the event-conditional potential for positive expected improvement in predictive quality under an admissible task-relative procedure; the criterion is met without a positive learning update on each repeated token. A highly expected word can remain indispensable for a decision, and a well-learned prediction can keep its value while producing little new learning. Low surprise, a small learning increment, or an exactly correct sensory prediction therefore leaves $G_t$ to be measured, and the Fundamental Predictive Loop $P_{int}\to V\to D_{cyc}$ of Definition 4 continues.

Theorem 8.2 quotients a predictive-weight ledger on a separating, protocol-complete, response-complete branch: the quotient preserves every retained operational response and removes only context labels that those responses do not distinguish. Hypothesis P.16b.15b.3 describes a change of semantic responses under a retained protocol. That change is an access allocation on the protocol family and lies outside the idle-label quotient of Theorem 8.2. Extending a repetition task to new semantic queries changes the comparison domain and requires a fresh equivalence check.

<a id="protocol-p16b15b5-discriminating-tests"></a>**Protocol P.16b.15b.5 (Discriminating Tests).**

Register a within-participant comparison that varies repetition and the usefulness of meaning while matching token identity, exposure time, spacing, response demands and incentives as closely as the manipulation permits. Independently measure recognition of the token's form, performance on semantic probes, and subjective loss of meaning. Randomize and counterbalance items and conditions; control fatigue, attention, familiarity, general slowing, and the reactivation of meaning by the semantic probe itself. Estimate sensory expectancy independently of the satiation response. Prespecify a primary semantic-access outcome $Y$, oriented so that higher values indicate better access, and calibrate its monotone relation to $g_t$ over the tested range. Subjective reports and task performance receive separate measurement mappings and need not covary. Before testing, register for each test the task, the comparators of Remark P.16b.15b.6, the measurement bridge, the independently constrained parameters, the predicted direction or interval, and the rejection criterion.

The calibrated law (P.16b.15b.3) is exposed to three directional tests.

1. **Usefulness moderates repetition.** Let $Y_{r,u}$ denote the prespecified outcome at low/high repetition $r\in\{0,1\}$ and low/high semantic usefulness $u\in\{0,1\}$. On a confirmatory branch on which independently calibrated $V_t$ trajectories in all four cells, initial allocations, exposure durations and the measurement mapping predict the contrast below to exceed $\delta_U$, the registered prediction is
   $$
   D_U:=(Y_{1,1}-Y_{0,1})-(Y_{1,0}-Y_{0,0})>\delta_U,
   \tag{P.16b.15b.5}
   $$
   for a positive smallest effect of interest $\delta_U$ registered before the confirmatory test. A qualitative decrease of $V$ in one condition is insufficient for this prediction. The interaction tests protection from the repetition-related decline, separately from a general advantage of doing a semantic task.

2. **Semantic recovery exceeds matched form novelty.** After matched induction, compare a context that makes the same word's meaning useful with a voice, font or acoustic change that adds perceptual novelty without comparable semantic usefulness. Include a no-change control and, where feasible, cross semantic usefulness with form novelty. Use matched initial allocation and independently estimated value-and-cost trajectories for both manipulations, and control ordinary context facilitation with matched non-satiated trials. On the branch on which those trajectories and the calibrated measurement mapping predict it, the registered prediction is greater recovery of $Y$ from semantic usefulness than from form novelty, by a preregistered margin $\delta_R>0$. Novelty can also change value or cost, so the predicted ordering comes from the calibrated trajectories and not from the manipulation labels. A new sentence context carries attention, priming, predictability and task effects, which require their own controls.

3. **Recovery follows a constrained trajectory.** Estimate $\eta$, $\beta$, the task-value model and the measurement relation outside the confirmatory recovery condition. Use them to predict the direction and time course of access changes when usefulness is restored while token form is held fixed. Predictive performance must exceed prespecified perceptual-adaptation and word-to-meaning-adaptation comparators on held-out data; only a prediction fixed before the recovery curve is seen counts as a test.

When the manipulation and measurement checks hold, an upper confidence bound below the registered minimum predicted effect counts against the corresponding quantitative prediction, and an interval containing both negligible and predicted effects is inconclusive. Reliable effects in the opposite direction, or failure of the calibrated law in held-out conditions, reject the calibrated law (P.16b.15b.3); other resource-sensitive laws for Hypothesis P.16b.15b.3 are tested on their own registrations. An experiment that fails to induce satiation is uninformative about the law.

<a id="remark-p16b15b6-comparators"></a>**Remark P.16b.15b.6 (Comparators).**

Sensory adaptation or habituation can reduce effective input; adaptation of the word-to-meaning association can reduce access; fatigue and attentional change can alter both reports and task performance. These mechanisms can coexist with task-sensitive allocation, and associative accounts can themselves be context-sensitive. Each comparator is specified in advance by its inputs, adaptation law, measurement model and allowed task dependence. Recovery after a pause, and recovery after a semantic-context manipulation, are predicted by several of these accounts; the discriminating evidence is the calibrated contrast of tests 2 and 3 of Protocol P.16b.15b.5. Repetition suppression and expectation effects are distinct variables and are measured separately (Summerfield et al. 2008). N400 and related electrophysiological effects constrain processing accounts as indirect measures of meaning, utility and prediction error, through their own registered measurement model (Ströberg et al. 2017).

### P.16b.16 Information Projections and Many-to-One Boundaries

<a id="definition-p16b161-finite-profile-projections"></a>**Definition P.16b.16.1 (Finite profile projections).**

Let
$$
\mathcal P_S(c)=(\Delta Q_S(c),\mu_S(c),\sigma_S(c))
$$
be a finite perspectival coordinate chart on the operational quotient $\mathcal F_S$ where defined.

A Shannon projection is a branch map
$$
\rho_H(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)=\Delta Q
$$
on a pure-information branch where $\Delta Q$ is identified with the Shannon entropy coordinate. A Kolmogorov-style projection is a branch map
$$
\rho_K(\Delta Q,\mu,\sigma)=K_S(c)
$$
when a registered finite-program coding defines $K_S(c)$ and the code cost is constant on every fiber of $\mathcal P_S$ in the retained domain. This fiber condition makes $\rho_K$ a function of the displayed profile; without it, $K_S$ is only a content-indexed cost and does not descend to that profile.

<a id="theorem-p16b162-shannon-recovery-on-the-pure-information-branch"></a>**Theorem P.16b.16.2 (Shannon recovery on the pure-information branch).**

On a branch where content $c$ is purely informational and the finite chart is normalized by
$$
\Delta Q_S(c)=H(c),
\qquad
\mu_S(c)=0,
\qquad
\sigma_S(c)=0,
$$
the Shannon projection recovers Shannon entropy:
$$
\rho_H(\mathcal P_S(c))=H(c).
$$

*Proof.* Substitute the branch normalization into Definition P.16b.16.1:
$$
\rho_H(\mathcal P_S(c))=\rho_H(H(c),0,0)=H(c).
$$
∎

<a id="corollary-p16b163-shannon-projection-is-many-to-one"></a>**Corollary P.16b.16.3 (Shannon projection is many-to-one).**

The Shannon projection does not classify full perspectival role. Distinct profiles
$$
(\Delta Q,\mu_1,\sigma_1)
\ne
(\Delta Q,\mu_2,\sigma_2)
$$
with the same first coordinate have the same Shannon projection.

*Proof.* Definition P.16b.16.1 ignores $\mu$ and $\sigma$ in $\rho_H$. Therefore all profiles with the same $\Delta Q$ have the same Shannon projection, even when their full operational roles differ. ∎

<a id="theorem-p16b164-information-projections-do-not-replace-role-position-equivalence"></a>**Theorem P.16b.16.4 (Information projections do not replace role-position equivalence).**

Equality of Shannon or Kolmogorov-style projections does not imply equality in $\mathcal F_S$ unless a separating projection branch is supplied.

*Proof.* By Theorem P.16b.7.4, equality in $\mathcal F_S$ is equality of operational response-presheaf role. By Corollary P.16b.7.5, finite coordinate equality is weaker than role-position equality unless the chart is separating. Since $\rho_H$ and $\rho_K$ discard response-presheaf data on their ordinary branches, equality of their values does not force equality of operational role without a separating hypothesis. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16b165-cogito-zero-boundary-for-profile-costs"></a>**Corollary P.16b.16.5 (Cogito-zero boundary for profile costs).**

For the positive-weight full-profile cost $E_S$ of Theorem P.16b.6.6, zero cost identifies the cogito exactly on the separating-origin branch of Definition P.16b.6.5. For a cost evaluated after an information projection, the same conclusion additionally requires a certificate that zero projected cost forces $\mathcal P_S(c)=(0,0,0)$ on the retained domain.

*Proof.* Theorem P.16b.6.6 uses positivity of all full-profile weights to force every profile coordinate to vanish. Definition P.16b.6.5 then identifies that zero profile with the cogito response class. A projection may discard nonzero coordinates, as Corollary P.16b.16.3 records, so a projected zero requires the additional zero-separation certificate before that argument applies. ∎

## P.16c Generative Non-Closure: Axioms as Stable Responses to Incompleteness

### P.16c.0 Standing and Scope

This section records the philosophical form of Appendix A.6. It adds no axiom, postulate, or physical branch. Its theorem-level content is the conjunction of two separately stated results:
$$
\text{same-cycle live-diagonal non-closure}
$$
and
$$
\text{a finite verified prediction-update cycle satisfying Theorem A.6.4}
\Longrightarrow
\text{a stable local axiom-stabilizer}.
$$
Historical or external processing of the targeted sentence remains possible. Theorem A.6.4 constructs the stabilizer from its independently supplied finite-cycle hypotheses, and the stabilizer supplies an axiom-like local formal system on its retained response domain (Theorem P.16c.2).

### P.16c.1 Generative non-closure reading

<a id="definition-p16c1-generative-non-closure-reading"></a>**Definition P.16c.1 (Generative non-closure reading).** A PU presentation has the **generative non-closure reading** when:

1. the primitive obstruction is the absence of a total standard-sound same-cycle Boolean closure on a live-diagonal-complete active domain, as established by Theorem A.6.2;
2. every stable axiom-stabilizer is the local finite object defined in Definition A.6.3;
3. axioms, inference rules, verification predicates, typing restrictions, bridge laws, and response quotients are read as finite partial-closure boundaries only on prediction-update cycles satisfying Theorem A.6.4;
4. PCE selects a least-cost representative only when the relevant minimum exists;
5. PPI admits only distinctions with finite protocol-response instantiation.

<a id="theorem-p16c2-axioms-as-stabilization-boundaries"></a>**Theorem P.16c.2 (Axioms as stabilization boundaries).** Every nontrivial finite prediction-update cycle satisfying all hypotheses of Theorem A.6.4 induces a stable partial-closure boundary. Conversely, every stable axiom-stabilizer supplies an axiom-like local formal system on its retained response domain.

*Proof.* The forward direction is Theorem A.6.4. For the converse, a stable tuple
$$
\mathfrak A_{S,B}
=
(D_{S,B},J_{S,B},\vdash_{S,B},V_{S,B},q_{S,B})
$$
supplies accepted seeds, a retained inference/update relation, a verification predicate, and a response quotient. These are exactly the local data of an axiom-like formal system on $D_{S,B}$. The live-diagonal guard prevents this local system from being read as a total same-cycle truth predicate. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16c3-predictionism-as-axiom-generation"></a>**Corollary P.16c.3 (Predictionism as axiom-generation).** On the conjunction of Theorem A.6.2 and the independent hypotheses of Theorem A.6.4,
$$
\text{same-cycle live-diagonal non-closure}
+
\text{guarded finite verified prediction}
\Longrightarrow
\text{stable local axiom-stabilizer}.
$$

*Proof.* Theorem A.6.2 gives the same-cycle obstruction. Remark A.0.1.1 gives the finite verification cut for the declared protocol. Theorem A.6.4 constructs the stabilizer from the independently supplied finite-cycle hypotheses. ∎

<a id="theorem-p16c4-conservative-inversion-of-the-usual-axiom-incompleteness-order"></a>**Theorem P.16c.4 (Conservative inversion of the usual axiom-incompleteness order).** Under the effectiveness, arithmetic-strength, and consistency or soundness hypotheses of the particular incompleteness theorem being invoked, its ordinary schematic presentation is
$$
\text{effective axiomatization}
\Longrightarrow
\text{diagonal fixed point}
\Longrightarrow
\text{relative incompleteness}.
$$
This presentation admits the following conservative PU reading:
$$
\left[
\text{same-cycle live-diagonal non-closure}
+
\text{guarded finite verified prediction}
\right]
\Longrightarrow
\text{stable finite partial closure}
\Longrightarrow
\text{axiom-like local formal structure}.
$$
This reading changes no theorem, branch condition, certificate status, or numerical value.

*Proof.* The first display is only a schematic summary under the stated hypotheses of the selected incompleteness theorem. In the second display, Theorem A.6.2 supplies the live-diagonal obstruction and Theorem A.6.4 supplies the stabilizer only after all of its independent finite-cycle hypotheses are assumed. Definition A.6.3 identifies the stabilizer's local formal roles. Theorem A.6.6 gives conservativity. ∎

**Selected-Rewrite Predictor Bridge.** On Remark A.0.1b's branch, one controller invocation prepares a local prediction from its finite control and current tree observation, verifies whether the nominated position is a saturated $\mathbf S$ redex, and updates the term by the verified contraction. The invocation reports normality when no redex exists. On the encoded universal trajectory, its checked contractions expose the exact source computation through the registered readers.

The verification and detector bounds certify finite work for each nominated invocation and observation. Iterating the update over the retained growing term realizes the computably enumerable complete halting event. With term mutation disabled, a fixed finite term admits only finitely many control-position states, so an indefinitely continued deterministic controller repeats a state and becomes periodic. The source's root-restarted implementation terminates each invocation under its all-input bound.

The bridge registers the syntax, controller, observation, prediction, verification and update maps. Its physical realization maps those operations to a predictive system's response ledger; its focal position has its own role, separate from the three full-context registers counted by Theorem 15.

### P.16c.5 Relation to ordinary mathematical foundations

The generative-non-closure reading separates three claims.

1. **Ordinary incompleteness claim:** a sufficiently strong fixed formal system may contain true but unprovable sentences relative to that system.
2. **PU active-access claim:** the time-indexed sentence $E_{S,t}$ cannot be correctly processed by $S$ at the targeted cycle, although external or faithful historical processing may be possible.
3. **Stable-boundary claim:** a finite prediction-update cycle satisfying Theorem A.6.4 induces a local axiom-stabilizer.

The first claim is formal-system-relative, the second is predictor-and-cycle-relative, and the third is conditional on the declared finite-cycle hypotheses. None implies either of the others without the stated bridge assumptions.

| Twisted-diagonal obstruction | Lemma P.16c.7.2; Proposition P.16c.7.3 | common fixed-point-free contradiction step on the registered typed instances |
| Certified finite diagonal ladder | Definition P.16c.8.1; Theorem P.16c.8.2 | finite rungwise accessibility with a fresh same-cycle boundary |

<a id="remark-p16c61-cogito-diagonal-type-separation"></a>**Remark P.16c.6.1 (Cogito--Diagonal Type Separation).** Foundational Certainty P.2.1 certifies the occurrence of an awareness or process, expressed by the existential $\exists\mathcal C$. Theorem A.6.2 instead quantifies over a trace-certified predictor $S$, a cycle $t$, a represented domain containing $E_{S,t}$, and an $S$-internal closure map. The existential occurrence supplies no closure-map verdict, and the active-register theorem has no occurrence-negation premise. The two results therefore retain their stated statuses without either serving as a premise for the other: Foundational Certainty supplies the epistemic root, while Theorem A.6.2 supplies the same-cycle boundary.

### P.16c.7 Twisted-diagonal schema and adjacent obstruction modes

<a id="definition-p16c71-live-twisted-valuation-datum"></a>**Definition P.16c.7.1 (Live Twisted-Valuation Datum).** A live twisted-valuation datum is a tuple
$$
\mathfrak V=(X,V,g,o,D,r,\delta)
$$
where $X$ and $V$ are nonempty sets, $g:V\to V$ has no fixed point, $o:X\to V$ is the realized-value map, $\varnothing\ne D\subseteq X$, $r:D\to V$ is a candidate valuation row, and $\delta\in D$ satisfies
$$
o(\delta)=g(r(\delta)).
\tag{P.16c.7.1}
$$
The row is **veridical** when $r(x)=o(x)$ for every $x\in D$.

<a id="lemma-p16c72-twisted-diagonal-obstruction"></a>**Lemma P.16c.7.2 (Twisted-Diagonal Obstruction).** No live twisted-valuation datum has a veridical row.

*Proof.* If $r$ were veridical, then at the live witness
$$
r(\delta)=o(\delta)=g(r(\delta)),
$$
so $r(\delta)$ would be a fixed point of $g$, contrary to Definition P.16c.7.1. ∎

<a id="proposition-p16c73-registered-twisted-diagonal-instances"></a>**Proposition P.16c.7.3 (Registered Twisted-Diagonal Instances).** The contradiction step in each result listed below is an instance of Lemma P.16c.7.2 on the stated data. All domain, representation, closure, timing, and intervention hypotheses remain those of the owning result.

| Owning result | Value set and twist | Candidate row and live witness |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Theorem 10; Theorem A.1.1 | $V=\{0,1\}$ and $g=\operatorname{NOT}$ | the nominated predictor's announced-bit row; $\delta=D(P)$ or $S_{\mathrm{diag}}^{P}$ |
| Theorem 10a | $V=\{0,1\}$ and $g=\tau$ | $r(x)=\operatorname{eval}(a_d,x)$, $o(x)=d(x)$, and $\delta=a_d$ |
| Theorem 11; Theorem A.1.3 | $V=[0,1]$ and $g(p)=0$ for $p>1/2$, $g(p)=1$ for $p\le1/2$ | the reported-marginal row; $\delta=S_{\mathrm{diag}}^{P}$ |
| Theorem A.6.2 | $V=\{0,1\}$ and $g=\operatorname{NOT}$ | a total standard-sound Boolean closure row; $\delta=E_{S,t}$ |
| Theorem 14.1 | $V=\{0,1\}$ and $g=\operatorname{NOT}$ | the transcript-output row on the support of the diagonal-policy experiment; $\delta$ is any realized transcript under policy (14.1b) |
| Theorem P.3.5.9, encoded branch | $V=\{0,1\}$ and $g=\operatorname{NOT}$ | the nominated binary-component row of the putative uniformly correct predictive-specification procedure; $\delta$ is the member constructed by Lemma P.3.5.4 |

*Proof.* The deterministic SPAP constructions set the realized bit to the negation of the announced bit at the nominated diagonal member. Predicate-realization closure in Theorem 10a gives $r=o=d$, while $d(a_d)=\tau(\operatorname{eval}(a_d,a_d))=\tau(r(a_d))$. For the probabilistic construction, the displayed $g$ has no fixed point: $p>1/2$ gives $g(p)=0\ne p$, while $p\le1/2$ gives $g(p)=1\ne p$. Equation (A.3) supplies the live witness. In Theorem A.6.2, totality restricts the closure row to $\{0,1\}$ and standard soundness makes it agree with the standard truth value, while Equation A.5.6a.3 supplies the Boolean twist at $E_{S,t}$. Under Theorem 14.1's intervention-stability hypothesis, policy (14.1b) supplies the live equation at every realized transcript in its support. Lemma P.16c.7.2 therefore gives pointwise disagreement throughout that support, so the agreement probability is zero and contradicts (14.1a) for every $\epsilon<1$. Lemma P.3.5.4 supplies the same Boolean diagonal member for the encoded branch of Theorem P.3.5.9. Lemma P.16c.7.2 gives each remaining contradiction after those owning hypotheses are instantiated. ∎

<a id="remark-p16c74-adjacent-obstruction-modes"></a>**Remark P.16c.7.4 (Adjacent Obstruction Modes).** Theorem P.14.9h uses a fresh zero-ary predicate and two model expansions to prove model-theoretic underdetermination; it requires no fixed-point-free endomap. The unfolded branch of Theorem P.3.5.9 uses the proper-component well-foundedness obstruction of Theorem P.3.5.5; it requires no valuation row. These two modes remain independently typed and adjacent to the twisted-diagonal schema. Their coexistence does not enlarge the quantifier domain of any of the three arguments.

### P.16c.8 Certified finite diagonal ladder

<a id="definition-p16c81-certified-finite-diagonal-ladder"></a>**Definition P.16c.8.1 (Certified Finite Diagonal Ladder).** A certified finite diagonal ladder of height $N\ge1$ is a finite record
$$
\mathfrak L_N
=
\left(
\{(S_n,t_n,E_n)\}_{n=0}^{N},
\{W_n\}_{n=0}^{N-1}
\right)
\tag{P.16c.8.1}
$$
with the following properties.

1. Each $S_n$ is trace-certified and $E_n=E_{S_n,t_n}$ is the live diagonal sentence of Definition A.6.1 for the represented cycle $(S_n,t_n)$.
2. Each $W_n$ is a finite checked witness for one of the two constructions in Theorem A.5.6a.4: either an external processor with the access and evaluation data of Equations A.5.6a.5--A.5.6a.6, or a faithful historical record and later evaluation satisfying Equations A.5.6a.7--A.5.6a.8.
3. The verified result supplied by $W_n$ is retained and available before the cycle $t_{n+1}$ is evaluated. The next triple $(S_{n+1},t_{n+1},E_{n+1})$ is separately trace-certified; predecessor access does not identify $E_{n+1}$ with $E_n$.

A rung carries a stable axiom-stabilizer only when the independent hypotheses of Theorem A.6.4 are certified for that rung.

<a id="theorem-p16c82-rungwise-accessibility-and-persistent-live-boundary"></a>**Theorem P.16c.8.2 (Rungwise Accessibility and Persistent Live Boundary).** Every certified finite diagonal ladder satisfies:

1. for each $n<N$, the predecessor sentence $E_n$ is processed by the external or historical witness $W_n$ and its verified result is available at rung $n+1$;
2. for every $n\le N$, no $S_n$-internal finite-cycle closure map is both total and standard-sound on a domain containing $E_n$;
3. every rung satisfying all hypotheses of Theorem A.6.4 induces a stable axiom-stabilizer on its retained finite-response domain; and
4. the final sentence $E_N$ remains subject to item 2. The finite ladder record supplies no total standard-sound closure map on a union domain.

*Proof.* Item 1 is Theorem A.5.6a.4 applied to the checked alternative recorded by $W_n$, together with Definition P.16c.8.1(3). Item 2 is Theorem A.6.2 applied independently to each trace-certified pair $(S_n,t_n)$. Item 3 is Theorem A.6.4 on exactly those rungs carrying its hypotheses. Applying item 2 at $n=N$ proves the first sentence of item 4. Definition P.16c.8.1 records only the finitely many rungwise maps and successor witnesses; it defines no union-domain closure map, so no such map is supplied by the ladder construction. ∎

## P.16d Operational Program Modules from the Finite-Response Quotient

### P.16d.0 Standing and Scope

This section records twenty operational program modules generated by the finite-response PPI/PCE quotient already developed in Section P.6.1b. The modules introduce no new primitive, no new physical degree of freedom, no new numerical prediction, and no promotion in the Global Strict-Certificate Ledger. A module has physical effect only when it changes a finite protocol-response presheaf, lowers an already-defined PPI/PCE cost, supplies a certificate accepted by the existing ledger, or records an explicitly retained finite branch degeneracy.

The common source is the same finite operational quotient used in Theorem P.6.1b.3, Theorem P.6.1b.7, Theorem P.6.1b.8a, Corollary P.6.1b.8, and Corollary P.6.1b.8b.

<a id="definition-p16d01-finite-predictive-budget"></a>**Definition P.16d.0.1 (Finite Predictive Budget).** A finite predictive budget is a tuple
$$
B=(\mathsf P_B,\Omega_B,q_B,\eta_B,\vartheta_B,\mathcal L_B)
$$
where:

1. $\mathsf P_B$ is a finite subcategory of MPU-admissible protocols.
2. Each $P\in\mathsf P_B$ has a finite retained outcome set $\Omega_{B,P}$.
3. $q_{B,P}$ is the retained coarse-graining or resolution map from the raw outcome record of $P$ to $\Omega_{B,P}$.
4. $\eta_B(P)\ge0$ is the retained operational tolerance for protocol $P$.
5. $\vartheta_{B,P}:\Delta(\Omega_{B,P})\to T_{B,P}$ is a registered tolerance quotient map onto a finite or compact response space $T_{B,P}$, with each fiber having $d_{TV}$-diameter at most $\eta_B(P)$. For every protocol arrow $f:P'\to P$ and admitted candidate $X$, register an induced map $T_{X,B}(f):T_{B,P}\to T_{B,P'}$ such that, on the admitted response-law domain,
   $$
   T_{X,B}(f)\circ\vartheta_{B,P}\circ(q_{B,P})_*
   =
   \vartheta_{B,P'}\circ(q_{B,P'})_*\circ\mathcal R_X(f).
   $$
   These maps satisfy the identity and contravariant composition laws and are the arrow maps of $\mathcal R_X^B$. A candidate without these data is outside the budget-level presheaf domain.
6. $\mathcal L_B$ is the finite PPI/PCE cost ledger restricted to the protocols, resolutions, tolerance quotients, and certificate data in $B$.

For a PPI-admissible candidate $X$, its raw retained $B$-response and tolerance-quotiented $B$-response are
$$
\widehat{\mathcal R}_X^B(P)
=
(q_{B,P})_*\mathcal R_X(P),
\qquad
\mathcal R_X^B(P)
=
\vartheta_{B,P}\!\left(\widehat{\mathcal R}_X^B(P)\right),
\qquad P\in\mathsf P_B.
\tag{P.16d.0.1}
$$

Two candidates are $B$-equivalent, written
$$
X\sim_B Y,
$$
when their tolerance-quotiented response presheaves are naturally isomorphic and all retained update, verification, and certificate maps agree after the same quotient:
$$
\mathcal R_X^B\simeq\mathcal R_Y^B
\quad
\text{and}
\quad
U_X^B=U_Y^B,\ V_X^B=V_Y^B,\ C_X^B=C_Y^B
\quad
\text{in the retained quotient.}
\tag{P.16d.0.2}
$$
This is an equivalence relation because it is equality or natural isomorphism after fixed quotient maps, not a raw threshold-neighborhood relation.

The finite predictive quotient is
$$
Q_B(\mathcal A)=\mathcal A/{\sim_B}
\tag{P.16d.0.3}
$$
for any admissible candidate family $\mathcal A$.

<a id="definition-p16d02-retained-program-module"></a>**Definition P.16d.0.2 (Retained Program Module).** A retained program module is a rule assigning to each finite predictive budget $B$:

1. a finite candidate family $\mathcal A_B$ or compact finite-response closure of such a family;
2. a quotient $Q_B(\mathcal A_B)$;
3. a descended nonnegative cost
$$
\bar{\mathcal L}_B:Q_B(\mathcal A_B)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\cup\{+\infty\};
$$
4. a status map into the existing theorem, branch, certificate-pending, model-layer, or conjectural ledger.

A retained module is conservative when it does not alter any accepted physical branch unless one of the following changes is supplied: a finite response presheaf, a descended cost, a certificate object, an overlap-commutativity proof, or a finite branch-degeneracy record.

<a id="theorem-p16d03-finite-response-module-master-lemma"></a>**Theorem P.16d.0.3 (Finite-Response Module Master Lemma).** Let $B$ be a finite predictive budget and let $\mathcal A_B$ be a nonempty finite candidate family, or more generally a nonempty compact finite-response closure of a raw finite-code family as in Theorem P.6.1b.8a. Suppose $\bar{\mathcal L}_B$ is the descended PPI/PCE cost on $Q_B(\mathcal A_B)$, equipped with the quotient finite-response topology. Then:

1. $Q_B(\mathcal A_B)$ is finite or compact in the finite-response topology.
2. $\bar{\mathcal L}_B$ attains a minimum whenever it is lower semicontinuous and finite on at least one quotient class.
3. A label, field, branch tag, coordinate, interpretation, or auxiliary variable that changes no $B$-response presheaf and no retained update, verification, or certificate map does not create an additional quotient point. PCE strictly excludes a representative carrying it only when an admitted equivalent comparator has a strictly smaller complete representative cost. Equal-cost representations require a separate tie convention for choosing one presentation.
4. Under the scalar strict-convexity branch of Theorem P.6.1b.7, the scalar-cost minimum is unique up to $B$-equivalence. Under its lexicographic branch, the sequential lexicographic minimizer of $(L_{\mathrm{viol}},L_{\mathrm{regret}},L_{\mathrm{desc}})$ is unique up to $B$-equivalence.
5. If the applicable nondegeneracy condition fails, equal-cost multiplicity among distinct quotient points is recorded as a finite-response branch degeneracy, not hidden physical surplus. It is a finite-cardinality degeneracy only when the relevant quotient or minimizer set is finite, or when an accepted certificate supplies a finite degeneracy record.

*Proof.* If $\mathcal A_B$ is finite, its quotient is finite. On the compact branch, use the hypothesized compact finite-response closure of complete retained records, including the presheaf arrow maps and the update, verification, and certificate data used by $\sim_B$. Equip $Q_B(\mathcal A_B)$ with the stated quotient topology. Its canonical projection is continuous and surjective, so $Q_B(\mathcal A_B)$ is compact. The product $\prod_{P\in\mathsf P_B}T_{B,P}$ describes object-response coordinates only; it certifies compactness of the complete record space only when the remaining retained data are included in a compact carrier with closed admissibility conditions or are supplied continuously by those coordinates. This proves item 1.

For item 2, the finite case is immediate because a real-valued function on a nonempty finite set attains its minimum. In the compact case, choose a class $q_0$ with $\bar{\mathcal L}_B(q_0)<+\infty$ and put
$$
m=\inf_{q\in Q_B(\mathcal A_B)}\bar{\mathcal L}_B(q).
$$
Then $m\le\bar{\mathcal L}_B(q_0)<+\infty$ and $m\ge0$. For each $n\ge1$, the sublevel
$$
F_n=
\left\{q:\bar{\mathcal L}_B(q)\le m+\frac1n\right\}
$$
is nonempty by the definition of $m$, closed by lower semicontinuity, and nested. Compactness gives $q_*\in\bigcap_{n\ge1}F_n$, and therefore
$$
\bar{\mathcal L}_B(q_*)\le m+\frac1n
$$
for every $n$. Hence $\bar{\mathcal L}_B(q_*)=m$.

A response-null addition changes neither the quotient point nor its retained maps. An admitted equivalent representative with strictly smaller complete cost excludes the more expensive representative by Corollary P.6.1a.4; a tie gives no strict preference. This proves item 3 in its representative-comparison scope. On the scalar branch, Theorem P.6.1b.7 applies to the descended quotient and gives its unique minimizer under the stated strict-convexity hypotheses. On the lexicographic branch, sequential minimization and injectivity of the cost triple give the unique lexicographic minimizer under that theorem's hypotheses. This proves item 4. Without the corresponding nondegeneracy hypothesis, distinct quotient points may have equal cost. Theorem P.6.1b.8a records that multiplicity as response-branch degeneracy; compactness alone does not make it finite. Cardinal finiteness requires the additional alternatives in item 5. ∎

<a id="corollary-p16d04-no-new-axiom-condition"></a>**Corollary P.16d.0.4 (No New Axiom Condition).** Any construction in Sections P.16d.1–P.16d.20 is admissible as a PU module only as a specialization of Definition P.16d.0.2 and Theorem P.16d.0.3.

*Proof.* Each module below is written as a rule on finite response presheaves, finite costs, update maps, verification maps, certificate commutativity, or finite branch degeneracy. Those are exactly the retained data of Definition P.16d.0.2. Since Theorem P.16d.0.3 supplies the quotient and selection rule, no additional axiom is used. ∎

---

### P.16d.1 Predictive Renormalization Group

<a id="definition-p16d11-predictive-renormalization-group-flow"></a>**Definition P.16d.1.1 (Predictive Renormalization Group Flow).** Let $B_1$ and $B_2$ be finite predictive budgets. Write
$$
B_2\preceq B_1
$$
when $B_2$ is no finer than $B_1$: every retained $B_2$ protocol, outcome, tolerance quotient, update, verification, certificate datum, and cost comparison is obtained from $B_1$ by deleting protocols, coarse-graining outcomes, enlarging tolerances through registered quotient maps, or discarding response-null cost coordinates. Equivalently, the coarsening is required to satisfy
$$
X\sim_{B_1}Y
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
X\sim_{B_2}Y.
$$

For $B_2\preceq B_1$, define the predictive renormalization map
$$
\Phi_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}:Q_{B_1}(\mathcal A)\to Q_{B_2}(\mathcal A)
\tag{P.16d.1.1}
$$
by
$$
\Phi_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}([X]_{B_1})=[X]_{B_2}.
$$

A distinction between $X$ and $Y$ is:

1. $B$-retained if $X\not\sim_B Y$;
2. $B$-irrelevant if $X\sim_B Y$;
3. cross-budget forced on a budget family $\mathcal B$ if it is retained by every quotient map in $\mathcal B$ and is invariant under all defined PRG flows.

<a id="theorem-p16d12-prg-functoriality-and-response-survival-criterion"></a>**Theorem P.16d.1.2 (PRG Functoriality and Response-Survival Criterion).** The maps $\Phi_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}$ are well-defined and satisfy
$$
\Phi_{B\leftarrow B}=\operatorname{id}_{Q_B},
\qquad
\Phi_{B_3\leftarrow B_2}\circ\Phi_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}
=
\Phi_{B_3\leftarrow B_1}
$$
whenever $B_3\preceq B_2\preceq B_1$. A distinction has physical content at budget $B$ exactly when it survives as a nontrivial distinction in $Q_B$, changes a retained update or verification map, supplies an accepted certificate role, or lowers the descended cost in $Q_B$.

*Proof.* If $X\sim_{B_1}Y$, the defining compatibility of $B_2\preceq B_1$ gives $X\sim_{B_2}Y$, so $\Phi_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}$ is independent of representative. The identity and composition equations follow from applying the same representative $X$ and then taking the appropriate quotient class. The final statement is Corollary P.6.1b.8 and Corollary P.6.1b.8b applied to $Q_B$: a distinction that changes no retained response or map, supplies no certificate role, and lowers no cost is quotient-null; the listed alternatives are exactly the retained channels. ∎

<a id="definition-p16d12a-finite-self-resolution-ratio"></a>**Definition P.16d.1.2a (Finite Self-Resolution Ratio).** Let $\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}$ be a registered finite family of complete self-description candidates, each carrying every response, update, verification, certificate, and cost datum required by Definition P.16d.0.1, and assume
$$
2\le|\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}|<\infty.
$$
Restrict $\sim_B$ to this family and define
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{S,B}(\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}})
:=
\frac{\log|\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}/{\sim_B}|}
{\log|\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}|}.
\tag{P.16d.1.3}
$$
The ratio is relative to the registered candidate family; values on different families are not comparable without a registered inclusion, weighting, or transport map.

<a id="theorem-p16d12b-self-resolution-bounds-and-prg-monotonicity"></a>**Theorem P.16d.1.2b (Self-Resolution Bounds and PRG Monotonicity).** For every family in Definition P.16d.1.2a,
$$
0\le\operatorname{Res}_{S,B}(\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}})\le1.
\tag{P.16d.1.4}
$$
The upper equality holds exactly when every $\sim_B$-class in $\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}$ is a singleton. The lower equality holds exactly when every candidate belongs to one $\sim_B$-class.

If $B_2\preceq B_1$ and the same candidate family is admissible under both budgets, then
$$
\operatorname{Res}_{S,B_2}(\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}})
\le
\operatorname{Res}_{S,B_1}(\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}).
\tag{P.16d.1.5}
$$

*Proof.* A quotient of a nonempty finite set has between one and the cardinality of that set many classes. Taking logarithms and dividing by the positive denominator in (P.16d.1.3) proves (P.16d.1.4). Equality at the upper endpoint means that the quotient has as many classes as elements, which is equivalent to every class being a singleton. Equality at the lower endpoint means that the quotient has one class.

For $B_2\preceq B_1$, Definition P.16d.1.1 gives
$$
X\sim_{B_1}Y\Longrightarrow X\sim_{B_2}Y.
$$
Therefore
$$
[X]_{B_1}\longmapsto[X]_{B_2}
$$
defines a surjection
$$
\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}/{\sim_{B_1}}
\twoheadrightarrow
\mathscr X_S^{\mathrm{self}}/{\sim_{B_2}}.
$$
The coarser quotient has no more classes. The denominator of (P.16d.1.3) is unchanged because the candidate family is fixed, so (P.16d.1.5) follows. ∎

---

### P.16d.2 Finite-Channel Covariance

<a id="definition-p16d21-finite-channel-equivalence"></a>**Definition P.16d.2.1 (Finite-Channel Equivalence).** Two finite predictive presentations $(B,\mathcal A,\mathcal R,\bar{\mathcal L})$ and $(B',\mathcal A',\mathcal R',\bar{\mathcal L}')$ are finite-channel equivalent when there are:

1. a protocol equivalence $F:\mathsf P_B\to\mathsf P_{B'}$;
2. finite stochastic isomorphisms of retained outcome distributions compatible with the tolerance quotient maps;
3. a bijection of quotient classes
$$
\Xi:Q_B(\mathcal A)\to Q_{B'}(\mathcal A')
$$
such that
$$
\mathcal R_{\Xi([X])}^{B'}(F(P))\simeq\mathcal R_X^B(P)
$$
for all retained protocols $P$, all retained update, verification, and certificate maps are transported to their counterparts, and
$$
\bar{\mathcal L}'(\Xi([X]))=\bar{\mathcal L}([X]).
$$

A law, constraint, or selection rule is finite-channel covariant when it is invariant under every finite-channel equivalence.

<a id="theorem-p16d22-finite-channel-covariance-of-ppipce-content"></a>**Theorem P.16d.2.2 (Finite-Channel Covariance of PPI/PCE Content).** Any physical claim expressible solely in terms of finite response presheaves, natural transformations, descended PPI/PCE costs, retained update or verification maps, or accepted certificate commutativity is finite-channel covariant.

*Proof.* A finite-channel equivalence preserves the response presheaves up to finite stochastic isomorphism, transports the retained maps, and preserves the descended cost. Therefore truth of any statement depending only on those preserved data is invariant under $\Xi$. Natural transformations are transported by conjugation with $F$ and the stochastic isomorphisms, preserving commutative diagrams. Certificate commutativity is equality in the retained quotient, which is preserved by $\Xi$. Hence PPI/PCE content does not depend on encoding, representation, observer protocol labels, or resolution labels when the finite response content is preserved. ∎

---

### P.16d.3 Anomaly-as-Paradox-Residue

<a id="definition-p16d31-paradox-residue"></a>**Definition P.16d.3.1 (Paradox Residue).** For a candidate branch $X$ at budget $B$, define its paradox residue as the tuple
$$
\mathfrak R_B(X)
=
(r_{\mathrm{nat}},r_{\mathrm{viol}},r_{\mathrm{SPAP}},r_{\mathrm{cert}},r_{\mathrm{sur}})
\tag{P.16d.3.1}
$$
where:

1. $r_{\mathrm{nat}}=0$ exactly when $\mathcal R_X^B$ is a natural presheaf on $\mathsf P_B$.
2. $r_{\mathrm{viol}}=0$ exactly when the branch violates no already-derived PU constraint in the retained ledger.
3. $r_{\mathrm{SPAP}}=0$ exactly when the branch asserts no unindexed single predictor that is uniformly exact over a diagonal-closed constructible class, no semantic role collapse, and no closure forbidden by the stated SPAP/RUD hypotheses. Exact readout on a nominated particular instance is not excluded by SPAP alone.
4. $r_{\mathrm{cert}}=0$ exactly when every certificate overlap square required for the claimed status commutes.
5. $r_{\mathrm{sur}}=0$ exactly when all response-null surplus has been quotiented or removed by PCE.

The total residue is zero when all five components vanish.

<a id="theorem-p16d32-residue-descent-equivalence"></a>**Theorem P.16d.3.2 (Residue-Descent Equivalence).** Relative to the finite budget $B$ and claimed status level $s$, suppose a candidate branch has complete retained response data, retained update and verification maps, and every certificate object required by status $s$ is present in the finite ledger. Then the candidate descends to an admissible finite-response PU branch at status $s$ exactly when its paradox residue is zero at the corresponding budget and certificate level.

*Proof.* If the branch descends, its response object is a natural presheaf by Definition P.6.1b.1; it satisfies the constraints required for admission; it asserts no uniformly exact predictor or closure forbidden on the declared diagonal-closed class and no role collapse forbidden by the semantic role indexing of Section P.16b; its status certificates must commute by Convention P.14.1k and the strict-certificate rules; and response-null surplus is removed by Corollary P.6.1b.8. Hence all residue components vanish.

Conversely, if all residue components vanish and the stated finite data are complete, $\mathcal R_X^B$ is a natural finite response presheaf, the branch violates no retained PU constraint, no SPAP/RUD obstruction is invoked, the certificate overlaps needed for status $s$ commute, and no surplus remains. Theorem P.6.1b.8a then places the branch in the admissible finite operational quotient. Theorem P.16d.0.3 supplies selection over that comparison class under its attainment and applicable nondegeneracy hypotheses; admission alone does not make every nominated candidate a minimizer. Thus the branch descends as an admissible branch relative to $B$ and $s$. ∎

---

### P.16d.4 Operational Naturalness

<a id="definition-p16d41-operational-naturalness"></a>**Definition P.16d.4.1 (Operational Naturalness).** Let $\lambda_B:Q_B(\mathcal A)\to\Lambda_B$ be a retained finite coordinate, parameter, or bridge-normalization readout. It is operationally natural on a budget family $\mathcal B$ when for every $B_2\preceq B_1$ in $\mathcal B$ there exists a deterministic finite map $\rho_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}$ such that
$$
\lambda_{B_2}(\Phi_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}([X]_{B_1}))
=
\rho_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}(\lambda_{B_1}([X]_{B_1}))
\tag{P.16d.4.1}
$$
for every retained class $[X]$, and the code length of the transition rule $\rho_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}$ is bounded on $\mathcal B$.

A parameter is operationally fine-tuned at $B$ when retaining it requires additional precision or description length that changes no finite response, changes no retained map, supplies no certificate role, and lowers no cost in $Q_B$.

<a id="theorem-p16d42-naturalness-equals-prg-stable-response-content"></a>**Theorem P.16d.4.2 (Naturalness Equals PRG-Stable Response Content).** On a strict finite PCE branch, operationally natural parameters are exactly the finite response coordinates that survive PRG flow with bounded transition description. Operationally fine-tuned precision is removed unless it changes a finite response, changes a retained map, lowers a cost, or is protected by a certificate.

*Proof.* If $\lambda$ is operationally natural, Equation (P.16d.4.1) says its coarser-budget value is determined by its finer-budget value under the PRG flow; hence it survives quotienting as response content with bounded description. Conversely, if a response coordinate survives every PRG flow in the family and its transition rule has bounded description, define $\rho_{B_2\leftarrow B_1}$ by the induced quotient map; this gives (P.16d.4.1). If additional precision changes no finite response, changes no retained map, supplies no certificate role, and lowers no cost, it is response-null surplus and is removed by Corollary P.6.1b.8. If it changes a response, changes a retained map, lowers cost, or is certificate-protected, it is not fine-tuned in this operational sense but retained as response, map, cost, or certificate data. ∎

---

### P.16d.5 Context-State Tomography

<a id="definition-p16d51-context-state-tomography-map"></a>**Definition P.16d.5.1 (Context-State Tomography Map).** Let $S$ be an MPU aggregate with context space $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ctx}}$ as in Definition L.1. For a finite intervention family $\mathsf I_B$ and finite readout protocols $\mathsf O_B$, define
$$
\Theta_{S,B}:\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ctx}}\to
\prod_{I\in\mathsf I_B,\ O\in\mathsf O_B}\Delta(\Omega_{I,O})
\tag{P.16d.5.1}
$$
by
$$
\Theta_{S,B}(c)_{I,O}
=
\Pr_S(\cdot\mid I,O,c).
$$
Equip the product with the retained pseudometric
$$
d_B^\Theta(c,c')
=
\max_{I\in\mathsf I_B,\ O\in\mathsf O_B}
d_{TV}\!\left(\Theta_{S,B}(c)_{I,O},\Theta_{S,B}(c')_{I,O}\right).
$$
Let $\vartheta_B^\Theta$ be the product tolerance quotient induced by the retained tolerance maps. The tomographic context quotient is
$$
\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ctx}}/{\sim_{\Theta,B}},
\qquad
c\sim_{\Theta,B}c'
\Longleftrightarrow
\vartheta_B^\Theta(\Theta_{S,B}(c))
=
\vartheta_B^\Theta(\Theta_{S,B}(c')).
\tag{P.16d.5.2}
$$

<a id="theorem-p16d52-tomographic-identifiability-criterion"></a>**Theorem P.16d.5.2 (Tomographic Identifiability Criterion).** A finite context-state tomography protocol always reconstructs at most the retained operational context class
$$
[c]_{\Theta,B}\in \mathcal C_{\mathrm{ctx}}/{\sim_{\Theta,B}}.
$$
It reconstructs a unique raw context state $c$ from the retained data if and only if
$$
\vartheta_B^\Theta\circ\Theta_{S,B}:\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ctx}}\to \prod_{I,O}T_{B,I,O}
$$
is injective on the candidate context domain under consideration. If this map is not injective, the protocol reconstructs only the quotient class $[c]_{\Theta,B}$.

*Proof.* By Definition P.16d.5.1, two contexts are identified exactly when their retained intervention-readout distributions agree after the registered tolerance quotient. Hence all observations in the finite protocol determine only the equivalence class $[c]_{\Theta,B}$. If the retained tomography map is injective on the candidate context domain, equality of retained responses implies equality of raw contexts, so the class contains one raw context. If injectivity fails, there are distinct contexts with the same retained finite response; no protocol in $\mathsf I_B,\mathsf O_B$ separates them at budget $B$, and selecting one of them adds response-null surplus. PCE therefore retains the quotient class and, when a minimum exists, a minimal sufficient representative within that class by Definition L.1 and Theorem P.16d.0.3. ∎

---

### P.16d.6 Thermodynamic Privacy and Reflexive Opacity

<a id="definition-p16d61-transparency-protocol"></a>**Definition P.16d.6.1 (Transparency Protocol).** Let $S$ be a Property-R aggregate with self-model $\mathcal M_S$. A transparency protocol at tolerance $\eta$ is a finite protocol $T$ that attempts to reconstruct a retained self-context coordinate $z(\mathcal M_S)$ while leaving the operational response class of $S$ unchanged within $\eta$ and paying finite cost $C_T$.

It is perfect when $\eta=0$, the reconstruction is complete for all retained self-context coordinates, $C_T=0$, and the protocol produces no retained disturbance of the response class.

<a id="theorem-p16d62-registered-reset-cost-bound-for-self-context-readout"></a>**Theorem P.16d.6.2 (Registered-Reset Cost Bound for Self-Context Readout).** Let a self-context readout be followed by a registered reset satisfying
$$
\Delta I\ge\Delta I_{\min}>0,
\qquad
H_q(P\mid R)\ge h_{\min}>0.
$$
Then
$$
\Delta I\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}
\ge\Delta I_{\min}h_{\min}>0,
\tag{P.16d.6.2}
$$
where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}=\langle Q_{\mathrm{bath}}\rangle/(k_BT)$. Consequently, a zero-bath-heat reset cannot satisfy both positive floors on this branch. The result neither proves retained-state disturbance nor excludes complete reconstruction; those require separate channel or representation certificates.

*Proof.* This is Proposition 15, equivalently Theorem 33 on the registered-reset branch, with the two positive lower bounds substituted into its reset-heat inequality. $\square$

<a id="definition-p16d62a-budget-relative-self-description-trace"></a>**Definition P.16d.6.2a (Budget-Relative Self-Description Trace).** Let $S$ satisfy the Effective Operational Property R and self-model domain conditions of Definition M.10.1 and Remark M.10.1. Fix a retained self-model parameter domain $\Theta_{S,B}$, a finite ordered time window $W$, a registered trajectory $\theta_S:W\to\Theta_{S,B}$, a registered admissible candidate family $\mathcal A_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}$ serving as the candidate component of a retained program module in Definition P.16d.0.2, and a complete self-description encoder
$$
X_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}:\Theta_{S,B}\longrightarrow\mathcal A_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}},
\tag{P.16d.6.3}
$$
where every candidate in $\mathcal A_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}$ carries the retained content, response presheaf, update map, verification map, certificate map, decoder, tolerances, and complete cost required by the budget $B$. Define
$$
\mathsf{IdClass}_{S,B}(t)
:=
\left[X_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}(\theta_S(t))\right]_{\sim_B}.
\tag{P.16d.6.4}
$$
The self-description is $B$-persistent on $W$ when this quotient class is constant on $W$. If the candidate family, encoder, or quotient datum changes, persistence is defined only after a registered continuation map identifies the compared quotients.

<a id="theorem-p16d62b-persistence-is-retained-response-constancy"></a>**Theorem P.16d.6.2b (Persistence Is Retained Response Constancy).** If the self-description is $B$-persistent on $W$, then its retained response presheaves, update maps, verification maps, and certificate maps agree after the fixed $B$-quotient throughout $W$. Under this persistence hypothesis,
$$
\theta_S(t)=\theta_S(t')
\qquad\text{for all }t,t'\in W
$$
if and only if the composite
$$
\Theta_{S,B}
\xrightarrow{\ X_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}\ }
\mathcal A_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}
\longrightarrow
\mathcal A_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}/{\sim_B}
\tag{P.16d.6.5}
$$
is injective on the trajectory image $\theta_S(W)$.

*Proof.* Constancy of (P.16d.6.4) is equality under $\sim_B$. Definition P.16d.0.1 makes that equivalence exactly natural isomorphism of the tolerance-quotiented response presheaves together with agreement of the retained update, verification, and certificate maps, proving the first statement. If the composite (P.16d.6.5) is injective on the trajectory image, equality of quotient classes implies equality of the corresponding parameters. Conversely, if it is not injective on that image, two distinct trajectory parameters have the same quotient class, so $B$-persistence does not imply their equality. ∎

<a id="definition-p16d62c-audited-generative-self-description-frontier"></a>**Definition P.16d.6.2c (Audited Generative Self-Description Frontier).** Let $\mathscr A_{S,B}\subseteq\mathcal F_{S,B}$ be a nonempty finite audited role family and $\mathsf P_B^{\mathrm{audit}}$ a nonempty finite retained protocol family. Choose positive weights $a_{\mathfrak r}$ and $w_P$, and for each $P$ a metric $d_{B,P}$ on the natural-isomorphism classes of its tolerance-quotiented responses. Write $\mathcal R_{\mathfrak r}^B(P)$ for the retained response class of any representative of $\mathfrak r$; this is well defined by the budget-level quotient in Definition P.16b.9.1a.

Let $\mathcal G_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}$ be a registered candidate class. Each $m\in\mathcal G_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}$ has complete code, decoder, and evaluation cost $C_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}(m)\ge0$ and generates tolerance-quotiented responses $\mathcal R_{m,\mathrm{gen}}^B(\mathfrak r;P)$. Define
$$
D_{S,B}(m)
=
\sum_{\mathfrak r\in\mathscr A_{S,B}}a_{\mathfrak r}
\sum_{P\in\mathsf P_B^{\mathrm{audit}}}w_P
d_{B,P}\!\left(
\mathcal R_{\mathfrak r}^B(P),
\mathcal R_{m,\mathrm{gen}}^B(\mathfrak r;P)
\right).
\tag{P.16d.6.6}
$$
All weights are positive and all $d_{B,P}$ are metrics, so $D_{S,B}(m)=0$ exactly when every audited response is reproduced. Define
$$
K_{S,B}^{\mathrm{exact}}
:=
\inf\left\{
C_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}(m):
m\in\mathcal G_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}},\ D_{S,B}(m)=0
\right\},
\tag{P.16d.6.7}
$$
with $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$, and for a scalar cap $b\ge0$ in the units of $C_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}$ define
$$
D_{S,B}^*(b)
:=
\inf\left\{
D_{S,B}(m):
m\in\mathcal G_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}},\
C_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}(m)\le b
\right\}.
\tag{P.16d.6.8}
$$
Again $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$. The scalar $b$ is an auxiliary cost cap inside the fixed tuple budget $B$; it is not a replacement for $B$.
All occurrences of exactness in this definition mean exact equality in the retained tolerance quotient, not equality of discarded raw responses.

<a id="theorem-p16d62d-exact-generative-obstruction-and-cost-distortion-frontier"></a>**Theorem P.16d.6.2d (Exact Generative Obstruction and Cost-Distortion Frontier).** For every scalar cap $b$ in a declared interval, assume the sublevel
$$
\mathcal G_b
:=
\{m\in\mathcal G_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}:C_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}(m)\le b\}
$$
is nonempty and compact in the retained finite-response topology and $D_{S,B}$ is continuous on $\mathcal G_b$. Then:

1. $D_{S,B}^*(b)$ is attained;
2. $D_{S,B}^*(b)$ is non-increasing in $b$;
3. if $b<K_{S,B}^{\mathrm{exact}}$, then $D_{S,B}^*(b)>0$ and no exact audited self-description is feasible at cap $b$;
4. for every $\lambda_D>0$, each minimizer, if one exists, of
   $$
   C_{S,B}^{\mathrm{self}}(m)+\lambda_DD_{S,B}(m)
   \tag{P.16d.6.9}
   $$
   is Pareto-undominated in the registered cost and audited distortion.

*Proof.* Compactness of $\mathcal G_b$ and continuity of $D_{S,B}$ give attainment by the extreme-value theorem. If $b_1\le b_2$, then $\mathcal G_{b_1}\subseteq\mathcal G_{b_2}$, so taking an infimum over the larger set cannot increase the value. If $b<K_{S,B}^{\mathrm{exact}}$, an exact candidate in $\mathcal G_b$ would contradict (P.16d.6.7). By attainment, $D_{S,B}^*(b)=0$ would itself supply such an exact candidate, so $D_{S,B}^*(b)>0$. Finally, if a minimizer of (P.16d.6.9) were dominated by another candidate in both cost and distortion, with at least one strict inequality, positivity of $\lambda_D$ would make the dominating candidate's objective strictly smaller, a contradiction. ∎

<a id="remark-p16d62e-non-equivalence-of-self-limits"></a>**Remark P.16d.6.2e (Non-Equivalence of Self-Limits).** The quotient obstruction $D_{S,B}^*(b)>0$, the diagonal self-prediction obstruction of Theorems 10--11, and the registered-reset cost bound of Theorem P.16d.6.2 are distinct. None implies either of the others without a registered reduction. In particular, reset heat proves no noninjectivity, and enumerative code length larger than $C_P(S)$ does not prove a generative obstruction because one shared generator may reproduce many audited responses.

### P.16d.7 Perspective Curvature

<a id="definition-p16d71-predictive-transport-and-perspective-curvature"></a>**Definition P.16d.7.1 (Predictive Transport and Perspective Curvature).** Let $\{U_i\}_{i\in I}$ be a finite perspective cover. For every overlap with admissible translation, let
$$
T_{ij}:Q_{B,i}\to Q_{B,j}
$$
be the finite predictive transport map. For a cycle
$$
\gamma=(i_0,i_1,\dots,i_n=i_0),
$$
define the holonomy
$$
H_\gamma
=
T_{i_{n-1}i_n}\circ\cdots\circ T_{i_0i_1}.
\tag{P.16d.7.1}
$$
The perspective-curvature defect on $\gamma$ is the retained equalizer failure of $H_\gamma$ and $\operatorname{id}$, measured by
$$
\operatorname{curv}_\gamma([X])
=
d_{B,i_0}\!\left(H_\gamma([X]),[X]\right)
\tag{P.16d.7.2}
$$
for the retained response metric or pseudometric $d_{B,i_0}$ on $Q_{B,i_0}$.

<a id="theorem-p16d72-curvature-as-path-dependent-predictive-transport"></a>**Theorem P.16d.7.2 (Curvature as Path-Dependent Predictive Transport).** Let the overlap graph be connected, register reverse-edge transports as inverses, and register nonempty retained domains on which every path under consideration is defined and the overlap maps are compatible. For a nominated base class $x$, a path-independent global response section extending $x$ exists exactly when every cycle based there satisfies $H_\gamma(x)=x$. Path-independent transport for every class in the registered base domain is equivalent to identity holonomy on that domain. A nonzero discrepancy detects failure for the tested class when the retained distance separates the compared responses; zero pseudometric discrepancy alone gives only equality in its metric quotient.

*Proof.* A section extending $x$ must return $x$ after transport around each based cycle. Conversely, transport $x$ from the base along a path to each vertex. For two such paths, one followed by the inverse of the other forms a based cycle. Its action on $x$ is trivial by hypothesis, so the two transported values agree. The registered common domains ensure that both composites exist, and overlap compatibility gives the section. Applying this argument to every base class yields the identity-holonomy criterion for all-class path independence. The discrepancy statement follows from the distinction between a metric and a pseudometric. ∎

---

### P.16d.8 Observer Calibration Theory

<a id="definition-p16d81-calibration-kernel"></a>**Definition P.16d.8.1 (Calibration Kernel).** For predictive systems $S$ and $T$ at budget $B$, a calibration kernel is a pair of finite stochastic natural transformations
$$
K_{S\to T}^P:\Delta(\Omega_{B,P}^S)\to\Delta(\Omega_{B,P}^T),
\qquad
K_{T\to S}^P:\Delta(\Omega_{B,P}^T)\to\Delta(\Omega_{B,P}^S),
\qquad P\in\mathsf P_B,
$$
compatible with retained coarse-grainings and tolerance quotients. Its calibration error is
$$
\operatorname{cal}_B(S,T)
=
\sup_{P\in\mathsf P_B}
\left[
d_{TV}\left(K_{T\to S}^P K_{S\to T}^P\widehat{\mathcal R}_S^B(P),\widehat{\mathcal R}_S^B(P)\right)
+
d_{TV}\left(K_{S\to T}^P K_{T\to S}^P\widehat{\mathcal R}_T^B(P),\widehat{\mathcal R}_T^B(P)\right)
\right].
\tag{P.16d.8.1}
$$
The systems are calibrated at tolerance $\eta$ when $\operatorname{cal}_B(S,T)\le\eta$ and the tolerance-quotiented response classes agree.

<a id="theorem-p16d82-reproducibility-as-common-response-class"></a>**Theorem P.16d.8.2 (Reproducibility as Common Response Class).** A finite experiment is reproducible in the retained finite-response sense across a finite observer network with registered calibration kernels exactly when the observers' calibrated response presheaves have a nonempty common quotient class at the stated tolerance.

For the selection statement, let $\mathfrak N_{B,\eta}$ be a registered nonempty finite family of calibration networks realizing such a common class, and let
$$
\overline C_{B,\eta}:\mathfrak N_{B,\eta}\to(-\infty,+\infty]
$$
be the complete descended PCE cost, finite on at least one registered network. Then
$$
\operatorname*{argmin}_{N\in\mathfrak N_{B,\eta}}\overline C_{B,\eta}(N)\ne\varnothing,
$$
and PCE selects a member of this argmin. The selected network is unique only if the registered costs have a unique minimizer.

*Proof.* If a common quotient class exists, each observer's retained response can be transported into the same class by the calibration kernels, so the experiment has the same operational result across the network. If the experiment is reproducible, the observed results define a shared finite response class after calibration; otherwise at least one observer remains in a distinct quotient class and reproducibility fails. The finite family $\mathfrak N_{B,\eta}$ is nonempty, and at least one member has finite complete cost, so $\overline C_{B,\eta}$ attains its least value. This is the finite-family branch of Theorem P.16d.0.3. Uniqueness is equivalent to the argmin being a singleton. ∎

---

### P.16d.9 Horizon Tomography Beyond Gravity

<a id="definition-p16d91-finite-predictive-horizon"></a>**Definition P.16d.9.1 (Finite Predictive Horizon).** For a system $S$ and budget $B$, the finite predictive horizon is the kernel of the retained response map:
$$
\mathcal H_B(S)
=
\{(x,y):\mathcal R_x^B\simeq\mathcal R_y^B\}.
\tag{P.16d.9.1}
$$
A distinction lies beyond the $B$-horizon when it belongs to $\mathcal H_B(S)$, i.e. no protocol inside $B$ separates it after the retained tolerance quotient.

<a id="theorem-p16d92-horizon-as-kernel-of-accessible-distinction"></a>**Theorem P.16d.9.2 (Horizon as Kernel of Accessible Distinction).** Horizon tomography reconstructs the quotient by $\mathcal H_B(S)$ and cannot reconstruct distinctions inside $\mathcal H_B(S)$ without increasing the budget or adding a new separating protocol. If $B_2\preceq B_1$, then
$$
\mathcal H_{B_1}(S)\subseteq\mathcal H_{B_2}(S).
\tag{P.16d.9.2}
$$

*Proof.* By definition, $\mathcal H_B(S)$ identifies exactly the distinctions with identical retained response presheaves. Therefore the maximal reconstructable object is the quotient by that kernel. A distinction inside the kernel changes no retained finite response, so selecting it would be response-null surplus. If $B_2$ is coarser than $B_1$, the compatibility condition in Definition P.16d.1.1 gives $x\sim_{B_1}y\Rightarrow x\sim_{B_2}y$, proving the inclusion. ∎

---

### P.16d.10 PCE-Based Experiment Selection

<a id="definition-p16d101-experiment-value-functional"></a>**Definition P.16d.10.1 (Experiment Value Functional).** Let $\mathcal A_B$ be a finite set of admissible response classes with prior weights $\pi$. A finite experiment $e$ has cost
$$
C(e)>0
$$
and outcome partition $\mathcal P_e$ of $\mathcal A_B$. Let
$$
\mathcal H(\pi)=-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_B}\pi(a)\ln\pi(a)
$$
and let $\pi_{e,o}$ be the posterior over classes after outcome cell $o\in\mathcal P_e$, with $\Pr(o\mid e)=\sum_{a\in o}\pi(a)$ on the deterministic partition branch. The expected response-class reduction is
$$
\Delta\mathcal H_B(e)
=
\mathcal H(\pi)
-
\sum_o\Pr(o\mid e)\mathcal H(\pi_{e,o}).
\tag{P.16d.10.1}
$$
The PCE experiment value is
$$
\operatorname{EV}_B(e)=\frac{\Delta\mathcal H_B(e)}{C(e)}.
\tag{P.16d.10.2}
$$

<a id="theorem-p16d102-single-step-pce-experiment-rule"></a>**Theorem P.16d.10.2 (Single-Step PCE Experiment Rule).** Register a nonempty finite experiment menu with positive finite costs and adopt $\operatorname{EV}_B$ as the complete single-step objective for response-class information gain per unit cost. A maximizer exists and is optimal for that registered ratio objective.

*Proof.* The finite prior and outcome partitions give finite expected entropy reductions. Division by each positive finite cost is defined, and a real-valued function on a nonempty finite menu attains its maximum. This proves optimality for the declared ratio. Identifying that ranking with another PCE ledger, such as cost minus weighted information benefit, requires a separate order-equivalence certificate. ∎

<a id="remark-p16d103-executed-comparison-of-selection-rules"></a>**Remark P.16d.10.3 (Executed Comparison of Selection Rules).** The rule of Theorem P.16d.10.2, with each candidate law its own response class, was run on synthetic law-identification tasks against two alternatives: expected reduction of the held-out Brier loss per unit cost, and a uniformly random affordable experiment. Each task supplied a finite dictionary of candidate laws with uniform prior weights ($147$ controlled modular dynamics, $64$ three-bit controlled circuits or $48$ discretized damped oscillators), experiment costs $1$, $2$ or $4$ (tripled for full-state circuit readouts), observation budgets $2$, $4$ and $8$, and $192$ held-out multi-step prediction questions. Observations were exact or replaced by a wrong category with probability $0.12$, the noisy case using the corresponding likelihood, and each condition had $40$ seeds shared by the three rules. At budget $4$, averaged over the six family and noise conditions, the held-out Brier loss was $0.141$ for $\operatorname{EV}_B$, $0.146$ for loss reduction and $0.346$ for random experiments; the paired difference between $\operatorname{EV}_B$ and loss reduction was $-0.005$, with $95\%$ seed-bootstrap interval $[-0.029,0.020]$, and between random experiments and $\operatorname{EV}_B$ it was $0.205$ $[0.167,0.241]$. On the three exact-observation conditions, which form the deterministic-partition branch of Definition P.16d.10.1, the three losses were $0.095$, $0.091$ and $0.289$. When the true oscillator law carried a cubic term absent from every candidate, $\operatorname{EV}_B$ at budget $8$ answered $17.2\%$ of the questions wrongly with confidence at least $0.9$, against $5.0\%$ for random experiments, and its Brier loss was $0.375$ against $0.323$. The run validates the rule as a selector on finite admitted classes that contain the true law; the misspecified case measures the effect of a true law outside $\mathcal A_B$, the hidden-competitor condition of Theorem 22c.

---

### P.16d.11 Self-Reference Spectroscopy

<a id="definition-p16d111-reflexive-burden-spectrum"></a>**Definition P.16d.11.1 (Reflexive Burden Spectrum).** Let $S$ be a self-modeling system and let $(\tau_{\mathrm{ext}},\tau_{\mathrm{self}})$ be a matched task pair with a declared matching map for all nonreflexive load. If the self task contains a separately identified introspective subprotocol, define
$$
\mathcal B_S(\tau_{\mathrm{self}},\tau_{\mathrm{ext}})
=
(\Delta E,\Delta t,\Delta N,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}^{\mathrm{int}},\Delta C),
\tag{P.16d.11.1}
$$
where $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}^{\mathrm{int}}$ is the dimensionless bath heat of the disjoint registered resets in that subprotocol and the other entries are the retained matched differences in energy, latency, noise, and process complexity. A generic total-entropy-production difference is not identified with this coordinate.

<a id="theorem-p16d112-registered-reset-spectroscopic-bound"></a>**Theorem P.16d.11.2 (Registered-Reset Spectroscopic Bound).** Suppose the isolated introspective subprotocol obtains $\Delta I\ge\Delta I_{\min}>0$ nats and contains at least one charged registered reset. Require the resets to be disjoint, to satisfy the implementation hypotheses of Theorem 33, and to obey $H_q(P\mid R)\ge h_{\min}>0$ in their common dimensionless heat normalization. Then
$$
\Delta I\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}^{\mathrm{int}}
\ge\Delta I_{\min}h_{\min}=: \kappa_r,
\qquad
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}^{\mathrm{int}}
\ge\kappa_r/\Delta I.
$$
No lower bound on a generic entropy-production difference follows without an additional source-exhaustive ledger-identification inequality. If all entries of $\mathcal B_S$ vanish, this spectrum records no burden difference at the stated budget; full operational equivalence follows only if the registered spectrum is proved separating for every retained response and cost.

*Proof.* The first inequalities are Proposition 15/Theorem 33 applied to the separately identified registered-reset subprotocol. The remaining statements follow from the distinction between one finite diagnostic tuple and the full response presheaf. $\square$

---

### P.16d.12 Proof-Cost Physics

<a id="definition-p16d121-finite-proof-cost-datum"></a>**Definition P.16d.12.1 (Finite Proof-Cost Datum).** For a finite verifier $S$, a proof-cost datum for a mathematical claim $\varphi$ is
$$
\mathfrak P_S(\varphi)=(\Pi_\varphi,V_S,C_S,\eta_S)
$$
where $\Pi_\varphi$ is a finite proof or certificate family, $V_S$ is the verification protocol, $C_S(\pi)$ is the physical resource cost of producing and verifying $\pi\in\Pi_\varphi$, and $\eta_S$ is the accepted verification tolerance.

<a id="theorem-p16d122-pce-selection-of-proof-representatives"></a>**Theorem P.16d.12.2 (PCE Selection of Proof Representatives).** If two proof certificates $\pi_1,\pi_2$ verify the same claim $\varphi$ to the same tolerance and induce the same finite verification response, while
$$
C_S(\pi_1)<C_S(\pi_2),
$$
then $\pi_2$ is not PCE-selected as the retained representative for $S$ unless it changes another retained response or supplies an independent certificate role.

*Proof.* The two proofs lie in the same finite verification response class for $\varphi$. If $\pi_2$ has strictly larger cost and no additional response or certificate role, it is dominated by $\pi_1$ in the same quotient class. Corollary P.6.1a.4 removes the higher-cost representative. If $\pi_2$ changes another retained response or supplies an independent certificate role, then it is not in the same quotient problem and must be evaluated in the enlarged ledger. ∎

---

### P.16d.13 PCE Curriculum Theory

<a id="definition-p16d131-curriculum-reconstruction-problem"></a>**Definition P.16d.13.1 (Curriculum Reconstruction Problem).** Let $S$ be a learner, $X$ a target response structure, and
$$
\mathbf q=(q_1,\dots,q_n)
$$
a finite instructional sequence. Let
$$
\operatorname{Rec}_S(\mathbf q)
$$
be the learner's reconstructed response presheaf after processing $\mathbf q$. For $\lambda,\gamma\ge0$, define curriculum loss
$$
L_{\mathrm{cur}}(\mathbf q)
=
d_B(\operatorname{Rec}_S(\mathbf q),\mathcal R_X^B)
+
\lambda C_S(\mathbf q)
+
\gamma A_S(\mathbf q)
\tag{P.16d.13.1}
$$
where $d_B$ is retained response discrepancy, $C_S$ is processing cost, and $A_S$ is ambiguity or reconstruction overhead.

<a id="theorem-p16d132-curriculum-pce-existence-and-minimality"></a>**Theorem P.16d.13.2 (Curriculum PCE Existence and Minimality).** For a nonempty finite admissible curriculum menu with real-valued $L_{\mathrm{cur}}$, a minimizer exists. On the registered curriculum-objective branch, PCE selects a minimizer. For two sequences with identical reconstruction, the second is excluded by strict comparison when
$$
\lambda\bigl(C_S(\mathbf q_2)-C_S(\mathbf q_1)\bigr)
+\gamma\bigl(A_S(\mathbf q_2)-A_S(\mathbf q_1)\bigr)>0.
$$

*Proof.* A real-valued function on a nonempty finite menu attains its minimum. Equal reconstruction cancels the discrepancy term, so the displayed expression is exactly $L_{\mathrm{cur}}(\mathbf q_2)-L_{\mathrm{cur}}(\mathbf q_1)$. Its positivity makes the second sequence strictly worse in the registered objective. If both weights vanish, larger unweighted cost or ambiguity does not give this strict comparison. ∎

### P.16d.14 Institutional Error-Correction Theory

<a id="definition-p16d141-institutional-predictive-code"></a>**Definition P.16d.14.1 (Institutional Predictive Code).** An institution at budget $B$ is a finite network
$$
\mathcal I=(\{S_i\},\mathsf R,\mathsf V,\mathsf C,\mathsf U)
$$
where $\{S_i\}$ are predictive agents or subsystems, $\mathsf R$ is a finite record channel, $\mathsf V$ is a verification protocol family, $\mathsf C$ is a correction map family, and $\mathsf U$ is an update rule on retained institutional records.

Let $E_B$ be a finite set of admissible record corruptions, written $e\cdot r$ for the corrupted record obtained from $r$. The code corrects $E_B$ when for every retained record $r$ and every corruption $e\in E_B$,
$$
\mathsf C(e\cdot r)\sim_B r.
\tag{P.16d.14.1}
$$

<a id="theorem-p16d142-institutional-preservation-criterion"></a>**Theorem P.16d.14.2 (Institutional Preservation Criterion).** An institutional predictive code preserves knowledge against $E_B$ exactly when its correction maps descend to the identity on the retained response quotient for all corruptions in $E_B$.

*Proof.* If $\mathsf C(e\cdot r)\sim_B r$ for every retained $r$ and $e$, the corrupted and corrected record induces the same finite response class as the uncorrupted record; hence the quotient knowledge state is preserved. Conversely, if knowledge is preserved in the quotient under all $e\in E_B$, then the corrected corrupted record and the original record must be equivalent in $Q_B$, which is exactly (P.16d.14.1). ∎
